# Decision log

One short entry per decision. Newest at the bottom. Template:

```markdown
## D-<number>: <title> (<date>)
- Context: <what forced a choice>
- Decision: <what you chose>
- Alternatives: <what you rejected and why>
- Consequences: <what this makes easier or harder>
```

Numbers are references; entries are never deleted. D-118 and D-119 are cited as planned designs but were never written as entries (D-117 holds the alternative-cost designs; the plans for spell copies and Cumulative upkeep became D-129 and D-127), and D-122 was never used. An entry marked superseded or partly superseded says by which decision; a final `Status:` line records what later happened to an entry that was not replaced. Older entries cite sections of `docs/ROADMAP.md`, `docs/MECHANICS.md` ("Stage Pn") and files in `docs/proposals/` or `docs/analysis/` by their names at the time: the roadmap was reduced to the open work, the per-stage parser sections of MECHANICS were collapsed into an index, three implemented proposals moved to `docs/design/` and the two analysis notes were removed in the docs cleanup.

## D-001: Two-phase event pipeline (2026-10-20)
- Context: Replacement and prevention effects (CR 614–616) must change an event before it happens, but the spec only described events as a record of what happened.
- Decision: Every state change is proposed, run through applicable replacement and prevention effects (ordered by the affected player when several apply), then committed and emitted. See SPEC 17.1 A1.
- Alternatives: Special-casing each replacement inside its primitive (enters-tapped inside the zone-change primitive, prevention inside damage). Rejected: it doesn't compose and each new replacement would touch every primitive.
- Consequences: One mechanism covers enters-tapped, exile-instead, prevention, draw replacement and CR 903.9b. Primitives become slightly more indirect: they propose, they don't mutate.

## D-002: Priority is a decision kind (2026-10-20)
- Context: The spec had two vocabularies for "what may this seat do now": `getLegalActions` for priority and `PendingDecision` for everything else. Two code paths in both the UI and the AI.
- Decision: The engine always waits on exactly one `PendingDecision` for one seat; having priority is a decision kind. Handlers live in a `Record<DecisionKind, Handler>` per consumer. See SPEC 17.1 A2.
- Alternatives: Keep both and reconcile in a wrapper. Rejected: the exhaustive-handler guarantee only holds if there is one vocabulary.
- Consequences: Adding a decision kind fails compilation until UI and AI handle it. The engine's main loop becomes "resolve the pending decision, run SBAs and triggers, compute the next one".

## D-003: Casting is a transaction with a snapshot (2026-10-20)
- Context: CR 601.2 is a sequence of sub-decisions, and both Arena-style cancel and the illegal-action rewind need the pre-cast state back.
- Decision: Starting a cast or activation stores a `CastingContext` and a pre-cast snapshot in state; cancel and rewind restore the snapshot. See SPEC 17.1 A3.
- Alternatives: Inverse actions (undo log). Rejected: state is plain data with structural sharing, so a snapshot is nearly free and cannot drift from the forward logic.
- Consequences: Mana abilities activated during payment are part of the transaction and are undone by cancel, matching CR 601.2h / 732.

## D-004: Last-known information is a first-class engine feature (2026-10-20)
- Context: Dies triggers, "its power", "return it" and leaves-the-battlefield triggers need the object as it last existed (CR 113.7a, 603.10). The spec did not mention LKI.
- Decision: Zone changes record LKI; trigger detection runs against the pre-event state. See SPEC 17.1 A4.
- Alternatives: Re-derive from the new object. Rejected: the new object has none of its old counters, pumps or attachments (CR 400.7).
- Consequences: Event records carry a reference to the LKI snapshot, which the log and UI can show too.

## D-005: Mana objects carry restrictions (2026-10-20)
- Context: Many ramp and ritual effects produce mana that can only be spent on some things. A pool of plain color counts cannot represent that.
- Decision: The pool holds typed mana objects with color, snow, source and an optional spend restriction; the payment planner respects them. See SPEC 17.1 A5.
- Alternatives: Treat restricted mana as unsupported. Rejected: it would exclude too many popular cards and the planner change is contained.
- Consequences: The planner becomes a small assignment problem over mana objects rather than a color count subtraction.

## D-006: Immutable state with structural sharing (2026-10-20)
- Context: `applyAction` must stay under 5 ms and the AI simulates many combat outcomes; deep-cloning a two-player board on every action would not meet that.
- Decision: Updates produce new state sharing unchanged subtrees; derived characteristics are cached per state version. See SPEC 17.1 A6.
- Alternatives: Mutable state with explicit clone. Rejected: cloning cost and accidental sharing bugs in the AI.
- Consequences: Engine code uses an immutable-update helper everywhere; replays and snapshots (D-003) become free.

## D-007: "Supported" includes a runtime guarantee (2026-10-20)
- Context: A card could parse into an AST that the interpreter cannot execute, which would silently break the honesty priority.
- Decision: `validateAst` runs at parse time; the interpreter has no not-implemented path; an interpreter failure is an engine bug with a one-click report and the card is downgraded for that game. See SPEC 17.2 A7.
- Alternatives: Trust the parser. Rejected: the parser and interpreter evolve independently and will drift.
- Consequences: Every primitive and decision kind the grammar can emit must be implemented before the grammar rule ships.

## D-008: Test coverage is per rule and primitive, not per card (2026-10-20)
- Context: "Supported cards are covered by tests" was ambiguous; a test per card does not scale to the card pool.
- Decision: Coverage is required for grammar rule IDs and primitives, plus the curated AST snapshot set. See SPEC 17.2 A8.
- Alternatives: A test per card. Rejected: unbounded test growth, and it tests templating rather than rules.
- Consequences: The card support loop adds tests per mechanic and ruling, which is what section 8.3 already says.

## D-010: The AI gets a `determinize` API and no hidden-info search in v1 (2026-10-20)
- Context: The AI only receives views, but simulation needs a full state. The spec implied determinization without an API for it.
- Decision: `determinize(view, rng)` in the engine with an AI-owned PRNG; v1 heuristic agent simulates only public-information combat; MCTS is v2. See SPEC 17.3 A10.
- Alternatives: Let the AI read the real state. Rejected: it cheats and the spec forbids it. Build MCTS in v1. Rejected: it is the largest optional piece of work and the heuristic agent is the stated v1 default.
- Consequences: The game PRNG and the AI PRNG never interact, so replays stay deterministic regardless of AI timing.

## D-011: Benchmark the AI against a greedy baseline (2026-10-20)
- Context: Beating a random agent 90% of the time is reached by any agent that attacks.
- Decision: Add `GreedyAgent`; M7 requires 70% against it, 95% against random, and near-symmetric self-play. See SPEC 17.3 A11.
- Alternatives: Keep the random-only bar. Rejected: it does not measure competence.
- Consequences: One more agent to maintain, which also serves as a difficulty level candidate.

## D-012: Scenario DSL is an M1 deliverable (2026-10-20)
- Context: Thirty required scenarios plus one test per ruling in the support loop means hundreds of state setups.
- Decision: M1 delivers a fluent scenario builder that all scenario tests use. See SPEC 17.3 A12.
- Alternatives: Hand-built states per test. Rejected: slow to write and easy to get subtly wrong.
- Consequences: The DSL is part of the engine package's test utilities and documented in `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`.

## D-013: Soak test split between PR and nightly (2026-10-20; partly superseded by D-126 and D-132)
- Context: 500 games per PR would make CI too slow to be useful.
- Decision: 20 games per PR, 500 nightly and before each milestone report. See SPEC 17.3 A13.
- Alternatives: 500 per PR. Rejected: CI latency. Nightly only. Rejected: PRs would miss deadlocks.
- Consequences: Two GitHub Actions workflows from M7 on.
- Status: The 20-game and 500-game split stands, but the shape changed: a soak test plays 20 games by default, `pnpm test:soak` plays 100, and the `Soak` workflow is manual and plays 500 (D-126, D-132). The complete suite runs nightly on GitHub's runners (`full.yml`, D-250), skipped when `main` has no new commit; the `Soak` workflow stays manual.


## D-014: Game end is expressed for any number of seats (2026-10-20)
- Context: The spec said "if both players lose at the same time, the game is a draw", which assumes two seats.
- Decision: If every remaining player loses simultaneously, draw; losing players leave the game per CR 800.4a. See SPEC 17.4 A14.
- Alternatives: Two-player special case. Rejected by the spec's own v2 rule.
- Consequences: The v2 multiplayer milestone inherits the rule unchanged.

## D-015: Cite rules with number and title (2026-10-20)
- Context: Rule numbers shift between CR releases.
- Decision: Comments cite `CR 702.19b (Trample)`. See SPEC 17.4 A15.
- Alternatives: Numbers only. Rejected: unresolvable after renumbering.
- Consequences: Slightly longer comments.

## D-016: MIT license (2026-10-20)
- Context: The spec described a free fan project but named no license.
- Decision: MIT for the code; card data and images are never committed except precon snapshots. See SPEC 17.4 A16.
- Alternatives: AGPL. Rejected: the project is a static site with no server, and MIT is the lowest-friction choice for contributors.
- Consequences: `LICENSE` is created in M0.

## D-017: Verify the rules baseline in M0 (2026-10-20)
- Context: The spec names a CR date and an Update Bulletin that must be confirmed against Wizards' site before relying on their rule numbers.
- Decision: M0 downloads the current CR, checks the bulletins and records what was actually found. See SPEC 17.4 A17.
- Alternatives: Trust the spec. Rejected by the spec itself ("when this spec and the CR disagree, the CR wins").
- Consequences: Rule references in the spec are updated in M0 if the numbering differs.

## D-018: Auto-pass is driven by relevant actions and default stops (2026-10-20)
- Context: "Auto-pass when the human has no legal action other than passing" almost never fires, because an untapped land plus any instant is a legal action. The player would click through every step and every stack resolution.
- Decision: A pure `shouldStop(view, settings)` policy in the web app, with Arena-style default stops and a "relevant action" test that requires the action to be affordable and instant-speed. Auto-passes are recorded as normal pass actions. See SPEC 17.5 A18.
- Alternatives: Put the policy in the engine. Rejected: the engine is the rulebook and must not encode UI preferences; the AI has its own policy. Stop only on empty legal-action lists. Rejected as above.
- Consequences: The policy needs the payment planner (affordability) exposed through the view, and an end-to-end test counts clicks.

## D-019: Fixed preview panel and dense-board grouping (2026-10-20)
- Context: Battlefield tiles must be small to fit a Commander board, so the player needs a reliable way to read any card, and 30-permanent boards need to stay legible.
- Decision: A fixed-position preview panel that shows the object as it currently is, rather than a cursor tooltip; hand cards enlarge in place; rows shrink then group identical tokens with a count badge. See SPEC 17.5 A19.
- Alternatives: Cursor-following tooltip. Rejected: it covers the board and breaks keyboard navigation. Never grouping tokens. Rejected: token-heavy decks become unreadable by midgame.
- Consequences: The UI needs a "current characteristics" renderer that reads derived characteristics from the view, which the overlays in section 10 already require.

## D-020: Spike external assumptions in M0 (2026-10-20)
- Context: The spec describes Scryfall fields and the CR download from memory and says not to trust it for API details.
- Decision: Throwaway scripts in M0 confirm each external assumption before anything is designed around it. See SPEC 17.6 A20.
- Alternatives: Discover problems in M4 and M6. Rejected: those are the milestones with the least slack.
- Consequences: M0 takes slightly longer; M4 and M6 start from verified data.

## D-021: Plan the grammar from a corpus (2026-10-20)
- Context: The 60% coverage target is only credible if grammar work is ordered by how many popular cards each template unlocks.
- Decision: A template-frequency tool over the top 1,000 cards runs before M6 and orders the work. See SPEC 17.6 A21.
- Alternatives: Write rules in the order the spec lists mechanics. Rejected: that list is a floor, not a priority order.
- Consequences: The same tool feeds the backlog report, so it is not extra code.

## D-022: STATUS.md and per-milestone progress files (2026-10-20)
- Context: The project spans many agent sessions; the spec asks for progress reports without saying where they live.
- Decision: `docs/STATUS.md` is the single handoff file; reports live in `docs/progress/`. See SPEC 17.6 A22.
- Alternatives: Reports in commit messages or chat. Rejected: not discoverable by a fresh session.
- Consequences: `AGENTS.md` instructs every session to read `docs/STATUS.md` first and update it last.

## D-024: Rules lookup script (2026-10-20)
- Context: The spec says to look rules up in `docs/rules/` instead of relying on memory, but offers no tool for it.
- Decision: `pnpm rule <number>` and `pnpm rule --search <text>`. See SPEC 17.6 A24.
- Alternatives: Grep. Rejected: the CR's numbering and subrule layout make grep output hard to read.
- Consequences: Tiny script in `tools/`, used by the playbook.

## D-025: Manual adjustments go through `applyAction` (2026-10-20)
- Context: Section 10's manual adjustments for unsupported cards would break determinism and replay if they mutated state directly.
- Decision: `ManualAdjust` is an action kind, logged and replayed like any other. See SPEC 17.6 A25.
- Alternatives: Direct state edits in the UI. Rejected: violates "one way to change state".
- Consequences: The engine gains one action kind whose legality check is "the human may always do this"; the log marks it as manual.

## D-026: Saves and replays are the action log (2026-10-20)
- Context: State snapshots become invalid when the engine changes; the spec already requires seed-plus-log reproducibility.
- Decision: Saves store seed, decklists, settings, action log and versions; loading replays; a version mismatch is refused. See SPEC 17.6 A26.
- Alternatives: Snapshot saves with migration. Rejected: migrations for a rules engine are error-prone and the honesty priority forbids best-effort loading.
- Consequences: Loading a long game replays every action, which the performance budget makes fast enough.
- Status: Partly superseded by D-165: there is no player-facing save, load, resume or replay export or import; the seed and the action log stay, and `replayGame` is a test tool for determinism.

## D-027: Real cards in the M1 test set (2026-10-20)
- Context: The M1 test cards could be invented, but real cards give M3 real names and images and seed the overrides registry and snapshots.
- Decision: Use the real cards listed in SPEC 17.6 A27.
- Alternatives: Synthetic cards. Rejected: no downstream reuse.
- Consequences: M1 needs a tiny card-data fixture for those cards; the M3 precons are built from them.

## D-028: Honesty summary, concede, AI watchdog (2026-10-20)
- Context: Three small gaps: the player should know before turn one what was dropped from either deck; there was no way to concede; the "never deadlock" rule had no enforcement.
- Decision: Pre-game dropped-abilities summary, concede as a decision option, Worker-side time-budget watchdog with logged fallback. See SPEC 17.6 A28.
- Alternatives: None worth recording.
- Consequences: One more decision option, one more Worker responsibility, one more soak-test failure condition.

## D-029: Stack choices before M0 (2026-10-20)
- Context: The spec names TypeScript, pnpm, React, Vite, Vitest, fast-check and Playwright but leaves the linter, state management, Worker RPC, schema validation and branching workflow open.
- Decision: Biome plus dependency-cruiser; React 19, Zustand, Comlink; Zod schemas for serialized data; one PR per milestone. See SPEC 17.7.
- Alternatives: ESLint plus Prettier plus eslint-plugin-boundaries. Rejected: slower and more configuration for the same result. Committing straight to `main`. Rejected: the milestone checkpoints already assume a review point.
- Consequences: All pinned in M0; changing any of them needs a new D-entry.

## D-030: TypeScript 6.0.3 instead of 7.0.2 (2026-10-20)
- Context: SPEC 4.1 asks for current stable versions, and TypeScript 7.0.2 is the latest. dependency-cruiser 18.7.0 (and 18.6.0) support TypeScript `>=2.0.0 <7.0.0` only. Under 7 it silently registers no `.ts` extension and scans zero modules, so the boundary rules reported no violations on any input. The first version of the boundary tests passed vacuously for that reason.
- Decision: Pin TypeScript to 6.0.3. The boundary test now fails when a cruise scans no TypeScript file, so this failure mode cannot return silently.
- Alternatives: Cruise with the swc transpiler under TypeScript 7. Rejected: swc erases type-only imports, so `import type { X } from '@commander-arena/cards'` in the engine would bypass every boundary rule. A different boundary tool (eslint-plugin-boundaries). Rejected for now: same TypeScript-compiler dependency risk plus ESLint, which D-029 chose not to use.
- Consequences: Revisit when dependency-cruiser declares TypeScript 7 support; listed in `docs/ROADMAP.md`.

## D-031: Determinism is enforced by compiler settings plus a Biome plugin (2026-10-20)
- Context: SPEC 4.2 forbids DOM, network, timers, `Math.random` and `Date.now` in the engine, and A10 gives the AI its own seeded PRNG. A lint rule that greps text breaks on strings and comments.
- Decision: Engine and AI tsconfigs set `lib` to ES2023 and `types` to an empty list, so DOM, timer and Node globals do not type-check. A Biome GritQL plugin (`tools/lint/no-nondeterminism.grit`), scoped by `overrides` in `biome.json` to `packages/engine/src` and `packages/ai/src`, bans `Math.random`, `Date.now`, `new Date`, `performance.now`, `localeCompare` and `toLocaleString`. The last two depend on the host locale and would break replays across machines. `tools/lint/nondeterminism.test.ts` reads the real overrides and proves the ban applies there and nowhere else.
- Alternatives: A grep script. Rejected as above. An ESLint rule. Rejected: D-029 chose Biome.
- Consequences: Time and randomness reach engine and AI code only through injected parameters. Extending the ban means adding a pattern to the plugin and a case to its test.

## D-032: pnpm 12.14.0 with its release-age guard, dependency-cruiser 18.6.0 (2026-10-20)
- Context: SPEC 4.1 asks for current stable versions. pnpm 12.14.0 is current; the container ships 10.28.0. pnpm 12 rejects packages published less than about a day ago (`minimumReleaseAge`). dependency-cruiser 18.7.0 was published on 2026-10-19 and tripped it.
- Decision: Use pnpm 12.14.0 (`packageManager` in `package.json`), keep its default release-age policy, and pin dependency-cruiser to 18.6.0, the newest release older than the cutoff. All checks pass under this combination.
- Alternatives: Stay on pnpm 10. Rejected: older than current and it lacks the guard. Disable the policy to take 18.7.0. Rejected: the guard is cheap supply-chain protection and 18.7.0 offers nothing the project needs.
- Consequences: Bump dependency-cruiser once a newer release has aged past the cutoff, and only together with a check of its TypeScript support (see D-030).

## D-033: Boundary tests build throwaway monorepos (2026-10-20)
- Context: M0 requires "a test proves the boundary rule rejects a forbidden import". Fixtures committed to the repo would be scanned by the real lint run, and relative-import fixtures would not exercise package-name resolution.
- Decision: `tools/boundaries/boundaries.test.ts` builds a small pnpm-style monorepo in a temp directory for each case, with packages symlinked the way pnpm links them, runs dependency-cruiser with the real rules from `tools/boundaries/rules.cjs`, and asserts which rules fire. A meta test fails when any rule has no case, and a guard fails when a cruise scans no TypeScript.
- Alternatives: Committed fixture directories. Rejected as above.
- Consequences: Adding a boundary rule requires adding a failing case for it.

## D-035: Rules baseline verified; bulletin applied by reference; 7xx shift handled by titles (2026-10-20)
- Context: A17 required confirming the CR baseline. The cloud session cannot reach Wizards, so the owner downloaded the file locally with `pnpm rules:fetch` and committed it. The October 19, 2026 bulletin was read from the owner's paste of the page.
- Decision: The baseline is the CR effective September 25, 2026 (sha256 in `docs/rules/RULES_VERSION.md`) plus the Mystery Booster Commander Edition bulletin. The bulletin's changes are applied to the project's rule references and plans, not to the text file, until Wizards publishes the file that contains them. Rule numbers are always cited with their title (A15), because the bulletin inserts 713 "Meld Cards" and shifts every later 7xx number by one. D-003's citation of 732 for Handling Illegal Actions was wrong; it is 733 in the September file and will be 734. Meld cards are no longer double-faced cards. Rulebreaker (new 903.5e) is unsupported in v1: deck validation flags a commander that has it. The committed CR text stays in the private repository; the redistribution question is a roadmap item to settle before going public.
- Alternatives: Wait for the republished CR before verifying. Rejected: the bulletin is the authoritative notice and the SPEC says to read bulletins for exactly this reason. Patch the text file by hand. Rejected: it would no longer match its hash or Wizards' file.
- Consequences: `tools/rules/cr-real.test.ts` fails if the parser ever drops a real rule or the file changes without updating the record. The next CR publication is a small, scripted update.

## D-037: The scenario DSL lives in the engine's public API (2026-10-20)
- Context: A12 puts the DSL in M1 and says every later test, including those the card support loop writes, uses it. Tests in `packages/ai`, `packages/cards` and `apps/web` can only import the engine through `src/index.ts`.
- Decision: The DSL is in `packages/engine/src/testing/` and exported from the engine index. It is pure (no Node, no clock, no randomness) so the engine's purity rules still hold. It writes the initial state directly and performs every later step through `applyAction`.
- Alternatives: A separate test-utils package. Rejected: a fifth library package for one module, and it would need the engine's internals. A subpath export. Rejected: `exports` currently has one entry and the boundary rules assume `src/index.ts` is the whole public API.
- Consequences: A few kilobytes of test builder ship in the engine bundle; if that matters, tree-shaking removes it from the web app because nothing imports it there. Scenario tests inside the engine use a few deep imports of engine internals, which is allowed within one package.

## D-038: A moved object ceases to exist; last-known information is kept separately (2026-10-20)
- Context: CR 400.7 says a card that changes zones becomes a new object. The first engine core kept the old object in the object map, so state-based actions kept finding a creature that had already died and never settled.
- Decision: `moveObject` deletes the old object and stores its last-known information in `lki`. Resolution skips an instruction whose object no longer exists, which is how a spell does as much as it can (CR 608.2b-c).
- Alternatives: Keep stale objects and mark them dead. Rejected: every zone scan and the object count grow without bound, and a dead flag is easy to forget.
- Consequences: `getObject` throws for an id that has left; code that may hold an old id (targets on resolution, instructions) uses `state.objects[id]` and handles absence. `checkInvariants` verifies one live object per card.

## D-039: Cancelling a cast restores the game, not the action count (2026-10-20)
- Context: A3 says cancel restores the pre-cast snapshot. `actionCount` is documented as the length of the action log, and the cast and the cancel were both applied.
- Decision: Restore the snapshot but keep the current `actionCount`. Tests that compare "same position before and after" use `positionHash`, which ignores the counter.
- Alternatives: Rewind the counter. Rejected: replays and saves are action logs, so the counter must count every applied action.
- Consequences: A saved game's log includes the cancelled cast attempt, and replaying it reproduces the same state.

## D-041: Combat declarations are accepted by validation, not enumerated (2026-10-21)
- Context: A legal attack declaration is any subset of the eligible creatures, each with a target; a legal block declaration is any assignment of blockers to attackers. With ten creatures that is over a thousand subsets, and damage divisions are larger still. SPEC 4.2 allows a decision to carry "the legal options (or a validator)".
- Decision: `declareAttackers`, `declareBlockers` and `assignDamage` carry the candidates (who may attack and at what, who may block what, how much is lethal to each blocker). `applyAction` validates any answer against the same legality code that built the candidates. `legalActionsForDecision` lists a representative subset (no attack, each attacker alone at each target, everyone at one target; no block and each legal single block; the default damage division) and every listed action is accepted. The decision for blockers carries each attacker's minimum blocker count (2 for menace) so a consumer can avoid illegal single blocks without reading hidden state.
- Alternatives: Enumerate every subset. Rejected: exponential, and the AI and UI would still build answers from the candidates. Let the AI call a rules helper with the full state. Rejected: it would need hidden information.
- Consequences: A UI builds answers from the candidates and may rely on the engine to reject mistakes. The AI's handlers construct their own legal answers; the property tests check that everything the engine lists is accepted.

## D-042: Damage the controller cannot influence is automatic; only real choices become a decision (2026-10-21)
- Context: CR 510.1 has players announce how every creature assigns damage. Almost all assignments are forced.
- Decision: The engine computes a damage plan for each combat damage step. An unblocked creature, a creature with one blocker and no excess, and every blocker's damage are assigned automatically. An `assignDamage` decision appears only for an attacker blocked by two or more creatures, or a trampler with more power than lethal to its single blocker (CR 510.1c, 702.19b). The decision lists the blockers in declaration order with lethal values that account for marked damage and deathtouch (CR 702.2c, 120.6). Excess trample damage goes to what the creature is attacking: a player, a planeswalker or a battle (CR 702.19b), and everything goes there when the blockers have all left (CR 702.19d). "Trample over planeswalkers" (CR 702.19c) is a separate keyword and is not supported.
- Alternatives: Always ask for every attacker. Rejected: it would stop the game for nothing and breaks the auto-pass goals of A18.
- Consequences: Most combats have no damage decision. The first-strike step records who had first or double strike when it began, so a creature that gains first strike afterwards still deals damage in the regular step (CR 510.4).

## D-043: Planeswalkers and battles are supported as attack targets with synthetic test cards only (2026-10-21)
- Context: M2 requires planeswalkers and battles as attack targets. Every real planeswalker has loyalty abilities (CR 606, M5) and every real battle has a back face (transform, M5), so none can be marked supported yet.
- Decision: The engine implements the card types: loyalty and defense counters on entering (CR 306.5b, 310.4b), damage removing them (CR 120.3c, 120.3h), the state-based actions (CR 704.5i, 704.5w), and being attacked and blocked for. `planeswalker` and `battle` are in `SUPPORTED_FEATURES.cardTypes`; real cards stay unsupported because their abilities and layouts are not. Tests use SYNTHETIC vanilla cards. In a two-player game the opponent of a battle's controller is its protector (CR 310.11); the choice among several opponents arrives with M10. Siege battles (CR 704.5v) are not supported.
- Alternatives: Leave the types out until M5. Rejected: M2's done-when and scenario tests need them, and the engine rules are the same either way.
- Consequences: Adding loyalty abilities in M5 makes real planeswalkers executable without touching combat.

## D-044: A framework-free game host behind a Comlink Worker; the page sees snapshots only (2026-10-21)
- Context: The engine and the AI must run off the main thread (SPEC 4.1, D-016), but the page and the tests both need to drive a real game.
- Decision: `apps/web/src/game/host.ts` is a plain class (`GameHost`) that owns the only `GameState`, applies the human's action, then lets the AI answer until the human is asked something or the game ends. `game/worker.ts` exposes it with Comlink; tests use it in process. The page receives a `Snapshot`: the human's `GameView`, the steps applied since the last snapshot with their events, the new log lines (built from events with names taken from the states around each action) and the AI fallback count. A refused action returns the unchanged view plus the engine's error. Time is injected (`performance.now` in the Worker). The AI watchdog (A28) measures each answer against its budget plus a margin and replaces a late answer with the safe fallback; a synchronous agent cannot be preempted, so the watchdog bounds the damage after the fact and counts it (the soak test treats a count above zero as a failure).
- Alternatives: Run the AI per step with a round trip to the page for each AI action. Rejected: it makes the AI's turn as slow as the message latency and gains nothing, since animation is driven from the returned events. Hand the page the `GameState`. Rejected: it breaks hidden information.
- Consequences: The AI's whole turn arrives as one snapshot, so M3 shows the result of the AI's turn at once and the log tells what happened; per-event animation (M8) will replay `steps`.

## D-045: Auto-pass details: only instants are relevant, and your own spell resolves without a click (2026-10-21; partly superseded by D-075, D-138 and D-143)
- Context: A18 defines a "relevant action" as an affordable instant-speed spell or non-mana ability, and says to stop when an object goes on the stack while you have one.
- Decision: The engine already lists a `castSpell` option only when timing, targets and the whole cost are satisfied, so `hasRelevantAction` is "a `castSpell` option whose card is an instant". The engine offers only mana abilities as `activateAbility` options in M3, and those are never relevant; a non-mana ability will need a flag on the option when it exists (docs/ROADMAP.md). With a non-empty stack the policy stops only when the top object belongs to someone else and the player has a relevant action; the player's own spell resolves without a click even while they hold an instant, which matches Arena and keeps one click per spell. Full Control restores a stop at every priority point.
- Alternatives: Stop for any object on the stack. Rejected: a player holding Counterspell would click through every one of their own spells.
- Consequences: A player who wants to respond to their own spell uses Full Control or the "Passing…" chip, which seizes priority before the next automatic pass.
- Status: Partly superseded: non-mana abilities became `activate` options (D-075), and what counts as a relevant action, the stops and the yields were reworked in D-138 and D-143.


## D-046: Cards are CSS frames in M3, mana symbols are drawn originally, and Playwright is pinned to match the sandbox Chromium (2026-10-21)
- Context: Fixture cards are not matched to Scryfall, the cloud network blocks Scryfall's image host, and bundling Wizards' mana-font glyphs is an undecided licensing question.
- Decision: Cards render as drawn frames (name, cost, type line, rules text, power/toughness, color band) behind one component seam where an image can replace them. Mana symbols are circles with a letter or number. `@playwright/test` is pinned at 1.56.1, the release whose Chromium build (1194) is preinstalled in the cloud sandbox, and tests run with `CHROMIUM_PATH` there; CI installs Chromium with `playwright install chromium`.
- Alternatives: Fetch images at runtime from Scryfall. Rejected until M4 gives each card its image URI. Use the latest Playwright. Rejected: it would need a browser download the sandbox blocks.
- Consequences: Swapping in real art and the mana font later changes two components. End-to-end tests are named `*.e2e.ts` so Vitest does not collect them.

## D-048: Scryfall bulk data is gzipped JSON Lines, and collection lookups take the front-face name (2026-10-21)
- Context: The A20 spikes ran live on 2026-10-21 (`docs/spikes/RESULTS.md`). Two assumptions in SPEC 6.2 did not hold.
- Decision: (1) `GET /bulk-data` entries carry `jsonl_download_uri` (gzipped JSON Lines on `data.scryfall.io`) and `compressed_size`, not `download_uri`, `size` and `content_type`; the `oracle_cards` file is about 25 MB compressed. The M4 importer streams the file through `DecompressionStream('gzip')` and parses it line by line, keeping memory constant, and reads the field names from this record instead of the SPEC. The bulk spike was amended to the real fields and no longer downloads. (2) `POST /cards/collection` matched a double-faced, split or adventure card only by its front-face name, so deck import sends the part of a decklist name before ` // ` and never the full name. Other observed limits stand: 75 identifiers per request, `Content-Type: application/json` required, results in request order, unknown names listed in `not_found` as `{name}`.
- Alternatives: Keep the SPEC wording and let the importer discover the format. Rejected: the importer would have been written against fields that do not exist.
- Consequences: SPEC 6.2 is out of date on the bulk fields; the SPEC changes only with the owner's approval, so this entry and `docs/spikes/RESULTS.md` are the record until then. The import code needs tests with a SYNTHETIC gzipped JSONL stream and with `A // B` lines.

## D-049: Deploy with Cloudflare, a static site on its free tier (2026-10-21)
- Context: D-023 chose GitHub Pages, but GitHub Pages was free only for public repositories, and this one was private then.
- Decision: The site is a static build (`apps/web/dist`, relative base, a module Worker), so any static host works. Use Cloudflare Pages connected to the repository through its Git integration: free tier, private repositories allowed, no secrets in the repository. Cloudflare's current dashboard creates a Workers project with static assets, so `wrangler.jsonc` at the repository root names the project (`commander-arena`) and the asset directory (`apps/web/dist`). Build command `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile && pnpm --filter @commander-arena/web build`; deploy command `npx wrangler deploy`; command for non-production branches (previews) `npx wrangler versions upload`; no `NODE_VERSION` variable (Cloudflare reads `22` from `.nvmrc`; a mistyped value `2` failed the first build) and pnpm comes from the `packageManager` field. Production branch `main`. `npx wrangler deploy --dry-run` accepts the config. `.github/workflows/pages.yml` stays but runs only by hand, as the GitHub Pages alternative.
- Alternatives: Make the repository public now. Rejected until the licensing questions are settled. Netlify or Vercel. Equivalent, but Cloudflare Pages has no bandwidth limit on the free tier. GitHub Enterprise trial. Rejected: it expires.
- Consequences: The deployed site is reachable by anyone with its URL; it contains only the built app, never `docs/rules/`. The deploy no longer depends on this repository's workflows.

## D-050: Undo takes back small human actions inside one priority window (2026-10-21)
- Context: After playing M3 the owner asked to undo small actions such as tapping or moving a card while still in the same step and before anything important happened. Magic has no undo, but this is a game against an AI and Arena offers a limited form for mana.
- Decision: The Worker host keeps a history of states, one per human action, and `undo()` pops one. Only `playLand`, `castSpell`, `activateAbility`, `chooseTargets`, `payAuto` and `payManual` are recorded, and only while no AI action followed and no event touched hidden information or the game's randomness or moved the turn forward (a draw, a shuffle, a mulligan, a new step or turn, the end of the game). Anything else clears the history: a pass, a declaration, a mulligan. Cancelling a cast returns to where it began and drops the points taken inside it. An undo restores the earlier state object and truncates the action and log lists to it, so an exported replay stays exact. The page shows an Undo button with a count and binds Ctrl+Z or Cmd+Z; after an undo the autopilot waits for the player.
- Alternatives: Allow undoing a resolved spell or a pass. Rejected: the AI has acted by then and the opponent's information has changed. Only mana taps (Arena's rule). Rejected: the owner asked for moves too. A snapshot per step. Rejected: it would forbid taking back a land play made earlier in the same step.
- Consequences: A spell the autopilot passes to resolution can no longer be undone, so the window to undo a cast is the "Passing…" chip or Full Control. States are shared structurally, so the history is cheap; it is capped at 40 points.

## D-051: A beginner AI for the playable game, the free first mulligan on by default (2026-10-21)
- Context: The owner saw the random opponent tap a land for mana and use it for nothing. Measured over one 40-turn game, `RandomLegalAgent` chose manual mana tapping 150 times and cast 16 spells. The owner also asked for a London mulligan with a free first mulligan.
- Decision: `CasualAgent` (`packages/ai/src/casual-agent.ts`) is the opponent in the web game. It never taps mana by hand (casting auto-pays) and never concedes; it plays a land, casts its most expensive castable spell, keeps hands of two to five lands, attacks when an attack is likely safe, blocks to survive or trade and chump-blocks only against lethal damage; instants and sweepers are held until their target condition holds. Over game seeds 1 to 60 it beat `RandomLegalAgent` in 47 games (78%) and cast about three times as many spells in the first twelve turns (4.5 against 1.5); over whole games the ratio is about 1.3 because the decks hold few spells. `RandomLegalAgent` stays for engine tests and soak games. The free first mulligan (`freeFirstMulligan`, the engine already supported it) is on by default in the web app with a checkbox on the menu; the London bottoming then starts from the second mulligan (CR 103.5, 103.5c).
- Alternatives: Filter mana abilities out of `RandomLegalAgent`. Rejected: it would stop the 100-game tests from exercising manual mana. Wait for the heuristic AI. Rejected: the owner is playing now.
- Consequences: The heuristics were tuned on the fixture pool only and model neither combat tricks nor holding blockers back; the real `HeuristicAgent` (SPEC 9) replaces this later.
- Status: Two notes. The engine default of `freeFirstMulligan` is off; the web host turns it on (`apps/web/src/game/host.ts`), so "on by default" is true of the web app only. `HeuristicAgent` and `GreedyAgent` (M7) are not built; `CasualAgent` is the only AI the web app uses.


## D-052: A small parser framework and an honest support status in M4 (2026-10-21)
- Context: SPEC 7.1 wants every imported card to be supported or unsupported with a diagnostic, but the Oracle grammar is M6. M4 still has to import and play real decks.
- Decision: `packages/cards/src/convert/parser/` is the framework M6 grows: Oracle text is normalized per face (reminder text out, self references to `~`), split into abilities, and matched against composable rules that must consume the whole ability. M4 has two rules, `keyword.line` (built from `SUPPORTED_FEATURES.keywordKinds`, so a keyword is understood exactly when the engine can run it) and `mana.tap-add`, plus intrinsic basic-land mana from the type line and empty text for vanilla cards. An ability no rule consumes is recorded as an `UnparsedAbility` with the text, where matching stopped and the closest rule, and is DROPPED from the definition; instants and sorceries with such text get no effect. A card is `supported` only if every ability on every face parsed, its layout and types are supported and `validateCard` is clean. `PARSER_VERSION` stays 1 and is bumped whenever rules change; support reports are cached per oracle id and parser version, so a bump recomputes them (SPEC test 30).
- Fixtures are the first overrides, matched by exact name, and used only when the Scryfall Oracle text and printed characteristics agree with the hand-written fixture. A disagreement means no fixture, the reasons `fixture mismatch` and the differing fields, and an unsupported card. This is the first time the unverified M1 and M2 fixtures meet real data.
- Alternatives: Write the grammar now. Rejected: M6 is ordered by a corpus of the most popular cards (A21). Mark partially understood cards as partly supported. Rejected by the honesty rule.
- Consequences: Coverage in M4 is low outside vanilla, keyword and mana-only cards, and the report says so. M5 adds oracle-id keyed overrides behind the same `OverrideRegistry` interface.

## D-053: Import pipeline rules (2026-10-21)
- Context: SPEC 6 describes the decklist formats, Scryfall resolution and Commander validation in prose.
- Decision: The decklist parser is a hand-written scanner with line-numbered errors; it never throws. Names go to Scryfall's collection endpoint by front face only (D-048) and results are matched by name, never by position; names the collection endpoint does not return are retried with `named?exact=` then `named?fuzzy=`, and a fuzzy match is used only after the player accepts it. Sideboard, maybeboard and companion lines are listed and never played; tokens sections are ignored with a note. A list that does not mark a commander gets a picker of eligible cards. Validation follows the baseline CR's text as read with `pnpm rule`: 903.3 eligibility (including legendary Vehicles and Spacecraft with power and toughness), 903.4 and 903.5 identity and size, singleton with the "any number" and "up to N" exceptions read from Oracle text, the partner family of 702.124 and a land that breaks identity through its basic land types (903.5d). Card data is cached in IndexedDB for 24 hours; a deck is saved as its text and re-resolved on demand; every IndexedDB operation fails soft to memory.
- Alternatives: Resolve every name individually. Rejected: it would take minutes at 2 requests per second. Use fuzzy matches silently. Rejected: a wrong card in a deck is worse than a question.
- Consequences: Known gaps: a commander that makes you choose its colors (CR 903.4b) and interchangeable names (CR 201.3) are not modelled. The sample decklists for each export format were written from memory of the formats; real exports may differ.

## D-055: Unsupported cards need an explicit confirmation to play (2026-10-21; superseded by D-056)
- Context: SPEC 7.1 lets the player use unsupported cards after a warning; A28 asks for a summary before the first turn.
- Decision: "Play this deck" lists every unsupported card with its count, says that unsupported abilities are ignored and never half-run, and requires "Play anyway". The engine already drops unparsed text, and an engine integration test plays whole games with decks full of unreadable and transform cards without a rejected action or a fallback.
- Alternatives: Refuse to play decks with unsupported cards. Rejected: the owner wants to play real decks while coverage grows.
- Consequences: The honesty summary in the game still lists them (A28).

## D-056: A deck with an unsupported card is invalid and cannot be played (2026-10-21)
- Context: D-055 followed SPEC 7.1: play with unsupported cards after a warning, their unparsed abilities dropped. The owner tried the import screen with a request for Korvold, Fae-Cursed King (triggered abilities the engine does not have) and said that card should not be imported as a whole and the deck should be invalidated.
- Decision: Supersedes D-055. The import service adds an error `unsupported` to the deck check, naming the cards, and `playable` is false whenever any card of the deck (a commander included) is unsupported. "Play this deck" stays disabled and the panel says why and what to do: request support or replace the card. The "Play anyway" dialog is removed. The coverage report, "Why unsupported?" and "Request support" are unchanged. SPEC amendment A29 records the change in 7.1 and A28. The engine still drops unparsed text; a test plays whole games with decks of unsupported cards to prove it cannot crash, but only hand-built decks can reach that path now.
- Alternatives: Keep the warning and let the player choose. Rejected by the owner. Hide unsupported cards from the deck silently. Rejected: it would change the deck without saying so.
- Consequences: Real decks are playable only when every card is supported, which M5 and M6 widen. Request support is now the way forward for a blocked deck, and `docs/design/` holds the proposal for the first request (triggers, Korvold).

## D-057: Template analysis of what the parser cannot read (2026-10-21)
- Context: The owner imported a real deck and 77 of 100 cards were unsupported. Requesting cards one by one cannot scale, and the engine, not the grammar, is the main limit (`docs/design/scaling-card-support.md`).
- Decision: `analyzeTemplates` groups the unparsed abilities of unsupported cards by sentence shape (numbers become N, mana costs {M}, `~` stays) and counts the cards each shape blocks; non-parse reasons (layout, type, fixture mismatch) are listed apart. The import screen shows it as "What blocks this deck?" with a copyable plain-text report. The same function will feed `pnpm corpus:templates` and the backlog report across the whole format.
- Alternatives: Count by card name. Rejected: names do not generalize. Wait for the bulk-file tooling. Rejected: the owner's deck is data we have now.
- Consequences: The slice order of M5 is chosen by measured template frequency, not by guess; the normalization is coarse on purpose and will be refined with the corpus.

## D-058: Corpus tooling design (2026-10-21)
- Context: The scaling plan (`docs/design/scaling-card-support.md`) orders work by measured template frequency over the whole format, so `pnpm coverage:cards` and `pnpm corpus:templates` were pulled forward from M6. They run the real card pipeline over Scryfall's `oracle_cards` bulk file, which only the owner can download.
- Decision: `tools` depends on `@commander-arena/cards` through its public API only. A small Node resolve hook (`tools/corpus/register.ts`, Node built-ins only) lets plain `node file.ts` load packages written with extension-less imports. `--check` compares supported counts (all, top 500, top 1,000) with `reports/coverage-baseline.json`, not percentages, because a newer bulk file adds cards and lowers the percentage without a regression. A card's weight is `1 / edhrecRank`, with 0.00001 for cards without a rank; a template's weight is the sum over its distinct cards. Reports carry no timestamps and do not depend on card order.
- Alternatives: Percentages in `--check`: rejected, they move when the bulk file changes. Compiling the packages for Node: rejected, a build step for tooling. Weighting every card equally: rejected, it would put obscure cards ahead of popular Commander staples.
- Consequences: The owner runs `pnpm coverage:cards --download --update-baseline` locally and commits or pastes `reports/`; the baseline must be refreshed when the bulk file changes. `--check` is not in CI yet. About 0.6 ms per card in `importCard` is the cost of a whole run (an estimate from a SYNTHETIC file, not the real one).

## D-059: Triggers are found in the event stream of each batch and wait in state until they go on the stack (2026-10-21)
- Context: Triggered abilities (CR 603) must be noticed after every state change, put on the stack after state-based actions and before a player receives priority (CR 117.5, 603.3), and see leaves-the-battlefield events as the objects were (CR 603.10a). The engine returns events from its rule functions; they are not stored in `GameState`, and decisions can stop a chain half way.
- Decision: `grantPriority(state, seat, prior)` takes the events of the change that led to priority; `settle` scans them (`rules/triggers.ts`), runs state-based actions and scans their events, then puts the waiting triggers on the stack (`rules/trigger-stack.ts`), repeating until nothing changes. Waiting triggers live in `GameState.pendingTriggers`. A resolution that stops for a decision scans its events before it stops, since they are never scanned again; every call site that gives priority passes its events. A batch is replayed in order over the battlefield as it was before it (undone from the zone-change events); `dies` and "whenever you sacrifice" use the battlefield before a run of simultaneous departures and `GameState.lki`, every other trigger the battlefield right after the event. A triggered ability on the stack is a `GameObject` with no card whose `StackData` carries the ability AST, so it resolves independently of its source (CR 113.7a); `ResolutionContext.source` is what "this" means (the source permanent, possibly gone). `ENGINE_VERSION` is now 2 (state shape and behavior changed).
- Alternatives: Store every event in state and keep a scan cursor. Rejected: unbounded state, and replays would hash the log twice. Scan inside `moveObject` and the other primitives. Rejected: triggers would be noticed before the state-based actions and before the whole change was done, and every primitive would need the trigger code. Scan once at the `applyAction` boundary. Rejected: triggers must be on the stack before the priority decision is built, which happens inside the chain.
- Consequences: Detection is one module, tested through scenarios. Permanents that leave in separate effect steps back to back in one resolution are treated as leaving together (`docs/ROADMAP.md`); no supported card can tell yet. Any new code path that gives priority must pass its events to `grantPriority`; forgetting loses triggers, so the path needs a scenario test.

## D-060: Three new decisions: choosePermanent, orderTriggers and confirmOptional (2026-10-21)
- Context: Korvold-like cards need the player to choose permanents to sacrifice (CR 608.2d), to order simultaneous triggers (CR 603.3b, scenario test 18, A18) and to answer "you may" (CR 603.5). The UI and AI handler records fail to compile until they answer them (A2).
- Decision: `choosePermanent` carries `source`, `purpose: 'sacrifice'`, `min`, `max` and the engine's `legal` set; the answer is `choosePermanents { objects }` and must be distinct, legal and between `min` and `max`. With no more candidates than `min` the engine chooses and emits `permanentsChosen` with `automatic: true`; with none nothing happens. `orderTriggers` lists the distinct waiting triggers of one seat in the engine's default order (identical ones, the same ability of the same source, are one entry with a `count` and ordered together); the answer `orderTriggers { order }` is a permutation of indices, in the order they are put on the stack (the first resolves last). A seat with one distinct trigger is never asked. `confirmOptional` is asked on resolution; `acceptOptional` runs the effect, `declineOptional` ends the ability. "May" covers the whole effect. `legalActionsForDecision` lists every permutation (two orders beyond five groups) and every combination of permanents up to 500 answers, but accepts any legal answer. The random agent chooses uniformly; `CasualAgent` sacrifices tokens and Treasures, then surplus lands, then the lowest mana value (never its commander while anything else is legal), orders triggers as listed and declines a "you may" whose text asks it to sacrifice, pay, discard, lose or exile.
- Alternatives: Reuse `chooseCards` for permanents. Rejected: it names cards in a hand and the UI needs the legal set and the purpose. One decision per trigger for ordering. Rejected: it asks N questions for one choice. Ask even for identical triggers. Rejected by A18.
- Consequences: The UI needs three dialogs (`docs/ROADMAP.md`). The "may" with a cost inside ("you may sacrifice a creature. If you do ...") is not expressible yet.

## D-061: Sacrifice and tokens in the AST, and the Treasure mana ability (2026-10-21)
- Context: S2 needs "sacrifice another permanent", "sacrifice a creature", Treasure and Soldier tokens, and the deck uses tokens everywhere (its analysis note was removed in the docs cleanup).
- Decision: The `sacrifice` effect keeps `objects` and gains one selector, `{ kind: 'choose', filter, count? }` (the filter always applies to the sacrificer's own permanents; `controller: 'opponent'` and a zone other than the battlefield are invalid); `SUPPORTED_FEATURES.sacrificeSelectors` is `this` and `choose`. Every sacrifice goes through `sacrificePermanent`, which emits `sacrificed { permanent, controller }` after the zone change; the trigger is `permanentSacrificed { by: 'you' | 'any', filter? }`. `createToken { token, count }` takes `{ kind: 'preset', preset }` or `{ kind: 'custom', definition: TokenDefinition }`; `TokenDefinition` moved to `ast/types.ts` and is re-exported from `cards/definition.ts`. Presets live in `cards/tokens.ts` from CR 111.10; only Treasure is in `SUPPORTED_FEATURES.tokenPresets`, because Food and Clue carry activated abilities, so a card creating them would make tokens that do nothing. A token changing zones is moved like any object (so it dies and triggers) and ceases to exist at the next state-based action check. Mana abilities may cost `tap`, `sacrifice this` or both (`manaAbilityCostKinds`); the payment planner puts them in its last tier (SPEC 10), and `payManual` taps gained an optional `color`. A triggered ability with targets is rejected by `validateCard` until choosing targets as it goes on the stack exists; "A or B" trigger conditions are two abilities.
- Alternatives: A `Sacrifice` selector kind shared by all effects. Rejected: only sacrifice chooses among the controller's own permanents. Mark Food and Clue supported with inert abilities. Rejected by the honesty rule. Put the sacrifice cost on spells and activated abilities now. Rejected: nothing needs it before activated abilities.
- Consequences: Korvold and the 19 token cards of the deck are within reach of the grammar; the parser agent targets these node shapes. Edicts ("each player sacrifices") and sacrifice as a cost need their own slices.

## D-062: Spell effects are parsed from named phrase-level clauses (2026-10-21)
- Context: Slice S1 of the scaling plan reads spell text for effects the engine already runs. The M4 framework matched whole abilities, which would need one rule per sentence.
- Decision: The spell grammar (`parser/effects/`) is built from small named clauses (`spell.damage`, `spell.destroy`, `spell.exile`, `spell.return`, `spell.counter`, `spell.tap`, `spell.untap`, `spell.mana`, `spell.player`, `spell.draw`, `spell.life`, `spell.shuffle`) joined into sentences and sequences, each gated by `SUPPORTED_FEATURES.effectKinds`. Targets are numbered after the whole text parses (`EffectDraft`), and `named()` parts give diagnostics a precise `closestRule` and `stoppedAt`. Enters-tapped and enters-with-counters are new ability rules. `PARSER_VERSION` is 2. Text that needs anaphora, conditions, "up to" or unsupported pieces stays unparsed, never half-read.
- Alternatives: One rule per card shape: rejected, it does not scale. Waiting for the parser redesign: rejected, S1 is useful now and the redesign (`docs/design/parser-architecture.md`) keeps these parts.
- Consequences: Few real cards become fully supported from S1 alone; the main finding is that target filters cannot say "or" (needs an engine change). Spell rules apply only to instant and sorcery faces.

## D-063: Two-stage parser: clause IR and typed lowering (2026-10-21)
- Context: 77 of 100 cards of the owner's first real deck were unsupported and the first corpus run (its analysis note was removed in the docs cleanup) shows about 13,000 distinct unparsed ability shapes. Whole-ability rules on the M4 combinator kit grow per sentence, not per vocabulary item. `docs/design/parser-architecture.md` (approved) is the design.
- Decision: Architecture (c) of the proposal. A segmenter splits an ability into trigger, costs, condition, sentences, clauses, modes and restrictions; small phrase rules, one family per slot (trigger, cost, effect, noun, amount, duration, condition, keyword, static, token, restriction, replacement), fill the slots into a typed clause IR; a binding pass resolves anaphora and targets; a lowering step turns IR into engine AST and declares the `FeatureRef`s it needs. The IR says what the text says, never how the engine runs it. Whole-ability rules are retired; `matchAbility` and `parseFaceText` stay as façades. Two amendments from the owner's review: (1) conditions and object filters get boolean combinators (`and`, `or`, `not` for `IrCondition`; `anyOf` for `IrFilter` and for the engine's `ObjectFilter`) in P0, so "creature or planeswalker" and "if A and B" are expressible before rules are written against the IR; (2) Flash, hexproof and shroud are enforced by the engine in the keyword slice, which comes right after mana and lands in the corpus-driven order, not in S3.
- Alternatives: (a) keep whole-line rules, (b) one rule per card, (d) a grammar DSL, (e) an external parser dependency; all rejected in section 2 of the proposal.
- Consequences: Grammar grows per verb or noun; the backlog can tell grammar gaps from engine gaps; the S1 phrase parts (`parser/effects/`) are kept and moved onto the IR; P0 owns `packages/cards/src/convert/parser/` for two sessions.

## D-064: Diagnostics v2 and support request schema 2 (2026-10-21)
- Context: Schema 1 (SPEC 8.2) records `stoppedAt` and `closestRule`, which cannot say whether a card is blocked by the grammar or by the engine.
- Decision: Each unparsed ability reports a reason (`unrecognised`, `notRunnable`, `unboundReference`), the slot family, the recognised rules, the missing `FeatureRef`s and the template. Request schema 2 adds these as optional fields and keeps every schema 1 field; `validateRequest` accepts both. SPEC amendment A30 records it.
- Alternatives: Replace schema 1: rejected, existing requests in `card-requests/` stay valid.
- Consequences: `reports/backlog.md` gains an engine-gaps table; the import screen can say "recognised, the engine cannot run it yet".
- Status: Partly superseded by D-166: the diagnostics v2 stand (parser, reports, "Why unsupported?"); the request schema 2 and `validateRequest` were removed with the request pipeline.

## D-065: Rule authoring contract and meta tests (2026-10-21)
- Context: Ambiguity between phrase rules must never be resolved by rule order at runtime.
- Decision: Every rule is `defineRule({ id, family, leading, parse, examples, rejects, cites })`. Three meta tests enforce that exactly one rule per family matches each golden example, that every `rejects` line fails, and that every rule id and feature ref is reached by a scenario test (A8).
- Alternatives: First-match-wins ordering: rejected, silent semantic drift.
- Consequences: Adding a rule means adding examples and rejects; CI catches overlap.

## D-066: Golden corpus, snapshot gate and hold-out split (2026-10-21)
- Context: Coverage must be measured in CI without Scryfall access.
- Decision: The owner exports 150 to 300 real cards' Oracle text (starting with the 77 and the fixtures) to `packages/cards/test/fixtures/corpus/golden.jsonl`; `golden.expected.json` is the CI coverage gate; 25% of the cards, chosen by `oracle_id` hash (the 77 exempt), are a hold-out whose coverage is reported separately to detect overfitting; the full-corpus baseline is pinned to `PARSER_VERSION`.
- Alternatives: Golden tests only locally: rejected, weaker CI.
- Consequences: Real Oracle text is committed, the same category of data as `card-requests/`; the licensing decision on bundling Scryfall data applies to it.

## D-067: Overrides keyed by `oracle_id` with text pinning (2026-10-21; superseded by D-071 and D-167)
- Context: The long tail needs per-card code, which must not become the main path.
- Decision: `defineOverride` pins the normalized Oracle text; a mismatch disables the override and flags the card; every override needs a scenario test; overrides are capped at 10% of supported cards; any override shape seen on three or more corpus cards becomes a grammar gap instead; an S-class card gets a proposal before an override, even when requested with "just make it work".
- Alternatives: Unlimited overrides: rejected, it is one rule per card again.
- Consequences: The cap is checked by a test over the registry.
- Status: Partly superseded by D-071: the `oracle_id`-keyed route was built as reviewed data (`card-definitions/`, `packages/cards/src/definitions/`), not as a `defineOverride` code registry (none exists). The 10% cap is a test over those files (`packages/cards/test/definitions-shipped.test.ts`).
- Status: Superseded by D-167: the data route that replaced it (D-071) was removed too, so no `oracle_id`-keyed route and no 10% cap exist any more.


## D-068: `SUPPORTED_FEATURES` gains dimensions and `FeatureRef` (2026-10-21)
- Context: Lowering must declare what it needs in the engine's terms.
- Decision: `SUPPORTED_FEATURES` gains costs, selectors, conditions, durations, statics, tokens and amounts; a `FeatureRef` string names one entry; each slice fills its own dimension in the change that tests it. D-007 is unchanged. Budget: at most 15 s for the full corpus in Node and 100 ms per deck in the browser.
- Alternatives: One flat list: rejected, it cannot name a missing piece precisely.
- Consequences: A dimension test keeps `FeatureRef` strings and the registry in step.

## D-069: No grammar DSL and no new parsing dependency (2026-10-21)
- Context: Section 2 of the proposal weighed a DSL and an external parser.
- Decision: The combinator kit stays the only parsing tool. A parsing dependency would need a new decision entry.
- Alternatives: PEG or parser-generator dependency: rejected, another language to learn and no gain for this vocabulary.
- Consequences: Rules stay plain TypeScript with tests.

## D-070: Web UI for the trigger decisions (2026-10-21)
- Context: S2 added `choosePermanent`, `orderTriggers` and `confirmOptional`, five events, and mana abilities with a sacrifice cost and a chosen colour. The web app must answer them without ever auto-answering.
- Decision: Trigger order is shown as resolution order (top resolves first, like the stack panel) and converted to the engine's put-on-stack order when sent. `orderTriggers` is undoable: it happens inside a priority window and resolves nothing. `choosePermanents`, `acceptOptional` and `declineOptional` clear the undo history: they answer a question asked mid-resolution, after the pass that started it already closed the undo window. The three decisions use dock panels or a small modal so the board and Undo stay visible. Manual mana: a source whose rules text says "mana of any color" asks for a colour before the tap; this reads text because `PayManaDecision.manaSources` does not list colours per source (a ROADMAP item). SYNTHETIC decks for e2e and manual checks are reachable by id only (`HIDDEN_DECKS` in `game/precons.ts`), never in the menu.
- Alternatives: A modal for ordering: rejected, it hides the board. Making every answer undoable: rejected, the engine cannot rewind inside a resolution.
- Consequences: The e2e trigger tests depend on fixed seeds with the hidden deck; a change in the AI or engine may need the seeds re-found.

## D-072: Mana and lands primitives (2026-10-21)
- Context: The first corpus run puts mana and lands at the top of the backlog by popularity: two-colour tap abilities, pain lands, signets, check lands, shock lands and "no maximum hand size". The lead fixed the AST shapes; a Sonnet agent built them.
- Decision: `ManaProduction` gains `oneOf` (two or more colours); a mana ability may carry `also` effects limited to damage or life change to its controller (CR 605.1a); mana abilities may have a `mana` cost, which auto-pay uses at exactly one level (a costed source never pays for itself or for another costed source; at most the six lowest-id costed sources are considered, `MAX_COSTED`), and the manual path pays the cost from the pool or refuses; `entersTapped` gains `unless: Condition` with `controlsAtLeast`, `opponentsAtLeast` and the `and`/`or`/`not` combinators of D-063; `entersTappedUnlessPays` asks through the existing `confirmOptional` decision (new optional `cost` field) before the permanent enters, with the move resumed by `entersPaid`; the first static ability is `noMaximumHandSize`, consulted at cleanup (CR 514.1). Auto-pay never picks a plan whose pain damage would bring life to 0; tapping by hand still may. `validateCard` now rejects an `addMana` spell effect with a non-fixed production, which the interpreter could never ask about. `PayManaDecision.manaSources` lists `colors` for choice sources, replacing the web's rules-text heuristic (D-070). `ENGINE_VERSION` is unchanged: every state change is additive.
- Alternatives: A new decision kind for the shock-land question: rejected, `confirmOptional` already means "accept or decline", and a new kind would force UI and AI work for the same answer. Unlimited planner depth for costed sources: rejected, exponential and no supported card needs it.
- Consequences: The web app must read `colors`, show "Pay N life?" when `cost` is set, and word the `optionalAnswered` log line without resolving the source by name (the shock land had not entered yet). Planner correctness is checked against a brute-force oracle over seeded instances, not against real cards.

## D-073: Parser P0 landed: PARSER_VERSION 3 and the departures from the proposal (2026-10-21)
- Context: The first stage of D-063 is built: segmenter, clause IR, phrase rules per family, binding, lowering with `needs`, diagnostics v2, request schema 2 (SPEC A30), the rule registry with its meta tests, the golden corpus harness and `pnpm corpus:extract`. Every card keeps its support status, but rule ids changed.
- Decision: `PARSER_VERSION` is 3: rule ids are renamed (`spell.*` became `effect.*`, `mana.tap-add` is read as `cost.tap` plus `effect.add-mana`) and diagnostics v2 make cached version 2 reports stale. Four departures from the proposal are accepted: `EffectDraft` (`effects/draft.ts`, `refs.ts`) is deleted rather than moved, since `bind` numbers targets and lowering collects them; clauses are split by trial (a join splits only where an effect rule reads the words after it), not by a verb vocabulary in the segmenter; X is gated by `validateCard`, not by `needs`, so X spells still read fully; when sibling rules fail at the same word, `closestRule` names the earlier registered one while `slot` and `recognised` stay exact. Engine: `anyOf` members may not set `zone` or `stackKind`; the outer filter owns them. Golden entries without an `oracle_id` are split into training and hold-out by a hash of the name; `corpus:extract` replaces an entry with the same `oracle_id`.
- Alternatives: Keep version 2 since no status changed: rejected, the support cache keys on the version and the old ids would persist in cached diagnostics.
- Consequences: The import screen still shows `closestRule` and `stoppedAt` only; showing reason, slot and `needs` is a web follow-up. `reports/coverage-baseline.json` says version 2 and must be regenerated by the owner. No trigger, condition, duration, static, token or restriction rules exist yet: the next stage registers them.

## D-074: Parser stage P1 landed: triggers, mana and lands grammar, PARSER_VERSION 4 (2026-10-21)
- Context: The engine primitives of part 1 (triggers, tokens, sacrifice, mana and lands, statics) had no grammar. Korvold, Fae-Cursed King was the acceptance card.
- Decision: `PARSER_VERSION` is 4 (many cards change status). Rule families trigger, condition, token and static exist, with the mana and lands rules; one triggered ability is emitted per event of "A or B" (D-059). "Unless X" is carried on the IR clause as `not(X)` and lowered to the engine's `unless: X`; "two or fewer" is `not` of "three or more". "You may" is read only in triggered bodies and lowers only for a single instruction, since the engine's `optional` covers a whole effect; otherwise the ability is reported `notRunnable`. A triggered ability with a target is lowered and then refused by `validateCard` with a reason string, not reported as unparsed. Ability words ("Landfall —") are stripped during normalization from a table checked against CR 207.2c, which changes the `text` shown for such lines. Token names are the creature types joined ("Soldier"), as in the engine fixtures. Korvold's golden entry carries power, toughness and colours added by hand from the printed card and marked UNVERIFIED; `pnpm corpus:extract` replaces it with Scryfall data.
- Alternatives: Keep version 3: rejected, cached verdicts would be wrong for every card that now parses. Reject "you may" entirely: rejected, the single-instruction case covers the common "you may draw a card".
- Consequences: The owner must re-run `pnpm corpus:extract` (names in `docs/MECHANICS.md`) and `pnpm coverage:cards --update-baseline`; the baseline still says version 2. Engine gaps found: opponent-lands mana production, Map and Blood presets, Food and Clue activations, per-effect "may", intervening-if, trigger targets (CR 603.3d).

## D-075: Activated abilities, until-end-of-turn effects, Cycling, library search and discard (2026-10-21)
- Context: Slices S3 and S5 of the scaling plan, engine side, built by two Sonnet agents in parallel to shapes fixed by the lead; the web card picker followed. The search agent corrected the CR numbers the lead had written from memory (Discard 701.9, Search 701.23, Shuffle 701.24, Reveal 701.20): rules are looked up with `pnpm rule`, never recalled.
- Decision: The priority option and action for a non-mana ability is `{ kind: 'activate', object, abilityIndex }` (`activateAbility` stays the mana-ability action). Payment order: targets, then tap, life, counters and "discard this card", then mana through the same `payMana` decision as spells, then any sacrifice last, through `choosePermanent` with `forCost: true` (cancel rewinds the activation); auto-pay treats a source that will be sacrificed as tapped. An activated ability may declare `functionsIn: 'hand'`; Cycling is `{ kind: 'cycling', cost }` expanded in `derive` into such an ability with the new `discardThis` cost (CR 702.29). `GameState.continuousEffects` holds until-end-of-turn P/T modifications, applied in layer 7c and expired at cleanup (CR 514.2); ids derive from the state timestamp; `ENGINE_VERSION` is 3. The `chooseCards` decision (search or discard; `legal`, `min`, `max`, `reveal`, `prompt`) answers with cards in an order that assigns search destinations; the searcher's view carries `pendingCards`, other seats only `waitingOn`; `legal` is name-sorted so library order never leaks; a search may always find fewer cards than asked. `ObjectView.activated` exposes activated abilities for labels. Food and Clue stay out of `tokenPresets` until tested.
- Alternatives: A new decision kind for a sacrifice cost: rejected, `choosePermanent` with a flag is the same answer. Forcing a find when the searched quality is checkable (CR 701.23d): deferred, no supported card needs it.
- Consequences: The web must offer activations (from the battlefield and from hand), a Cancel on the cost sacrifice dialog, stop the autopilot when an activation is possible, and decide undo for `activate`; the parser needs lowerings for activated abilities, search, discard and durations (stage P2). A sacrifice cost whose only candidate auto-pay spent as mana is refused at payment time (ROADMAP).
- Status: The forced find deferred here was built in D-076 (CR 701.23d).


## D-076: Parser stage P2 landed: activated abilities, searches, discard, Cycling, choice of types; PARSER_VERSION 5 (2026-10-21)
- Context: The engine primitives of D-075 had no grammar. The backlog's largest remaining shapes were pumps (`{M}: ~ gets +N/+N until end of turn.`, 226 cards), Cycling (293), sacrifice-and-tap draw abilities, loot and discard, ramp and fetch searches, and "artifact or enchantment" targets.
- Decision: `PARSER_VERSION` is 5. An activated ability lowers with `needs` per cost kind and `timing: 'sorcery'` from "Activate only as a sorcery." A mana ability (first clause `Add`, no target) lowers only to the engine's mana-ability node: `{T}` and/or "Sacrifice ~" costs, at most one mana cost, riders limited to damage or life change to you; anything else (`{T}: Add {G}. Draw a card.`, `Pay 1 life` in the cost) is reported `notRunnable` naming `manaAlso:` or `manaCost:`, never lowered as an ordinary activation, which would put the mana on the stack (CR 605.1a, 605.3). A search "for a card" with no stated quality lowers with an empty filter; the engine now forces the find (CR 701.23d), so tutors are read correctly. Choice of types ("artifact or enchantment", "artifact, creature, enchantment, or land") lowers to `anyOf` for one object with no modifiers in front; `that creature` after such a target stays unbound. Search anaphora ("put it", "that card", "those cards") is read inside the search rule and must agree in number. `SimpleKeyword` in the grammar is an explicit list, so a new engine keyword is never read by accident.
- Alternatives: Lowering unsupported mana abilities as activated abilities: rejected, wrong timing and stack behaviour. Holding tutors back until the engine forced a find: rejected, the engine change was one line and the CR is clear.
- Consequences: `reports/coverage-baseline.json` still says version 4; the owner regenerates it and extracts the cards named in `docs/MECHANICS.md` "Stage P2". Regenerate, "can't be blocked", keyword-granting pumps and Food stay unparsed with named gaps where a `FeatureRef` exists.

## D-077: Auras, Equipment and static abilities with subjects (2026-10-21)
- Context: `Enchant creature` blocks 892 cards and `Equip {M}` 568, the two largest shapes of the corpus; both need attachment and continuous static effects (CR 303.4, 301.5, 702.6, 611.3, 613).
- Decision: Attachment reuses `GameObject.attachedTo` (null when unattached); `attached` and `unattached { reason: 'left' | 'illegal' | 'replaced' }` events; the view carries `attachedTo` and `attachments`. Keyword `enchant { filter }` gives an Aura spell one target from its filter (CR 303.4a); it enters attached on resolution and SBA CR 704.5m sends an illegally attached Aura to the graveyard; an Aura entering the battlefield without being cast is rejected at validation (CR 303.4f) rather than guessed. Keyword `equip { cost }` is expanded in `derive` into "{cost}: Attach this to target creature you control. Activate only as a sorcery." (CR 702.6a) with the new `attach` effect; CR 704.5n and 704.5p unattach an Equipment from an illegal host and leave it on the battlefield. Static effects gain subjects: `{ kind: 'attached' }` and `{ kind: 'filter', filter, other? }`, with `modifyPt` applied in layer 7c and `grantKeyword` in layer 6 (CR 613); all 7c contributions are additions, so timestamp order does not matter yet. Grantable keywords are the parameterless ones plus shroud; flash is excluded. The filter subject is matched on characteristics before layers 6 and 7, which must move to layer 4 output once type-changing effects exist (ROADMAP). `ENGINE_VERSION` is 4. The casual AI casts Auras on its own creatures unless the Aura's rules text reads as hostile (a regex heuristic, unverified against real text) and equips its best unequipped creature at most once per turn.
- Alternatives: A separate attachment table in state: rejected, the field already existed. Timestamp-ordered layer 7 now: deferred, nothing but additions exists.
- Consequences: The web draws attachments with their host and labels equip; the parser's stage P3 produces `enchant`, `equip`, `static:modifyPt` and `static:grantKeyword` with `staticSubject:attached` or `filter` (the exact table is in the S4a section of `docs/MECHANICS.md`).

## D-078: Parser stage P3 landed: Auras, Equipment and static grants; PARSER_VERSION 6 (2026-10-21)
- Context: The engine's S4a primitives (D-077) had no grammar; `Enchant creature` and `Equip {M}` are the two largest shapes of the corpus.
- Decision: `PARSER_VERSION` is 6. `Enchant <permanent phrase>` lowers on any face so that the engine's own reason ("only an Aura has an enchant ability", CR 702.5a) reaches the player; `Equip {M}` and `Equip—Pay N life` lower to the equip keyword; restricted equip stays unparsed with a precise diagnostic. A static statement lowers to one `static` ability per effect in text order (`modifyPt`, then one `grantKeyword` per keyword), compared exactly against the engine fixtures. "Enchanted creature" requires the Aura subtype and "Equipped creature" the Equipment subtype on the face, stricter than the engine; Bestow creatures stay unparsed. Creature types are read from the CR 205.3m list (checked against the CR text) and only after "other"; a capitalized word at the start of a line is no evidence of a type. The grantable keyword list is copied from the engine's `validate-attach.ts` with a test that keeps the copies equal (exporting it is a small engine follow-up). A new `quiet()` combinator keeps a failed subject from changing earlier diagnostics.
- Alternatives: Reading "Enchanted creature" without checking the face: rejected, it would lower on creatures with Bestow and mean the wrong thing.
- Consequences: Engine follow-ups: the word after "Enchanted"/"Equipped" is not checked against the host's type (an `Enchant permanent` Aura saying "Enchanted creature gets +1/+1" would also buff a land host); `StaticSubject.attached` needs an optional `types` filter, queued for the next engine slot. Restricted equip, "can't attack or block", granted quoted abilities and group combat modifiers have named gaps or none.

## D-079: Conditional effects, Kicker and Flashback (2026-10-21)
- Context: `Kicker {M}` blocks 187 corpus cards and `Flashback {M}` 189; both need cast-time choices the engine lacked, and "if" effects needed a node.
