- Decision: `Effect` gains `conditional { condition, effect, else? }`, evaluated when the instruction runs (CR 608.2c); `Condition` gains `kicked`. Kicker is `{ kind: 'kicker', cost }` (mana and life, one per card); the question is asked through `confirmOptional` with `purpose: 'kicker'` and `cost` set, BEFORE targets (CR 601.2b then 601.2c, which 702.33g depends on), only when the kicked total is payable and the caster stays above 0 life; otherwise the spell is cast unkicked without a question so `getLegalActions` and `applyAction` agree. `StackData.kicked` is copied to `GameObject.kicked` when the spell becomes a permanent, and the condition reads last-known information after the source leaves. A target used only in the kicked branch is refused by `validateCard` (CR 702.33g unsupported). Flashback is `{ kind: 'flashback', cost }` (mana only) cast from the owner's graveyard through `castSpell` with `alternative: 'flashback'`; a stack object flagged `flashback` goes to exile from `moveObject` whatever zone was asked (resolve, counter, fizzle), ahead of the commander replacement. `spellCast` carries `kicked` and `alternative`; no `optionalAnswered` is emitted for the kicker answer. `ENGINE_VERSION` is 5.
- Alternatives: Asking kicker after targets: rejected by the CR order. Exile handling in `stack.ts`: rejected, `moveObject` is the one place every leave-the-stack path goes through.
- Consequences: The web must word the kicker question from `purpose`/`cost` with a Cancel, offer "Flashback" on graveyard cards and send `alternative` (today the plain cast would be sent and refused), show `kicked`/`flashback` badges, and word `spellCast`. The parser produces `kicker`, `flashback`, and `conditional(kicked, ...)` including the "instead" form; the intervening "if" of CR 603.4 is not modelled yet, so "When ~ enters, if it was kicked" triggers and does nothing when unkicked (ROADMAP, next engine slot).

## D-081: Intervening "if", host-typed attached subjects, Food and Clue (2026-10-21)
- Context: Follow-ups named by D-078 and D-079: "When ~ enters, if it was kicked" must not trigger at all when unkicked (CR 603.4); "Enchanted creature" on an `Enchant permanent` Aura must not buff a land; Food and Clue could run once activated abilities existed.
- Decision: `triggered.interveningIf?: Condition` is checked when the event happens (no pending trigger otherwise) and again on resolution, where a false condition removes the ability with `fizzled { reason: 'interveningIf' }` rather than a new event kind. A permanent-counting condition on a `dies` or sacrifice trigger is refused by `validateCard` (CR 603.10a: the engine would read the battlefield after the event). `StaticSubject.attached` gains `types?` and `supertypes?`, checked against the host before layers 6 and 7; `GRANTABLE_KEYWORDS` is exported. `tokenPresets` gains Food and Clue with no new engine code; the casual AI eats below 15 life and cracks with fewer than 3 cards in hand, on spare mana only (untuned thresholds, shape-based, never by name). `PARSER_VERSION` is 7 because cards that create Food or Clue change status.
- Alternatives: A new `triggerRemoved` event: rejected, the web's exhaustive event switch is owned by another agent and `fizzled` with a reason says the same.
- Consequences: The parser's stage P4 produces `interveningIf` for "if it was kicked" and typed attached subjects; the web may word an intervening-if removal as an ordinary fizzle until it reads the reason.

## D-082: Parser stage P4 landed: Kicker, Flashback, kicked conditions, intervening ifs; PARSER_VERSION 8 (2026-10-22)
- Context: The engine primitives of D-079 and D-081 had no grammar.
- Decision: `PARSER_VERSION` is 8. `Kicker {M}` / `Kicker—<cost>` and `Flashback {M}` / `Flashback—<cost>` lower to the keywords; multikicker, `Kicker {A} and/or {B}` and non-mana flashback costs are read and refused as `notRunnable` with no `needs` (no `FeatureRef` exists; an engine change would add one), which gives a precise diagnostic instead of an unrecognised line. Flashback lowers on any face so the engine's own reason reaches the player. A leading `If ~ was kicked,` is a sentence-level condition; `<base>. If ~ was kicked, <E> instead.` merges into one `conditional(kicked, E, else: base)` and requires a single-clause base; `it deals N damage instead` copies the recipients of a damage base. `When ~ enters, if it was kicked,` lowers to `interveningIf`, never to a conditional inside the trigger. `~ enters tapped unless ~ was kicked.` lowers through the existing `unless` rule. Attached subjects carry `types`/`supertypes` from the word after "Enchanted"/"Equipped".
- Alternatives: Gating flashback on instant or sorcery in the parser: rejected, the engine's message is the better diagnostic.
- Consequences: The dash forms of Cycling and Equip (`Cycling—Pay 2 life.`) probably end with a period in real text and are not read yet (ROADMAP, one-line fixes once the owner confirms). Pronoun nouns (`on it`) stay unparsed; mapping the trigger subject to `this` is the next grammar follow-up. The engine lacks a power field on filters and a condition on `entersWithCounters`.

## D-083: Continuous effects in layers, the `moved` reference, prowess (2026-10-22)
- Context: SPEC scenario tests 3, 17 and 20 needed a general layer system, a way for a later instruction to refer to the object an earlier one moved, and the prowess keyword.
- Decision: `ContinuousEffect` is `{ id, timestamp, objects (fixed set, CR 611.2c), until, change }` with changes `modifyPt`, `setPt`, `loseAllAbilities`, `grantKeyword`, `setTypes`, `setColors`; `derive` recomputes from the base in layer order (CR 613.1): 4 types in timestamp order, 5 colours, statics of permanents matched against the result of 4 and 5, 6 abilities merged by timestamp with "lose all" emptying the list as it stands, 7b the last `setPt`, 7c counters plus additions. Dependencies (CR 613.8) are out of scope. `setTypes` replaces creature types and keeps non-creature subtypes (CR 205.3); the additive "in addition to its other types" form is not built. Noncreature permanents have no P/T on the battlefield (CR 208.3). `ObjectRef { kind: 'moved' }` names the new objects the previous `exile`, `destroy` or `moveToZone` produced (`ResolutionContext.lastMoved`), so "exile it, then return it" is a sequence; a flickered token returns nothing (CR 111.8); a flicker whose target could be an Aura is refused (CR 303.4f). `moveToZone.controller` accepts `'owner' | 'you'`. Prowess expands in `derive` into its CR 702.108a trigger; it is not grantable by an effect because granted keywords are never expanded. `ENGINE_VERSION` is 6. The casual AI puts pumps and keyword gains on its own best creature.
- Alternatives: Requiring `types: ['creature']` on `setTypes`: rejected, Turn to Frog sets only a creature type and must keep "artifact" on an artifact creature. A `permanent` duration in `durationKinds`: deferred, no supported card needs it.
- Consequences: SPEC tests 3, 17 and 20 pass; the parser's stage P5 produces `grantKeyword`, `setPt`, `loseAllAbilities`, `setTypes`, `setColors`, the flicker sequence and the `Prowess` line. The web needs only a prowess chip label. The Giant Growth, Turn to Frog and Cloudshift texts in tests and docs are from memory and marked as such.

## D-084: Ward, token copies, copy effects and the legend rule (2026-10-22)
- Context: SPEC scenario tests 14 and 19 needed ward (CR 702.21), copy effects (CR 707) and the legend rule (CR 704.5j).
- Decision: Ward expands in `derive` into the triggered ability the rule defines: trigger `becomesTarget { what: this, by: 'opponent' }` (new trigger kind; `becameTarget` events are emitted when a spell or ability finishes choosing targets) with the effect `counterUnlessPays { objects: triggerSubject, cost }`, accepted by `validateCard` only on ward-like triggers; `triggerSubject` is a new `ObjectRef` valid there and as a copy source, and an ability that reads it carries the subject in its identity, so two warded targets give two triggers to order. The question is asked of the targeting spell's controller through `confirmOptional { purpose: 'ward', subject }` only when the cost is payable; mana is paid mid-resolution through `payMana { purpose: 'ward' }`, where `cancel` means "do not pay" and counters the whole spell. Copies: `TokenSpec { kind: 'copyOf', object }` and the effect `becomeCopy` (until end of turn) use copiable values (CR 707.2) through a layer 1 `copy` change; `copiableValues` is the single reader of printed characteristics; token copies of Auras or lands and copies from off the battlefield are refused. The legend rule runs in the SBA check after the other actions of that pass, through `choosePermanent { purpose: 'legendRule' }`, never automatically; the others go to the graveyard together so their dies triggers fire. `ENGINE_VERSION` stays 6 (optional fields only).
- Alternatives: A generic "counter unless pays" for Mana Leak: deferred, its decision purpose would differ. Reusing the casting transaction for ward mana: rejected, a minimal mid-resolution path is smaller.
- Consequences: The web must word the ward question and payment cancel, the legend-rule choice, and two log lines, and fix three exhaustive switches; the parser produces `Ward {cost}` and copy tokens (`selector:triggerSubject` for "a copy of it"). SPEC tests 14 and 19 pass.

## D-085: Control on entering (CR 110.2a), Vehicles and Crew, additive type changes (2026-10-22)
- Context: D-083 said `moveToZone` without `controller` means the owner; CR 110.2a says an object an effect puts onto the battlefield enters under the control of the player performing the effect. `Crew N` blocks 180 corpus cards and needs a type change that adds types (CR 205.1b).
- Decision: `moveToZone` to the battlefield defaults to `'you'` (the resolving effect's controller); `'owner'` stays explicit; the parser's bare "return ... to the battlefield" now gives the caster control, which is the rule. `Keyword { kind: 'crew', power }` expands in `derive` into "{tapCreatures N}: this becomes an artifact creature until end of turn" with the new cost `tapCreatures { totalPower }`, paid last and never combined with mana or a sacrifice, through `choosePermanent { purpose: 'crew', forCost, minTotalPower, powers }` (automatic with one candidate); `setTypes.additive` makes layer 4 add rather than replace. `ObjectView` gains `printedPt` and `wouldBeSummoningSick` for noncreature permanents so the AI and UI can judge an uncrewed Vehicle. A crew is logged as `permanentsChosen { purpose: 'crew' }` rather than a new event. The engine's smoke tests get a 30 s limit. `ENGINE_VERSION` stays 6.
- Alternatives: A dedicated `crewed` event: deferred until 702.122e triggers need it. Allowing crew with other costs: rejected, the creatures are chosen after the other costs and a mana plan could not promise they stay untapped.
- Consequences: The web must word the crew choice (total against N, Cancel), log crews, label the cost, badge a crewed Vehicle and show printed P/T; the parser produces `Crew N` and the additive `setTypes`; "becomes a <creature type> artifact creature" has no node yet.

## D-086: Damage prevention shields (2026-10-22)
- Context: M5's scope includes prevention effects (CR 615); Fog-style spells and "prevent the next N damage" are common.
- Decision: Prevention shields are continuous effects with the change `preventDamage { scope: all | combat | noncombat, amount: number | 'all', recipients?, sources? }` on `objects` and `players`, created by the effect node `preventDamage { scope, amount, to, by?, duration: untilEndOfTurn }`; `dealDamage` is the single routine every damage path goes through, and shields apply there: "all" shields first, then numeric ones oldest first (CR 616.1's choice is not asked; a player would always pick a free "all" shield first), numeric shields are reduced and removed at 0 and never consumed when they prevent nothing (CR 609.7b); prevented damage emits `damagePrevented` and causes nothing (no life loss, marked damage, lifelink, deathtouch or commander damage; CR 615.8, 120.3); "all" shields on a group ("creatures you control") are dynamic filters (CR 611.2c), numeric ones are one shield per permanent matched now (CR 615.11). "Can't be prevented" (CR 615.12 in this edition), chosen sources, "the next time", "instead" riders and triggers on prevented damage are out of scope. `ENGINE_VERSION` is 7. The casual AI casts a Fog or "to you" shield only to survive near-lethal combat damage.
- Alternatives: Asking the affected player to order shields: deferred, no supported card makes the order matter.
- Consequences: The web logs `damagePrevented` but cannot show shields (not in the view, ROADMAP); the parser's stage P7a reads the shapes; `PARSER_VERSION` 11.

## D-087: Split, Adventure, modal double-faced and transforming layouts (2026-10-22)
- Context: M5's scope includes double-faced, split and adventure cards (Sagas are a separate slice).
- Decision: `castSpell` and `playLand` carry an optional `face`; the engine lists one option per castable face only for split, adventure and modal_dfc cards; `GameObject.face` is the face on the stack or the battlefield and 0 in every other zone (CR 709.3, 712.8, 715.2). Split halves are judged alone when cast and combined elsewhere (name `A // B`, summed mana value); Fuse, Aftermath and Rooms are refused. An Adventure that resolves goes to exile `onAdventure` and the creature may then be cast from exile as face 0 (CR 715.3d, 715.4); a countered or fizzled Adventure goes to the graveyard. A modal back-face land counts as the land drop; a shock-land back face asks its question with the face carried. `transform` flips `face` on the same object, keeping counters, damage, attachments and effects (CR 712.8e: the back face's mana value is the front's); an ability put on the stack before the last transform does not flip it again (CR 701.27f); modal permanents may transform (CR 712.3, 712.9 in this edition). A transformed permanent keeps its timestamp (CR 613.7g not applied, ROADMAP); a token copy of a double-faced permanent is single-faced (CR 707.8a, ROADMAP); transforming into a planeswalker or battle is refused. No `transformed` event yet. `SUPPORTED_FEATURES.layouts` is normal, split, adventure, modal_dfc, transform; `ENGINE_VERSION` is 8.
- Alternatives: A separate object per face: rejected, CR 712 keeps one object. Blocking modal transforms as the brief said: rejected, the current CR allows them.
- Consequences: The web needs a face chooser (several options share one object), the exile click path with an "on an Adventure" badge, face display and log lines; the cards package must gate layouts by string, name `A // B`, take identity from both faces and lower "transform"; Sagas, flip, meld, day/night remain unsupported.

## D-088: Saga cards and the chapter trigger (2026-10-22)
- Context: M5's scope includes Saga cards (CR 714). A Saga needs a layout, a trigger that fires when lore counters reach a chapter, a counter put on it as it enters and at its controller's precombat main phase, and the sacrifice after its final chapter.
- Decision: `layout: 'saga'` has one enchantment face with the subtype Saga and `CardFace.finalChapter` (validation data: at run time the final chapter is the greatest chapter among the abilities the permanent has now, `finalChapterOf`, CR 714.2d). A chapter line is a triggered ability with the trigger `chapter { from, to }` ("I, II" is 1 to 2, CR 714.2c), found in the `counterAdded` events (CR 714.2b), once per chapter reached, whoever added the counters. The engine adds the entering lore counter for every Saga (CR 714.3a, part of entering, so chapter I triggers at once) and the turn-based counter at the precombat main phase (CR 714.3c, no stack) for each Saga with a chapter ability; the state-based action sacrifices a Saga at its final chapter unless a chapter ability of it is pending or on the stack (CR 714.4, 704.5s). The chapter number travels to the stack and the view for display only. `ENGINE_VERSION` stays 8 (optional fields only). The parser's stage P8 (`trigger.chapter`, `PARSER_VERSION` 13) reads the Roman-numeral lines; a list that is not a consecutive range is recognised but not runnable.
- Alternatives: A dedicated lore event kind: rejected, `counterAdded` carries the counter name and the trigger scan already reads it. Letting an effect read its chapter: deferred, no supported card needs it. Checking gaps and repeats in the parser: rejected, `validateCard` already does and the import keeps one diagnostic per cause.
- Consequences: Sagas whose chapters the grammar reads are supported; a chapter with a target waits on the general targeted-trigger gap, read ahead is unsupported (`docs/ROADMAP.md`). The web shows the lore badge and names the chapter on the stack. CR numbers in the brief (714.2a to c for the counters) were wrong and the code cites the repository's text.

## D-089: Targets for triggered abilities (2026-10-22)
- Context: `validateCard` refuses every triggered ability with a target (CR 603.3d not built). By the owner's backlog this is the largest single engine gap left: "When ~ enters, destroy target ...", "exile target player's graveyard", most real Sagas, many attack and death triggers.
- Decision: Targets are chosen as each triggered ability is put on the stack (CR 603.3d, 601.2c), by its controller, with the existing `targets` decision (`source` is the ability's stack object). The engine keeps a `TriggeringContext { seat, queue }` in state (like `casting`) holding the seat's triggers still to be put on the stack in the order chosen, so a target question can pause between two triggers of one seat and the rest follow after the answer. When a slot has fewer legal targets than its minimum, the ability is removed from the stack and an `abilityRemoved` event says why (CR 603.3d). When every slot has exactly as many legal targets as it needs (min = max = number of legal targets), the engine chooses them without asking, as it does for other forced choices. After the answer the chosen objects "become the target" (`becameTarget`, so ward triggers), then the remaining triggers go on, then priority. No cancel: putting a trigger on the stack is not optional. Targets are checked again on resolution like any ability's (CR 608.2b). `ENGINE_VERSION` 9 (a new state field).
- Alternatives: Choosing targets at resolution: rejected, it is not the rule and would break ward and "becomes the target" triggers. Asking for every trigger's targets before ordering: rejected, CR 603.3b and 603.3d interleave them per ability. Asking even when the choice is forced: rejected, it adds clicks for "target opponent" in a two-player game and the engine already auto-chooses forced choices.
- Consequences: Triggered abilities with targets become supported as soon as their effect is; the parser needs no new rule, only `PARSER_VERSION` 14 because cards change status. The web reuses the target prompt with the trigger's source named; `CasualAgent` must tell a helpful trigger from a harmful one by the ability's effect.

## D-090: Coverage non-regression runs in its own CI workflow (2026-10-22)
- Context: SPEC 7.3 says CI fails if coverage drops. `pnpm coverage:cards --check` compares supported counts with `reports/coverage-baseline.json`, but needs Scryfall's bulk file, which the cloud sandbox cannot reach. GitHub's runners can.
- Decision: A separate workflow, `.github/workflows/coverage.yml`, runs `pnpm coverage:cards --download --check` on pull requests and pushes to `main`, with the bulk file cached by `actions/cache` for a UTC day (Scryfall asks bulk clients not to download more often than needed; the tool already sends its `User-Agent` and `Accept` headers and reuses a cached file of the same version). It is separate from `ci.yml` so a Scryfall outage shows as its own red check and the owner decides in branch protection whether it is required.
- Alternatives: Only the golden corpus snapshot (offline): kept, but it covers 40 cards and cannot see a drop elsewhere. A nightly run: rejected as the only check, because a regression would land before anyone sees it.
- Consequences: A pull request that makes a card unsupported fails the coverage check; a parser change that supports more cards passes and the owner refreshes the baseline (`--update-baseline`) when convenient. A new bulk file can only add cards, so counts do not drop by themselves, except when Oracle text changes (errata), which shows as a failure to look at. The check depends on Scryfall being up.

## D-091: Arranging the top of a library: scry, surveil and "put them back in any order" (2026-10-22)
- Context: "When ~ enters, scry 1." (68 cards) and "surveil 1" (46) are among the heaviest unread templates in the replay of the owner's backlog, with "look at the top N cards, then put them back in any order" and Brainstorm's "put two cards from your hand on top of your library in any order". The engine has no decision that orders cards.
- Decision: One new decision kind, `arrangeCards { source, purpose: 'scry' | 'surveil' | 'reorder', cards, piles }`, answered by the action `arrangeCards { top, other }`: `cards` are the cards looked at (top first), `top` lists the ones that go back on top in order (the first is the new top card) and `other` the rest, which go to the bottom in that order for scry (CR 701.22a; the last is the new bottom card) or into the graveyard for surveil (CR 701.25a); `reorder` has no `other` pile. Every card must be placed exactly once. The engine skips the decision for 0 cards (CR 701.22b, 701.25c: no event) and when the library holds fewer cards than N it uses what is there. The looked-at cards are visible to that player only (`view.ts`), the opponent sees how many went where (`scried { seat, top, bottom }`, `surveiled { seat, top, toGraveyard }` with the graveyard cards public as they move). Putting chosen cards from a hand on top (Brainstorm) is `chooseCards` with `purpose: 'putOnTop'`, whose answer order is the order from the top. `CasualAgent` keeps lands on top when it has few in hand and play, and spells otherwise.
- Alternatives: Reusing `chooseCards` for scry: rejected, it chooses a subset and cannot express two ordered piles. One decision per card ("top or bottom?"): rejected, the order inside each pile is part of the rule.
- Consequences: The web needs an arrangement panel (two ordered piles, drag or arrows, keyboard), hidden-information care in the view, and log lines. The grammar reads "scry N", "surveil N", "look at the top N cards of your library, then put them back in any order" and the Brainstorm shape once this lands.

## D-092: References to a target's controller, owner and values; other players acting (2026-10-22)
- Context: The P9 work order (replay of the owner's backlog) puts a family of popular removal and counter spells first: Swords to Plowshares ("Its controller gains life equal to its power"), Path to Exile ("Its controller may search their library ..."), Beast Within ("Its controller creates a 3/3 green Beast creature token"), counters that give the spell's controller Treasure, "exile target player's graveyard" (5 cards), "Counter target spell unless its controller pays {3}" (27 cards), "return a land you control to its owner's hand" (bounce lands, 12 cards). The AST has `controllerOf` and `powerOf`, but `amountOf` does not see the resolving ability's targets, effects are performed by the ability's controller only, a graveyard cannot be selected by its owner, `counterUnlessPays` accepts only the triggering object, and a return cannot choose among permanents.
- Decision: (1) Amounts read the resolving object's chosen targets with last-known information (CR 608.2h): `powerOf { of: target }` and a new `manaValueOf { of }`. (2) Effects that a player other than the controller performs carry the player: `createToken { controller?: PlayerSelector }` (CR 111.2: the token is created under that player's control), `search { player }` with an optional `optional: true` whose "may" is asked of that player, not of the ability's controller (CR 608.2d), and the same for `shuffle`. (3) `ObjectFilter.owner?: PlayerSelector` selects cards by owner, so "exile target player's graveyard" is `exile { each { zone: graveyard, owner: target } }`. (4) `counterUnlessPays` accepts a target spell; the payer is the spell's controller, asked with the existing ward path (`confirmOptional` and `payMana`) under a new purpose `counterUnlessPays`. (5) `moveToZone` accepts the `choose` selector already used by `sacrifice` ("return a land you control to its owner's hand": the controller chooses with `choosePermanent`, purpose `effect`). Each one is a primitive with scenario tests; no new decision kind. `ENGINE_VERSION` bumps with the slice.
- Alternatives: A dedicated "Swords" effect: rejected, card-shaped. Performing the search as the ability's controller with the other player's library: rejected, CR 701.23a makes the searching player the one who chooses.
- Consequences: The parser's lowerings that P9 refused (`amount.power-of` on a target, `noun.its-controller` as the subject of create, search and shuffle) become runnable; a stage P10 reads the rest. The AI must answer a "may" asked of it on the opponent's spell (Path: it searches) and a counter-unless payment.

## D-093: Details of the arrangement slice that D-091 left open (2026-10-22)
- Context: building D-091 raised a few questions its text did not answer: what a scry of an empty library does, when the engine asks about one card, how a put on top with a small hand behaves, whether "look and reorder" is a scry, who may scry, and what a surveil moves.
- Decision: (1) A scry or surveil of N > 0 with an empty library asks nothing but still emits `scried { top: 0, bottom: 0 }` or `surveiled { top: 0, toGraveyard: 0 }`, because CR 701.22d and 701.25d say a trigger on scrying or surveilling happens "even if some or all of those actions were impossible"; N = 0 emits nothing (CR 701.22b, 701.25c; the brief and D-091 cite 701.25b for the surveil case, which is the rule about additional cards: the CR text of this repository has it in 701.25c). (2) A scry or surveil of one card is asked (top or bottom is a real choice); "look at the top N cards, then put them back in any order" is not asked when only one card is there (it can only go back where it is) and emits no event, because it is not the keyword action scry. (3) The cards a scry moves to the bottom and the ones it keeps on top are not moved between zones: only the order of the library changes (CR 701.22a), so their `ObjectId`s stay. A surveil's graveyard cards do change zone (CR 400.7), one `zoneChanged` each after the `surveiled` event, in the order of `other`; a surveil never asks the commander question (CR 903.9b is about the hand and the library). (4) `scry` and `surveil` take `player?` (absent means the controller); `validateCard` accepts only `you` or none, so another player's scry (a second seat deciding) is refused. (5) "Put N cards from your hand on top" asks even when the hand holds no more than N cards, if it holds two or more, because the order is a choice; a hand of exactly one card (or none) asks nothing. The cards go back through `move` instructions with the last chosen first, so a commander put on top asks its owner (CR 903.9b) like any move to the library. (6) `legalActionsForDecision` lists every arrangement for up to four cards looked at (the identity first, then all in the second pile) and six representative ones beyond; a put on top lists the ordered choices (up to 500). (7) The view of the other seat during an arrangement is `waitingOn { seat, purpose, sourceName }` with `purpose` one of `scry`, `surveil`, `reorder` (and `putOnTop` for the hand choice); it never lists a card.
- Alternatives: Emitting nothing for an empty library: rejected, it would make a future "whenever you scry" trigger skip a scry that CR 701.22d says happened. Making reorder a scry event: rejected, an ability that triggers on scrying must not trigger on Impulse-like effects. Moving scried cards through zones: rejected, it would give them new objects for no rules reason and leak the order through ids.
- Consequences: The web needs the arrangement panel and log lines for `scried` and `surveiled`; the parser reads "scry N", "surveil N", "look at the top N cards of your library, then put them back in any order" and the Brainstorm shape. `ENGINE_VERSION` 10.

## D-094: Restrictions, requirements and evasion (2026-10-22)
- Context: The replay's unread list has "~ can't block" (91 cards), "~ can't be countered" (87), "~ can't be blocked" (60), "~ attacks each combat if able" (61), "~ doesn't untap during your untap step" (35), "{4}, {T}: Target creature can't be blocked this turn" (Rogue's Passage), "Equipped creature can't be blocked", and the evasion keywords landwalk (islandwalk and the rest, 30 to 40 cards each), fear and intimidate. The engine has none of them.
- Decision: A restriction is one of `cantBlock`, `cantBeBlocked`, `attacksEachCombat`, `doesntUntap`, `cantBeCountered`. It reaches an object two ways: a static ability (`StaticEffect { kind: 'restriction', subject, restriction }`, subjects as for `grantKeyword`: `this`, `attached`, `filter`), which "loses all abilities" removes; or a continuous effect (`ContinuousChange { kind: 'restrict', restriction }`, created by an effect `restrict { objects, restriction, duration }`, "target creature can't be blocked this turn"), which it does not, because a rules-modifying effect is not an ability (CR 613.11, applied after the layers). `derive` exposes the set as `restrictions` on the derived object. They are read where the rule acts: blockers (CR 509.1b: `cantBlock`; `cantBeBlocked`), the untap step (CR 502.3: `doesntUntap`), declaring attackers (CR 508.1d: a creature with `attacksEachCombat` that is able to attack must be declared; no attack costs exist yet, so "able" is untapped, not summoning sick, no `cantAttack`), and counter effects (CR 101.2, 701.6: a spell with `cantBeCountered` is not countered and stays on the stack, including by ward and `counterUnlessPays`). Landwalk (CR 702.14: a land type, or `nonbasic`), fear (702.36), intimidate (702.13) and shadow (702.28) are keywords read by the same blocker check. `ENGINE_VERSION` bumps with the slice.
- Alternatives: Modelling the restrictions as keywords: rejected, "can't be blocked" granted by an effect must survive "loses all abilities" (CR 613.11), and they are not keyword abilities in the CR. One generic "can't" predicate language: deferred; five named restrictions cover the measured lines.
- Consequences: The web must show restrictions as chips and explain refused blocks and attacks; the AI must respect `attacksEachCombat` and use evasion. The grammar reads the lines above, the landwalk keywords, fear, intimidate and shadow.

## D-095: Additional costs, cost reductions, counted amounts and free casts with a commander (2026-10-22)
- Context: The replay's unread list has "As an additional cost to cast ~, sacrifice a creature" (58 cards), "... discard a card" (17), "... sacrifice an artifact or creature" (14), "... sacrifice a land" (6), "~ costs {1} less to cast for each creature on the battlefield" (Blasphemous Act), "Artifact spells you cast cost {1} less to cast", "Instant and sorcery spells you cast cost {1} less to cast" (16), "If you control a commander, you may cast ~ without paying its mana cost" (5, popular), and about 0.32 of weight in "for each ..." and "equal to the number of ..." amounts.
- Decision: (1) A counted amount `countOf { filter }` (permanents, or cards in a zone, matching an object filter, counted as the effect or cost is determined). (2) Additional costs to cast: `CardFace.additionalCosts: Cost[]`, paid with the total cost (CR 601.2f-h), with the choices made at payment: `sacrifice` (`choosePermanent`, `forCost`, as activations do) and a new `discard` cost (`chooseCards`, purpose `discard`, `forCost`), also usable by activated abilities and ward ("Ward—Discard a card"). A spell whose additional cost cannot be paid is not castable. (3) Cost reductions: `StaticEffect { kind: 'costReduction', spells: ObjectFilter, amount: Amount }`, from a permanent ("Artifact spells you cast") or the spell itself while it is being cast ("~ costs {1} less ... for each"), applied at CR 601.2f after additions; a reduction lowers only the generic part and never below zero. (4) Alternative cost "without paying its mana cost" with a condition (`castSpell` `alternative: 'free'`, CR 118.9), the condition `controlCommander` (CR 903.3d: a permanent on the battlefield that is a commander). Additional costs still apply to a free cast (CR 118.9d checked by the implementer with `pnpm rule`). `ENGINE_VERSION` bumps with the slice.
- Alternatives: Additional costs as part of the mana cost: rejected, the choices (what to sacrifice) are not mana. Reductions as negative generic symbols: rejected, they must apply after additions and stop at zero.
- Consequences: The web needs the sacrifice and discard choices during a cast and the reduced cost shown on castable cards; the AI must count the real cost. The grammar reads the lines above and the "for each" amounts on effects it already reads.

## D-096: Details of the references slice that D-092 left open (2026-10-22)
- Context: building D-092 raised questions its text did not answer: which purpose a "may search" asked of another player carries, what declining does, where `owner` may be read, what the `choose` selector of a move may name, what the question for a target spell is called, and what a `powerOf` or `manaValueOf` of a gone target reads.
- Decision: (1) A "may" search is a `confirmOptional` with `purpose: 'search'` asked of the searching player (`seat`), `source` the spell or ability resolving; declining ends only that search (no put, no shuffle) and the rest of the sequence goes on (CR 608.2d); it is asked even when nothing matches, because a player may search and shuffle anyway. A `search` effect names its searcher with `player` (any selector; several players search in seat order) and the shuffle that ends it is the searcher's. (2) `ObjectFilter.owner` is read in an effect's `each` selector only; every other place that takes a filter (target slots, triggers, conditions, statics, searches, costs, shields) refuses it in `validateCard`, and the matcher fails closed (no resolved owners, no match). (3) The `choose` selector of `moveToZone` is "a permanent you control that matches": `controller: 'you'` is required in its filter (omitting it would read as "any player's"), the destination is the hand, graveyard or library, and the question is a `choosePermanent` with `purpose: 'effect'` (new; not `sacrifice`, which other abilities watch). (4) The question and the payment of "Counter target spell unless its controller pays" carry `purpose: 'counterUnlessPays'`, set by the effect (a target object) while a `triggerSubject` object keeps `'ward'`; the engine path is shared. (5) `powerOf` and `manaValueOf` read the target as it is when it is still where the effect expected it and from `GameState.lki` otherwise; an {X} in a mana cost counts as 0 because spells with X are not supported. (6) `SUPPORTED_FEATURES` lists `amount:manaValueOf` and `selector:ownerRef`. `ENGINE_VERSION` 11.
- Alternatives: A new decision kind for the other player's "may": rejected, `confirmOptional` already goes to a seat. Reading `owner` in every filter: rejected, a trigger or static filter cannot know a target and would silently match nothing. Reusing `purpose: 'sacrifice'` for a return: rejected, a "whenever you sacrifice" watcher and the AI's sacrifice heuristic would treat a bounce as a sacrifice.
- Consequences: The web needs wording for `confirmOptional` purposes `search` and `counterUnlessPays`, `payMana` purpose `counterUnlessPays` and `choosePermanent` purpose `effect` (and the `permanentsChosen` log line); the parser's P10 lowerings use the shapes in `docs/MECHANICS.md`. A commander put into a library and drawn is a known engine error that the soak found (`docs/ROADMAP.md`).

## D-097: Drawing a commander from a library asks its owner, one card at a time (2026-10-22)
- Context: a commander can be in a library when its owner declined the command zone as it was put there (the put-from-hand-on-top effect of D-093, `moveToZone` to the library), and `drawCard` raised an engine error when it drew one. CR 903.9b: if a commander would be put into its owner's hand from anywhere, its owner may put it into the command zone instead; CR 121.1: a player draws by putting the top card of their library into their hand; CR 121.2: cards are drawn one at a time; CR 121.6b: a sequence of draws resumes after a replacement of one of them is completed. The CR text in this repository (`pnpm rule 121`, `903.9b`) has no example and does not say whether a draw that 903.9b turned into a move to the command zone counts as a card drawn.
- Decision: (1) Every draw goes through `drawCard`, which returns the question as a result (`needsDecision`, the `commanderZone` decision with `from: 'library'`) instead of throwing, and takes the owner's answer on the second call. (2) A "draw N" effect is a `draw { seat, count, commanderChoice }` instruction that draws one card and queues the rest, so the question comes between two draws, the answer is recorded on the instruction at the head of the queue (as for a move) and the remaining draws go on. (3) The turn-based draw of the draw step (CR 504.1) has no resolution to hold the instruction: it sets the pending decision, notes what had triggered (the step beginning) and `resumeDrawStep` finishes the draw and goes on to priority when the answer arrives (`api.ts` tells it from the state-based action of CR 903.9a by `from: 'library'`, no resolution in progress and the draw step). (4) A draw replaced by the command-zone choice put no card into the hand, so it is not a card drawn: no `cardDrawn` event (CR 121.1 defines drawing as that move); it still counts as one of the instruction's draws, so "draw two" with the commander first leaves one card drawn. (5) The empty library check (CR 121.4) is unchanged: a draw from an empty library is noted for the next state-based action check, per draw.
- Alternatives: Never putting a commander into a library (declining is not offered for a library): rejected, it takes a choice CR 903.9b gives to the owner. Drawing the commander and then asking: rejected, the card would already be in the hand. Counting the replaced draw as a card drawn: rejected, nothing in the CR text says so and 121.1 says otherwise; revisit if an official ruling says it counts (a future "whenever you draw" trigger would then need the event).
- Consequences: the engine needs no new decision kind; the web already has the commander question and now also gets it in the draw step and mid-resolution. `CasualAgent` always sends its commander to the command zone, so it never keeps one in a library. `ENGINE_VERSION` 12 with the slice below.

## D-098: Details of the restrictions slice that D-094 left open (2026-10-22)
- Context: building D-094 raised questions its text did not answer: how a spell's own "can't be countered" is read, what "can't be countered" does to a "counter unless pays" question, what the `this` subject is, which restrictions an effect may give, which keywords can be granted, how the legal-action list handles a required attacker, and what the view shows.
- Decision: (1) `StaticSubject` gains `this` (the permanent itself, or for `cantBeCountered` the spell on the stack, CR 113.6g: an ability that says it can't be countered functions on the stack). `cantBeCountered` accepts only `this`; the other four restrictions accept `this`, `attached` and `filter`. A static ability of a permanent that gives spells the restriction ("spells you control can't be countered") is not built. (2) `derive` lists the restrictions in `Derived.restrictions`: from the index of static abilities for permanents (a permanent that lost all its abilities has none left, CR 613.1f) and, for a spell on the stack, from its own `this` abilities; `restrict` effects add theirs and are never removed by "loses all abilities" (CR 613.11). (3) The `restrict` effect gives `cantBlock`, `cantBeBlocked` or `attacksEachCombat` until end of turn; `doesntUntap` needs a duration that ends at the next untap step and `cantBeCountered` belongs to a spell's text, so `validateCard` refuses both as effects. (4) A counter effect, ward and "counter unless pays" skip a spell that can't be countered: nothing happens and its controller is not asked, because paying would only waste the cost; the spell stays on the stack and resolves. (5) Fear, intimidate and shadow can be granted (`GRANTABLE_KEYWORDS`); landwalk cannot (its land type is a parameter and the ability layer keeps one keyword per kind). Landwalk takes a land subtype or `nonbasic`; snow and artifact landwalk (CR 702.14a, 702.14c with a supertype or card type besides the land type) are not built. Intimidate treats a colorless attacker as sharing no color. (6) `DeclareAttackersDecision.mustAttack` lists the candidates that attack each combat if able (CR 508.1d: untapped, not summoning sick, no defender, a target to attack); a declaration that leaves one out is refused with "A creature that attacks each combat if able must attack"; the legal-action list holds no empty declaration then and adds the required creatures to every other. With no attack cost in the game, "able" is "is a candidate". Where several requirements conflict (CR 508.1d's maximum rule) nothing is built, because no restriction that stops an attack (other than the ones that remove a candidate) exists yet. (7) `ObjectView` gains `restrictions` and `landwalks` (public, absent when none). `ENGINE_VERSION` 12.
- Alternatives: Asking the controller of a spell that can't be countered whether to pay a ward or "unless" cost: rejected, no choice is real. Landwalk as a flag on a generic keyword: rejected, the land type is data. A `restriction` dimension in the feature registry: deferred, the five restrictions are checked in `validateCard` and a parser lowering names `effect:restrict`, `static:restriction`, `staticSubject:this` and the keyword kinds.
- Consequences: The web shows `restrictions` as chips, can explain a refused block with the engine message, and must tell the player which creatures `mustAttack` forces. The parser reads the wordings in `docs/MECHANICS.md` (restrictions, requirements, evasion). The legacy `static:cantBeBlocked` feature name stays in `STATIC_KINDS` but is unsupported; the lowering should use `static:restriction`.

## D-099: More mana production: "could produce", combinations, activation conditions and life costs (2026-10-22)
- Context: The replay's heaviest unread line is "{T}: Add one mana of any color that a land an opponent controls could produce." (Exotic Orchard, Fellwar Stone and two more, weight 0.17), then the filter lands "{R/W}, {T}: Add {R}{R}, {R}{W}, or {W}{W}." (10 cards), "{T}: Add {C}{C}. Activate only if you control five or more lands.", "{T}: Add {B} or {G}. Activate only if you control a Swamp.", "{T}, Pay 1 life: Add one mana of any color." (6 cards, refused today as `manaCost:payLife`), and "Lands you control have "{T}: Add one mana of any color."".
- Decision: (1) `ManaProduction { kind: 'couldProduce', lands: ObjectFilter }`: one mana of any type that a matching permanent could produce (CR 106.7), computed from the derived mana abilities of those permanents when the ability is activated (so it changes as the board changes), never recursive through another `couldProduce` ability (CR 106.7 says such abilities are ignored for the check; cite the subrule). Corrected by D-102: the CR has no such subrule, and its example requires a least fixed point over the board. An empty set produces no mana and the ability is not offered as a source. (2) `ManaProduction { kind: 'combination', options: ManaColor[][] }`: one of several fixed combinations chosen as the ability resolves ("{R}{R}, {R}{W}, or {W}{W}"). (3) Hybrid mana symbols in mana ability costs, paid by the planner like spell costs (CR 107.4e). (4) `activateOnlyIf?: Condition` on activated and mana abilities (CR 602.5b), using the existing conditions ("you control five or more lands", "you control a Swamp"); the planner and legal actions skip an ability whose condition fails. (5) `payLife` costs in mana abilities (CR 119.4: a player can pay life only if their life total is at least that much). (6) `StaticEffect { kind: 'grantAbility', subject, ability }` restricted to mana abilities for now ("Lands you control have ..."), in layer 6. The payment planner (`mana/`) must treat all of these as sources with their real cost and output; mana restrictions ("Spend this mana only ...") stay out (A5 typed mana exists, but no spending restriction is built).
- Alternatives: Treating "could produce" as "any color": rejected, it is wrong whenever opponents have only some colors. Precomputing it at the start of the game: rejected, the board changes.
- Consequences: The web's manual mana payment must list the new sources and ask the combination; the AI's planner already goes through `mana/`. The grammar reads these lines afterwards.

## D-100: Choices made as a permanent enters, and "the chosen" references (2026-10-22)
- Context: "As ~ enters, choose a creature type." (56 cards, weight 0.066) and "As ~ enters, choose a color." (43), with what reads the choice: "Creatures you control of the chosen type get +1/+1." (9), "~ is the chosen type in addition to its other types." (5), and many lords and cost reducers. The engine has no choice as a permanent enters other than the shock land's life payment.
- Decision: A replacement `asEntersChoose { what: 'creatureType' | 'color' }` (CR 614.12, 614.1c) asks the permanent's controller as it enters with a new decision kind `chooseOption { purpose: 'creatureType' | 'color', options }` (creature types from the CR's list in 205.3m, read from the repository's CR text by a generated table, not typed by hand; colors the five); the answer is stored on the object (`GameObject.chosen { creatureType?, color? }`) and lost when it leaves (CR 400.7). Filters and subjects may say "of the chosen type" or "of the chosen color" (`ObjectFilter.chosenType` / `chosenColor` relative to the source), and `setTypes` additive may add "the chosen type". A copy entering makes its own choice (CR 707.? checked by the implementer). The AI chooses its most common creature type in library, hand and battlefield, or its commander's color. `ENGINE_VERSION` bumps with the slice.
- Alternatives: A free-text type: rejected, the type must be a real creature type. Asking at resolution of the spell: rejected, the choice is part of entering (CR 614.12), so a permanent put onto the battlefield by an effect also asks.
- Consequences: The web needs a searchable type picker and a color picker and shows the choice on the permanent; the grammar reads the choice lines and "the chosen" references.

## D-101: Details of the costs slice that D-095 left open (2026-10-22)
- Context: building D-095 raised questions its text did not answer: where the alternative cost lives on a card, what `spells` of a reduction names for the spell itself, which costs a spell may add, in what order they are paid and what a Treasure does to that order, what is reduced and what "less" does to hybrid and Phyrexian mana, what a count counts while a spell is being cast, what the commander condition means, whether commander tax applies to a free cast, how Ward and an ability pay a discard, and what the view shows.
- Decision: (1) The free alternative cost is data on the face, `CardFace.alternativeCosts: [{ kind: 'free', condition? }]` (at most one; no condition means always), not an ability; the action is `castSpell { alternative: 'free' }`, listed as a separate option beside the ordinary cast, from the zones the card can be cast from anyway (hand, command zone, exile on an Adventure), and the spell on the stack remembers it (`StackData.free`, the `spellCast` event's `alternative: 'free'`, `ObjectView.free`). The condition is read for the caster with the card as the source (CR 118.9, 903.3d). (2) A reduction names its spells with `spells: { kind: 'this' } | ObjectFilter`: `this` is the spell's own ability (functions on the stack, CR 113.6d), a filter is a static ability of a permanent and describes the spell on the stack (no `zone`, `stackKind` or `owner`; `controller: 'you'` is "spells you cast" relative to the permanent). `amount` is a positive number or a `countOf`. (3) `CardFace.additionalCosts` may hold one `sacrifice` of a filter (never "this"), one `discard` of N cards, a fixed `payLife` and a `mana` cost without X ("pay X life" and any X are refused: spells with X are not supported). A `payLife` is castable only if the caster keeps at least 1 life (as for a kicker, so the planner's rule for a player at 0 life cannot strand the cast). (4) Order, CR 601.2f-h: the total cost is determined and locked in (mana cost, alternative cost or nothing, plus commander tax, kicker and additional mana, minus reductions), life is paid, then the mana (CR 601.2g: mana abilities come first), then the sacrifice, then the discard, each with a decision (`choosePermanent` / `chooseCards` with `forCost`; one candidate or exactly N cards is chosen by the engine; `cancel` rewinds the whole cast, CR 733). A mana plan must leave a permanent for the sacrifice: `planFor` takes `avoidSacrificing` and the payment code tries it when the first plan would sacrifice the only candidate (a Treasure for "sacrifice an artifact"); a payment by hand that does so is refused and can be redone. (5) A reduction affects only the numeric (generic) symbols of the cost, summed, and is never below zero (CR 118.7a, 601.2f); a cost with no generic mana is unchanged; reduced to nothing it is the empty cost and nothing is asked. Hybrid, Phyrexian and snow symbols are not reduced (CR 118.7e-g are not built). (6) `countOf` counts the objects in `filter.zone` (the battlefield by default) that match, with `controller` and `other` read as everywhere, and is counted when the instruction runs or at CR 601.2f; a spell being cast is on the stack (CR 601.2a), so it counts as nothing in its old zone (`SelectContext.excluded` for the check done before it has moved, and the hand a discard cost chooses from never holds it). (7) `controlCommander` is true when the condition's controller controls a permanent on the battlefield whose card is designated a commander, whoever owns it; a token and a permanent copying a commander are not commanders (CR 903.3, 903.3d); an intervening "if" on a `dies` or sacrifice trigger may not use it (CR 603.10a, as `controlsAtLeast`). (8) Commander tax is an additional cost, so it applies to a free cast from the command zone and the reductions reduce it (CR 118.9d, 903.8); the cast still counts as a cast from the command zone. (9) Ward and "counter target spell unless its controller pays" may cost `discard`: the payer is asked first (`confirmOptional`), accepting pays life, then the cards (all of the hand when it holds exactly N, else a `chooseCards` with no `cancel`, since they accepted; instruction stage `discard`), then the mana; a payer with fewer cards than N cannot pay and the spell is countered unasked (CR 118.3). An activated ability may have one `discard` cost, not from the hand and not with a crew cost; it is paid last (after the mana and the sacrifice) with `forCost` and `cancel`. (10) `ObjectView` gains `castCost` (the front face's mana cost now, after tax and reductions, for a card in a hand or command zone with a mana cost), `additionalCosts` (rules text of a non-permanent) and `free`. (11) The Cost kind `discard` stays `{ count }`: a filter ("discard a creature card") is not built. `ENGINE_VERSION` 13.
- Alternatives: The free cost as a static ability with a `cast` subject: rejected, it is a cost of the card, not something that applies to a permanent, and a face field lets `canCast` read it without deriving abilities from a card in hand. Choosing the sacrifice before the mana (to dodge the Treasure problem): rejected, CR 601.2g puts mana abilities first and the player may tap a creature for mana and then sacrifice it. Making an unpayable sacrifice a rejected `payAuto`: rejected, the engine would list an action it refuses. Reducing hybrid mana by the cheaper half: deferred, no measured card needs it.
- Consequences: The web needs the sacrifice and discard questions during a cast (`choosePermanent` and `chooseCards` with `forCost`, stage `sacrifice` and `discard` of the casting context), the free option as its own cast button and `ObjectView.castCost` on castable cards, and wording for the ward discard. The parser lowers the wordings in `docs/MECHANICS.md`. The AI counts `castCost`, skips a spell whose additional cost is not worth paying and casts a free option.

## D-102: Details of the mana slice that D-099 left open (2026-10-22)
- Context: building D-099 raised questions its text did not answer, and one claim in it was wrong: D-099 says CR 106.7 has a subrule that tells to ignore other "could produce" abilities. It has none (`pnpm rule 106.7` lists no subrule), and the example of 106.7 says the opposite: "if you control a Forest and an Exotic Orchard, and your opponent controls an Exotic Orchard, then each Exotic Orchard could produce {G}", while "you and your opponent each control no lands other than Exotic Orchards" produce nothing. The CR wins over the SPEC and over D-099 (AGENTS.md).
- Decision: (1) What a permanent could produce (CR 106.7) is the least fixed point over the board: the types its own mana abilities make, plus, for each "could produce" ability it has, the types of the permanents that ability looks at, repeated until nothing is added (`rules/mana-outcomes.ts`). Two Orchards alone make nothing, an Orchard that faces a Forest and the other Orchard makes {G} for both, and a Reflecting Pool that sees an Orchard that sees an Island makes {U}. "Ignore whether any costs of the ability could or could not be paid" is read as: the tapped state, summoning sickness, a mana cost, a life cost, a sacrifice cost and a restriction on activating (`activateOnlyIf`) of the abilities looked at do not matter, only what they would produce. A restriction is not literally a cost, but 106.7 asks what the ability "would produce if the ability were to resolve at that time", and the restriction decides whether it may be activated, not what it makes. Replacement effects of mana ("in any possible order") change no mana in this engine. (2) `couldProduce { lands: ObjectFilter, anyType?: boolean }`: the filter describes permanents on the battlefield (`validateCard` refuses another zone), `controller` is relative to the ability's controller; "any color" leaves colorless out (CR 106.1a, 106.1b), `anyType: true` ("any type") keeps it. The outcomes are one single mana per type, in the order W, U, B, R, G, C, read when the ability is activated; none means the ability makes no mana and is not offered, not a payment source and not in `manaSources`. (3) `combination { options }`: at least two combinations that differ as multisets, each at least one mana; each is stored and offered in the order W, U, B, R, G, C ({R}{W} is `['W', 'R']`). The choice is part of the activation: `Action` `activateAbility` and the `PriorityOption` of the same kind gain `combination?: ManaColor[]` (with `color: null`), a `payManual` tap gains `combination?`, and `PayManaDecision.manaSources[]` gains `combinations?` instead of `colors?`. A combination is accepted in any order; a color for a combination ability, or a combination for another, is refused with a message that names what is on offer. (4) Hybrid symbols in a mana ability's cost: `{R/W}`, `{C/W}` and `{2/W}`; X, snow and Phyrexian stay refused. The planner keeps the one-level rule: the cost of the ability is paid by the pool and by sources whose own abilities cost nothing. A symbol with two colored halves is one unit of demand in a class dimension that either color pays, so the search chooses the half and the number of searches does not grow; a symbol with a generic half is one search for each way of choosing (identical symbols give n + 1, not 2^n). A chain (a filter land paid by another filter land's mana) is not planned and works by hand. (5) `activateOnlyIf?: Condition` is on `activated` and `mana` abilities, read for the permanent's controller with the permanent as the source, when the ability is activated, by the same `evaluateCondition` as every condition. It is checked in the priority options, the payment sources, a manual tap and `activationRefusal`, so all of them agree; `FeatureRef` `ability:activateOnlyIf`. (6) A `payLife` cost on a mana ability needs a life total of at least the amount (CR 119.4); a manual tap may take the player to 0 (they lose at the next check, CR 704.5a) and the automatic planner may not: `PaymentSource.lifeLoss` (the life a source costs plus the damage it deals to its controller) and Phyrexian life share the budget `lifeAvailable`, which `planFor` sets to life - 1, so `planPayment` leaves the costly sources out when a plan would go over (this replaces the second planning pass `planFor` had for pain lands). A source that loses life ranks with the sources that have an extra effect, so a plain source is used first. (7) `StaticEffect` `grantAbility { subject, ability }` gives a mana ability to `this`, `attached` or `filter` subjects in layer 6 with the permanent's timestamp, so "loses all abilities" removes it when it came later and does not when the effect came first (CR 613.7). Granted abilities come after the printed ones and the expansions of keywords, so existing indexes do not move; one written the same way as an ability the object already has is not added twice. The ability keeps its own restriction (CR 602.5c). Only a mana ability can be granted. (8) `ENGINE_VERSION` 14. `SUPPORTED_FEATURES`: `manaProductionKinds` gains `couldProduce` and `combination`, `manaAbilityCostKinds` gains `payLife`, `staticKinds` gains `grantAbility`, and a new `abilityFeatures: ['activateOnlyIf']` (like `triggerFeatures`).
- Alternatives: Ignoring other "could produce" abilities (D-099): rejected, it contradicts the CR's own example. A new "restriction" kind for `activateOnlyIf`: rejected, the existing conditions already say "five or more lands" and "a Swamp". Choosing the combination at resolution through a decision: rejected, a mana ability has no stack and resolves as it is activated (CR 605.3b), so the activation carries the choice, as it does for a color. Enumerating the hybrid halves as separate searches: measured, four times slower with six filter lands on the board than the class dimension. Paying life in the planner without a budget: rejected, a payment that kills its own player is never chosen by auto-pay (the rule `planFor` already had for pain lands).
- Consequences: The web lists `combinations` and asks one (a button per combination); `activateAbility` with `combination` from the priority options; a source with a life cost or a restriction is simply absent from the lists when it cannot be used. The parser lowers the wordings in `docs/MECHANICS.md` ("More mana production"). Mana spend restrictions ("Spend this mana only ...") are still not built. `couldProduce` reads every permanent on the battlefield when an ability needs it, once per state (cached), so a board without such an ability pays nothing.

## D-103: X in mana costs (2026-10-22)
- Context: `validateCard` refuses every spell with {X} in its mana cost, and "X" appears in about 0.12 of the replay's unread weight (104 cards in the top 1,000 templates): "deals X damage", "X +1/+1 counters", "~ enters with X +1/+1 counters on it" (55 cards), "Draw X cards", "pay X life".
- Decision: A spell with {X} in its mana cost (CR 107.3, 107.3a) announces X as it is cast (CR 601.2b, after modes and before targets, kicker order as the CR gives it), as part of a new casting stage `x` answered by an action `chooseX { value }` from a bounded list the engine offers (0 up to the largest value the caster could pay from all their mana sources and pool, computed by the planner); the total cost adds X generic per {X} (CR 601.2f); the value is stored on the stack object (`StackData.x`) and read by `Amount { kind: 'x' }` on resolution and by "enters with X counters" (CR 107.3m: X is 0 in any other zone, and a permanent that entered from a spell with X remembers it only for its "enters with" replacement). Activated abilities with {X} in their cost use the same stage. "Pay X life" as an additional cost follows (D-101 refused it for want of X). X is never chosen for a spell cast without paying its mana cost (CR 107.3b: X is 0). `ENGINE_VERSION` bumps with the slice.
- Alternatives: A free number input: rejected, the engine offers every legal answer as a list (the AI and replay need it), and the web can present it as a stepper.
- Consequences: The web needs an X stepper during a cast and shows X on the stack; the AI picks X as the largest useful value; the grammar reads the X wordings.

## D-104: Keyword batch 1: Changeling, Devoid, Partner, Exalted, Annihilator, Persist, Infect, Toxic and poison, Split second, typecycling, Multikicker (2026-10-22)
- Context: Keyword lines are the largest unread group in the replay (about 0.43 of weight, 2,600 cards). This batch takes those whose rules fit existing machinery.
- Decision: Changeling (CR 702.73a, a characteristic-defining ability: every creature type, in layer 4 first, CR 613.3) and Devoid (702.114a, colorless in layer 5 first) work in every zone; Partner (702.124) has no game effect and is accepted (deck validation already checks the pair, D-053); Exalted (702.83a) and Annihilator (702.86a) expand in `derive` into the triggered abilities the CR defines (exalted: "attacks alone"; annihilator: the defending player sacrifices N permanents, with the existing choose-permanent decision); Persist (702.79a) expands into its dies trigger with a -1/-1 counter and the "had no -1/-1 counters" condition read from last-known information; Infect (702.90) and Toxic (702.164) change combat and other damage into -1/-1 counters to creatures and poison counters to players, with the state-based action at ten poison counters (704.5c) and poison in the view; Split second (702.61) stops players from casting spells and activating abilities that are not mana abilities while the spell is on the stack; typecycling (702.29e: "Basic landcycling", "Islandcycling", "Plainscycling" and the rest) expands like Cycling into a search for a card of the type; Multikicker (702.33c) asks how many times to pay, kept as a count on the stack object for "for each time it was kicked". `ENGINE_VERSION` bumps with the slice.
- Alternatives: Treating Changeling as a long subtype list on the card: rejected, it must also apply in hidden zones and to copies, which a CDA does. Poison as life loss: rejected, they are separate counters.
- Consequences: The web needs poison counters on the player strip, chips for the new keywords and a multikicker count; the AI must value infect and toxic damage and avoid casting into split second.

## D-105: Modal spells and abilities (2026-10-22)
- Context: "Choose one —", "Choose two —", "Choose one or both —" and "Choose one or more —" spells (charms, commands) and modal triggered abilities: about 0.10 of the replay's unread weight; `validateCard` refuses `modes` today although `SpellText` has them.
- Decision: The caster chooses modes as the first step of casting (CR 601.2b, 700.2a) with a new casting stage `modes` answered by `chooseModes { modes }`, the engine listing the legal sets (a mode whose targets cannot all be chosen is not offered, CR 700.2a; the same mode at most once unless the card says otherwise, 700.2d); each chosen mode keeps its own targets in order (601.2c) and its effect runs in printed order on resolution (700.2b? the implementer cites the rule); modal triggered abilities choose as they go on the stack (603.3c), using the D-089 trigger flow; a modal activated ability chooses at activation (602.2b). "If you control a commander as you cast ~, you may choose both instead" is a condition that widens `chooseModes.max`. `ENGINE_VERSION` bumps with the slice.
- Alternatives: One spell option per mode set in the priority list: rejected, the list would explode for "one or more" with four modes and hides the decision from the UI.
- Consequences: The web needs a mode chooser before targets; the AI scores mode sets; the grammar reads the bullet lists ("•" lines) under "Choose ...".

## D-106: Details of the choice slice that D-100 left open (2026-10-22)
- Context: building D-100 raised questions its text did not answer: the shape of the decision, the action and the event; where the question is asked for each way a permanent can enter (a land played, a spell resolving, an effect, a token or a copy); what a face may ask; what the answer is called and compared with, given that the CR spells two creature types with a typographic apostrophe; how a static ability can be "the chosen type" when "loses all abilities" comes later; what a gone source still reads; what the AI can count when the view shows no library. CR 614.12's own example settles the copy: "An effect creates a token that's a copy of Voice of All. As that token is created, the token's controller chooses a color for it." (614.12a: the choice is made before the permanent enters; 607.2d: the ability that refers to the choice is linked to the one that made it).
- Decision: (1) `PendingDecision` `chooseOption { purpose: 'creatureType' | 'color', options: string[], source, sourceName, sourceOracleText, face? }`, answered by `Action` `chooseOption { option }`, one action per option in the decision's order plus concede; there is no cancel. The options are the CR 205.3m creature types spelled as the rules spell them ("Time Lord" is one option; `C’tan` and `Shi’ar` keep their typographic apostrophe) or the five colors as `W`, `U`, `B`, `R`, `G`. An answer outside the list, for the other purpose, or from the other seat is refused. The event is `optionChosen { seat, source, purpose, option }`. (2) The creature types are `CREATURE_TYPES` (`packages/engine/src/data/creature-types.ts`), generated by `pnpm creature-types:generate` (`tools/creature-types/generate.ts`) from the repository's CR text and checked by `tools/creature-types/creature-types.test.ts`, which parses the rules again and compares the table and the file byte for byte. Names are compared with `sameCreatureType`, which treats `’` and `'` as one, because a card definition may write the plain apostrophe; the options and the stored answers keep the CR spelling. (3) A face asks at most one question as its permanent enters: one `asEntersChoose` (a type or a color), and not together with `entersTappedUnlessPays`; only a permanent face may have one; `validateCard` refuses the rest (`ast/validate-chosen.ts`). This keeps a land played from the hand, which answers by playing the land again with one extra answer, from having to carry several. (4) Where it is asked: `moveObject` answers `needsDecision` with the `chooseOption` before anything moves, the same way as the shock land's `confirmOptional`, and the callers resume with `entersChosen`: `playLand` (the land stays in the hand; `face` is kept), a resolving permanent spell (`rules/stack.ts` `finish`, which stays paused with the spell on the stack), and the `move` instruction of an effect, a flicker or a search (`ResolutionContext.entersChosen`, cleared once that move is done). A token has nothing to point at, so `createToken` makes one `enterToken` instruction for each token that asks (`rules/enter-token.ts`); the decision's `source` is then the resolving spell or ability and `sourceName` the token's name, and the answer is kept on the instruction. A token copy asks for its own choice; the original's is not copied (CR 707.2 lists what is copied, and a choice is not among it). The question goes to the controller of the permanent as it enters: the caster of a spell, otherwise the owner of a card put onto the battlefield without being cast, the effect's controller for a token. (5) `GameObject.chosen { creatureType?, color? }` is set on the new object only; it is public (`ObjectView.chosen`), is the new object's own and is gone when the permanent leaves (CR 400.7), and `checkInvariants` checks that a permanent has it only on the battlefield, from a question its card or token asks. A copy effect does not give it. (6) `ObjectFilter.chosenType` and `chosenColor` are read through `matchesFilter` (`FilterContext.sourceChosen`), relative to `ctx.source`: the object matches when it has that type or color now (after layer 4 and 5) and fails closed when the source made no such choice. A source that has left the battlefield reads its last-known information (`chosenOf`, CR 113.7a, 608.2h), so a "dies" trigger still knows what its creature chose. Every place a filter is read can use them: static subjects, triggers, target slots, cost reductions, conditions, searches. (7) A static `setTypes { subject: { kind: 'this' }, chosenType: true, additive: true }` adds the chosen creature type in layer 4 with the permanent's timestamp, in order with the continuous effects of resolved spells (a later "becomes a Frog" replaces the creature types it added). It is read from the printed abilities, not from the ones left after layer 6, so a later "loses all abilities" ends the lord's pump (layer 7c, read from the abilities left) and keeps the type (CR 613.1, 613.6: an effect that has begun to apply goes on applying when the ability is removed afterwards). The subject is `this` only and the type is the chosen one only; other statics of this shape are refused. (8) `validateCard` requires every card, and every custom token definition, that refers to a choice to ask for it itself (the scan finds `chosenType` and `chosenColor` anywhere in the face's abilities, spell text and costs, and a custom token's definition is its own owner); a choice nothing reads is allowed. (9) AI: `RandomLegalAgent` picks uniformly among the options; `CasualAgent` (`casual-options.ts`) picks the creature type that most cards in its hand and creatures it controls have, or the color most of its hand and permanents have, ties to the first listed option, and falls back on its commander (command zone or battlefield), then the first option; it draws nothing. It does not count its library: a view never contains one (SPEC test 28, `hidden-info.test.ts`), and D-100's "it may know its own library" would need a library list in the view; that was not added. (10) `SUPPORTED_FEATURES`: `replacementKinds` gains `asEntersChoose`, `staticKinds` gains `setTypes`, `selectorKinds` gains `chosenType` and `chosenColor` (`FeatureRef`s `replacement:asEntersChoose`, `static:setTypes`, `selector:chosenType`, `selector:chosenColor`). `ENGINE_VERSION` 15. (11) The scenario DSL gains `PermanentOptions.chosen`, `Actor.chooseOption(option)` and `expect.chosen(card, chosen | null)`.
- Alternatives: Asking when the spell resolves, before it becomes a permanent, as a separate step: rejected, the permanent's replacement effects are applied as it enters (CR 614.12), so putting it onto the battlefield by an effect must ask too. Storing the answer in the game state by name: rejected, the choice belongs to the object and ends with it (CR 400.7). A choice among free text: rejected, the type must be a real creature type. Applying the layer 4 type only while the permanent still has its abilities: rejected, it is wrong by CR 613.6 and layer order, and would make a creature stop being the chosen type when something later takes its abilities away. Counting the library for the AI by adding it to the view: rejected, it would break the hidden-information rule and its test for one heuristic. Allowing several questions on one face (a choice and a shock payment): rejected for now, no measured card needs it.
- Consequences: The web needs a searchable creature type picker and a color picker for the `chooseOption` decision (a hand-written list of 300 types is a dropdown with a filter), a log line for `optionChosen`, the choice shown on the permanent (`ObjectView.chosen`), and a handler in the three places that map every decision kind (`Overlays.tsx` twice, `decisions/model.ts`) and in the e2e bot. The parser reads "As ~ enters, choose a creature type." and "choose a color.", the "of the chosen type" shapes and "~ is the chosen type in addition to its other types." as `docs/MECHANICS.md` says. Not built: "protection from the chosen color" (a protection keyword whose color is read from the choice), other "choose" words (a card name, a number, a basic land type, an opponent, a player), a permanent that enters as a copy of another (Clone; its choices), Changeling matching every chosen type (D-104), a second question on one face, and the effect-level `setTypes` with "the chosen type". `docs/ROADMAP.md` lists them.

## D-107: Details of the X slice that D-103 left open (2026-10-22)
- Context: building D-103 raised questions its text did not answer: where in the casting steps X is announced and what the decision looks like, how the "largest X" is found and what it includes, what a spell cast without paying its mana cost does with X when the card also says "pay X life", how "pay X life" is written in the AST and how much life may be paid, where an effect reads X (spells, activated abilities, what the resolution knows), how "enters with X counters" finds the X of the spell it came from, what the mana value of a spell with X is, and what is not built (CR 107.3j, 107.3n, copies).
- Decision: (1) The decision is a new kind `chooseX { source, sourceName, sourceOracleText, purpose: 'spell' | 'ability', min, max, perX: { mana, life } }` (`source` the spell or ability on the stack), answered by `Action` `chooseX { value }`; `cancel` rewinds the cast or activation (CR 733). `CastingContext.stage` gains `'x'`. `min` is 0 and every value up to `max` is legal, so `legalActionsForDecision` lists one `chooseX` for each value plus `cancel` and `concede`; `applyAction` refuses a value that is not a whole number in that range. `perX.mana` is the number of {X} symbols of the cost (two {X} is 2, so X costs 2X, CR 107.3a) and `perX.life` the number of "pay X life" costs. It is asked only when `max` is at least 1; with `max` 0, or when the spell has nothing to announce, X is 0 and nothing is asked (`StackData.x` is 0 for the first and stays null for the second). (2) Order, CR 601.2b-c: kicker first (the kicked total is asked about with X = 0, so a spell is never offered a kicker it could not pay), then X, then the targets; for an activation (CR 602.2b) the ability goes on the stack, then X, then the targets. CR 601.2b lists "modes, splice, alternative and additional costs, variable cost", so a mode question (D-105) will come before the kicker. (3) The total cost (CR 601.2f) is the mana cost with X generic mana for each {X} (the generic mana takes the place of the first {X}), plus commander tax, kicker and additional costs, minus the reductions: X is announced at 601.2b, before the cost is determined, so a reduction of generic mana reduces the generic mana of the total with X in it (`rules/cast-cost.ts` `spellCost` takes `x`). `largestSpellX` asks `canPaySpellCost` for each candidate X, on the stack object, with the kicker as chosen: doubling until X cannot be paid, then narrowing (`rules/x-value.ts` `largestPayableX`), which is right because a larger X only adds to the cost; the planner sees every source, the pool, Signets and the life budget. A thousand is the largest X ever offered (`MAX_X`), so the search always ends. An activation asks `costRefusal` for each candidate (`costRefusal` and `breakDown` take `x`). (4) CR 107.3b: a spell cast without paying its mana cost (the `free` alternative cost) or by paying a flashback cost has no {X} to pay and its X is 0, nothing asked. When the same card also says "pay X life" the CR's wording is that X is 0 only for a spell that "has an {X} in its mana cost", so such a card is also not asked (`rules/x-value.ts` `spellXCost`); a card whose only X is in an additional cost ("pay X life", no {X} in its mana cost) announces it even when cast free. X in a kicker cost, a flashback cost, an additional mana cost, a ward cost or Cycling or Equip cost, and in a mana ability, is refused by `validateCard`. (5) "Pay X life" is a new cost kind `payXLife` with no fields, valid in `CardFace.additionalCosts` (at most one) and in an activated ability's cost, not in keyword costs or on a mana ability. It is not `payLife` with an amount that can be X, so no code that reads a fixed `payLife.amount` could meet it. Life is paid with the rest of the cost: for a spell at CR 601.2f-h (after the targets), so cancel gives it back; for an activation it is one of the costs that need no choice, paid right after the targets. A spell keeps at least 1 life (the same rule as a fixed `payLife`, D-101: `canPaySpellCost`), so X is offered up to life minus 1; CR 119.4 allows paying the whole life total and an activated ability does (X up to the life total). The difference is kept on purpose: a cast that takes the caster to 0 life would be offered to the planner at 0 life, which D-101 rules out; no card wants it. (6) Reading X: `Amount` `{ kind: 'x' }` is read through `SelectContext.x`, which `runEffect` fills from the `StackData.x` of the spell or ability that is resolving (`ResolutionContext.object`, so an ability reads its own X, not its source's, CR 107.3k); without a context X it reads the source's own stack data and is 0 otherwise (CR 107.3g). `validateCard` allows it in the effect of a spell with an {X} or "pay X life" (`SpellText.x`, which must be true) and of an activated ability whose cost has one (`xAllowed`), and nowhere else: a triggered or static ability, or one a permanent was given (CR 107.3j), has no X of its own. `modifyPt` takes plain numbers (D-101) and so cannot say X. (7) `Replacement` `entersWithCounters.count` is `number | { kind: 'x' }`: `moveObject` reads `StackData.x` of the spell it moves from the stack (CR 107.3m) and 0 for a card that comes from any other zone and for a token (CR 107.3g: a flickered or reanimated permanent enters with no counters); the permanent itself has no X (CR 107.3m: "the value of X for that permanent is 0"), its `stack` is null and `ObjectView.x` is absent. `validateCard` requires an {X} in the mana cost of a card that says so. Enters-the-battlefield triggers that read X (CR 107.3m's other half) are not built. (8) CR 202.3e: `manaValueOf` counts X for a spell on the stack, and for a spell that left it from last-known information (`LastKnownInfo.object` keeps the stack data), so "counter target spell, its controller loses life equal to its mana value" is right for a spell with X. (9) Surfaces: `ObjectView.x` (a spell or ability on the stack with an announced X), `ObjectView.castCost` shows each {X} as printed in front of the reduced rest, `spellCast.x` and `abilityActivated.x` events (present when an X was announced, even 0), `checkInvariants` (an announced X belongs to a stack object that has an X to announce), scenario DSL (`Actor.chooseX`, `CastHandle.x`, `CastOptions.x`, `ActivateOptions.x`). `ENGINE_VERSION` 16. `SUPPORTED_FEATURES`: `amountKinds` gains `x`, `costKinds` gains `payXLife`, and `abilityFeatures` gains `xCost` (`FeatureRef`s `amount:x`, `cost:payXLife`, `ability:xCost`: an {X} in a mana cost or an activation cost).
