(10) AI: `RandomLegalAgent` picks any value 0 to `max`; `CasualAgent` (`casual-x.ts`) reads what X does from the text it can see: "deals X damage" gets the opponent's life if that is within reach, else enough to kill the opposing creature with the most power among those it could kill (and the targets decision aims there once X is known), else everything at the face; "draw X cards" everything but the last card of its library; "pay X life" no more than leaves it above `PAY_LIFE_ABOVE`; anything else everything. It casts an instant or sorcery with an {X} only when it has a land or mana to spend beyond the rest of the cost, never as the free alternative (X is 0), and "put X +1/+1 counters on target creature" counts as helping its target.
- Alternatives: Asking X for a free cast and offering only X = 0: rejected, a question with one answer. A `payLife` cost with an `Amount`: rejected, several places read `payLife.amount` as a number (the mana ability code, the shock land, the AI) and one that missed the new shape would pay NaN. Reducing generic mana before adding X ("{X}{R}" reduced then X paid in full): rejected, CR 601.2f determines the total cost with X in it and reductions apply to it (cards such as a spell-cost reducer reduce an X spell the same as any). A number input with `min` and `max` and no list: the decision does carry only `min` and `max` and the legal actions list every value; the web shows a stepper. Letting a spell pay all of the life total: rejected, see (5). Looking for the largest X one value at a time: rejected, a player with twenty mana sources would cost twenty planner runs for each question; doubling and narrowing is about ten.
- Consequences: The web shows a stepper (`chooseX` decision with `min`, `max` and what each point costs, `cancel` allowed), `ObjectView.x` on the stack ("X is 3") and the printed {X} in `castCost`, and handles `chooseX` in the places that map every decision kind. The parser lowers the wordings in `docs/MECHANICS.md`. Not built (`docs/ROADMAP.md`): copies of a spell with X (CR 707.10, there are no spell copies yet), "X can't be 0" (a minimum for X), the letter Y (CR 107.3p), X defined by the text of the spell or chosen as it resolves (CR 107.3c, 107.3f), X in an alternative cost other than the two that have none, X in a delayed triggered ability or an enters-the-battlefield trigger that reads the spell's X (CR 107.3m, 107.3n), X in `modifyPt`, and X for a special action (CR 107.3d).

## D-108: More trigger kinds (2026-10-22)
- Context: The P15 report puts triggers first among the unread engine groups, about 0.31 of the replay's weight: steps with no trigger (beginning of combat, the draw step, an opponent's upkeep; 18 templates, 102 cards), "whenever a card is drawn" (17, 33 cards, popular: Smothering Tithe style and Rhystic Study style "an opponent draws a card"), qualities of the creature that entered or attacked ("with power 4 or greater", 14 templates), the attached permanent as the subject ("whenever equipped creature dies, draw two cards", 6), combat damage dealt ("whenever a creature you control deals combat damage to a player", 12 templates, 59 cards), leaves the battlefield (7, 32 cards), extra triggers (Panharmonicon, 7), and "an opponent casts" triggers with "unless that player pays" (several popular cards).
- Decision: Each is a new `Trigger` kind or a widening of one, found in the event stream (D-059) with no new machinery: (1) `step { step: 'beginCombat' | 'draw' | 'main1' | 'main2' | 'combatEnd' | 'upkeep' | 'endStep', whose: 'you' | 'each' | 'opponent' }` generalising `upkeep` and `endStep` (CR 503 to 514; the old kinds stay), triggering as the step begins (CR 603.2, 500.2). (2) `drawn { who: 'you' | 'opponent' | 'any', nth?: number }`, from `cardDrawn` events (CR 121.1; "whenever you draw your second card each turn": `nth`, counted from the turn's draw events; a card replaced by the commander zone does not count, D-097). (3) `dealsCombatDamage { what, to: 'player' | 'creature' | 'any', filter? }` from the damage events with their combat flag (CR 120.2a, 510.2), once per damaged object and source group as the CR says. (4) `leavesBattlefield { what, to?: Zone }` (CR 603.6c, 603.10a: looks back, uses last-known information). (5) `ObjectFilter` gains `power`, `toughness` and `manaValue` comparisons (`{ cmp: 'atLeast' | 'atMost' | 'equal', value }`) read from derived values, last-known information for look-back triggers, so "a creature with power 4 or greater enters" works in triggers, targets and conditions alike. (6) `what: { kind: 'attached' }` as a trigger subject ("equipped creature", "enchanted creature"): the permanent this is attached to, last-known information when it dies. (7) `castSpell` gains `by: 'opponent'` and "unless that player pays {N}" as an effect `unlessPays { player, cost, effect }` (the may-pay machinery of ward and D-092 in a general form: the named player is asked, on a decline the effect happens). (8) Doubling replacement "triggers an additional time" (Panharmonicon) is left for later: it changes how triggers are put on the stack. `ENGINE_VERSION` bumps with the slice.
- Alternatives: One generic "event matcher": rejected for now, the typed kinds keep validation and the web's wording simple.
- Consequences: The AI reads no new decisions (triggers use the existing ones); the web needs only wording for the new log events if any; the grammar reads each wording once the kinds exist.

## D-109: Powers and toughnesses from counts, X and characteristic-defining abilities (2026-10-22)
- Context: `modifyPt` and `setPt` take plain numbers, which blocks "gets +1/+1 for each artifact you control" (10 cards), "~'s power and toughness are each equal to the number of ...", "All creatures get -X/-X until end of turn", "gets +X/+0" (about 0.08 of replay weight, 91 cards), and the lords scaled by counts.
- Decision: `modifyPt` takes `Amount` for power and toughness, and `setPt` too; the amount is evaluated each time `derive` computes the object, so it follows the board (CR 611.3a: a static ability's effect applies continuously and is not locked in; a resolving effect's amount is locked in when it resolves, CR 611.2c), with `X` from the resolving spell for "until end of turn" effects. A characteristic-defining ability (CR 604.3, 613.4a) is a static `StaticEffect { kind: 'characteristicPt', power, toughness }` applied in layer 7a before 7b and 7c, working in all zones where it has meaning (CR 604.3a), with `countOf` over zones the object can see. Counting uses the derived state without recursion: an amount that counts creatures while being a creature's P/T counts itself as it stands in layers before 7 (layer 4 types) and never reads layer 7 results of any object (CR 613.8? the implementer finds the dependency rule; no dependency loops are needed for the measured wordings, which count types, not powers). `ENGINE_VERSION` bumps with the slice.
- Alternatives: Snapshotting the count when the ability starts: rejected, it is wrong for static abilities.
- Consequences: The grammar reads "for each" and "equal to the number of" in P/T text and CDA lines; the web shows derived P/T already; the AI evaluates derived P/T already.

## D-110: Details of the keyword batch that D-104 left open (2026-10-22)
- Context: building D-104 raised questions its text did not answer: where Changeling and Devoid are read and what they do to a non-creature, how Exalted's "that creature" and Annihilator's "defending player" are written as AST nodes, how Persist finds "it" in the graveyard and reads "had no -1/-1 counters", where infect, wither and toxic change damage and what deathtouch does with damage that is not marked, how split second reaches both the legal actions and `applyAction`, what the Multikicker question looks like and where the count is kept, and what a typecycling keyword carries.
- Decision: (1) Changeling (CR 702.73a) and Devoid (CR 702.114a) are read by `derive` from the object's printed (copiable) abilities, so they work in every zone, for copies and tokens, and a later "loses all abilities" (layer 6) does not undo what layer 4 or 5 already applied (CR 613.6, as D-106 does for the chosen type). They are applied first in their layer (CR 613.3), so "becomes a Frog" replaces the types Changeling gave and "becomes blue" colors a devoid object. Changeling adds every creature type of `CREATURE_TYPES` to the subtypes only for an object that is a creature or kindred (CR 205.3d), so a derived `subtypes` of a changeling creature holds about 300 names (`ObjectView.subtypes` too). Neither can be granted. Partner has no effect in the game and no code; `packages/cards` checks the pair of commanders (D-053). (2) New AST: `Trigger` `attacks` gains `alone: true` (CR 506.5: the only creature declared as an attacker; `trigger:alone`); `PlayerSelector` `{ kind: 'defendingPlayer' }` (CR 508.5: the player the source attacks, the controller of the planeswalker or the protector of the battle it attacks, kept after the creature has left combat, nothing once the combat has ended; `rules/defending.ts`); the `sacrifice` effect gains `player?: PlayerSelector`, valid only with a `choose` selector, so each player the selector names chooses among the permanents they control (`Instruction` `chooseSacrifice` and `sacrifice` carry `seat`); `ObjectRef` `{ kind: 'thisCard' }` (the card the source became in another zone, found through `LastKnownInfo.successor`, which `moveObject` sets as an object moves, and only while that card has not moved again, CR 400.7); `moveToZone.withCounters { counter, count }` (the counters are on the permanent as it enters, CR 122.6); `Condition` `{ kind: 'sourceHasCounter', counter }` (read from last-known information once the source has left, CR 603.10a); `Amount` `{ kind: 'timesKicked' }`; and `modifyPt` accepts `triggerSubject` as its object ("that creature gets"). (3) `derive-keywords.ts` expands Exalted (`attacks` of a creature you control, `alone`, `modifyPt` +1/+1 on the `triggerSubject`), Annihilator N (`attacks` of this, `sacrifice` of N chosen permanents by the `defendingPlayer`), Persist and Undying (`dies` of this with the intervening "if" `not sourceHasCounter` of `-1/-1` or `+1/+1`, `moveToZone` of `thisCard` to the battlefield under its owner's control with one such counter) and typecycling (an activated ability from the hand, cost plus `discardThis`, `search` for `max: 1` matching the keyword's `filter`, to the hand, revealed, then shuffled), after the printed abilities like the older expansions. The exalted triggers of different permanents for one attack are one group when the controller orders triggers (A18: the effect reads only the attacker). A returned permanent is a new object (CR 400.7), a token does not come back (CR 111.8), a card that left the graveyard before the trigger resolves is not found. (4) `dealDamage` stays the one routine: after the prevention shields, damage from a source with infect gives the player poison counters and no life loss (CR 120.3b, new event `poisonChanged { seat, from, to }`), damage from a source with infect or wither to a creature is -1/-1 counters (`counterAdded`) and not marked damage (CR 120.3d), combat damage from a creature with toxic also gives its total toxic value (CR 120.3g, 702.164b); lifelink, planeswalker loyalty, commander damage and `damageDealt` are unchanged. Deathtouch looks at damage dealt, not damage marked, so the state-based action reads `damagedByDeathtouch` alone (CR 704.5h). Infect and wither are read from the source's abilities after layer 6, or its last-known information (CR 702.90d), so they can be granted (`GRANTABLE_KEYWORDS`); toxic is parametric and cannot. Poison counters and the loss at ten (CR 704.5c) were already in state and in the view. (5) Split second (`rules/split-second.ts`): `canCast` and `activationRefusal` refuse while a spell with the keyword is on the stack, so the priority options (hence `getLegalActions`) and `applyAction` agree; mana abilities, triggers and a pass are untouched. (6) Multikicker: the question is `PendingDecision` `chooseX` with `purpose: 'multikicker'`, `cost` the cost of one time, `perX` zero, asked in the `kicker` stage before X and the targets only when at least one kick can be paid, `max` the most times the whole cost can be paid (`largestPayableX` over `canPaySpellCost`, life leaves at least 1 as for Kicker), answered by `chooseX { value }` (0 is not kicked), `cancel` rewinds (CR 733). `StackData.kicks` and `GameObject.kicks` keep the count (absent for 0 and for plain Kicker), `StackData.kicked` stays "at least once", `CostRequest.kicks` multiplies the cost, `spellCast.kicks`, `ObjectView.kicks`, `timesKicked` reads it (1 for a kicked spell with Kicker, 0 for none). A card has one kicker or multikicker ability. (7) `Keyword` `typecycling { filter: ObjectFilter, cost }` (any type, subtype, supertype or combination, CR 702.29e; the filter sets neither zone nor controller and is not empty), `annihilator { count }`, `toxic { count }`, `multikicker { cost }`, and the plain `changeling`, `devoid`, `partner`, `exalted`, `persist`, `undying`, `infect`, `wither`, `splitSecond`. All are in `SUPPORTED_FEATURES.keywordKinds`, `triggerFeatures` gains `alone`, `selectorKinds` gains `defendingPlayer` and `thisCard`, `conditionKinds` gains `sourceHasCounter`, `amountKinds` gains `timesKicked`. `ENGINE_VERSION` 17. (8) AI: `CasualAgent` counts life damage and poison damage apart (`casual-poison.ts`: infect damage is poison, toxic's N is read from the text), attacks all out when either is lethal and chump-blocks lethal poison; answers the Multikicker count with the most it can pay, life only above `PAY_LIFE_ABOVE`, and does not cast a spell that is only its kicks with no mana to kick; typecycles for a land when its hand has none, nothing is worth casting and it controls fewer than eight lands; sacrifices for Annihilator by `permanentValue` as for any sacrifice; the engine lists no cast under split second, so it passes. `RandomLegalAgent` needed no change.
- Alternatives: A `moveToZone` of `this` for Persist: rejected, `this` names the old object, which is gone. Putting the counter on after the return with `addCounters`: rejected, the permanent would not have it as it enters (CR 122.6) and an enters trigger would not see it. A per-card answer for "defending player" in `sacrifice` (a flag): rejected, a selector is what "each opponent" already is. Counting kicks as the one `kicked` boolean plus a second field only for Multikicker: rejected, `kicks` absent for plain Kicker keeps the older cards and tests unchanged while `timesKicked` hides the difference. A new decision kind for the Multikicker count: rejected, `chooseX` already is "a whole number from 0 to a maximum, with cancel", and the web has it. Changeling as a list of 300 subtypes on the card: rejected in D-104, it must work in every zone and for copies.
- Consequences: The web needs a wording for the `poisonChanged` event and the poison counters on the player strip (the view has had `poison`), chips for the new keywords, the Multikicker count in the `chooseX` stepper (`purpose: 'multikicker'`, `cost`, `perX` zero), `ObjectView.kicks`, and handles `defendingPlayer` and `thisCard` in the ability labels. A changeling creature's view lists every creature type, which the web should fold into "every creature type". The parser reads the wordings in `docs/MECHANICS.md`. Not built (`docs/ROADMAP.md`): granting Changeling, Devoid, Exalted, Persist or Undying (a keyword that is expanded or read in layer 4 or 5 cannot be granted in layer 6), "Partner with" and the other partner variants' enters trigger, Multikicker with X or an unusual cost, a card with both Kicker and Multikicker, several defending players (the engine has two seats), Persist or Undying on a card that is not a creature (the "dies" trigger only sees creatures).

## D-111: Details of the trigger slice that D-108 left open (2026-10-22)
- Context: building D-108 raised questions its text did not answer: how "your second card each turn" is counted, where the draw step's trigger sits against the turn-based draw, what "one trigger per damaged object" means for blockers and trample, how a comparison reads an object that has left, what a static ability that compares power does about CR 613.8, how "equipped creature" finds its host once the host is dying, who answers first in "you may draw a card unless that player pays {1}", and which extra shapes the wordings need.
- Decision: (1) `step` maps `upkeep`, `draw`, `main1`, `beginCombat`, `combatEnd`, `main2`, `endStep` to the `stepBegan` events of the steps of those names (`main1` and `main2` are the precombat and postcombat main steps, `combatEnd` the end of combat step, CR 511); `whose: 'opponent'` is any turn whose active player is not the controller of the ability. The older kinds `upkeep` and `endStep` stay. The draw step already draws before it gives priority (CR 504.1, 504.2): the step's trigger is noticed from `stepBegan` and goes on the stack at the same moment as the draw trigger of the drawn card, after the draw; the end of combat step and the beginning of combat happen with no attacker (CR 507, 508.8). (2) `drawn`: `SeatState.cardsDrawnThisTurn` counts the cards each player drew this turn (reset for every seat as a turn begins, the commander replaced into the command zone is not counted, D-097), and `cardDrawn` carries `nth`, the count including that card, so the trigger needs no state beyond its event. "Your second card each turn" is `nth: 2`. (3) `dealsCombatDamage` is read from `damageDealt` events with `combat: true`, one occurrence for each source and each recipient: a creature blocked by two creatures that divides its damage triggers "deals combat damage to a creature" twice, a trampler that damages a blocker and the player triggers `to: 'any'` twice, `to: 'player'` once and `to: 'creature'` once, a double striker triggers in each of its two steps, damage prevented entirely has no event and so no trigger (CR 603.2g), a creature that deals 0 deals no damage. `to` also takes `'opponent'` (a player the controller of the ability does not control), which "deals combat damage to an opponent" needs; `filter` narrows a creature recipient (`to: 'creature'` only). Infect and toxic do not change it: infect damage to a player is damage. (4) `leavesBattlefield` is read from `zoneChanged` events with `fromZone: 'battlefield'` (the token that goes to another zone included, CR 603.6c), with the zone it went to for `to`; it is a look-back kind (`LOOK_BACK_TRIGGER_KINDS`, CR 603.10a), so an intervening "if" that counts permanents is refused on it as on `dies`. (5) `NumberComparison { cmp: 'atLeast' | 'atMost' | 'equal', value }` on `ObjectFilter.power`, `toughness` and `manaValue`. `matchesFilter` describes an object that is still in the game by `derive` (with the {X} of a spell on the stack counting as the announced X, CR 202.3e, `rules/mana-value.ts`) and an object that has left by its last-known information (characteristics, power and toughness as recorded when it moved, CR 603.10a; this also replaces `derive` of the stale object for the older look-back filters). An object with no power or toughness matches no power or toughness comparison, not even `atMost`. In static abilities only `modifyPt` may compare power or toughness (validateCard refuses the others, CR 613.8): such an effect depends on the effects that change power (CR 613.8a), so `derive-statics` applies the `modifyPt` effects that do not compare first, then the comparing ones in battlefield order, each reading the target's own power and toughness (`ptWith`: its effects, counters and the bonuses added so far); a cycle among comparing effects is settled by that order (CR 613.8b). Mana value comparisons are valid in every static subject. (6) `TriggerSubject` adds `{ kind: 'attached' }` ("equipped creature", "enchanted creature") to `dies`, `attacks`, `becomesTapped`, `becomesTarget`, `dealsCombatDamage` and `leavesBattlefield` (not to `entersBattlefield`, no permanent is attached as it enters): the trigger matches when the subject's id is what the source is attached to, read from the source's `attachedTo` as it was (live, or last-known information when the source left too). The attachment is only undone by a later state-based action (CR 704.5m, 704.5n), so a host that dies is still the host while its trigger is noticed. (7) `castSpell.by` gains `'opponent'`. `unlessPays { player, cost, effect, optional? }` runs as CR 118.12a says: the payer is asked first (`confirmOptional` with `purpose: 'unlessPays'`, then `payMana` of the same purpose; `cancel` of the payment is "do not pay"), with Ward's question, payment and discard code (`rules/pay-unless.ts` now serves `counterUnlessPays` and `unlessPays`); a payer who cannot pay the whole cost is not asked (CR 118.3); when the payer does not pay `effect` runs, for each player the selector names, and `optional: true` ("you may draw a card unless...") asks the controller after that with a new instruction `mayEffect` (an ordinary `confirmOptional` question; declining drops only that effect, where the ability-level `optional` ends the ability, CR 603.5). `controllerOf` and `ownerOf` of the `triggerSubject` are now valid player selectors in any effect of a trigger that has a subject ("that spell's controller loses 1 life"); the controller of a spell that was countered meanwhile is read from last-known information (CR 608.2h). (8) Not built: the doubling replacement "triggers an additional time" (Panharmonicon) changes how triggers are put on the stack and stays in `docs/ROADMAP.md`. `ENGINE_VERSION` 18. (9) AI: `unlessPays` questions are answered like Ward's (pay unless a life part of the cost would put the agent in danger; a discard cost only with cards it is glad to lose); nothing else is new to decide. The trigger kinds make no new decisions.
- Alternatives: Asking the controller "you may" first by the ability's own `optional`: rejected, CR 118.12a puts the payer's choice first and the order is information. Counting the turn's draws from a log in the state: rejected, a counter per seat is smaller and exact. Reading the recipient of combat damage once for all the damage a source deals in a step: rejected, the CR has one event for each recipient and the wordings ("to a creature", "to a player") differ by recipient. Applying power-comparing statics by timestamp with the rest: rejected, a 3/3 with an anthem would not count as a 4/4 for "power 4 or greater" depending on which permanent is older, against CR 613.8a.
- Consequences: The grammar reads the wordings in `docs/MECHANICS.md` once the kinds exist. The web needs a wording for the new `unlessPays` purpose in the confirm and payment dialogs (the question comes from the ability on the stack, `source`, with no `subject`), the `cardDrawn.nth` field in nothing visible, and ability labels for the new trigger kinds, `unlessPays`, and the `attached` subject and filter comparisons. Two copies of the same watcher are two groups when their player orders triggers (their sources differ); this is unchanged from D-059. Not built (`docs/ROADMAP.md`): Panharmonicon, power or toughness comparisons in the subject of a keyword grant or restriction, "deals combat damage" for damage a source dealt after it left combat, a trigger for noncombat damage.

## D-112: "Enchanted creature" as a trigger subject is read only where the engine knows the host (2026-10-22)
- Context: Stage P18 (trigger wordings, D-108, D-111) reads "equipped creature" and "enchanted creature" as the trigger subject `attached`. The engine's `attached` trigger subject has no host-type check, so on an Aura it cannot tell that the permanent it enchants is a creature, which matters when the Aura is enchanting something else after a type change.
- Decision: The grammar lowers "enchanted creature" on an Aura to `attached` only for `dies`, `attacks` and `dealsCombatDamage`, where the event itself shows the subject was a creature. For `becomesTapped`, `becomesTarget` and `leavesBattlefield` the line is read and refused (`notRunnable`), reported as an unread shape in `docs/ROADMAP.md`. "Equipped creature" is unrestricted (Equipment attaches only to creatures, CR 301.5c). An engine host-type check for the `attached` subject (as `StaticSubject.attached.types` has, D-081) lifts the refusal and is the next class-P item for these lines.
- Alternatives: Reading all six kinds and accepting the rare wrong match: rejected, honesty comes first (an unsupported card is flagged, never guessed).
- Consequences: A few Aura lines stay unsupported until the engine slice; no card is misread.

## D-114: Details of the modal slice that D-105 left open (2026-10-22)
- Context: building D-105 raised questions its text did not answer: how the decision and the action look, what order the announcements come in, what the AST of a modal ability is, how the targets of several modes are asked and kept apart, when the engine asks and when it chooses, how a mode that cannot be chosen is told from one that can, what resolution and fizzling do, how the commander widening is written, what the validator refuses, and what is not built.
- Decision: (1) The decision is a new kind `chooseModes { source, sourceName, sourceOracleText, purpose: 'spell' | 'ability' | 'trigger', modes: { index, text, legal }[], min, max, sets, forTrigger? }`, answered by `Action` `chooseModes { modes }`. `sets` is every legal choice, each in printed order, fewest modes first (so "choose one" lists the modes one by one); `max` already counts the commander widening; a mode is `legal` when it is in some set. `applyAction` accepts exactly one of the sets, in any order, and stores the modes in printed order. `legalActionsForDecision` lists one `chooseModes` for each set, then `cancel` (a spell or an activation: it rewinds, CR 733; not a trigger, CR 603.3c) and `concede`. (2) Order, CR 601.2b: the modes come first, then the kicker or multikicker question, then X, then the targets (D-107 said so); an activation is modes, X, targets, costs; a trigger is modes, then targets. `CastingContext.stage` gains `'modes'`. (3) The engine asks only when more than one set is legal. With exactly one it chooses it and says so (`modesChosen { automatic: true }`), the same rule as X (D-107: no question with one answer); with none the spell is not castable (`canCast` and `targetsPossible` look for a legal set), the activated ability is not offered (`activationRefusal`) and a triggered ability is removed (`abilityRemoved { reason: 'noLegalModes' }`, CR 603.3c, 700.2b). A mode is legal when every slot of its targets has at least its minimum of legal targets now (CR 700.2a); the sets are the subsets of the legal modes with between `min` and the limit of them (CR 700.2, 700.2d: no mode twice; "You may choose the same mode more than once" is not built). With `max` above the number of legal modes the limit is the number of legal modes. (4) AST: `SpellText.modes` and `chooseModes: ModeChoice { min, max, maxIf? }` (already there) and the same two fields on `triggered` and `activated` abilities. A modal ability keeps `effect` (it is not optional in the type, so no reader of the AST breaks) as the empty sequence `{ kind: 'sequence', effects: [] }` and has no `targets`; `validateCard` refuses anything else. Two to eight modes (the engine lists every set, 2^8 at most). (5) Targets: the chosen modes' target specs are asked in one `targets` decision, mode by mode in printed order, each slot tagged `TargetChoiceSpec.mode`; the target ids are unique across all the modes of a spell or ability (`validateCard` refuses a clash), so `chosenTargets` needs no namespace and an effect's `{ kind: 'target', id }` reads its own slot. D-105 said "namespaced per mode": uniqueness gives the same separation without a rewrite of every reader of `specId` (Ward, `becameTarget`, the AI), and the parser, which numbers targets itself, can make the ids unique by mode. A mode that was not chosen has no slots (CR 700.2c). (6) Resolution: `targetSpecsOf` is the chosen modes' specs; the effect that runs is the chosen modes' effects in printed order as one sequence (`chosenEffect`, CR 608.2c). CR 608.2b is the ordinary rule: the spell fizzles when it has targets and every one is illegal, a mode with an illegal target does nothing while the others happen, a mode with no target neither saves nor sinks a spell whose other modes' targets are all gone. (7) Triggers (CR 603.3c): `runQueue` of `rules/trigger-stack.ts` checks the sets before the targets; with several sets the ability is put on the stack first (as for targets) and `GameState.triggering.awaiting` is its object; the `chooseModes` decision has `forTrigger` and the answer (`answerTriggerModes`) goes on to the chosen modes' targets with the same `targets` decision, then the rest of the queue. A forced choice of targets is made by the engine. (8) The widening is `chooseModes.maxIf: { condition, max }`: when the condition holds for the controller as the modes are chosen (read with the spell or ability as the source), `max` is replaced by `maxIf.max` (more than `max`, at most the number of modes). The one condition the parser needs is `controlCommander` (D-101, CR 903.3d: a commander permanent on the battlefield; a commander in the command zone or on the stack is not controlled). (9) X: a modal spell with an {X} announces it once for the whole spell (D-103) and every mode reads it; a modal activated ability reads the X of its own cost; a triggered ability never has an X (CR 107.3j). That is the existing rule for X, so nothing about modes is refused for it. A mode with an additional cost (CR 700.2h) and pawprint modes (CR 700.2i) are not built. (10) Surfaces: `modesChosen { seat, source, modes, automatic }` event (spell, activation and trigger alike), `abilityRemoved.reason` `'noLegalModes'`, `ObjectView.modes` (the chosen indices, printed order) and `ObjectView.modeTexts` (the text of every mode, so the indices can be worded for a spell, whose AST the view does not carry), `TargetChoiceSpec.mode`, `TriggerChoice.trigger` (the trigger of the waiting ability, for the ordering panel), an invariant (chosen modes are distinct, in order, within what the text allows, and present on every modal spell or ability that is on the stack for good), scenario DSL (`Actor.chooseModes`, `CastHandle.modes`, `CastOptions.modes`, `ActivateOptions.modes`), `SUPPORTED_FEATURES.abilityFeatures` gains `modal` (`ability:modal`). `ENGINE_VERSION` 19. (11) AI: `RandomLegalAgent` picks any of the sets; `CasualAgent` (`casual-modes.ts`) scores a mode from its text against the board (a kill of a creature of the opponent's or lethal damage or life loss is best, a card next, life small; a mode that needs a target the board lacks, such as "destroy target creature" with only its own creatures, scores below zero; one that adds nothing, such as damage that kills nothing, counts as zero), takes the set with the highest total (the first of equal ones, so the answer does not depend on chance, which means the most good modes when all are good), aims each slot by its mode's text (or, for an ability, its effect), casts a modal spell when some mode is worth choosing and activates a modal ability for a mode worth at least 3.
- Alternatives: One `targets` decision for each mode: rejected, the slots of all the chosen modes are one choice of the cast (CR 601.2c) and a second decision kind would be one more place for the web and AI to handle. Namespaced spec ids (`m1:t1`): rejected, see (5). Making `effect` optional on abilities: rejected, every reader of `ability.effect` in the engine, the parser and the web would change; an empty sequence is a valid effect that does nothing. Asking when one set is legal: rejected, see (3). Offering one `castSpell` option for each set: rejected in D-105.
- Consequences: The web needs a mode chooser (a list of checkboxes or radio buttons from `modes`, `min`, `max`, `sets`, with `cancel` for a spell and an activation and none for a trigger), the stage `'modes'` in the cast flow, the `modesChosen` event and the new `abilityRemoved` reason in the log, `ObjectView.modes` and `modeTexts` on the stack, `TargetChoiceSpec.mode` to group the target slots, and `TriggerChoice.trigger` in the ordering panel. The parser reads the bullet lists (`docs/MECHANICS.md`). Not built (`docs/ROADMAP.md`): Escalate, Spree and Entwine (they change the cost by the number of modes chosen), choosing the same mode more than once (CR 700.2d), a mode chosen by another player (CR 700.2e), copies of modal spells and abilities (CR 700.2g, 707.10: there are no copies of spells or abilities yet), modes with their own additional cost (CR 700.2h), pawprint modes (CR 700.2i), a mode that has an X of its own beyond the spell's, and the AI weighing a mode by the targets it could really get (it reads the mode's text).

## D-115: Details of the power and toughness slice that D-109 left open (2026-10-22)
- Context: building D-109 raised questions its text did not answer: how "-X/-X" and "-1/-1 for each ..." are written when an `Amount` is never negative, where a counted amount is read in a static ability without `derive` calling itself, how a characteristic-defining ability (CDA) is written, in which zones and for which objects it works, what a printed `*` needs, what the dependency rule (CR 613.8) requires here, and what a creature that loses all abilities is.
- Decision: (1) Shapes. `PtAmount = Amount | { kind: 'times', factor, of: Amount }` is the type of `power` and `toughness` of the effects `modifyPt` and `setPt`: "-X/-X" is `times` with factor -1 of `{ kind: 'x' }`, "+X/+0" is `{ kind: 'x' }` and 0, "+1/+1 for each artifact you control" is a `countOf` for both, "-1/-1 for each ..." a `times` of -1 of a `countOf`. `times` is not an `Amount` kind: nothing else may be negative, and `validateCard` refuses it anywhere but a power or toughness (the features list it as the amount kind `times`). `StaticEffect` `modifyPt` takes `StaticPtAmount` (a number, a `countOf` or a `times` of a `countOf`). `StaticEffect` `{ kind: 'characteristicPt', power?, toughness? }` takes `DefinedPtAmount` (a `countOf` or a positive `times` of one) for the stat it defines, one or both (power only: "~'s power is equal to the number of creatures you control" is supported, with a printed `*` power and a number for the toughness). `ContinuousChange` keeps numbers: what a resolving effect's amounts came to is stored (CR 611.2c, 608.2h), so "-X/-X" with X = 2 is `{ kind: 'modifyPt', power: -2, toughness: -2 }`, older saved states and golden ASTs do not change, and the X comes from the resolving spell or ability (`SelectContext.x`, or the stack data of the source). (2) Counting inside `derive` (`rules/derive-count.ts`, `rules/derive-view.ts`): a static amount is read each time the object is derived (CR 611.3a, nothing is stored), from `typeViewOf` (the copiable values with layers 4 and 5 applied, `rules/derive-view.ts`), never from `derive`, so counting cannot loop. This is the dependency rule: CR 613.8a says an effect depends on another when applying the other would change what the first applies to or does, within one layer or sublayer, so the question is only whether an effect applied in sublayer 7a or 7c can change what a count in 7a or 7c reads. A count reads types, subtypes, colors, controller, tapped status, zone and mana value, which layers 1 to 6 settle before layer 7 begins (CR 613.1), and never a power or toughness, so nothing in layer 7 changes what it counts and no dependency, and so no loop, exists; two characteristic-defining abilities in 7a do not read each other's results for the same reason (CR 613.8a part c lets only characteristic-defining abilities depend on each other, and none here does). `validateCard` refuses what would break that: a `powerOf`, `manaValueOf`, `x` or `timesKicked` amount in a static ability or a CDA (CR 107.3j: a static ability has no X), and a filter that compares `power` or `toughness` in a counted filter, in any `anyOf` member too; mana value is allowed (a copiable value no layer 7 effect changes). "You" is the controller of the source and, outside the battlefield and the stack, its owner (CR 109.5, 108.4a); `other` leaves out the source. (3) A CDA works in every zone (CR 604.3, 208.2a): `derive` reads it from the copiable abilities of an object in any zone (a creature card in a graveyard or a hand, a spell on the stack, a permanent), counting the zones that object can see (in the hand it counts itself, on the stack and the battlefield it does not). A copy has it (CR 604.3a, 707.2: the copiable values include abilities). It is layer 7a: before a `setPt` effect (7b) and before counters, `modifyPt` effects and static bonuses (7c), whatever their timestamps (CR 613.4a). A noncreature permanent has no power or toughness whatever defines it (CR 208.3). The last-known information of a creature that left keeps the derived power and toughness (`GameState.lki`), so a dies trigger reads "its power" as it died (CR 113.7a, 608.2h). (4) Loses all abilities: a CDA is an ability, so a creature that lost all abilities (CR 613.1f) has none; the CR does not say what a printed `*` is then, and the engine reads it as 0 (the rule for a number that cannot be determined, CR 208.2a, is the nearest), which kills a `*/*` creature (CR 704.5f) and leaves the printed number of the stat a power-only or toughness-only CDA did not define. A later `setPt` effect (layer 7b) gives it a base value anyway ("loses all abilities and becomes 1/1"). This reading is the engine's, not a quoted rule; the Gatherer rulings I know for it are from memory and UNVERIFIED. (5) Printed `*`: `validateCard` accepts a `'*'` power or toughness only together with exactly one `characteristicPt` of the same face that defines that stat, and refuses a CDA that defines a stat the card prints as a number (it would silently override it) and a stat defined twice; a token definition prints numbers only, so a token with a `*` is still refused, and so is a CDA on a token with numbers. `unsupportedFeatureIssues` says the same in its own words for a face checked alone. `SUPPORTED_FEATURES.staticKinds` gains `characteristicPt` and `amountKinds` gains `times`. (6) Not built: a CDA with an offset ("1+*", "*+1": the Scryfall string is not a bare `*`, so the converter already marks the card unsupported), a CDA that counts the opponent's or a chosen player's objects ("the number of creatures the chosen player controls": `owner`), a CDA that sets colors or subtypes, "equal to your life total" or the highest power among your creatures (no such amount), a static `modifyPt` that reads X or another object's power, and layer 7d. `ENGINE_VERSION` 20.
- Alternatives: Storing the amounts in `ContinuousChange` and reading them at derive time: rejected, a resolving effect's amounts are locked in (CR 611.2c, 608.2h) and an `Amount` of `x` could not be read later. A negative kind in `Amount` ("neg"): rejected, every reader of `Amount` (draw, life, counters) would have to refuse negatives. `derive` calling `derive` to count (read each counted object's types after the full layers): rejected, it loops for any creature that counts creatures, and the types are final before layer 7 anyway. A separate card field for a CDA ("definedPt") instead of a static ability: rejected, CR 604.3 says it is a static ability, and the static kind reuses the abilities lists (copiable values, loses all abilities, the face validator).
- Consequences: The parser reads "for each", "equal to the number of ..." in a P/T line and a CDA line, and "-X/-X"/"+X/+0" in a pump (`docs/MECHANICS.md`). The web wording of a modifyPt effect whose power is not a number needs a case (`apps/web/src/ui/decisions/ability-label.ts`, the one place that stopped type-checking). The AI reads derived power and toughness from the view as before; `pumpOf` and the target planner skip or sign a pump whose size is not a number. A creature card whose printed `*` is defined by a CDA shows its derived numbers in every zone where the view shows the card.

## D-116: Keyword batch 2: cost-paying keywords, simple triggers and regeneration (2026-10-22)
- Context: After batch 1 (D-104), the largest unread keyword lines by card count are Convoke (102 cards), Morph and its relatives, Devoid done, Cumulative upkeep (57), Storm (33), Cascade (34), Exalted done, Extort (17), Evolve (22), Improvise (23), Delve (27), Affinity (37), Battle cry, Mentor, Bushido (12), Skulk, Regenerate (118 cards in the replay, 133 in all), Unearth (55), Madness (56) and Ninjutsu (35). This batch takes those that fit existing machinery. Alternative-cost and other-zone keywords (Madness, Unearth, Ninjutsu, Foretell, Evoke, Dash, Overload) are a separate slice (D-117).
- Decision: (1) Convoke (CR 702.51a), Improvise (702.126a) and Delve (702.66a) are cost-payment options during casting at CR 601.2f-h: the caster may tap untapped creatures (convoke: of the colour of each coloured mana, or any for generic), untapped artifacts (improvise) or exile graveyard cards (delve) for each mana, chosen with a `choosePermanent` / `chooseCards` question in a new casting stage `payOptions` before the mana payment, listing only what can reduce the cost; the legal actions and the planner count them, so a spell is castable when the extra resources make it payable. Affinity for [text] (702.41a) is a self cost reduction (`costReduction { spells: this, amount: countOf }`, D-101) and needs no new primitive. (2) Triggered keywords expand in `derive` into their defined triggers: Extort (702.101a: on casting a spell, optional {W/B} payment, then drain; uses `unlessPays`-style may-pay, D-111), Evolve (702.100a, with the power/toughness comparisons of D-108), Battle cry (702.91a, an effect on each other attacking creature), Mentor (702.134a, targets, D-089), Bushido N (702.45a, blocks or becomes blocked: a new trigger kind `blocks`/`becomesBlocked` found in the declare-blockers events), Cascade (702.85a: exile until a nonland card with lower mana value, may cast it free: a new effect `cascade` using the free cast of D-101 and the library handling of D-091), Storm (702.40a: needs a spell copy; deferred until copies of spells exist, D-118). (3) Skulk (702.118a) is an evasion keyword read by the blocker check (D-098). (4) Regenerate (701.19) is a replacement shield like prevention (D-086): `effect regenerate { objects }` creates a shield that, the next time the permanent would be destroyed this turn, taps it, removes it from combat, removes all damage and prevents the destruction (CR 701.19b-c); "can't be regenerated" is honoured by destroy effects that say so. Cumulative upkeep (702.24) and the keyword-action batch (monarch, initiative, proliferate, explore and the rest) follow in D-119. `ENGINE_VERSION` bumps with the slice.
- Alternatives: Treating convoke as a mana ability of the creatures: rejected, it taps creatures as part of paying the cost of a spell, not as mana abilities (no mana is produced). Implementing Storm now with a stub copy: rejected, honesty first; spell copies are their own slice.
- Consequences: The web needs a pay-options stage (tap creatures and exile cards while casting), a blocked/blocks log, and regenerate wording; the AI chooses convoke creatures that are not needed for attack or defence.

## D-117: Alternative costs and casting from other zones (2026-10-22)
- Context: The P15 report puts alternative costs at 0.082 of unread weight (Overload, Evoke, Dash, Blitz, Bestow, Spectacle, Madness, Miracle: 355 cards) and casting from or returning to other zones at 0.055 (Foretell, Plot, Suspend, Escape, Unearth, Encore, Disturb, Rebound: 418 cards).
- Decision: Generalise the alternative cost of D-101 (`CardFace.alternativeCosts` with `free`) to a list of named alternatives, each an `AlternativeCost { kind, cost?, condition?, effectChanges? }`: `overload` (cost; every "target" becomes "each", CR 702.96: a transformed spell text, not a second spell), `evoke` (cost; sacrifice trigger on entering if evoked, CR 702.74), `dash` (cost; haste; return to hand at end step, CR 702.109), `bestow` (cost; the permanent becomes an Aura as it enters, CR 702.103: its own slice because of the Aura/creature switch), `madness` and `miracle` (cast as a triggered window: later), `spectacle` (cost if an opponent lost life this turn, CR 702.137), `escape` (cast from the graveyard exiling other cards, CR 702.138), `unearth` and `encore` (activated from the graveyard, CR 702.84, 702.141), `foretell` and `plot` (exile then cast later, CR 702.143, 702.170), `suspend` (time counters, CR 702.62), `rebound` (702.88). Each is its own tested step in the order of card count: overload, evoke, dash, escape, unearth, spectacle first; the others as the corpus asks. The casting stage `alternative` already exists for flashback and free (D-079, D-101); the choice among alternatives is made at the first step of casting (CR 601.2b). `ENGINE_VERSION` bumps with each step.
- Alternatives: One slice for all: rejected, each has separate rules and hidden-information needs (foretell and plot exile face down).
- Consequences: Each step is small and independently shippable, with the web showing a cast option per alternative and badges for the zone and the counters.

## D-120: Details of keyword batch 2 that D-116 left open (2026-10-22)
- Context: building D-116 raised questions its text did not answer: how the pay-options question is shaped and what it may refuse, how a may-pay trigger (Extort) is written, how Cascade casts a card in the middle of a resolution and what it reports, how Battle cry, Mentor and Evolve read the other creatures, how regeneration is kept, and what the AI does with each.
- Decision: (1) Pay options. The decision is `choosePayOptions { source, mechanism: 'convoke' | 'improvise' | 'delve', cost, candidates, colors?, maxUsable, suggested, choices }` (D-116 said "a `choosePermanent` / `chooseCards` question"; one kind with a `mechanism` field keeps the three keywords in one place and lets the AI treat them alike), answered by `Action` `choosePayOptions { objects }` (empty pays everything in mana). They are asked in the order convoke, improvise, delve, each only when at least one candidate could pay a mana of what is left of the cost (CR 601.2f-h, 702.51a, 702.126a, 702.66a). The cost is read as slots: numbers are generic, a colored symbol, a hybrid of two colors, the colored half of {2/W} and {C/W} and the colored part of {W/P} are colored slots; {C} and {S} are not paid this way and stay. A creature pays a colored slot of one of its colors or any generic slot; artifacts and cards pay generic only. The engine works out which mana each pays, colors first (`remainders`, the first that leaves the rest payable). `suggested` is the planner's minimal set (lands first, then creatures, then artifacts) and `choices` lists payable sets near it; the engine refuses an answer whose remainder cannot be paid, so there is no answer that strands a cast (a deliberate difference from "accept any set that pays for a mana each"). `cancel` rewinds the whole cast (CR 733). Castability uses the same exact planner with the candidates added as virtual `PaymentSource`s with `genericOnly` (a creature that can also tap for mana counts once). Several instances of one keyword are redundant (CR 702.51d, 702.126c, 702.66c). The costs that reductions and increases leave are the ones paid for, as CR 702.51b says. Casting stage `'payOptions'`; events `tapped` and `moved` as usual (no new event); `payMana.purpose` unchanged. (2) May-pay. Extort is `castSpell { stackKind: 'spell' } by you` with the effect `mayPay { cost, effect }`: a new effect that reuses the `unlessPays` machinery (D-111) with the question purpose `'mayPay'`, `ifPaid` run on payment; the `mayPay` mana payment is `payMana.purpose: 'mayPay'`. `Amount` `lifeLostThisWay` is the life lost by the `loseLife` effects earlier in the same resolution (`ResolutionContext.lifeLost`); it counts the life actually lost (CR 702.101a: "the total life lost this way"), zero when prevented. The cost is `{W/B}`, paid with either color. Several extort instances trigger separately (CR 702.101b); each is its own question. The extort trigger is grouped as a source-free trigger for the stack order (`SOURCE_FREE_JSON`). (3) Triggers. `castSpell` gets `self: true`: the trigger is found on the spell itself as it is cast (it functions on the stack, CR 603.3b, 702.85a). `blocks` and `becomesBlocked` are found in the `blockersDeclared` event; a creature blocked by several blockers triggers once (CR 702.45b, 509.3g). Filters `attacking` (an attacking creature now) and `powerLessThanSource` (power below the power of the source of the ability, read as the trigger goes on the stack and again on resolution, CR 608.2b); both are refused in statics. Condition `subjectGreaterPt` (power or toughness of the entering creature greater than the source's, intervening if, CR 603.4, 702.100a) is read as the trigger is found and on resolution, with the entering creature's last-known values when it has left (CR 113.7a). Battle cry's set is read as it resolves and fixed (CR 611.2c). (4) Cascade. The effect `cascade` is an instruction in three stages (`start`, `ask`, `bottom`). The free cast happens during resolution (CR 608.2g): the steps of CR 601.2a-i, the spell goes on the stack above the cascade ability, which goes on resolving first (no priority between), `StackData.byEffect` marks it (so the invariant "cast without paying its mana cost has such an alternative cost" holds, CR 118.9). Only the front face of a card is cast (a modal double-faced or split card is cast as its front face; split cards and the other faces are listed in `docs/ROADMAP.md`). The question is asked only when the card could be cast (a legal target for each target, additional costs payable). "Less than" compares the card's mana value with the spell's, an X counting as announced on the stack and as 0 in the library (CR 202.3e); a card cast this way has X = 0 (CR 107.3b). The exiled cards that were not cast go to the bottom in a random order from the seeded `shuffle`; the order is not reported, only `cardsBottomed { seat, count }` (nobody sees it, CR 701.24 style); a commander (CR 903.9b) is offered the command zone first, as an ordinary `move`. Hidden information: the cards exiled are public (CR 400.2), the library order is not. (5) Regeneration. A shield is a `ContinuousEffect` with change `{ kind: 'regenerate' }` for one permanent, until end of turn, one per resolution (CR 701.19a); the `destroy` effect and the lethal damage and deathtouch state-based actions (CR 704.5g, 704.5h) apply it: damage removed, the permanent tapped, removed from combat, a `regenerated` event, shield used up. `destroy { cantBeRegenerated: true }` leaves the shield in place (CR 701.19c); sacrifice, 0 toughness, the legend rule and exile are not replaced. `ObjectView.regenerationShields` shows how many a permanent has. Casting the shield spell is not regenerating. (6) Skulk is read by the blocker check (`evades`), CR 702.118a: a creature with greater power can't block it; it can be granted. Affinity is `costReduction { spells: this, amount: countOf { filter ∧ controller: you } }` (D-101), expanded from the keyword in `derive-keywords.ts` and read by `reductionFor` through `expandKeywords`; it never goes below the colored part (CR 601.2f, 702.41a). (7) AI. `RandomLegalAgent` picks from `choices` (and a crafted decision test). `CasualAgent` answers `choosePayOptions` by starting from `suggested` and swapping in resources it values less (equivalent colors; a creature that makes mana or a mana artifact is never swapped in; attackers stay untapped on its own turn; lands, instants and sorceries in the graveyard are exiled before creatures and other permanents, which recursion could bring back), activates a regenerate ability first when a creature of its own would die (lethal damage or deathtouch in combat, a destroy on the stack) and it can afford it, pays extort when it has mana to spare after its plans, and answers cascade yes. `ENGINE_VERSION` 21.
- Alternatives: Separate `choosePermanent` and `chooseCards` questions (D-116 text): rejected, see (1). Accepting any answer and failing at payment: rejected, a cast could not be taken back without losing the answer and the planner already knows what is payable. Reporting the bottom order of cascade: rejected, it is hidden. A `castFree` instruction run outside the resolution (CR 608.2g says during): rejected. Reading Battle cry as a static ability: rejected, it is a trigger (CR 702.91a).
- Consequences: The web needs the new decision kind `choosePayOptions` in every `DecisionHandlers` record and in the action builder, the new `Action` kind, the events `regenerated` and `cardsBottomed`, the `confirmOptional` purposes `'mayPay'` and `'cascade'`, the `payMana` purpose `'mayPay'`, the casting stage `'payOptions'`, wording for the new keyword, trigger (`blocks`, `becomesBlocked`, `castSpell` with `self`), effect (`regenerate`, `mayPay`, `cascade`) and amount (`lifeLostThisWay`) kinds, and `ObjectView.regenerationShields`. Not built (`docs/ROADMAP.md`): Storm (D-118), Cumulative upkeep (D-119), Madness, Unearth, Ninjutsu and Morph (D-117), convoke for {C} and {S}, a hybrid choice in delve and improvise beyond generic mana, cascade of a split or double-faced card by a face other than the front, "can't be regenerated" as a static ability or a player-wide effect, and Bushido granted after blockers are declared (the trigger is found at the declaration only).

## D-121: Details of the named alternative costs that D-117 left open: Overload, Evoke and Dash (2026-10-23)
- Context: D-117 named the alternatives and their order but left open how the list is represented, how Overload rewrites a spell, where the Evoke and Dash abilities live (Dash needs a delayed triggered ability and the engine had none), the shape of the cast options and of the view, and what the AI chooses. `ENGINE_VERSION` 22.
- Decision: (1) Representation. `CardFace.alternativeCosts` is a list with at most one alternative of each kind: `AlternativeCost = { kind: 'free', condition? } | { kind: 'overload' | 'evoke' | 'dash', cost: Cost[], condition? }`. D-117 wrote `{ kind, cost?, condition?, effectChanges? }`; `effectChanges` is dropped because the CR fixes what each keyword changes, so the engine derives it from the kind (Overload in `ast/overload.ts`, Evoke and Dash in `rules/derive-alt.ts`, `rules/stack.ts`) and the card data cannot contradict the rules; `cost` is required for a named kind and is mana only, with no {X} (`validateCard` refuses anything else with a message, CR 107.3b: X would be announced for a cost that has none). The kinds are one type, `CastAlternativeKind = 'flashback' | 'free' | 'overload' | 'evoke' | 'dash'`, used by the `castSpell` action's `alternative`, the `spellCast` event, `SUPPORTED_FEATURES.castAlternatives` and a new `FeatureRef` dimension `castAlternative:<kind>` (so a parser lowering declares `needs: ['castAlternative:overload']`). The `condition` field of D-101 is read for the named kinds too (the card as source, the caster as controller). A face may list several kinds (CR 118.9a is per spell, not per card). (2) The choice. It is made with the first casting step: one `castSpell { object, alternative }` option for each alternative whose whole cost (the alternative, commander tax, additional costs, minus reductions) can be paid, listed after the ordinary cast and the `free` option (`alternativeCastObjects`, the same `canCast`); the card is cast from the zones it could be cast from anyway, so an alternative from a graveyard, exile (but an Adventure card) or library is refused. The spell on the stack carries it as `StackData.alt`; `spellCast.alternative`, `ObjectView.alternative` (a spell on the stack, and a permanent that entered from an evoked or dashed spell) and `ObjectView.alternativeCosts: { kind, cost }[]` for a card in a hand or the command zone (each named alternative's cost now, after tax and reductions, like `castCost`). `checkInvariants` checks `alt` (a spell on the stack, one alternative at most, listed on the face; a permanent only on the battlefield). (3) Overload (CR 702.96). The text change is made by the engine from the face's spell text (`overloadedText`): every `{ kind: 'target', id }` that is an effect's `objects` or `to` selector becomes `{ kind: 'each', filter }` with the filter of its slot on the battlefield, and the slots go. It is the same spell, not a second one (CR 702.96c): `targetSpecsOf` returns no slots for it and `resolveTop` runs the changed text, so no targets decision, no `becameTarget` (Ward does not trigger) and no fizzling; `each` does not look at hexproof, shroud or protection (CR 702.96b, 702.11b). It is refused (the card is unsupported, with a reason) for a modal spell, a player or "any target" slot, a slot in a zone other than the battlefield or on the stack, a `target` read anywhere but as an effect's selector (an amount `powerOf` a target, the `owner` of cards in "target player's graveyard"), a spell with no target, and a card that is not an instant or sorcery. (4) Evoke (CR 702.74a). A permanent that entered from an evoked spell has `GameObject.alt = 'evoke'` (set in `moveObject`; a new object after any zone change has none, CR 400.7) and `derive` gives it, appended after its printed abilities and removable by "loses all abilities", the triggered ability `entersBattlefield this: sacrifice this`. There is no intervening "if": the ability exists only for an evoked permanent. It is found, ordered, stacked and resolved by the ordinary trigger code, so it uses the stack, can be responded to, is independent of its permanent once on the stack, and is ordered by its controller with the creature's other enters triggers (`orderTriggers`). "Sacrifice this" needs the same controller (CR 701.21a), so a creature whose control changed before the trigger resolves is not sacrificed (CR 702.74a says "its controller sacrifices it"; `docs/ROADMAP.md`). (5) Dash (CR 702.109a). A dashed permanent has `alt = 'dash'`, and `derive` gives it a keyword ability `haste` (so it has haste as long as the cost was paid and loses it with its abilities). The return is a delayed triggered ability, the first of the engine: `GameState.delayedTriggers: { source, controller, ability }[]`, `DelayedTrigger` in `state/types.ts`. A resolving dash spell adds `{ source: the permanent, controller: the spell's controller, ability: endStep(each) -> moveToZone this to hand }` (`DASH_RETURN_ABILITY`, CR 603.7d); `collectTriggers` also scans the list (`findDelayedTriggers`), makes a `PendingTrigger` with `abilityIndex: -1` (it is among no object's abilities) the first time its event occurs and removes it, so it triggers once, at the first end step after it was created. The ability names the permanent by object id, so a creature that left and came back is a new object and is not returned (CR 603.7c), and it is the spell's ability, not the permanent's, so it still returns a creature that lost its abilities (CR 603.7e). When the permanent is gone the trigger still triggers (CR 603.7) and does nothing. It returns the creature to its owner's hand whoever controls it, a commander through the usual command-zone choice (CR 903.9b). (6) The AI (`casual-alt-costs.ts`). `RandomLegalAgent` needs nothing. `CasualAgent` chooses among the options of one card: Overload when the text names only the opponent's objects (`you don't control`, `an opponent controls`) and three or more are on the table (one when the ordinary cast has no target); Evoke only when the ordinary cast cannot be paid and the card says it enters (and a "target creature" has an opposing creature); Dash when the ordinary cast cannot be paid or, in the first main phase of its turn, when nothing untapped can block and the creature has power. (7) The versions: `ENGINE_VERSION` 22; the test cards are SYNTHETIC (`fixtures/synthetic-alt-costs.ts`).
- Alternatives: Keep `effectChanges` as data: rejected, see (1). Store the rewritten Overload text on the face: rejected, the parser would have to emit every overload card twice and the two could disagree. Make Evoke's and Dash's abilities parser output (`keyword` abilities with a cost): rejected, the cost is an alternative cost chosen as the spell is cast and the abilities are fixed by the CR, so the engine owns them. Dash's return as an ability of the permanent (`at the beginning of each end step, if its dash cost was paid`): rejected, it would stop when the permanent loses its abilities and would be controlled by whoever controls the permanent now (CR 603.7d, 603.7e). Skipping the dash trigger when the permanent is gone: rejected, the rules say it triggers (CR 603.7); the cost is one empty trigger on the stack. One option per card with a follow-up "which cost?" question: rejected, the engine would then list a cast it cannot finish (the choice is part of the action, as for flashback and free).
- Consequences: The web shows one cast button for each option of a card (a hand card with `alternativeCosts`: "Overload {3}{R}{R}", "Evoke {1}{U}", "Dash {1}{R}"), sends the option's `alternative` back unchanged (`castAction` already copies it), words `spellCast.alternative` ("You cast X for its overload cost" and so on), badges `ObjectView.alternative` on the stack ("overloaded", "evoked") and on the permanent ("evoked: sacrificed when it enters", "dashed: returns at end of turn"), words an ability on the stack whose source is a dashed permanent ("Return X to its owner's hand") and tolerates `abilityTriggered.abilityIndex` of -1. The parser lowers `Overload {M}`, `Evoke {M}` and `Dash {M}` (a keyword line, reminder text dropped) to `alternativeCosts` entries (`docs/MECHANICS.md`, "Named alternative costs"). Not built (`docs/ROADMAP.md`): Evoke and the other alternative costs whose cost is not mana ("Evoke—Exile a white card from your hand"), Overload on modal text, a Dash creature whose control changed before the end step (it returns to its owner, which is right, but no test steers it), delayed triggers other than Dash's, Blitz, Bestow, Spectacle and the other D-117 steps.

## D-123: How parser stage P23 reads the second slice of named alternative costs (2026-10-23)
- Context: D-124 built Spectacle, Escape and Unearth in the engine and said what the parser must produce; the grammar had to choose the exact wordings it reads and what it does with the sentence "sacrifice it unless it escaped", which is not an "if" in the text but is an intervening "if" in the engine.
- Decision: (1) `Spectacle {M}` and `Unearth {M}` are lines of their own with a plain mana cost, like the P22 keywords; Spectacle is an `alternativeCosts` entry and Unearth is the keyword `unearth` (the engine expands it). (2) `Escape—{M}, Exile N other cards from your graveyard.` is read with the number as a word from one to nine, the line ending with a period (as the real line does); the singular "one other card" is read although no real line with a count of one is in the repository (it is the only grammatical form of the count, and `validateCard` still decides); a digit, "ten" and every other component of the cost stay unread. (3) "Unless it escaped" is the rule `condition.unless-escaped`, read only with the pronoun "it" after one clause of a triggered ability's body (the sentence option `unless`, shared with "unless that player pays"). It produces `not escaped` on the clause, and `lowerTriggered` lifts it to the ability's `interveningIf` (D-124: the ability does not trigger for a permanent that escaped), only when it is the whole body of an enters trigger of the permanent and the one clause is a sacrifice that is not optional; every other place is refused. (4) `effect.sacrifice` reads "sacrifice it"; the lowering sacrifices only when the binding pass bound "it" to `~` (an enters trigger of `~`), so "it" bound to a target or to another object is not lowered (CR 701.21a). (5) An escape trigger on a card whose Escape line was not read blames that line alone (`isRedundant`), as for Overload in D-121. (6) "Escapes with" (CR 702.138c), "escapes with [ability]" and Underworld Breach stay unread: the repository holds no real line of the first (the shapes file has only the four lines above) and the engine does not build the others.
- Alternatives: Read "unless it escaped" after any effect and lift it for any trigger: rejected, a lifted "draw a card unless it escaped" would not trigger at all for an escaped permanent, which is not what the text says, and no real card writes it. Read "if it escaped" and "~ escaped": rejected, no real wording, and `rules/replacement/unless.ts` reads any condition rule after "unless", so a general rule would widen other lines. Lower "sacrifice it unless it escaped" by a clause condition of the engine (`conditional` effect): rejected, D-124 settled on the intervening "if" and the engine has no condition on a sacrifice that reads the permanent's history other than `escaped`. Read digits for the count: rejected, the real line writes a word.
- Consequences: The four shapes (Spectacle 11 cards, Escape 30, Unearth 55, the sacrifice line 3; the three cards that have two of them are counted twice) are read; a card is supported only when its other lines are read too. `PARSER_VERSION` 28. Any later form of the escape sentence ("escapes with") needs the real wording first.

## D-124: Details of the named alternative costs that D-117 left open: Spectacle, Escape and Unearth (2026-10-23)
- Context: D-121 built Overload, Evoke and Dash and refused every alternative cast from a graveyard. Spectacle needs a record of life lost this turn the engine did not keep; Escape is the first alternative cost with a part that is not mana (exiling other cards, chosen by the caster) and the first named alternative cast from the graveyard; Unearth is an activated ability that works from the graveyard, which no ability did. `ENGINE_VERSION` 23 for the three.
- Decision: (1) Spectacle (CR 702.137a). `AlternativeCost` `{ kind: 'spectacle', cost, condition? }` (mana only, no X, on a card that is not a land). The condition "if an opponent lost life this turn" is the engine's, not data (as in D-121(1)): `opponentLostLifeThisTurn` (`rules/legality.ts`) is read in `alternativeCostAllowed`, that is at the first casting step (CR 601.2b), by the option list and by `canCast`, for the player casting: some opponent still in the game (`opponentsOf`) has `lifeLostThisTurn` above 0; life lost by the caster, or by a player who left the game, does not count. The record is `SeatState.lifeLostThisTurn`, one number for each player, reset for every seat as each turn begins (`startTurn`: "this turn" is the game turn, so life lost in an opponent's turn counts for a spell cast then), written only by `loseLifeBy` (`state/ops.ts`): every reduction of a life total goes through it, which is combat and other damage (`rules/damage.ts`; damage that is prevented or turned into poison is not life lost), `loseLife` effects, life paid for a spell or ability cost, a mana ability, Ward and "unless pays", and a shock land (CR 119.3, 119.4: paying life is losing it). Gaining life is not recorded. `SeatView.lifeLostThisTurn` shows it. The record is plain state, so replay and `stateHash` cover it. (2) Escape (CR 702.138a). `AlternativeCost` `{ kind: 'escape', cost, exile }`: `cost` is mana only (no X) and `exile` the number (at least 1) of OTHER cards of the caster's graveyard exiled as part of the cost; one entry per face, on the front face, on a card that is not a land and has no Delve (both would exile the same cards; `validateCard` refuses the pair). `castZone` accepts the owner's graveyard for `escape` (D-121 allowed it for flashback alone; the other named alternatives are still cast from the hand or the command zone only), `escapeObjects` lists one `castSpell { object, alternative: 'escape' }` option for each card in the graveyard whose `canCast` holds, after flashback; the option exists only when the escape mana, commander tax (none: CR 903.8 taxes the command zone only, and a commander cast from the graveyard is not counted as cast from it), additional costs and `exile` other cards can all be paid (`SpellCost.exile`, `canPaySpellCost`, `exilable` leaves out the card itself). The exile is part of the cost: after the mana, the sacrifice and the discard of the cast (`rules/cast-additional.ts`, `rules/exile-cost.ts`, casting stage `'exile'`, CR 601.2h): with exactly `exile` other cards in the graveyard they are exiled without a question, otherwise the caster is asked `ChooseCardsDecision` `{ purpose: 'exile', zone: 'graveyard', legal, min: n, max: n, reveal: true, forCost: true }` (the purposes `'search' | 'discard' | 'putOnTop'` and the zones `'library' | 'hand'` were the only ones), answered with the `chooseCards` action and refused unless exactly `n` distinct cards of `legal` (the same `validCardsChoice` as a discard); `cancel` rewinds the whole cast (CR 733) and gives the cards back. `choosePayOptions` (D-120) was considered and rejected: it is for optional resources that pay a share of the mana (Convoke, Improvise, Delve), with a remainder planner and a count the caster picks, and an escape cost is exactly `n` cards with no effect on the mana. The cards exiled are public (`zoneChanged` events, no new event). The spell is ordinary otherwise: it goes to the graveyard when it resolves or is countered (not exiled: that is flashback), so a card in the graveyard again can escape again. The permanent that spell becomes has `GameObject.alt = 'escape'` (`PermanentAlternativeKind` now holds `'unearth'` too), the new object's own (CR 400.7), which `ObjectView.alternative` shows. Two things read it: the Condition `{ kind: 'escaped' }` (CR 702.138b: the resolving spell, the permanent, or its last-known information; "sacrifice it unless it escaped" is a triggered ability with `interveningIf: not escaped`) and `entersWithCounters { ifEscaped: true }` ("This creature escapes with a +1/+1 counter on it", CR 702.138c), a replacement applied as the permanent enters through the same path as "enters with counters" (D-100, `rules/enters.ts`, `rules/zones.ts`), so nothing goes on the stack. Both are refused by `validateCard` on a face with no escape cost (CR 702.138b: nothing could have escaped). Not built: "escapes with [ability]" (CR 702.138d), the triggered ability linked to "enters this way" (CR 702.138c), and Underworld Breach (a static grant of escape to the cards of a graveyard with a cost computed from their mana cost). (3) Unearth (CR 702.84a). `Keyword` `{ kind: 'unearth', cost }` (mana only, no X; on a permanent card, one per face), expanded by `derive` (`rules/derive-keywords.ts`) into `{ kind: 'activated', cost, effect: { kind: 'unearth' }, timing: 'sorcery', functionsIn: 'graveyard' }`: `functionsIn` is widened from `'battlefield' | 'hand'` to include `'graveyard'` (no new type: it is the field Cycling already uses), `activationRefusal` already compares the zone, `activatableAbilities` adds the seat's graveyard cards that have a printed unearth keyword (the other cards of a graveyard are not derived at every priority), and `validateCard` gives an ability from the graveyard the restrictions of one from the hand (no tap, sacrifice, counters). The effect `unearth` is valid only in such an ability (`Scope.fromGraveyard`); it runs a `move` instruction of the source card to the battlefield under its controller's control with the new field `alt: 'unearth'` (`MoveRequest.alt`), and does nothing if the source is no longer the same object in a graveyard (every zone change makes a new object, CR 400.7, so a card exiled in response is simply not there). The ability is not a spell: it uses the stack as any activated ability (`abilityActivated` with the card as the source, no `spellCast`, nothing to counter with Counterspell). Resolving it makes the permanent a new object with `GameObject.alt = 'unearth'`, from which three things follow: `derive` gives it the keyword haste (as Dash does, `rules/derive-alt.ts`: a later "loses all abilities" takes it away, ROADMAP); `moveObject` exiles it instead of putting it anywhere else when it would leave the battlefield, whatever the cause and whether or not it still has abilities (CR 614.6; the replacement belongs to the object, as Flashback's belongs to the spell; it runs before the commander replacement, and a commander so exiled is then offered the command zone by CR 903.9a, as for any commander in exile), so it never dies and its "when this dies" does not trigger; and the move instruction creates the delayed triggered ability `UNEARTH_EXILE_ABILITY` (`endStep` of each player: `exile this`, the second use of `GameState.delayedTriggers` after Dash, CR 603.7, 603.7c), which belongs to the activator (CR 603.7d) and is independent of the permanent's abilities (CR 603.7e). (4) The AI. `RandomLegalAgent` needs nothing. `CasualAgent`: Spectacle is chosen whenever the engine offers it (it only replaces the mana cost); Escape is a play of its own after the hand spells and flashback, the most valuable worthwhile card by printed mana value, and `chooseEscapeExile` answers the exile question with the cards it wants least (lands, instants and sorceries, then permanents by mana value; a card with flashback, escape or unearth in its text is kept while another will do); Unearth (`wantsUnearth`) is activated in the first main phase of its own turn for a creature with power that would attack safely (no untapped opposing creature with power at least its toughness) or for the win. (5) The versions and tests: `ENGINE_VERSION` 23; the test cards are SYNTHETIC (`fixtures/synthetic-alt-costs.ts`); `scenario-xx-spectacle.test.ts`, `scenario-xx-escape.test.ts`, `scenario-xx-unearth.test.ts`; the `altCosts` soak holds the new cards.
- Alternatives: Compute "an opponent lost life this turn" from the event history: rejected, the state keeps no history, and a per-turn number in the state is what replay and the hash already cover. Keep the Spectacle condition as card data: rejected, the CR fixes it (D-121(1)). Count the card with escape itself among the cards it may exile: rejected, "other" (CR 702.138a) and the card is on the stack when the cost is paid. A `choosePayOptions` for the escape exile: see (2). Exile the escape cards before the mana: rejected, the cost is paid in any order (CR 601.2h) and the existing sacrifice and discard are after the mana, so a cancel and the planner for the mana stay as they are. Make unearth a spell cast from the graveyard (`alternative: 'unearth'`): rejected, CR 702.84a says it is an activated ability; a spell would be counterable and trigger "whenever you cast". Give the haste, the exile at the end step and the replacement as three effects of the ability (the card's own continuous effects): rejected, the engine has no effect that creates a delayed trigger or a replacement for one object, and building those general nodes for one keyword is a separate slice; `GameObject.alt` is the pattern D-121 set. Remember the unearth by a counter-like flag copied by copy effects: rejected, the status is not a copiable value (CR 707.2), so a copy of an unearthed creature was not unearthed.
- Consequences: The web shows, for a card in the graveyard with `ObjectView.alternativeCosts` of kind `escape`, a cast button that says the cost and the number of cards (`exile` is the count), sends `castSpell { object, alternative: 'escape' }`, answers the `chooseCards` question with `purpose: 'exile'` and `zone: 'graveyard'` (the cards to choose from are in the viewer's graveyard; the prompt text is in the decision), tolerates `waitingOn.purpose: 'exile'` for the other seat, words `spellCast.alternative` `'spectacle'` and `'escape'` (as for the other named alternatives), badges `ObjectView.alternative` of `'spectacle'` and `'escape'` on the spell, `'escape'` and `'unearth'` on the permanent, shows an `activate` option for a card in the graveyard (`ObjectView.activated` has it) with wording for the new effect node `unearth`, and a delayed trigger of unearth on the stack (an `exile` of `this` at each end step, `abilityIndex` -1), and may show `SeatView.lifeLostThisTurn`. The parser lowers `Spectacle {M}` and `Escape—{M}, Exile N other cards from your graveyard.` to `alternativeCosts` entries, `Unearth {M}` to the keyword, and "unless it escaped" and "escapes with" as above (`docs/MECHANICS.md`, "Named alternative costs: Spectacle, Escape, Unearth"). Not built (`docs/ROADMAP.md`): a non-mana cost in any of the three, two unearth instances on a card, a grant of unearth or escape by another card, "escapes with [ability]", Blitz and Encore (which would reuse the delayed exile), and the other D-117 steps.

## D-125: Play rules: additional land drops, looking at the top card, the cost of attacking and the optional untap (2026-10-26)
- Context: four static abilities of the backlog change what a player may do in a turn rather than what a card does: "You may play an additional land on each of your turns" (17 cards), "You may look at the top card of your library any time" (44), "Creatures can't attack you unless their controller pays {M} for each creature they control that's attacking you" (Propaganda, Ghostly Prison, Windborn Muse, Koskun Falls; with the planeswalker form Norn's Annex, Baird, Archon of Absolution, Sphere of Safety), and "You may choose not to untap ~ during your untap step" (44). Each needed a place in the engine: the land limit was a number in the turn state, the library was never in a view, a declaration of attackers was a free choice, and the untap step asked nothing. `ENGINE_VERSION` 24 for the four.
- Decision: (1) Additional land drops (CR 305.2). `StaticEffect` `{ kind: 'additionalLandDrops', count, eachPlayer? }`; `landPlaysAllowed(state, seat)` (`rules/statics.ts`) is 1, plus what the effects of this turn add for the active player (`turn.extraLandDrops`), plus `count` for each battlefield permanent of the seat with the ability (any permanent when `eachPlayer`), read from the derived abilities so a permanent that lost its abilities adds nothing and the limit follows the board. `canPlayLand` compares the lands played with it (CR 305.2a); `SeatView.landPlaysAllowed` shows it. The CasualAgent casts a permanent that grants a drop first while a land waits in the hand. (2) Looking at the top card (CR 401.5). `StaticEffect` `{ kind: 'lookAtTopOfLibrary' }`; `topCardVisibleTo` (`rules/statics.ts`) says whether the seat controls a battlefield permanent with it, and `SeatView.libraryTop?: ObjectView` carries the top card in the view of that seat and in no other view. Nothing is stored, emitted or logged: it is a view, so the state, the events, the action log and every hash are as before, and replay is unchanged. While a spell is being cast or an ability activated (`state.casting` is set) the top card is shown only if it is the card that was on top when the transaction began (`casting.snapshot`): a new top card stays hidden until the spell is cast (CR 401.5). "Play with the top card of your library revealed" is a different ability and is not built; the other player never learns the card, so the AI's hidden-information audit (`hidden-info.test.ts`) allows exactly this one exception, for the viewer's own seat and with a permanent that says so. The CasualAgent (`knownTopCard`) does not typecycle for a land it knows it will draw. (3) The cost of attacking (CR 508.1d, 508.1h). `StaticEffect` `{ kind: 'attackTax', cost: Cost[], planeswalkers?: true }` (mana only, at least one symbol, no {X}; Phyrexian and hybrid symbols are the planner's and work).
