The tax is on attacking its controller and, with `planeswalkers`, the planeswalkers that controller controls (a battle is never taxed); several add up for one target and each attacker pays the whole of it (`rules/attack-tax.ts`). The declaration stays the single `declareAttackers` answer. When the chosen attackers are taxed, the engine does not declare them: it validates the whole declaration (`validateAttacks`: legal attackers and requirements as before, and the cost payable with the attackers tapped, CR 508.1f, 508.1h, by the same planner as every payment, so a creature that attacks cannot tap for its own tax unless it has vigilance), then makes `payMana` the pending decision with `purpose: 'attackTax'`, `attacks` (the declaration), `totalCost` and `source` the first taxing permanent. `payAuto` or `payManual` taps the attackers, pays, and declares them (events in that order: `tapped`, the payment, `attackersDeclared`), then priority; `cancel` takes the declaration back and asks `declareAttackers` again (CR 733); a payment that does not cover the cost is refused and the question stays. Nothing about the state is kept between the two answers except the pending decision itself, so replay and hashes need nothing new. A declaration that cannot be paid is invalid, so the player declares fewer attackers; a player is never required to pay (CR 508.1d), so a creature that attacks each combat if able is required only when one of its targets is not taxed (`mustAttack` leaves the others out) and is declared at that target. `DeclareAttackersDecision.attackCosts?` (only when a target is taxed) lists, for each taxed target, `cost` (the symbols one attacker pays) and `affordable` (the most attackers that can be paid for, counted with every non-vigilance candidate already tapped, so it is a floor: a declaration within it is always accepted). `legalActionsForDecision` has only the decision, so the list is filtered by `affordable` (a taxed target gets "the first N that can be paid for" in place of "everyone"). The AI: the CasualAgent (`payForAttacks`) attacks the taxed target with as many of the creatures it wants to send as it can pay for, strongest first, and only those whose power is at least the mana they cost (or all, when lethal); the others go to a planeswalker that costs nothing or stay home; the RandomLegalAgent trims its random declaration to the budget after its draws (`withinAttackBudget`, so games without a tax are unchanged). (4) The optional untap (CR 502.3). `StaticEffect` `{ kind: 'optionalUntap' }`, on the permanent itself. In the untap step the permanents of the active player untap as before, except the tapped ones whose derived abilities have it and that do not also have `doesntUntap`: for those the controller is asked once, a `choosePermanent` decision with `purpose: 'untap'`, `legal` those permanents, `min` 0, `max` `legal.length`, `source` the first of them (as for the legend rule: no spell or ability is involved). The answer is an ordinary `choosePermanents` action in the log and names the permanents that untap; the rest stay tapped and are asked again next turn. With nothing to ask, no decision exists, so every game without the ability is unchanged. No player receives priority in the untap step (CR 502.4): the step ends when the question is answered. The AI untaps everything (`'untap'` answers `legal`); the random agent answers a random subset.
- Alternatives: (1) A fixed `additionalLandDrops` number in the turn state for every source: rejected, a permanent that leaves must lower the limit. (2) Putting the top card in the state or in an event (a `libraryTopLookedAt` event): rejected, the log and the events are visible to both seats and the replay would carry a secret; a view is the engine's existing way to show something to one seat. A per-seat revealed flag: rejected, nothing is revealed (CR 401.5 says "look at" and "revealed" are different). Showing the new top card during a cast: rejected, CR 401.5 forbids it. (3) A separate `declareAttackersPay` action or a second decision kind for the payment: rejected, `payMana` already carries the payment, the manual-tap answer and `cancel`, and the web already renders it; a `declareAttackers` action that carries its payment would have to name the sources before the engine knows the cost. Declaring the attackers first and paying with a rewind on cancel (as a spell is): rejected, it needs the snapshot machinery of casting for no gain, since nothing changes until the payment is made and the attackers can be tapped in a copy of the state to plan it. Asking one question per attacker: rejected, CR 508.1h fixes the total once the attackers are chosen. Computing `affordable` exactly: rejected, it depends on which creatures attack; the floor is honest and the engine checks the exact cost. (4) One `confirmOptional` per permanent: rejected, the untap step would have to resume once per permanent and the log would hold a question for each; one list is one decision and the web shows it as a checklist. Answering with the permanents to leave tapped: rejected, "untap" is what the rules say happens and the list the AI gives most often is the whole one. A `restriction` value `optionalUntap` beside `doesntUntap`: considered, but a restriction only forbids; this one asks.
- Consequences: The web shows `SeatView.libraryTop` (a card face beside the library count for the viewer only), words `payMana` with `purpose: 'attackTax'` ("Pay {2} for each attacker" with the attackers named from `attacks`, the same mana panel, "Cancel" meaning "choose other attackers"), reads `DeclareAttackersDecision.attackCosts` to tell the player what each taxed target costs and how many creatures the mana covers before the declaration is sent (and may show the error text when it is refused), and words the `choosePermanent` decision with `purpose: 'untap'` as a checklist "Untap these permanents?" with all selected. The parser lowers the four lines as in `docs/MECHANICS.md`. Not built (`docs/ROADMAP.md`): "play with the top card of your library revealed" and the abilities that let a player play or cast cards from the top of the library, taxes with a cost that is not mana (Ghostly Prison is mana; "{X}" where X is a count, Sphere of Safety), a cost to block, a planeswalker tax for battles, "choose not to untap" for an effect that is not the permanent's own static ability, and the lose-abilities interaction of the optional untap (read from derived abilities, like `doesntUntap`, but no test steers an effect that lasts across the untap step).

## D-126: Faster checks: soak counts per D-013, and a verification routine by stage (2026-10-26; partly superseded by D-132)
- Context: A full local `pnpm test` took about 28 minutes and the browser tests about 10, and CI repeated both. Most of the unit-test time is the 28 AI soak files, each playing 100 whole games on every run, five times the 20 per pull request that D-013 (SPEC A13) set; the nightly 500-game run of D-013 was never built. The owner asked for faster development without giving up much quality.
- Decision: (1) A soak test plays `soakGames()` games (`packages/ai/test/soak.ts`): 20 by default, `SOAK_GAMES` overrides it; `pnpm test:soak` plays 100; the `Soak` workflow (`.github/workflows/soak.yml`) plays 500 nightly and on demand, in four shards, and opens an issue on failure. Timeouts scale with the count and never go below the old 100-game ones. The M1 done-when test (`games-100.test.ts`) and the CasualAgent win-rate test keep their fixed counts. (2) The routine (`AGENTS.md`): while working, run the tests of the touched packages and the affected ones (`vitest related`, the package's project), the browser tests of new or changed specs only, and mutation checks only for engine rules, a handful per mechanic; before a pull request, `pnpm format`, `typecheck`, `lint` and the tests of what changed; the full `pnpm test` and `pnpm e2e` are not run locally (amended by the owner on 2026-10-26: CI runs everything on every push, and a failure it finds is fixed on the branch).
- Alternatives: Keep 100 games per run: rejected, it is most of the time and more than D-013 asked. Drop the soaks from the default run: rejected, 20 games still catch the common faults on every run. Rely on CI alone before a pull request: rejected, the owner merges without waiting for CI.
- Consequences: A fault that shows only after many games is found by the nightly run, at most a day later, instead of on the next local run; a fixed seed found that way becomes a scenario test. Run `pnpm test:soak` or the `Soak` workflow before a milestone report.
- Status: Partly superseded by D-132 and D-250: the `Soak` workflow is manual only (no nightly schedule) and the complete suite runs nightly on GitHub (`full.yml`, skipped when `main` has no new commit). The soak counts stand.


## D-127: Upkeep slice: Echo, Cumulative upkeep and the monarch (2026-10-26)
- Context: three mechanics of the backlog that live at the upkeep and the end step: Echo (47 cards, the shape `Echo {M}`), Cumulative upkeep (57 cards, `Cumulative upkeep {M}`, 14 of them blocked by nothing else) and "When ~ enters, you become the monarch." (38 cards). Echo and Cumulative upkeep are triggered abilities of the controller's upkeep that pay with the machinery of "unless pays" (D-108, D-111); the monarch is the first player designation, and its two abilities have no source (CR 725.2). The brief for the slice said CR 724 for the monarch; in the CR of `docs/rules/` the monarch is CR 725 ("The Monarch") and CR 724 is "Ending Turns and Phases", so the code cites CR 725; the monarch has no keyword-action number. `ENGINE_VERSION` 25 for the slice. SYNTHETIC fixtures: `cards/fixtures/synthetic-upkeep.ts`.
- Decision: (1) Echo (CR 702.30a). `Keyword` `{ kind: 'echo', cost: Cost[] }` (mana only, no X; `validateCard` and `isSupported` refuse any other cost with a reason). `derive` (`rules/derive-keywords.ts`, `echoAbility`) expands it, one ability for each instance (CR 702.30a says nothing about several, each is a trigger of its own), into `{ trigger: upkeep of you, interveningIf: cameUnderControlSinceLastUpkeep, effect: unlessPays { player: you, cost, effect: sacrifice this, upkeep: 'echo' } }`. The condition `{ kind: 'cameUnderControlSinceLastUpkeep' }` (CR 603.4: checked as the ability triggers and as it resolves, by the existing intervening-if code) holds when the source is on the battlefield under the control of the ability's controller and its `GameObject.timestamp` (the moment it came under its current controller's control, CR 302.6, set as it enters) is later than `SeatState.previousTurnStartTimestamp`, a new field: the value `turnStartTimestamp` had before the seat's current turn began (set in `startTurn`, 0 before the first). That is "since the beginning of your last upkeep": the upkeep begins right after the turn does and no one can act in between (CR 502.4), so the turn's start stands for the upkeep's and no timestamp is spent on the step. A permanent that came in during an earlier turn of its controller's or after the last upkeep began is due; one that has been there since before the last turn began is not, so it pays once. A source that left the battlefield (a new object after any move, CR 400.7) or whose controller changed fails the condition, so the trigger is removed as it resolves (`fizzled` with reason `interveningIf`) and nobody is asked: the player who bounced it in response does not pay for nothing. The engine has no effect that changes control, so the "changed control" case is covered by placing a permanent under the other seat's control in a scenario (`controller` option): the trigger is the controller's, at the controller's upkeep. The question is the ordinary `unlessPays` one (`confirmOptional` then `payMana`, purpose 'unlessPays'), with a new optional field `upkeep: 'echo'` on both decisions, copied from `unlessPays.upkeep` (which only the expansion sets) through the instruction; declining, backing out of the payment (cancel) or being unable to pay (CR 118.3: nobody is asked) sacrifices the permanent. (2) Cumulative upkeep (CR 702.24a). `Keyword` `{ kind: 'cumulativeUpkeep', cost: Cost[] }` (mana, `payLife` and `discard`, no X: exactly what `unlessPays` can pay; "sacrifice a creature", "put a counter on a creature" and the like are refused with the usual "cost ... is not implemented" reason; the reports list only the mana form, so no share of the others is stated). `derive` expands it into `{ trigger: upkeep of you, effect: cumulativeUpkeep { cost } }`. The effect (`rules/effects.ts`) does nothing unless the source is on the battlefield under the ability's controller ("if this permanent is on the battlefield" is checked as it resolves, not as an intervening "if", so a permanent that left gets no counter and no question), puts an age counter on it (`counterAdded`, counter name `age`), then pushes the same `unlessPays` instruction with the cost repeated once for each age counter now on the permanent (`cost: [cost x N]`, so `manaSymbolsOf`, `lifeOf` and `discardOf` sum it: {1} then {1}{1}, 1 then 2 life, one then two cards) and `effect: sacrifice this`, `upkeep: 'cumulativeUpkeep'`. The whole cost is paid or none of it (CR 702.24a: partial payments are not allowed); a cost that cannot be paid sacrifices without a question. Two instances each count all the age counters there are as they resolve (CR 702.24b: {1}, then {1}{1} with the second). The decision's `cost` is the whole payment (`totalCost` for the mana). (3) The monarch (CR 725). `GameState.monarch: SeatId | null`, public, `null` until an effect names a player (CR 725.1); one at a time (CR 725.3: `becomeMonarch` in `rules/monarch.ts` replaces it). `Effect` `{ kind: 'becomeMonarch', player: PlayerSelector }` (one player: `eachPlayer` and `eachOpponent` are refused, CR 725.3); an enters trigger, a spell or a mana-less effect all use it; nothing happens, and nothing is emitted, for a player who already is the monarch or has left. The designation belongs to the player: it stays when the permanent that gave it leaves (the state is not tied to any object). The event `{ kind: 'monarchChanged', from: SeatId | null, to: SeatId | null }` records every change. `GameView.monarch` shows it to both seats. The two inherent abilities of CR 725.2 are found by `findMonarchTriggers` (called by `collectTriggers`): the beginning of the end step of the active player who is the monarch ("draws a card"), and each combat `damageDealt` of positive amount from a creature (last-known types) to the monarch ("its controller becomes the monarch": `becomeMonarch` of `controllerOf(triggerSubject)`, read from last-known information if the creature is gone). They are pending triggers with no source: `PendingTrigger.source` is `ObjectId | null` and `PendingTrigger.inherent` is `'monarchDraw' | 'monarchSteal'`; `abilityIndex` is -1 as for a delayed trigger. They go on the stack through the same code as every trigger (APNAP, the controller orders them, they can be responded to), as an ability object whose `StackData.source` is null (the engine already read a null source as "the ability itself") and `StackData.inherent` is set; they are controlled by the monarch at the moment they triggered (CR 725.2, an exception to CR 113.8), so a monarch who loses the designation in response still draws and the old monarch still controls a steal trigger. The view shows such an object as "The monarch" with the rule's text (`MONARCH_TEXT`, the CR 725.2 sentences); `TriggerChoice.source` of the ordering decision is null for it (`sourceName` "The monarch"); the `abilityTriggered` event names the stack object as `source` (as the resolution already does). When the monarch leaves the game the active player becomes the monarch in the same step, or, if the active player is the one leaving, the next player in turn order still in the game, or nobody (CR 725.4, `monarchAfterLoss`, run where state-based actions mark a loss and by `concede`). The invariants check the monarch is a seat and, while the game goes on, still in it. (4) AI (`packages/ai/src/casual-costs.ts`, `upkeepAnswer`). A decision with `upkeep` is answered by value: the CasualAgent pays while `permanentValue` of the source (3 plus its mana value, counters, +50 for a commander) minus 2 is at least the price (the mana value of the cost, half a point for each life, one for each card), never when the life part would take it to `PAY_LIFE_ABOVE` or the cards are not ones it is glad to lose (`expendable`); a cumulative upkeep that has grown past the permanent's worth lets it go. The random agent chooses at random as for every confirmation. (5) The soak `packages/ai/test/upkeep-games.test.ts` (20 games per run, D-126) and a deck style 'upkeep'.
- Alternatives: (1) Echo as its own effect (`echoPayment`): rejected, `unlessPays` already is the effect and only needs the marker; the condition is the one new rule. A stored "echo owed" flag on the permanent set when it enters: rejected, it would have to be cleared by every path that pays or loses it and says nothing a timestamp does not (a permanent returned under another player's control gets a fresh timestamp for free, CR 302.6). A new timestamp spent at the upkeep step: rejected, it would shift every timestamp of every game for a rule that needs only the turn's start (CR 502.4). Reading "your last upkeep" as `turnStartTimestamp` of the turn now under way: rejected, that is the turn that began just before this upkeep and would make every permanent that came in earlier "not new". A check on the permanent that it was still the same object at resolution through a stored id: rejected, a zone change already makes a new object (CR 400.7). (2) Cumulative upkeep as a counter-adding effect plus `unlessPays` in a `sequence`: rejected, the cost needs the counter count after the counter is added and `unlessPays` takes a fixed cost; a new effect that scales it is smaller than a general "N times" cost. Refusing every non-mana cost: rejected, "Pay 1 life" and "discard a card" are payments `unlessPays` already runs and tests; refusing what the machinery cannot do (sacrifice, put a counter) is honest. An "each choice made separately" model (CR 702.24a: `{W} or {U}` costs): not built, the cost shapes of the reports are plain mana. (3) A source object for the monarch (an emblem-like object in the command zone): rejected, the engine has no emblems, an object would show up in zones, counts and views, and the CR says the abilities have no source. Immediate resolution of the draw and the steal (no stack): rejected, they are triggered abilities with a window to respond (an instant that changes the monarch, removal of the creature), their controller is fixed when they trigger, and the stack is where the engine already does all of that. A sentinel object id for the source: rejected, every reader of a source would have to know the sentinel; a null the type system makes everyone handle is the honest shape (only the trigger-stack code and two web components needed a change). Making `abilityTriggered.source` nullable: rejected, tests and the web read it as an object id; the ability's own stack object is the source the resolution already uses. The monarch as a per-seat flag: rejected, one player at a time is a single field, and the draw and the steal read it directly. (4) A fixed "always pay" for upkeep payments as for Ward: rejected, an echo cost the agent cannot afford next turn or a cumulative upkeep of 6 on a 2/2 is not worth paying.
- Consequences: The parser lowers `Echo {M}` and `Cumulative upkeep {M}` to the two keywords, and `When ~ enters, you become the monarch.` to an enters trigger with `becomeMonarch` (real lines in `docs/MECHANICS.md`, "Echo, Cumulative upkeep and the monarch"); other monarch wordings ("you become the monarch" as a spell, "Whenever ~ deals combat damage to a player, you become the monarch", "if you're the monarch") need `needs` ids the parser may declare once it reads them; a condition for "if you're the monarch" is not built (`docs/ROADMAP.md`). The web needs: the log line for `monarchChanged` (a minimal one is in this slice), a marker for the monarch on the player strip from `GameView.monarch`, words for `ConfirmOptionalDecision.upkeep` and `PayManaDecision.upkeep` ("Pay {1}{1} to keep X (age counters: 2)" and "Sacrifice X unless you pay"), the "The monarch" stack object (it has no `abilitySource` and no card to hover), and the ordering panel for a `TriggerChoice` whose `source` is null (this slice makes the panel not crash; it shows no hover card). Saved states and logs record `ENGINE_VERSION` (SPEC 17.6 A26); `SeatState` and `GameState` each grew a field, so a state saved by version 24 does not have them.

## D-128: The "cast later" family: delayed triggers from effects, Suspend, Madness and Foretell (2026-10-26)
- Context: four mechanics of the backlog act on a card or an effect at a later time: "You draw a card at the beginning of the next turn's upkeep." (Arcane Denial, 1 card, and its second sentence "Its controller may draw up to two cards at the beginning of the next turn's upkeep."), `Suspend N—{M}` (65 cards), `Madness {M}` (56) and `Foretell {M}` (50). D-117 planned them as steps of the alternative-cost slice ("madness and miracle (cast as a triggered window: later)", "foretell and plot (exile then cast later)", "suspend (time counters)") and D-121 and D-124 built the named alternative costs, `castZone`, the cast from the graveyard and `GameState.delayedTriggers` (Dash and Unearth only). The brief said Madness lets the owner "may exile it instead"; CR 702.35a says the player "exiles it instead of putting it into their graveyard", with no choice, and gives the choice to the cast that follows; the engine follows the CR. The brief also said "play it" for Suspend's last counter; CR 702.62a says "play ... if able" and a card with suspend is never a land here (`validateCard` refuses it), so it is a cast. `ENGINE_VERSION` 26 for the slice. SYNTHETIC fixtures: `cards/fixtures/synthetic-later.ts`.
- Decision: (1) Delayed draw (CR 603.7). A new effect `{ kind: 'delayedTrigger', at: { step: TriggerStep, whose: 'you' | 'each' }, effect }` creates, as the spell or ability resolves, a `DelayedTrigger` `{ source: the spell, controller: its controller as it resolved, ability }` (CR 603.7d, 603.7e) in `GameState.delayedTriggers`, the list Dash and Unearth already used and `findDelayedTriggers` already scans; the ability is `{ trigger: { kind: 'step', step, whose }, effect }`, so "the next turn's upkeep" is `at: { step: 'upkeep', whose: 'each' }` and "your next upkeep" is `whose: 'you'`. It triggers once, at the first matching step that begins after it was created (CR 603.7a: a step already begun does not count; CR 603.7b), goes on the stack like every triggered ability (ordered by its controller, shown under the name of the spell by last-known information, can be responded to) and does what it says whatever became of the spell (CR 603.7c). Dash and Unearth are unchanged (they still push their own constants). What the delayed effect may do is limited by `validateCard` to `draw`, `gainLife` and `loseLife` with a fixed count of at least 1 and the player selectors `you`, `eachPlayer` and `eachOpponent`: nothing in it names an object of the spell (gone by then), a target or an X, and a nested delayed trigger is refused. Arcane Denial's second sentence is not built: "Its controller" is the controller of the target spell, a player that has to be remembered from the resolution (a target that has left, CR 608.2h) and that, not the ability's controller, draws; and "up to two" is a number chosen by that player, which no effect asks. The card stays unsupported, with that reason; the first sentence alone is `docs/MECHANICS.md`. (2) Suspend (CR 702.62, 116.2f). `Keyword` `{ kind: 'suspend', count, cost }` (mana only, no X, a positive count, one per face, not on a land). The three abilities are the engine's, not derived from the keyword by `derive`: (a) the static special action is the priority option and action `suspend { object }` (`PriorityOption`, `Action`; listed by `suspendableObjects`, `rules/special-legality.ts`): the card is in the player's hand, "could begin to cast" (CR 702.62a, 702.62c: the card's timing, an instant or a card with flash any time the player has priority, anything else in their main phase with an empty stack, and no split second on the stack; a legal target or the mana cost of the spell is not asked then, CR 601.2c and 601.2f come when it is cast) and the suspend cost can be paid; (b) paying is the `payMana` decision with the new purposes `'suspend'` and `'foretell'` (`source` the card in the hand, `totalCost`), answered by `payAuto`, `payManual` or `cancel`, which gives priority back with nothing changed (the same shape as the cost of attacking, D-125); a cost of {0} is taken at once (`rules/special-actions.ts`); (c) the action exiles the card face up (`suspended { seat, object, count }` after the `zoneChanged`, then `counterAdded` for the counter named `time`, `TIME_COUNTER`), does not use the stack (CR 116.1) and returns priority to the same player. (d) "At the beginning of your upkeep, if this card is suspended, remove a time counter from it" and (e) "When the last time counter is removed from this card, if it's exiled, you may play it without paying its mana cost if able" work from exile, which the trigger scan (the battlefield) never reads, so `findLaterTriggers` (`rules/later-triggers.ts`, called by `collectTriggers`) makes their `PendingTrigger`s: the source is the card in exile, `abilityIndex` is -1, the controller its owner, the ability a constant (`SUSPEND_TICK_ABILITY`, `SUSPEND_CAST_ABILITY`) whose effects are two new engine-only effects, `removeTimeCounter` and `castExiled { mode }` (`validateCard` refuses both anywhere in a card, with a reason; `SUPPORTED_FEATURES.effectKinds` lists them as the engine's expansions, as `cumulativeUpkeep` is). One tick trigger for each suspended card of the player whose upkeep begins, ordered by that player; the "if this card is suspended" is read as the trigger is found and again as it resolves (`removeTimeCounter` does nothing for a card that left exile or has no counter, CR 603.4); the cast ability triggers from the `counterRemoved` event that takes the last counter off a card with suspend that is in exile. (f) `castExiled` runs as the instruction of the same name (`rules/cast-exiled.ts`, answers in `rules/cast-exiled-answer.ts`), modelled on Cascade (D-120): at `start` the ability's card must still be the exiled object of its owner; when it could be cast (`canCastDuringResolution`: a legal target for each target, the additional costs payable, no timing: CR 608.2g) the owner is asked `confirmOptional { purpose: 'suspend', subject: the card }`, otherwise nothing is asked and the card stays exiled with no counters ("if able"; it is not suspended any more, so nothing triggers again); accepting is `beginCast(card, 'free', face 0, resolving, suspended)`: the steps of CR 601.2a-i, targets chosen at that point, no payment, no priority, the spell the topmost object of the stack and the ability finishing; `cancel` rewinds to the question; declining leaves the card exiled. The spell carries `StackData.suspended` (`spellCast.suspended`, `ObjectView.suspended`), and a creature spell makes a permanent with `GameObject.alt = 'suspend'`, which gives it the keyword haste (`rules/derive-alt.ts`: removable by "loses all abilities", the new object of any later zone change has none, CR 400.7); a noncreature spell sets nothing. "Until you lose control of the spell or the permanent it becomes" is not modelled: the engine has no effect that changes control. A suspended card is public (exile): `counters.time` is in both views. A commander with suspend is in exile like any card (CR 903.9a asks its owner as for any move to exile); left there it is cast from exile, so no commander tax and no cast from the command zone. (3) Madness (CR 702.35). `AlternativeCost` `{ kind: 'madness', cost }` (mana only, no X, not on a land; `NamedAlternativeKind`, `CastAlternativeKind`, `castAlternative:madness`). The replacement is `discardOne` (`rules/madness.ts`), now the one place a card leaves a hand as a discard: the discard effect (`rules/search.ts`), the cleanup step (`rules/flow.ts`), a discard paid as a cost of a spell or an ability (`rules/discard-cost.ts`, Ward's and "unless pays" discard too) and Cycling's "discard this card" (`rules/activate-costs.ts`); a card with madness goes to exile instead of the graveyard (the `zoneChanged` event goes to exile, the `discarded` event still follows with the id the card had in the hand, so "whenever you discard" would see it, then `madnessExiled { seat, object }`). The exile is not a choice. `findLaterTriggers` finds the ability from `madnessExiled` (source the card in exile, controller its owner: the one who discarded it) with `{ effect: castExiled { mode: 'madness' } }`; when it resolves the owner is asked `confirmOptional { purpose: 'madness', subject, cost: the madness cost }` if the card could be cast now (the same check with the madness cost, `canCastDuringResolution(..., 'madness')`); accepting is `beginCast(card, 'madness', face 0, resolving)`: an alternative cost, so the `payMana` decision, kicker and additional costs as for any cast, `spellCast.alternative: 'madness'`, `ObjectView.alternative`; declining, or a card that could not be cast, puts the card into its owner's graveyard (`moveInstructions`, CR 702.35a). A commander discarded this way is in exile and its owner may move it to the command zone first (CR 903.9a): then the ability finds no card. The madness cast is never offered from a hand: `castZone(..., 'madness')` is null, so `canCast` and the option lists never list it and `applyAction` refuses it; `ObjectView.alternativeCosts` of a card in a hand omits it (the cost is in the question). (4) Foretell (CR 702.143). `AlternativeCost` `{ kind: 'foretell', cost }` (the foretell cost: what the cast from exile costs; mana only, no X, not on a land). The special action is the priority option and action `foretell { object }` (`foretellableObjects`): during the player's own turn (the active player) any time they have priority, the card with foretell in their hand, {2} payable; paid like suspend (purpose `'foretell'`); it exiles the card with `GameObject.foretoldTurn` = the turn number (`foretold { seat, object }`, which carries no card id, no name and no cost). A foretold card is face down: `getView` shows it in full (and `faceDown`, `foretold`, `foretoldTurn`, `alternativeCosts: [{ kind: 'foretell', cost }]`) to its owner only; every other viewer gets a placeholder object (`faceDownView`: its id, `owner`, `zone: 'exile'`, `name: 'Face-down card'`, empty types, text and counters, `isCommander` false, `faceDown: true`), because that a face-down card is in exile is public (CR 702.143a, 406.3) and what it is is not. The boundary is tested in the view, in the events (`foretold` and the `zoneChanged` of the exile name no card: the card id every event carries is an opaque id, as for a card drawn), in the action log (the action carries the hand object's id) and in the pending decision (`getView` hands a pending payment to its seat only); `packages/ai/test/hidden-info.test.ts` audits every view of games with the 'later' deck style (the card's name and card id are secrets of the other seat, its object id is not). The cast is `castSpell { object, alternative: 'foretell' }` from exile (`castZone`: the card is the owner's, foretold, and `state.turn.number` is later than `foretoldTurn`: "after the current turn has ended"; `foretellCastObjects` lists it, `ObjectView.specialActions` lists the actions of a hand card with their costs, `ObjectView.alternativeCosts` the foretell cost of the foretold card), for the foretell cost instead of the mana cost (`spellCost`, an alternative cost: commander tax, additional costs and reductions as ever), with the spell's own timing; it is not an ordinary cast and not a cast by anyone else. The spell is a new object, public, not foretold. A commander foretold is in exile (CR 903.9a, and `isCommander` is false in the other seat's view of a face-down card). Not built: CR 702.143d (an effect that makes a card in exile foretold, with its own foretell cost), the reveal of CR 702.143f when a player leaves the game, and conditions on "foretold" spells ("If this spell was foretold, ..."). (5) The AI (`packages/ai/src/casual-later.ts`). `RandomLegalAgent` needs nothing beyond the answers it already gives (`payAuto`, the confirmations, the options). `CasualAgent`: a special action only in its own main phase with an empty stack and only after the spell step found nothing worth casting; it suspends a permanent card, or a spell worth casting now (`worthCasting`: a hostile target exists for a spell that needs one), the fewest time counters first, then the biggest card; it foretells the card whose later cast saves the most mana (at least one); it answers the Suspend and Madness questions yes when `worthCasting` says the card is worth casting (the engine asks only when it could be cast and paid); a card with madness is the first one it discards at the cleanup step; a foretold card is cast like any spell (`chooseNamedAlternative` picks `foretell`). (6) Tests: `scenario-xx-delayed-draw.test.ts`, `scenario-xx-suspend.test.ts`, `scenario-xx-madness.test.ts`, `scenario-xx-foretell.test.ts` (scenario DSL verbs `suspend` and `foretell`, the action specs `{ suspend }` and `{ foretell }`), the soak `packages/ai/test/later-games.test.ts` (20 games, D-126, the `later` deck style, replay hashed, the hidden-information check in every step) and the heuristics in `casual-later.test.ts`. The checks of the engine's invariants cover the new state (`stack.suspended`, `alt: 'suspend'`, `foretoldTurn`).
- Alternatives: (1) Deriving Suspend's two triggers from the keyword in `derive` with new trigger and condition kinds (`lastCounterRemoved`, `suspended`, `sourceExiled`): rejected, the trigger scan reads the battlefield and each of those kinds would have to be validated, listed, worded by the web and matched, for abilities no card can write (the rules fix them); the two effects are enough and stay engine-only. Putting the abilities in the `inherent` mechanism of the monarch (D-127): rejected, those abilities have no source and the engine resolves them from a constant; these have a card as the source (the stack and the web show the card). One trigger that removes the counter and casts at once: rejected, CR 702.62a has two abilities and the player can respond between them. Asking the player to name a target or paying the spell's mana cost to suspend ("could begin to cast" read as "could cast"): rejected, CR 601.2a is the first step of casting; the engine would refuse suspending a spell whose target appears later, which the rules allow. Making the suspend cost part of a `castSpell` option: rejected, it is a special action and the card is not cast (CR 116.2f). (2) A general `removeCounters` effect and a "play" that can put a land onto the battlefield: rejected, no card needs them yet and each would need its own tests. A madness exile the player may refuse: rejected, CR 702.35a. Exiling in the cast step (a replacement applied by `moveObject`): rejected, then Cycling's `discardThis`, cost payments and the cleanup would still need the `discarded` event and the commander question in the right order; `discardOne` is the one place that says "discard". A madness cost in the keyword list (`Keyword` `madness`): rejected for consistency with the other named alternative costs, which the cast code reads from `alternativeCosts` (`namedAlternativeCostOf`). (3) Foretold cards hidden by moving them out of `state.exile` into a per-seat list: rejected, the engine would need a new zone with its own move, view and invariant code; one optional field on the exile object and one place that builds the view is smaller, and exile stays one list that both players see the length of. Naming the card in the `foretold` event or giving the hand object id: rejected, the id is not a secret but the name and the card id are, and the event is part of the public log. Showing the foretold turn to the other seat: rejected, it says when the card was exiled, which is public, but the field would invite the placeholder to grow; the placeholder is exactly what CR 702.143a says is known. A separate `foretell` alternative on `castSpell` from the hand: rejected, the foretell cost is paid from exile only. (4) Reading "a delayed trigger of any effect" with object selectors by capturing them at creation: rejected, "Its controller may draw up to N cards" shows what that needs (a captured player and a chosen number) and nothing else in the corpus wants it.
- Consequences: The parser lowers `You draw a card at the beginning of the next turn's upkeep.` to `delayedTrigger` (`at: { step: 'upkeep', whose: 'each' }`, `effect: draw you 1`, declaring `effect:delayedTrigger`), `Suspend 2—{1}{B}` to the keyword `suspend { count: 2, cost }` (declaring `keyword:suspend`, `cost:mana`), `Madness {1}{B}{B}` to `alternativeCosts: [{ kind: 'madness', cost }]` (declaring `castAlternative:madness`) and `Foretell {4}{R}{R}` to `alternativeCosts: [{ kind: 'foretell', cost }]` (declaring `castAlternative:foretell`), reminder text dropped (`docs/MECHANICS.md`, "Cast later"). The web needs: the two special actions as buttons on a hand card from `ObjectView.specialActions` and the priority options `suspend` and `foretell` (and an `isOffered`-style match of those two kinds in its option lists), the `payMana` decision with `purpose` `'suspend'` or `'foretell'` (the same mana panel; Cancel gives the priority back), the `confirmOptional` purposes `'suspend'` and `'madness'` (a madness question carries `cost` and `subject`), a cast option for a foretold card (`castSpell` with `alternative: 'foretell'`, the cost in `ObjectView.alternativeCosts` of the exile card), the face-down card (`faceDown`, `foretold`, `foretoldTurn` on the owner's exile objects, the placeholder name for the other seat), time counters on the suspended card in exile (`counters.time`, a chip "time N"), the events `suspended`, `foretold` and `madnessExiled` (minimal lines are in `game/describe.ts`), `spellCast.suspended`, `ObjectView.suspended`, `alternative` values `'madness'`, `'foretell'`, `'suspend'`, the words of the engine's abilities on the stack (an ability whose `ability.effect.kind` is `removeTimeCounter` or `castExiled`), and an exile viewer that shows both players' exile with the foretold cards of the viewer marked. Not built (`docs/ROADMAP.md`): "Its controller may draw up to N cards at the beginning of the next turn's upkeep." (Arcane Denial), a delayed effect other than draw, gain life and lose life, Suspend and Foretell granted by another card or with a cost that is not mana, "until you lose control" for the haste of Suspend, an effect that foretells or suspends a card from another zone, CR 702.143d and 702.143f, Miracle and Plot (the other D-117 steps), and the web steps above. `docs/RULES_COVERAGE.md`, `docs/MECHANICS.md`, `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` and `docs/ROADMAP.md` are updated.

## D-129: Copies of spells on the stack, Storm and Replicate (2026-10-26)
- Context: D-118 planned "Storm (needs spell copies)" and `docs/MECHANICS.md` ("Keyword batch 2", "Not built") still lists it, but no design entry was ever written; this is it. The backlog (`reports/backlog.md`, `reports/templates.json`, oracle_cards 2026-10-22) has `Storm` (33 cards blocked, 16 by it alone), `Replicate {M}` (16 cards, 7 alone), `Casualty N` (14, 5 alone) and the wordings that copy a spell: `Copy target instant or sorcery spell. You may choose new targets for the copy.` (6 cards), `{M}, {T}: Copy target instant or sorcery spell you control. You may choose new targets for the copy.` (2), `When ~ enters, copy target instant or sorcery spell. You may choose new targets for the copy.` (1), `Whenever you cast a spell of the chosen type, copy that spell.` (1), `Copy target instant or sorcery spell, then return it to its owner's hand. You may choose new targets for the copy.` (1) and "Whenever you cast or copy an instant or sorcery spell, ..." (6 cards in three shapes). The engine already had copies of permanents (token copies, `becomeCopy`, `copiableValues`, D-0xx "Ward, copies and the legend rule") and a stack object that was a spell or an ability; a copy of a spell was named in code comments as something that "ceases to exist" (`rules/zones.ts`) but nothing made one. Of the three mechanics asked, Storm and Replicate are built and Casualty is not (below). `ENGINE_VERSION` 27 for the slice. SYNTHETIC fixtures: `cards/fixtures/synthetic-copies.ts`.
- Decision: (1) What a copy of a spell is (CR 707.10, 707.2). A new optional field `GameObject.copyOf: CardId`: the object is a spell on the stack with `card: null` and `token: null` (it is not a card and has no card to be a commander, to be cast again or to be counted by the invariant "every card is one object"), and the face it copies is the card's definition at the object's own `face`. One helper, `printedCard(obj)` (`state/ops.ts`), is the card whose face an object shows (`card ?? copyOf`), and `faceOf`, `copiableValues` (the only reader of printed values), `derive`, the type view, the printed abilities, the spell-cost reader, the view and the invariants use it, so a copy has the characteristics, the spell text, the modes and the abilities that work on the stack (a "can't be countered" copy cannot be countered, a split-second copy has split second) without any special case in the rules code. A copy stores no characteristics of its own: a copy of a copy names the same card. The copy's `StackData` has the original's targets, X, modes, `kicked` and `kicks`, `replicated` and `alt` (CR 707.10: "all decisions made for it, including modes, targets, the value of X, and additional or alternative costs": an overloaded copy has the overloaded text, an evoked or dashed copy of a permanent spell becomes an evoked or dashed token), and not `flashback`, `free`, `suspended`, `byEffect`, `castFromCommandZone` or the cast count, which are about how a spell was cast and a copy is not cast (CR 707.10). Choices made on resolution are stored nowhere, so they are not copied. It is owned and controlled by the player who puts it on the stack (the controller of the resolving effect). (2) Leaving the stack (CR 707.10a, 704.5e, 707.10f, 608.3f). `moveObject` already removed a stack object with no card and no token without a zone change (an ability, CR 608.2n); a copy of a spell now does the same wherever it goes (countered, fizzled, an instant or sorcery that resolved, returned to a hand): it ceases to exist at once, emits no `zoneChanged` and is in no graveyard, so nothing triggers on it (the engine treats the state-based action of 704.5e as part of the move, as it does for abilities; a token is the same case only on the battlefield). The one exception is a copy of a permanent spell that resolves: `moveObject` to the battlefield turns it into a token (`token` = `copiableValues` of the copy, `card` null, `copyOf` gone, CR 707.10f: "no longer a copy of a spell and is not 'created'", so the event is `zoneChanged` into the battlefield and not `tokenCreated`), through the same pipeline as a card, so "enters tapped", "enters with counters" and X counters (CR 107.3m reads the X of the copy), "As this enters, choose a type" (the usual `chooseOption` question), Sagas, planeswalker loyalty, Auras (it attaches to the object it targeted, CR 608.3c), the kicked fact and the evoke and dash marks all work for the token; the web and the AI see an ordinary permanent with `isToken`. The invariants that look a permanent's kicked fact or alternative cost up in its card's face read the token's own abilities for the kicker keyword and skip the alternative-cost check for a token (it has no list of alternative costs). (3) The effect `copySpell { spell: ObjectRef, newTargets: 'may' | 'no' }` (CR 707.10, 707.10c). `spell` is a `target` slot (the effect finds the target still on the stack as it resolves, CR 608.2b, otherwise it does nothing) or the `triggerSubject` of a cast trigger ("Whenever you cast ..., copy that spell"), which is read from last-known information when the spell has left the stack (CR 113.7a: the trigger on the stack above a spell can be answered by countering the spell, and Storm's ruling is the same); `validateCard` refuses any other reference, an unknown `newTargets`, a `triggerSubject` outside a trigger about a stack object and a target slot the ability does not declare, each with a reason. At resolution it queues one instruction `copySpell { spell, count, newTargets, stage, copy }` (like Cascade and `castExiled`, run by `rules/stack.ts` because it reads the legality code): stage `make` creates the copy (`rules/copy-spell.ts`) on top of the stack, emits `spellCopied { seat, original, copy }` (no `spellCast`: nothing that triggers on casting sees a copy and it is not counted for Storm), and when the controller may choose new targets and has something to choose goes to stage `targets`, which asks and is answered by `chooseTargets`. (4) The new targets (CR 707.10c). The question is the existing `TargetsDecision` with two new optional fields: `forCopy: true` and `current: ChosenTarget[]` (the targets the copy has now). Each slot's `legal` is every legal target for it (the same computation as casting, with the copy as the source so it never targets itself and a modal copy has the slots of its chosen modes with `mode`) plus the target the copy already has in that slot when that is not legal any more, because "the player may leave any number of the targets unchanged, even if those targets would be illegal; if the player chooses to change some or all of the targets, the new targets must be legal" (CR 707.10c); the one validator of answers (`targetAnswerError`) and the one list of legal actions then accept exactly the answers of the rule and no code outside the decision knows the exception. There is no `cancel` (the copy is on the stack already). The question is not asked when it has only one answer: a spell with no targets, a copy that must have a target with a single legal choice (the product of the ways each slot can be filled is 1), or `newTargets: 'no'`; the web and the AI are not bothered for nothing. After the answer the copy has its targets, one `becameTarget` event for each object it targets follows (a copy is a new spell that targets: Ward triggers for it whether or not the target changed, tested), and the next copy is made. A copy that has an illegal target when it resolves does what it can (CR 608.2b, the existing code). (5) Storm (CR 702.40a, 702.40b). The keyword `{ kind: 'storm' }` has no data; `derive` expands each instance into the trigger `{ castSpell by you, self: true } → { kind: 'storm' }` (the same shape as Cascade, found on the spell as it is cast and put on the stack above it, CR 603.3b; two instances are two triggers, CR 702.40b). The effect `storm` is engine-only like `cascade` (`validateCard` refuses it anywhere but as the whole effect of a self cast trigger): it queues `copySpell` for the spell itself, `newTargets: 'may'`, with the count `StackData.spellsCastBefore`, from the spell on the stack or its last-known information. The count is the number of spells cast this turn by every player before this one (CR 702.40a "each other spell that was cast before it this turn": the spells of the opponent count, spells countered or still on the stack count, copies never do). It is kept as two new facts: `SeatState.spellsCastThisTurn` (reset for every seat as each turn begins, in `startTurn`, like `cardsDrawnThisTurn`; incremented as the spell becomes cast, `rules/cast.ts` `finishCast`, so a cast during a resolution, by Cascade or Suspend, counts) and `StackData.spellsCastBefore` (the sum over the seats at that moment, written into the spell as it is cast): the trigger reads the spell's own number, so a spell cast in response to the trigger does not change it, and a spell countered in response to the trigger still makes its copies. The field is a public count in the view (`SeatView.spellsCastThisTurn`) and is also the base of "second spell this turn" conditions later. (6) Replicate (CR 702.56a, 702.56b). `Keyword` `{ kind: 'replicate', cost }` (mana only, no X, a non-empty cost, one per face: a second instance is refused with the usual "not implemented" reason, CR 702.56b being the part not built). The count is asked as the spell is cast, after the kicker and before X and the targets (CR 601.2b), as `chooseX { purpose: 'replicate', min: 0, max, cost, perX: 0 }` (a purpose beside `multikicker`: the same decision, answer, view and legal actions; `max` is the most times the whole cost, with the kicker as it was answered, could be paid; nothing is asked when it could not be paid even once; the answer can be taken back with `cancel`, CR 733); the cost is charged once for each time (`CostRequest.replicas`, `rules/cast-cost.ts`, so the total, the check that X can still be paid, the legal actions and the planner all read the same number); the count is kept on the spell as `StackData.replicated` (absent for 0) and in `spellCast.replicas`. `derive` expands the keyword into the trigger `{ castSpell by you, self: true }` with `interveningIf: { kind: 'replicated' }` (a new condition: "a replicate cost was paid for it", read from the spell or its last-known information; `validateCard` refuses it on a face with no replicate ability) and the engine-only effect `replicate`, which queues `copySpell` with `count = replicated` and `newTargets: 'may'`. So no trigger exists when it was not paid (CR 603.4). (7) Views and events. `ObjectView.copy` marks a copy on the stack (public; the other fields are the copy's: name, types, text, `targets`, `x`, `modes`, `kicked`); `ObjectView.replicated`; `SeatView.spellsCastThisTurn`; events `spellCopied` and `spellCast.replicas`; the decision `TargetsDecision.forCopy` and `current`; the scenario DSL names a copy by what it is (`nameOf`) and has the verb `replicas(n)` and the cast option `replicas`. (8) The casual AI (`packages/ai/src/casual-copies.ts`, `casual-priority.ts`, `casual-choices.ts`, `casual-x.ts`): a spell that says "Copy target ... spell" is worth casting only while the object on top of the stack is a spell of the agent's own (a copy without new targets of the opponent's burn would burn the agent) and it targets the topmost such spell; the question about the new targets of a copy is answered like the cast of the spell it copies (the copy has its text in the view), so a hostile copy goes on the opponent's best thing and a helpful one on the agent's best creature; a Storm spell is cast after every other spell worth casting (so as many spells as possible are cast before it), and when it is all that is left it is cast at once; the Replicate count is as many as it can pay, half of that (rounded up) for a spell with an {X}, which is asked after it. The soak `copy-games.test.ts` (20 games, D-126) checks each rule from the events.
- Alternatives: (1) A copy as an object with the same `card` as the original: rejected, `invariants.ts` and every reader of a card would count two objects for one card, the commander and "cast from a hand" code would treat a copy as the card, and the copy would be found by anything that looks a card up. A copy that stores its own `Characteristics` and abilities (the shape of a token): rejected, a spell has a spell text (effects, targets, modes, additional and alternative costs) that `TokenData` does not hold, and storing the face twice would let the copy and the card disagree; a field that names the card keeps one reader of printed values (`copiableValues`), as D-0xx wanted. A copy created as a token and turned into a spell: rejected, a token that is not on the battlefield would be removed by the state-based action and the object would need a second model. A new `Zone` or a `StackData.kind: 'copy'`: rejected, a copy is a spell ("A copy of a spell is itself a spell", CR 707.10) and every rule that reads `stack.kind === 'spell'` (split second, counters, Ward's "spell", filters by `stackKind`) must apply to it. (2) Making the copy leave the stack through the graveyard and then cease (CR 704.5e as a state-based action after a real move): rejected, it would put a non-card in a graveyard for a moment, emit a zone change that "dies" and "leaves the stack" triggers could see, and need a sweep in `sba.ts` for a case `moveObject` handles for abilities already; the visible result of the rule (no object in any zone) is the same. (3) Asking the controller of the copy for the targets before the copy exists (the rule's order: "once the player has decided what the copy's targets will be, the copy is put onto the stack with those targets"): rejected, the decision needs a source object that is on the stack for the web (a name, a text) and the engine's resolution can only pause at an instruction that has not changed the state, so the copy is created first and the question follows; nothing can happen in between (no player has priority), and the copy has no effect on the stack until the question is answered. A separate `Action` `chooseCopyTargets` and decision `copyTargets`: rejected, the UI and the AI already answer `targets` and the only difference is one legal exception, which `legal` carries. Adding the illegal current target to `legal` only when it is illegal and leaving the rule to the validator: that is what is done; the alternative of a flag on each target ("unchanged") was rejected because `chooseTargets` answers are plain target lists everywhere (the replay log, the AI). Asking even when the player has nothing to choose: rejected, a Storm count of 3 against a spell with one possible target would make three dialogs with one button. (4) Storm as a count `Amount` ("the number of spells cast before this one this turn") on `copySpell`: rejected for now, the keyword is the only reader, and an `Amount` would need a place in the amount table, the validator and the parser for no other user; the effect is engine-only. Counting by scanning the action log or the `spellCast` events: rejected, the state must answer by itself (a saved game, a replay, the view). Counting only in the active player's turn or only the caster's spells: wrong (CR 702.40a). Reading the count live when the trigger resolves: wrong (spells cast in response). (5) Replicate as the multikicker cost (`multikicker { cost }` + `timesKicked` copies): rejected, a card with replicate may also have kicker, the cost, the condition and the view are the card's own, and "kicked" is read by other cards. Replicate with no intervening "if" (the trigger always goes on the stack and copies zero times): rejected, CR 702.56a says "if a replicate cost was paid for it" and an empty trigger on the stack is visible and answerable. A `Condition` for it that reads a `StackData` field the validator cannot see: a condition kind `replicated` with the face check (`checkCastFace`) is the same shape as `kicked`. Several instances of replicate: not built (CR 702.56b: each is paid separately; the cast flow asks one count). (6) Casualty (CR 702.153; 14 cards, 5 by it alone) was not built: "As you cast this spell, you may sacrifice a creature with power N or greater. When you do, copy this spell" needs an optional additional cost that chooses a permanent while the spell is being cast (a question the engine has for no cost: the kicker is a yes or no, the sacrifices of D-095 are mandatory), the choice of the creature with a `cancel` at each step (CR 733) and a reflexive trigger (CR 603.12); that is a general "announce additional costs" step, which `docs/ROADMAP.md` already lists, and Replicate (16 cards, 7 by it alone) reuses what exists (a count question, an intervening-if trigger).
- Consequences: The parser lowers `Storm` to `{ kind: 'storm' }` and `Replicate {2}` to `{ kind: 'replicate', cost: [mana] }` (real lines in `docs/MECHANICS.md`), declaring `keyword:storm` or `keyword:replicate` (and `cost:mana`); the copy wordings above lower to `copySpell` with a target slot `{ what: object filter { stackKind: 'spell', anyOf: [instant, sorcery] }, controller: 'you' where the text says "you control" }`, `newTargets: 'may'` for "You may choose new targets for the copy" and `'no'` for "copy that spell", declaring `effect:copySpell` (a lowering for the cast-trigger form needs the trigger `castSpell` and the `triggerSubject` reference, which the parser may declare once it reads them). Not built (`docs/ROADMAP.md`): Casualty; copies of activated and triggered abilities ("Copy target triggered ability", CR 707.10 for abilities, 707.10b); "except" copies (Fork: "except the copy is red"; CR 707.9); "may cast the copy" (CR 707.12); "for each player or object it could target" (CR 707.10d) and a copy with a given new target (CR 707.10e); "Whenever you cast or copy an instant or sorcery spell" (6 cards: the `spellCopied` event is there for a trigger, which needs a `castSpell` variant that also looks at it); "Copy target instant or sorcery spell, then return it to its owner's hand"; "copy ~ for each creature sacrificed"; several instances of Replicate; a Storm count as an `Amount` or a condition on the number of spells cast ("if it's the second spell you've cast this turn", the field is there); the objects "used to pay the costs" of a copy (CR 707.10: nothing the engine has reads them yet); a copy of an evoked or dashed permanent spell remembers the alternative cost (CR 707.10, `StackData.alt` is copied and the token gets the mark) but no test builds that case. The web needs: the log line for `spellCopied` (a minimal one is in this slice: "X copied Y"), a mark on a copy on the stack from `ObjectView.copy` and the card art of the card it copies (the view has the name and the text, not a card id), the `targets` decision with `forCopy` ("Choose new targets for the copy" with the targets in `current` selected and a button that keeps them; no cancel), the replicate question (the `chooseX` dialog with `purpose: 'replicate'`, worded like the multikicker one: "Pay the replicate cost {R} how many times? You can afford up to 3."), `ObjectView.replicated` ("replicated 2 times" next to "kicked"), `SeatView.spellsCastThisTurn` if it wants a counter, and the chip "Storm" and "Replicate" for the two keywords. Saved states record `ENGINE_VERSION`; `SeatState` gained a field and `StackData` and `GameObject` optional ones, so a state saved by version 26 does not have them. `docs/RULES_COVERAGE.md`, `docs/MECHANICS.md`, `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` and `docs/ROADMAP.md` are updated.

## D-130: The engine stays one unit; per-deck loading is for data, not rules (2026-10-26)
- Context: The owner asked whether the engine would grow too heavy to ship whole, and suggested loading a core rule set plus the extra rules each deck needs. Measured on the cast-later branch: the worker bundle (engine and AI, every mechanic through D-128) is 462 kB raw and 113 kB gzipped; the UI bundle is 294 kB gzipped; the engine source is about 40,000 lines and a slice adds a few kilobytes gzipped.
- Decision: The engine ships as one unit. Rules interact (layers, replacement effects, triggers, the stack), so loading them in parts would put a boundary inside tested logic, make saves and replays depend on what was loaded, and multiply the test surface, all to save a few hundred kilobytes. Per-deck loading applies to data instead: card definitions (`definitions.json` split per card and loaded for the two decks in play when it grows), precon snapshots (one file per precon, M9), and images (already on demand). The parser's `needs` list per card already records which features a deck uses, for coverage and for the "why unsupported" text. Revisit if the worker bundle passes 500 kB gzipped.
- Alternatives: Core rules plus lazily loaded rule modules: rejected for the reasons above. A build check that warns at the threshold: deferred (ROADMAP).
- Consequences: No engine refactor. Data loading per deck is planned work, not a change of architecture.

## D-131: Counted amounts, "where X is", tokens, player effects, one-sided damage and designation conditions (2026-10-26)
- Context: `pnpm corpus:decks` over the owner's five precon decks (`reports/decks.md`, parser version 32) lists 220 blocking shapes, nearly all of them one card; the large families are generic effects with small variants. The biggest is counted amounts ("where X is the number of Zombies you control", "for each ...", "equal to ..."), then token creation, life gain and loss, and player effects. The owner asked for general primitives in the AST (who, action, filter, amount), not card code, and that the parser be the next task. `ENGINE_VERSION` 28. SYNTHETIC fixtures: `cards/fixtures/synthetic-amounts.ts`, `synthetic-player-effects.ts`.
- Survey (row numbers are the `#` column of "Blockers across the decks"; the owner's counts of 37 amount rows and 14 token rows were approximate, these are counted by reading the real lines). **Amount rows (55, every row that reads a number from the game):** (a) 8 that the engine already ran, only the parser was missing (6 Mutilate, 24 Graveborn Muse, 135 Chain Reaction, 136 and 137 the two Swamp drains, 138 Wight of Precinct Six, 160 the Equipment, 181 "put X counters ... where X is that creature's power"); (b) 20 that lacked an amount kind or a slot and are complete after this slice (7 counters on this creature in a cost reduction, 14 and 212's condition total power, 16 half rounded down, 20 creature cards in your graveyard, 22 opponents with more cards in hand, 34 "who drew a card this way", 36 "creature sacrificed this way", 54 and 78 and 99 and 186 a creature dealing damage equal to its power or X, 57 and 155 the greatest power, 62 devotion, 102 and 190 that creature's toughness, 107 two life for each, 131 total power in a cost reduction, 218 enters with a counter for each, 220 a sum of two counts); (b') 6 whose amount is built but another clause is not (4 and 5: "pay life equal to" as a cost and "add mana for each" need a cost and a mana production with an amount; 26 prevention by "non-Spider creatures"; 53 "each other creature" after a bite; 55 trample excess; 61 the filter "with flying"); (c) 21 that are not amount problems (19 and 150 "the one with the greatest ... or tied", 29 discover, 41 fights, 66 per-opponent targets, 91 combat history, 94 "tap X untapped", 97 play from exile, 114 the power of a creature sacrificed as a cost, 118 cost reduction of an activation, 119 a filter compared with an amount, 133 divided damage, 134 the filter "without flying", 147 and 219 statics on life, 156 a replacement for other permanents, 161 greatest mana value among commanders, 162 and 182 "that many", 171 a choice by greatest power, 212 play the exiled card). **Token rows (26: 21 create tokens, 5 investigate):** (a) 2 (28 Fateful Absence's "its controller investigates", 67 the kicked Zombie Knights); (b) 11 (16 half, 17 and 21 "if you're the monarch", 22 and 177's counts and conditions, 26's count, 27 and 37 and 96 and 194 "tapped", 36 "for each creature sacrificed"); (c) 13 (29, 41, 58, 76, 80, 84, 103, 114, 127, 163, 184, 189, 191: discover, fights, modal exile, trigger shapes such as "nontoken creature", replacement of dying, behold). **Life rows (20):** (a) 3 (24, 136, 137); (b) 6 (62 drain by devotion, 68 mill and gain, 102 and 190 toughness, 107, 178 "if an opponent has more life"); (c) 11 (4 pay life as a cost, 77 and 82 and 88 and 195 and 196 and 201 trigger shapes, 127 and 147 and 219 life above the starting total, 164 a replacement of gaining life). The remaining families in the owner's list: "each player sacrifices" 3 rows (37, 63, 171: the shape existed; 37 and 63 need only the parser, 171 is a choice by greatest power), "bite" 4 rows (53, 54, 55, 78: 54 and 78 complete here, 53 and 55 partly), monarch 4 rows (17 and 21 complete here, 158 a static with a player condition, 183 existed), mill 2 rows (68 and 180: complete here), special mana abilities 6 rows (not an amount problem, not built).
- Decision: (1) **Amounts** (`Amount` in `ast/types.ts`, read by `rules/amounts.ts` `amountOf`, which moved there from `effect-support.ts` so that conditions can read amounts without an import cycle): `toughnessOf` and `countersOn` of an `ObjectRef` (a target, `this` or the `triggerSubject` permanent, last-known information once it left, CR 113.7a); `aggregate { how: 'greatest' | 'total', stat: 'power' | 'toughness' | 'manaValue', filter }` over the objects a filter matches (an object with no such stat is left out, nothing matched is 0, a negative result is 0, CR 107.1b); `devotion { colors }` (CR 700.5: a symbol counts once if it is one of the colors, so a hybrid symbol counts for each color it has among them and a generic or colorless one for none; the mana cost the permanent has now, 700.5a); `commanderColors` (CR 903.4, all the controller's commanders); `half { of, round }` (CR 107.1a: the rounding is always stated); `multiple { factor >= 2, of }` (`times` stays a power and toughness shape, it can be negative); `sum { of: Amount[] }`, also in a characteristic-defining ability when every part is a count (CR 604.3); `opponentsWithMore { stat: 'life' | 'cardsInHand' | 'creatures' }`; `thisWay { what: 'sacrificed' | 'destroyed' | 'playersDrew' }` (what the earlier instructions of this resolution did, added up as `ResolutionContext.thisWay`; valid only after a `sacrifice`, `destroy` or `draw` in the same sequence, never after a `conditional` that may not have run, as `lifeLostThisWay` and `moved` are). `ObjectFilter.attackingYou` ("creatures attacking you": attackers whose target is the controller as a player, CR 508.1b; refused where `attacking` is, in statics and counts that `derive` reads). `Condition` `amountIs { amount, compare: NumberComparison }`: any amount that reads the game now (`validateCard` refuses `x`, a target, the trigger subject and `thisWay` there with a reason). A `costReduction` amount and an `entersWithCounters` count may be such an amount (`countOf` for the latter: counted as it enters, for its controller, without the permanent, CR 614.12). (2) **"Where X is ..."**: CR 107.3c says that when the text defines X, "that's the value of X while that spell or ability is on the stack ... the value of X may change". So the definition is read wherever X is, as that instruction runs, and a second slot that says X reads it again; nothing is stored. The parser writes the definition into each slot ("you draw X cards and lose X life, where X is the number of Zombies you control" has the `countOf` in the draw and in the loss); there is no `defineX` node and no new field in `StackData`, and the announced X of D-103 (`Amount` `x`) stays for the X of a cost only (CR 107.3a). `Zombie Toll` in the tests ("sacrifice a Zombie, then draw X") pins the changing value. What the plumbing did need: slots that held only a number now take an amount (`entersWithCounters` count, a `choose` selector's `count` of `sacrifice` and `moveToZone`, tokens, mill). "As you cast ~" X (Monstrous Onslaught) is a value fixed at announcement and is not built. (3) **Tokens**: `createToken` gains `tapped: true` ("tapped Treasure tokens", CR 110.5b; the token enters tapped, nothing "becomes tapped"); the count was already an `Amount` and the token definition already carried keywords. (4) **Player effects**: `PlayerSelector` `{ kind: 'all', of: PlayerSelector[] }` names several selectors at once and is usable by every effect that takes a `player` (draw, discard, gain and lose life, mill, shuffle, search, sacrifice, token controller, unless-pays); the players are each taken once and acted on in the order of CR 101.4 (the active player first, then turn order: `rules/select.ts` `apnapOrder`), which `eachPlayer` and `eachOpponent` now follow too (before, they started with the controller, which is wrong for an instant cast in the opponent's turn). `validateCard` refuses `all` with fewer than two members or nested, and as the one player who becomes the monarch; scry and surveil stay the controller's alone. "Each player sacrifices N creatures of their choice" is the existing `sacrifice { objects: choose { filter, count }, player: eachPlayer }`; `count` may now be an `Amount`; each player gets the choice in APNAP order with the existing `choosePermanent` decision (purpose `sacrifice`), the engine takes everything of a player who has no more candidates than needed, and the AI already answers that decision. Not simultaneous: CR 101.4 has all choices first and then the actions together; here each player's permanents are sacrificed right after their choice (ROADMAP). `mill { player, count }` (CR 701.17: the top cards one after another, all of them when fewer, not a loss, CR 701.17b, 121.4; `milled` event with the new objects) is the one new effect kind. "You and target opponent each draw N cards" is `draw` with `player: all [you, target]`; "each opponent draws, then you draw for each opponent who drew" is `thisWay playersDrew` (a commander put into the command zone instead is not a card drawn, CR 903.9b). (5) **Bite**: `dealDamage` gains `from?: ObjectRef` (a `target`, `this` or the `triggerSubject` permanent): the creature is the source of the damage (CR 120.1, 120.3: its lifelink, deathtouch, infect and wither apply, prevention for that source applies, never combat damage, so no commander damage, CR 903.10a) and takes none back, unlike a fight (CR 701.14). A source that is no longer a legal target deals none (CR 608.2b); a trigger's subject or this that left deals as it last existed (CR 113.7a). The amount is `powerOf` the same reference. (6) **Designations**: not `youAreMonarch` but `Condition` `playerHasDesignation { player: PlayerSelector, designation: 'monarch' }` (the monarch is a designation, CR 725.1, not an emblem; the closed union is the place for the initiative and the like). It holds when the holder is one of the players the selector names ("if you're the monarch" is `you`, "if an opponent is the monarch" `eachOpponent`; `not` for the negative); a condition names players without targets or a trigger subject (`you`, `eachPlayer`, `eachOpponent`, `defendingPlayer`, `all` of those, the controller or owner of this permanent). "If an opponent has more life / creatures than you" is `amountIs` of `opponentsWithMore` at least 1, not a condition of its own. (7) **Generic is not permissive**: `validateCard` refuses a combination the interpreter cannot run, with a reason: an unknown aggregate, stat, rounding or designation, a `multiple` below 2, a `sum` of one, `thisWay` without the effect it counts before it, a `from` that is a spell or an `each`, an `x`, a target or a trigger subject in a condition or cost reduction, a count of `attackingYou` in a static power, a condition naming a target's player. Feature ids: `amount:` toughnessOf, countersOn, aggregate, devotion, commanderColors, half, multiple, sum, opponentsWithMore, thisWay; `condition:` amountIs, playerHasDesignation; `selector:` attackingYou, all, damageSource; `effect:mill`; `token:tapped`. (8) AI: the creature that deals the damage of a bite is the agent's strongest (`packages/ai/src/casual-bite.ts`); the sacrifice, draw, mill and amount effects add no decision. Web: the log line of `milled`, and the gist of an `all` selector and an `Amount` count in `ui/decisions/ability-label.ts` (minimal exhaustiveness fixes, listed in `docs/MECHANICS.md`).
- Alternatives: A `defineX` node that stores X when the effect starts: rejected, CR 107.3c says the value may change, so a stored value is wrong for "sacrifice, then draw X". `youAreMonarch` and `opponentHasMore` conditions: rejected by the owner's brief, the generic `playerHasDesignation` and `amountIs` cover them. A new effect kind for "each player sacrifices N creatures": rejected, the existing shape fits with an `Amount` count. A draw effect for "you and target opponent": rejected, the selector is reused by every effect. A `cardsInGraveyard` condition (the parser's old name): the generic `amountIs` of a `countOf` replaces it. Making the sacrifices simultaneous: deferred, it needs a two-phase instruction (choose all, then sacrifice all) for one rules detail (CR 101.4) that changes only trigger order.
- Consequences: The parser (next task) lowers the real lines listed with each primitive in `docs/MECHANICS.md` ("Counted amounts that read the game", "Tokens that enter tapped", "Several players, each player sacrifices, mill and what happened this way", "A creature that deals damage", "Designations and conditions about players"); the parser's `needs` use the feature ids above. The 21 rows of (c) and the six of (b') stay unsupported with their reasons in `docs/ROADMAP.md`. Behavior change: `eachPlayer` and `eachOpponent` act in turn order from the active player. The web shows `milled` in the log and needs wording for an amount of "the greatest power among" and the like when the preview panel summarizes such a text (`docs/MECHANICS.md`, "Web").

## D-132: Quick CI on every push, the complete suite run nightly (2026-10-27; the nightly run is on GitHub since D-250)
- Context: Every job of CI and Coverage began failing in one to three seconds with no runner assigned and no billable time (pull request 29, 2026-10-27). The cause is the monthly limit of included GitHub Actions minutes for a private repository on the free tier; the full CI (four test shards, browser tests, typecheck, lint, build) costs roughly 90 job-minutes per push and many pushes were made in one week. The owner decided to run the complete tests locally every night and to keep CI for pull requests quick.
- Decision: (1) `ci.yml` (push to `main`, pull requests) runs `typecheck, lint, build` and one job `unit tests (no soak, no browser)` (`vitest run packages/engine packages/cards apps/web tools`), behind the final aggregate job still named `check`. The AI package (whose soak tests are the longest) and the browser tests are not in it. (2) The former complete CI moves to `full.yml`, manual only (`workflow_dispatch`), for when minutes allow; `soak.yml` loses its nightly schedule and stays manual (500 games, opens an issue on failure). `coverage.yml` is unchanged (about one minute). (3) The complete verification is a scheduled routine run in the cloud environment every night on `main` (`pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm lint`, `pnpm test`, `pnpm test:soak`, `pnpm build`, `pnpm e2e`); a failure opens an issue on GitHub. This replaces the nightly `Soak` workflow of D-126 and the "CI runs everything on every push" of D-126 as amended.
- Alternatives: Pay for more minutes (a spending limit): left to the owner, not needed for this decision. Make the repository public (free Actions): done later, which made the nightly run on GitHub possible (D-250). Keep the full CI and accept red checks: rejected, red checks that say nothing hide real failures.
- Consequences: A pull request gets a result in minutes and costs about a tenth of before. A failure that only the AI soak tests or the browser tests would show is found the same night, on `main`, not on the pull request; fix it on the next branch, and a seed that fails becomes a scenario test. A pull request that touches `packages/ai` or `apps/web/e2e` is verified by the author's local checks (D-126) until the nightly run.
- Status: Partly superseded by D-250: the repository is public, so the complete suite runs every night on GitHub's runners (`full.yml`, scheduled and manual) when `main` has a new commit, and opens an issue when it fails; the quick `ci.yml` and the job `check` stand.

## D-133: Filtered subjects, lords and conditions, creature costs, a death replacement and casting from the graveyard (2026-10-27)
- Context: After the amounts slice (D-131) `reports/decks.md` (parser version 33) lists 174 blocking rows for the owner's five decks. The owner asked for the biggest families still open as general primitives in the who, event, filter and amount style, never one rule for one card: triggers whose subject is a filtered creature, static lord effects, grants until end of turn to a filter, and activated abilities whose cost taps or sacrifices other permanents, with the smaller rows next to them (a replacement of a death, casting a card from the graveyard). `ENGINE_VERSION` 29. Only the real wordings of the report are used below; the row numbers are the `#` column of "Blockers across the decks".
- Survey (68 rows read one by one; (a) the engine already ran it and only the parser lacks the wording, (b) a small engine gap, built in this slice, (c) a larger gap, left out with a reason in `docs/ROADMAP.md`). **Triggers on a filtered subject or about a player (28 rows):** (a) 3: 71 (cast "a noncreature or Dragon spell": `castSpell` with an `anyOf`), 84 (Kappa Cannoneer: an `entersBattlefield` of a filtered artifact with two effects on `this`), 148 (a Dragon enters: a counter on `this` and an additive `setTypes` plus `grantKeyword`). (b) 16: 64, 65, 85, 149 (a nontoken creature dies, "~ or another nontoken Zombie dies" as two abilities), 150 (another nontoken Dragon enters), 67 (another nontoken creature enters: "it" gets a counter and haste), 62 (a creature with flying enters: "it" gains haste), 153 (a colorless spell is cast), 60 and 61 (a creature attacks you or a planeswalker you control: investigate, "that creature's controller loses N life"), 80 (combat damage to a player: "that player discards a card"), 66 (an opponent draws: "that player loses N life"), 57 (a Dragon you control becomes the target of an opponent's spell or ability: damage "to that player"), 82 and 159 (is dealt damage: draw a card, "you gain that much life"), 83 (Noxious Ghoul: "~ or another Zombie enters" and "all non-Zombie creatures get -N/-N until end of turn"). (c) 9: 55 and 56 (a batch of creatures that together deal combat damage, and a choice not yet made this turn), 151 and 152 (several creatures that attack together), 58 (a trigger of a card in the graveyard), 59 and 73 (the commander as a filter), 68 (Angelic Sleuth: a condition on the counters the leaving permanent had), 74 (stun counters). **Statics (21 rows):** (a) 2: 33 (Lord of the Undead: a lord over "other Zombie creatures", every controller), 39 (Death Baron: an `anyOf` of "Skeletons you control" and "other Zombies you control", two statics). (b) 10: 32 and 34 (nontoken lords), 122 (colorless lord), 8 (Angelic Field Marshal: "as long as you control your commander"), 10 and 174 (as long as you have N life, or N more than your starting life), 115 (as long as it's untapped), 118 (as long as you control N artifacts), 120 (an attack tax as long as ~ is untapped), 24 (Challenger Troll: "can't be blocked by more than one creature" for creatures with power 4 or greater).
