(c) 9: 9 (grants a triggered ability), 121 (grants a keyword the engine cannot grant), 127 (an Aura's "unless that player is the monarch": the controller of the host is no reference there), 133 (base power and toughness and creature types set by a lord), 134 (a keyword in the subject of a static ability: a dependency in layer 6, CR 613.8), 136 (Rhonas: "can't attack or block unless": no `cantAttack` and a power in a condition), 111 and 132 (can't be blocked by creatures with power N or less, by Walls: an evasion that names the blockers), 119 (creatures can't block unless their controller pays: a tax on blocking). **Grants until end of turn to a filter (3 rows):** (a) 3: 96 (All Zombies gain menace), 170 (Dragons you control get +N/+N), 158 (each creature you control with power N or greater gets +N/+N and gains trample). **Costs that tap or sacrifice other permanents (8 rows):** (b) 5: 40 (Cryptbreaker), 41 (Whirler Rogue), 137 (tap N untapped artifacts), 93 (Sai: sacrifice two artifacts), 95 (Ghoulcaller Gisa: sacrifice another creature, "X is the sacrificed creature's power"). (c) 3: 94 (return an artifact you control to its owner's hand as a cost, then "put an artifact card from your hand onto the battlefield"), 162 (an alternative cost that taps untapped creatures with flying), 78 (an effect, not a cost: "tap X untapped Myr"). **A death replacement and casting from the graveyard (4 rows):** (b) 2: 30 (Kalitas), 92 (Gravecrawler). (c) 2: 7 (a static ability that works from the graveyard), 109 (an effect that lets a player cast a creature card from a graveyard this turn). **Filter parts of rows outside the four families (4 rows):** (b) 4: 49 (destroy all creatures with flying), 112 (each non-Dragon creature), 114 (each creature without flying and each planeswalker), 147 (target nontoken creature): the engine runs them once the filter has the parts. **Totals: (a) 8 rows, (b) 37, (c) 23**; the parser can lower 45 rows after this slice.
- Decision: (1) **Filter parts** (`ObjectFilter`, read by `rules/filter-match.ts`): `token` (`true` tokens, `false` "nontoken", CR 111.1: an object whose `token` data is set, also for a permanent that was a copy of a spell, CR 707.10f, and for the last-known information of one that left), `notSubtypes` ("non-Zombie"), `colorless`, `keywords` and `notKeywords` ("with flying", "without flying", the keywords without parameters, read from the derived abilities, or from the last-known abilities of a permanent that left). A static ability may not name a keyword in its subject or in a count it reads (they would depend on layer 6, CR 613.8): `validateCard` refuses it. Feature ids `selector:token`, `selector:nontoken`, `selector:notSubtypes`, `selector:colorless`, `selector:keywords`. (2) **Triggers.** The subject of every trigger that names a permanent already took a filter, so nontoken, subtype, controller and `other` needed only (1). New: `attacks.at` (`you`, or `youOrPlaneswalkers`: the attack is declared at the controller of the ability as a player, or also at a planeswalker that player controls, CR 508.1b; feature `trigger:attacksAt`), the trigger kind `dealtDamage { what, combat? }` ("whenever ~ is dealt damage", once for each source that damages the permanent, in the moment the damage is dealt, so it triggers for lethal damage and not for prevented damage, CR 120.3, 603.2g), `PlayerSelector` `triggerPlayer` ("that player", "that creature's controller": the drawer of `drawn`, the player damaged by `dealsCombatDamage` (not for `to: 'creature'`), the caster of `castSpell`, the controller of what targeted for `becomesTarget`, the attacking player of `attacks`, the sacrificing player of `permanentSacrificed`, the controller of the damage source (last-known information) for `dealtDamage`), `Amount` `triggerDamage` ("that much": the damage of a `dealtDamage` or `dealsCombatDamage` event), and `triggerSubject` as the object of any continuous effect and of `addCounters` ("it gains haste until end of turn", "put a +1/+1 counter on it"); `PendingTrigger.player`/`damage` become `StackData.triggerPlayer`/`triggerDamage` and `ResolutionContext`/`SelectContext`, and an ability that reads them joins them into the identity of its triggers (`rules/trigger-stack.ts`, as the subject does). `controllerOf` of `triggerSubject` already existed (D-111). `validateCard` allows each only where the trigger has it (`hasPlayer`, `hasDamage` in `ast/validate.ts`). "~ or another nontoken Zombie you control dies" stays two abilities (one event is one of them, because "another" leaves the source out). (3) **Lords and grants.** Nothing new: a static `modifyPt` and `grantKeyword` over a `filter` subject with `other` and `anyOf` (layer 7c and layer 6, CR 613.4c, 613.1f) and an `each` selector of `modifyPt` or `grantKeyword` for "until end of turn" (the set is fixed as the effect resolves, CR 611.2c) were run since D-094 and D-115; `scenario-xx-lords.test.ts` pins them (several lords stack, a lord that leaves mid-turn, a Zombie that enters later, anyOf with `other`, the set of a grant). (4) **Conditional statics.** `Ability` `static` takes `condition?`: the ability applies "as long as" it holds. It is read by `derive` through `rules/static-conditions.ts` (`staticConditionHolds`), which reads only what no layer 7 effect changes (CR 613.8): counts by `typeViewOf` (as the amounts of D-115), the life total, commanders, designations and the source's own types and tapped status; it never imports `derive`, and the answers are kept per state (`WeakMap`, never stale: a state is not changed in place). Conditions: `controlsAtLeast`, `controlCommander` (new field `yours`: a commander the controller owns, CR 903.3, so another player's commander that you control is not "your commander"), `lifeTotal { compare, aboveStarting? }` (CR 119.1: the life total, or its difference from the starting life total, `GameSettings.startingLife`), `thisMatches { filter }` (this permanent against a filter: "as long as it's untapped"), `playerHasDesignation`, `and`, `or`, `not`. `lifeTotal`, `thisMatches` and `controlCommander.yours` also run as an intervening "if", in a `conditional` effect and as "activate only if" (`rules/conditions.ts`, sharing `rules/condition-reads.ts`). Only `modifyPt`, `grantKeyword`, `grantAbility` and `restriction` (not `cantBeCountered`) go through `derive`; `attackTax` and `castFromGraveyard` read the condition where they act, with `evaluateCondition`; every other static ability is refused with a condition (`ast/validate-static-condition.ts`), because it would silently ignore it. A condition that reads power, toughness, keywords, the combat, X, kicks or counters is refused. Feature ids `ability:staticCondition`, `condition:lifeTotal`, `condition:thisMatches`. (5) **A limit on blockers.** `Restriction` `cantBeBlockedByMoreThanOne` (CR 509.1b): `validateBlocks` refuses a second blocker, the declare-blockers decision carries `maxBlockers: 1` for the attacker (the random agent keeps within it), and with menace nothing can block it (CR 702.111b: two blockers needed, one allowed). A restriction is read where the rule acts, after the layers, so its static subject may now compare power (`supported.ts` allowed it for `modifyPt` only; the comparison reads the power after the effects that change it, CR 613.8). (6) **Costs.** `Cost` `tapPermanents { filter, count }` ("tap three untapped Zombies you control": the permanents the player controls that match and are untapped, the source among them unless `other`; summoning sickness does not apply, CR 302.6; with more candidates than `count` a `choosePermanent` decision of purpose `tap` and `forCost` asks, with as many as needed the engine taps them and says so with `permanentsChosen`; it is paid before the sacrifice and the discard; refused with a mana cost, another tap cost or a crew cost, because the player could tap the permanents for mana first), `Cost` `sacrifice` takes `count` (2 or more, only for the cost of an activated ability), and `ObjectRef` `sacrificedCost` ("the sacrificed creature") read by `powerOf`, `toughnessOf`, `manaValueOf` and `countersOn` in an activated ability whose cost sacrifices something: the activation remembers the permanents it sacrificed (`StackData.sacrificedAsCost`, old ids) and the amount reads their last-known information (CR 113.7a, 608.2h: power with every effect, tokens too). Feature ids `cost:tapPermanents`, `selector:sacrificedCost`. (7) **A death replacement.** `Replacement` `wouldDie { what, instead: 'exile', alsoCreate? }` (CR 614.1a, 700.4): `moveObject` asks `rules/die-replacement.ts` for every creature moved from the battlefield to a graveyard, so destruction, lethal damage, zero toughness, a sacrifice and the legend rule are all replaced; the creature is exiled and never dies (no "dies" trigger, "leaves the battlefield" triggers do fire), and the controller of the permanent with the ability creates `alsoCreate.count` tokens. `what` is relative to the controller of that permanent. Creatures that die together (a "destroy all" effect, a state-based action, CR 704.3) replace each other's deaths (CR 614.12): the permanents with the replacement as the event began are named once (`replacementSources`, carried by the `move` instructions and by the state-based action loop as `MoveRequest.replacers`), so a Kalitas that dies with the opponent's creatures still replaces theirs. Several replacements for one creature: the oldest permanent's is applied and nothing is asked (CR 616.1, `docs/ROADMAP.md`). Feature id `replacement:wouldDie`. (8) **Casting from the graveyard.** Static `castFromGraveyard` (CR 113.6b), with the ability's `condition`: the owner may cast the card from their graveyard at the timing its type allows, paying its ordinary cost (no alternative cost is combined with it, no commander tax); `castZone` and `castableObjects` read it (`mayCastFromGraveyard` in `rules/legality.ts`), the scenario DSL's `cast` finds a card of that name in the graveyard when none is in the hand, and a face has it once and is not a land. Feature id `static:castFromGraveyard`. (9) `SUPPORTED_FEATURES`, `FeatureRef` and the lists gain the ids above (`trigger:dealtDamage`, `selector:triggerPlayer`, `amount:triggerDamage`, `restriction` list). The web has only the wording its type check needs (listed in `docs/MECHANICS.md`).
- Alternatives: A `token` filter field written `nontoken: true`: rejected, one boolean says both tokens and nontokens and the parser needs both. A new trigger kind for "attacks you or a planeswalker you control": rejected, `attacks` with a field is the same event with a narrower occurrence, as `alone`. "That player" as `controllerOf` of the trigger subject for every event: rejected, a drawn card, a damaged player and a spell's caster are not permanents the player controls (the drawn card changes object as it moves). A condition on every static ability, read by every consumer: rejected, a consumer that forgot it would run the ability unconditionally; the validator refuses the kinds that do not read it. Evaluating conditions in `derive` with `evaluateCondition`: rejected, it derives other permanents and loops (a condition that counts creatures while the creature's own power is being worked out); `static-conditions.ts` reads the layer 4 and 5 view only. Static `setPt`/`setTypes` over a filter, "grants an ability" and a keyword filter in a static subject: not built (rows 133, 9 and 134), each a larger change to the layers. Making tapping a creature for a cost wait for the mana: rejected, tapping first and refusing the combination with mana keeps the legal actions sound (an ability the engine offers is one it can pay). A "tapped" flag on the filter of `tapPermanents`: refused with a message, the engine adds it. Reading the sacrificed power from the stack object's `lki`: rejected for a list of old ids, which reads the right entry of `GameState.lki` and works for several permanents. Choosing among several death replacements: left for a slice with a replacement-choice decision (also for the commander replacement of CR 903.9b, which has its own).
- Consequences: The parser (next task) lowers the real lines listed with each primitive in `docs/MECHANICS.md` ("Filter parts", "Triggers on a filtered subject and the player an event is about", "Lords and grants until end of turn to a filter", "Conditional static abilities", "A limit on blockers", "Costs that tap or sacrifice other permanents and the sacrificed creature", "If a creature would die", "Casting a card from the graveyard"); its `needs` use the feature ids above. The web needs the decision purpose `tap`, `maxBlockers`, the graveyard cast option, wording for the conditions and the new trigger, and the log line for the tapped permanents. The 23 rows of (c) stay unsupported with their reasons in `docs/ROADMAP.md`. Behavior changes: none for a card without the new nodes; a state-based action loop and a destroy effect carry the list of replacers, which is empty unless a permanent has a replacement of a death.

## D-134: Creature types in the grammar come from the CR table, and their plurals from English endings (2026-10-27)
- Context: Parser stage P29 reads groups of creatures by type ("Other Zombie creatures get +1/+1", "Skeletons you control and other Zombies you control", "Wolves you control have trample", "Merfolk you control", "Time Lords you control"). The owner asked for general grammar, not a rule for one type. Before, the parser had its own word list of types; the engine already has `CREATURE_TYPES`, 324 types generated from CR 205.3m (`pnpm creature-types:generate`), among them the two-word "Time Lord", the typographic apostrophe of C’tan and Shi’ar, and the hyphenated Assembly-Worker.
- Decision: (1) The grammar asks the engine table (`rules/noun/creature-types.ts` imports `CREATURE_TYPES`; no type is listed by hand). (2) The plural of a type is generated from its ending (`regularPlurals`: "s", "es" after s, x, z, ch and sh, "ies" after a consonant and y, "ves" after f and fe), and both forms are read for the f and fe types ("Elves" and "Elfs"), because the table cannot say which of "Wolves" and "Giraffes" is which and a form no card prints reads harmlessly. (3) The only two places that name a type are `IRREGULAR_PLURALS` (Child, Cyberman, Cyclops, Fungus, Hero, Homunculus, Mouse, Nautilus, Octopus, Ox, Pegasus) and `INVARIANT_TYPES` (types that are their own plural: Aurochs, Astartes, Custodes, Eldrazi, Fish, Kithkin, Merfolk, Moonfolk, Nephilim, Sheep, Thalakos, Treefolk). These come from English usage, not from the text of a card: the 1000 shapes of `reports/` and the blocker rows of `reports/decks.md` show only regular plurals ("Zombies", "Dragons", "Skeletons", "Orcs", "Birds", "Frogs", "Otters", "Rats", "Humans", "Squirrels", "Bats", "Juggernauts", "Walls"), so every irregular form is UNVERIFIED against an Oracle text until a real line shows one. (4) A plural form that two types would share is left out (nothing is guessed); a word that is the singular of a type is that type. (5) The dispatch words of a rule that may start with a group of creatures (`TYPE_LEADING_WORDS`) are derived from the table.
- Alternatives: A hand-written plural for every type: rejected, 324 entries from memory would be invented data. Reading any capitalized word as a type: rejected, "Other Elves" and "Target Creature" would read as types and nothing would tell a type from a name. Only the plurals the reports show: rejected, the next deck brings a type that is not in the reports and the owner asked for the general rule. Leaving the f/fe ambiguity to a list of the types that keep "s": rejected for the same reason as the hand-written plurals.
- Consequences: `parser-p29-types.test.ts` loops over all 324 types and proves that each reads in the singular and in each generated plural form, that no two types share a form, that the two lists name only types of the table and forms the ending rules do not already give, and that a lord, a trigger subject, a group grant and a tap cost lower for every type; five sample types, a two-word type and "of the chosen type" are tested with the same rules, so no rule is tied to one type. A real line with an irregular plural that is not in the lists reads as unrecognised (never half run); adding it means one entry in `IRREGULAR_PLURALS` with the Oracle line as evidence.

## D-135: Moving cards with a condition on the card, "you may ... if you do", reflexive triggers, Gift, graveyard casting and abilities, "enters untapped" and life paid by an amount (2026-10-27)
- Context: The owner's Zombies precon lacks seven cards (`reports/decks.md`, parser 34): Cemetery Recruitment, Consumed by Greed, God-Eternal Bontu, Razorlash Transmogrant, Undead Butler, Witch's Cottage and Zul Ashur, Lich Lord; War Room blocks a card in four decks, Scrapshooter (Dinosaurs) needs Gift, and Bitter Reunion and Hazoret's Monument wait for `condition:didPrevious`. The owner asked for general primitives in the who, action, filter and amount style (D-131, D-133), never a rule for one card, with the parser to follow once the exact Oracle text of these cards was extracted (`packages/cards/test/fixtures/corpus/golden.jsonl`, the last nine lines). `ENGINE_VERSION` 30. SYNTHETIC fixtures: `cards/fixtures/synthetic-recursion.ts`, `synthetic-gift.ts`, `synthetic-graveyard.ts`, each of the shapes over several creature types (Zombie, Goblin, Angel, Dinosaur).
- Survey (what existed, what was built). 1 Return a creature card from a graveyard to the hand, the battlefield, or the top of the library: already built (`moveToZone` of a target with a graveyard filter, `withCounters`, `position`); missing was a condition on the moved card and the position "third from the top". 2 `didPrevious` and reflexive triggers: missing. 3 Gift: missing; "target opponent sacrifices a creature with the greatest power among creatures they control": a sacrifice chosen by another player existed (`sacrifice.player`), the maximum did not. 4 "Sacrifice any number of other permanents, then draw that many": `thisWay` `sacrificed` existed, "any number" did not. 5 "dies or is put into exile from the battlefield": `leavesBattlefield.to` took one zone. 6 "You may cast target Zombie card from your graveyard this turn": D-133's static permission only; missing as an effect with a duration. 7 Activated abilities that work from the graveyard: `functionsIn: 'graveyard'` existed for Unearth only; missing the reduction of the cost and "nonbasic". 8 "When this land enters untapped": missing. 9 War Room: the amount `commanderColors` existed (D-131), `payLife` took a number.
- Decision: (1) **A condition on a card an earlier instruction moved.** `Condition` `objectMatches { of, filter }` with `of` a `target` or `moved` reference: the object as it is or, once it has left, from last-known information (CR 113.7a, 608.2h), against a filter with no zone, controller or owner (it describes the object, in whatever zone it was in). Only a `conditional` effect reads it (`validateCard` refuses it as an intervening "if", "activate only if" and the like): `ConditionContext` gains `targets`, `moved` and `performed`, passed by the interpreter. "If it's a Zombie card" and "if it's an Angel" are the same node with another subtype. (2) **"You may", "if you do" and reflexive triggers.** `Effect` `may { effect }` asks the controller (the existing `mayEffect` instruction); `ResolutionContext.performed` counts what the instructions since the last `may` actually did (a move, a sacrifice, the cards discarded, drawn or milled, reported by each instruction in `StepOutcome.performed`; a `may` resets it), so an empty hand or library is "not done". `Condition` `didPrevious` reads `performed > 0` and is valid only in a `conditional` after a `may` in the same sequence. `Effect` `reflexive { targets?, effect }` (CR 603.12) creates, if `performed > 0`, a `PendingTrigger` of the source of the ability (`abilityIndex` -1, as delayed triggers have, `rules/may-effects.ts`) that goes on the stack the next time a player would receive priority with its targets chosen then (CR 603.3d), so a card the first part put into the graveyard can be named and an ability with no legal target is removed; it knows nothing of the targets, `moved` or trigger subject of the ability that made it, and is the last effect of its sequence. `may` wraps only `discard`, `sacrifice`, `exile`, `moveToZone`, `draw` or `mill`: the effects whose doing the engine can tell. (3) **Sacrifice choices.** `ChooseSelector` gets `anyNumber` (the choice has `min` 0 and `max` the number of candidates, asked even with one candidate) and `greatest` (`power`, `toughness` or `manaValue`: the candidates limited to those with the greatest value among them as `derive` gives it now; the player who sacrifices, the one named by `sacrifice.player`, chooses among the tied ones); both belong to `sacrifice`. (4) **Library position and several zones.** `moveToZone.position` takes a number of 2 or more, "Nth from the top" (CR 401.7: below the first N - 1 cards, or last when the library has fewer than N; `addToZone`), and `leavesBattlefield.to` takes a list of two or more zones ("dies or is put into exile from the battlefield" is `['graveyard', 'exile']`). `exile` accepts `thisCard` ("you may exile it"). (5) **Gift** (CR 702.174). `Keyword` `gift { gift: 'card' }`. As a spell is cast, after the kicker and replicate questions and before X and the targets (CR 601.2b), `rules/cast-gift.ts` asks `confirmOptional` of purpose `gift` naming the opponent the gift would go to (`ConfirmOptionalDecision.giftTo`; with several opponents each is offered in turn order; `cancel` rewinds the cast, CR 733), and keeps the chosen opponent on the spell (`StackData.giftTo`; a copy of the spell copies it, CR 707.10) and on the permanent it becomes (`GameObject.giftTo`). `Condition` `giftPromised` reads it with last-known information, `PlayerSelector` `giftRecipient` ("the chosen player") likewise. The engine writes the two abilities itself: a permanent gets the trigger "when this enters, if the gift was promised, the chosen player draws a card" (`GIFT_ABILITY` in `rules/derive-keywords.ts`, with an intervening "if" checked twice); an instant or sorcery with a promised gift runs the draw before every other effect as it resolves (`giftEffectOf`, `rules/stack.ts`) and so never when it is countered (CR 702.174j). `TargetSpec.ifGiftPromised` marks a slot that exists only when the gift was promised (CR 702.174m): `targetSpecsOf` leaves it out otherwise, the gift is not offered when such a slot could not be filled, and `validateCard` requires every use of the slot to sit in the effect of a `giftPromised` `conditional`. Only "Gift a card" is built. (6) **A cast permission with a duration.** `Effect` `mayCast { objects: target, duration: 'untilEndOfTurn' }` adds a continuous effect `castPermission { seat }` (kept in `continuousEffects`, so the cleanup step ends it, CR 514.2) on each card of the controller's graveyard the target names; `mayCastFromGraveyard` (`rules/legality.ts`) also reads it, so the card is cast at the timing of its type for its ordinary cost, with no alternative cost, no commander tax and no exile. The card is a new object if it leaves the graveyard (CR 400.7), so the permission is gone with it. (7) **An ability that works from the graveyard, with a cheaper cost under a condition.** A card's activated ability with `functionsIn: 'graveyard'` is listed from the owner's graveyard (`hasGraveyardAbility`). `Ability` `activated.costReducedIf { generic, condition }`: when the condition holds as the ability is activated, `generic` is taken off the generic part of its first mana cost (CR 601.2f; `rules/activate-adjust.ts` `adjustedAbility` gives the ability that is paid and put on the stack, with the amounts of its life payments worked out and no `costReducedIf` left, so the stack object shows what was paid and the rest of the activation code reads a plain cost). `Condition` `opponentControlsAtLeast { filter, count }` (some one opponent controls that many matching permanents) and `ObjectFilter.notSupertypes` ("nonbasic land") are its parts. (8) **"Enters untapped".** `entersBattlefield.tapped` (`false` "enters untapped", `true` "enters tapped") is read as the event is noticed (the state its enters replacements left it in), not as an intervening "if" that is read again as the ability resolves (a land tapped for mana in response would fail that, CR 603.6a). (9) **Life paid by an amount.** `Cost` `payLife.amount` is an `Amount` (a number, or an amount that reads the game now: the same set as `amountIs`); `adjustedAbility` works it out once as the ability is activated (CR 118.3, 119.4: the player must have that much life, which `costRefusal` checks), and the costs of a spell, a mana ability, "unless pays" and "enters tapped unless you pay" stay numbers (`unsupportedFeatureIssues` refuses an amount there). (10) `SUPPORTED_FEATURES`, `FeatureRef` and the lists gain: effects `may`, `reflexive`, `mayCast`; conditions `didPrevious`, `objectMatches`, `giftPromised`, `opponentControlsAtLeast`; selectors `notSupertypes`, `anyNumber`, `greatest`, `giftRecipient`; the keyword `gift`; trigger features `entersUntapped`, `leavesToAnyOf`; ability features `costReducedIf`, `ifGiftPromised`.
- Alternatives: A separate cost kind for life by an amount: rejected, `payLife` with an `Amount` is the same cost and the parser's IR already carries an `IrAmount` for it. Telling "if you do" from the events of the resolution: rejected, a sacrifice that found nothing to sacrifice emits nothing, while a counted `performed` says "not done" exactly. Making every effect report what it did: rejected for the six kinds a `may` may wrap; the others are refused by `validateCard` rather than guessed. The reflexive ability as a plain `triggered` ability the card lists: rejected, it triggers from the resolution that made it (CR 603.12), not from an event. "Enters untapped" as `interveningIf` `thisMatches { tapped: false }`: rejected, see (8). Gift as an `additionalCosts` entry: rejected, the cost is a choice of an opponent, and the two abilities the keyword stands for are the engine's own, as for the other keywords. A kicker-style detection of the target that exists only if the gift was promised (`kickerOnlyTargets`, refused): rejected, the explicit flag lets the engine ask for it. The permission as a list in the game state: rejected, continuous effects already end with the turn. Making the gift offered by a `chooseOption` of seats: rejected, a yes or no for each opponent needs no new decision kind.
- Consequences: The parser (next task) lowers the real lines listed with each primitive in `docs/MECHANICS.md` ("Recursion, Gift and graveyard abilities (D-135)"). The web must word: the decision `confirmOptional` with purpose `gift` (`giftTo`), the event field `spellCast.gift`, the `choosePermanent` decision with `min` 0 (any number), `Cost` `payLife` with an amount (`costText`, built as a basic sentence), `leavesBattlefield.to` as a list (built), `PlayerSelector` `giftRecipient` (built), a graveyard `activate` option (the ability is listed under the card in the graveyard) and a cast permission (a `castSpell` option of a card in the graveyard, as D-133's). Behavior changes: none for a card without the new nodes. Limits, each in `docs/ROADMAP.md`: Gift of a card only; `may` of the six kinds; one reflexive trigger as the last effect of its sequence; the gift offered to each opponent in turn (the engine runs two seats, so that path has no test); a life amount only as the cost of an activated ability; `greatest` only in a sacrifice; the permission only for a card in a graveyard.

## D-136: The parser reads the recursion slice: conditions on "it", offers and reflexive abilities as sentences, one graveyard source, and costs and amounts (2026-10-27)
- Context: D-135 built the engine primitives and listed, for each, what the parser must produce. The golden corpus now holds the real Oracle text of the nine cards the Zombies precon still lacked (`packages/cards/test/fixtures/corpus/golden.jsonl`): Cemetery Recruitment, God-Eternal Bontu, Scrapshooter, Undead Butler, Razorlash Transmogrant, Witch's Cottage, War Room, Zul Ashur, Lich Lord and Consumed by Greed. The owner's brief was general rules (D-131, D-133, D-134): a condition on any creature type of the CR table, a filter on any card type, a count of any kind of permanent, never a rule for a card. `PARSER_VERSION` 35, stage P30.
- Decision: (1) **"If it's a Zombie card" is a condition on the pronoun.** `condition.it-matches` reads "it's a/an <creature types and card types, or modifiers and card types>" [card] and builds `IrCondition` `objectMatches { who, filter }`; the binding pass binds `who` as it binds every "it" (to the most recent single object, a target of the text); lowering gives the engine's `objectMatches` of that target, or of `moved` once an earlier instruction put the target onto the battlefield (`LowerContext.movedOnto`, CR 400.7), and `RefOptions.moved` carries the same substitution to counters ("put two +1/+1 counters on it") and nowhere else, because an amount that reads the target as it was ("equal to that card's mana value") must keep naming the target. (2) **An offer is a sentence and the sentence after it.** `lowerMay` lowers an optional sentence of one instruction followed by "If you do," (`IrCondition` `didPrevious`, read since stage P21) or "When you do," (`IrSentence.reflexive`) to `may` plus `conditional` or `reflexive`; only the six effects the engine can tell were done are wrapped (`MAY_KINDS` mirrors `MAY_EFFECT_KINDS` of the engine's validator, which stays the last gate); the reflexive ability is the last effect and its targets are taken out of the ability's own list. A lone "you may" instruction stays the ability's `optional`; the offer to pay stays `mayPay`. Only a triggered ability's body reads "you may" and these two lead words, as before. (3) **"It" in a dying trigger is the card.** When every event of a trigger is `~` dying or leaving the battlefield (`LowerContext.itIsCard`), "it" is `thisCard` for the two effects that move that card (`exile`, `putLibrary`); `noun.it` also reads "her" and "him" (CR 109.1) so "put her into her owner's library" is the same rule as "put it ...". (4) **Library position, how it entered, where it went.** `effect.put-library-nth` (second to tenth), `trigger.enters-state` and `trigger.leaves-to` (a list or one zone). (5) **Gift** is the keyword line "Gift a card" only (the other gifts are other abilities of the engine's table and stay unread); a sentence that begins "If the gift was promised," marks the targets it declares `ifGiftPromised` (CR 702.174m), and the intervening "if" of a permanent's trigger does not. (6) **A graveyard source.** "Return this card from your graveyard to the battlefield [with counters]" lowers only inside the lowering of an ordinary activated ability, which sets `LowerContext.graveyardSource`; the ability must be one instruction with mana costs and then has `functionsIn: 'graveyard'`. "This ability costs {N} less to activate if ..." is a restriction sentence (the segmenter treats it like "Activate only ...") and lowers to `costReducedIf` for an ordinary activation. (7) **Costs and amounts.** `cost.pay-life-amount` is its own rule so Ward, Cycling and Equip keep reading a number; the lowering takes an amount only in an ordinary activated ability. `amount.that-many` is `thisWay sacrificed`, and `thisWaysAreSupported` refuses it unless an instruction before it in the text sacrificed. `noun.any-number-permanents` and `noun.a-greatest-permanent` (the same kind of permanent said twice) are the nouns of the two sacrifice choices; "nonbasic" is a filter part (`notSupertypes`, CR 205.4). (8) **Diagnostics are kept.** The new rules that start like an older one carry a lookahead or sit before it, so the lines the grammar does not read still stop where they stopped.
- Alternatives: Naming the card or the creature type in a rule: rejected, the engine's primitives are general and the brief asked for general rules. `moved` for every "it" after a move: rejected, it changed the reading of "equal to that card's mana value" after a reanimation (a P11 test caught it); the option is given to the lowerings that act on the object. Reading "you may" and "if you do" in spells, activated abilities and modes: not done, the sentence parser asks for "you may" in a triggered ability only, and widening it for the others means a lowering for each body kind; the engine could run it. Extending `cost.pay-life` in place: rejected, the keyword rules that name `cost.pay-life` would then read "Ward—Pay life equal to ...", which the engine does not pay. Reading "unless it's a Zombie card" as `not`: not done, no real line asks for it. Reading the other gifts: not done, the engine runs only a card. A `may` for any effect: rejected, "if you do" after a gain of life could not be told from "not done".
- Consequences: The nine cards read and `validateCard` passes (the golden snapshot marks them supported: six training, three hold-out), and the siblings of `reports/decks.md` (Bitter Reunion, Hazoret's Monument, the Angels' counters, a Scrapshooter and an instant with Gift) read by the same rules; no card that was supported changed status or AST. Every lowering declares its features (`condition:objectMatches`, `giftPromised`, `opponentControlsAtLeast`, `didPrevious`; `effect:may`, `reflexive`, `mayCast`; `trigger:entersUntapped`, `leavesToAnyOf`; `keyword:gift`; `ability:costReducedIf`; `selector:thisCard`, `anyNumber`, `greatest`, `notSupertypes`; `amount:thisWay`), so an engine without one reports it by name. The lines the rules leave unread are in `docs/ROADMAP.md`, "Parser stage P30 known limitations". The owner reruns `pnpm corpus:decks` (and `pnpm coverage:cards` if the full run is wanted) with the bulk file: no coverage number was computed here.

## D-137: The player-facing decks are real precons from committed snapshots, and a game starts only from a valid, fully supported deck (2026-10-27)
- Context: The owner's Zombies deck reached 100% supported (`reports/decks.md`, parser 35), so M9's first real precon exists. The M3 test decks (D-047) were the only decks the menu offered, were not singleton and ignored color identity, and the import screen's sample list was one of them. SPEC 6.2, 15 M9 and A16 say precons ship with a pre-fetched card-data snapshot so Quick start works offline, and D-056 says a deck with an unsupported card cannot be played. The sandbox cannot reach Scryfall and does not hold the bulk file, so the owner generates the snapshot.
- Decision: (1) **A precon is a decklist plus a snapshot**, `apps/web/src/precons/snapshots/<id>.json`: id, name, blurb, the bulk file's base name, the decklist exactly as given and the stored cards (`StoredCard` of SPEC 6.2 without `fetchedAt`; deterministic: fixed key order, sorted cards, no timestamp). The format and its reader and writer live in `packages/cards/src/precon/` (the one small addition to a package: the tool and the web app must read and write the same thing). `pnpm precon:snapshot` (`tools/precon`) writes it from the bulk file, matching names with the code of `pnpm corpus:decks`; a name that is not found, or an unreadable decklist line, exits 1 and writes nothing; unsupported cards and Commander-rule errors are warnings. (2) **A precon goes through the import pipeline**: the web app builds an import service with a client that answers from the snapshot (`snapshotClient`) and the same support cache, overrides and community definitions as a pasted list (`createImportEnvironment().serviceFor`), then applies the shared rule. The menu lists exactly the snapshots that exist (eager `import.meta.glob`; none is fine: "No precon is installed yet" and Start is disabled). The opponent's precon reaches the Worker as prepared cards (`NewGameOptions.aiCards`, like `humanCards`). (3) **One rule for starting a game**: `checkPlayable(report)` in `import/deck.ts` (`unplayableReason` is its text): every name resolved, a commander, `validateDeck` ok (100 cards, singleton, color identity, legality, partners) and every card fully supported; it rechecks each condition and does not trust `report.playable` alone. The menu, `?autostart=` for real ids, "Play this deck" and a saved deck opened on the import screen all end in it; a refused deck shows its reason and nothing starts. (4) **The test decks left every player-facing list**: the three M3 decks moved into `HIDDEN_DECKS` (`game/precons.ts`, test fixtures, never offered to players), which stay reachable by id with `?autostart=<human>,<ai>` in every build. That is the one deliberate exception to (3), by the owner's decision: no dev or build flag gates them, so the end-to-end tests run against the built preview. A real precon id is checked first, so it wins over a hidden id of the same name. `?autostart=` also accepts real precon ids and `&freeMulligan=0`.
- Alternatives: Fetching the precon's cards from Scryfall at start: rejected, Quick start must work offline. Importing the snapshot lazily: rejected for now, the list is needed synchronously and one snapshot is small. Defining the snapshot type in the web app and again in the tool: rejected, two copies drift. Gating the hidden decks behind a dev flag: rejected by the owner, the tests need them in the built preview. Letting the AI mirror an imported deck when no precon is installed: rejected, it adds a feature for a state that ends with the first snapshot.
- Consequences: Without a committed snapshot the menu cannot start a game and the e2e tests that click a real menu entry or "Play this deck" skip with a reason; the lead reruns them once the owner commits `zombies.json`. A test over every shipped snapshot fails if one is not legal and fully supported, and a named test does so for the Zombies precon. D-047's decks are now fixtures only. A second precon is another `pnpm precon:snapshot` run and file, with no code change.

## D-138: Playtest fixes: stops before combat damage and for what is aimed at you, hover after a drag, the token frame, the HUD, mana untap (2026-10-27)
- Context: The owner played the Zombies precon and filed issues 35, 36, 34, 19, 8 and 7. Issue 35 looked like a rules bug: "when I hit confirm blockers, the game killed my creature immediately", with no time to use an ability of another card, even with Full Control on.
- Finding for issue 35 (a policy bug, not an engine bug). The engine is right: after blockers are declared the active player gets priority (CR 509.2), then the next player in turn order (CR 117.3d), and the step ends only when both pass in succession with an empty stack (CR 117.4), so combat damage cannot happen before the defender has had priority. `scenario-xx-combat-priority-before-damage.test.ts` pins this, for the declare blockers step and the declare attackers step, and for the human as the defending seat. The page's autopilot (A18, D-045) passed that window: with an empty stack it stopped only at the steps with a stop, and the default stops are the main phases of your own turn, so a player holding an affordable instant or non-mana ability was never asked. `apps/web/e2e/combat-priority.e2e.ts` reproduces it (the step jumps on to the next turn) and fails without the fix. Full Control could not be reproduced as broken: with it on, `shouldStop` is true at every priority, a seeded game played through the real host and store gives the defender priority in the step after every block (`combat-priority.test.ts`, which also passed before the policy change), and the Playwright test with Full Control (block, then the prompt reads "Opponent's turn, Blockers" and nothing has been dealt) passes. The owner's Full Control part of the report is not explained; it is recorded as not reproduced.
- Decision: (1) **Combat windows.** With an empty stack and a relevant action (`hasRelevantAction`: an instant-speed spell or a non-mana ability), the policy stops in the declare blockers step on either turn, and in the declare attackers step on the opponent's turn, when combat has attackers. On your own turn the declare attackers step does not stop by default (you just declared; the declare blockers step follows, and the player can add a stop in Settings). Nothing else stops by default as before. (2) **Targeted at you.** An opponent's spell or ability on the stack that targets the viewer or a permanent the viewer controls (CR 115.1) stops the autopilot even when the player has no response, so it can be read before it resolves; `StopSettings.stopWhenTargeted`, default on, a checkbox in Settings. The player's own objects still resolve without a click (D-045). (3) **Hover after a drag (issue 8).** The hover preview is held back while a card is dragged. When a drop plays the card, the dragged element leaves the hand, its `dragend` need not arrive, and the flag stayed set for the rest of the game while right-click still pinned: the symptom of the issue. A drop now ends the drag itself, and a pointer entering with no button held clears a stale flag (the browser sends no mouse events during a native drag). The sandbox's synthetic drag still sends `dragend`, so a test that fails without the fix could not be written; the fix is the plausible cause, not a proven one, and the owner should say if hover still stops. (4) **Tokens (issue 36).** Grouping already keeps tapped and untapped tokens apart; what looked mixed was the decorative card behind a group tile, always drawn upright behind a tapped (rotated) front card, and it now turns with it. Tokens have no card image, so they get the generic frame of SPEC 6.2 drawn from the view alone (colour tint, double border, a "Token <types> - <subtypes>" line, "Token" in the preview's type line). Real token images need `all_parts` data (Scryfall) that the snapshots do not carry, so none is fetched or invented. (5) **HUD (issue 34).** Both already existed but were easy to miss: the monarch chip was inside the life box and the commander damage text sat in the command box, which the action dock covers on the player's own strip. The top bar now names the monarch ("You are the monarch"), and commander damage taken is a chip beside the life total ("Cmdr 7/21", named in its tooltip); the command box text stays. The log's card names are hoverable one by one, each showing that card in the preview panel, also for a card that has since moved (a creature that died shows its graveyard card). The first main phase button says "Pass Turn" instead of "To Combat" when nothing the viewer controls can attack (read from the view: an untapped, non-sick creature without defender, or a Vehicle that could be crewed). (6) **Mana untap and attack buttons (issue 19).** Clicking a permanent tapped for mana whose mana is unspent takes the tap back: the store remembers the run of mana abilities used with nothing in between and clicking one takes back all the taps down to it (several `undo` calls, D-050), only while the history still ends at the last tap and the game waits for priority; it adds no engine path. The declare attackers buttons read "Attack with all" (left) and "Declare attackers (N)" (right). (7) **Issue 7** (repeated cards in a deck) is already covered by D-137: a game starts only from a valid, fully supported Commander deck, which includes the singleton rule; a test now starts from an import with a repeated nonbasic card and refuses it, with the legal basic land repeats accepted.
- Alternatives: Stop at every combat step for any holder of an instant: rejected, it would stop on the player's own attack with an instant in hand every turn; the windows are the two steps before blocks and before damage. A new engine step or flag for "the player must get priority": rejected, the engine already does. Showing the full card in the log on hover by object id only: rejected, a card that changed zone is a new object (CR 400.7) and the old id no longer resolves; names are matched against what is in view instead. Fetching token images from Scryfall: rejected for now (offline, no invented data). Making the mana untap an engine action: rejected, `undo` already exists and is the one way to take back a small action.
- Consequences: A player holding an instant or an activated ability is now asked once more per combat on defense (and after blocks on offense): `Settings` can turn off nothing but the targeted stop; a per-step toggle for these windows can follow if it annoys. The AI soak tests and the engine are untouched. Open (docs/ROADMAP.md): animation and pacing of combat, damage, destruction and fast spells; blocker grouping with arrows; the removal of the "Play this deck" box; token art.

## D-139: The Artifacts slice: mass effects, colors, living weapon, abilities that cost less or put counters, statics for a creature type, triggered mana, batch combat damage, a turn log, tapping a chosen number and reselecting an attack (2026-10-28)
- Context: After the Zombies slice (D-135) the owner's Artifacts precon (`reports/decks.md`, parser 35) lists 20 cards that block it: Adaptive Omnitool, Aetherize, All Is Dust, Duplicant, Fall from Favor, Forsaken Monument, Graaz Unstoppable Juggernaut, Master Transmuter, Mazemind Tome, Misleading Signpost, Myr Battlesphere, Nettlecyst, Nevinyrral's Disk, Padeem Consul of Innovation, Shimmer Myr, Soul-Guide Lantern, Steel Hellkite, Tamiyo's Logbook, Thirst for Knowledge and Thopter Spy Network. The owner asked for general primitives in the who, action, filter and amount style, never one rule for one card, with the parser and the web following in their own tasks (the exact Oracle text of the 20 is in the golden corpus, `packages/cards/test/fixtures/corpus/golden.jsonl`).
- Survey (the 20 lines of Oracle text read one by one against `SUPPORTED_FEATURES`). (a) The engine already ran it and only tests were missing: Aetherize (a mass move over a filter with `attacking`), Nevinyrral's Disk (a union of types with `anyOf`, indestructible and regeneration honored) and Soul-Guide Lantern (`exile each` with an `owner` filter); Padeem's hexproof, Forsaken Monument's lord and cast trigger, Steel Hellkite's flying and {2} pump, Thopter Spy Network's upkeep trigger and Nevinyrral's "enters tapped" were already general. (b) Built here, as 13 primitives and one way of asking their questions (below). (c) Left out with a reason, in `docs/ROADMAP.md`: a "considered to have attacked" record for a reselected attacker (CR 508.7a), a group `setTypes` that reads a post-static view (the dependency chains of CR 613.8), a cancel for a commander's question in the middle of a cost, choices among another player's cards, and linked exile from other than an ability's `exile` effect. No item is an S-class subsystem needing a proposal.
- Decision. (1) **Mass effects over a filter** (Aetherize, All Is Dust, Nevinyrral's Disk, Soul-Guide Lantern): `sacrifice` with an `each` selector (every permanent the filter names is sacrificed by its own controller, in APNAP order, CR 101.4, 701.21a); `ObjectFilter.colorCount` ("one or more colors", "two or more", "monocolored": a number compared with the colors the object has now, CR 105.2); the `kindred` card type (CR 308: All Is Dust is a Kindred Sorcery). (2) **A greatest value among permanents** (Padeem): `Condition` `controlsGreatest { filter, stat }`, true when the condition's controller controls one of the permanents with the largest `power`, `toughness` or `manaValue` among all matching battlefield permanents (a tie counts). (3) **Living weapon** (Nettlecyst; CR 702.92): `Keyword` `livingWeapon`, which `expandKeywords` turns into the enters trigger "create a 0/0 black Phyrexian Germ creature token, then attach this to it" (a `createToken` followed by an `attach` of `this` to `moved`); a `createToken` effect now reports the tokens it made as `moved` (CR 400.7j); only an Equipment may have the keyword. (4) **An activated ability that costs less for each of something** (Tamiyo's Logbook): `activated.costReducedBy { amount }` with any `Amount` that reads the game (a `countOf`, a `multiple`), worked out once as the ability is activated for its controller (CR 601.2f, 602.2b), after `costReducedIf`, generic mana only. (5) **Counters as a cost and a state trigger** (Mazemind Tome): `Cost` `putCounters { counter, count }` (paid with the {T}, before the mana, so the counters are there when something triggers from them), `Trigger` `state { condition }` (CR 603.8: triggers when the condition becomes true, once until it leaves the stack, found after every change by `rules/state-triggers.ts`), and `didPrevious` readable after any effect that reports what it did. (6) **Returning a permanent as a cost and putting a card onto the battlefield** (Master Transmuter): `Cost` `returnToHand { what, count }` (the `choosePermanent` decision with purpose `bounce` and `forCost`, a commander's owner asked in the middle of the activation, CR 903.9b), and `moveToZone` with a `choose` selector over the cards in your hand or graveyard (`ChooseSelector.optional`: none up to `count`; onto the battlefield, tapped or not). (7) **Statics for a creature type** (Graaz, Shimmer Myr, Duplicant, Fall from Favor): `StaticEffect` `setPt` (layer 7b, CR 613.4b), `setTypes` with named subtypes or card types for a subject group in addition to the rest (layer 4, CR 613.1d), `cantBeBlockedBy { subject, blockers }` (CR 509.1b), `castAsThoughFlash { spells }` (CR 601.3b: a filter on the spell), "exiled with this creature" (`exile.linked` remembers what an ability exiled, `takeFromLinkedExile` gives the power, toughness and creature types of the last such card, CR 607.2a), and `ObjectRef` `attached` (the creature an Aura or Equipment is attached to) for "tap enchanted creature". (8) **Discard unless, and look at the top cards** (Thirst for Knowledge, Adaptive Omnitool): `discard.unless { filter }` (an answer is the full count, or one single card of the list: `chooseCards` with `orSingle`), and `lookAtTop { count, take: { filter, max }, rest }` (`chooseCards` with purpose `lookTake` and `looked`, then the rest on the bottom in a random order from the game's generator, or into the graveyard). (9) **A triggered mana ability** (Forsaken Monument; CR 605.1b): `Trigger` `tappedForMana { what, by: 'you', mana? }` with an `addMana` of fixed mana, resolved without the stack into the same pool (CR 605.4a) and counted by the payment planner. (10) **Batch combat damage** (Thopter Spy Network; CR 603.2c): `Trigger` `combatDamageBatch { what, to, atLeast? }`, once for each player damaged in an event by sources the filter names. (11) **A log of the turn** (Steel Hellkite): `GameState.turnLog` (the activated abilities activated and the combat damage dealt to players, emptied as each turn begins), read by `activated.oncePerTurn` (CR 602.5b), `ObjectFilter.controllerDealtDamageBySource` (CR 510.2) and `ObjectFilter.manaValueX` (the X of the ability that resolves, CR 107.3a, 202.3), the last two only in an effect's `each` selector. (12) **Tapping a chosen number** (Myr Battlesphere; CR 701.26a): `tap` with a `choose` selector (`anyNumber` or `count`) among the untapped permanents you control, `Amount` `thisWay` `tapped`, `didPrevious` after a `tap` (tapping none is not doing it), and `dealDamage.to` `attackedBy { of }` (the player, planeswalker or battle the creature attacks, CR 508.1b). (13) **Reselecting an attack** (Misleading Signpost; CR 508.7): `Effect` `reselectAttack { objects }` (the controller of the effect chooses among what the creature's controller could attack, CR 508.7c; the creature stays in combat and nothing triggers again) and `Condition` `duringStep { step }` ("enters during the declare attackers step", as an `interveningIf`). (14) **No new decision kind.** The new questions reuse the existing ones with new purposes or fields, so the exhaustive handlers of the AI and the web keep compiling: `choosePermanent` purposes `bounce` (the return cost) and `effect` (tap a chosen number), `chooseCards` purposes `move` and `lookTake` and the fields `orSingle` and `looked`, `chooseOption` purpose `attackTarget` with `attacker` and `attackTargets` (options `player:<seat>` and `permanent:<object id>`); the events are `topCardsLooked`, `permanentsChosen` with purpose `bounce` and `optionChosen` with purpose `attackTarget`. `ENGINE_VERSION` 31.
- Alternatives: A `Cost` kind for "tap X untapped creatures" with a free number: rejected, the effect is not a cost and the number is the player's choice as it resolves, so the effect `tap` takes the choice. A new `chooseAttackTarget` decision kind: rejected for the same reason as every kind since D-002, it breaks every exhaustive handler for a question `chooseOption` can ask with a purpose. `duringStep` as a field of every trigger: rejected, a condition composes (`and`, `not`) and the intervening "if" already reads it at the same two points. A `Cost` for counters in the existing `removeCounters`: rejected, the direction is a different cost with a different rule (a state trigger reads the counters, so they must be there before the mana is paid). Reading the turn from the action log: rejected, the log is for replays and not for rules, a few lists in the state are cheaper and are part of the state hash. Per-card code for Duplicant, Graaz or Padeem: rejected by AGENTS.md; each is a primitive over a filter, a stat or a creature type, and the tests run each over two or three types or values.
- Consequences: The parser (next task) lowers the real lines listed with each primitive in `docs/MECHANICS.md` ("The Artifacts slice (D-139)"). The web must word: the `Cost` kinds `putCounters` and `returnToHand`; the effects `lookAtTop`, `reselectAttack`, `tap` with a `choose` selector, `discard.unless`, `exile.linked` and `moveToZone` of a chosen card from the hand or graveyard; `dealDamage.to` `attackedBy`; the ability fields `costReducedBy` and `oncePerTurn`; the triggers `state`, `tappedForMana` and `combatDamageBatch`; the conditions `controlsGreatest` and `duringStep`; the statics `setPt`, `cantBeBlockedBy`, `castAsThoughFlash`, `takeFromLinkedExile` and the named `setTypes`; the keyword `livingWeapon`; the filter parts `colorCount`, `manaValueX` and `controllerDealtDamageBySource` and the type `kindred`; the amount `thisWay` `tapped`; the decisions above (a dialog for `chooseOption` purpose `attackTarget`, which today would draw the creature type picker over `player:1`; the prompts and the `waitingOn` purposes `move` and `lookTake`; the cards of a `lookTake` shown only to the player who looks); and the events `topCardsLooked`, `permanentsChosen` purpose `bounce` and `optionChosen` purpose `attackTarget`. CasualAgent answers each new question (an attack target to reselect, the best card to take, one card or the full count for a discard with an alternative) and RandomLegalAgent takes the engine's listed answers; the `artifacts` deck style and `artifacts-games.test.ts` restate the rules of the slice from the events. Every primitive was mutation-checked on a scratch copy, three to seven mutants each; the survivors that were not equivalent became tests, and the ones left are defensive checks the validator makes unreachable (a counter cost off the battlefield, a returned permanent of another controller, a block limit whose filter names a controller, group types of a card that is not on the battlefield).

## D-140: The parser reads the Artifacts slice: groups and states as filter parts, three sentences as one instruction, a linked exile across lines, and "If you do" after what the engine can tell was done (2026-10-28)
- Context: D-139 built the engine primitives for the twenty cards the owner's Artifacts precon lacked and listed, for each, what the parser must produce (`docs/MECHANICS.md`, "The Artifacts slice (D-139)"). The golden corpus holds their real Oracle text (Adaptive Omnitool, Aetherize, All Is Dust, Duplicant, Fall from Favor, Forsaken Monument, Graaz, Master Transmuter, Mazemind Tome, Misleading Signpost, Myr Battlesphere, Nettlecyst, Nevinyrral's Disk, Padeem, Shimmer Myr, Soul-Guide Lantern, Steel Hellkite, Tamiyo's Logbook, Thirst for Knowledge, Thopter Spy Network). The brief was general rules (D-131, D-133, D-134): creature types from the CR table, card types and filters generic, no card names, and the obvious siblings read too.
- Decision: (1) **Filter parts, not rules per card.** "attacking", "monocolored", "multicolored" are modifiers of every permanent phrase; "with mana value X" and "whose controller was dealt combat damage by ~ this turn" are suffixes the lowering accepts only in an effect's `each` selector (where the engine reads them); a union of plural card types ("all artifacts, creatures, and enchantments") is a noun of its own; "each opponent's graveyard" and "each player's graveyard" select by owner. (2) **"Each player sacrifices all permanents they control that ..."** is `noun.all-they-control`, lowered to the engine's `sacrifice` of an `each` selector with no player (each permanent by its controller; "each opponent" adds `controller: 'opponent'`; another subject is not lowered). (3) **Three sentences, one instruction.** The segmenter keeps "Look at the top N cards of your library." with the "You may reveal ... from among them and put it into your hand." and "Put the rest ..." sentences after it, only when all three are there, and `effect.look-take` reads them as `lookAtTop`. (4) **A linked exile is found across lines.** `parseFaceText` keeps the static "a card exiled with ~" only when exactly one triggered or activated ability of the face exiles, once, and marks that exile `linked` (CR 607.2a); otherwise the static is refused. (5) **"If you do" after an instruction that is not an offer** ("exile it. If you do, you gain 4 life") is a `conditional` on `didPrevious` when the sentence before is one plain instruction of a kind the engine can tell was done (discard, sacrifice, exile, move, draw, mill, tap); "you may tap X untapped Myr you control" is the offer itself (choosing none is declining), so it is not wrapped in `may`, and its X is the engine's `thisWay` `tapped` in the sentence after it. (6) **Statics:** "can't be blocked by <plural group>", "have base power and toughness N/N", "are <type> in addition to their other creature types" (a group only), "You may cast <spells> as though they had flash" and "unless that player is the monarch" after "doesn't untap during its controller's untap step"; a static whose subject reads combat ("Attacking creatures you control have deathtouch") is read and not run, since the engine refuses it. (7) **Costs and restrictions:** "Put a page counter on ~", "Return an artifact you control to its owner's hand" (an ordinary activation only), "Activate only once each turn" (not on a mana ability) and "This ability costs {N} less to activate for each ..." (`costReducedBy`, a `multiple` for N above one). (8) **Triggers:** a batch ("one or more <group> you control deal combat damage to a player / an opponent", "two or more"), "you tap a <permanent> for {C} / for mana" with "add an additional {C}" as its only effect (refused anywhere else), a state of counters on `~`, and "~ enters during the <combat step>" as the intervening `duringStep`. (9) **"Myr" is its own plural**, read from real Oracle text (Myr Battlesphere), the first entry of `INVARIANT_TYPES` verified that way (D-134). (10) Rules that start like an older one read quietly up to the words that make them theirs, so the lines they do not read stop where they stopped before. `PARSER_VERSION` 36, stage P31.
- Alternatives: A rule for each card's sentence ("Juggernauts you control can't be blocked by Walls"): rejected, the brief asked for general rules, and the group and the blockers are any phrase. Reading "with mana value X" in a target: rejected, the engine reads it only in an `each` selector; the line is read and not run. Linking every exile of a face to the reader: rejected, two exiles would be a guess at which one the text means. Wrapping the "tap X" offer in the engine's `may`: impossible (the engine's `may` does not take a tap) and redundant (none is the decline). Lowering "add an additional {C}" as plain mana anywhere: rejected, outside a triggered mana ability it would be mana on the stack.
- Consequences: The twenty cards read and pass `validateCard`; the golden snapshot marks them supported (fifteen new training cards and Steel Hellkite, which was in the corpus as training and unsupported; four hold-out) and no other card changed status or AST. Training is 105 of 139 and hold-out 33 of 43. Siblings that now read: "Return all attacking creatures", "Destroy all artifacts and enchantments", "Exile each player's graveyard", "can't be blocked by creatures with power 2 or less", "one or more creatures you control deal combat damage to a player", "Activate only once each turn" on an ordinary ability, "costs {2} less for each", "you may put a creature card from your graveyard onto the battlefield", "Look at the top four cards ... a creature or land card ... into your graveyard", "Whenever you tap a land for mana, add an additional {G}", "Living weapon" on any Equipment, "the creature with the greatest power or tied". Some lines that stayed unread now stop at a later point or are read and not run (the tests that pinned their diagnostics are updated). Not read: `docs/ROADMAP.md`, "Parser stage P31 known limitations". The web's plural table (`game/filter-text.ts`) should learn "Myr" too.

## D-141: HUD quick wins: the pass button names the next step, Concede moves to Settings, a text size setting and numbered block pairs (2026-10-28)
- Context: The owner's playtests (issues 42 and 43, the closed 39, and a note about four Zombie tokens of which three were blocked and every blocker said only "blocking Zombie"). The pass button said "Next Step" or "Pass", Concede sat in the action bar beside Full Control, the board text was hard to read outside the preview panel, and identical blockers could not be matched to their attackers.
- Decision. (1) **The pass button** (`ui/decisions/priority.ts` `nextStepLabel`) names the step the pass leads to, read from the view alone and following the rules that skip steps: no declared attackers means no declare blockers or combat damage step (CR 508.8), and the first strike damage step happens only when an attacking or blocking creature has first strike or double strike (CR 510.4). On the opponent's turn it says the same ("To Declare Blockers" once attackers are declared, "To Your Turn" at their end step). "Resolve" for a non-empty stack and "Pass Turn" for a first main phase with nothing able to attack (issue 34) stay. (2) **Concede** is a labelled button in the Settings panel with an inline confirm; it is gone from the action bar and hidden once the game is over. The action is the same `concede`. (3) **Text size**: one root variable `--text-scale` (Large 1.2, the default, or Normal 1) multiplies every in-game font through `calc(Npx * var(--text-scale))`; the tile and hand card sizes, which are drawn from numbers, read the same factor (`ui/panels/text-size.ts`, `useTextScale`) and grow only where the row has room, so 1366x768 keeps its layout. The preview panel resets the variable to 1: it is the reference size, and so do the row of thirteen step chips, which must share one line at 1366 wide, and the action dock, which at the larger text grew tall enough to cover the commander tile of the player strip (found by an e2e run at 1280x720). The hand area keeps its 108 px height (the board needs the room): a bigger hand card shows the same top part with larger text, and a hand so full that a bigger card would hide the middle of its neighbours (step under 0.65 of the card width, as when a neighbour is lifted by the pointer) keeps the normal card size (`handScale`). The choice is remembered in localStorage like the theme (which may be unavailable) and applied before the first render. (4) **Block pairs**: attackers are numbered 1, 2, 3 in the order the engine lists them (`combatRoles`, the same order as `view.combat.attackers` and the declare blockers question); a blocked attacker and each creature blocking it show that number in a badge of one of eight Okabe-Ito colours, so the number is the reliable cue and the colour the quick one; an unblocked attacker shows its number in outline once a block exists or while the viewer chooses blocks. Hovering or focusing either end lights the counterparts, the tile name and the preview say "Blocking Zombie (#2)", the log says "X blocks Y (#2)", and the declare blockers question pairs the picked blocks as they are made (`Interaction.pendingBlocks`). The grouping key of identical tokens now includes the combat state (`roleKey`), so tokens that differ in attacker number, blocked or not, or which attackers they block never share a tile.
- Alternatives: Numbering only the blocked attackers: rejected, the numbers would change as the player picks blocks and would differ between the question and the declared blocks. CSS `zoom` on the whole app: rejected, it shrinks the room the board has at 1366x768. A Normal/Large choice per panel: rejected, one setting is enough for the one user. Arrows between blockers and attackers: not built (ROADMAP); the numbers and colours say the same with no geometry. Storing the numbers in the store so they survive an attacker leaving combat: rejected for now; they come from the view each time, so both ends always agree, and only an older log line can show the number an attacker had before another attacker left combat.
- Consequences: The engine is untouched: `view.combat` has what is needed (attackers in order, `blocked`, `blockedBy`); damage assignment order is not in the view, so none is shown. The grouping fix may also have been part of the owner's confusion: when a row overflowed, identical Zombie tokens were folded into one tile that showed only the first member's role. New CSS tokens `--pair-1` to `--pair-8` and `--text-scale` live in `styles.css`.

## D-142: One side column for the highlighted card, the stack and the log; a drawer below 1100px (2026-10-28; superseded by D-144)
- Context: Issue 43a: "put the highlight card, the stack and the log all on the same column, so that we have more space to the battlefield". The game screen had three columns: the card preview (260px, left), the board and a column with the stack, the log and Settings (300px, right), so the board was 806px wide at 1366x768 and `.app` forced a 1366px minimum width (a page scroll at 1280). The owner did not say which side.
- Decision. (1) **One column**, `.game-side` in `App.tsx`: the preview, the stack, the log and the Settings panel, top to bottom, on the right; the board takes the rest of the width. The column is `clamp(300px, 18vw, 400px)` wide (`--side-width`). (2) **The preview has a fixed height** (the card at most `max(31vh, 236px)` wide, 488:680, plus a hint line and 60px of details that scroll), empty or not. A height that followed the card would move the stack and the log under the pointer while it hovers a card name in the log, and the hover would flicker. The stack grows with its items up to `clamp(110px, 28vh, 300px)` and scrolls; the log takes what is left (at least 90px). (3) **A Side panel setting** in Settings (Right by default, Left), remembered in localStorage like Text size (`ui/panels/side-panel.ts`, `data-side-panel` on the root); it is only a flex `order` and a border. (4) **Below 1100px** the column is a drawer over the board, opened by a "Card, stack and log" button that shows the stack size; the page minimum width drops from 1366 to 720px and the minimum height from 768 to 680px. (5) Two things the narrower stack list exposed: arrows now start at the middle of the facing edge of the stack item, and an item scrolled out of the list keeps its arrow, drawn from the list's edge (`clipBox`, `facingEdge` in `ui/panels/arrows.ts`), and the arrow layer clips at the window (a fixed layer's overflow made the page scroll); the visually hidden text of a stack item is now contained by its list.
- Alternatives: Keeping the preview on the left beside the board: rejected, it is the column the owner asked to merge. A preview that shrinks to a hint when empty: rejected for the pointer-shift problem above. Smaller preview cards on short windows: rejected, a card narrower than about 236px clips the rules text of real cards. A Settings gear that frees the foot of the column: not built.
- Consequences: The board is 1066px wide at 1366x768 (806 before), 980 at 1280x720, 1574 at 1920x1080 (1360) and 2160 at 2560x1440 (2000). On a 720px-high window the empty preview takes about 440px, leaving about 180px for the stack and the log together; a deep stack shows about one item and the log a few lines (ROADMAP). `e2e/sidecolumn.e2e.ts` checks the order, the widths, the hover stability, reachability and the drawer.
- Status: The one-column layout is superseded by D-144 (two columns); D-146 refines the order inside the controls column. Its drawer, text size and arrow-edge parts stay.


## D-143: Pass Turn is a yield until the end of the player's turn, with its own button and key (2026-10-28)
- Context: Issue 46: in the first main phase the button said "Pass Turn" but only passed priority once, and the owner wanted a real pass that skips combat and the other steps of the turn. The label of issue 34 (`Pass Turn` when nothing can attack) was the misleading part; the autopilot (A18, D-045) already passes everything that has no stop, so a real pass only needs to ignore the player's own step stops for one turn.
- Decision. (1) **A transient yield in the store**: `yieldTurn` (the turn number) is set by `passTurn()` and read by the pure `passTurnVerdict` of `policy/should-stop.ts` in the autopilot loop. While it runs the autopilot passes the player's priority at every step of that turn, ignoring `myTurnStops` and `thisTurn` (the point of the button) and nothing else: `shouldStop` still decides, so Full Control, an opponent's object on the stack that is aimed at the player or that the player holds a relevant instant-speed action against (D-138, `stopWhenTargeted`) and the combat-damage window end it. It also ends when the turn changes (the opponent's turn keeps its normal stops), at any decision other than priority (targets, choices, optional triggers, discards: never answered), on a click of the player, Esc, "Cancel pass", an undo, a new game and whenever the autopilot stops for any reason (`driveAndEnd`). Every move is an ordinary `pass` action; the yield only passes the player's own priority, so the engine still gives the opponent theirs in every step. (2) **Skip combat**: the one decision the yield answers is the declaration of attackers, with no attackers, when no creature is required to attack (CR 508.1d); a required attacker ends the yield instead of being overridden. A yield started in the first main phase therefore skips combat, which is what "skip the combat phase" asks for. (3) **Buttons** (`priority.ts`, `model.ts`): the primary button keeps naming the single step ("To Combat", issue 42), and `nextStepLabel` no longer says "Pass Turn" for any one-step pass. In the first main phase with nothing able to attack there is no combat to skip, so the primary button is itself the real "Pass Turn". In the main phases of the player's turn with an empty stack, when the primary names a step, a separate secondary "Pass Turn" button (accessible name "Pass turn: skip to the end of my turn") sits next to it. While it runs the bar says "Passing turn... Esc to cancel" with a "Cancel pass" button. (4) **Keys**: P presses Pass Turn where it is offered; Esc cancels a running pass before it does anything else. (5) **Full Control** is not overridden: Pass Turn then moves one step and the stop holds; the tooltip says so while Full Control is on.
- Alternatives: Answering every decision with a default during the yield: rejected, decisions are never auto-answered (A18). A yield that survives a question and resumes after the answer (Arena's end-turn behaviour): not built now, see `docs/ROADMAP.md`; every interrupt cancels, which is predictable and cannot pass a window by mistake. Putting the yield in `StopSettings`: rejected, it is a one-turn intent, not a preference. An engine action for "end turn": rejected, the engine would need a notion of the player's future intent and replays must stay a list of ordinary passes.
- Consequences: Space in the first main phase with nothing able to attack now passes the whole turn, so a player holding an instant for their own second main or end step gets no stop there unless Full Control or a step stop on the opponent's side says otherwise (the opponent's spells aimed at them or answerable still stop). The engine is untouched. Tests: `apps/web/test/pass-turn.test.ts` (labels, buttons, keys, the verdict, a scripted store simulation of each interrupt, one real game) and `apps/web/e2e/pass-turn.e2e.ts`.

- Consequences: The board is 1066px wide at 1366x768 (806 before), 980 at 1280x720, 1574 at 1920x1080 (1360) and 2160 at 2560x1440 (2000). On a 720px-high window the empty preview takes about 440px, leaving about 180px for the stack and the log together; a deep stack shows about one item and the log a few lines (ROADMAP). `e2e/sidecolumn.e2e.ts` checks the order, the widths, the hover stability, reachability and the drawer. **Superseded in part by D-144:** the one column became two (the card and the log, the stack and the controls); the drawer, the Side panel setting's storage, the text size and the arrow-edge changes stay. The test file is now `e2e/columns.e2e.ts`.

## D-144: Two side columns: the card and the log on one side, the stack and the controls on the other (2026-10-28)
- Context: Issue 47 (the owner, after the one-column layout of D-142): "The new space for the highlighted card is too short. It has to show a scroll bar if there are a couple of abilities, which is almost always true. Let's put on one side the highlight and the log, and on the other side the stack and controls. Doing so, the highlight is enough space to show all the abilities and state, and the control stays close to the stack, which is useful for when you have to accept something to resolve but you don't know what is being resolved." In D-142 the preview had a fixed height of about 440px at 1280x720 and clipped the rules text twice: the details below the card scrolled, and the card frame itself (`aspect-ratio` 488:680, `overflow: hidden`) cut a long text (Kappa Cannoneer lost its last sentence). The action dock floated over the bottom right of the board, away from the stack, and the hand made room for it with a `padding-right` rule.
- Decision. (1) **Two columns** around the battlefield, both full height. The *info* column (`.game-side-info`, `App.tsx`) holds the preview and the log; the *controls* column (`.game-side-controls`) holds the stack, the action dock directly under it, and Settings at its foot. Default: info on the left, controls on the right. (2) **The dock moves into the controls column** by a portal: `DecisionLayer` still builds it (it owns the decision), `App.tsx` provides the slot element through `DockSlotContext` (`ui/decisions/dock-slot.ts`), and the layer draws the dock there; without a provider (a test that renders the layer alone) the dock stays inside the layer. The hand's `padding-right` and `--dec-dock-w` are gone: nothing floats over the board any more, so the dock no longer needs its own text size (it follows the Text size setting) and cannot cover the commander tile or a hand card. The dock caps at 62vh and scrolls inside. (3) **The preview takes the column height the log leaves** (`flex: 1 1 0`, a constant whatever it shows, so the log does not move under the pointer); the log has `clamp(104px, 100vh - 640px, 480px)`. The card frame is at least card-shaped (`min-height` of 1.3935 times the card's width) and grows with its rules text instead of clipping it, and the art band follows the card's width (36%, 56 to 140px). (4) **Widths:** info `clamp(252px, 16vw, 380px)`, controls `clamp(236px, 14vw, 340px)` (`--info-width`, `--controls-width`). The owner suggested `clamp(260px, 15vw, 360px)` for each; two such columns leave 846px at 1366x768, below the 880px asked for, so the controls column (buttons and stack items that wrap) is 16px narrower and the card column 8px: 878px at 1366x768. (5) **Side panel setting:** the same key and values, relabelled "Stack and controls" (Right by default): it names the side of the controls column and the info column takes the other. A remembered value of the one-column layout keeps its meaning (the side of the stack). (6) **Below 1100px** both columns are one drawer over the board (`.game-sides`), opened by "Stack, controls, card and log" with the stack size on it, the controls column first in the page order and at the outer edge. (7) Side effects of narrower boards: the player strip wraps its command zone to a second line when the counts leave less than 280px (a strip with "Spells cast this turn" at 1280px), and a stack item's name takes two lines before it is cut. Stack arrows needed nothing: `facingEdge` already starts them at the item edge that faces the target, so with the stack on the right it is the left edge and with the setting on Left the right one (`e2e/trigger-targets.e2e.ts` checks both).
- Alternatives: Equal columns of `clamp(260px, 15vw, 360px)`: rejected for the 846px board at 1366x768. A preview of fixed height that scrolls: what failed. A preview whose height follows its card: rejected as in D-142, the log would move under the pointer while hovering a name in it. Keeping the dock over the board and only moving the stack: it would not be next to the stack, the owner's point. A drawer that holds only the info column, with the controls column always on screen: it keeps the pass button reachable under 1100px, but the owner asked for one drawer with both; recorded in the ROADMAP. Rendering the dock inside the controls column from `App.tsx` by lifting the decision state: a larger change of the decision layer for the same result.
- Consequences: The board is 878px wide at 1366x768 (1066 with one column, 806 before that), 792 at 1280x720 (980), 1344 at 1920x1080 (1574) and 1840 at 2560x1440 (2160). The preview card is about 217px wide at 1366x768 (it was 236px in D-142) and shows every card of the two precons whole, with 83px to spare under the longest at 1280x720 (`e2e/columns.e2e.ts`). Under 1100px the button of the turn is inside the closed drawer. D-142's one-column part is superseded; its drawer, text size and arrow-edge parts stay.
- Status: The order inside the controls column (the dock directly under the stack) is refined by D-146: the stack on top grows downward and the dock sits at the bottom.


## D-145: The Dinosaurs slice: commanders, stun counters, "unless" restrictions, mana "instead", lost abilities, doubling, prevention by source, trample excess, escalate, reveal until, fight, free casting, Hideaway and divided damage (2026-10-29)
- Context: The owner's third precon (Dinosaurs) has twenty cards the engine did not run: Arachnogenesis, Clifftop Lookout, Collective Resistance, Ezuri's Predation, Goreclaw, Ilysian Caryatid, Kenrith's Transformation, Loot, Monstrous Onslaught, Mosswort Bridge, Pugnacious Hammerskull, Ram Through, Rhonas the Indomitable, Rishkar's Expertise, Rishkar, Scavenging Ooze, Tangleweave Armor, Thickest in the Thicket, Unnatural Growth and Witch's Clinic.
