Each gap was grouped by the capability it needs and built as a general primitive (a filter, an amount, an effect, a static, a keyword), never as a card, with SYNTHETIC cards for the tests (`src/cards/fixtures/synthetic-*.ts`, all named "SYNTHETIC ..."). The golden corpus now holds the exact Oracle lines; the parser (a later task) lowers them to the shapes in `docs/MECHANICS.md`, "The Dinosaurs slice (D-145)".
- Decision: (1) **Commanders.** `ObjectFilter.commander` ("target commander", CR 903.3: a card a player designated; a token or a copy is not one) and `Amount` `commanderManaValue` (the greatest mana value among the controller's commanders, wherever they are, as printed; also a `StaticPtAmount`). `ObjectFilter.hasCounter` (`true` for any counter, or a counter's name) is the other new filter part; counters belong to no layer, so a static ability may name them. (2) **Stun counters** (CR 122.1d in `docs/rules/`; an older note in the ROADMAP says 122.1g): the replacement lives in one place, `rules/untap.ts` `untapPermanent`, which the untap step and the `untap` effect both call, so a permanent with a stun counter that would untap loses one counter instead and stays tapped. There is no AST node: the counter is named "stun" in `addCounters`. (3) **A condition that is part of the trigger event** (`Ability.triggered.triggerCondition`, CR 603.2: "Whenever this creature attacks while you don't control another Dinosaur"): read once, as the event happens, with the controller as "you" and the source as "this", never again on resolution (the intervening "if" of CR 603.4 stays `interveningIf`). (4) **"Can't attack or block unless"**: `Restriction` `cantAttack` (CR 508.1a, read in `combat-legality.ts` and the legal-action lists) and `StaticEffect` `restrictionUnless { subject: this, restrictions, unless: Condition }` (read where the rule acts, never in a layer, and gone with the ability: a creature that loses all abilities may attack and block). (5) **Mana "instead"**: `ManaAbility.instead { condition, production }` (CR 605.3b, 608.2c) replaces the production while the condition holds, read when the ability is activated and wherever the engine asks what a source can make (`rules/mana-outcomes.ts` `effectiveManaAbility`, so the planner, the pool and the legal actions agree); `ManaProduction` `anyColor` gains `count` (two mana of one color). (6) **Statics that rewrite a permanent**: `loseAllAbilities { subject: attached }` (CR 613.1f; a later-timestamp grant still applies, CR 613.7; `rules/lost-abilities.ts`, split out of `derive-layers.ts` to avoid an import cycle), `setColors` (layer 5) and the named `setTypes` without `additive` (replaces the card types and the creature types, CR 205.1a, 205.3d). Together with the existing `setPt` they are "Enchanted creature loses all abilities and is a green Elk creature with base power and toughness 3/3". Only `attached`: a group that loses abilities would depend on the abilities (CR 613.8; ROADMAP). (7) **Doubling** (CR 701.10a-c): `PtAmount` `{ kind: 'affected', stat }` in the amounts of a `modifyPt` effect, one continuous effect per creature affected, all read before any applies. (8) **Prevention by source**: `preventDamage.byFilter` (CR 615.1, 609.7a: "Prevent all combat damage that would be dealt this turn by non-Spider creatures") reads the source as each damage event would happen, so a creature that enters later is covered. (9) **Trample excess for noncombat damage**: `dealDamage.trampleExcess` (CR 702.19b, 120.6, 702.2c: lethal damage first, the rest to the creature's controller, as one event each by the same source; `rules/damage.ts` `lethalDamageTo`, `dealDamageWithExcess`, which combat damage now uses too). (10) **Escalate** (CR 702.120a): `Keyword` `escalate { cost }` on a modal spell, added to the cost once for each mode beyond the first (`CostRequest.modes`); a set of modes the caster cannot pay is not offered. (11) **Reveal until** (CR 701.20, 401.4): `Effect` `revealUntil { filter, put, tapped }`, and `lookAtTop.take` gains `to` (hand, battlefield, `exileFaceDown`), `tapped`, `min` and `manaValueAtMost: Amount` ("a creature card with mana value less than or equal to the number of lands you control"). (12) **Fight** (CR 701.14): `Effect` `fight { fighters, against, pairing }`; `pairing: 'differentChosen'` ("each of those tokens fights a different one of those creatures") asks the controller of the effect, one creature at a time, which of the group each fights (`choosePermanent` purpose `fight` with `subject`; the last one is not asked); event `fought`. (13) **Casting and playing for free** (CR 608.2g, 118.9, 305.1): `Effect` `castFree { objects, play }` over a card chosen from the hand (a `choose` selector with `zone: 'hand'`) or a reference (`moved`, `linkedExile`); the answer is `chooseCards` of purpose `cast` (none or one) and starts a cast during the resolution (`rules/cast-free-answer.ts`, like Cascade); with `play` a land card is put onto the battlefield as a land play (own turn, land drop left; `canPlayLandByEffect`), a land is never cast. (14) **Hideaway** (CR 702.75a, 607.2a): `Keyword` `hideaway { count }` expands in `derive-keywords.ts` to a `lookAtTop` that must take one card face down into exile (`to: 'exileFaceDown'`, `min: 1`), remembered by the permanent (`GameObject.hideaway`, read by `ObjectRef` `linkedExile`) and visible only to the controller of that permanent while it is on the battlefield (`view.ts`: everyone else, and everyone once it left, sees a face-down card). "Enters tapped" is its own replacement (CR 702.75b). (15) **Divided damage** (CR 601.2d, 608.2b): `TargetSpec.divide { total }` (the total is read once, as the spell is cast), `ChosenTarget.share` (at least 1 each, adding up to the total, announced in the same `chooseTargets` action), `TargetChoiceSpec.divide`, and `Effect` `dealDividedDamage { to: target }` (an illegal target gets nothing and its share is not given to the others); only in a spell's own text. `legalActionsForDecision` lists two divisions for each set of targets. (16) **Already supported, parser only**: Goreclaw's cost reduction and attack trigger, Rishkar's counters and its group grant by `hasCounter`, Scavenging Ooze (`exile` then `objectMatches`), Thickest in the Thicket (`powerOf`, `controlsGreatest`) and Rhonas's pump are pinned with SYNTHETIC cards of the same shape (`synthetic-parser-shapes.ts`, `scenario-xx-parser-shapes.test.ts`). (17) **AI**: `casual-divide.ts` divides among what it can kill, cheapest first, the rest on the last target; `casual-free.ts` takes the best card for a free cast and the creature a subject fights that it kills and survives, and activates "play the exiled card" on spare mana in its own main phase; the soak deck style `dinosaurs` (`packages/ai/test/helpers.ts`, `dinosaurs-games.test.ts`) restates the rules of the slice from the events. (18) **Web**: typecheck-only fixes (a wording for `cantAttack`, `linkedExile`, the `affected` amount, the `fought` log line and the waiting text of purpose `cast`); the rest is listed in `docs/MECHANICS.md` for the web step. `ENGINE_VERSION` 32.
- Alternatives: A rule for each card: rejected, the brief and AGENTS.md ask for primitives. Putting the stun replacement in the untap step only: the effect `untap` would then ignore it, which CR 122.1d does not allow. Storing the division on the stack object (`StackData`): rejected, `ChosenTarget.share` travels with the targets through the legality checks of resolution and copies for free. A `dealDamage` with `divided: true`: rejected, its amount would be read twice (as cast and as resolved). Hideaway as a special case of `exile.linked`: rejected, the card is chosen from the library and hidden. A land chosen for a free cast moved by an ordinary `moveToZone`: rejected, it must count as a land play. `loseAllAbilities` for any group: needs the dependency order of CR 613.8, not built. Making `triggerCondition` an `interveningIf`: rejected, CR 603.2 and 603.4 differ for the Hammerskull ("while ..." is not "if ...").
- Consequences: The twenty cards are covered by the engine (`docs/MECHANICS.md`, "The Dinosaurs slice (D-145)", per card and per shape) and the parser can lower them. Limits are in `docs/ROADMAP.md`, "The Dinosaurs slice (D-145)": the commander mana value ignores a copy effect, a free cast or a Hideaway play of a card its caster does not own is not offered, a copy of a divided spell asks the division anew, `loseAllAbilities` is for an Aura or Equipment only. The web must word the new kinds (listed in `docs/MECHANICS.md`) and give the `cast` question, the fight choice and the division of damage a dialog; until then they show the generic prompts. Soak: `SOAK_GAMES=100 pnpm exec vitest run packages/ai/test/dinosaurs-games.test.ts`.

## D-146: The controls column keeps the buttons at the bottom: the stack on top grows downward, the dock grows upward (2026-10-28)
- Context: The owner, after trying D-144: "i didnt like that now the control buttons are moving depending on the stack. better keep them more or less fixed on the botton, growing upwards, and the stack on the top growing downwards." In D-144 the dock sat directly under the stack, so it moved up and down as the stack grew and shrank, and a click aimed at Pass Turn could land on something else when the stack changed under the pointer. This refines the order inside the controls column of D-144; the two columns, the drawer, the widths and the Side panel setting stay.
- Decision. (1) **The column is stack, flexible gap, dock, Settings**, top to bottom. `.pnl-stack` is the flexible middle (`flex: 1 1 0`, `overflow: hidden`, minimum `--stack-min`, 230px: the heading and about three items); its list (`.pnl-stack-list`) is anchored to the top, grows downward and scrolls inside the stack's own area when it reaches the dock. The dock slot and Settings take their own height (`flex: 0 1 auto` and `flex: none`), so nothing above them changes the dock's bottom edge. With an empty stack there is space between the "Stack is empty" heading and the dock. (2) **The dock keeps its bottom edge and grows upward.** Inside it the panels of the decision (targets, payment, order, card pickers) come first and the action bar last: prompt, then the buttons, then the chips (Undo, Full Control, Manual mana). A panel or a longer prompt therefore pushes the dock's top up and leaves the buttons where they were. The modal decisions stay modals. (3) **The footer chips reserve two rows** (`min-height` of two chip rows), because "Undo" alone, "Undo (13)" and a wider column change whether the three chips fit on one row, and a row more or less under the buttons would move them. (4) **When the column is too short** the dock shrinks before the stack loses its minimum: the decision panels scroll inside the dock and the action bar stays whole (`.dec-dock > :not(.dec-bar)` shrinks and scrolls; the old `max-height: 62vh` on the whole dock is gone, it hid the bar when it scrolled). At 1280x720 a Storm Bolt target question (the tallest dock the synthetic decks make, 354px) leaves the stack 277px. (5) **The same in the drawer below 1100px**, where the controls column is the same column. Measured primary button position (top y): identical to within 1px with 0, 1 and 8 objects on the stack and with a target question showing, at 1366x768, 1920x1080 and 1280x720 (`e2e/controls-bottom.e2e.ts`).
- Alternatives: Keeping the dock under the stack and giving the stack a fixed height: the button would not move, but a short stack would waste the room and a long one scroll early. Putting the primary button first in the dock with the panels under it: the panels would grow downward and push Settings away; the owner asked for growth upward. A stack that grows upward from the dock (newest at the bottom, next to the buttons): rejected, the top of the stack is the next thing to resolve and the owner asked for the stack at the top growing down. Letting the dock overflow the column when too tall: it would cover Settings or the stack.
- Consequences: The buttons are where the hand expects them at every stack size. The stack heading and first item are always at the top of the column. The stack area is a tall box even when empty (its heading and one line, then blank space). Opening Settings, which grows upward from the foot (up to 40vh), does move the dock, as it is the player's own action. `docs/ROADMAP.md`, "Two side columns (D-144) known limitations".

## D-147: The parser reads the Dinosaurs slice: tests of the game before and after an instruction, an activated body that reads a spell's sentences, conditions as the event or the restriction, and statics that remake a creature (2026-10-29)
- Context: D-145 built the engine primitives for the twenty cards the owner's Dinosaurs precon lacked and listed, for each, what the parser must produce (`docs/MECHANICS.md`, "The Dinosaurs slice (D-145)"). The golden corpus holds their real Oracle text (Arachnogenesis, Clifftop Lookout, Collective Resistance, Ezuri's Predation, Goreclaw, Ilysian Caryatid, Kenrith's Transformation, Loot, Monstrous Onslaught, Mosswort Bridge, Pugnacious Hammerskull, Ram Through, Rhonas the Indomitable, Rishkar's Expertise, Rishkar, Scavenging Ooze, Tangleweave Armor, Thickest in the Thicket, Unnatural Growth, Witch's Clinic), and the Angels and Dragons extracts for the next slices. The brief was the one of D-131, D-133, D-134 and D-140: general rules, creature types from the CR table, no card names, the obvious siblings read too, and text not fully understood flagged, never half-executed.
- Decision: (1) **A test of the game may end or begin a sentence.** "draw two cards if you control the creature with the greatest power or tied for the greatest power" (a trailing " if <test>", only after one instruction, so the test cannot be taken for another instruction's) and "If you control a creature with power 4 or greater, ..." (a leading test) are the engine's `conditional`; the tests are the counts of permanents (new `condition.dont-control-a`, and `condition.control-a` widened to "another"), the greatest of a stat, a commander, the life total and the tests of the game. An activated ability's body reads the sentences of a spell (`ACTIVATED_SENTENCE`), so "{G}: Exile target card from a graveyard. If it was a creature card, ..." and "... if creatures you control have total power 10 or greater" read; the mana-ability reading refuses any sentence with a test, except the one shape of (6). (2) **A condition that is part of the event is not an "if".** "Whenever ~ attacks while you don't control another Dinosaur" is `trigger.attacks-while` and the engine's `triggerCondition` (read once as the event happens), and "if" stays the intervening `interveningIf` of CR 603.4. (3) **Statics.** `static.cant-attack-block-unless` is `restrictionUnless` (the permanent's own restriction, lifted by a condition read for its controller); `static.attached-becomes` is "loses all abilities and is a <color> <creature types> <card types> with base power and toughness N/N" as `loseAllAbilities`, `setTypes` (replacing), `setColors` and `setPt` of the attached permanent, in the order of the layers, with no host type, and at least one creature type (the text that names none would leave the creature types to guesswork); `static.pt-amount` is "gets +X/+X, where X is the greatest mana value among your commanders" (or a count of permanents, which follows the board as "for each" does) and refuses any other amount at lowering (CR 613.8); cost reductions compare the spell's power, toughness or mana value ("Creature spells you cast with power 4 or greater cost {2} less"). (4) **Filter parts and nouns.** "with a counter on it" / "with a +1/+1 counter on it" / "with counters on them" is `hasCounter` in every permanent phrase; "target commander" and "target creature commander" are `noun.target-commander` (an operand of every verb that takes a permanent); "any number of target creatures" is `noun.any-number-targets`, lowered only by a divided damage. (5) **Effects.** `effect.double-pt` (`affected`, a stat the text does not name gets nothing), `effect.fight` (two single creatures) and `effect.fight-each` ("Each of those tokens fights a different one of those creatures": lowered only after an instruction that made a token for each creature of a filter, `LowerContext.createdPer`, and only when "those creatures" is that filter), `effect.excess-damage` ("excess damage is dealt to that creature's controller instead": the lowering joins the sentence to the bite before it as `trampleExcess` and only when the condition names that bite's creature and trample and the recipient is the controller of the creature bitten; the bind pass reads "the creature you control" as the most recent object of the text that says "you control"), `effect.reveal-until` (two sentences kept together by the segmenter, `revealUntil`), `effect.look-take` widened (onto the battlefield, "with mana value less than or equal to the number of lands you control", "on the bottom in a random order"), `effect.cast-free` ("cast a spell with mana value 5 or less from your hand without paying its mana cost", "play the exiled card ..."; `castFree`, `linkedExile`), `effect.for-each-create`, `effect.damage-divided` (the targets slot gets `divide`; the total is the one amount read once as the spell is cast, an `aggregate` marked `asCast`, which every other place refuses), `byFilter` on a prevention of all damage, "add two mana of any one color", the mana ability's "instead" (`manaInstead`) and "Another target creature gets +2/+0 and gains trample". (6) **Keywords.** "Hideaway N" joins the numbered keywords; `keyword.escalate` is a costed keyword line (mana only). (7) **A legendary name "X the Y" is also "X"** in its own text (Rhonas the Indomitable), unless the word before "the" is a preposition ("Gideon of the Trials"). (8) Rules that start like an older one read quietly up to their own words (the restriction, the "for each" token, a group of sources), so the lines they do not read stop where they stopped before. `PARSER_VERSION` 37, stage P32.
- Alternatives: A rule for each card's sentence ("Rhonas can't attack or block unless ..."): rejected, the brief asked for general rules; the condition is any test the grammar has. Reading a trailing "if" after several clauses: rejected, "Draw a card and gain 1 life if ..." may attach the test to either; only one instruction. A lowering of "the total as the spell is cast" that reads it as the spell resolves: rejected, it changes the number (the creatures may change between the two); the amount carries `asCast` and anywhere but the divided slot it is read and not run. A `may` around the free cast: redundant, the engine's `castFree` already lets the controller decline. `setTypes` with no creature type ("is a green creature"): rejected as above. Reading "target commander" only on the battlefield: the engine says where a commander can be; the filter says only that it is one.
- Consequences: The twenty cards read and pass `validateCard`; the golden snapshot marks them supported (Mosswort Bridge was in the corpus as unsupported; nineteen are new) and no other card changed status or AST. Angels and Dragons: none of the fifty-two new cards is supported yet (that is expected, they are the next slices), and most of them read at least one line. Siblings that now read: "can't attack unless you control a Dragon", "attacks while you control a Dragon", "double the power of target creature", "reveal cards ... until you reveal a nonland card ... into your hand", "You may cast a creature spell from your hand without paying its mana cost", "Escalate {2}{R}", "Hideaway 5", "Each creature you control with a stun counter on it ...", "Prevent all damage that would be dealt by Dragons this turn", "If you control a Dragon, draw a card", "draw a card if you control a Dragon". Some lines that stayed unread now stop at a later point or are read and not run (the tests that pinned their diagnostics are updated). Differences of detail from D-145: a group named by a creature type alone has no `types: ['creature']` ("another Dinosaur"), `attached` carries the host type `creature` for "Equipped creature gets ...", and "At the beginning of each combat" is the step trigger with `whose: 'each'` (every player's combat). Not read: `docs/ROADMAP.md`, "Parser stage P32 known limitations".

## D-148: The web side of the Dinosaurs slice: dividing damage, face-down placeholders and the dock (2026-10-29)
- Context: the engine asks for a division of damage among the targets (D-145), a Hideaway card is exiled face down (D-145), and the dock of the controls column (D-146) must stay usable while a long panel is open.
- Decision: the targets panel of a divided spell starts with an even split (the remainder on the first target), restarts it when the set of targets changes, and gives each target a stepper that never goes below 1; Confirm is off until the shares add up, and the answer carries `share` on each target. An unseen face-down card is shown as a card back labelled "(face down)", no longer "(foretold)", because the view cannot tell a foretold card from a Hideaway card; the controller of a Hideaway card sees it, marked "Hideaway". The log never names a face-down card of the opponent (the old zone-move line leaked it). The dock keeps the design of D-146: the panels scroll and the action bar stays whole at the foot (the sticky bar this slice first added was dropped when the branch met D-146, which makes it redundant).
- Alternatives: asking for a number per target in a text field (slower and easy to get wrong); a separate label for foretold and Hideaway cards (the view would need a new field); sticky bar in addition to D-146 (two mechanisms for one problem).
- Consequences: Monstrous Onslaught can be cast from the UI; a Hideaway card is a card back for the opponent and in the log. The mana color popover of a count-2 "any one color" source still says "Add W" (the view does not carry the count; the log shows what was added). Recorded in `docs/ROADMAP.md`.

## D-149: The Angels slice: life gain, counters added, attack batches, creatures that enter with counters, commanders entering or attacking, proliferate, protection and "can't" statics, a tax on blocking, restricted and chosen-color mana, exile until, Auras that enter by an effect, grants by keyword, and an alternative cost that taps creatures (2026-10-29)
- Context: The owner's fourth precon (Angels) has twenty-three cards the engine did not run: Angel of Vitality, Angel of the Ruins, Angelic Destiny, Angelic Sleuth, Archangel of Tithes, Emeria Shepherd, Endless Atlas, Exemplar of Light, Exorcise, Firemane Commando, Giada, Font of Hope, Grasp of Fate, Herald of Eternal Dawn, Heraldic Banner, Merchant of Truth, Metallic Mimic, Metropolis Reformer, Norn's Choirmaster, Sephara, Sky's Blade, Seraph of the Sword, Serra Avenger, Tome of Legends and Vanguard Seraph. As for the Dinosaurs slice (D-145) the brief asked for general primitives (who, action, filter, amount), tested with SYNTHETIC cards, and for each card the AST the parser must write. Two things left from the Dinosaurs slice (D-145, D-148) were fixed with it: a copy of a divided spell, and Hideaway after a control change.
- Decision: (1) **Life.** The replacement `lifeGainBonus {amount}` (CR 119.10, "you gain that much life plus 1 instead") and the trigger `lifeGained {who, firstEachTurn?}` (CR 119.9, "whenever you gain life [for the first time each turn]"). Both go through one function, `gainLife` (`rules/life-gain.ts`), used by the `gainLife` effect and by lifelink, which emits `lifeGained` with the amount after the replacements and `nth` (the player's gains this turn, in `TurnLog.lifeGained`). (2) **Counters added.** The trigger `countersAdded {what, counter?, by}` (CR 122.6, 122.6a: "whenever you put one or more +1/+1 counters on this creature"; `counterAdded.by` names the player who put them, a permanent's own "enters with" counters count as its controller's) and the flag `oncePerTurn` on a triggered ability ("This ability triggers only once each turn", CR 603.2; `TurnLog.triggered`). (3) **Attack batches.** The trigger `attackBatch {who, atLeast, what?}` ("whenever you attack with two or more creatures", "whenever another player attacks with two or more creatures"), once per declaration, with `triggerPlayer` as the attacking player and the condition `attackersAttackedYou` ("none of those creatures attacked you", CR 508.1b). (4) **Creatures that enter with counters.** The replacement `othersEnterWithCounters {what, counter, count}` (CR 614.1c, 614.12, 122.6): a permanent on the battlefield gives the permanents that enter and match `what` extra counters, counted as they enter (`rules/enters-group.ts`); `count` may be a `countOf` (for each Angel you already control). (5) **Commanders.** `ObjectFilter.commander` takes `'yours'` beside `true` (your commander, a card you own and designated), for "whenever your commander enters or attacks"; a commander "you control" is `commander: true` with `controller: 'you'`. (6) **Proliferate** (CR 701.34a): the effect `proliferate`; the controller chooses any number of permanents with a counter and of players with poison counters (`choosePermanent` purpose `proliferate`, with `players`), and each gets one more counter of each kind it has (`rules/proliferate.ts`). (7) **A player's protection and the "can't" statics.** `playerHexproof` (CR 702.11b, "You have hexproof"), `cantLoseGame` (CR 104.3, SBA 704.5a-c and 704.6c skip the player), `opponentsCantWin` (CR 104.2: a no-op, because CR 104.2a, a last player in the game wins, overrides it), `cantCastThis` with a required condition (CR 101.2: "You can't cast ~ during your first, second, or third turns", read by every way to cast: `rules/cast-restrictions.ts`) and the condition `ownTurnNumber`, `preventDamageToThis {scope}` (CR 615.1: prevention of all combat, noncombat or all damage to the permanent itself). (8) **A tax on blocking.** `blockTax {cost, whileAttacking?}` (CR 509.1b-d): each creature declared as a blocker costs mana to its controller, paid after the declaration by `payMana` with purpose `blockTax`; the declaration lists `blockCost {cost, affordable, source}`; a declaration that cannot be paid is refused, and the legal-action list holds none (`rules/block-tax.ts`). (9) **Mana.** `ManaAbility.spendOnly {types?, subtypes?}` ("Spend this mana only to cast an Angel spell", CR 106.6; the mana stays in the pool as restricted mana, never pays an ability) and `ManaProduction` `chosenColor` ("one mana of the chosen color", read from `asEntersChoose` of `color`). (10) **Exile until.** `exile.until: 'sourceLeaves'` (CR 610.3) with a slot `TargetSpec.onePerOpponent` ("for each opponent, exile up to one target nonland permanent that player controls"); the cards come back under their owners' control when the source leaves, by a delayed triggered ability (`EXILE_RETURN_ABILITY` in `rules/derive-alt.ts`). (11) **An Aura that enters by an effect** (CR 303.4f, 303.4g): `moveToZone` of an object selector other than `choose` to the battlefield puts an Aura card onto the battlefield and its controller chooses what it enchants (`choosePermanent` purpose `auraHost`, `subject` the Aura); with nothing to enchant it stays where it was (`rules/aura-entry.ts`). (12) **Granted exalted and prowess** (CR 702.83b, 702.108b: every instance is its own triggered ability): both are grantable; each grant adds one instance with its triggered ability (`INSTANCE_KEYWORDS`, `expansionOf` in `rules/derive-layers.ts`). A static `grantKeyword` may name a keyword in its subject (CR 613.8a, "other creatures you control with flying have indestructible"): such a subject is evaluated after the effects that do not read keywords, over the keywords the target has with the grants so far, and the effects that did not apply are looked at again until none more does (`keywordsWith` in `rules/derive.ts`, `rules/derive-statics.ts`). Every other static ability still refuses a keyword in its subject. `Condition.sameNameAtLeast` ("three or more lands with the same name"). `objectMatches.of` may be `triggerSubject` (the land that triggered a landfall: "If that land is a Plains"). (13) **An alternative cost that taps permanents** (CR 118.9, 601.2h): `AlternativeCost` kind `tapPermanents {cost, filter, count}` ("pay {W} and tap four untapped creatures you control with flying rather than pay this spell's mana cost"). The engine pays the mana first, planning it so that enough permanents stay untapped to tap (`castManaPlan`, `PlanOptions.avoidObjects`), then asks which ones (`choosePermanent` purpose `tap` and `forCost`; none when exactly `count` qualify). Not with Convoke, Improvise or Delve. (14) **A copy of a divided spell keeps the division** (CR 707.10, 115.7f): the question for new targets of such a copy has as many targets as the original, no share to name (`TargetChoiceSpec.keepsDivision`); a target left as it is keeps its share and a new one takes the share of the one it replaces. (15) **A free cast or a play by an effect after a control change** (CR 702.75a, 608.2g): `canCastDuringResolution` and `canPlayLandByEffect` no longer require the owner for a card in exile; the effect names it, so the controller of the ability may cast or play it. (16) `ENGINE_VERSION` 33.
- Alternatives: A rule for each card: rejected. A separate decision kind for proliferate and for the Aura host: rejected, `choosePermanent` has the right shape and the new purposes follow D-145. Making the block tax a restriction of `cantBlock`: rejected, the cost is paid after the choice and the planner must see the mana (the same split as the attack tax, D-125). Returning an exiled card immediately when the source leaves (CR 610.3 says "immediately"): not built, a delayed trigger uses what exists (the cost is that the card is back one resolution late, recorded in `docs/ROADMAP.md`). Resolving a dependency between effects that read keywords (CR 613.8) by sorting: rejected for a repeated pass, which gives the same answer for the cards in the deck and cannot loop. Keeping `opponentsCantWin` out of the engine: rejected, the parser must read the card's line and the node is honest (a no-op by CR 104.2a, tested). Re-announcing the division for a copy: what D-145 built, and wrong (CR 115.7f).
- Consequences: The twenty-three cards are covered by the engine (`docs/MECHANICS.md`, "The Angels slice (D-149)", per card and per shape) and the parser can lower them; the golden snapshot marks Merchant of Truth supported already, because the parser read "Clues you control have exalted" once exalted became grantable. The parser grammar now reads a granted prowess and exalted and an Aura returned by an effect, so the tests that pinned those as unread were changed (`packages/cards/test`). Limits are in `docs/ROADMAP.md`, "The Angels slice (D-149)". The web has minimal wording only (the typecheck and the trigger kinds): the nodes it must word are listed in `docs/MECHANICS.md`. Tests: `scenario-xx-angels-shapes`, `-life-gain`, `-attack-batch`, `-enters-group`, `-commander-triggers`, `-angels-statics`, `-granted-exalted`, `-proliferate`, `-mana-restricted`, `-exile-until`, `-landfall-return`, `-block-tax`, `-tap-alt`, `-copy-divided`, `-hideaway-control` and `ast-tap-alt-validate`; the AI plays the `angels` deck style (`packages/ai/test/angels-games.test.ts`, 100 games with every card of the style cast).

## D-150: The parser reads the Angels slice: life gained, counters put and attack batches as triggers, protections and taxes as statics, restricted and chosen-color mana, exile per opponent, and "instead" after a "may" (2026-10-29)
- Context: D-149 gave the engine the primitives for the twenty-three cards of the owner's Angels precon and listed, for each, the AST the parser must write (`docs/MECHANICS.md`, "The Angels slice (D-149)"). The golden corpus holds their real Oracle text; twenty-two read nothing before this stage (Merchant of Truth already read). The brief: general rules over the engine's creature type table (D-134), no card names, and text the engine cannot run stays unread.
- Decision: (1) **Triggers** (`rules/trigger/angels.ts`): `trigger.life-gained` ("you gain life [for the first time each turn]", also an opponent or a player), `trigger.counters-added` ("you put one or more +1/+1 counters on ~", "one or more counters are put on ..."), `trigger.attack-batch` ("you / another player / an opponent attacks with N or more <creatures>"), and the commander subjects of `triggerSubject` ("your commander", "a commander you control", `commander: 'yours'`). (2) **Conditions** (`rules/condition/angels.ts`): "it had counters on it" is folded by the lowering into the filter of the leaves/dies trigger (`hasCounter`; standalone it is refused, the engine has no test of the object after it left), "none of those creatures attacked you" is `attackersAttackedYou` (refused outside an attack batch), "you control three or more lands with the same name" is `sameNameAtLeast`. (3) **Statics and a replacement** (`rules/static/angels*.ts`, `rules/replacement/angels.ts`): player hexproof, "can't lose / opponents can't win", prevention of damage to `~`, "You can't cast ~ during your first, second, or third turns of the game", the block tax with an optional "As long as ~ is attacking, ", "Each other creature you control of the chosen type enters with an additional +1/+1 counter", the tap alternative cost, "If you would gain life, you gain that much life plus N instead", and the attached "is an Angel in addition to its other types". A grant may name a keyword as its subject ("Other creatures you control with flying have ..."). (4) **Effects** (`rules/effect/angels.ts`): proliferate, "for each opponent, exile up to one target <permanent> that player controls [until ~ leaves the battlefield]" (`perOpponent`, `until`), "This ability triggers only once each turn" and "Spend this mana only to cast an Angel spell" (both are sentences about the ability before them: the lowering of that ability sets `oncePerTurn` or `spendOnly` and drops the sentence; anywhere else they are read and not run), "one mana of the chosen color". (5) **"[you may] A. If C, you may B instead."** (`lowerMayInstead`) lowers to a conditional whose true branch offers B and, if the player declined, A. (6) **Nouns:** "that [nonland permanent] card" is an anaphor bound to an earlier graveyard target; "that land" no longer binds to a nonland card; a type choice joins with "and/or" and a power or toughness comparison may end it ("creature with power 2 or less" applies to the creature member only); "nonland permanent card" in a graveyard. (7) **New rules are quiet** (`quietly` in `rules/registry.ts`): a failure of a new rule is not recorded as a closest rule or a stopping point, so the diagnostics of lines it does not read stay what they were. (8) `PARSER_VERSION` 38.
- Alternatives: A rule for Exemplar's whole ability, or for each card: rejected. Reading "it had counters on it" as a condition on a standalone object: rejected, the engine looks at the object as it last was only for the trigger's own filter. Reading "or a planeswalker you control" after "attacked you" as "you": rejected, it says the opposite of the engine's `attackersAttackedYou` (the player alone); the rule refuses it. Making the limit sentences ordinary effects: rejected, an instruction that reads a previous sentence has no place in the engine's sequence; the ability's lowering owns it. Counting a spend-only restriction by color or chosen type: not read, the engine's `spendOnly` has card types and creature types only.
- Consequences: The twenty-two cards read and pass `validateCard`; the golden snapshot marks them supported and no other card changed status or AST (Cavern of Souls stays unsupported; its diagnostic slot moved from `effect` to `noun`). Siblings read: other types, numbers and players for each shape (`docs/MECHANICS.md`, "Stage P33"). The Dragons precon is not covered by this stage (its extract stays unsupported except the cards that already read: nine of the thirty-eight Dragons-deck cards in the golden corpus). Limits: `docs/ROADMAP.md`, "Parser stage P33 known limitations and deferred work". The owner reruns `pnpm corpus:decks` and `pnpm precon:snapshot` at parser version 38 to see whether the Angels precon is fully supported; no coverage number was invented. Tests: `parser-p33.test.ts`, `parser-p33-needs.test.ts` and `convert-grammar-engine-p33.test.ts`.

## D-151: The Dragons slice: playing exiled cards, abilities from the graveyard, the turn log, mana for Dragons, casting from the library, an enters-as-copy replacement, Read ahead, extra combat, other targets, reveals, Discover, behold and paying any amount (2026-10-29)
- Context: The owner's fifth precon (Dragons) has thirty cards the engine did not run (listed with their Oracle lines in `docs/MECHANICS.md`, "The Dragons slice (D-151)"). Their shapes are a few families with small variants, so the brief was general primitives, never a card name, with tests over synthetic cards and a mutation check for each. Face-down cards (Morph) need a proposal and the owner's approval (S class) and are not in this slice.
- Decision: (1) **Playing exiled cards.** The effects `exileTop {count}` and `mayPlay {objects: moved, lasts}`: a play permission (`ContinuousChange` `playPermission`) for the cards exiled, to cast them or play a land, ending with the turn, with the controller's next turn or as their next end step begins (`rules/impulse.ts`); the amount `exiledStillThere` is written into a delayed trigger as it is created (Dragonhawk). (2) **Abilities from the graveyard.** `functionsIn: 'graveyard'` on a static `grantKeyword` or `modifyPt` over a group and on a triggered ability (Anger, Spit Flame): the engine looks at the owner's graveyard as one more place that has abilities. (3) **The turn log** (`TurnLog`: `entered`, `damageTaken`, `attacked`, `modesChosen`, reset as each turn starts) and what reads it: `Condition` `enteredThisTurn` and `playerDealtDamage`, `attacks.firstTimeEachTurn`, `ModeChoice.notRepeatedThisTurn`. Conditional layer 4, 5 and 7b statics (types, colors, base power and toughness) may read only the conditions that need no layer (`plainConditionHolds`, CR 613.8), and a static may grant an activated or a triggered ability (Goddric, Tyrant's Familiar). (4) **Mana.** `fixed.times`, `anyCombination`, `spendOnly` with a type and a subtype together and `alsoAbilities`, `spentRider` ("if that mana is spent on a Dragon creature spell, it gains haste") and `unspentManaStays`. (5) **Casting from the top of the library**: `castFromTopOfLibrary {spells, gainsHaste}`. (6) **Choices as a permanent enters**: `asEntersChoose` of `option` with names the card gives and `Condition.chosenOption`; `Replacement.entersAsCopy` (asked before the permanent moves, so what triggers as it enters sees the copy; a continuous `copy` effect with the keywords the copy gains); the keyword `readAhead` (the chapter is a choice among "1" to the final chapter, and the turn the Saga enters only the chapter its lore counters name triggers) with `discard.anyNumber` and the `thisWay` amount `discarded`. (7) **Combat.** `extraCombat` (`TurnState.extraCombats`, one more combat phase after the one that ends, asked for only by a triggered ability of an attack), `enterAttacking`, the keyword `dethrone` (expands into a trigger), `Condition` `attackingMostLife` and `attackersTotalPower`, the keyword `myriad` (nothing to do with two players). (8) **Damage and targets.** `each.except`, `TargetSpec.differentFrom` (the answer checks it and `legalActionsForDecision` lists only answers that satisfy it), `ControllerFilter` `triggerPlayer` and `defendingPlayer`, `PlayerSelector` `eachOtherOpponent`. (9) **The library.** `revealTop`, `exileUntilCast` (Discover and Breaching Dragonstorm: the Cascade instruction with other limits, `variant`), the amount `shortfall`, `lookAtTop.rest: 'top'`, `behold` (a `chooseCards` of purpose `behold` over the matching cards of the hand and the matching permanents). (10) **Paying any amount**: `payAnyAmount` (a `chooseX` of purpose `payAnyAmount`, then the payment of that many symbols, then a reflexive ability whose "that much" is the number paid). New decision purposes: `chooseOption` `option`, `choosePermanent` `entersCopy`, `chooseCards` `behold`, `chooseX` `payAnyAmount`; the `discard` decision may have `min` 0; `confirmOptional` `cascade` is also Discover's question. `ENGINE_VERSION` 34. The AI answers every new decision (`packages/ai/src/casual-dragons.ts`) and a `dragons` soak style plays the cards (`packages/ai/test/dragons-games.test.ts`).
- Alternatives: A rule for each card: rejected. A new "enters or attacks" trigger: rejected, the parser writes two triggered abilities with one effect. A separate decision kind for the number paid, for beholding and for the copy: rejected, `chooseX`, `chooseCards` and `choosePermanent` have the right shape. Implementing Discover as its own instruction: rejected, it is Cascade's instruction with a limit on the card found, a limit on the card cast, a hand fallback and a choice of where the rest goes. Letting an extra combat phase be added from anywhere: rejected, it is added by a triggered ability of an attack only, where "after this phase" means this combat phase. Reading `triggerPlayer` as an effect-only selector: rejected, "target artifact that opponent controls" needs it in a filter, so `ControllerFilter` has it too and the pending trigger carries the player when a target reads it.
- Consequences: The thirty cards are covered by the engine (a few only in shape, listed per card in `docs/MECHANICS.md`) and the parser can lower them; the parser, the web wording and the golden snapshot are the steps that follow. What the engine does not do is in `docs/ROADMAP.md`, "The Dragons slice (D-151)": Myriad does nothing with more than two players (the engine has two), a creature that enters attacking attacks a player (no planeswalker), an extra combat phase is added only from an attack trigger, and `entersAsCopy` is not asked for a token.

## D-152: The parser reads the Dragons slice: exiling and playing the top cards, Discover and the casts of exiled cards, an additional combat, paying any amount, mana for Dragons, casting from the library, abilities from the graveyard, named options and an enters-as-copy replacement (2026-10-29)
- Context: D-151 gave the engine the primitives for the thirty cards of the owner's Dragons precon (the fifth and last) and listed, for each, the AST the parser must write (`docs/MECHANICS.md`, "The Dragons slice (D-151)"). The golden corpus holds their real Oracle text; none of the thirty was supported at parser version 38. The brief: general rules over the engine's creature type table (D-134), no card names, every line of every card read (saga chapters, Myriad, Dethrone, Read ahead and Discover included), the obvious siblings widened, and text the engine cannot run left unread and flagged.
- Decision: (1) **Segmenting.** The sentences that are one instruction stay together (`segment.ts`): "Exile cards from the top of your library until you exile a nonland card. You may cast it ... If you don't, put that card into your hand.", "The owner of target creature shuffles it into their library, then reveals the top card ... If it's a creature card, they put it onto the battlefield.", "Look at the top card of your library. If it's a Dragon card, you may reveal it and put it into your hand." and "Exile the top N cards ... You may play them this turn." read as one sequence. "As ~ enters, choose Khans or Dragons." keeps its bulleted options as separate lines (`normalize.ts`, `AbilitySkeleton.option`); the lowering writes each bullet's abilities with a `triggerCondition` of `chosenOption`. (2) **Effects** (`rules/effect/dragons.ts`, `dragons-more.ts`, widened `mana.ts`, `put.ts`, `bite.ts`, `library.ts`): `effect.exile-top`, `effect.may-play` (a duration phrase before or after: "this turn", "until the end of your next turn", "until your next end step"), `effect.extra-combat`, `effect.discover`, `effect.discover-treasures` (the shortfall under the Discover limit), `effect.exile-until-cast`, `effect.shuffle-reveal-top`, `effect.look-top-take`, `effect.behold`, `effect.pay-any-amount` (with the reflexive "When you do, it deals that much damage"), `effect.mana-rider` ("If that mana is spent on an Elf creature spell, it gains haste"), `effect.damage-other-targets` ("each of up to three other targets", `differentFrom`), `effect.discard-any-number`, "Add three mana in any combination of colors", "Add {R} for each ...", "put a ... card from your hand onto the battlefield tapped and attacking", "each other creature" with `except` and "Spend this mana only to cast Dragon spells or activate abilities of Dragons". (3) **Conditions, triggers, nouns, amounts** (`rules/condition/dragons.ts`, `trigger/dragons.ts`, `noun/dragons.ts`, `amount/dragons.ts`): `condition.attacking-most-life`, `condition.attackers-total-power`, `condition.player-dealt-damage`, `condition.entered-this-turn` (a creature, or a token), `trigger.attacks-first-time`, `noun.each-other-opponent`, `noun.other-targets`, `amount.for-each-still-exiled`. (4) **Statics and replacements** (`rules/static/dragons.ts`, `quoted.ts`, `replacement/dragons.ts`): `static.unspent-mana`, `static.cast-from-top`, a static with "As long as this card is in your graveyard" (`functionsIn`), "As long as a creature entered the battlefield under your control this turn", a quoted ability in the "is a Dragon with base power and toughness 4/4, flying, and \"{R}: ...\"" static of the card itself (`static.quoted-ability`, mana abilities excluded), `replacement.enters-as-copy` ("you may have it become a copy of any artifact on the battlefield, except it has flying"), "Each Zombie you control enters with an additional +1/+1 counter" over any creature type (without "other" only when the face itself cannot match), and `modal.choose-not-repeated`. The keywords Dethrone, Myriad and Read ahead are printed abilities only. The planeswalker types (CR 205.3j) are in the subtype table. (5) **Lowering** (`lower/dragons.ts`, `sentences.ts`, `statics.ts`, `conditions.ts`, `amounts.ts`): each clause lowering declares its features (`DRAGON_NEEDS`); a delayed trigger counted "for each of those cards that are still exiled" and the offer to pay any amount with its reflexive ability are lowered at sentence level (`lowerPayAnyAmount`); a reflexive ability that names its own source strips the trigger-subject reference (`ownSource`). (6) **Honest limits.** "You may play that card this turn" after anything but an exile of the top cards, "you may play them" with no duration, the Discover Treasures sentence alone, "Add three mana in any combination of colors" as a spell (the engine needs a chosen color), "activate abilities of Elves" after another type, and a quoted ability granted to a subject other than `~` are not read (`notRunnable` or unrecognised), never guessed. (7) `PARSER_VERSION` 39.
- Alternatives: A rule for each card's whole text: rejected, the brief asked for general rules. Reading Minion of the Mighty's "you may" as the engine's `choose.optional`: rejected, the parser's ability-level `optional` runs the same and is how every other "you may put" trigger reads. Reading the bulleted options of "choose Khans or Dragons" as modes: rejected, a permanent keeps the choice for as long as it is on the battlefield (CR 614.12, 607.2d), which is what `asEntersChoose` with `option` names says. Reading the quoted abilities granted to another subject (a group of creatures with a quoted ability): not read, the lowering of a granted ability (`lowerGrantedAbility`) handles the source only. Splitting the effect rules in two files (`dragons.ts`, `dragons-more.ts`): done to keep each file near 400 lines.
- Consequences: The thirty cards read and pass `validateCard`; the golden snapshot marks them supported and no other card changed status or AST. Siblings that read are listed in `docs/MECHANICS.md`, "Stage P34". Training share 160 of 192 and hold-out 51 of 61 (83.3% and 83.6%), a gap under one point. The owner reruns `pnpm corpus:decks` and `pnpm precon:snapshot` at parser version 39 to see whether the Dragons precon is fully supported; no coverage number was invented. Limits: `docs/ROADMAP.md`, "Parser stage P34 known limitations and deferred work". With this stage the five precons (Zombies, Artifacts, Dinosaurs, Angels and Dragons) have an engine and a parser; what remains for M9 is the card snapshots the owner commits. Tests: `parser-p34.test.ts`, `parser-p34-needs.test.ts` and `convert-grammar-engine-p34.test.ts`.

## D-153: A turn is named by its round, "Your turn 5", and the active player's whole area is highlighted (2026-10-29)
- Context: Issue 52: "you are counting turns on each player ... I prefer to see "Turn 5", or any other official name, when all players are in their 5th round", so that the player can count lands, ramp and the speed of the game ("everyone played 4 or 5 turns"). The top bar read "Turn 9" and "Opponent's turn" (the engine's counter, which counts every player's turn), and the log said "Turn 9: Opponent's turn." The owner's decision on the wording: "let's call 'Player's {P} turn {R}', so we keep the official naming but the round counting." The same session asked to make the active player clearer by highlighting the whole player battlefield instead of a name badge.
- Decision: (1) **The official word stays, the number is the round.** The top bar, the line of a new turn in the log and the log's turn headings say "Your turn 5" and "Opponent's turn 5": whose turn it is, "turn", and the round, the number of rounds started, `floor((turn - 1) / seats) + 1` with the real number of seats of the game (`roundOf` in `apps/web/src/game/turn-label.ts`; two players: engine turns 1 and 2 are round 1, 3 and 4 round 2). Before the first turn (setup) there is no round and the log heading says "Setup". A log line carries the active seat and the round (`LogEntry.activeSeat`, `LogEntry.round`) so a heading can say them; a log without them falls back to "Turn N". (2) **The engine's turn counter is unchanged.** `GameView.turn`, `TurnState.number`, the `turnBegan` event and everything that counts turns (the player's own turns for "your first three turns" use `SeatState.turnsTaken`, D-149) are as before; only the words and the number on screen change, in the web app. The log line is built in the web (`game/describe.ts`) from the event's seat and turn number, so no engine change was needed. The line reads "Your turn 5 begins." (3) **The active player's area is highlighted as a whole** (the owner's follow-up): while it is a player's turn, their strip, their battlefield and, for the viewer, their hand carry `is-active-area` (a tint of `--active-edge` mixed into the ground, a 4px bar along the left edge and a 3px line on the outer edge of the area), and the other area carries `is-idle-area` and stays on the plain ground. The bars are inset box shadows and a border colour that was already 4px wide, so no box moves: the controls column, the dock and the commander tile (D-144, D-146) are where they were (`e2e/turn-label.e2e.ts` compares the boxes with and without the classes at 1280x720 Large). The highlight follows the active player (CR 102.1), not who has priority; the "Turn" and "Priority" badges stay. It is not colour alone: each battlefield is a region named "Your battlefield, your turn" or "Opponent's battlefield, opponent's turn" while it is that player's turn, and the strip keeps its "Turn" badge. `--active-edge` is the accent in the dark theme and a darker gold in the light theme, so the edge keeps contrast on both.
- Alternatives: Numbering the round on its own ("Round 5"): the owner chose to keep the official word. Counting rounds in the engine (a `round` field on the turn state): rejected, nothing in the rules needs it and the engine's turn number must keep meaning every player's turn. Recording a round counter per log entry from the host's own count: rejected, it is a function of the turn number and the number of seats. Highlighting the active area with a frame around the board only, or by dimming the idle one: the tint is enough, and dimming would make the opponent's board harder to read during the player's turn (the idle area stays neutral). A `border-left` on the field and the hand: it would shift their content by the border's width; the inset shadow does not.
- Consequences: With two players "Your turn 5" and "Opponent's turn 5" are both in round 5, so counting lands or ramp per round reads directly. The number is derived from the turn number, so extra turns (the engine has none yet) would count as a turn of their own, and a player who has left a game with more than two players still counts as a seat; if the engine gains extra turns or removes seats, `roundOf` is the one place to change. Tests that read the old "Turn N" text (the smoke test) read "Your turn N" now.

## D-154: "Exile ... until this leaves the battlefield" returns the card as a second one-shot effect, not a triggered ability (2026-10-30)
- Context: Cleanup C re-checked the deviation audit (DEV-01) against CR 610.3. D-149 built "exile ... until this enchantment leaves the battlefield" with a delayed triggered ability (`EXILE_RETURN_ABILITY`) that triggered when the permanent left, went on the stack and returned the card when it resolved. CR 610.3 says "Some one-shot effects cause an object to change zones 'until' a specified event occurs. A second one-shot effect is created immediately after the specified event. This second one-shot effect returns the object to its previous zone." A one-shot effect created by an event is not a triggered ability (CR 603.7 is a different mechanism with its own wording), so nothing goes on the stack and no player can respond: the audit was right. The stack version also gave a player priority while the card was still in exile, ordered two returns as two triggers (a choice CR 610.3d does not give, which makes simultaneous events produce simultaneous one-shot effects), and let a player respond to the return.
- Decision: The exile records an `ExileReturn {source, card, controller}` in `GameState.exileReturns` (a new state field, empty at setup) instead of a `DelayedTrigger`. `settle` (`rules/settle.ts`), which runs before any player would get priority, calls `releaseExiled` (`rules/exile-return.ts`) at the top of every round, before state-based actions and before triggers are put on the stack: every record whose source is no longer on the battlefield (its object id is gone or in another zone, CR 400.7) is released at once, as one batch, so the returns that follow simultaneous leaving are simultaneous (CR 610.3d) and the triggers of everything that enters are collected together. The batch runs as a resolution with no object on the stack (`ResolutionContext.object` is the source's last-known id; `finish` only moves an object that is on the stack), so a decision inside it (the host an Aura chooses, CR 303.4f; an "as it enters" choice) pauses it like any resolution and is answered by the same handlers; `SettleResult.paused` tells `grantPriority` and the cleanup step to stop there. The card returns under its owner's control (CR 610.3c). A card that left exile in the meantime is a new object and is dropped from the batch (CR 400.7). CR 610.3a and 610.3b (the event already happened as the exile would occur: nothing moves) stay in the `exile` effect, so such a record is never made. `withAuraEntries` (`rules/aura-entry.ts`) is shared by the `moveToZone` effect and by the batch. The delayed-trigger `subject` field and `EXILE_RETURN_ABILITY` are removed. A synthetic "destroy all enchantments" fixture covers CR 610.3d.
- Alternatives: Keeping the delayed trigger and putting it on the stack above the effect that caused it: rejected, it is still a triggered ability and a player still gets to respond. Returning the card from inside `moveObject` as the source leaves: rejected, the zone-change pipeline has no resolution context to ask an Aura's host or an "as it enters" question, and the leaving of several permanents would have to be batched there. Running the batch in `collectTriggers`: rejected, it returns only a state, and the events of the return have to be scanned for triggers.
- Consequences: The return happens when the engine next settles (after the spell or ability that removed the source has finished resolving, or after the state-based action that did), which is the engine's "immediately after" for every event, the same granularity as state-based actions. It no longer appears as an ability on the stack, so the web shows no "return" entry and the log has no `abilityTriggered` for it. Existing tests keep passing because they passed priority until the stack was empty; `test/scenario-xx-exile-until-return.test.ts` pins the new timing (no trigger, nothing on the stack, both cards back together). `ENGINE_VERSION` 35: a replay recorded at 34 may differ for a game that used such a card. The docs that still name `EXILE_RETURN_ABILITY` and the delayed trigger (`docs/MECHANICS.md`, `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`) are fixed by the docs rewrite.

## D-155: A spell's life cost may take the caster's whole life total (2026-10-30)
- Context: Cleanup C re-checked DEV-03 of the deviation audit against CR 119.4: "If a cost or effect allows a player to pay an amount of life greater than 0, the player may do so only if their life total is greater than or equal to the amount of the payment." `canPaySpellCost` (`rules/cast-cost.ts`) refused a spell whose life cost (an additional cost "pay N life", a kicker or multikicker cost of life, or "pay X life") left the caster below 1 life, so a player could not pay exactly their life total. D-101 chose that on purpose ("so the planner's rule for a player at 0 life cannot strand the cast"). That reason does not hold: after the life is paid the mana planner gets a budget of `max(0, life - 1)` for Phyrexian mana and sources that damage, so at 0 life it simply spends none, and the mana of an ordinary source is still paid. Activated abilities, Ward and a shock land already allowed the whole total (`rules/activate-costs.ts`, `rules/pay-unless.ts`).
- Decision: `canPaySpellCost` requires `life >= cost.life`. Everything that reads it follows: a spell with an additional life cost is castable with exactly that much life, a life kicker is offered, a multikicker's most is `floor(life / cost)`, and the largest X of "pay X life" is the whole life total. The caster is at 0 life after paying; state-based actions end the game for them (CR 704.5a) before the spell resolves, as with a real Toxic Deluge for X equal to the life total. The AI is unchanged: it never pays life at or below `PAY_LIFE_ABOVE` (`casual-costs.ts`, `casual-x.ts`), so it does not use the new option. Tests that asserted the old limit were changed after reading CR 119.4: `scenario-xx-additional-costs` (3 life with a 3-life cost is legal, 2 is not), `scenario-xx-kicker` (a 3-life kicker at 3 life is offered; the double kicker at 1 life), `scenario-xx-multikicker` (the most kicks), `scenario-xx-x-costs` (X up to 20 at 20 life, up to 1 at 1 life, and a new case that pays all 4 and loses).
- Alternatives: Keeping the 1-life floor as a UI protection: rejected, the rules allow the payment and the engine's priority is rules correctness; an agent that wants the protection has the AI's `PAY_LIFE_ABOVE` rule, and a human who does not want it can decline a kicker or choose a smaller X. Letting the mana planner also pay Phyrexian mana with the last life: not done here, see the consequences.
- Consequences: Known limit that stays: the automatic mana planner never takes its own player to 0 life for Phyrexian mana or a source that damages (`lifeAvailable` is `life - 1` in `rules/mana-sources.ts` and `rules/pay-manual.ts`); CR 119.4 would allow a Phyrexian payment of exactly the life total, and damage from a source is not a payment. A player who wants either pays by hand. `ENGINE_VERSION` 35 (the same bump as D-154).

## D-156: Replacement-effect ordering (CR 616.1) stays unbuilt: a known, deliberate gap while the owner's proposal is on hold (2026-10-30)
- Context: DEV-04 of the deviation audit, re-checked in cleanup C against the code and CR 616.1 ("If two or more replacement and/or prevention effects are attempting to modify the way an event affects an object or player, the affected object's controller ... chooses one to apply", with 616.1a-e fixing which must be chosen first and 616.1f repeating the process). Verified: `rules/die-replacement.ts` (header) applies the `wouldDie` replacement of the oldest permanent and asks nothing; `rules/prevention.ts` (header) applies the shields that prevent all damage first and then the numeric ones, oldest first, and asks nothing. The zone-change pipeline (`rules/zones.ts`, `rules/enters.ts`) has no general replacement library: the replacements it knows (enters tapped, enters with counters, "you may pay N life or it enters tapped", the commander replacement, `wouldDie`, `lifeGainBonus`, `othersEnterWithCounters`, `entersAsCopy` and "as it enters, choose") are applied in a fixed order. The audit's reach statement is unchanged: no card of the four fully supported precons has two replacements that compete for one event, and the counter replacements that exist add, so their order does not matter.
- Decision: No engine change. A proposal for an `orderReplacements` decision (which kind to add, and where the pipeline asks it) exists and the owner has put it on hold, so this is recorded as a known deviation: CR 616.1 is Partial in `docs/RULES_COVERAGE.md` ("Known deviations from the CR", status "on hold"), the limit is in `docs/ROADMAP.md` ("Rules deviations (cleanup C)"), and the engine keeps its fixed orders. The wrong-outcome cases are two competing replacements for one event: a doubler and an adder of counters, two numeric prevention shields, two "would die" replacements (an exile and a shuffle into the library). Until the proposal is unblocked no card with such a pair may be marked supported on the strength of the current order; the support playbook's rule that a card the engine does not fully understand is flagged applies.
- Alternatives: A partial ordering question for `wouldDie` only: rejected, the owner asked for the whole proposal to wait and a one-off decision would have to be redone. Silently keeping the fixed order with no record: rejected, the audit found the gap and the honesty rule of `AGENTS.md` asks for it to be written down.
- Consequences: No behavior change and no `ENGINE_VERSION` change. When the owner unblocks the proposal, this entry, the "Partial" rows (614, 616; 614.1a, 700.4, 614.12, 704.3) and the ROADMAP bullets are the work list. **Superseded for damage events by D-191** (2026-11-02): prevention effects on a damage event are ordered by the affected player; the rest of this entry stays in force.

## D-157: "Each player sacrifices a creature": all choose, then all are sacrificed together (2026-10-30)
- Context: DEV-06 of the deviation audit, re-checked in cleanup C against CR 101.4: "If multiple players would make choices and/or take actions at the same time, the active player ... makes any choices required, then the next player in turn order ..., followed by the remaining nonactive players in turn order. Then the actions happen simultaneously." Its example is exactly "Each player sacrifices a creature." (the choices first, then all creatures chosen are sacrificed simultaneously), and CR 101.4b says each player knows the choices of the previous ones. The engine emitted one `chooseSacrifice` instruction per player and each one sacrificed its player's creature as soon as it was chosen. The observable difference was real, not only cosmetic: a player's decision pauses the resolution and the engine collects the triggers of the events so far at that pause, so a creature sacrificed by the first player was looked back at in a batch of its own and did not see the second player's creature die (CR 603.10a: abilities that trigger from a simultaneous event look back in time). With a "whenever a creature dies" permanent on the battlefield (Blood Artist style) the first player's watcher missed the opponent's sacrifice.
- Decision: `chooseSacrifice` carries `together: {later, held}` when more than one player sacrifices (`rules/effects.ts`, `rules/sacrifice-choice.ts`, `state/types.ts`): the instruction asks the first player (active player first, as `resolvePlayers` already orders them), and when that player has chosen (or the engine chose for them, or they have no candidate) it puts the same instruction back for the next player with the earlier choice held in `held`; the last player's instruction turns every held choice into `sacrifice` instructions, in that order, one after another with no other event between them, which `findTriggers` reads as one run of departures (`beforeDepartures`). The decisions, their wording and the `permanentsChosen` events are unchanged. A single player (the controller, or one named player) takes the old path. The effect "sacrifice all ..." (`each` selector) has no choices and was already one run.
- Alternatives: A new instruction kind and a `ResolutionContext` field that holds the choices: rejected, a field on the instruction that already waits for the answer needs no new step type, no change to `continueResolution` and no new answer handler. Marking the events of one resolution as simultaneous: rejected, DEV-07 shows that a run of departures is read from the event order and a general marker would be a different change (D-160).
- Consequences: `ENGINE_VERSION` 35 (a replay with two players sacrificing differs only in when the first player's creature leaves: after the second player has chosen). A choice by the second player cannot depend on the first player's creature having left (CR 101.4b says it is known, not gone). Not changed: the other effects in which each player chooses (discard, return to the hand) still act after each choice; no supported card was found that needs them. Tests: `test/scenario-xx-sacrifice-together.test.ts` (the order of the questions, the Watcher that sees both die, a player with no creature, one creature each).

## D-158: A reselected attacker (CR 508.7a): the audit named a reader that is already right, so nothing changes (2026-10-30)
- Context: DEV-08 of the deviation audit says a creature whose target was reselected "is no longer recorded as having attacked the first target", so "none of those creatures attacked you" (`attackersAttackedYou`, Firemane Commando) would read the new target. CR 508.7a: "The attacking creature isn't removed from combat and it isn't considered to have attacked a second time. That creature is attacking the reselected player or permanent, but it's still considered to have attacked the player or permanent chosen as it was declared as an attacker."
- Decision: No code change; the claim is wrong for the reader it names. `reselectAttack` (`rules/reselect-attack.ts`) changes only `combat.attackers[].target`, which is what "attacking you" reads for as long as the creature is in combat (`attackersOfPlayer` in `rules/select.ts`, the rule's "is attacking the reselected player"). The batch trigger takes the players the creatures were declared at from the declaration event as the trigger is collected (`attackBatch` in `rules/triggers.ts`, `PendingTrigger.attacked`, `StackData.triggerAttacked`), and `attackersAttackedYou` reads that copy, so a reselect after the declaration cannot change it: the creature "is still considered to have attacked" the target it was declared at. A test pins it (`test/scenario-xx-reselect-attack.test.ts`, "a reselected attacker is still considered to have attacked the first target": two attackers, one declared at the player is moved to a planeswalker by a Signpost-style trigger, and the attacker's opponent does not draw from the Marshal's "none of those creatures attacked you"; the control case with both declared at the planeswalker does draw).
- Alternatives: Adding a per-attacker list of the targets it has attacked: rejected, nothing reads it (no supported card or primitive asks "who did this creature attack, as declared" after the declaration step), and a field with no reader is a stub.
- Consequences: The limit that remains is latent: a future condition or trigger that asks about the declared target after the declaration step must read it from the `attackersDeclared` event or add a record then; today `TurnLog.attacked` holds creatures, not their targets. The "Partial" 508.7 row of `docs/RULES_COVERAGE.md` and the ROADMAP bullet of the Artifacts slice that say the record is not kept are out of date in this respect; no `ENGINE_VERSION` change.

## D-159: Layer dependency (CR 613.8) stays partial: a known gap while the owner's decision is on hold (2026-10-30)
- Context: DEV-05 of the deviation audit, re-checked in cleanup C against CR 613.8 (dependency: "If a dependency exists, it will override the timestamp system"; 613.8a defines "depends on"; 613.8b says a dependent effect waits until just after the effects it depends on and that a dependency loop is applied in timestamp order; 613.8c reevaluates after each effect). Verified in `rules/derive-statics.ts` (the case of D-111 and D-149: an effect that reads power, toughness or keywords is applied after the others and looked at again until none more applies), `rules/derive-group-types.ts` (a group type effect reads the view from before the other statics), `rules/copiable.ts` (copy effects: the last by timestamp wins): there is no general dependency graph, a loop (613.8b) is not told apart, and effects on a type that another static changes (a Humility-like chain) apply in timestamp order. `docs/RULES_COVERAGE.md` already says "Partial" in the 613.8 rows.
- Decision: No engine change. How general to go (the full 613.8 graph, or more special cases like D-111) is a design choice the owner has put on hold. The gap is recorded here and in `docs/ROADMAP.md` ("Rules deviations (cleanup C)"). The audit's reach statement stands: the keyword-reading case that a supported card reaches (Sephara with Angelic Destiny or Kenrith's Transformation) is handled; the loop and type-chain cases are reached by no supported card.
- Alternatives: More special cases now: rejected, the owner asked for the decision to wait and each special case makes the later general solution harder to introduce. Refusing the cards that could reach it: not needed, none is supported.
- Consequences: No behavior change and no `ENGINE_VERSION` change. Wrong outcomes remain possible for chains of layered effects with no supported card (Blood Moon with Urborg style effects, three-step chains, Mycosynth Lattice with March of the Machines); a card that needs one must not be marked supported until this is decided.

## D-160: Look back in time (CR 603.10a) across separate steps of one resolution: verified deviation, known limit (2026-10-30)
- Context: DEV-07 of the deviation audit was marked unverified. CR 603.10a: some zone-change triggers (leaves-the-battlefield, a player sacrificing a permanent, a card leaving a graveyard, ...) "look back in time"; its example is one spell that destroys artifacts, creatures and enchantments together, so the artifact's "whenever a creature dies" triggers for both creatures. What looks back is the event; a permanent that left in an earlier instruction of the same spell is not on the battlefield when a later instruction moves another one, so it cannot see that one leave (CR 608.2c carries a spell's instructions out one after another).
- Decision: Verified as a deviation, not fixed. `findTriggers` (`rules/triggers.ts`) collects the triggers of all the events of a resolution at once and keeps the battlefield "before departures" (`beforeDepartures`) for as long as the events are consecutive departures; two instructions that each move a permanent and that produce no other event in between are read as one run. The test `test/scenario-xx-lookback-steps.test.ts` ran: a spell "Destroy target creature. Then destroy another target creature." aimed at a "whenever a creature you control leaves the battlefield, you gain 1 life" creature first and a Grizzly Bears second gives the player 2 life, the rules give 1 (the watcher is gone before the Bears leave); the same two in the other order (22) and a single instruction that destroys both (22) are right. The first case is pinned with `test.fails`, so it turns into a failure, and the line must go, when the deviation is fixed. The fix is a marker between the effect steps of a sequence that ends a run (a new event kind, or the start of each `effect` instruction, but not each instruction, because "sacrifice all" is one run of many `sacrifice` instructions); it changes the event type and what every consumer of events (the web log, the AI, the replays) sees, so it is left for a change of its own.
- Alternatives: Fixing it in this pass with an `instructionBoundary` event: rejected for now, see above. Treating each instruction as a step: rejected, it would split "destroy all" and "each player sacrifices" into many events, which is the opposite deviation (D-157 relies on one run).
- Consequences: Reach: a resolution with two effect steps that move permanents back to back and a leaving or dying watcher that is itself one of the first to leave. Whether a card pair of the five precons does that was not searched (the audit could not name one), so it is a live but narrow deviation. No behavior change and no `ENGINE_VERSION` change.

## D-161: The AI plays forward on a determinized sample of the real state, and may know the opponent's decklist (2026-10-30)
- Context: The `HeuristicAgent` (M7) scores blocks, attacks and plays by playing them forward on a copy with `applyAction`, which needs a `GameState`. SPEC A10 said `determinize(view, rng)` and that the AI does not know the opponent's decklist. The owner decided (2026-10-30): the AI may know the opponent's initial decklist and every card revealed in play, but not a hand and not the order of any library.
- Decision: SPEC A31 amends A10. `determinize(state, viewer, rng)` (`packages/engine/src/determinize.ts`, exported from the engine) runs on the host side, where the real state is, and returns a copy in which what the viewer cannot know is drawn again from the supplied `RngState` alone. For every other seat the cards of its hand, library and face-down exile (foretold, Hideaway: `isFaceDownTo`, shared with `getView`) are pooled and dealt back into the same slots; a foretold slot only receives a card with a foretell cost. Every library, the viewer's own included, is reordered, except the top card a permanent lets the viewer look at (CR 401.5) and the cards of the viewer's own pending `chooseCards` or `arrangeCards` decision. Commander cards are public and are not pooled. The seed and `rng` of the state, and of the snapshot a casting transaction holds, are replaced by values drawn from the supplied rng. The agent reaches it through `DecideContext.sample(seed)`, which `runGame` and the web host build lazily from the state and the deciding seat. Because the AI may know the decklist, "decklist minus public cards" equals the hidden cards as a multiset, so the pool needs no decklist input.
- Alternatives: Rebuild a state from the view alone: rejected, the view lacks continuous effects, timestamps, delayed triggers and library order. Simulate on the true state: rejected, it leaks the real next draws and the opponent's hand. Give the agent the decklist and sample from it: rejected, the pool of the real state is the same multiset and cannot disagree with the zones' counts.
- Consequences: The agent plays the sample with `applyAction` and never sees the hidden truth; the sample's objects keep the ids of their slots and are given other cards, so an id does not name its card (setup numbers the objects and the cards of a deck alike, so in the real state the id of an untouched library object names its card). What the sample forgets: what the viewer learned earlier and the state does not record (a card revealed from a hand, a card scried to the top, a tutored card put on top). What it does not handle: a pending decision of another seat that lists cards of a hidden zone (a sample is meant for the deciding seat, whose decision is its own), and a `resolution` context that holds hidden cards of another seat in the middle of an effect. No `ENGINE_VERSION` change: no rule changed.

## D-162: M7b: the board evaluator, reason codes, GreedyAgent and the paired-seed match harness (2026-10-30)
- Context: M7 is done when `HeuristicAgent` beats `GreedyAgent` in 70% of 200 games, beats `RandomLegalAgent` in 95%, and mirrored self-play lands between 40% and 60% per seat (SPEC A11, D-011). M7b builds what that measurement and the stronger agent need: a benchmark agent, a way to run matches, a score for a position and a record of why an agent chose an action (PRIOR_ART 7.2 heuristics 4, 7 and 10; heuristics 1 and 2 as far as A11 needs them). The ideas of the evaluator are common to Magic AIs (the PRIOR_ART table cites XMage's `GameStateEvaluator2` and Forge's `CreatureEvaluator` as idea-only sources); the numbers and the code are ours and nothing was copied.
- Decision, evaluator (`packages/ai/src/evaluate.ts`): `evaluate(view, seat)` returns `{ score, terms }`, every term `{ seat, reason, value }`. The score is the ADVANTAGE of `seat`: strength(seat) minus the strength of every other seat, so in a two-seat game `evaluate(v, a).score === -evaluate(v, b).score` (a property test pins it) and a search can maximise for one side and minimise for the other with one function. It reads public view data only (`handCount` for every seat). Terms: a concave life curve `36 * (1 - e^(-life / 18))` (strictly increasing everywhere, the 41st point worth about a tenth of the 5th); the worst single commander's damage as its own clock, `30 * (d / 21)^2`, labelled "danger" from 70% and a loss at 21 (CR 704.6c); poison the same toward 10 (CR 704.5c); a body term per creature from power and toughness (damage marked counts against toughness) and one term per valued keyword (flying, menace, trample, first strike, double strike, deathtouch, lifelink, hexproof, indestructible, vigilance, haste, reach), with evasion and combat keywords growing with power; tokens at 0.6 of the same card, tapped at 0.8, summoning-sick at 0.9; a point per other permanent and loyalty; a small bonus per card in hand and per land (flattening past seven and eight). A seat that has lost is worth 1000 less. Not valued: abilities beyond the keyword list, defender and "can't block" (the evaluator does not read text), the graveyard, the library and the stack. The numbers are first values, to be tuned by the M7c measurements, not by hand.
- Decision, reason codes (`reasons.ts`): `Reason` is a closed string union; `ReasonRecord` is `{ decisionKind, action, reason }`; an agent that explains itself implements `ExplainingAgent` (an `Agent` with `reasons`). The `Agent` interface is unchanged. The match harness counts the reasons by agent.
- Decision, `GreedyAgent` (`greedy-agent.ts`, `greedy-combat.ts`): priority, attackers and blockers are its own; every other decision kind is answered by `createCasualHandlers` (the casual handlers, composed, not copied), so it handles every kind and cannot deadlock; its PRNG is its own and a throwing handler falls back to the first safe legal action and is recorded, as on the `CasualAgent`. (1) It plays a land when one is offered (an untapped one first).
