- Alternatives: Lowering Tireless Provisioner's choice as a modal triggered ability (D-105, D-114, "choose one" with two modes): rejected, a mode is chosen as the ability goes on the stack, so a player could respond knowing it, which CR 608.2d does not allow, and it would put the card's text into modes that it does not have. A card-specific token choice: rejected, the node is general (any two to eight instructions). Reading "dies" for a non-creature in the lowering only (an Aura's `leavesBattlefield` trigger with `to: ['graveyard']`): rejected, it would leave the engine's `dies` wrong for every other permanent and every card text that says "dies". A `chooseBackground` field on the face instead of a keyword: rejected, `partner` is a keyword and the parser, the validator and the web already know that shape.
- Consequences: Tireless Provisioner and its kind ("create a Food token or a Treasure token", and later "draw a card or gain 1 life") are expressible. Every game now sees `died` events for tokens such as a sacrificed Treasure and for lands and Auras; the triggers for creatures read types as before, so nothing that ran changes: the nine seeded games of `derive-differential.test.ts` reproduce their old fingerprints with `ENGINE_VERSION` left at 35 and the new `died`, and differ only by the version (the state hash carries it), so `derive-digest.expected.json` was recorded again for 36 (`UPDATE_DERIVE_DIGESTS=1`, as that file says to do after a new `ENGINE_VERSION`). One test of an old scenario (`scenario-03-object-identity.test.ts`) asserted that no `died` event existed in a log in which an Aura had died earlier; it now looks only at the events of the step it is about. The log shows "X dies." for a non-creature permanent, the CR's own word. The casual agent's choice reads the words of the options, which is a limit: an option it cannot tell apart by them is the first listed. Tests: `scenario-xx-choose-one.test.ts`, `scenario-xx-dies-permanent.test.ts`, `scenario-xx-choose-background.test.ts` (engine, SYNTHETIC cards `synthetic-choose-one.ts`), `casual-choose-one.test.ts` (AI), `korvold-model.test.ts`, `korvold-render.test.tsx` and `e2e/choose-one.e2e.ts` (web, hidden deck `synthetic-choose-one`).

## D-176: The parser reads the Korvold slice, text and tokens: tokens with abilities in quotes, a number of tokens equal to a power, one of two tokens, the enchanted creature, "that creature" on the next line, a card chosen from the graveyard, the graveyard shuffled in, "it" as the card a permanent became, the controller of a permanent, Equip with mana and life, Choose a Background (2026-11-02)
- Context: D-175 gave the engine the three pieces the twelve cards of slice 1 needed; the other nine lines read once the grammar said them. Per card, what was unread and why at parser 39 (the first piece of each line; a second piece behind it was looked for by running every line and its siblings again after each rule): Awakening Zone, "It has \"Sacrifice this token: Add {C}.\"" (a sentence about the token just made); Beledros Witherbloom and Nesting Dragon, a token with an ability in quotes, nested for the Dragon Egg; Goldvein Hydra, "a number of tapped Treasure tokens equal to its power"; Tireless Provisioner, "a Food token or a Treasure token"; Rancor, "return it to its owner's hand" in a trigger of the card going to the graveyard; Gilt-Leaf's Embrace, "enchanted creature gains trample and indestructible until end of turn"; Temur Battle Rage, "That creature also gains trample ... if you control a creature with power 4 or greater" on a line of its own; The Mending of Dominaria, "then you may return a creature card from your graveyard to your hand" and "shuffle your graveyard into your library"; My Precious, "Equip—{2}, Pay 2 life."; Ganax, "Choose a Background"; Cindervines, "that permanent's controller" as the recipient of damage. Pieces that hid behind the first unread one: Awakening Zone, Beledros and Nesting Dragon each needed the end of a sentence that closes with a quotation (the period is inside the quote); Goldvein Hydra's "its power" was unbound until the binding pass visited the count of a token (`selector:bound`); Temur Battle Rage's line needed "that creature" as a noun, "also", and the target of the line before; Rancor needed "it" lowered as the card the permanent became and then the engine's `died` event (D-175); Mending's chapters I and II needed the chosen card from the graveyard, not only chapter III's shuffle.
- Decision: (1) **Normalizing** (`normalize.ts`): "this token" inside a quotation is `~`, the token (a card's own text never says it, so it is rewritten only inside quotes). **Segmenting** (`sentence.ts`): a sentence that ends with an ability in quotes ends at the period inside the closing quote, also with a quote inside the quote (`.'"`), once that quote is the last thing of the text. (2) **Tokens with abilities** (`rules/token/index.ts`, `rules/static/quoted.ts`, `lower/tokens.ts`, `lower/late.ts`): `token.custom` reads `with <keywords>`, `with "<ability>"` and `with <keywords> and "<ability>"`; the ability is an activated, a mana or a triggered ability read by the same rules as a card's, a quote inside it (`'{R}: ...'`) is the ability of another token, and the lowering gives each to the token's `TokenDefinition.abilities` (`validateCard` checks them). The shared reader `readQuotedAbility` replaces the body of the granted-ability reader of D-152 (`static.quoted-ability`), which keeps its behaviour. The lowering of a token's ability needs the lowerings of triggered and activated abilities, which sit above the clause lowerings and could not be imported by them (`no-circular`): `lower/index.ts` registers them in `lower/late.ts` as it loads. `effect.it-has-ability` reads "It has \"...\"" and the binding pass folds that sentence into the `createToken` clause before it when that is one described token (`ir/fold-token.ts`); anywhere else the sentence stays and is flagged. (3) **Counts** (`token.number-of`): "a number of [tapped] Treasure tokens equal to <amount>" (a predefined or a described token, plural), the pronoun of the amount bound by the binding pass as for any amount (`ir/bind.ts`). (4) **One of two tokens** (`effect.create-token`): " or a Treasure token" after one predefined token of one; the lowering is `chooseOne` of two `createToken` with the labels "create a Food token" and "create a Treasure token" (`lower/effects.ts`). (5) **Subjects** (`rules/effect/pump.ts`, `gain.ts`, `rules/noun/korvold.ts`): a pump or a gain may be said of the permanent an Aura or an Equipment is attached to ("enchanted creature gains ..."), lowered as the engine's `attached`; `noun.that-object` ("that creature", "that permanent", ...) and "also" after the subject ("That creature also gains trample"); in a spell a "that creature" on a line of its own is bound to the last single target of the line before (`BindScope.lastTarget`), and no other pronoun crosses a line (a test of `parser-diagnostics.test.ts` keeps "Tap it." unbound). (6) **Graveyard** (`rules/effect/korvold.ts`): `effect.return-chosen-card` ("you may return a creature card from your graveyard to your hand", chosen, not targeted, `moveToZone` of a `choose` selector, `optional` with "you may", the words read inside the clause so that one after "then" can say them) and `effect.shuffle-graveyard` (every card of the graveyard to the library, then `shuffle`). (7) **"It" as the card** (`rules/effect/index.ts`, `lower/effects.ts`): `return it to its owner's hand` is read, and the lowering gives `thisCard` in a trigger of the permanent dying or leaving, `this` where it is still there, and refuses it for anything that is gone or anything else. (8) **The controller of a permanent** (`rules/effect/operands.ts`, `lower/nouns.ts`): `noun.its-controller` is a recipient of damage ("~ deals 2 damage to that permanent's controller", `controllerOf`, read from last-known information, CR 608.2h). (9) **Equip** (`rules/keyword/attachments.ts`, `lower/abilities.ts`): "Equip—{2}, Pay 2 life." is a mana cost and a payment of life, each once (the rule is tried at every keyword line, as the cost begins the line). (10) **Keyword** `choose a background` (`rules/keyword/vocabulary.ts`). `PARSER_VERSION` is 40; five new rule ids (`effect.it-has-ability`, `effect.return-chosen-card`, `effect.shuffle-graveyard`, `token.number-of`, `noun.that-object`), and the golden snapshot (`packages/cards/test/fixtures/corpus/golden.expected.json`) changed only in the version and in the text of one unread line of a card that already was unsupported (Urza's Saga: "this token" inside quotes reads `~` now); training and hold-out supported shares are as before, 160 of 192 and 51 of 61 (83.3% and 83.6%, a gap of 0.3 points), because none of the twelve cards is in the corpus (the owner's extraction of `docs/proposals/korvold-acceptance-names.txt` adds them as acceptance cards).
- Alternatives: A rule for each card's whole text: rejected, every rule above is a phrase of the grammar with its examples and refusals. Binding every pronoun across the lines of a spell: rejected, the test that one line's "it" is unbound is deliberate (`parser-diagnostics.test.ts`) and only "that creature", which cannot stand without an antecedent, reaches the line before. Putting a token's quoted ability in the grammar of statics: rejected, a mana ability and a "when this token dies" trigger are abilities of the token, not statements about something else. Importing the lowerings of triggered and activated abilities into the clause lowerings: rejected, a cycle the boundary rules forbid; the registration is one function call in the one module that sits above both. Reading "a number of ... equal to" as an amount that follows a token of count one: rejected, "a" would then have two meanings; the token rule that reads it says so.
- Consequences: The twelve cards read and pass `validateCard` (parser version 40), and their wording, a game of each and the lines near them are tested (below). Limits, also in `docs/ROADMAP.md`: a token with an ability in quotes that is a static ability or a keyword the engine cannot grant ("with \"This creature gets +1/+1 for each artifact you control.\"") stays unread; a card that names itself in the quoted ability of a token it makes would be read as naming the token (the normalizer writes both as `~`; no card of the slice does); a sentence with an ability in quotes that is followed by another sentence in the same text is not split after the quote's own period (it reads only where the line goes on as one clause list, "... token with \"...\" Then draw a card."); "It has" reads only after one described token; `chooseOne` is read only for two predefined tokens of one; "return it" is for the card a permanent became; the casual agent's choice reads the words of the options. Tests: `parser-p35.test.ts` (the twelve real cards as the nodes the engine runs, the siblings, the refusals, the words), `parser-p35-needs.test.ts` (each feature named when missing), `convert-grammar-engine-p35.test.ts` (a game of each shape with SYNTHETIC cards that carry the real wording), the rules' `examples` and `rejects` (`parser-registry.test.ts`) and the updated expectations of `parser-p3`, `parser-p15`, `parser-p17`, `convert-grammar-corpus-p3` and `-p18`, which named lines that are read now.

## D-177: The Korvold slice 2, fetch lands, reflexive sacrifice and Treasure grants, engine: what a search finds is "it", the sacrificed permanent is readable in the reflexive ability, and a trigger for spells only (2026-11-02)
- Context: Slice 2 of the owner's Korvold deck is nine cards (`docs/proposals/korvold-deck-analysis.md`): Cabaretti Courtyard, Maestros Theater, Riveteers Overlook, Jund Panorama, Fabled Passage, Far Wanderings, Ziatora, the Incinerator, Goldspan Dragon and Bootleggers' Stash. Each was run through today's parser and `validateCard` before planning, from the owner's request file with a placeholder power and toughness for the two creatures (the file has none); the pipeline reports only the first unread piece of a line, so each line was then run again piece by piece. Per card, what was unread and why, and the engine facts that came out: the three Courts and Jund Panorama stopped at "a basic Mountain, Forest, or Plains card" (the list of types after "basic"); behind it the Courts' "When you do" after "sacrifice it" was `notRunnable`, the lowering read a reflexive ability only after a "you may" offer, while the engine's `reflexive` was already valid after a plain `sacrifice` (`MAY_EFFECT_KINDS`), counted by `performed`, and ran (a scenario test proves it); Fabled Passage stopped at "Then if you control four or more lands, untap that land", and behind it `search` left nothing for "it": the engine's `moved` (CR 400.7j) was set by `exile`, `destroy` and `moveToZone` only; Far Wanderings' second line "If there are seven or more cards in your graveyard, instead search ..." was unread, and behind it the line was lowered apart from the one it replaces and the condition "there are seven or more cards in your graveyard" did not exist; Ziatora needed `selector:bound`: "that creature's power" in the reflexive ability, which no engine reference named (`sacrificedCost` is the permanent sacrificed as the cost of an activated ability); Goldspan's "attacks or becomes the target of a spell" needed an engine trigger for spells only and `trigger.or` for it, and its granted "{T}, Sacrifice this artifact: Add two mana of any one color." was refused by the parser (a `~` in a granted ability, a group), not by the engine; Bootleggers' Stash's "Lands you control have \"{T}: Create a Treasure token.\"" was refused by the lowering (only `this`), not by the engine. Class corrections: the three Courts, T + P in the analysis, are T (the reflexive after a plain sacrifice needed no engine change; the engine reads the `sacrifice` it counted); Goldspan's grant, P in the analysis, is T (a mana ability that sacrifices its permanent is still a mana ability, CR 605.1a, and the payment planner already has a tier of sacrifice sources, the Treasure's own; a Treasure that has two such abilities offers both and the planner uses one, a source is tapped once); Bootleggers' Stash stays T and the engine check the analysis asked for passed (each land offers the ability, `scenario-xx-fetch-grants.test.ts`); Fabled Passage is P + T, Ziatora P, Goldspan P (spells only) + T, Far Wanderings T.
- Decision: (1) **A search leaves "it"** (`rules/effects.ts`, `ast/validate-parts.ts`): the `search` effect starts the `moved` reference empty (CR 400.7j) and each card it puts somewhere (the battlefield, the hand, the graveyard) is added as that move runs, so the instructions after it ("untap that land", "you gain life equal to its power") name what it found; a second search replaces what it names, as a second `moveToZone` does; `validateCard` accepts `moved` after a `search`. (2) **`sacrificed`** (`ObjectRef`, `rules/select.ts`, `state/types.ts`, `rules/stack.ts`, `rules/effects.ts`, `rules/may-effects.ts`, `rules/trigger-stack.ts`, `rules/ability-object.ts`): "that creature" for the permanent a `sacrifice` of the same resolution sacrificed (CR 701.21), read in an amount (`powerOf`, `toughnessOf`, `manaValueOf`, `countersOn`) from last-known information (CR 113.7a, 608.2h: it is always gone); the ids of the sacrificed permanents are kept in the resolution (`ResolutionContext.sacrificed`, added to by each `sacrifice` instruction), and a `reflexive` ability carries them to the ability that goes on the stack (`PendingTrigger.sacrificedBefore`, `StackData.sacrificedBefore`, CR 603.12: the reflexive ability is an ability of its own, which knows what the first part did). `validateCard` accepts it after a `sacrifice` (or the `may` of one) in the same sequence and in the `reflexive` ability that follows it (`Scope.sacrificedEarlier`), and refuses it anywhere else; the first permanent sacrificed is the one read. Feature `selector:sacrificed`. (3) **`becomesTarget` with `spellOnly`** (`ast/types.ts`, `rules/triggers.ts`): "becomes the target of a spell" (CR 603.2, 601.2c): the object whose targets were chosen is on the stack as a spell (`stack.kind` `'spell'`, a copy of a spell too), not as an ability; left out it is a spell or an ability as before (Ward). Feature `trigger:becomesTargetSpell`. (4) **Granted abilities for a group need no engine change**: `grantAbility` already gives a mana ability that sacrifices its permanent and an activated ability to every permanent its subject names (layer 6, CR 613.1f), and the mana planner, the legal actions and the activation run them; `scenario-xx-fetch-grants.test.ts` pins them (two abilities on one Treasure, two mana of one color, paid by hand and by the planner, an opponent's Treasure without it, lands that arrive later with it). (5) **AI and web.** No new decision: the reflexive search is a `chooseCards`, the target a `targets`, the sacrifice a `choosePermanent`, all answered already, so the casual agent has no new handler. The web says "the sacrificed creature's power" for the amount (`game/amount-text.ts`, `ui/decisions/ability-label.ts`) and "Whenever this creature becomes the target of a spell" (`game/trigger-text.ts`). `ENGINE_VERSION` is 37.
- Alternatives: Reading the permanent sacrificed through `sacrificedCost`: rejected, that reference is the cost of an activated ability (its scope and its stack data say so), and a reflexive ability has no cost; the new reference keeps the one meaning of each. Making the lowering find the sacrificed permanent by its filter in the reflexive ability ("another creature"): rejected, the permanent is gone and the filter would match others. Counting "that creature" in the reflexive ability by the `thisWay` counts: rejected, they are numbers, not objects. A second trigger kind for "of a spell": rejected, it is the same event with a narrower subject. Resetting `performed` at every `sacrifice` so that "When you do" after a plain sacrifice counts only that sacrifice: rejected for now, it would change what `didPrevious` means in texts that already run; the lowering reads a reflexive ability after a plain instruction only when that instruction is the first of its body, where nothing earlier is counted (D-178). Giving the planner a rule for a Treasure with two abilities: rejected, a source is tapped once, so the abilities of one object are alternatives (`mana/payment.ts`), and the manual payment names the one it wants.
- Consequences: Fetch lands, Fabled Passage's untap, "search, then gain life equal to its power", and the reflexive ability that reads a sacrificed creature (Ziatora's shape) are expressible; "becomes the target of a spell" is; Treasures and lands given abilities by a group are (parser, D-178). The recorded derive digests were recorded again (`UPDATE_DERIVE_DIGESTS=1`): the version is in the state hash, and the new SYNTHETIC cards with static abilities (`synthetic-fetch-grants.ts`) join the pool the soup decks of that test are drawn from, so the games differ too. A search that finds nothing leaves `moved` empty, so "untap that land" does nothing, as it should. Limits, also in `docs/ROADMAP.md`: `sacrificed` is read only in an amount and names the first permanent sacrificed; the ids are not reset by a later `may`; a reflexive ability after a plain instruction counts what the whole resolution did before it (the parser reads it only as the first instruction of a body). Tests: `scenario-xx-fetch-grants.test.ts` (engine, SYNTHETIC cards `synthetic-fetch-grants.ts`; mutation-checked: the `moved` reset of a search, the permanents carried to the reflexive ability, the record of a sacrifice and the spell test of the trigger each make a test fail), `ast-fetch-grants-validate.test.ts`, `ast-supported.test.ts`, `fetch-grants-text.test.ts` (web).

## D-178: The parser reads the Korvold slice 2: a list of basic land types, "When you do" after a sacrifice that is not an offer, "that creature" for the sacrificed permanent, "that land" for what a search found, a line that starts "If ..., instead", "there are seven or more cards in your graveyard", "becomes the target of a spell", and abilities in quotes given to a group (2026-11-02)
- Context: D-177 gave the engine the three pieces the nine cards needed; the rest was the grammar and the lowering. The reading of each card at parser 40 is in D-177. The golden corpus has one of the nine, Fabled Passage (training), which changes from unsupported to supported; Tear Asunder's entry (slice 3) was not touched.
- Decision: (1) **A list of basic land types** (`rules/noun/library.ts`, `noun.library-card`): "a basic Mountain, Forest, or Plains card" is the supertype `basic` once for the whole list, `{ supertypes: ['basic'], anyOf: [{ subtypes: ['Mountain'] }, ...] }`; lists of one kind with commas and "or", at least two, no repeats ("a basic Forest, or Island card" and "a basic Forest or creature card" are not read). (2) **"When you do" after a plain instruction** (`lower/sentences.ts`, `lowerDoneReflexive`): a body whose first sentence is one plain instruction of a kind the engine can tell was done (the kinds an offer may wrap: `sacrifice`, `exile`, `moveToZone`, `draw`, `mill`, ...) and whose second is "When you do, ..." and the last is lowered to the instruction and a `reflexive` ability (shared with the offer's reflexive ability, `lowerReflexive`: targets of its own, the source's damage as "it"); a sentence before the instruction (the engine counts what the whole resolution did) or after the reflexive ability is flagged. (3) **"That creature"** (`lower/effects.ts`, `lower/nouns.ts`, `lower/amounts.ts`, `lower/types.ts`): the lowering context remembers the noun of the last sacrifice of one chosen permanent (`sacrificedRef`); "that creature's power" or "its power" bound to it, in an amount, is `sacrificed`; two creatures sacrificed, or another antecedent, is not. (4) **"Untap that land"** (`rules/effect/index.ts`, `lower/effects-more.ts`, `lower/sentences.ts`, `lower/nouns.ts`): `effect.untap` and `effect.tap` take "that creature", "that land" and the like (`noun.that-object`, D-176); after a search (`LowerContext.searched`, the noun the search looked for) the pronoun is `moved`; any other move, destroy or exile of the text takes it away; "those lands" and "untap two lands" stay unread. (5) **"If ..., instead" on a line of its own** (`sentence.ts`, `parse-face.ts`, `rules/condition/game-state.ts`): a leading "instead" after the test of a sentence says what a trailing one does, that the sentence replaces the one before it (CR 608.2c, 614.1a); the lines of a spell are lowered apart and a replacement needs the instruction before it, so a line of a spell that starts "If ..., instead" or ends "... instead." after a line that ends in a period is read as one text with that line (`joinInsteadLines`; a keyword line before it, "Kicker {2}", is not what it replaces); `condition.amount-count` reads "there are seven or more cards in your graveyard" beside "you have seven or more creature cards in your graveyard". (6) **"Becomes the target of a spell"** (`rules/trigger/index.ts`, `ir/types.ts`, `lower/triggers.ts`): `trigger.becomes-target` reads "of a spell" alone as the engine's `spellOnly` (and "of a spell or ability" as before; "of an ability" alone is not read), and `trigger.or` reads "becomes the target of a spell" as one of its events, so "Whenever ~ attacks or becomes the target of a spell" is an `attacks` and a `becomesTarget` ability with the same body (CR 603.2c). (7) **Abilities in quotes given to a group** (`rules/static/grants.ts`, `lower/statics.ts`, `lower/activated.ts`, `normalize.ts`, `parse-face.ts`, `compile.ts`): the quoted mana or activated ability is lowered for a group subject (`filter`) as it was for `this`, `~` inside the quotes being the permanent that has the ability ("Sacrifice this artifact" is `{ kind: 'sacrifice', what: { kind: 'this' } }`); the normalizer writes the card's own name and "this artifact" alike as `~`, so the face is checked before it is rewritten (`namesItselfInQuotes`): a card that puts its own name inside a quotation is not given a group's ability, the card itself still is. `PARSER_VERSION` is 41; no new rule id (the rules above are extended, each `examples` and `rejects` list with them), and the golden snapshot (`packages/cards/test/fixtures/corpus/golden.expected.json`) changed only in the version and in Fabled Passage (unsupported to supported); training supported is 161 of 192 (83.9%, 160 before), hold-out 51 of 61 (83.6%, unchanged), a gap of 0.2 points (D-066 guideline: about 5).
- Alternatives: A rule for each card's whole text: rejected, every reading above is a phrase of the grammar with its examples and refusals. Lowering the second line of a spell with the first (a spell-parts level replacement): rejected, the targets of the two lines are numbered across the lines and a replacement that declares a target of its own would need the same rules as the sentence form has; joining the text of the two lines gives the existing sentence machinery and its refusals. Joining every "If" line to the line before: rejected, a keyword line is not a sentence and the line stays what it was. Reading `~` in a group's quoted ability always as the permanent: rejected, a card that names itself in a quotation would then give its own name's abilities to the group; the face check keeps that unread. Reading "it" after a search by the binding pass (`bindingVerbs`): rejected, nothing uses it yet and the lowering knows which noun the search looked for.
- Consequences: The nine cards read and pass `validateCard` (parser version 41), their wording, a game of each and the lines near them are tested (below). The engine runs the grants for a group; an Aura's "Enchanted creature has \"{T}: ...\"" is still read and not run (`attached` subject), as before. A text with an ability in quotes for a group of a card that names itself in a quotation, a rider inside the quotes, or a reflexive ability after something that is not the first instruction of the body, stays unread (honest: flagged, never half run). Limits, also in `docs/ROADMAP.md`. Tests: `parser-p36.test.ts` (the nine real cards as the nodes the engine runs, the siblings, the refusals, the face check), `parser-p36-needs.test.ts` (each feature named when missing), `convert-grammar-engine-p36.test.ts` (a game of each shape with SYNTHETIC cards that carry the real wording), the rules' `examples` and `rejects` (`parser-registry.test.ts`) and the updated expectations of `parser-p14`, `parser-p15`, `parser-p3-statics`, `convert-grammar-corpus-p2` and `-p15`, which named lines that are read now.



## D-179: The Korvold slice 4, triggers and small statics, engine: a trigger for a cycled card, the mana value of a spell in a trigger's amount, the colors among permanents, opponents that cannot cast on your turn, lands that enter untapped, a requirement on a group of creatures until your next turn, the permanents a player controls, a card put into a graveyard from the battlefield this turn, and a creature that was attacking as it died (2026-11-02)
- Context: Slice 4 of the owner's Korvold deck is seven cards (`docs/proposals/korvold-deck-analysis.md`): The Balrog of Moria, Kaervek the Merciless, Lavalanche, Lobelia Sackville-Baggins, Spelunking, Kardur, Doomscourge and Conqueror's Flail. Each was run through today's parser and `validateCard` before planning, from the owner's request file with a placeholder power and toughness for the creatures (the file has none), and each line again piece by piece. Per card, what was unread and what the engine lacked: the Balrog stopped at "When you cycle this card" (no trigger for a cycled card: Cycling's cost discarded the card with the same cost as any "discard this card", nothing marked it); Kaervek stopped at "that spell's mana value", and behind it the validator refused the trigger's subject as the object of an amount when the subject is a spell (`checkSubjectRef` wants a permanent), while the interpreter already read the mana value of a spell on the stack; Lavalanche stopped at "or planeswalker", behind it "each creature that player ... controls" needed a filter on the controller of a permanent named by a target (`ObjectFilter` had `controller` relative to the ability and `owner` by reference, for cards); Lobelia stopped at "that was put there from the battlefield this turn" (the turn log had no entry for a card put into a graveyard) and then at "where X is the exiled card's power"; Spelunking stopped at "If you put a Cave onto the battlefield this way" and "Lands you control enter untapped" (a replacement of how a permanent enters existed only for "enters tapped"); Kardur stopped at "until your next turn, creatures your opponents control attack each combat if able and attack a player other than you if able" (`restrict` has one object or a set fixed at resolution and only `untilEndOfTurn`), and, found only when the card was played, its second ability "Whenever an attacking creature dies" read but never ran: the filter `attacking` reads `state.combat.attackers` through the permanents that are still on the battlefield, and a creature that has died is not; Conqueror's Flail stopped at "for each color among permanents you control" (no such amount) and at "As long as ~ is attached to a creature, your opponents can't cast spells during your turn" (a condition on the attachment, and a restriction on casting that is a player's, not a card's: `cantCastThis` is for the card itself). Class corrections: Kaervek, T + P in the analysis, is P with one line in the validator (the interpreter already ran it) and a rule of the grammar; Lavalanche, P, is P (a new filter) plus a T (the target "player or planeswalker"); Kardur, P, hid a second engine gap (a creature that was attacking as it died); the rest stand.
- Decision: (1) **`cycled`** (`ast/types.ts` `Trigger`, `state/events.ts`, `rules/activate-costs.ts`, `rules/derive-keywords.ts`, `rules/triggers.ts`): "When you cycle this card" (CR 702.29c, 702.29f). The cost the engine writes for Cycling and typecycling, `discardThis`, carries `cycling: true` (a card cannot write it, `validateCard`); paying it emits a `cycled` event with the card where it wound up (the graveyard, or exile for a card with madness, CR 702.35a) after the `discarded` event, and the trigger is found on that object, from whatever zone it is in (CR 702.29c), and only on the card that was cycled; a card discarded any other way (cleanup, an effect, a cost that is not a cycling cost) does not trigger it. `validateCard` wants a face with Cycling or typecycling. Features `trigger:cycled`. (2) **The mana value of a spell as the amount of a cast trigger** (`ast/validate-parts.ts`): `manaValueOf` of the `triggerSubject` is accepted when the trigger's subject is a spell or ability on the stack (the other stats stay refused: a spell has none, CR 202.3, 208.1). No interpreter change. (3) **`ObjectFilter.controlledBy`** (`ast/types.ts`, `rules/select.ts`, `rules/filter-match.ts`, `ast/validate-parts.ts`): "each creature that player controls", the permanents the players a selector names control (CR 109.4), read in the `each` selector of an effect like `owner` (which is for cards) and refused anywhere else, and together with `controller`. Feature `selector:controllerRef` (it was named and unsupported before). (4) **`ObjectFilter.putFromBattlefieldThisTurn`** and `TurnLog.graveyarded` (`rules/zones.ts`, `rules/select.ts`, `state/types.ts`): a card put into a graveyard from the battlefield this turn (CR 700.4) by the id it has there, emptied as a turn begins; a token is not a card, a card that moved on is a new object; only a filter of the graveyard, never a static ability. Feature `selector:putFromBattlefieldThisTurn`. (5) **`colorsAmong`** (`StaticPtAmount`, `rules/derive-count.ts`): "+1/+1 for each color among permanents you control", how many of the five colors the permanents a filter names have between them (CR 105.2), read through `typeViewOf` like a count (layers 1, 4 and 5, never layer 7), for a static ability's "+N/+N" only and not for a characteristic-defining ability; a step other than one is not a multiple the engine reads. Feature `amount:colorsAmong`. (6) **`opponentsCantCastOnYourTurn`** (`StaticEffect`, `rules/cast-restrictions.ts`, `rules/legality.ts`) and the condition of a static ability **`objectMatches` of `attached`** (`rules/static-conditions.ts`, `ast/validate-static-condition.ts`): while the permanent has the ability, and its condition holds ("as long as this Equipment is attached to a creature": the permanent it is attached to matches a filter), no opponent of its controller can cast a spell in a turn of that controller, by any means (`canCast` and `canCastDuringResolution`: "can't" beats "can", CR 101.2); abilities, lands and special actions are not spells. (7) **`groupEntersUntapped`** (`Replacement`, `rules/enters-group.ts`, `rules/zones.ts`): "Lands you control enter untapped" (CR 614.1c, 614.12): read from the permanents already on the battlefield as the new one enters, against the permanent as it would be there; the permanent enters untapped whatever else would have it enter tapped (its own "enters tapped", an effect that puts it onto the battlefield tapped), and a land that would ask whether to pay life to avoid entering tapped is not asked. CR 616.1 lets the controller of the permanent choose the order when two replacement effects apply; the engine does not ask (D-156) and takes the order the controller would choose, untapped (the official rulings, on Scryfall, are not reachable from the sandbox, so the card's rulings were not read: `docs/ROADMAP.md`). The effect does nothing for a token and not for the permanent with the ability itself. (8) **`requireAttack`** (`Effect`, `ContinuousChange`, `rules/continuous.ts`, `rules/combat-legality.ts`, `rules/flow.ts`): "until your next turn, creatures your opponents control attack each combat if able and attack a player other than you if able" and "creatures your opponents control attack this turn if able" (CR 508.1d, 611.2a, 611.2c): one continuous effect with no set of objects (a requirement changes the rules and no characteristic, so it reaches creatures that arrive after it began), read whenever attackers are declared for the creatures its filter matches then, with `controller` as "you"; `EffectEnd` has `turnStart` ("until your next turn": the effect waits for the next turn of its controller, not this one even if it is theirs, and ends as that turn begins in `startTurn`). `awayFromYou`: a creature under it that could attack a player other than the controller attacks one (only those players are left among its attack targets; planeswalkers and battles are not players); with two players none exists and the creatures are only required to attack, which is what the CR says (508.1d: as many requirements as possible). Features `effect:requireAttack`, `duration:untilYourNextTurn`. (9) **A creature that was attacking as it died** (`rules/select.ts`): `attackingCreatures` and `attackersOfPlayer` list the creatures of the combat record whether or not they are still on the battlefield, so that a trigger that looks back in time (CR 603.10a: "Whenever an attacking creature dies") finds, in the last-known information of the creature, that it was attacking (CR 506.4); a filter matches an object on the battlefield or its last-known information, never an object in another zone, so nothing else changes. (10) **AI and web.** No new decision: the casual agent and the heuristic agent have no new handler; the attack requirement reaches them through `mustAttack`, and the narrowed targets through the candidates' target lists, as an `attacksEachCombat` creature did. The web says "When you cycle this card" (`game/trigger-text.ts`), "for each color among permanents you control" (`game/pt-text.ts`), "Lands you control enter untapped" (`game/static-text.ts`), "Your opponents can't cast spells during your turn as long as this permanent is attached to a creature" (`game/angels-text.ts`, `game/condition-text.ts`), "Until your next turn, creatures your opponents control attack each combat if able and ..." (`game/korvold-text.ts`) and a "cycles" line in the log (`game/describe.ts`). `ENGINE_VERSION` is 38.
- Alternatives: A trigger kind for "cycle or discard" with a flag: rejected, the CR makes them different events (702.29d) and only the first is needed. Finding the cycled card's trigger by marking the ability `functionsIn: 'graveyard'`: rejected, a card with a dies trigger and a cycled trigger would then have the first work from the graveyard too. Reading the cycled trigger from the `discarded` event: rejected, that event carries the id the card had in the hand, which no longer exists. `controller: { selector }` in place of a new field: rejected, `controller` is read everywhere a filter is, relative to the ability, and a selector that needs a target is read in one place only, as `owner` is. A `restrict` with a new duration for Kardur: rejected, it names a set fixed at resolution, which is wrong for a requirement (CR 611.2c) and for "creatures your opponents control" that arrive later; the dynamic effect has its own node. Applying the new requirement to the old `restrict` ("creatures your opponents control attack this turn if able" of `effect.restrict-all`): not done here, it keeps its fixed set (`docs/ROADMAP.md`). Marking Spelunking's land as untapped by asking the order of the two replacement effects: rejected, the engine asks no order today (D-156) and the player's own best choice is untapped. Counting the colors with `countOf` and a filter per color: rejected, a static ability's amount would then be a sum of five counts that overlap. Making the opponents' casting restriction a flag of the player: rejected, it ends with the permanent's abilities, so it is read from the permanents each time a spell is cast.
- Consequences: A cycled card's trigger, "that spell's mana value", damage to a player and the permanents that player controls, a card put into a graveyard from the battlefield this turn, a count of colors, a restriction on casting that depends on an attachment, lands that enter untapped, and a requirement on the creatures of the opponents that lasts to the next turn are expressible; a creature's trigger "whenever an attacking creature dies" runs. The recorded derive digests were recorded again (`UPDATE_DERIVE_DIGESTS=1`): the version is in the state hash and the new SYNTHETIC cards join the pool the soup decks are drawn from. The cycling test of the derived abilities names the marked cost. Limits, also in `docs/ROADMAP.md`: `cycled` is "this card" only; Spelunking's order against another replacement effect is the controller's best choice, not asked, and a token land is not covered; `colorsAmong` is for a step of one; `requireAttack` has no "this turn" use (the older `restrict` keeps it) and reads the filter as it is when attackers are declared; `awayFromYou` narrows the targets of a creature only when it could attack a player other than the controller, which needs three players (tested on a state with a third seat, the scenario builder has two); `opponentsCantCastOnYourTurn` has no "spells with ..." variant. Tests: `scenario-xx-korvold-triggers.test.ts` (engine, SYNTHETIC cards `synthetic-korvold-triggers.ts`), `ast-korvold-triggers-validate.test.ts`, `ast-supported.test.ts`, `ast-features.test.ts`, `scenario-xx-cycling.test.ts` (the marked cost), `korvold-triggers-text.test.ts` (web), `trigger-text.test.ts`.


## D-180: The parser reads the Korvold slice 4: "When you cycle this card", "that spell's mana value", "target player or planeswalker", "each creature that player controls", "that was put there from the battlefield this turn", "the exiled card's power", "If you put a Cave onto the battlefield this way", "Lands you control enter untapped", "until your next turn, creatures your opponents control attack each combat if able ...", "for each color among permanents you control" and "Your opponents can't cast spells during your turn" (2026-11-02)
- Context: D-179 gave the engine the pieces the seven cards needed; the rest was the grammar and the lowering. The reading of each card at parser 41 is in D-179. The golden corpus has none of the seven (the acceptance names are for the owner's extraction).
- Decision: Stage P37, one rule or two for each reading, each with `examples` and `rejects`. (1) **`trigger.cycled`** (`rules/trigger/korvold.ts`): "you cycle this card" and "you cycle ~" (the card with the ability; "a card", "another card", "or discard" are other events and are not read); lowered to `cycled` for `you` and the card itself. (2) **"That spell's mana value"** (`rules/amount/index.ts` `amount.mana-value-of`, `lower/amounts.ts`): read as the object whose event caused the trigger (`triggerSubject`), beside a target; a mana value of `~` stays unread. (3) **`noun.player-or-planeswalker`** (`rules/noun/korvold.ts`): "target player or planeswalker" and "target opponent or planeswalker", the recipient of damage only, read as the target player (`player: any` or `opponent`), with `orPlaneswalker` kept in the filter. The engine has no planeswalker permanents to target (loyalty abilities are not run and no real planeswalker is supported, `docs/ROADMAP.md`), so a player is the only legal target there is; this is the honest reading only while that is true, and a planeswalker card that is played with its text dropped can be on the battlefield and cannot be the target (`docs/ROADMAP.md`). (4) **`noun.each-permanent-of-player`** (`rules/noun/korvold.ts`, `lower/nouns.ts`): "each creature that player controls" and "each creature that player or that planeswalker's controller controls", the kind of permanent a phrase of the permanent family names and the player "that player", which the binding pass makes the target before it (`filter.controller = { noun }`, the IR hook that the lowering refused as `selector:controllerRef` until now); lowered to an `each` selector with `controlledBy` the target; with no player before it the reference is unbound and the line is flagged ("target creature or planeswalker and each creature that player controls"). (5) **"That was put there from the battlefield this turn"** (`rules/noun/phrases.ts` `graveyardPhrase`, `lower/nouns.ts`): the suffix after the owner of a graveyard phrase (`putFromBattlefieldThisTurn`); and **"where X is the exiled card's power"** (`rules/amount/value.ts`): "the exiled card's" is "that card" to the binding pass, so it is the target the instruction before it exiled, read from last-known information (CR 400.7j, 608.2h). (6) **`condition.put-this-way`** (`rules/condition/korvold.ts`, `sentence.ts`): "you put a Cave onto the battlefield this way" at the start of a sentence, any description of what an object is (a land type, a card type, modifiers); lowered to `objectMatches` of `moved`, which `validateCard` allows only after an instruction that moves a card; "you may put ..." with no instruction before it that the engine can tell was done is read and refused (`notRunnable`). (7) **`static.group-enters-untapped`** (`rules/static/korvold.ts`, `lower/korvold.ts`): "Lands you control enter untapped." for a plural group of the controller's own, lowered to `groupEntersUntapped`; a permanent that would be one of the group (a land with it) is read and refused, since the engine reads the effect from the permanents already there and CR 614.12 would apply it to itself. (8) **`static.opponents-cant-cast`** and its unit (`rules/static/korvold.ts`, `rules/static/conditional.ts`): "Your opponents can't cast spells during your turn." alone and as the statement of "As long as ~ is attached to a creature, ..." (prefix or suffix), with **`condition.attached-to`** (`rules/condition/self-state.ts`): "~ is attached to a creature" (a creature host only), lowered to `objectMatches` of `attached`. (9) **`effect.require-attack`** (`rules/effect/korvold.ts`, `lower/korvold.ts`): "until your next turn, creatures your opponents control attack each combat if able [and attack a player other than you if able]" for "creatures" and a controller (`you` or `opponent`), lowered to `requireAttack` with `untilYourNextTurn`; "this turn" is the older `effect.restrict-all`. (10) **`amount.for-each-color`** (`rules/amount/korvold.ts`, `rules/static/pt-count.ts`, `lower/amounts.ts`): "for each color among permanents you control" (any plural group of the controller's own permanents) as the count of a static "+N/+N", lowered to `colorsAmong`; a step other than one is read and refused. `PARSER_VERSION` is 42; the golden snapshot changed only in the version and in the diagnostic of one unsupported card (its closest rule); training supported is 161 of 192 (83.9%, unchanged), hold-out 51 of 61 (83.6%, unchanged), a gap of 0.2 points (D-066 guideline: about 5).
- Alternatives: A rule for each card's whole text: rejected, every reading above is a phrase of the grammar with its examples and refusals. Reading "target player or planeswalker" for every verb: rejected, "draws a card" of a planeswalker means nothing; it is an operand of damage only. A planeswalker target as a second target kind in the engine: rejected, `TargetSpec` has no union of a player and an object, and no planeswalker permanent can be played with its text. Reading "each creature they control" with "they" like "that player": left unread, no card of the slice needs it. Making "the exiled card's power" read the card the move produced (`moved`) instead of the target: the engine reads a target that has left from its last-known information (CR 608.2h), which is the same number, and the binding pass needs no new case. Reading "As long as ~ is attached to a creature" for any host: rejected, the engine's condition takes a filter and the card says a creature; other hosts would be new text.
- Consequences: The seven cards read and pass `validateCard` (parser version 42), their wording, a game of each and the lines near them are tested (below). Lines that read now and did not: "Counter target spell. You lose life equal to that spell's mana value", the modal line whose first mode is "~ deals 4 damage to target player or planeswalker" (the replay line of the corpus of stage P19), "Enchanted creature gets +1/+1 for each color among permanents you control"; the tests that listed them as unread changed (`convert-grammar-corpus*.test.ts`, `parser-p11`, `parser-p20`, `parser-p3-statics`). The closest rule of a few lines that stay unread shifted to `noun.each-permanent` (`parser-p13`, `convert-grammar-corpus`), since the new noun rule fails at the same place. Limits, also in `docs/ROADMAP.md`: see D-179. Tests: `parser-p37.test.ts` (the seven real cards as the nodes the engine runs, the siblings, the refusals), `parser-p37-needs.test.ts` (each feature named when missing), `convert-grammar-engine-p37.test.ts` (a game of each shape with SYNTHETIC cards that carry the real wording), the rules' `examples` and `rejects` (`parser-registry.test.ts`) and `convert-parser.test.ts` (the ids).

## D-181: The Korvold slice 3, casting and targets, engine: a target chosen only if the spell was kicked or only if it was not, an additional cost paid in one of two ways, a spell's own cost reduction with a condition, and the change of the target of a spell or ability with a single target (2026-11-02)
- Context: Slice 3 of the owner's Korvold deck is three cards (`docs/proposals/korvold-deck-analysis.md`): Tear Asunder, Stir Up Trouble and Bolt Bend. Each was run through today's parser and `validateCard` before planning, from the owner's request file, and each line again piece by piece. Tear Asunder was read completely and refused by the validator ("target is chosen only if the spell was kicked", CR 702.33g: the engine asked every declared target, so it would have demanded a second target the card does not need); Stir Up Trouble stopped at "or pay {4}" (the face's `additionalCosts` are all paid, there is no choice between costs); Bolt Bend stopped at "if you control a creature with power 4 or greater" (a `costReduction` of the spell itself had no condition) and at "Change the target of ..." (no effect and no decision for the target of a stack object). Class corrections: none of the three is a keyword or a subsystem; all stay P (a primitive with its tests), and the "two new dialogs" of the analysis came out as one new purpose of the existing optional question (the cost choice) and a flag on the existing targets question (the new target), so no new dialog was built and no Playwright test added. The slice did not need the approval gate of S: it reuses the cast transaction, the `confirmOptional` and `targets` decisions and the instruction queue of a resolution (as D-089 and D-129 did).
- Decision: (1) **`TargetSpec.ifKicked` and `unlessKicked`** (`ast/types.ts`, `rules/legality.ts` `targetSpecsOf`, `rules/cast.ts` `toKicker`, `ast/validate-cast.ts`, `ast/validate.ts`): "If this spell was kicked, exile target nonland permanent instead" has a slot that exists only if the spell was kicked, and the slot of the sentence it replaces exists only if it was not (CR 702.33g, 601.2c: "a spell may require alternative targets only if an alternative or additional cost was chosen for it"). `targetSpecsOf` takes the kicked fact (the spell on the stack says; a card not cast yet is asked both ways). The kicker question is asked as before, except for a face with such slots: the unkicked way needs its slots to have legal targets and its total cost payable, the kicked way its own, and the spell is cast the way that is possible without asking (kicked or not), asked only when both are (`canCast`, `canCastDuringResolution` and `toKicker` agree; the legal list offers the cast when one way can be cast). `validateCard` wants a slot used only in the matching branch of a `kicked` conditional (`kickedTargetsUsedOutsideTheirCase`, a `not` turns the branches round, any other condition says nothing sure about the kicker), a face with Kicker (not Multikicker, whose count the engine asks elsewhere), no modes, and a spell's own text (an ability chooses its targets as it triggers, whatever its condition says); the old refusal stays for a slot used in one case that is not declared so. Feature `ability:ifKicked`. (2) **`CardFace.additionalCostChoice`** (`cards/definition.ts`, `rules/cast.ts` `toCostChoice` and `answerCostChoice`, `rules/cast-cost.ts` `canPayRequest`, `state/decisions.ts`, `ast/validate-cost.ts`): "As an additional cost to cast this spell, sacrifice an artifact or creature or pay {4}": two ways, each a list of the costs `additionalCosts` takes, paid with the face's own additional costs (CR 118.8, 601.2b: announced with the other additional costs, so after the kicker, the replicate count and the gift and before X and the targets). A way that cannot be paid with the choices already made is not offered, nothing is asked when only one can be (`StackData.costOption` keeps it either way). The question is a `confirmOptional` of purpose `costChoice` (accept is the first way, decline the second; `cost` and `otherCost` say them; cancel rewinds the cast, CR 733). Every place that asked "can this be paid" for a spell not yet cast asks `canPayRequest`, which is true when either way can be paid; `spellCost` reads the chosen way from the request or the spell on the stack. The view of the card lists both ways (`ObjectView.additionalCostChoice`). No "pay X life" and no {X} in a way, the two ways differ, and a face has one choice. Feature `ability:additionalCostChoice`. (3) **A conditional `costReduction` of `this`** (`ast/validate-static-condition.ts`, `rules/cast-cost.ts` `reductionFor`): "This spell costs {3} less to cast if you control a creature with power 4 or greater" is the spell's own reduction with a `condition`, evaluated when the total cost is determined (CR 601.2f) for the caster with `evaluateCondition`, so it may compare a power (a static ability read by `derive` may not, CR 613.8: this one is not read there); a reduction of other spells (a permanent's) takes no condition. The cost the view shows is the reduced one. Feature `ability:selfCostReducedIf`. (4) **`changeTarget`** (`ast/types.ts` `Effect`, `ObjectFilter.singleTarget`, `rules/change-source.ts`, `rules/change-target.ts`, `rules/change-target-answer.ts`, `rules/effects.ts`, `rules/stack.ts`, `rules/filter-match.ts`, `state/events.ts` `targetChanged`, `state/decisions.ts` `forChange`): "Change the target of target spell or ability with a single target". The slot is a stack object whose filter says `singleTarget` (CR 115.9a: put on the stack with exactly one target, one chosen twice counting twice; `validateCard` wants it, because the engine changes the one target and never several: CR 115.7a would change all or none). As it resolves, the target of the object, if it is still on the stack with a single target (CR 608.2b), is changed to another legal target for its slot: the slot of the spell or ability read as it is now, for the controller of the spell or ability with it as the source, so hexproof, shroud and the slot's own words count (CR 115.7a), and the current target is not an alternative. With no other legal target nothing changes and nothing is reported, even if the target is illegal by now (CR 115.7a); with one it is taken; with several the controller of the effect is asked a `targets` decision with `forChange` (`subject`, `current`, one slot, no cancel; the answer goes on with the resolution, `answerChangedTarget`). A divided spell keeps its division (CR 115.7f: the new target takes the share). The new target becomes a target: `targetChanged` and `becameTarget` (Ward and the like trigger, CR 603.2c). The interpreter makes the instruction and the stack runs it, as for `copySpell` (the interpreter cannot import the legality code: `change-source.ts` is the light half). Features `effect:changeTarget` and `selector:singleTarget`. (5) The scenario DSL: `cast(card, { additionalCost })` and the handle's `additionalCost(first)`.
- Alternatives: Marking the kicked-only slot by reading the effect (the old `kickerOnlyTargets` alone, so that a card needs no flag): rejected, a flag that the card's author writes is checked against the effect (a slot used in the wrong branch is refused), whereas an inferred one silently changes the targets a card asks. A single flag `ifKicked` with the unkicked slot always asked: rejected, Tear Asunder would then ask a target artifact or enchantment that a kicked cast does not have (CR 601.2c names "alternative targets"). Asking the kicker question first and letting the cast fail when its targets are missing: rejected, the engine never offers what it would then refuse (as for the kicked total of D-110). A new decision kind for the cost choice: rejected, `confirmOptional` already has the purposes of the casting transaction (kicker, gift), the dialog, the legal actions, the AI handler and the cancel are the same; a third or fourth way would need a new kind, no card has one. A `Cost` kind `oneOf` inside `additionalCosts`: rejected, `Cost` is the type of every activated ability's cost and each switch over it would have to say what a choice means there. Evaluating the choice at payment (after the mana): rejected, the total cost is locked in at 601.2f, so the way must be known before it. Putting the condition of the cost reduction in the amount (a count that is 0 or 3): rejected, a condition over a power has no count. Making `changeTarget` change any number of targets (CR 115.7a "all or none", 115.7b one of them, 115.7c any): rejected, no card of the deck needs it and it needs a choice of which; the validator refuses a slot that could name a spell with several targets. Reusing `forCopy` for the new target: rejected, a copy keeps targets that are illegal and may leave all of them, a change takes exactly one new legal target. Redirecting to a planeswalker: not claimed, the engine has no planeswalker permanents to target (`docs/ROADMAP.md`), so "another legal target" is any object or player the slot allows.
- Consequences: Tear Asunder, Stir Up Trouble and Bolt Bend are expressible and run (parser D-182); the "kicked-only target" refusal of the engine is lifted for the shape that has a flag, and a card with the target in a modal spell, with Multikicker or in an ability stays refused (flagged, never half run). The recorded derive digests were recorded again (`UPDATE_DERIVE_DIGESTS=1`): the version is in the state hash and the new SYNTHETIC cards join the pool the soup decks are drawn from. `ENGINE_VERSION` 39. Limits, also in `docs/ROADMAP.md`: the slots that depend on the kicker are for Kicker, not Multikicker, and not in a modal spell; `additionalCostChoice` has two ways of costs the existing additional costs take (no X, no tapping, no exile) and one per face; a spell with the choice and an alternative cost (Overload, Escape) asks it too (CR 118.9d, additional costs still apply); `changeTarget` is for a spell or ability with a single target and the controller of the effect picks among the targets (CR 115.7a); the AI's choice is a heuristic (mana before a card or life before a permanent; a harmful spell to the opponent's side). Tests: `scenario-xx-casting-targets.test.ts` (engine, SYNTHETIC cards `synthetic-casting-targets.ts`; mutation-checked: a kicked slot or an unkicked slot always asked fails 7 and 4 tests, the forced kick dropped 1, the chosen way ignored 7, the cost choice always asked 2, the reduction's condition ignored 3, the current target kept as an alternative 5, the division dropped 1, "single target" not checked 1), `ast-casting-targets-validate.test.ts`, `ast-kicker-validate.test.ts`, `casual-casting-targets.test.ts` (AI), `casting-targets-text.test.ts` (web).

## D-182: The parser reads the Korvold slice 3: a target only a kicked spell has, "A or B" additional costs, "costs {3} less to cast if you control ..." and "Change the target of target spell or ability with a single target" (2026-11-02)
- Context: D-181 gave the engine the pieces the three cards needed; the rest was the grammar and the lowering. The reading of each card at parser 42 is in D-181. Tear Asunder was in the golden corpus (a hold-out card, unsupported) and changes status; Stir Up Trouble and Bolt Bend are in the owner's acceptance names (`docs/proposals/korvold-acceptance-names.txt`) and not in the corpus yet.
- Decision: Stage P38. (1) **The slots of a kicked sentence** (`lower/sentences.ts` `markKickedTargets`): the targets a spell's "If this spell was kicked, ..." sentence declares are `ifKicked`; with "... instead" the targets of the sentence it replaces that the replacement does not name again are `unlessKicked` (a replacement that names the target again, "deals 4 damage to it instead", keeps it for both ways, so a card of the usual shape has no flag). Only a spell's own text (`ctx.owner === 'spell'`): an ability's targets are chosen as it triggers, so none is marked. A `Step` records the slots its sentence declared. The need `ability:ifKicked` is named. (2) **`static.additional-cost`** (`rules/static/cost.ts`, `lower/spell-costs.ts`, `parse-face.ts`, `convert/face.ts`): after the costs, " or " and one more cost: "sacrifice an artifact or creature or pay {4}", "pay 5 life or pay {2}", "sacrifice a creature or discard a card"; the first way is one cost (a way of several costs, a third way, "pay X life" and a choice of two sacrifices are not read), lowered to the face's `additionalCostChoice` (the IR `additionalCost` has `orCosts`); a face with two such lines drops the second (`notRunnable`). The need `ability:additionalCostChoice` and the cost kinds are named. (3) **`static.self-cost-reduction`**: " if " and a condition of what the controller has (`condition.control-a`, `control-at-least`, `control-at-most`, `control-none`, `control-commander`, `control-your-commander`), also after "for each ..."; lowered (`lower/statics.ts`) to the `costReduction` of `this` with `condition`, the need `ability:selfCostReducedIf` named; a condition about another player's permanents and a reduction of other spells with a condition are not read. (4) **`effect.change-target`** (`rules/effect/change-target.ts`, `lower/change-target.ts`): "Change the target of target spell or ability with a single target", "... target spell with a single target" and "... target activated or triggered ability with a single target": a target of the stack (`ObjectFilter.singleTarget`, the IR filter's `singleTarget`, the need `selector:singleTarget`) and the effect `changeTarget` (need `effect:changeTarget`); "Change a target", "the targets", a spell with no such words ("Change the target of target spell"), a spell with a quality and a new target named ("to ~") are not read. The rule registry has 'effect.change-target' after 'effect.copy-spell'.
- Alternatives: Reading "A or B" for any pair of cost lists: rejected, "sacrifice a creature and discard a card or pay {2}" has no clear grouping in English and no card in the deck says it. Reading "if" of the reduction for every condition of the condition family: rejected, the engine reads the controller's own permanents and commander as the cost is determined; the others are phrases of other statics. Marking the replaced sentence's target `unlessKicked` always: rejected, a replacement that names it again ("it") uses it in both ways.
- Consequences: The three cards read and pass `validateCard` (parser version 43). Lines that read now and did not: the third bullet of the "choose one" with "Change the target of target spell or ability with a single target" (the replay line of the corpus of stage P19 stops at the next bullet now), "pay 5 life or pay {2}", "sacrifice an artifact or discard a card", "~ costs {3} less to cast if you control a creature with power 4 or greater" and "If ~ was kicked, destroy target creature." (the tests that listed them as unread changed: `convert-grammar-corpus-p4`, `-p13`, `-p19`, `parser-p4`, `-p13`, `-p19`, `convert-parser` for the rule ids and the new field of the face). The golden corpus: Tear Asunder (hold-out) is supported now, hold-out 52 of 61 (51 before), training 161 of 192 unchanged; the card's reasons and AST hash are in `golden.expected.json`. Limits: see D-181 and `docs/ROADMAP.md`. Tests: `parser-p38.test.ts` (the three real cards as the nodes the engine runs, the siblings, the refusals), `parser-p38-needs.test.ts` (each feature named when missing), `convert-grammar-engine-p38.test.ts` (a game of each shape with SYNTHETIC cards that carry the real wording), the rules' `examples` and `rejects` (`parser-registry.test.ts`).

## D-183: The Korvold slice 5, mana spent to cast a spell, engine: the mana spent is recorded as the cost is paid, with the card types of the sources that made it, and read by "the amount of mana spent to cast it" and by an "enters with a counter" replacement (2026-11-02)
- Context: Slice 5 of the owner's Korvold deck is two cards (`docs/proposals/korvold-deck-analysis.md`): Prossh, Skyraider of Kher and Coin of Mastery. Each was run through today's parser and `validateCard` before planning, from the owner's request file, and each line again piece by piece. Prossh stopped at "When you cast ~," (no rule read the cast trigger of the spell itself, though the engine has had `castSpell` with `self` since D-120), then at "named Kobolds of Kher Keep" and at "the amount of mana spent to cast it"; Coin of Mastery stopped at "for each mana from an artifact source spent to cast it" after a static that the grammar already read for "each other Angel". Class corrections: the analysis called the slice P and P + T, and the engine part is a P with one real piece, not an S: the engine already knew the mana pool objects with their source (`ManaObject.source`), the planner already chose which pool mana and which sources paid, and a spell already kept facts about its casting on its stack data (`kicks`, `giftTo`, `hasteUntilEnd`, D-151). What it lacked was a record of which mana paid the cost, so "tracking mana spent by colour/source through payment" turned out to be one field on the mana, one list in the plan and one field on the spell, not a subsystem; no approval gate, no proposal, no new dialog (so no Playwright test) and no new decision for the agents. The card rulings could not be read (Scryfall is not reachable from the sandbox); the behaviour below rests on the CR text (601.2h: the total cost is paid with mana; 106.1: mana is spent to pay costs; 202.1a; 107.4h for the same idea about a snow source) and on how the two cards read, and the points that depend on a ruling are listed under Limits.
- Decision: (1) **`ManaObject.sourceTypes`** (`mana/types.ts`): the card types of the permanent that made the mana, written when it is made (a mana ability by hand, `rules/mana-engine.ts`; mana a planned payment produced and the cost did not use, `mana/payment.ts`; mana an effect adds, `rules/effects.ts`, from the source as it is or as it last was, CR 113.7a), because a Treasure is sacrificed to make its mana and the permanent is gone when the mana is spent; the planner's `PaymentSource.types` is the same list for a source that has not been tapped yet (`rules/mana-sources.ts`). Absent when unknown (mana a test adds). (2) **`PaymentPlan.spentTypes`** (`mana/payment.ts`): one entry for each mana the plan spends on the cost itself, with the types of its source. The search now tells the mana that pays the activation cost of a costed mana ability (`{1}, {T}: Add {U}{B}`, CR 605.3a) from the mana that pays the cost of the spell (`actMask` next to `usedMask`: a demand dimension from `ACT_BASE` on is an activation cost), so a Signet's own {1} is not mana spent on the spell. Life paid for Phyrexian mana, mana left over and what Convoke, Improvise or Delve pays instead of mana are not listed. `applyPaymentPlan` and `payByTapping` return it as `spent`. (3) **`StackData.manaSpent`** (`state/types.ts`, `ManaSpent`): `{ total, fromTypes }`, written by `rules/cast.ts` `withManaSpent` as the payment is made, by the automatic payment and by the payment by hand alike (CR 601.2h; a source with two types counts for each). Absent for a spell cast for no mana (cast without paying its mana cost, a cost of {0}), for a copy of a spell (CR 707.10: a copy is not cast; the copy is built field by field and never takes it) and for an ability. (4) **The `Amount` `manaSpent { fromType? }`** (`ast/types.ts`, `rules/amounts.ts`, `rules/mana-spent.ts`): "the amount of mana spent to cast it", all of it or, with `fromType`, from sources of that card type. In the effect of "When you cast this spell" (`castSpell` with `self`) the spell is the source and the amount reads it from the spell on the stack or from its last-known information once it has left (CR 113.7a: a spell countered in response to its own trigger still gives the number its trigger counts); `validateCard` refuses it in any other effect (`scope.selfCast`) and a `fromType` that is not a card type. (5) **`othersEnterWithCounters.count` may be `manaSpent`** (`ast/types.ts` `ManaSpentAmount`, `rules/enters-group.ts`, `ast/validate-angels.ts`): "Each creature you control enters with an additional +1/+1 counter on it for each mana from an artifact source spent to cast it" reads the spell the entering permanent came from (`entering` is the spell object as it enters, so its stack data is there); a permanent that was not cast, a token, a copy that becomes a token and a card put onto the battlefield by an effect have 0, and so does one cast without paying its mana cost. Features `amount:manaSpent` (listed in `ast/features.ts`). (6) The tests that built a plan by hand were changed for the new field (`spentTypes`), and the scenario DSL needed nothing.
- Alternatives: Keeping a list of the mana objects spent on the spell (with colour, source id and restriction): rejected, both cards need a count and a count by card type, the engine reads nothing else of the mana a spell was paid with, and a list per spell would be copied with every state. Reading the types of the source from the game at payment time only: rejected, mana by hand goes through the pool and its Treasure is already gone when it is spent. Storing a flag "from an artifact" instead of the types: rejected, a second card that counts mana from creatures or lands would need the engine changed again, and the types are the same fact. Counting every mana the plan used, activation costs included: rejected, "mana spent to cast it" would then be wrong for the Signet-style sources the planner already supports. Keeping the count on the permanent as `kicks` is kept (the analysis said so): rejected for now, no card of the deck reads "mana spent" from the permanent after it entered (the counter is read as it enters, from the spell); a later "when this enters, if at least {R}{R} was spent" would add it. Reading `manaSpent` in any spell's effect (a sorcery's "draw cards equal to the mana spent to cast it"): not built, no card of the deck needs it and the source of a resolving spell has other rules (X, copies); the validator refuses it there so it is flagged, never half run. Making `othersEnterWithCounters.count` any `Amount`: rejected, it is read while a replacement effect applies and the other amounts read the resolving object.
- Consequences: Prossh and Coin of Mastery are expressible and run (parser D-184). `ENGINE_VERSION` 40. The recorded derive digests were recorded again (`UPDATE_DERIVE_DIGESTS=1`): the version is in the state hash and the new SYNTHETIC cards join the pool the soup decks are drawn from. Limits, also in `docs/ROADMAP.md`: the amount is read in the cast trigger of the spell itself and in the enters-with count only; an amount for a mana that an effect added carries the types of the source as it is when the effect resolves; the mana a trigger adds to a mana ability (D-139) takes the types of the permanent that made the mana, as the ability does; mana a spell added by its own effect (Dark Ritual) counts for the source as a spell, with its own card types; rulings could not be read, so these points are from the CR and the card text, not from a ruling: that mana paid for additional costs and cost increases (commander tax, kicker) is mana spent to cast the spell (the whole total cost is, CR 601.2h), that a mana from a Treasure is mana from an artifact source (it is an artifact, CR 111.10a, 205.3g), and that a spell cast without paying its mana cost has spent none. Tests: `scenario-xx-mana-spent.test.ts` (engine, SYNTHETIC cards `synthetic-mana-spent.ts`: six lands, unused sources, the pool, a Treasure, commander tax, a cost reduction, a counter in response, Sol Ring, lands only, a Treasure made earlier and tapped by hand, a cascaded creature, all the mana, two effects together), `mana-payment.test.ts` (the planner: the types of each mana spent, left over, pool mana, Phyrexian life, the activation cost of a costed ability), `ast-mana-spent-validate.test.ts`.

## D-184: The parser reads the Korvold slice 5: "When you cast this spell", a token "named ...", "the amount of mana spent to cast it" and "for each mana from an artifact source spent to cast it" (2026-11-02)
- Context: D-183 gave the engine the amount; the rest was the grammar and the lowering. The reading of each card at parser 43 is in D-183: neither card was in the golden corpus (both are acceptance names of the owner's `docs/proposals/korvold-acceptance-names.txt`, for the owner's `pnpm corpus:extract`).
- Decision: Stage P39. (1) **`trigger.cast-self`** (`rules/trigger/korvold.ts`, `lower/triggers.ts`): "you cast this spell" and "you cast ~" (CR 601.2i, 603.2), the event `castSelf`, lowered to the engine's `castSpell` with `self`, `by: 'you'` and the filter `{ stackKind: 'spell' }`; the spell is the one with the ability (the subject is `~`, so "it" in the body is the spell), and only "this spell" is read, not "a spell" or a description of one (`trigger.cast` is the other rule). The lowering sets `LowerContext.selfCast` in the body of such an ability. The need is the existing `trigger:castSpell`. (2) **A named token** (`rules/token/index.ts`, `lower/effects.ts`): "X 0/1 red Kobold creature tokens named Kobolds of Kher Keep", before any "with ..." (CR 111.4: the effect sets the name and the subtypes); the name is capitalized words that "of", "the" and the like may join, up to the comma, the period or the "with"; `IrToken.named` becomes the token definition's `name` (it was the creature types). (3) **`amount.for-each-mana-spent`** and the atom "the amount of mana spent to cast it" (`rules/amount/mana-spent.ts`, `rules/amount/value.ts`, `rules/amount/kicked.ts` for the `for each` list): "for each mana spent to cast it", "for each mana from an artifact source spent to cast it" (the five card types a permanent can have as a source: artifact, creature, enchantment, land, planeswalker) and "where X is / equal to the amount of mana spent to cast it", the IR `manaSpent` with `fromType` and `who` (`it` or `~`); the lowering (`lower/amounts.ts`) reads it only in the body of "When you cast this spell" (`selfCast`) and, for `it`, only when the ability is about the source itself; the need is `amount:manaSpent`. (4) **`static.others-enter-with-counters`** (`rules/static/angels-play.ts`, `lower/angels.ts`) takes the new "for each" amount (with `it`, the creature that enters; `~` would be the permanent with the ability, which is not read) and lowers it to the replacement's `count` (needs `amount:manaSpent` and `replacement:othersEnterWithCounters`). The rule registry has `trigger.cast-self` after `trigger.cycled` and `amount.for-each-mana-spent` after `amount.for-each-still-exiled`.
- Alternatives: Reading "When you cast ~" in `trigger.cast`: rejected, that rule describes a spell by a filter and its `rejects` list has "you cast ~" on purpose; the spell itself is another event with its own engine shape. Lowering the amount for any ability and leaving the refusal to `validateCard`: rejected, a line the engine will refuse should be reported as not runnable at the lowering with the reason, and the validator stays as a second check. Naming a token by a capitalized word only: rejected, "Kobolds of Kher Keep" has lower-case small words.
- Consequences: Both cards read and pass `validateCard` (parser version 44), and `parser-p39.test.ts` holds their real wording as the nodes the engine runs. Lines that read now and did not: the cast trigger of a spell itself, a "named" token, and the two amounts; the tests that listed the rules changed (`convert-parser.test.ts`, `parser-registry.test.ts`). The golden corpus: neither card is in it, but a training card changes status, found only by reading the diff of `golden.expected.json`: Sowing Mycospawn ("When you cast this spell, search your library for a land card, put it onto the battlefield, then shuffle." and "When you cast this spell, if it was kicked, exile target land.") is supported now, because `trigger.cast-self` reads both of its cast triggers; they run with the engine's existing `castSpell` trigger with `self` (a search, and a target land chosen as the trigger goes on the stack with the intervening "if" checked as it triggers, CR 603.4), and `convert-grammar-engine-p39.test.ts` plays a SYNTHETIC card with that wording (unkicked, kicked, and the second trigger absent when not kicked). Training is 162 of 192 (161 before), hold-out 52 of 61 (unchanged), a gap of 0.9 points (training 84.4%, hold-out 85.2%). Limits: see D-183 and `docs/ROADMAP.md`. Tests: `parser-p39.test.ts`, `parser-p39-needs.test.ts`, `convert-grammar-engine-p39.test.ts` (a game of each shape with SYNTHETIC cards that carry the real wording), the rules' `examples` and `rejects` (`parser-registry.test.ts`), and the web wording (`mana-spent-text.test.ts`: "When you cast this spell", "tokens named ...", "the amount of mana spent to cast it", "for each mana from an artifact source spent to cast it").

## D-185: The Korvold slice 6, keywords, engine: Encore, Devour and Riot, the exile of the card itself as a cost, a requirement to attack a given player, and "Creature spells you control can't be countered" (2026-11-02)
- Context: Slice 6 of the owner's Korvold deck is three cards (`docs/proposals/korvold-deck-analysis.md`): Impulsive Pilferer (Encore {3}{R}), Dragon Broodmother (a token with flying and devour 2 at the beginning of each upkeep) and Rhythm of the Wild ("Creature spells you control can't be countered." and "Nontoken creatures you control have riot."). Each line was run through the parser and `validateCard` from the owner's request file before planning, and the three keywords were read in the CR text of the repository (`pnpm rule 702.141`, `702.82`, `702.136`; never from memory). The official rulings could not be read (Scryfall is not reachable from the sandbox), so no behaviour below rests on a ruling; the points a ruling could change are listed under Limits. Class corrections: the analysis called Encore K and said the pieces exist; they did, except two: the cost "Exile this card from your graveyard" (the engine had no cost that exiles the source) and a requirement to attack a given player (the existing `requireAttack` is for a group and for "each combat", and a battle or a planeswalker would have satisfied it). Devour was K with a new decision "as it enters" on a token and on a card: the pipeline already asked such questions (D-100, D-151), so it is K and not S. Rhythm of the Wild was K + P, and the analysis proposed reading its riot line as a replacement of an entering creature; that would have been wrong for a creature that has riot of its own (CR 702.136b: each instance works separately, so such a creature under Rhythm asks twice), so riot is a real keyword and a static ability can give it, read from the battlefield as the creature enters (CR 614.12). No approval gate was needed.
- Decision: (1) **Encore** (CR 702.141a). The keyword `{ kind: 'encore', cost }` expands in `derive` (`rules/derive-keywords.ts`) into an activated ability that works from the graveyard: the cost, the new cost `{ kind: 'exileThis' }`, the effect `{ kind: 'encore' }`, timing `sorcery`, `functionsIn: 'graveyard'`; `hasGraveyardAbility` (`rules/activate-legality.ts`) lists the card as a candidate. `exileThis` (`rules/activate-costs.ts`, `CostBreakdown.exileThis`) moves the source from its owner's graveyard to exile with the costs that need no mana and no choice, so it is a cost (CR 118.1) and a cancel rewinds it (CR 733); it is valid only on an ability that functions from the graveyard (`checkActivationCosts`), so a card may also write "{2}{B}, Exile this card from your graveyard: ..." with it.
