The effect `encore` (`rules/effects.ts`) reads the card from its last-known information in the graveyard (CR 113.7a, 608.2h: the card is already a new object in exile) and makes one `enterToken` instruction for each opponent (`resolvePlayers` `eachOpponent`; with two seats, one token), each with `encoreFor: <opponent>`: the token is a copy (`copiableValues`, CR 707.2) created like any token, so a question it asks as it enters is asked (below); `rules/encore.ts` then binds it: a continuous effect `mustAttackPlayer { seat }` (new `ContinuousChange`, until end of turn), a continuous effect `grantKeyword haste` until end of turn and a delayed triggered ability (`GameState.delayedTriggers`, the pattern of Unearth) that sacrifices the token at the beginning of the next end step. `mustAttackPlayer` is read in `rules/combat-legality.ts` (`playersToAttack`): a creature able to attack that player has only that player among its targets (a battle or a planeswalker does not satisfy it) and is a required attacker (CR 508.1d), unless every target costs mana (CR 508.1d, D-125, as for any requirement). (2) **Devour** (CR 702.82a) and **Riot** (CR 702.136a) are static abilities applied as the permanent enters (CR 614.12) and share `rules/enters-keywords.ts`. A permanent that enters from a card (`moveObject` in `rules/zones.ts`: a spell resolving, an effect, a copy of a spell that becomes a token) and a token (`rules/enter-token.ts`, the instruction `enterToken`, which an effect uses when `tokenAsks` says the definition asks: a choice, riot of its own or given, or devour with a creature to sacrifice) ask, in this order: the "As this enters, choose" question, riot once for each instance, then devour. Riot is a `chooseOption` of purpose `riot` with the options `counter` and `haste`; `riotSoFar` carries the answers already given so the second instance of riot asks again with the first answer known; an instance is a printed `keyword riot` or a static `grantKeyword riot` of a permanent already on the battlefield whose group filter the entering permanent matches (`riotInstances`: the entering permanent is read as it would be there, as `groupEntryCounters` reads one, and the static ability's `condition`, if any, must hold). Devour is a `choosePermanent` of purpose `devour` (`min` 0, `max` the number of creatures, the legal creatures all those the controller controls; not asked when there is none, the permanent being not on the battlefield and so never one of them); the answer is sacrificed by `moveObject`'s wrapper (`sacrificeForDevour`, with the `sacrificed` event) before the permanent is on the battlefield and the permanent enters with N counters for each. A chosen counter is part of its counters as it enters (`keywordEntryCounters`); a chosen haste is `GameObject.riotHaste`, which `derive` turns into the haste keyword (`rules/derive-alt.ts`), so "loses all abilities" takes it away as it does the haste of a dashed creature. The answers travel as `ResolutionContext.entersDevour`, `entersRiot` or as fields of the `enterToken` instruction, and are routed by `answerResolutionRiot` and `answerResolutionDevour` (`rules/stack.ts`, `api.ts`); a land played from the hand (a creature land with riot) waits in the hand and is played again with the answers (`playLand`). `validateCard`: devour is on a permanent card that is not a land, one per face or token and with N a positive whole number; riot is given only by a static ability whose subject is a group (`filter`), never by an effect, an "enters as a copy" or an attached permanent (`GRANTABLE_KEYWORDS` lists it, and each of those places refuses it); a token that a replacement effect creates as a creature dies has no devour or riot, because it is made with no question. (3) **`spellsCantBeCountered { spells }`** (a `StaticEffect`, `rules/restrictions.ts` `canBeCountered`): while a permanent has it, a spell on the stack that the filter describes, for the controller of the permanent, is not countered (CR 101.2, 701.6a). The filter names no zone (`checkDescribing`), the engine adds `zone: 'stack'`; it is the ability of a permanent on the battlefield, so "loses all abilities" ends it. The spell's own `cantBeCountered` restriction is unchanged.
- Alternatives: Reading Rhythm's riot line as a replacement of the entering creature (the analysis's proposal): rejected, it would make a riot creature ask once under Rhythm instead of twice (CR 702.136b). Making Encore one `moveToZone` plus `createToken` plus `grantKeyword` plus `delayedTrigger` in the AST: rejected, the AST has no "for each opponent" with "that opponent" as a reference, a delayed trigger names no object (D-128) and the exile of the card is a cost; a single effect, as Unearth's, is honest and short. Giving the token the attack requirement through `restrict attacksEachCombat`: rejected, it would not say which player and a battle could satisfy it. Asking devour through the existing `sacrifice` purpose: rejected, the answer belongs to the entering permanent, not to an instruction at the head of the queue, and the dialog and the agents want to know it is devour. Keeping the riot choice in `GameObject.chosen`: rejected, `chosen` is the "chosen type" of CR 607.2d and a Saga's read ahead uses `option`. A continuous effect for the haste of riot: rejected, a permanent effect would stay in the state after the permanent left. Asking riot and devour in the order the controller likes (CR 616.1): not built, the two never interact (the counter and the haste are the same whichever comes first), so it is not asked; devour comes last because it sacrifices, which no later question may need to see. A new Playwright test: not added, no new dialog (the riot question reuses the named-option dialog, the devour question the permanent picker).
- Consequences: The three cards are expressible and run (parser D-186). `ENGINE_VERSION` 41; the recorded derive digests were recorded again (`UPDATE_DERIVE_DIGESTS=1`: the version is in the state hash and the new SYNTHETIC cards join the pool the soup decks are drawn from). The web says the new decisions (`game/keywords-text.ts`: the riot buttons "A +1/+1 counter" and "Haste", the devour prompt, the log line "You choose a +1/+1 counter for X (riot)", the chips "Enc", "Dev 2" and "Riot", "Encore {3}{R}" on the card in the graveyard, the effect on the stack, "Exile this card from your graveyard" as a cost, the group "can't be countered"), the casual agent answers them (`casual-keywords.ts`: devour sacrifices only tokens of power 1, never a card; riot takes haste when the creature can attack at once and nothing can block it, else the counter; `casual-activations.ts`: Encore is activated as Unearth is, for a creature that would attack safely or for the win), and the random agent already answers any decision legally. Limits, also in `docs/ROADMAP.md`: rulings not read, so nothing rests on one; Encore makes a copy for each opponent but the scenario DSL builds two seats, so only the one-token case is run in tests, and "attacks that opponent" is not obeyed with a battle or a planeswalker as the only choice (neither is in the engine's supported cards); the token copies keep the abilities of the card as it last was in the graveyard, and a copy of a card with a "dies" trigger triggers it when sacrificed; "Devour [quality]" (CR 702.82c) and "it devoured" (CR 702.82b) are not built (no card of the deck); riot and devour cannot be granted by an effect, only riot by a static group (a creature that gains riot after it entered has no choice to make, CR 702.136a); "enters tapped unless ..." is read after devour's sacrifices (the order CR 616.1 lets the controller choose is not asked); a creature land with riot that is also asked to pay life as it is played is not supported (no card), and the answers of such a land are carried through its decision. Tests: `scenario-xx-encore.test.ts`, `scenario-xx-devour-riot.test.ts` (SYNTHETIC cards `synthetic-korvold-keywords.ts`), the changed lists of `ast-features.test.ts` and `ast-supported.test.ts`, `casual-korvold-keywords.test.ts` (AI), `korvold-keywords-games.test.ts` (the soak of the deck style `korvoldKeywords`: 100 games with random and casual agents, no fault, exact replay, consistent state, the Encore tokens gone before the next turn, no creature spell countered under Rhythm, and every card, the devour question, the riot question and Encore played; the cards are kept out of the generic soak pools in `packages/ai/test/helpers.ts`, because they ask `chooseOption` and `choosePermanent` as a permanent enters and `games-100.test.ts` expects `chooseOption` only from the dedicated styles; that test still fails on the trample check that is being fixed on its own branch), `korvold-keywords-text.test.ts` (web). Mutation-checked on a scratch copy (engine): each of the three mechanics has between 1 and 7 tests that fail for each mutation tried, except the narrowing of the attack targets to the opponent, which with two players and no battle or planeswalker in the game changes nothing.

## D-186: The parser reads the Korvold slice 6: "Encore {M}", "Devour N", "Riot", a token "with flying and devour 2", "Creature spells you control can't be countered." and "have riot" (2026-11-02)
- Context: D-185 gave the engine the keywords; the rest was the grammar. The reading of each card at parser 44 (from the owner's request file): Impulsive Pilferer stopped at "Encore {3}{R}" (no rule), Dragon Broodmother at "devour 2." (the token rule knew the keywords the engine can grant and "devour" takes a number), Rhythm of the Wild at its first line (no rule: the static rule that reads "~ can't be countered" is for the spell itself and its `rejects` list this very line) and at "riot." (the keyword was not a word of the grammar). None of the three cards is in the golden corpus (acceptance names for the owner's `pnpm corpus:extract`).
- Decision: Stage P40. (1) **`keyword.encore`** (`rules/keyword/alt-costs.ts`): "Encore {3}{R}", a line of its own like Unearth, lowered to the keyword `encore` with the plain mana cost (`lower/abilities.ts`, `lowerCostedKeyword`; the need is `keyword:encore` and `cost:mana`). (2) **"Devour N"** is a numbered keyword (`rules/keyword/numbered.ts`, read by `keyword.line`, lowered to `{ kind: 'devour', count }`; "Devour [quality]" is not read, the number must follow the word) and **"Riot"** a keyword without a parameter (`rules/keyword/vocabulary.ts`, with the engine's `GRANTABLE_KEYWORDS`, which now lists it, so the static rule `static.permanents` reads "Nontoken creatures you control have riot." and lowers it to the engine's group `grantKeyword`, needing `keyword:riot` too). (3) **A token "with flying and devour 2"** (`rules/token/index.ts`, `lower/effects.ts`): the keywords of a token may be one grantable keyword and "devour N", or "devour N" alone; the number rides in the keywords as "devour 2" and the lowering builds the keyword with its count. A longer list ("flying, trample, and devour 2") is not read, because the grantable list is written "A, B, and C" and stops at a word it does not know. (4) **`static.spells-cant-be-countered`** (`rules/static/korvold.ts`, `lower/korvold.ts`): "Creature spells you control can't be countered.", also "Spells you control ...", "Noncreature spells ...", "Dragon spells ..." and the lists of types the cost reduction reads (`spellSubject`, now exported); lowered to `spellsCantBeCountered` with the filter (`controller: 'you'`), the need `static:spellsCantBeCountered`. The rule is read quietly, so no diagnostic of a cost reduction moves. The rule registry has `keyword.encore` after `keyword.unearth` and `static.spells-cant-be-countered` after `static.group-enters-untapped`.
- Alternatives: A rule for "have riot" of its own: rejected, the shared grantable words already read it once the engine lists the keyword, and its validators refuse every way the engine cannot run (an effect, an attached permanent). Letting `isGrantable` add riot on the parser's side only: rejected, the parser test keeps the grammar's words and the engine's list the same list. Reading a token's keyword list with "devour N" last for any length: rejected, it would need a second list parser; no card needs it.
- Consequences: All three cards read completely and pass `validateCard` (parser version 45), and `parser-p40.test.ts` holds their real wording as the nodes the engine runs. The golden corpus: no card changed status, only the version moved (training 162 of 192, hold-out 52 of 61, unchanged; a gap of 0.9 points, training 84.4%, hold-out 85.2%). Two lines that the tests listed as unread are read now (`Creature spells you control can't be countered.`, `Nontoken creatures you control have riot.`): `convert-grammar-corpus-p12.test.ts` and `convert-grammar-corpus-p3.test.ts` say so, and `parser-p12.test.ts` keeps "Spells your opponents control can't be countered." as the line that stays unread. `parser-p3-statics.test.ts` leaves riot out of the "attached permanent has the keyword" loop and holds its own test. Limits: see D-185 and `docs/ROADMAP.md`. Tests: `parser-p40.test.ts`, `parser-p40-needs.test.ts`, `convert-grammar-engine-p40.test.ts` (a game of each card's wording with SYNTHETIC cards), the rules' `examples` and `rejects` (`parser-registry.test.ts`), and the web wording (`korvold-keywords-text.test.ts`).

## D-187: The Korvold slice 7a, expensive singles, engine: a sacrifice of one or more with "up to that many" targets, +1/+0 for each time a creature attacked, a combat phase added after a main phase, and the top cards of another library exiled face down to look at and play (2026-11-02)
- Context: Slice 7 of the owner's Korvold deck was four cards (`docs/proposals/korvold-deck-analysis.md`); Ancient Adamantoise needs a decision of the owner first (damage redirection, `docs/proposals/damage-redirection.md`) and is handled apart, so this slice, 7a, is three: Swashbuckler Extraordinaire, Decadent Dragon // Expensive Taste and Moraug, Fury of Akoum. Each text was run through the parser from the owner's request file before planning (the failures: Swashbuckler stops at "attack, you may sacrifice one or more Treasures ...", Moraug at "for each time it has attacked this turn" and at "it's your main phase", Expensive Taste at "the top two cards of target opponent's library face down"; the Dragon half already read), and the CR text was read in the repository (`pnpm rule 406.3`, `406.3a`, `500.8`, `500.9`, `500.10`, `505.1`, `603.12`, `608.2d`, `701.21`, `715.3d`). The official rulings could not be read (Scryfall is not reachable from the sandbox), so no behaviour below rests on one; the points a ruling could change are under Limits. Class corrections: the analysis called all three P (hard); they are P, none is S. The part the analysis feared most for Moraug, "an ordered list of added phases", is a short list in the turn state because CR 500.8 puts an added phase directly after the phase that is going on (so a new one always goes first), and the hidden information of Expensive Taste is the one the engine already had for Hideaway and Foretell (a card that only some players may look at), with a new owner of the look. No S-class subsystem and no approval gate.
- Decision: (1) **Sacrifice of one or more, "up to that many".** `ChooseSelector.atLeastOne` (with `anyNumber`, only in a `sacrifice`): the player who says yes chooses at least one of the candidates (`chooseSacrifice.atLeastOne`, `choosePermanent` with `min` 1; `rules/sacrifice-choice.ts`). The `may` before it is not asked when there is no candidate (`rules/effects.ts`: nothing to say yes to, so no dialog at every attack of a deck with no Treasure). `TargetSpec.upToThatMany` (a slot of a `reflexive` ability after a `sacrifice`, no `min`, `max` or `divide`): as the reflexive ability is created (CR 603.12) the engine writes `min` 0 and `max` the number of permanents that resolution sacrificed into the ability that goes on the stack (`rules/may-effects.ts`, CR 601.2c, 603.3d: the number is fixed then and the targets are chosen as the ability goes on the stack); none sacrificed, no ability. `validateCard` refuses the field anywhere else. The trigger of "Whenever you attack" is the existing `attackBatch` with `atLeast` 1 (`validate-angels.ts` used to refuse fewer than two; one is "Whenever you attack" and the engine already ran it). (2) **The count of attacks.** `StaticPtAmount` `timesAttacked`: the number of times the permanent being looked at was declared as an attacker this turn, read from `TurnLog.attacked` (a creature that attacks in two combat phases counts twice, CR 508.1), in a `modifyPt` of a group, plain +N/+N only (`staticAmountOf` takes the recipient: `rules/derive-count.ts`, `derive-statics.ts`; a characteristic-defining ability refuses it). (3) **A combat phase added after a main phase.** `Condition` `yourMainPhase` (CR 505.1: the precombat or postcombat main phase of a turn of the controller; as an intervening "if" it holds as the event happens and as the ability resolves, CR 603.4). `TurnState.addedPhases` replaces the counter `extraCombats` of D-151: the phases an effect added, in the order they will occur; `Effect` `extraCombat` puts a new combat phase first in the list (CR 500.8: directly after the phase that is going on, and the most recently created one occurs first) with `after`, the phase of the turn's own sequence it follows (`TurnState.addedAfter` while an added phase is going on, so a phase added from an added phase follows that one); when the last step of a phase ends (`draw`, `precombatMain`, `endOfCombat`, `postcombatMain`; `rules/flow.ts`) the first of the list begins, and when the list is empty after an added phase the turn goes on with the phase that follows the one it followed (a combat after the precombat main phase comes before the combat of the turn; one after the postcombat main phase is followed by the end step, with no new main phase, CR 500.10). `extraCombat.atBeginning` is "At the beginning of that combat, untap all creatures you control" (CR 603.7): a group untap that a delayed triggered ability of the controller runs as the beginning of combat step of that phase begins; the engine creates that ability as the phase begins (not as the effect resolves; nothing in between can tell them apart, and one for each phase, so two added phases untap twice), as a `step` trigger of `beginCombat`, and it goes on the stack like any trigger. `validateCard`: `extraCombat` stays refused except in an ability of an attack or one whose intervening "if" is `yourMainPhase` (the places the phase that is going on is known to be a main phase or a combat phase), and `atBeginning` must be a group untap. An effect that adds a phase in the ending phase is lost (the list is read when the draw step, the precombat main phase, the combat phase or the postcombat main phase ends; no card adds a phase in the ending phase, and one added in the beginning phase would follow the draw step, which no test runs). (4) **Exiled face down, to look at and play.** `Effect` `exileTop` has `from` (a target player's library; the controller's own when left out) and `faceDown` (CR 406.3); the cards are exiled one after another from the top and belong to that library's owner. `GameObject.exiledFaceDown` and `lookers`: a card exiled face down has no characteristics, and only the players in `lookers` may look at it until it leaves exile (CR 406.3: once allowed to look, a player may go on looking; the card turns face up as it is cast or played, CR 406.3a, which is the new object a cast makes, so both fields are gone with it); `getView` shows every other player the placeholder "Face-down card" (`isFaceDownTo` also feeds `determinize`) and `ObjectView.exiledFaceDown` marks both views. `Effect` `mayPlay` has `lasts: 'whileExiled'` ("for as long as they remain exiled": a continuous effect with no end of its own, which a card leaving exile ends because it is a new object, CR 400.7) and `lookAt` (the controller is added to `lookers` of each card that is face down). A card in exile that another player owns may be cast or played by a player an effect let (`castZone` in `rules/legality.ts`; its cost is the ordinary one, a land counts as a land play and enters under the player's control, a permanent that leaves goes to its owner's zone), and an Adventure that its caster did not own is on an adventure for its controller (`GameObject.adventureBy`, CR 715.3d: "its controller exiles it. For as long as that card remains exiled, that player may play it"). `Decadent Dragon // Expensive Taste` is played through its real faces in the tests (cast face 1, face 0 from exile).
- Alternatives: A counter of extra combats that also records where the phase goes (the analysis said a counter is not enough): rejected for the list, which is also what the older counter becomes (an attack in the combat phase is `after: 'combat'`, so the Dragons cards run as before). A delayed trigger created as the effect resolves with a "next combat" moment for "that combat": rejected, with two phases added in one main phase both triggers would untap in the first one and the second phase would have none; tying the ability to the phase it belongs to is the only reading that gives each combat its own untap. Reading "you may sacrifice one or more Treasures" as "sacrifice any number" with no `may`: rejected, the player may choose none there and the "may" is the text. A `Condition` for any phase (`duringPhase { phase }`): not built, nothing needs it. A `lookers` list on the Hideaway objects as well: not done (Hideaway names the permanent whose controller may look, CR 702.75a, and changes when that permanent leaves). A DSL change for casting another player's card: none needed (a card ref takes a seat).
- Consequences: The three cards are expressible and run (parser D-188). `ENGINE_VERSION` 42; the recorded derive digests were recorded again (`UPDATE_DERIVE_DIGESTS=1`: the version is in the state hash and the new SYNTHETIC cards join the pool the soup decks are drawn from). `scenario-xx-extra-combat.test.ts` reads `addedPhases` where it read `extraCombats` (the same claim: nothing is left when the turn goes on). `scenario-xx-attack-batch.test.ts` now refuses `atLeast` 0, not 1. The web says the new shapes (`condition-text.ts` "it's your main phase", `pt-text.ts` "+1/+0 for each time it has attacked this turn", `dragons-text.ts` the library of another player, "face down", "You may look at and play those cards for as long as they remain exiled" and the added phase with what happens at its beginning, `ability-label.ts` "up to that many target creatures" and "one or more", `permanents.ts` the prompt "Sacrifice one or more Treasures you control for ...", `later-text.ts` the mark and the fact of a card face down that its viewer may look at, `describe.ts` the log line that names no card, `OtherZonesStrip.tsx` the cards the viewer may cast from exile whoever owns them), and the casual agent needs nothing new: it declines a "you may sacrifice" (`COSTLY_OPTION`), answers a sacrifice of a minimum of one with its cheapest permanents (`choosePermanentToSacrifice`, the Treasures first) and a number of targets with the targets decision it already has; the cards of another player in exile are ordinary `castSpell` options for it. No new decision kind, so no Playwright test. Limits, also in `docs/ROADMAP.md`: rulings not read, so nothing rests on one; `atLeastOne` only for a sacrifice, `upToThatMany` only in a reflexive ability and for `sacrifice` (the number of other things "that many" can mean is not built); an added phase is a combat phase only (an added main phase or end step is not), in an ability of an attack or one that checks that it is the controller's main phase, and none is added by an effect that resolves in the beginning or ending phase; `exileTop` with `from` is one target player (not each opponent); the cards a player may look at are not shown to a player who may only play them ("play" without "look at" leaves them hidden, though the engine lets the player cast them: a card with that wording is not in the deck); a face-down card cast as a spell with morph (CR 708.4) is not built (the card is turned face up as it is cast); the spend of mana "as though it were mana of any type" that some cards of this kind add is not built; the permission outlives the player's own game only as long as the card stays in exile (a flicker or a Commander-zone move gives a new object). Tests: `scenario-xx-korvold-singles.test.ts` (SYNTHETIC cards `synthetic-korvold-singles.ts`: the sacrifice and its number of targets, the count of attacks, the phases added in the precombat and the postcombat main phase, two in one main phase, none outside a main phase or in the opponent's, the cards face down seen by their caster and not by the opponent, cast and played from the pile, kept in later turns, an Adventure of the pile cast by its taker), the changed lists of `ast-features.test.ts` and `ast-supported.test.ts`, `korvold-singles-games.test.ts` (AI: the soak of the deck style `korvoldSingles`; the cards are kept out of the generic soak pools in `packages/ai/test/helpers.ts`), `korvold-singles-text.test.ts` (web). Mutation-checked on a scratch copy (engine): each of the fourteen mutations tried (`atLeastOne` ignored, a target too many, the question asked with no Treasure, every attacker counted, a wrong resume after the postcombat main phase, the main-phase condition ignoring whose turn, no delayed untap, a new phase put last, the card shown to every player, `lookAt` ignored, a card of another player not castable, a permission that ends with the turn, `adventureBy` not recorded, the move not marking the card) makes between 1 and 5 tests fail.

## D-188: The parser reads the Korvold slice 7a: "Whenever you attack", "sacrifice one or more ...", "up to that many target creatures gain ...", "gets +1/+0 for each time it has attacked this turn", "if it's your main phase", "there's an additional combat phase after this phase" with "At the beginning of that combat, ...", "Exile the top ... cards of target opponent's library face down" and "You may look at and play those cards for as long as they remain exiled" (2026-11-02)
- Context: D-187 gave the engine the pieces; the rest was the grammar. The reading of each card at parser 45 (from the owner's request file): Swashbuckler Extraordinaire stopped at "attack, you may sacrifice ..." (no rule for "Whenever you attack" alone); Moraug at "for each time it has attacked this turn" (`static.each` knows no such count) and, in the second ability, at the condition "it's your main phase"; Expensive Taste at "the top two cards of target opponent's library face down" (`effect.flicker`, the nearest). Decadent Dragon read at once. None of the three cards is in the golden corpus (acceptance names for the owner's `pnpm corpus:extract`).
- Decision: Stage P41. (1) **`trigger.you-attack`** (`rules/trigger/korvold.ts`): "you attack", lowered as `attackBatch` with `atLeast` 1; the longer "you attack with ..." stays `trigger.attack-batch`'s (the rule refuses a trigger that goes on with "with", "alone", "you", "or" or "and"). (2) **`noun.one-or-more-permanents`** (`rules/noun/choose.ts`): "one or more Treasures", "one or more other creatures"; read by `effect.sacrifice`, lowered as the choose selector with `anyNumber` and `atLeastOne` (the need `selector:atLeastOne`). (3) **"up to that many target creatures"**: a branch of the target noun (`rules/noun/index.ts`, plural, `upTo`, no count), lowered as `upToThatMany` (the need `selector:upToThatMany`), and **`effect.gain-keyword-targets`** (`rules/effect/korvold.ts`): "up to that many target creatures gain double strike until end of turn", also "up to two target creatures gain flying ..." (the verb "gain" of `effect.gain-keyword`'s own parser, now exported, for a plural target subject with "up to"; the singular "target creatures gain" is still refused by `effect.gain-keyword`). "When you do" after "you may sacrifice ..." is the reflexive ability of D-135 and D-178. (4) **`static.pt-times-attacked`** (`rules/static/korvold.ts`): "Each creature you control gets +1/+0 for each time it has attacked this turn", step +1 or +0 for each stat (not both 0), lowered as the `modifyPt` with `timesAttacked` (the need `amount:timesAttacked`; `IrStaticEffect` `ptTimesAttacked`). (5) **`condition.your-main-phase`** (`rules/condition/korvold.ts`): "it's your main phase" ("it is" too), the need `condition:yourMainPhase`. (6) **`effect.extra-combat-after`** (`rules/effect/korvold.ts`): "there's an additional combat phase after this phase" (the other order of words of `effect.extra-combat`), the same clause `extraCombat`; and the sentence "At the beginning of that combat, ..." is a delayed sentence (`IrSentence.delayed` step `thatCombat`, `sentence.ts`) that `lowerAtThatCombat` (`lower/sentences.ts`) folds into the `extraCombat` before it as `atBeginning`, which must be one group untap and the only thing the sentence does; any other sentence of this shape stays unread. (7) **`effect.exile-top-face-down`** ("Exile the top two cards of target opponent's library face down", one or more cards, a target player) lowered as `exileTop` with `from` and `faceDown`, and **`effect.may-look-and-play`** ("You may look at and play those cards for as long as they remain exiled", also "them" and "that card ... as long as it remains exiled") lowered as `mayPlay` with `lasts` `whileExiled` and `lookAt`, which the lowering reads only after cards exiled face down (`LowerContext.exiledFaceDown`; `IrDuration.scope` `whileExiled`). The rule registry has the new rules after their neighbours (`convert-parser.test.ts` lists them).
- Alternatives: Reading "that many" as a count in the amount grammar: rejected, it is not an amount of an effect but the number of targets of a slot, which the engine fixes as the ability goes on the stack. A rule for "target creatures gain" in general: rejected, "target creatures" without a number is not English and the plural subjects are numbered nouns; the new rule takes only a plural noun with "up to". Letting `static.each` read a count tail: rejected, one rule for one wording keeps the others (Each creature gets +1/+1) as they were. A face-down rule for your own library ("exile the top card of your library face down"): not read, no card (and the old `effect.exile-top` still rejects it).
- Consequences: All three cards read completely and pass `validateCard` (parser version 46), the Dragon half unchanged; `parser-p41.test.ts` holds the real wording of the three cards as the nodes the engine runs. The golden corpus: no card changed status, only the version moved (training 162 of 192, hold-out 52 of 61, a gap of 0.9 points, unchanged). Limits: see D-187 and `docs/ROADMAP.md`. Tests: `parser-p41.test.ts`, `parser-p41-needs.test.ts` (each feature the engine lacks is named: `selector:atLeastOne`, `selector:upToThatMany`, `amount:timesAttacked`, `condition:yourMainPhase`, `effect:extraCombat`, `effect:exileTop`, `effect:mayPlay`), `convert-grammar-engine-p41.test.ts` (a game of each card's wording with SYNTHETIC cards, the Adventure through a two-face stored card), the rules' `examples` and `rejects` (`parser-registry.test.ts`), and the web wording (`korvold-singles-text.test.ts`).

## D-189: The Korvold slice 8a, control change, engine: the controller of a permanent is derived (layer 2), `gainControl` with four durations, the trigger "whenever an opponent taps an artifact for mana" (2026-11-02)
- Context: Slice 8a of the owner's Korvold deck is the control-change subsystem of `docs/design/control-change.md` (the owner approved the Korvold slices and the proposals were presented to them) and its one card, Treasure Nabber. No effect could change who controls a permanent: the controller was a stored field (`GameObject.controller`) that 359 places of the engine read (found with the type checker: the field renamed once, every read listed). The CR text was read in the repository (`pnpm rule 613`, `613.1b`, `613.7`, `611.2`, `611.2b`, `611.2c`, `302.6`, `110.2`, `108.3`, `400.3`, `506.4`, `603.10`, `800.4`, `106.12`, `605.1b`, `702.62a`); the official rulings could not be read (Scryfall is not reachable from the sandbox), so no behaviour below rests on one. The CR itself decides the points the proposal left open: CR 611.2b's own example (Master Thief) is the rule for "for as long as you control this" ("if you lose control before the ability resolves, it does nothing"), CR 800.4a's example is Act of Treason, CR 506.4 removes a permanent from combat when its controller changes, and 302.6 is "continuously since their most recent turn began".
- Decision: (1) **A pure refactor first** (the first commit of the slice, `controllerOf`). `rules/control.ts` has `controllerOf(state, obj)`; the about 110 reads of the field that are about a GameObject (the rest of the 359 are the controller of a resolution, an event or a request) in the rules, the view and the test DSL go through it, and it returned the stored field. Last-known information is frozen with the controller the object had as it left (`recordLki`), so what a leaves-the-battlefield or "dies" ability reads is the player who controlled it then. `matchesFilterWith`, `subjectAffects`, `subjectContextOf`, `legendRuleDecision`, `seatOfObject` and `describeLocation` took the state for it. `test/control-reads.test.ts` scans the sources and fails when a rule reads the field of an object directly (a read that is meant says `stored controller` on its line). Checked as the proposal asks (D-173): `node tools/perf/precon-digest.ts` (10 seeded precon games) printed the same digests before and after, and the engine tests passed unchanged. (2) **Layer 2** (CR 613.1b). `ContinuousChange` `control { seat }`: `controllerOf` reads the effects on the permanent (`rules/effects-on.ts`, the grouping `derive-layers.ts` already used, moved to a leaf so that `control.ts` imports no layer) in timestamp order and the last one decides (CR 613.7); one that ends leaves the others. It reads nothing from `derive` (layer 2 comes before the layers `derive` applies and static abilities match "you control" against it). The stored controller stays the player the object entered under (CR 110.2) and is what a spell or ability on the stack has; the owner never changes (CR 108.3), so a stolen permanent goes to its owner's graveyard, a token ceases to exist, a commander asks its owner, and commander tax is untouched. (3) **The effect** `gainControl { objects, duration }` (`rules/control-effects.ts`): the objects are a `target` or the `triggerSubject` permanent, fixed as it begins and a permanent that is gone is skipped (CR 611.2c, 608.2b: a Treasure sacrificed for the mana that triggered the ability is such an object); the controller of the effect is who gains control. Durations: `untilEndOfTurn` (cleanup, CR 514.2), `untilEndOfYourNextTurn` (as `playEnd` of D-151: the next turn of the controller that comes after this moment, even when this turn is theirs), `forAsLongAsYouControlThis` and `permanent` (CR 611.2a). A new `EffectEnd` `whileControlling { seat, source }`: `forAsLongAsYouControlThis` does nothing when `this` is not on the battlefield under the controller as the effect would begin (CR 611.2b, the Master Thief case), and otherwise ends for good as that stops being so; `endLostControlEffects` runs first in `checkStateBasedActions` (the duration is a state of the game, so no moment of it is missed) and makes the check run again. `validateCard` refuses `forAsLongAsYouControlThis` in a spell. (4) **Expiry** reports events: `expireEndOfTurnEffects`, `expireEndStepEffects` and `expireTurnStartEffects` return `{ state, events }` (through `dropEffects`), so a permanent that goes back to whoever had it is one `controlChanged` event (`from`, `to`; the web log says "X gain(s) control of Y"). (5) **CR 506.4**: a permanent whose controller changes, as an effect begins or ends, is removed from combat (`rules/combat-removal.ts`, the function regeneration used, moved; a creature it blocked stays blocked, CR 509.1h, the existing rule of that removal). (6) **Summoning sickness** (CR 302.6): `controlledSince(state, obj)` is the later of `timestamp`, the new `GameObject.controlChangedAt` (set when an effect ended and control went back to somebody: the permanent is sick again for them) and the effect on it that gave control to a player other than the one who had it; `wouldBeSummoningSick` and Echo's `cameUnderControlSinceLastUpkeep` read it. So a creature taken this turn cannot attack or use {T} abilities without haste, one that stays under the thief's control through their next turn can, and one that returns in the middle of its owner's own turn is sick. A permanent that is not a creature has no sickness (CR 302.6 is about creatures), so a stolen Sol Ring is tapped at once. (7) **Who may do what**: activating abilities, mana abilities, the untap step, sacrifice, attacking and blocking, hexproof, the legend rule per controller and the static abilities of the permanent ("creatures you control") all read the derived controller, so the old controller loses them and the new one has them, and the triggers of the permanent trigger for the new controller; a triggered ability already on the stack or waiting to go on it keeps the controller it had (CR 603.3, 112.7a). The legal-actions list and the view (`ObjectView.controller`, the new `controlEnds`) follow. With two seats the game ends when a player loses, so CR 800.4a (objects of a player who left, effects that give them control) has nothing to do: the stolen permanent and the effect are irrelevant once the game is over; multiplayer needs it (`docs/ROADMAP.md`). (8) **The trigger** `tapsForMana { who, what }` and the event `tappedForMana { object, seat }` (`payManaAbilityCosts`, right after `tapped`): CR 106.12 says tapping a permanent for mana is activating a mana ability of it with {T} in its cost, and a Treasure's is one ({T}, Sacrifice this artifact), so "whenever an opponent taps an artifact for mana" triggers for a Treasure and its effect finds nothing (the object is gone by then). It is an ordinary triggered ability that uses the stack (CR 603.3: it goes on the stack the next time a player would receive priority, after the spell the mana was being paid for), not the triggered mana ability of the existing `tappedForMana` (CR 605.1b: one that adds mana, no stack); `validateCard` refuses an effect that adds mana in `tapsForMana` and tells the author to use `tappedForMana`. This is the one place the proposal ("extend `tappedForMana` with `by: 'opponent'`") was not followed to the letter: extending a trigger whose validator and lowering insist on a plain `addMana` would have mixed two rules; the proposal's idea of one event for it stands (`tappedForMana`). Durations are named as the proposal does (`untilEndOfYourNextTurn`, `forAsLongAsYouControlThis`).
- Alternatives: Changing the stored controller as the effect resolves and again as it ends: rejected by the proposal (not layer 2: a second effect and the timestamps break it, and ending needs a record anyway). Renaming the field so the compiler forbids a raw read: rejected (the test project alone reported 176 errors, mostly tests and fixtures that build objects, for what the source scan test guards); the scan is a text check, weaker than the type checker, and a read through a name it does not know (a new variable name for a GameObject) escapes it, which review has to catch. A new timestamp on the object when control changes: rejected, CR 613.7d gives a timestamp when an object enters a zone, not when it changes controller, and static abilities are ordered by it; `controlChangedAt` is a separate value. Ending "for as long as" when the SBA pass sees it, but also reading it in `controllerOf`: rejected, a read that depends on another permanent's controller would recurse and nothing can look at the state between actions (the check runs before anyone has priority).
- Consequences: Treasure Nabber is supported (SYNTHETIC fixture `synthetic-control.ts`, wording of the real card; parser D-190). `ENGINE_VERSION` 43 (the recorded derive digests were recorded again: the version is in the state hash and the new SYNTHETIC cards join the pool the soup decks draw from). `ObjectView.controlEnds` and the events `tappedForMana` and `controlChanged` are new (the web, D-190). Existing tests changed in three places only: the list of trigger kinds of the feature registry, the events of a hand-tapped Forest (`tappedForMana` follows `tapped`) and the filter test that builds an object by hand (it passes a state). Limits (all in `docs/ROADMAP.md`): Suspend gives haste "until you lose control of the spell or the permanent" (CR 702.62a) and the engine gives it to the permanent whoever controls it (`derive-alt.ts`); an effect that gives control to another player than the controller of the effect ("target opponent gains control of ...", Switcheroo's exchange) has no node; control-giving statics (an Aura "you control enchanted creature") are not built (layer 2 can take them: a `control` change from a static ability with its permanent's timestamp); a permanent that returns to the battlefield by a move that starts on the battlefield would come back under its stored controller, not its owner (no card of the engine moves like that); the Evoke sacrifice, the Dash return and Unearth are not tested with a stolen permanent (they read the derived controller, and CR 701.21a means the sacrifice does nothing to a permanent its controller no longer controls). Tests: `scenario-xx-control-change.test.ts` (the layer, each duration, the view and the log, timestamps, summoning sickness and haste, who may use it, triggers of the new and of the old controller, ownership and dying, commander, tokens, combat, "for as long as" and the Master Thief case, the end of the game, the Nabber in each shape), `ast-control-validate.test.ts`, `control-reads.test.ts`, and the soak `packages/ai/test/korvold-control-games.test.ts` (deck style `korvoldControl`).

## D-190: The parser reads the Korvold slice 8a: "gain control of ..." with its durations and "whenever an opponent taps an artifact for mana" (2026-11-02)
- Context: D-189 gave the engine the layer 2 effect and the trigger; the rest was the grammar. Treasure Nabber's text at parser 46 stopped at its trigger ("opponent taps an artifact for mana", closest rule `trigger.or`, from the owner's request file); no rule read "gain control of". The card is not in the golden corpus (it is in the acceptance names for the owner's `pnpm corpus:extract`).
- Decision: Stage P42. (1) **`trigger.taps-for-mana`** (`rules/trigger/control.ts`): "an opponent taps an artifact for mana", "a player taps a land for mana": the player relative to the controller, a plain "a/an" permanent phrase with no owner or controller, no type of mana ("for {C}" and several permanents are not read); lowered as `tapsForMana`. "You tap ... for mana" stays `trigger.tapped-for-mana`'s (a triggered mana ability), so one text never has two readers. (2) **`effect.gain-control`** (`rules/effect/control.ts`): "gain control of target creature until end of turn", "... of that artifact until the end of your next turn", "... for as long as you control ~" and none; one object (a target, "that artifact", "it"); lowered as `gainControl` (`lower/control.ts`, the need `effect:gainControl`; the lowering takes the duration itself). The new IR duration `whileYouControlSelf`. The binder already gives "that artifact" to the permanent a trigger is about when it is an artifact ("that permanent" when the trigger names any permanent; a land trigger with "that artifact" is an unbound reference, never a guess). The sentences after it of a steal spell ("Untap that creature. It gains haste until end of turn.") were read before and bind to the same target. (3) Refused, so flagged: "until your next turn", "until end of combat", "for as long as ~ remains tapped", "for as long as you control a Dragon", a group, "up to", a player ("target opponent gains control of ..."), "~".
- Alternatives: Reading the duration as the tail the clause machinery already knows (`duration.until-end-of-turn`): rejected, only that one duration has a rule and the others are part of the words of this one verb, as the Dragons rules (D-152) do for "until the end of your next turn". A rule for "whenever you tap an artifact for mana" with a non-mana body: not built, no card, and the rule that reads the text already is the mana ability's.
- Consequences: Treasure Nabber reads completely and passes `validateCard` (parser version 47); the golden corpus: no card changed status, only the version moved (training 162 of 192, hold-out 52 of 61, a gap of 0.9 points, unchanged). Limits: see D-189 and `docs/ROADMAP.md`. Tests: `parser-p42.test.ts` (the real wording as nodes, each duration, the sentences after it, the refused lines), `parser-p42-needs.test.ts` (`trigger:tapsForMana` and `effect:gainControl` named when the engine lacks them), `convert-grammar-engine-p42.test.ts` (a game of each wording with SYNTHETIC cards), the rules' `examples` and `rejects` (`parser-registry.test.ts`), and the web wording (`korvold-control-text.test.ts`).

## D-191: Damage events lifted out of D-156: the affected player chooses the order of prevention effects on one damage event (2026-11-02)
- Context: D-156 left CR 616.1 unbuilt (the engine applied the shields that prevent all damage first, then the numeric ones oldest first, and asked nothing) while the proposal was on hold. The owner decided on 2026-11-02 (`docs/proposals/damage-redirection.md`) to follow the rule for damage events, because Ancient Adamantoise needs it (a redirect and a shield on the same player are two effects whose order changes the result), and approved `docs/proposals/damage-replacement-order.md` with all its recommendations: skip the question when the order cannot matter; "Then: ..." on each button; casual and greedy take the first option (prevent first), the heuristic agent picks by what each choice leads to, random picks uniformly; the rider of a mana ability takes the default order; a combat damage step asks all its questions before any damage is dealt; the "would die" replacements stay under D-156; a redirect to another player's creature stays refused. The CR text was read in the repository (`pnpm rule 616.1`, `616.1e`, `616.1f`, `616.2`, `614.5`, `615.7`, `510.2`). This entry is steps 1 to 3 of the proposal (the refactor, the question, the agents and the web); step 4 (the redirect and `keepsDamage` for Ancient Adamantoise) is a later slice, and no card is added or changed here.
- Decision: (1) **`damageModifiers(state, event)`** (`rules/damage-order.ts`) lists the effects that apply to one damage event as it is now, in the default order: the static `preventDamageToThis` abilities of the recipient, then the shields that prevent all damage, then the numeric shields, oldest first; the building blocks stay in `rules/prevention.ts` (`isShield`, `shieldApplies`, `staticPreventions`). `applyModifier` applies one (all damage prevented and nothing used up, or up to the size of the shield, which is reduced and gone at 0, CR 615.7) and the list is made again after every step (CR 616.1f). The default order is exactly what `applyShields` did, so with nothing to ask every result is the same (the precon fingerprint `tools/perf/precon-digest.ts` is identical before and after, and at engine version 42 after step 2). (2) **The search.** `damageOrderMatters` searches every order exactly, up to six effects (more ask without searching, so a question that should be asked is never skipped), and says whether the order can change what the player ends with: a result is what reaches the recipient and what each group of interchangeable shields has left (without ids or timestamps, so two equal shields used in either order are one result, and a 3 and a 2 against 3 damage always leave one shield of 2). The question is skipped when every order ends the same, and when the default order is at least as good as every other (a shield for all damage first leaves the numeric one whole, which no player would answer otherwise); two orders that each keep something the other loses ask. Memoised on the result so far, not on the set of effects applied (the proposal's wording), because the same set can leave different shields. (3) **The decision.** No new kind: `chooseOption` with the purpose `'replacement'`, asked of the affected player (the damaged player, or the controller of the damaged permanent), `options` the keys of the effects (`shield:<id>`, `static:<object>:<index>`) in the default order, `replacement: { event, choices, resume? }` with each choice's words (`text`, built by the engine in `rules/damage-order-text.ts`) and `outcome` (what reaches the recipient, and what is prevented, if the choice goes first and the rest follow the default order; the proposal called it `then`, which the lint rejects as a property name). The answer is an ordinary `chooseOption` action, refused unless it is one of the options, with the new event `replacementChosen`; there is no way out. (4) **The pause.** `dealDamage` stays synchronous and never asks (the default order); the instruction that deals damage as a spell or ability resolves (`rules/damage-effects.ts`: `dealDamage`, `dealDividedDamage`; `rules/fight.ts`; excess damage in `rules/damage.ts`) is simulated from the state it began with, event after event, with the answers so far (`ResolutionContext.damageAnswers`); an event that needs one more answer returns the question with nothing dealt and no trigger collected, the instruction stays at the head of the queue and runs again with the answer, so a pause is invisible to the rest of the engine. Combat damage (`rules/combat.ts`, `rules/combat-flow.ts`): the whole batch is simulated the same way, a question carries the plan (`DamageResume`: the step, the assignments, the answers so far), and the answer deals the same batch again, to the next question or to the end, then priority goes to the active player (CR 510.3); the batch stays simultaneous (CR 510.2). The rider of a mana ability (`runImmediateEffects`) uses a flow that never asks, so it takes the default order. (5) **The agents.** `CasualAgent` and `GreedyAgent` (through `chooseOptionAnswer`) take the first option; `HeuristicAgent` (`heuristic-replacement.ts`) takes the choice with the least damage reaching its player or creature, then the most prevented, ties to the first; `RandomLegalAgent` picks among `options` as for any `chooseOption`. (6) **The web.** `NamedOptionDialog` ("Damage replacement", the prompt "3 damage from X would be dealt to you. Several effects apply. Choose which to apply first.", one button for each effect with "Then: 0 damage" under it), the log line "You apply "Prevent the next 3 damage that would be dealt to you this turn" first (X).", and a hidden SYNTHETIC deck (`synthetic-damage-order`) for the browser test.
- Alternatives: Always asking when two or more effects apply (simpler, the letter of CR 616.1, but it asks about two Fogs and two equal shields): rejected by the owner. A search whose result is only the shields that remain, with no notion of "at least as good": it would ask for every prevent-all plus numeric pair, where the prevent-all first is always right. A new decision kind: rejected (every handler map would need a case for no gain). Dealing the damage for real as each answer arrives and keeping the earlier damage: rejected, a pause that collects triggers of the events so far is the problem D-157 found, and combat damage is simultaneous. Naming the shield's source in the question: not done, a shield (`ContinuousEffect`) records no source, and adding one would change the state hash of every game with a shield; the words of the effect identify it.
- Consequences: `ENGINE_VERSION` 44 (a replay with two prevention effects that do not commute now has an extra action). 43 is the control-change slice (D-189), which merged first; the digests were recorded again here after merging it (`UPDATE_DERIVE_DIGESTS=1`) for the version and for the new SYNTHETIC cards (`synthetic-damage-order.ts`, which join the pool the soup decks are drawn from). The precon fingerprint is identical at version 42 (no precon game asks, as D-156 said) and differs at 43 only through the version in the state. D-156 is superseded for damage events; its other parts (the "would die" replacements, the zone-change pipeline, the counter replacements) stay in force, as do their fixed orders. The scenario test "two shields on one player: the older is used first" keeps its shape with equal shields (nothing asked); shields of different sizes ask (`scenario-xx-damage-order.test.ts`). The existing prevention soak (`prevention-games.test.ts`) never reached the question, and at 100 games it already fails the "a numeric shield is used up" path on the base branch (not changed here); the new soak `damage-order-games.test.ts` begins its games at the question. Limits, also in `docs/ROADMAP.md`: the rider of a mana ability takes the default order; "would die", enters and counter replacements are not asked; a shield names no source, so the question and the log say what the effect does and not whose it is; the search stops at six effects; the redirect (step 4) will add a modifier of another kind and a recipient that can change in the middle of the process, which the question and the web already carry (`outcome.to`) but do not yet use.

## D-192: Damage redirection (CR 614.9) and damage that stays through cleanup steps: Ancient Adamantoise, step 4 of the damage order (2026-11-02)
- Context: Steps 1 to 3 (D-191) built the question of the order of prevention effects on a damage event; step 4 of `docs/proposals/damage-replacement-order.md` and `docs/proposals/damage-redirection.md` is the redirect itself and `keepsDamage`, for Ancient Adamantoise of the owner's Korvold deck: "Damage isn't removed from this creature during cleanup steps." and "All damage that would be dealt to you and other permanents you control is dealt to this creature instead." (the card's text comes from the owner's request file of 2026-10-29; the file gives no power or toughness, so the SYNTHETIC fixture's 6/8 is invented). The owner decided (2026-11-02) to follow CR 616.1 precisely: the affected player chooses the order, "prevent first" being the default, and a redirect to another player's creature stays refused. The CR text was read in the repository (`pnpm rule 616.1`, `616.1e`, `616.1f`, `616.2`, `614.9`, `614.5`, `614.1a`, `120.3`, `120.4`, `514.2`, `704.5g`, `704.5h`). The official rulings could not be read (Scryfall is not reachable from the sandbox): nothing below rests on one; the points a ruling could change are under Limits.
- Decision: (1) **The AST.** The replacement `redirectDamage { you: boolean, permanents?: ObjectFilter }` (the controller of the creature and the other permanents the filter matches, read as they are on the battlefield for the controller of the creature: `controller: 'you'` is required, so the player who orders the effects is the one who chose it) and the static `keepsDamage { subject: this }`; both in `SUPPORTED_FEATURES`; `ast/validate-redirect.ts` (a recipient is named, no zone, owner, stackKind, X or "this turn" reading, a creature face only, no condition). (2) **`rules/damage-redirect.ts`: `redirectsFor(state, to, used)`.** A redirection applies to damage that would be dealt to `to` when it is read from the abilities its creature has now (so "loses all abilities" turns it off, CR 613.1f), has not been applied to this event already (CR 614.5: `used`), the creature is on the battlefield and is a creature (CR 614.9) and is not the recipient ("other"), the recipient is the controller (`you`) or a permanent that is a creature, planeswalker or battle (CR 614.9: damage is dealt only to those and to players) that the filter matches. Oldest creature first. (3) **One more modifier in `damageModifiers`.** `{ kind: 'redirect', key: 'redirect:<object>:<ability index>' }` (`damageModifiers(state, event, used)`), owned by its permanent. `Settling` now carries the recipient (`to`), the keys used, the events of the earlier recipients and what the current recipient had prevented; `applyModifier` of a redirection makes the creature the recipient and emits `damageRedirected { source, from, to, amount, combat }` (new), and `settleDamage` returns `Settled.to`; `dealDamageAsking` deals the damage to that recipient by the same source, so everything CR 120.3 says is the result for the creature that gets it (marked damage, -1/-1 counters for wither and infect, deathtouch, lifelink to the source's controller) and nothing happens to the player (no life loss, no poison, no commander damage, no "dealt combat damage" record). A shield on the creature applies once the damage is redirected to it (CR 616.2) and one on the first recipient no longer does; `damagePrevented` is one event for each recipient that had damage prevented. (4) **The default order is "prevention first".** The statics and the shields that prevent all damage, then the numeric shields, oldest first, then the redirections, oldest first: the owner's decision. The proposal's section 1 wrote "then redirection, then numeric shields", which contradicts its own section 5 and the owner; with it a numeric shield on the recipient would never see the damage. With no redirection the order is exactly D-191's. (5) **The search.** The shields tracked in the outcome are all the shields of the game, not only the ones that apply to the event as it began (a redirection can make one apply, CR 616.2); an outcome is the amount, the recipient it is dealt to (not compared when nothing is left) and the shields left; the default order dominates another only when no more damage reaches the same recipient and no shield has less left; the memo also holds the recipient and the redirections used. So with a shield for a number on the player a redirect asks (3 and 3: prevent it all and use the shield, or deal it to the Adamantoise and keep the shield); a shield on the player and a shield on the Adamantoise ask (each order uses one of them); two Adamantoises ask which applies first (the one applied last ends with the damage, since the other then redirects it to itself, CR 616.1f, and each is used once, CR 614.5); a shield that prevents all damage to the player does not ask, as in D-191 (prevent all first leaves nothing to deal and nothing used up), which differs from the proposal's example. (6) **The question.** `ReplacementChoice.kind` is `'redirect'` for a redirection, with its creature as `object` and `objectName` and the words "Deal it to Ancient Adamantoise instead"; `outcome` has `toName` (the recipient the choice ends with, when it is a permanent); the asker is the controller of the recipient at that step. (7) **`keepsDamage`.** `rules/statics.ts` `keepsDamage(state, obj)` is read in `afterDiscard`: the damage marked on the creature, and the memory that a source with deathtouch dealt it damage (which goes with the damage), stay through the cleanup step; "until end of turn" effects still end (CR 514.2); lethal damage still kills (CR 704.5g), regeneration and leaving the battlefield still clear it. (8) **The agents.** Casual and greedy take the first option (prevention); the heuristic agent weighs the damage that reaches the player as life (1 a point) and the damage that a redirection puts on a permanent at half a point, then the most prevented, ties to the first; random picks among the options. (9) **The web.** The log line "Lightning Bolt's 3 damage to you is dealt to SYNTHETIC Ancient Adamantoise instead.", "Then: 3 damage to X" under the button of a choice that changes the recipient (and "Then: 0 damage" when nothing is left), and the words of the two abilities from the AST (`game/redirect-text.ts`). (10) **Fixtures and soak.** `cards/fixtures/synthetic-adamantoise.ts` plays the card with its real wording (type line, mana cost and Oracle text of the request file; 6/8 invented); `packages/ai/test/helpers.ts` keeps it out of the generic pools and has the deck style `adamantoise`.
- Alternatives: The redirect as a shield plus a second damage event: rejected (prevention is not replacement, and the results of CR 120.3 would be those of another source). A redirection that is a static ability: rejected, CR 614.1a makes "instead" a replacement effect (the proposal's `Replacement`), and the parser's segmenter routes a line with "would" and "instead" to the replacement family. A fixed order (redirect first, or the shields of the first recipient first): rejected by the owner. Always asking when two or more effects apply: rejected in D-191. The tracked shields limited to the ones that apply at the start: a wrong "the order cannot matter" when a shield of the creature becomes applicable.
- Consequences: `ENGINE_VERSION` 45 (a game with an Adamantoise redirects damage, asks a question that D-191 never asked, and keeps damage through a turn; a game with no redirection plays as at 44: the precon fingerprint of `tools/perf/precon-digest.ts` is identical at version 44 before and after this change, and differs at 45 only through the version in the state). Ancient Adamantoise is supported through the grammar (D-193) and has no hand-written route. Limits, also in `docs/ROADMAP.md`: a redirect to another player's creature and one to a recipient controlled by another player are refused (`validate-redirect.ts`); only a creature face redirects (CR 614.9 also names planeswalkers and battles); the engine redirects damage dealt to a planeswalker or a battle the controller has (the filter is "permanents you control") and to a creature, never to a land or an artifact that is not a creature, as damage is not dealt to them; combat damage is simulated one event after another on the state the batch began with plus the events before it, so an Adamantoise that has taken lethal damage in the batch is still a legal recipient for the rest of it (the damage is simultaneous, CR 510.2, and the creature dies at the next state-based check); the rider of a mana ability takes the default order, as in D-191; rulings that could change a point: whether a second Adamantoise redirects what the first redirected (CR 614.5 and 616.1f say yes, once each), and whether damage marked on it that is lethal when a turn begins kills it at once (CR 704.5g says yes, at the next check). Tests: `scenario-xx-damage-redirect.test.ts` (the only effect, damage to the player, to another permanent, to a planeswalker, to the Adamantoise itself, to the opponent and its creatures, a pain land rider, lifelink, infect, wither, deathtouch, commander, combat with blockers, a fight, a shield on the player, on the creature and on both, two Adamantoises, the creature leaving the battlefield and losing its abilities, damage that stays across turns and is lethal, the log replaying), `damage-order.test.ts`, `ast-redirect-validate.test.ts`; AI: `damage-order-agents.test.ts`, `adamantoise-games.test.ts`; web: `redirect-text.test.ts`.

## D-193: The parser reads Ancient Adamantoise: "All damage that would be dealt to you and other permanents you control is dealt to ~ instead." and "Damage isn't removed from ~ during cleanup steps." (2026-11-02)
- Context: D-192 gave the engine the redirection and `keepsDamage`; the rest was the grammar. At parser 47 the card's two lines were `unrecognised`, closest rule `none` (the owner's request file); the other lines of the card (Vigilance, ward {3}, the dies trigger that exiles it and makes ten tapped Treasures) already read. The card is in the acceptance names for the owner's `pnpm corpus:extract`; it is not in the golden corpus.
- Decision: Stage P43. (1) **`replacement.redirect-damage`** (`rules/replacement/adamantoise.ts`): "All damage that would be dealt to <recipients> is dealt to ~ instead." with the recipients "you", "other <permanents> you control" or "you and other <permanents> you control" (the group is a `noun.plain-permanents` phrase of the controller's own, after the word "other"); the line goes to the replacement family because the segmenter sends a line with " would " and " instead" there. It lowers (`lower/adamantoise.ts`, called from `lower`) to `redirectDamage` and only on a creature face (the engine refuses it on another, so a card with it elsewhere is flagged `notRunnable`, never run). Not read: damage dealt by something, combat damage only, "the next 3", "target", another creature than `~`, another controller, a condition, a second part, the singular, "another permanent". (2) **`static.keeps-damage`** (`rules/static/adamantoise.ts`): "Damage isn't removed from ~ during cleanup steps." (both apostrophes); lowered to `keepsDamage`; not read: another permanent, "during the cleanup step", other steps, a duration, a condition, a second part. Both rules have `examples` and `rejects`, are listed in the stable rule ids test and have an embedding in the registry meta test.
- Alternatives: A static rule for the redirection: not reached, the segmenter routes the line to the replacement family. The recipients as a fixed phrase "you and other permanents you control": rejected, the rule is general over the group (any plural phrase of the controller's own) and over "you" alone or the group alone.
- Consequences: Ancient Adamantoise reads completely and passes `validateCard` (parser version 48); its parsed abilities equal the engine fixture's (`parser-p43.test.ts`). Golden corpus: see the numbers in `docs/STATUS.md`. Tests: `parser-p43.test.ts` (the real wording as nodes, the recipients, the refused lines, a non-creature face), `parser-p43-needs.test.ts` (each missing feature named), `convert-grammar-engine-p43.test.ts` (the parsed card played through `applyAction`: the redirect, the question, the damage that stays). The per-card status is in `docs/proposals/korvold-deck-analysis.md`.

## D-194: Voting (CR 701.38): "starting with you, each player votes for profit or security", engine, for Emissary Green (2026-11-02)
- Context: Emissary Green of the owner's Korvold deck: "Whenever Emissary Green attacks, starting with you, each player votes for profit or security. You create a number of Treasure tokens equal to twice the number of profit votes. Put a number of +1/+1 counters on each creature you control equal to the number of security votes." (the owner's request file of 2026-10-29; the file gives no power or toughness, so the SYNTHETIC fixture's 3/4 is invented). The playbook calls voting a subsystem (S): players other than the controller choose in the middle of a resolution. `docs/proposals/voting.md` recommended building one effect and one amount on the machinery that already exists, and the owner approved all the Korvold slices after the subsystems were presented to them (2026-11-02). Built as the proposal says; it is a P-sized change in practice, as the proposal itself noted. The CR text was read in the repository (`pnpm rule 701.38`: 701.38a to 701.38d). The official rulings could not be read (Scryfall is not reachable from the sandbox): nothing below rests on one; the points a ruling could change are under Limits.
- Decision: (1) **The effect `vote { options: string[], startingWith: 'you' }`** (CR 701.38a, 701.38b): two to eight distinct non-empty words with no rules meaning, each connected to an effect the rest of the text gives; `startingWith` is `you`, the only wording the engine reads. `validateCard` checks the counts, the words and the starting player. (2) **The amount `votesFor { option }`**: how many players voted for that option in the latest `vote` of the same resolution; 0 when nobody did. `validateCard` refuses it with no `vote` before it in the same sequence and for an option that vote does not offer (`Scope.voteOptions`, set after a `vote` child of a sequence, as `thisWay` is). The count of Treasure tokens is `multiple { factor: 2, of: votesFor profit }` and the counters are `addCounters` over `each` creature the controller controls with `votesFor security`; both existing nodes, no change to them. (3) **The run.** The effect becomes an instruction `vote { options, cast }` in the queue (`rules/vote.ts`): the next voter is the first player still in the game, in turn order from the controller of the spell or ability (`seatsInOrder`, CR 701.38a), who is not in `cast`; a `chooseOption` decision (`purpose: 'vote'`, the options as the card words them, asked of that player) pauses the resolution, and the answer (`rules/vote-answer.ts`, `answerResolutionVote`, called from `api.ts`) adds `{ seat, option }` to `cast` and goes on. When everyone has voted the instruction ends and the tally is written to `ResolutionContext.votes` (`StepOutcome.votes`), which `amountOf` reads for `votesFor`; a second `vote` in one resolution replaces it. The shape is that of `chooseOne` (D-175) and of the other answers kept on the instruction at the head of the queue. (4) **Public information.** A vote is public as it is cast: the decision carries `vote: { controller, cast }` (the votes so far, in order, and who controls the effect) and each vote is logged as an `optionChosen` event of purpose `vote` with the voter's seat and the option. The decision is only visible to the voter (`getView.pending`), as every decision is; `decidingSeat` is public. (5) **No new dialog kind and no new action kind.** The decision is a `ChooseOptionDecision` and the answer is the existing `chooseOption` action; refused unless the option is one of the offered and the seat is the voter's. (6) **The loop is written over the seats of the game**, in turn order, skipping a player who has lost, so the multiplayer work does not redo it; tested on a three-seat state built from the two-seat scenario. (7) **The agents.** `CasualAgent` and `GreedyAgent` (`casual-vote.ts`): the player who controls the effect votes for the first option the card lists; any other player votes for the option with the fewest votes so far, the later one on a tie (with two options, the one the controller did not choose): a rule that needs no knowledge of what the options do, which the decision does not say (CR 701.38b), always legal, deterministic. `HeuristicAgent` (`heuristic-vote.ts`): on its determinized sample it casts each option through `applyAction`, lets the players still to vote answer as the casual agent does, plays on until the vote is over and scores the board with the evaluator from its own seat; the best score wins, ties to the first option; the same rule serves the controller (best for it) and the others (best for them, which is the worst for the controller); with no sample, or when no candidate runs, the casual answer stands. `RandomLegalAgent` picks among the options. This was the open question of the proposal ("the board evaluator on the two outcomes, or simply the second option"); the owner can change the policy. (8) **The web** reuses the named-option dialog (`NamedOptionDialog`): the title is the source, the prompt is "Vote for profit or security." followed by the votes already cast ("Opponent voted for profit."), one button for each option with a capital, no way out; the log says "You vote for profit (Emissary Green)." and "Opponent votes for security (Emissary Green)." (CR 701.38a); the words of the effect ("Starting with you, each player votes for profit or security") and of the amount ("the number of profit votes") are in `ui/decisions/ability-label.ts` and `game/amount-text.ts`. (9) **Fixtures and soak.** `cards/fixtures/synthetic-vote.ts` has SYNTHETIC Emissary Green with the real wording and SYNTHETIC Ballot Rite (three options and an effect against the opponent, to test what Emissary's two options cannot); `packages/ai/test/helpers.ts` keeps them out of the generic pools and has the deck style `vote`.
- Alternatives: A vote that is a `chooseOption` of the controller only: rejected by the proposal (the other player's vote changes the result, the card would be played wrongly). The tally stored on the object or in the game state: not needed, no text reads a vote after its resolution, and the resolution is where `thisWay` and `lifeLost` already live. One decision for all the voters at once: rejected, the votes are made in turn order and public (CR 701.38a). A fixed policy for the AI (always the second option): rejected for the heuristic agent, which can read the outcome; kept in a simple form for the casual agent. A Playwright test: not added, the dialog kind is the existing one (named options), covered by a render test of the vote, the log line and the prompt.
- Consequences: `ENGINE_VERSION` 46 (a game with a vote asks a question no earlier game asked; a game with no vote plays as at 45: the precon fingerprint of `tools/perf/precon-digest.ts` is identical before and after at the same version, and `derive-bench` does not regress). The derive digests are recorded again for the version. Emissary Green is supported through the grammar (D-195) and has no hand-written route. Limits, also in `docs/ROADMAP.md`: one vote for each player (CR 701.38d, a player with several votes, is not built, and the parser does not read a card that gives them); the vote starts with the controller (a card that starts with another player is not read); the options are words (a vote for objects or players, "each player votes for a creature", is not built); the tally lives for the resolution of the one spell or ability (a later spell cannot ask what was voted); the casual agent's rule and the heuristic agent's simulation assume the other voters answer as the casual agent does, which is a guess about the other voter, not a model of it. Rulings that could change a point (unreadable): whether "starting with you" is the controller or the active player when they differ (this engine: the controller, as "you" is), and what happens to a vote when a voter leaves the game in the middle of it (this engine: they are skipped). Tests: `scenario-xx-vote.test.ts` (the order, who is asked, the public votes, the refusal of another seat and of a word that is not an option, the log, ties and the tally, a spell controlled by the second seat, three seats and a player who has lost, Emissary Green's profit, security and split votes, no trigger without an attack, replay and determinism), `ast-vote-validate.test.ts`, `ast-references-validate.test.ts` (the amount is listed); AI: `vote-agents.test.ts` (every agent answers legally, the casual rule, the heuristic agent's choice read apart from the agent), `vote-games.test.ts` (the `vote` style, every agent kind, a sample for the heuristic agent, the rules of the slice restated from the events); web: `vote-text.test.ts`, `vote-render.test.tsx`. Mutation-checked (the vote and validation tests, one change at a time): the first voter being seat 0 instead of the controller fails 1 test, no tally 14, `votesFor` reading 0 14, the tally not kept in the resolution 14, a tally merged with the earlier vote's instead of replacing it 1, a decision that hides the votes cast 4, the vote not logged 1, a player who has lost still voting 2, an amount without its factor of two 4, `votesFor` accepted with no vote before it or for an option the vote does not offer 1 each; the check of the option in `api.ts` is redundant with the one in `answerResolutionVote` (removing it changes nothing, an equivalent mutant). The casual rule (ties, the controller's first option), the heuristic choice (worst option wins) and the grammar (a pronoun or a capitalised word as an option) fail 1 to 3 tests each.

## D-195: The parser reads Emissary Green: "starting with you, each player votes for A or B", "the number of A votes", "You create a number of Treasure tokens equal to ...", "Put a number of +1/+1 counters on each creature you control equal to ..." (2026-11-02)
- Context: D-194 gave the engine the vote and the amount; the rest was the grammar. At parser 48 the card's trigger was `unrecognised` at "starting with you, each player votes ...", slot `effect`, closest rule `ability.triggered` (the owner's request file); the two sentences after it were not read either (`token.predefined` stopped at "number of" after "You create a", and no counters rule read "a number of"). The card is in the acceptance names for the owner's `pnpm corpus:extract`; it is not in the golden corpus.
- Decision: Stage P44. (1) **`effect.vote`** (`rules/effect/vote.ts`): "starting with you, each player votes for <word>, <word> or <word>" (two to eight lowercase words, with or without the comma before "or"); the clause verb `vote` has the options as an `IrChoiceArg` of kind `option` (the same node as "As ~ enters, choose Khans or Dragons"); `lower/korvold.ts` `VOTE` lowers it to the engine's `vote` with `startingWith: 'you'` (`effect:vote`). Not read: another starting player, "each opponent votes", "secretly", objects or names as options (capitals, "a creature"), "may vote", a vote that is one option, words after the list. (2) **The amount atom `votes`** (`rules/amount/votes.ts`): "the number of profit votes", an atom of the value family, so "equal to the number of profit votes", "equal to twice the number of profit votes" and a sum or half of them read through `amount.equal-to` (its examples and rejects have the new phrases); the option is one lowercase word that is not "your", "all", "total", "each", "extra" and the like; lowered to `votesFor` (`amount:votesFor`). The grammar does not check the order (a count of votes with no vote before it, or of an option the vote does not offer): `validateCard` refuses it, so such a card is flagged unsupported and never run. (3) **`token.number-of` as the object of "you create"** (`effect.player`'s `createAction`): "You create a number of Treasure tokens equal to ..." (before, only the imperative "Create a number of ..." read it; the other players the verb is said of, "its controller creates", take it too). (4) **`effect.add-counters-number-of`** (`rules/effect/counters.ts`): "Put a number of +1/+1 counters on <operands> equal to <amount>", the same operands as `effect.add-counters`, the count the amount after "equal to"; lowered by the existing `addCounters`. Both new rules have `examples` and `rejects`, are listed in the stable rule ids test and need no special embedding in the registry meta test.
- Alternatives: A rule that reads the whole card or the whole three sentences: rejected, each piece is general (the vote, the votes, the "number of" tokens and counters). A check in the lowering that the votes come after a vote with that option: the engine's validation already refuses it with the same words, and a second check would drift; the engine's refusal is tested through the importer (`convert-grammar-engine-p44.test.ts`).
- Consequences: Emissary Green reads completely and passes `validateCard` (parser version 49); its parsed abilities equal the engine fixture's (`convert-grammar-engine-p44.test.ts`). Golden corpus: only the version moved (the snapshot is unchanged otherwise): training 162 of 192, hold-out 52 of 61 (a gap of 0.8 points). Tests: the rules' own examples and rejects in the registry meta tests, `convert-grammar-engine-p44.test.ts` (the parsed card played through `applyAction`: the votes, the Treasures, the counters, a three-option vote worded the same way, the refused lines), `parser-p44-needs.test.ts` (each missing feature named, a blocked line leaves no ability). The per-card status is in `docs/proposals/korvold-deck-analysis.md`.

## D-196: The Ring tempts you (CR 701.54), engine, for There and Back Again (2026-11-02)
