- Context: Slice 8c of the owner's Korvold deck is the Ring (`docs/design/the-ring.md`, moved from `docs/proposals/` as implemented; the owner approved all the Korvold slices and the proposals were presented to them, and the proposal's own recommendation, to swap the card out, was not taken) and its one card, There and Back Again: chapter I "Up to one target creature can't block for as long as you control this Saga. The Ring tempts you." (the owner's request file of 2026-10-29). The CR text was read in the repository (`pnpm rule 701.54`, `701.54a` to `701.54e`, `509.1b`, `509.3d`, `509.1h`, `603.7`, `611.2b`, `704.5j`, `400.7`, `110.2`); the official rulings could not be read (Scryfall is not reachable from the sandbox), so no behaviour below rests on one. Where the task text and the CR differed on the words of the levels, the CR decides: the third ability is "Whenever your Ring-bearer becomes blocked by a creature, the blocking creature's controller sacrifices it at end of combat" (CR 701.54c).
- Decision: (1) **State.** `SeatState.ring?: { tempted: number }` is the emblem named The Ring (CR 701.54c): a record on the seat, not an object (the engine has no emblem objects and nothing reads an emblem's characteristics), present from the first time the Ring tempts the player. `GameObject.ringBearer?: SeatId` is the designation (CR 701.54b: not a copiable value, so it is a field of the object, not a characteristic). The proposal wrote `true`; the value is the player whose Ring-bearer it is because CR 701.54a ends the designation when another player gains control of it and a creature that goes back to its first controller must not become their Ring-bearer again (CR 701.54e: "on the battlefield under your control and has the designation"). A new object after any zone change has none (CR 400.7: `moveOne` builds the object field by field). `rules/ring-bearer.ts` (a leaf, so `derive` can read it) has `ringLevel`, `isRingBearerOf`, `ringBearerOf`, `ringBearerSeat`. (2) **The effect `ringTempts`** (a keyword action, no operand: "you"), run as the instruction `ringTempts { chosen }` (`rules/ring.ts`, `runRingTempts`): with two or more creatures the controller answers a `choosePermanent` decision of the new purpose `ringBearer` (exactly one of the creatures they control, as `derive` types them; the instruction stays at the head and nothing has changed until the answer, as `fightPairs` does); with one it is chosen at once and nothing is asked; with none only the count moves (CR 701.54d). Then, at once: the emblem if there was none, the count one more, the designation of the player's earlier Ring-bearer gone (the same creature chosen again stays it, with no loss), the designation on the new one, and the event `ringTempted { seat, times, bearer, first }` (a lost designation is `ringBearerLost`). (3) **Level 1, "Your Ring-bearer is legendary and can't be blocked by creatures with greater power"**: `derive.finish` adds the supertype legendary in layer 4 (an ability of the emblem, so no loss of abilities of the creature removes it, and a static ability that reads supertypes sees it) and `combat-legality.ts` `evades` treats a creature with greater power than the attacking Ring-bearer, as derived as blockers are declared, as unable to block it (CR 509.1b; the same place as skulk). (4) **Levels 2 to 4 are inherent abilities of the Ring**, found like those of the monarch (`rules/triggers.ts`, `findRingTriggers`): no source, controlled by the player (`StackData.inherent` is `ringLoot`, `ringBlocked` or `ringDamage`, shown as "The Ring" with the rule's own text: `rules/inherent.ts`). Two or more times: when the Ring-bearer is among the attackers declared, "draw a card, then discard a card" (the player chooses the discard). Three or more: for each creature declared as a blocker of the Ring-bearer (CR 509.3d: once for each creature that blocks it; the blocker is the subject), the engine's effect `delayedSacrifice` creates a delayed triggered ability about that creature that, as the next end of combat step begins, makes its controller sacrifice it (the new `sacrifice { byController }`: each permanent is sacrificed by the player who controls it as the effect resolves; a creature that has left is skipped, CR 603.7c). Four or more: when the Ring-bearer deals combat damage to a player (damage prevented entirely has no event and triggers nothing, CR 603.2g), each opponent loses 3 life. The level is read after the events, so a tempt and an attack in one step see the new level. (5) **The designation ends with control** (`endLostRingBearers`, first in the state-based actions after `endLostControlEffects`, D-189): a Ring-bearer whose controller is no longer the player it is the Ring-bearer of loses the designation for good, with the event `ringBearerLost`; it does not come back when control does. The designation is also part of the invariants (`checkInvariants`: on the battlefield, of a player the Ring tempted, one at most for a player). (6) **"Whenever the Ring tempts you"** is the trigger `ringTempted` (once for each tempt, even with no creature to choose, CR 701.54d); **"if you control your Ring-bearer"** is the condition `controlsRingBearer` (CR 701.54e; not for a static ability). (7) **"For as long as you control this Saga"**: `restrict` takes the duration `forAsLongAsYouControlThis` (CR 611.2b), with the end `whileControlling` of D-189 (`endOf` is shared with `gainControl`): the effect does nothing when the permanent with the ability is not on the battlefield under its controller's control as it would begin, and otherwise ends for good as that stops being so (so it also ends if the Saga changes controller); `validateCard` allows it in the ability of a permanent only. `delayedSacrifice` and the view are described in `docs/MECHANICS.md`; `validateCard` refuses `delayedSacrifice` in a card (the engine's own effect) and `sacrifice.byController` with `player` or a `choose` selector. (8) **Views and the DSL.** `ObjectView.ringBearer?: SeatId` and `SeatView.ringTempted?: number` are public (the Ring and the designation are public information; there is no hidden information in this slice). The scenario DSL has `seat.ring(n)`, `{ ringBearer: true }` on a permanent, `expect.ringLevel` and `expect.ringBearer`.
- Alternatives: The Ring as an object of the command zone: rejected by the proposal (a new object kind with no other use). The designation as `true` on the object: rejected for the reason above (the player must be remembered). The designation stored on the seat (`ring.bearer: ObjectId`): rejected, it would outlive the object it names (a new object after a zone change has a new id, but the invariant and the view would have to check it) and `derive` would have to search the seats; the object field is dropped with the object. Ending the designation inside `controllerOf`: rejected for the reason D-189 gave for durations (a read that depends on state must not mutate it). A general `delayedTrigger` that may sacrifice an object: rejected, its validator allows only player-only effects with fixed amounts because the spell that creates it is gone; the Ring's ability names the blocker, which is the ability's own subject, so the engine's own effect (`delayedSacrifice`, refused in a card) is the smaller change. `sacrifice.byController` is general: "its controller sacrifices it". Letting the heuristic agent choose the Ring-bearer by simulation: not built, the choice has one decision and a static score is enough (see the agents below).
- Consequences: `ENGINE_VERSION` 47: the state hash covers the new fields, but a game with no Ring plays as at 46 (the precon fingerprint of `tools/perf/precon-digest.ts`, 10 seeded games, is identical before and after at the same version, `derive-bench` does not regress), and the derive digests are recorded again for the version and the new SYNTHETIC cards. There and Back Again is supported through the grammar (D-197) and has no hand-written route; the SYNTHETIC fixture (`synthetic-ring.ts`) has the real wording and invents nothing (a Saga has no power or toughness and Smaug's 6/6, flying, haste and death trigger are in the card's text); the other fixtures (a rite, a watcher, an oath) are invented and say so. Agents: the casual and greedy agents choose the creature with the most power (the first the engine lists on a tie), the heuristic agent scores each creature by power, half the toughness, the keywords that help it connect or survive (flying, menace, trample, first and double strike, deathtouch, lifelink, indestructible, haste, vigilance), three quarters for each untapped opposing creature with greater power (which can no longer block it) and a little less when it cannot attack yet; the random agent picks one. The web reuses the permanent panel (no new dialog kind, so no browser test): "The Ring tempts you: choose your Ring-bearer, a creature you control, for ...", the badge "Ring-bearer" on the chosen creature, a "Ring-bearer" flag on the tile, a "Ring N" chip on the player's strip whose tooltip lists the four lines and which are on, the log lines "The Ring tempts you (the first time). Grizzly Bears becomes your Ring-bearer." and "... is no longer your Ring-bearer.", and the words of the Ring's abilities on the stack and in the trigger order panel. Limits (also in `docs/ROADMAP.md`): "the Ring tempts you" only; no card text for "target Ring-bearer" or "your Ring-bearer" as the subject of an effect or a trigger (`ObjectFilter` has no `ringBearer` field: no card of the list needs it); the Ring-bearer must be a creature when chosen but keeps the designation if it stops being one (CR 701.54e says only "on the battlefield under your control"); an emblem is a record of the seat, so nothing can destroy, copy or count it; with a third seat "each opponent" is read for all, as the engine already does; no official ruling could be read. Tests: `test/scenario-xx-ring.test.ts` (the question and its answers, one creature, none, the second tempt, the opponent's own Ring, each level, the loss of the designation by death and by control, the condition, replay and hash, the Saga's three chapters and the Smaug trigger), `test/ast-ring-validate.test.ts`, and the soak `packages/ai/test/ring-games.test.ts` (deck style `ring`) with `ring-agents.test.ts`. Mutation checks (a scratch copy of each file, then restored): no end of the designation when control changes, the greater-power check removed, the blocked ability at level 2, `byController` ignored, the legendary supertype removed and the drain at level 3 each fail the scenario tests.

## D-197: The parser reads There and Back Again: "The Ring tempts you.", "Whenever the Ring tempts you", "if you control your Ring-bearer", "... can't block for as long as you control ~", and a named legendary token (2026-11-02)
- Context: D-196 gave the engine the Ring; the rest was the grammar. At parser 49 the card's chapter I stopped at "can't block for as long as you control ~. The Ring tempts you." (closest rule `effect.gain-keyword-targets`, slot `noun`) and chapter III at "Smaug, a legendary 6/6 red Dragon creature token with flying, haste, and ..." (closest rule `effect.create-token`, slot `token`), from the owner's request file; chapter II (Search for a Mountain) already read. The card is in the acceptance names for the owner's `pnpm corpus:extract`; it is not in the golden corpus.
- Decision: Stage P45. (1) **`effect.ring-tempts`** (`rules/effect/ring.ts`): "the Ring tempts you", lowered as `ringTempts` (`lower/korvold.ts`, `effect:ringTempts`); not read: another player, "twice". (2) **`trigger.ring-tempts`** (`rules/trigger/korvold.ts`): "the Ring tempts you" as the event of "Whenever ...", lowered as `ringTempted` (`trigger:ringTempted`). (3) **`condition.ring-bearer`** (`rules/condition/korvold.ts`): "you control your Ring-bearer", lowered as `controlsRingBearer` (`condition:controlsRingBearer`); it reads as the intervening "if" of a triggered ability. Not read: "a Ring-bearer", another player's, a negation. (4) **`effect.restrict-while-controlling`** (`rules/effect/restrict.ts`): "up to one target creature can't block for as long as you control ~" (also "can't be blocked", and a target with no "up to"), as the same clause verb `restrict` with the IR duration `whileYouControlSelf` (D-190); `lower/continuous.ts` `RESTRICT` lowers it to `restrict` with the duration `forAsLongAsYouControlThis` (`duration:forAsLongAsYouControlThis`, now a duration kind of the registry). "Up to one" is the target slot with `min: 0`. Not read: the plural, another restriction, another duration ("for as long as you control a Dragon", "remains tapped"). (5) **`token.named-legendary`** (`rules/token/index.ts`): "Smaug, a legendary 6/6 red Dragon creature token with flying, haste, and \"When Smaug dies, create fourteen Treasure tokens.\"": a token with a name of its own that the effect gives (CR 111.4) and the supertype legendary (`IrToken.legendary`, lowered into `TokenDefinition.supertypes`, CR 205.4); one token ("a"); the name inside the quotes is the token (read as `~`, `QuotedOptions.self`). The "with" part also reads a list of keywords with an ability in quotes as the last item (`TOKEN_WITH` of every token: "with flying, haste, and \"...\"", at least two keywords with the commas of the list, none repeated), which the other tokens now read too. (6) Everything else of the card reads with what existed: the chapter symbols, "up to one target creature", the sentence after it, the search for a Mountain and the saga layout.
- Alternatives: Reading "for as long as you control ~" as a generic duration clause for every verb: rejected, as for D-190 (only these verbs have an engine node for it). A token rule for "Smaug" by name: rejected (no card names in the grammar; the rule reads any named legendary token). Reading the name as the token's creature types: no, CR 111.4 and D-184. Making the list "A, B, and \"...\"" a keyword-list rule shared with the static grants: not needed, only tokens say it.
- Consequences: There and Back Again reads completely and passes `validateCard` (parser version 50); its parsed abilities equal the engine fixture's (`convert-grammar-engine-p45.test.ts`). Golden corpus: no card changed status or AST, only the version moved (training 162 of 192, hold-out 52 of 61, acceptance 1 of 1: a gap of 0.8 points). Limits: see D-196 and `docs/ROADMAP.md`. Tests: the rules' own examples and rejects (registry meta tests), `parser-p45.test.ts` (the real chapters as nodes, each rule's siblings and refused lines), `parser-p45-needs.test.ts` (each missing feature named, a blocked line leaves no ability), `convert-grammar-engine-p45.test.ts` (the parsed Saga played through `applyAction`, the parsed Ring cards), and the web wording (`apps/web/test/ring-text.test.ts`, `ring-render.test.tsx`).

## D-198: A legendary card named "<Given name> <Family name>" is its given name in its own Oracle text (2026-11-03)
- Context: The owner's first real run of `pnpm corpus:decks` on the Korvold deck (`decks/korvold.txt`, `reports/decks.md`) found one card the engine did not read: Lobelia Sackville-Baggins, whose real text says "When Lobelia enters, ..." where the SYNTHETIC test text of slice 4 (D-180) said "When ~ enters". Normalization (stage P32, D-147) shortened a legendary name only at the first comma or before " the ", so "Lobelia" was left as a word and no rule read the trigger. This is the gap between a SYNTHETIC copy of a card's wording and the real Oracle text that the acceptance extraction exists to catch; nothing else of the 42 acceptance cards was affected.
- Decision: Stage P46, `selfNames` in `packages/cards/src/convert/parser/normalize.ts`: for a legendary card with no comma and no " the " in its name, the first word is also a name of the card when the name has two or more words, the first word is capitalized, at least three letters, no possessive, and not a type of permanent (the creature types of the engine's table, CR 205.3m, and a short list of land, artifact, enchantment and other kinds, `NOT_A_GIVEN_NAME`), and the next word is capitalized too (so "Gideon of the Trials" and "Liliana of the Veil" are titles, not given names). The replacement is of the whole capitalized word, after the longer names. `PARSER_VERSION` 51; the golden corpus was regenerated (the owner's 41 new acceptance cards read with their real text: 42 of 42 acceptance cards supported; training 162 of 192 and hold-out 52 of 61, unchanged).
- Alternatives: Naming the short name per card in a table: rejected (card-name data in code, and the next card with a given name would fail the same way). Replacing the first word of every legendary name: rejected, "Goblin Chieftain" or a planeswalker's subtype would turn ordinary words of the text into `~`. Reading the short name from the text ("When X enters" for the first capitalized word before a verb): rejected as a guess about the text rather than a fact about the name.
- Consequences: Lobelia reads completely at the real text. A legendary card whose first word is an ordinary capitalized word that is neither a creature type nor in the short list would have that word read as itself in its text; no card of the golden corpus does, and `pnpm coverage:cards --check` on the owner's bulk file is the real check for the rest. Tested in `parser-p46.test.ts` (the real text of Lobelia, the near misses).

## D-199: The player always sees an opponent's spell before it resolves; the card, its X and what it did are on screen (2026-11-04)
- Context: Three playtest issues. Issue 105: the opponent cast a board wipe and the player saw "everything vanish": `shouldStop` (A18, D-045, D-138) stops for an object of the opponent on the stack only when the player holds a relevant instant-speed action or the object is aimed at them or their permanents (D-138, `stopWhenTargeted`), so a spell with no target (Wrath-like) was passed for the player, and the log showed only "X dies." lines, since a spell that is not a permanent has no `resolved` event. Issue 82: to read the card that waits on the stack the player moved the pointer to the stack and back to the dock. Issue 107: an ability with an X on the stack did not say how much X was.
- Decision: (1) **Stop for opponent spells.** `StopSettings.stopForOpponentSpells`, default on, a checkbox "Stop for opponent spells" in Settings. With it on, `shouldStop` returns true while the top of the stack is a spell (no `ability` and no `abilitySource` in the view: a card, a copy, a permanent spell) of another player, so the player gets priority, reads it and presses Resolve; the stop applies on either turn, to "Pass turn" (`passTurnVerdict` ends there) and is overridden by nothing but Full Control being already a stop. It is the conservative choice: only spells, not the opponent's triggered or activated abilities (a trigger on every attack or an equip would stop the game constantly; those keep the D-138 rules: an instant to answer with, or aimed at the player). The auto-pass for everything else (own objects, the steps) is unchanged, and the setting off restores the exact old behaviour. SPEC 10 ("Resolutions pass automatically while they hold none") is not edited (it needs the owner's approval); this entry is the amendment until then. (2) **The highlight box shows the top of the stack.** `previewChoice` (`ui/board/resolve.ts`): a pinned card, else the hovered one while the viewer can see it, else the object on top of the stack, flagged "Top of the stack"; and an object that newly lands on top of the stack clears the hover (`store.ts` `apply`), so it takes the box even while the pointer rests on a card (a pin stays). The card image, rules text and details are those of the existing preview; no new component. (3) **X.** No engine change: the announced X is already in the view (`ObjectView.x`, D-103) for spells and for activated abilities, on the log lines "cast ... with X = 3" and "activates ... with X = 3", and as the "X = 3" badge on the stack item and the card face. `withAnnouncedX` (`game/amount-text.ts`) now writes it into the words that say X for an object on the stack: the stack item's words ("You draw X (3) cards") and the rules text of the preview ("Deals X (3) damage to any target.", "2X (6)"); the {X} of a cost stays, and a text that defines its own X ("where X is ...") is left alone (CR 107.3c). (4) **The log names what resolved.** `describeEvents` adds "<Spell> resolves." or "<Source>'s ability resolves." ahead of what the resolution did, on the controller's side, for a spell that is not a permanent and for any ability that left the stack (a permanent spell keeps its own `resolved` detail line; a countered or fizzled object and one still waiting for an answer get none). It is a main line when what followed shows in the log (the "dies", "goes to the graveyard" lines) and a detail line otherwise. `ENGINE_VERSION` is unchanged.
- Alternatives: Turning auto-pass off for all opponent objects or by default Full Control on the opponent's turn: rejected, far too many clicks (every Llanowar Elves, every trigger). Stopping only for spells that are not permanents (the ones that wipe boards): rejected, an unseen creature that arrives is the same complaint, and the player cannot tell from the stack in advance; the setting turns the stop off for whoever finds it too much. A thumbnail of the card inside the stack item: not done, the highlight box already is the card at full size and the issue named either place. Computing the current value of a defined X ("where X is the number of Dragons you control") for the stack: needs the engine's amount evaluation in the view (a public API change with its own version bump); the words already carry the definition, the value is in ROADMAP. A highlight on the permanents an effect touched: no animation layer exists to hang it on, so it is deferred (ROADMAP); the log names them.
- Consequences: Every opponent spell costs the player one click (Resolve), including creature spells; `e2e/stack-legibility.e2e.ts` and the unit tests pin the stop, the preview and the log. Tests that assumed an opponent spell passes unseen (`should-stop.test.ts`, `pass-turn.test.ts`, the main-phase search of `dnd-render.test.tsx`) now say so with the setting off or look for the player's own turn. The e2e tests that press the primary button until a state arrives are unaffected (the button says Resolve).

## D-200: Planeswalkers, engine: the model, loyalty abilities, the target "player or planeswalker", the combat edges and the commander keyword (2026-11-04)
- Context: The owner approved the whole planeswalker subsystem of `docs/proposals/planeswalkers.md` (now `docs/design/planeswalkers.md`) on 2026-11-04 ("do it all at once ... a PR with full support for planeswalkers") and accepted all ten recommendations of its section 7 (emblems moved into this work; the AI minimal; the chooser UI with rows first; one or a few `D-` entries for the whole work; Myriad and enter-attacking aimed at players only; trample over planeswalkers only if a card needs it). The planeswalker had existed since M2 as a type with loyalty counters, attacks and damage (D-043); what a real one has on top did not exist. The real texts are in the owner's golden corpus (`corpus-vraska-planeswalkers`: 23 planeswalkers and the cards of the Vraska deck that need them), and the grammar was driven from those lines.
- Decision: (1) **Loyalty abilities (CR 606).** A loyalty ability is an ordinary `activated` ability with the new cost kind `loyalty { change: number | 'x' }` (CR 606.2: "an activated ability with a loyalty symbol in its cost"), so the engine derives the property from the cost and nothing else carries a flag (`rules/loyalty.ts`). Legality (`rules/activate-legality.ts`): sorcery timing whatever the ability's `timing` says (CR 606.3), and no other loyalty ability of that permanent this turn, read from a `loyalty: true` mark that `finishActivation` writes into `state.turnLog.activated` (CR 606.3: "no player", so a stolen walker is held to the same count); the 606.6 refusal in `immediateRefusal` ("it has fewer than N loyalty counters"). Payment (`rules/activate-costs.ts`): the counters are put on or removed with the other costs that need no mana and no choice, `[0]` neither; `[-X]` makes X announced by the ordinary `chooseX` decision (`perX.loyalty`), at most the loyalty (`largestPayableX` over `costRefusal`). The validator (`checkLoyaltyAbility`): one symbol, `functionsIn` the battlefield, no `oncePerTurn` of its own, never `timing: 'instant'`, only on a planeswalker face or token, never granted, never a cost of a spell or a mana ability; an activated ability that adds mana with a loyalty cost is not a mana ability (CR 606.2, 605.1a). (2) **The model.** A planeswalker or battle token, and a token copy (also a copy of a permanent spell that resolves, CR 707.10f, and a permanent that enters as a copy), enters with its loyalty or defense counters (CR 306.5b, 310.4b: `createTokens`, `moveObject`); `TokenDefinition.loyalty` is validated, `tokenTypes` lists `planeswalker`. The planeswalker types are generated from CR 205.3j and the planeswalker types the applied bulletin adds (`pnpm planeswalker-types:generate`, `tools/creature-types/generate-planeswalker.ts`, 87 names) into `data/planeswalker-types.ts` and joined to `isNonCreatureSubtype`, so an effect that sets creature types leaves them alone (CR 205.3d). `ObjectView.printedLoyalty` (a card in a hand or a graveyard), `ObjectView.loyaltyUsed` (CR 606.3). (3) **The target `playerOrObject { player, filter }`** (the design's D3 option a): "target player or planeswalker", "target opponent or planeswalker"; the filter names planeswalkers, battles or both. A chosen target is a player or an object, so `dealDamage` and every selector read it unchanged; "that player or that planeswalker's controller" is the `all` selector of the target and `controllerOf` of the target (no new selector). Lavalanche reads with it. (4) **Combat edges (CR 506.4, 506.4c, 508.5).** An attacker of a planeswalker or battle records its defending player as it is declared (`AttackerState.defender`); a planeswalker removed from combat because its controller changed gets `targetGone` on its attackers (`combat-removal.ts`, `control-effects.ts`), and one that stopped being a planeswalker or battle is read at damage time (`defending.ts` `attackedTarget`): the creature stays in combat, its former defending player may block it, and unblocked it deals no combat damage. Tested with a stolen planeswalker, a planeswalker that loses its type, and a creature that is also a planeswalker (animated; summoning sickness, CR 302.6). (5) **`canBeCommander`** (CR 903.3, 113.6n): a keyword with no effect in play, like Partner, so a card with "~ can be your commander." validates; a planeswalker commander is cast from the command zone with the tax, comes back by CR 903.9, and deals commander damage only as a creature (tested).
- Alternatives: A new ability kind `loyalty` next to `activated`: rejected by the design (every reader of `kind === 'activated'` would miss it). `removeCounters` with `counter: 'loyalty'`: rejected (no `[0]`, no X, and CR 606.4 and 606.5 modifiers are about loyalty symbols). A defender recorded on every attacker: only the attackers of a permanent have one. The lazy check of the controller at damage time instead of `targetGone`: tried first, redundant with the mark and removed (a mutation check showed it was dead). Trample over planeswalkers (CR 702.19c) and Myriad or enter-attacking choosing a planeswalker (CR 508.4): not built, as the owner accepted (no card of the corpus needs them).
- Consequences: `ENGINE_VERSION` 48. A game with no planeswalker plays as at 47: `node tools/perf/precon-digest.ts` is identical before and after at the same version (the check was run with the version put back to 47 for it), and `derive-bench` does not regress. The derive digests are recorded again for the version and the new SYNTHETIC cards (`synthetic-planeswalkers.ts`). Limits: the ROADMAP section "Planeswalkers". Tests: `scenario-xx-loyalty`, `scenario-xx-planeswalker-model`, `scenario-xx-planeswalker-damage`, `scenario-xx-planeswalker-combat`, `scenario-xx-planeswalker-commander`, `ast-loyalty-validate`, `tools/creature-types/planeswalker-types.test.ts`; mutation checks on a scratch copy (each caught by those tests): the once-per-permanent mark ignored, sorcery timing dropped, the 606.6 check off by one, the `[0]` cost refused, a token that enters with no loyalty, the `targetGone` mark not written.

## D-201: Emblems (CR 114), Empower Jace (CR 701.71a) and the life total that becomes a number (CR 119.5), engine (2026-11-04)
- Context: Three of the big planeswalkers' ultimates make emblems (Elspeth, Sun's Champion, Gideon, Ally of Zendikar, Chandra, Torch of Defiance, Teferi, Hero of Dominaria, ...), two cards of the Vraska deck create a Jace token (Protege's Awakening "Empower Jace 6.", Keeper of the Quiet Hour "empower Jace 2."), and Vraska, Relic Seeker's ultimate is "Target player's life total becomes 1." The proposal put emblems in their own proposal at about 0.3; the owner asked for them in this work if a clean design exists with what is in the repository, and the command zone existed (commanders live there).
- Decision: (1) **Emblems.** The effect `createEmblem { abilities, text }` ("You get an emblem with \"...\""): the controller gets a new object in their command zone (`rules/emblem.ts`): `card: null`, a `token` record with the characteristics of CR 114.3 (nothing but a name) and the quoted abilities (static or triggered, at least one; `validateCard` refuses any other kind), `emblem: true`, owner and controller that player. It is no permanent (not on the battlefield) and the state-based action for tokens (CR 704.5d) leaves it alone (CR 114.5: it cannot be removed; no effect names it). Its static abilities are read with the permanents' in `derive-statics.ts` `buildIndex` (and its cost reductions, flash permissions) and its triggered ones in `triggers.ts` `graveyardTriggerCards` (now "objects outside the battlefield whose triggered abilities work there", the emblems added), so a trigger of an emblem goes on the stack like any other and its damage is dealt by the emblem. The event `emblemCreated`; `ObjectView.emblem` (`isToken` is false); the web shows it in the command zone strip with its text. The Ring (D-196) stays the record on the seat it is, as the task said: the monarch and the Ring are designations of the game, not emblems made by an effect. (2) **Empower Jace N** (CR 701.71a): the effect `empowerJace { amount }` (a positive number); `rules/empower.ts` creates the engine's blue Jace planeswalker token (`JACE_TOKEN` in `cards/tokens.ts`: loyalty 0, `[-1]: Surveil 1`, `[-3]: Draw a card.`) if the controller controls no Jace planeswalker token, chooses one (a `choosePermanent` decision of purpose `empowerJace`, asked only with two or more) and puts N loyalty counters on it, all in one resolution so no state-based action sees the token at 0 (CR 704.3). A Jace planeswalker card is not a token and does not count. (3) **`setLifeTotal { player, amount }`** (CR 119.5): the player gains or loses the difference, as the gain or loss it is (CR 119.9 triggers read them); nothing happens to a player who has the total already; a total that becomes a count is not read.
- Alternatives: Emblems as a record on the seat, like the Ring: rejected (a trigger of an emblem needs a source object, an anthem needs a timestamp and a controller, and a seat record per emblem would need all of that again). A new zone `emblem`: rejected (CR 114.2 says the command zone). Teferi, Temporal Archmage's emblem ("You may activate loyalty abilities of planeswalkers you control on any player's turn any time you could cast an instant") would need a static that changes the timing of loyalty abilities: not built, the card stays unsupported on that line (and on "Look at the top two cards ..."). Empower Jace as a special case of the token: rejected by the design (D6).
- Consequences: `ENGINE_VERSION` 48 (same version as D-200: one release). The command zone now holds objects that are no cards: `legal-actions` never offers one (`canCast` refuses `card: null`), `checkInvariants` passes with a commander and an emblem together (tested). A control-changing or leaving effect cannot reach an emblem; a Spark-like copy effect that copies a planeswalker gets loyalty counters as it enters (CR 306.5b). Tests: `scenario-xx-emblems` (anthem and trigger emblems, two emblems, the opponent's spells, the command zone with a commander, invariants, validation), `scenario-xx-empower-jace`, `scenario-xx-set-life`, and the real cards in `convert-grammar-engine-p47` (Elspeth's and Gideon's emblems, Protege's Awakening, Keeper of the Quiet Hour, Vraska's ultimate); mutation checks: the emblem exemption of CR 704.5d removed, its static abilities not read, its triggers not scanned, the Jace token never created.

## D-202: The parser reads the loyalty lines, the emblem, Empower Jace, "~ can be your commander." and the planeswalkers that become creatures (stage P47, 2026-11-04)
- Context: At parser 51 every loyalty line ("+1: ...", "−2: ...", "0: ...", "−X: ...") fell through the segmenter to `other` and was `unrecognised` with no closest rule (the proposal's probe), on a planeswalker and on a creature face. The real lines of the golden corpus (U+2212 for the minus, no brackets) were the work order.
- Decision: Stage P47. (1) **`cost.loyalty`** (`rules/cost/index.ts`): "+N", "−N" (U+2212; a hyphen-minus and an en dash too), "0", "−X", with or without the square brackets of the rules text; the segmenter (`segment.ts`) calls a line "activated" when it starts with a loyalty symbol and a colon, before the replacement test (a loyalty line whose effect says "would ... instead" is an ability, not a replacement). The lowering (`lower/activated.ts`) reads it as the cost of an ordinary activation only on a planeswalker face, once and alone (no second cost, no "Activate only" restriction: CR 606.3 has its own), with `ability:xCost` for "−X"; a loyalty ability with an `addMana` effect is activated, never a mana ability. A loyalty ability's body is read with the sentence of a triggered ability's body (`LOYALTY_SENTENCE`: "You may ...", "If you do, ...", reflexive), which the other activated abilities do not get (no golden card changed because of it). (2) **`keyword.can-be-commander`** ("~ can be your commander.") lowers to the engine's `canBeCommander`. (3) **`effect.get-emblem`**: `You get an emblem with "..."`; the quoted text is read as an ability of its own (static or triggered, "this emblem" read as `~`: `readQuotedAbility` with `statics`) and lowered by the late lowerers (`lower/late.ts` now has `static`), `lower/planeswalker.ts`. (4) **`effect.empower-jace`** ("Empower Jace 6", "empower Jace 2"; a number, not X, not 0), **`effect.life-total-becomes`** ("Target player's life total becomes 1"), **`effect.lead-becomes-creature`** ("Until end of turn, ~ becomes a 6/6 Human Soldier creature that's still a planeswalker.", with "with indestructible"), and the recipient "to him"/"to her"/"to ~" of `effect.prevent-all` ("Prevent all damage that would be dealt to him this turn."). (5) **`noun.player-or-planeswalker`** lowers to the engine's `playerOrObject` target, and `noun.each-permanent-of-player` with "or that planeswalker's controller" to the `all` selector (D-200); the D-180 reading as a player is gone.
- Alternatives: A loyalty prefix as a keyword-like ability kind of its own in the IR: rejected (the effect body is the shared grammar). Reading "him"/"her" everywhere as the card: only the recipient of the prevention shield, where the pronoun can only be the permanent itself. Stopping an emblem's quoted text at activated and triggered abilities (the existing quoted reader): rejected, the anthems of Elspeth and Gideon are static.
- Consequences: `PARSER_VERSION` 52. Golden corpus (the owner's extraction of 2026-11-04, 138 acceptance cards): acceptance 80 of 138 supported (73 before this work), training 162 of 192 and hold-out 52 of 61 unchanged (a gap of 0.8 points). Real cards that moved to supported: Garruk Wildspeaker, Jace Beleren, Elspeth, Sun's Champion, Gideon, Ally of Zendikar, Vraska, Relic Seeker, Protege's Awakening, Keeper of the Quiet Hour; Lavalanche stays supported with the real target. Still unsupported, each on the line that needs more than a planeswalker: Chandra, Torch of Defiance ("You may cast that card. If you don't, ..."), Teferi, Hero of Dominaria ("untap up to two lands": no untap that chooses), Teferi, Temporal Archmage (the emblem that changes the timing of loyalty abilities, and "Look at the top two cards ..., put one into your hand"), Vraska, Golgari Queen (the emblem's "that player loses the game"), Vraska, Scheming Gorgon (a granted triggered ability to a group), Gideon Jura ("creatures that player controls attack ~ if able"), Ugin, Liliana of the Veil, Jace the Mind Sculptor, Jace, Wielder of Mysteries, Narset, Nissa Who Shakes the World, Nahiri, Lord Windgrace, Tamiyo (Compleated and a hybrid Phyrexian symbol), and the flip walkers Garruk Relentless, Nissa, Vastwood Seer and Jace, Vryn's Prodigy (a transform with a planeswalker back face, and "exile ~, then return him transformed"); Theorist's Sanctum ("As ~ enters, you may behold a Jace": no enters replacement with a behold), Forge of Heroes ("Choose target commander that entered this turn ... a loyalty counter on it if it's a planeswalker"), Face Yourself (a copy of each creature) and Refute Destiny ("that's green or blue": no colour list on a noun) are the cards of the Vraska deck that stay, none of them for lack of planeswalkers. Tests: `parser-p47.test.ts` (the real lines, the signs and brackets, the refused shapes, the registry examples and rejects), `convert-grammar-engine-p47.test.ts` (the real cards played in the engine).

## D-203: The agents and the web for planeswalkers (2026-11-04)
- Context: The AI decks are the precons and the arena decks (no planeswalker in any), and the human plays the planeswalkers, so the agents mostly attack and answer the human's; the owner chose the minimal AI (the proposal's D5) and the chooser with loyalty rows (D4 a).
- Decision: (1) **Agents** (`packages/ai/src/casual-loyalty.ts`): a planeswalker of the agent's is used once a turn, in a main phase (the engine lists the options only then and only when payable). A candidate leaves the walker with at least 1 loyalty, or is an ultimate (a cost of 6 or more); the choice: an ultimate, else a minus ability with a hostile target while the walker keeps at least 2, else the highest plus, else a zero, else a minus that keeps 2; "[-X]" is left unused. The casual agent does it in `chooseActivation` (the heuristic agent reaches it through the casual rules for what is left, `heuristic-main.ts` item 4), the greedy agent after its spells (reason `loyalty`), the random agent plays any legal option. Attack: when the safe attackers' power covers an opposing planeswalker's loyalty (and the attack is not lethal at the player), the strongest of them are sent at it and the rest at the player (`aimAtPlaneswalkers`); the heuristic agent already built that candidate. Defence: the block rules read every attacker listed, so a good block of an attacker at the agent's planeswalker is made as for any attacker; no chump block for a planeswalker. The `choosePermanent` purpose `empowerJace` takes the default (the first Jace token). (2) **Web**: the cost words ("+1", "−2" with U+2212, "0", "−X"); the chooser always opens for a loyalty ability, even the only one, so its cost is read; the corner of a planeswalker card in a hand or graveyard shows its printed loyalty; a "used" flag on a tile while a loyalty ability was activated this turn; the emblem in the command zone strip (its text as the title); the words of the new effects and of "target player or planeswalker"; the log line "You get an emblem." The attack at a planeswalker needed no new UI. A hidden SYNTHETIC deck `synthetic-planeswalkers` and `e2e/planeswalkers.e2e.ts`. (3) **Soak**: the deck style `planeswalkers` (`PLANESWALKER_NAMES` kept out of every other pool, like the other slices) and `planeswalker-games.test.ts` (20 games per run, 100 with `pnpm test:soak`): every agent kind, loyalty abilities at most once per permanent per turn, at sorcery timing, the counters as the cost says, no planeswalker left at 0 loyalty, emblems that stay in the command zone, exact replay.
- Alternatives: The planeswalker card face with clickable rows (D4 b): not built, as the owner chose. A heuristic agent that plays each loyalty option out on its sample (the design's idea): not built, the rule above is the minimal AI the owner chose and the random and casual agents cover the soak; it is a listed upgrade. An AI that never uses its planeswalker: rejected by the design (the casual agent would look broken the first time it is given one).
- Consequences: The AI is a documented limit, not a strength claim (`docs/ROADMAP.md`). Nothing in the precons changed: the precon digest is identical, and the generic pools and `games-100` are unchanged.

## D-204: Flavor words (CR 207.2d) are taken off a line that does not read as written (stage P48, 2026-11-04)
- Context: The Vraska deck's new set labels nearly every named ability with an italic flavor word ("Rage —", "The Allagan Eye —", "Dance —", "Gae Bolg —", "A Test of Your Reflexes! —"). CR 207.2d says a flavor word, like an ability word, has no rules meaning, but "each flavor word is tailored to the specific ability it appears with" and the CR lists none, so a table like `ABILITY_WORDS` (CR 207.2c) cannot name them. The owner approved a generic strip on 2026-11-04 as a fallback only.
- Decision: `stripFlavorWord` (`normalize.ts`) takes off a leading label: a capitalized phrase of one to six words (letters, apostrophes, hyphens, "!" and "?"), then " — " (an em dash with a space on each side), followed by a sentence that starts with a capital letter or "{". It never takes off the head of a mode list ("Choose one —"), a chapter list ("I, II —"), a bullet, the keywords written with spaces around their dash (Boast, Forecast, Companion, Solved, Level, To solve) or the keyword forms written without spaces ("Escape—", "Ward—", "Equip—"). It is not part of `normalizeOracleText`: `parseFaceText` reads the line as written first and reads it again without its label only when the first reading failed as `unrecognised`, so no line that reads today changes, and a wrong strip can only turn an unread line into a read one. A line that still does not read keeps its text as written and the diagnostic of the stripped line (it says what is really unread).
- Alternatives: A longer list of flavor words: rejected (the CR does not list them and the set adds new ones). Stripping in the normalization pass for every line: rejected (it would change lines that read today and every golden AST hash would be at risk). Reading the label as an ability word in the grammar: rejected, the label carries no rule.
- Consequences: `PARSER_VERSION` 53 with D-205. The label is never shown to the engine, so the card's rules text shown to the player still has it (it is the Oracle text). Tested in `parser-p48.test.ts` (labels that strip, labels that must not, the real cards).

## D-205: Slice 1 of the Vraska deck: tokens, "that token", delayed return, color lists, base power and toughness (stage P48, 2026-11-04)
- Context: The first group of the whole-deck program (`docs/proposals/vraska-deck-analysis.md`, "Build status"): the cards whose only gap was a sentence the grammar did not read, driven from the real lines of the golden corpus.
- Decision: (1) **`that token`** and "it" as the token the sentence made (`noun.that-object`, `effect.attach`; the binding pass names the token, the lowering reads it as `moved`): "create a 2/2 red Dwarf creature token, then attach ~ to it" (Dwarven Shortsword), "That token gains haste until end of turn" (Loyal Apprentice). (2) **Delayed return** (`effect.return-delayed`, lowered as a `delayedTrigger` whose effect is a `moveToZone` of what the exile before it moved): "Exile up to one target creature or land you control. If you do, return it to the battlefield under its owner's control at the beginning of the next end step" (Roll-Roll-Roll-Roll). The engine creates one delayed ability for each card the exile moved (CR 603.7c, 400.7j); a token that was exiled never returns (CR 111.8); a land that returns asks its entering question (CR 614.12). `checkDelayedTrigger` accepts the new shape only after an exile. (3) **A color list on a target** (`withColorList`): "target creature or planeswalker that's green or blue" becomes an `anyOf` of one member for each type and color (Refute Destiny). (4) **`effect.lead-becomes-target`**: "Until end of turn, target artifact or creature becomes an artifact creature with base power and toughness 4/5" (Mind Transfer Protocol). (5) **`effect.have-base-pt`**: "have ~'s base power and toughness become 4/2 until end of turn" (Mirkwood Meditator). (6) **`noun.each-of-them`** for "Put a stun counter on each of them" (Homesickness). (7) **Two triggers with one body** (`When ~ enters and whenever you cast a spell with mana value 4 or greater`, Flaring Cinder).
- Alternatives: A delayed trigger that names the card by id in the AST: rejected (the id exists only at resolution; `moved` is what the engine already uses for "if you do"). Reading "that's green or blue" as the engine's `colors` (all of them): rejected, CR 105.1 says a color list means any of them.
- Consequences: `ENGINE_VERSION` 49 (the delayed return) and `PARSER_VERSION` 53. Cards that moved to supported are in the build status of `docs/proposals/vraska-deck-analysis.md`. Limits: `docs/ROADMAP.md`. Tests: `parser-p48.test.ts`, `convert-grammar-engine-p48.test.ts` (the real cards played), `scenario-xx-delayed-return.test.ts` (engine, SYNTHETIC cards).

## D-206: Group 2 of the Vraska deck: Job select, "during your turn", must be blocked, discard and dies triggers, untap, the mana spent and the zone it was cast from (stage P49, 2026-11-04)
- Context: The second group of the whole-deck program (`docs/proposals/vraska-deck-analysis.md`, "Build status"): Dragoon's Lance, White Mage's Staff, Magitek Scythe, Gau, G'raha Tia, Sahagin, Inkshape Demonstrator, Key to the City, Retrieve the Esper and the first line of Currency Converter. Every rule was driven from the real line of the golden corpus.
- Decision: (1) **Job select** (CR 702.182a): the keyword `jobSelect`, expanded in `derive-keywords.ts` into the enters trigger of Living weapon's shape with a 1/1 colorless Hero token (`keyword.job-select`, `validateCard`: only an Equipment). (2) **`yourTurn`** (CR 611.3a, 613.8): a condition read by statics (`static-conditions.ts`) and by intervening ifs; the rule `static.during-your-turn` reads "During your turn, equipped creature has flying." (3) **A quoted triggered ability given to an attached permanent** (`has "Whenever ~ attacks, you gain 1 life,"`, White Mage's Staff): the lowering accepts the subject `attached` for a triggered grant (an activated one stays unread, as before); a quote that ends the clause with its own comma ("life,\"") is read as the ability with its period (American punctuation). (4) **`mustBeBlocked`** (CR 509.1c): a restriction an effect gives for the turn ("and must be blocked this turn if able", also after "gains first strike until end of turn and"); `validateBlocks` obeys the maximum number of such requirements any legal declaration could (attackers with menace need two blockers; a small search), the decision marks the attacker (`mustBeBlocked`) and every agent's declaration goes through `withinBlockBudget`, which first adds the required blocks (`withRequiredBlocks`). (5) **"You may attach it to target creature you control. If you do, ..."**: `attach` performs only when something was attached (`performed`), and `may` wraps it. (6) **Triggers**: `becomesUntapped` (the untap step now notes the triggers its events cause, which wait for the upkeep: CR 502.4, 603.2), `discarded` (the `discarded` event gained the card's new object; "that card" is the trigger's subject and `exile` accepts it, CR 701.9a), `diesBatch` (one trigger for the permanents that die in the same events, CR 603.2c, 603.10a; a look-back trigger). (7) **Conditions**: `cardLeftYourGraveyard` (the turn log gained `leftGraveyard`, CR 400.7), `manaSpentAtLeast` (the spell that caused a cast trigger, read again as the ability resolves: `readsTriggerSubject` now keeps the subject) and `castFromZone` (the stack data gained `castFrom`, CR 601.2a). (8) **A filter on what a spell targets** (`ObjectFilter.targetsObject`, CR 601.2c): "an instant or sorcery spell that targets a creature". (9) Parser: "Then if ..." starts a conditional sentence, `noun.that-token`, "put N counters on that token", "its power" in "~ deals damage equal to its power" after any trigger, " and it can't be blocked" no longer joins a list of objects, "up to one target creature can't be blocked this turn".
- Alternatives: A new `becomesUntapped` flag on `becomesTapped`: rejected (a kind of its own reads better in every table). Reading the discarded card from the hand object: rejected (CR 400.7: it is a new object in the graveyard). A flag on the decision instead of the helper for the AI: the helper is the one place every agent already calls. Reading "that creature" for counters: rejected (it needs an antecedent no rule gave it; "that token" has one).
- Consequences: `ENGINE_VERSION` 50, `PARSER_VERSION` 54. Cards that moved to supported: Dragoon's Lance, White Mage's Staff, Magitek Scythe, Gau, G'raha Tia, Sahagin, Inkshape Demonstrator, Key to the City, Retrieve the Esper. Tests: `convert-grammar-engine-p49.test.ts` (the real cards played), `required-blocks.test.ts` (the agents' helper), the registry examples and rejects of every new rule. Currency Converter's other lines are built in a later group.

## D-207: Group 3 of the Vraska deck: discard costs with a card or a name, a reduction that reads the target, an Aura that returns attached, countering an ability, a duration bound to the Saga, removing all counters, the linked exile as a choice (stage P50, 2026-11-04)
- Context: The third group (`docs/proposals/vraska-deck-analysis.md`, "Build status"): Solitary Cell, Page, Loose Leaf, Magnificent End, Enchanted River's Grasp, Eagle's Rescue, Consign to Memory, Old Fat Spider Can't See Me and the two other lines of Currency Converter. Each rule was driven from the real line.
- Decision: (1) **A discard cost with a filter or a name** (`Cost` `discard` gains `filter` and `named`, CR 701.9, 118.8, 201.2): "Discard a legendary card" and "Discard another card named ~". The cards that may be discarded are the hand cards the filter matches (and, for "named", those with the name of the permanent with the ability, never that permanent): `discardCandidates` in `rules/discard-cost.ts`, read by the legality of the activation and by the payment; only the cost of an activated ability (`validateCard` refuses it in an additional cost). (2) **`spellTargets`** (CR 601.2c, 601.2f): a condition on the source spell's chosen targets for the spell's own `costReduction` ("costs {3} less to cast if it targets a tapped creature"). The question "may this spell be cast at all" is asked before any target exists, so it counts such a reduction as holding (`CostRequest.optimistic`, `spellTargetsMayHold`); the cost as paid is determined after the targets and without it, and a cast whose real cost cannot be paid is not completed. (3) **`moveToZone.attachTo`** (CR 303.4f, 303.4g): "return this card from your graveyard to the battlefield attached to target creature you control with power 1 or less" enters the Aura attached to the target, no choice of host. (4) **Countering a triggered ability** (CR 113.3c, 701.6): `ObjectFilter.stackKind` gains `triggeredAbility`, and a member of an `anyOf` may set the stack kind when the outer filter (zone `stack`) does not: "target triggered ability or colorless spell". (5) **`forAsLongAsThisRemains`** (CR 611.2b): the duration of `grantKeyword` and `preventDamage` in an ability of a permanent, kept as the continuous effect end `whileOnBattlefield { source }`, which ends for good as the source leaves (`endLostControlEffects`, with the state-based actions) and does nothing when the source is not there as the effect would begin. (6) **`removeAllCounters`** (CR 122.1, 122.2): every counter of every kind. (7) **A choice among the cards the permanent exiled** (CR 607.2a, 406.3): `moveToZone` of a `choose` whose filter zone is `exile` chooses among the permanent's linked exile that is still in exile; the parser links the exile of the face (also inside a `may`) to such a reader as it did to Imprint's static reader. (8) Parser: `cost.discard-filtered`, `condition.it-targets`, `noun.target-triggered-ability-or-spell`, `effect.remove-all-counters`, `effect.put-exiled-with`, `effect.return-self-attached`, `effect.gain-keyword-while-remains`, "Prevent all damage that would be dealt by up to one target creature for as long as ~ remains on the battlefield", "loses all abilities and doesn't untap during its controller's untap step", and "it" for the permanent an Aura is attached to ("Tap enchanted creature and remove all counters from it").
- Alternatives: A new ability kind or a card-name field for "another card named ~": rejected (a flag on the discard cost is the whole need). Reading the targets when the spell is on the stack only: rejected (a cast would be refused before the player could choose the cheaper target). A duration `untilSourceLeaves` shared with the exile of D-149: rejected (that one returns cards; this one ends an effect). Per-kind abilities for the counter effect: rejected, `counter` already removes an ability from the stack.
- Consequences: `ENGINE_VERSION` 51, `PARSER_VERSION` 55. Cards that moved to supported: Solitary Cell, Page, Loose Leaf, Magnificent End, Enchanted River's Grasp, Eagle's Rescue, Consign to Memory, Old Fat Spider Can't See Me, Currency Converter. Limits: an AI that casts Magnificent End on an untapped creature with too little mana gets an unpayable payment (the cast is cancelled), the check is optimistic by design. Tests: `convert-grammar-engine-p49.test.ts` (each card played), the registry examples and rejects.

## D-208: Group 4 of the Vraska deck: lands that ask for a revealed card, a mill cost and a rider that scries on a mana ability, "that entered this turn" (stage P51, 2026-11-04)
- Context: The fourth group (`docs/proposals/vraska-deck-analysis.md`, "Build status"): Furycalm Snarl, Theorist's Sanctum, Millikin, Path of Ancestry and Forge of Heroes. Each rule was driven from the real line of the golden corpus.
- Decision: (1) **`Replacement` `entersTappedUnlessReveals`** (CR 614.1c, 614.12, 701.20a, 701.4a): "As ~ enters, you may reveal a Mountain or Plains card from your hand. If you don't, ~ enters tapped" and "you may behold a Jace". It asks the question of a shock land (`confirmOptional`, answered with `entersPaid`) with no cost and the words of the replacement for the dialog; accepting reveals a card of the hand that matches the filter (the engine reveals the first it lists: which one does not change the game, only what the opponent learns) or, for behold, also chooses a permanent the controller controls that matches. When no card qualifies nothing is asked and the land enters tapped. The AI agents accept the question when a card is there to reveal. (2) **`Cost` `mill` on a mana ability** (CR 701.17a, 701.17b, 605.3): "{T}, Mill a card: Add {C}". A library with fewer cards cannot pay the cost, so the ability cannot be activated, and the planner of mana does not count it. (3) **`ManaAbility.spentRider.grants` of `{ scry: n }` and `spells.sharesTypeWithCommander`** (CR 106.6, 603.2, 701.22a, 903.3, 205.3m, 702.73a): "When that mana is spent to cast a creature spell that shares a creature type with your commander, scry 1". The mana carries the rider (`ManaRider` of kind `scry` with its source); when it pays for a spell that matches, a triggered ability of the permanent that made it waits to go on the stack above the spell, one for each mana spent. The creature types of the commander are read from its card (`commanderCreatureTypes`): the front face, a changeling having all of them. (4) **`ObjectFilter.enteredThisTurn`** (CR 400.7): the permanent entered the battlefield this turn and is still the same object (the turn log). Read where the filter is matched against the game (a target slot, an `each` selector), refused in a static ability and for another zone than the battlefield. (5) Parser: `replacement.enters-tapped-unless-reveals`, `cost.mill`, `effect.mana-rider-scry`, `effect.choose-target` ("Choose target commander that entered this turn": the target of the ability and no effect of its own), `effect.counters-if-it-is` ("put a +1/+1 counter on it if it's a creature and a loyalty counter on it if it's a planeswalker": each instruction wrapped in the engine's `conditional` on `objectMatches` of the target, so a permanent of both kinds gets both) and "target commander that entered this turn" in `noun.target-commander`. A clause may carry its own `objectMatches` test only for a lowering that says so (`takesObjectTest`, today the counters).
- Alternatives: Asking which card to reveal: rejected for now (nothing in the game depends on it, `docs/ROADMAP.md`). A rider that is a general delayed triggered ability on the mana: rejected, the one shape (a scry on a matching spell) is the whole need and the rider stays data on the mana. Reading the commander's types from the permanent on the battlefield: rejected (a commander in the command zone has no permanent; the card is what "your commander" names). A new effect kind for "if it's a creature ... if it's a planeswalker": rejected, `conditional` and `objectMatches` already say it.
- Consequences: `ENGINE_VERSION` 52, `PARSER_VERSION` 56. Cards that moved to supported: Furycalm Snarl, Theorist's Sanctum, Millikin, Path of Ancestry, Forge of Heroes. Limits: a commander that changed its creature types somewhere else is read as printed; the Path's scry trigger is put on the stack above the spell as it is cast, as CR 603.2 says. Tests: `convert-grammar-engine-p49.test.ts` (each card played from its real text, negative cases for each), `dragons-words.test.ts` and `vraska-words.test.ts` (web wording), the registry examples and rejects.

## D-209: Group 5 of the Vraska deck: energy counters, a random discard, connive (stage P51, 2026-11-04)
- Context: The fifth group (`docs/proposals/vraska-deck-analysis.md`, "Build status"): Tune the Narrative ("You get {E}{E}"), Rush of Inspiration // Crackling Falls ("discard a card at random unless you pay {E}{E}") and Unstable Experiment ("up to one target creature you control connives"). Each rule was driven from the real line of the golden corpus.
- Decision: (1) **Energy** (CR 107.14, 122.1): a player's own counters, `SeatState.energy` (optional: absent until the first, so a game that never uses it keeps the state it had), public in the view (`SeatView.energy`) and as the event `energyChanged`. `Effect` `gainEnergy { player, amount }` gets them; `Cost` `energy { count }` pays them by removing them (CR 107.14) and exists only in the cost of an `unlessPays` (`activationCostIssues` refuses it in an activated ability, a spell and a mana ability; the planner of the payment of that question, `canPayUnless` in `rules/pay-unless.ts`, needs the counters, CR 118.3, and pays them as the life is paid). (2) **`discard.random`** (CR 701.9b): the cards come from the hand as the game's seeded generator shuffles it, nobody chooses; fewer cards than asked discards the hand. Never with `anyNumber` or `unless`. (3) **`connive`** (CR 701.50a, 701.50f): for each creature the selector names that is still on the battlefield, its controller draws a card, then discards a card (their choice); a nonland card discarded puts a +1/+1 counter on it if it is still there. Several creatures connive one after the other in the order of the selector (CR 701.50c's player order is not read); a creature that left is skipped (CR 701.50b's last-known information is not read). (4) Parser: `cost.energy`, `effect.player.energy` ("you get {E}{E}"), "discard a card at random" in the imperative and with a player subject, `effect.connive`, and the "unless you pay {E}{E}" of a spell's sentence (only the energy cost, so "Counter target spell unless ..." keeps its frontier: `SPELL_SENTENCE` has `unless: 'energy'`).
- Alternatives: A required `energy` field on every seat: rejected (every test seat and digest would change for a counter nobody has). The energy as a counter object: rejected (a player's counters are numbers, as poison is). A `connive` built from `draw`, `discard` and a conditional counter in the parser: rejected (the discarded card is known only at the discard; the instruction carries the creature). The general "unless you pay" in spells: rejected for now (its diagnostics are pinned by other texts).
- Consequences: `ENGINE_VERSION` 53, `PARSER_VERSION` 57. Cards that moved to supported: Tune the Narrative, Rush of Inspiration // Crackling Falls, Unstable Experiment. The agents accept the question "pay {E}{E}?" as they accept any payment of an "unless" (`confirmOptional`, purpose `unlessPays`); the web shows the energy as a chip of the player strip, as a line of the log and the cost as `{E}`. Tests: `convert-grammar-engine-p51.test.ts` (each card played from its real text), `vraska-words.test.ts`, the registry examples and rejects.

## D-210: Group 6 of the Vraska deck: the players an effect asks, and what a discard or a mill did (stage P52, 2026-11-04)
- Context: The sixth group (`docs/proposals/vraska-deck-analysis.md`, "Build status"): Ruin Grinder ("each player may discard their hand and draw seven cards"), Combustible Gearhulk ("target opponent may have you draw three cards. If the player doesn't, you mill three cards, then this creature deals damage to that player equal to the total mana value of those cards") and Mog, Moogle Warrior ("each player may discard a card. Each player who discarded a card this way draws a card. If a creature card was discarded this way, you create a 1/2 white Moogle ... Then if a noncreature card was discarded this way, put a +1/+1 counter on each Moogle you control"). Each rule was driven from the real line of the golden corpus.
- Decision: (1) **`Effect` `playersMay { players, effect, runsAs?, otherwise? }`** (CR 608.2d, 101.4): each player the selector names, in turn order, is asked a `confirmOptional` (the instruction `playerMay`, answered by that player; a player who has lost is never asked); a player who accepts has `effect` done, a player who declines has `otherwise` done, if any. `effect` is done by the controller of the ability or, with `runsAs: 'chooser'`, by the player asked, who is "you" in it: the instruction `effect` has an `as` seat, the effect runs with that player as the controller, and what it queues next runs as them too. (2) **What a discard or a mill did, read by the effects after it** (`ThisWayKind`): `milledValue` (the total mana value of the cards a `mill` milled), `discardedCreature` and `discardedNoncreature`, the `Condition` `thisWayAtLeast` ("if a creature card was discarded this way") and the `PlayerSelector` `discardedThisWay` ("each player who discarded a card this way", the players of the `discard` effects of the resolution so far, in turn order). All are valid only after an effect that makes them in the same sequence, as every `thisWay` count is. (3) Parser: a sentence that begins "each player may", "target opponent may" or "target opponent may have you" (`IrSentence.mayBy`, read only in a triggered ability's body; the question belongs to the sentence, not to each clause), "If the player doesn't," as the sentence that says what is done otherwise, `condition.player-declines`, `condition.discarded-this-way`, `noun.each-player-discarded`, `amount.milled-value-this-way`, `effect.discard-hand` ("discard their hand": as many cards as the hand holds, counted as the instruction comes up) and "that player" after such a sentence meaning the player asked, never "you".
- Alternatives: Two sentences "each player may discard a card" and "each player who discarded draws" as one per-player effect: rejected (the draws come after every player has decided, and the creature and noncreature counts are read across the players). A `PlayerSelector` for "the player asked" shared with `triggerPlayer`: rejected (it is not the player of an event). Running the effect "as" another player by a new selector inside it: rejected (every selector of every effect would need it; the controller of the resolution is what "you" already reads). Asking all players at once: rejected (CR 101.4 order, and the agents answer one at a time).
- Consequences: `ENGINE_VERSION` 54, `PARSER_VERSION` 58. Cards that moved to supported: Ruin Grinder, Combustible Gearhulk, Mog, Moogle Warrior. Limits: the players are asked one after another in turn order and a later player can see the earlier player's answer (CR 101.4 has them choose without knowing it); a player with no card in hand is still asked "may discard a card" (nothing happens when they say yes). The agents answer the question as any "may" (`confirmOptional`): they accept unless the card's text is a costly option. Tests: `convert-grammar-engine-p51.test.ts` (each card played from its real text, each answer), the registry examples and rejects.

## D-211: Group 7, first part: a token that is a copy of a land asks what the land asks (stage P53, 2026-11-04)
- Context: Relm's Sketching ("Create a token that's a copy of target artifact, creature, or land") was refused because the engine had no step for a token copy of a shock land (CR 614.12), which asks to pay life as it enters.
- Decision: `enterToken` (`rules/enter-token.ts`) asks a token the questions of the land it copies, as a permanent asks them (`rules/zones.ts`): "As this enters, you may pay 2 life. If you don't, it enters tapped" (`entersTappedUnlessPays`) and "you may reveal a Mountain or Plains card from your hand ..." (`entersTappedUnlessReveals`, D-208). The player who creates the token is asked before it exists (the source of the question is the resolving spell or ability), the life is paid or the card revealed as the token enters untapped, and a "no" (or a question that cannot be asked: not enough life, nothing to reveal) makes it enter tapped. `tokenAsks` is true for such a token, so a `createToken` makes it with an `enterToken` instruction; the answer is recorded as `ResolutionContext.entersPaid` (`answerResolutionEntersPaid` also takes the head `enterToken`). `copySourceIssues` no longer refuses a source that could be a land (a source that could be an Aura is still refused, CR 303.4f). The question of a land that reveals a card is now answered when it comes up in a resolution (`answerResolutionEntersPaid` looked for a cost only, so a reveal land put onto the battlefield by an effect could not be answered).
- Alternatives: Entering a copied land tapped always: rejected (half-executing a "may"). Asking nothing and entering untapped: rejected (free untapped lands). Still refusing the copy of a land: rejected (Relm's Sketching and every copy effect that can target a land would stay unsupported).
- Consequences: `ENGINE_VERSION` 55, `PARSER_VERSION` 59. Relm's Sketching is supported. Limits: a token copy of a land that "may enter as a copy" (`entersAsCopy`) does not ask (it enters as the land itself); the dialog names the spell that makes the token, with the words of the token's land. Tests: `convert-grammar-engine-p51.test.ts` (a creature, a shock land accepted and declined, a land that reveals a card with and without a card to reveal), and the updated `ast-ward-copy-validate`, `parser-p6-copies` and corpus P6 tests.

## D-212: Group 7, second part: become a copy that keeps its name, and a pump of two named permanents (stage P54, 2026-11-04)
- Context: Gogo, Mysterious Mime ("you may have Gogo become a copy of another target creature you control until end of turn, except its name is Gogo, Mysterious Mime. If you do, Gogo and that creature each get +2/+0 and gain haste until end of turn and attack this turn if able").
- Decision: (1) **`becomeCopy.keepName`** (CR 707.2, 707.9a, 613.2a): each permanent that becomes the copy keeps the name it has now, every other copiable value is the original's; the effect is made one permanent at a time, and a `becomeCopy` that made an effect is something done (`performed`), so "if you do" can follow a `may` of it (`MAY_EFFECT_KINDS`, `MAY_KINDS`). (2) Parser: `effect.become-copy` ("have ~ become a copy of another target creature you control until end of turn, except its name is ~": this permanent, a target, for the turn, no other exception), `effect.gain-each-of-two` ("~ and that creature each get +2/+0 and gain haste until end of turn and attack this turn if able": `gainParser` with a list of exactly two nouns before "each" as its subject; the `restrict` lowering takes a list), and the binding pass binds the pronouns of a noun list before its other members, so "~ and that creature" does not point "that creature" at "~".
- Alternatives: A copy exception as a general list of overrides: rejected for now (the name is the only exception a card of this deck says; Face Yourself's "except it has haste and \"...\"" is another shape, `docs/ROADMAP.md`). Reading "that creature" as the nearest noun: rejected (it named Gogo itself and pumped it twice).
- Consequences: `ENGINE_VERSION` 56, `PARSER_VERSION` 60. Gogo, Mysterious Mime is supported. Limits: the copy has the copied creature's abilities for the turn, so a copied triggered ability of the Angel (none here) fires for Gogo; "attack this turn if able" for both creatures is the engine's `restrict` (`attacksEachCombat`) for the turn. Tests: `convert-grammar-engine-p51.test.ts` (the copy, the name, the pump of both, the requirement to attack, declining).

## D-213: Group 8, first part: a token copy of each permanent of a group, with the abilities the exceptions add (stage P55, 2026-11-04)
- Context: Face Yourself ("For each creature target player controls, create a token that's a copy of that creature, except it has haste and \"At the beginning of the end step, if you don't control a planeswalker, sacrifice this creature.\""). The engine's token copy took one permanent (`this`, a target or the triggering permanent) and no exception.
- Decision: (1) **`Effect` `createCopies { objects, abilities? }`** (CR 707.2, 707.9b, 111.4): `objects` is an `each` selector; for each permanent it names the controller of the effect creates a token with the copiable values of that permanent as they are now (last-known information for one that left, CR 608.2h) and `abilities` besides the ones it copies. A keyword the exception gives is a `keyword` ability, a quoted ability is that ability, so the exceptions of this deck need no other shape. A token that asks a question as it enters (devour, riot, a land, D-211) asks it as `createToken` does; a source that could be an Aura is refused (`copySourceIssues`). (2) Parser: `effect.copy-each` ("for each creature target player controls, create a token that's a copy of that creature, except it has haste and \"...\"": the group is the engine's `controlledBy` of a target player, the keyword is haste, the quoted ability is read as the ability of a token, `lowerTokenAbility`).
- Alternatives: `createToken` with a `copyOf` that takes a selector and an exception list: rejected (a token copy of one permanent and a copy of each of a group differ in how many tokens are made and in what "that creature" means; the new node keeps `createToken` as it was). A general `forEach` effect with an iterated reference: rejected (every effect would need to read it).
- Consequences: `ENGINE_VERSION` 57, `PARSER_VERSION` 61. Face Yourself is supported. Limits: the only exception read is "has haste and \"ability\""; the tokens of one resolution trigger together, so the end step asks the order of their triggers (CR 603.3b). Tests: `convert-grammar-engine-p51.test.ts` (the tokens, their haste, the sacrifice at the end step, the planeswalker that keeps them), the soak style `vraska` (`SYNTHETIC Copy Mirror`), the registry examples and rejects.

## D-214: Group 8, second part: preparation cards (CR 722): the layout prepare, the designation, the copy of the prepare spell in exile (stage P56, 2026-11-04)
- Context: Pompous Battlemage // Improvised Act and Fatehold Chronologist // Peer Review. The owner approved prepare in scope and asked for it to be built; the plan is `docs/design/prepare.md` (moved from `docs/proposals/`, with an "Outcome" section).
- Decision: (1) **Layout** `prepare` (`CardLayout`, `SUPPORTED_FEATURES.layouts`, `convert/layout.ts`, `validate-layouts.ts`): two faces, the second an instant or sorcery, the first a creature; the card is only the creature in every zone (CR 722.4) and its prepare spell is never cast from it (CR 722.3: `castableFaces` is the first face). (2) **`Replacement` `entersPrepared`** ("This creature enters prepared.", CR 722.3a): `GameObject.prepared` on the permanent and, made in the same step (`rules/prepare.ts`, called from `moveObject`), the copy of its prepare spell in exile (CR 722.3c): an object of the exile zone with `card` null, `copyOf` the card and `face` 1, as the copy of a spell on the stack is made, so its characteristics are the prepare spell's and a copy of it (CR 722.3d) is a prepare spell without more code; `prepareOf` names the permanent and `prepareCopy` the copy. The copy is not a card, and the engine applies CR 704.5e only as such a copy leaves the stack, so the exception needs no code. It ends when the permanent leaves the battlefield (`moveObject`), becomes unprepared or is cast. (3) **Casting it** (CR 722.3c, 601.2i): the controller of the prepared permanent may cast the copy from exile, for as long as the permanent is on the battlefield and prepared (`preparedPermanentOf`); `castZone`, `canCast`, `castableObjects` and `beginCast` treat it as a spell with its own face and no alternative cost; the permanent loses the designation as the spell moves to the stack (a cancelled cast restores the state before it); the copy resolves like any spell and ceases to exist after it (CR 707.10a). (4) The view has `ObjectView.prepared` and `preparedSpell`, the event `prepared`, and checkInvariants states that a prepared permanent and its copy name each other. (5) Parser: `replacement.enters-prepared`, and "You may discard a card. If you do, draw a card." for a spell (`SPELL_SENTENCE` reads "you may" only before "discard"). (6) Web: a "prepared" chip, the copy in the exile list with the existing "Cast from exile" button and badge, the log line, the autopilot stop.
- Alternatives: No exile object, the cast offered on the permanent: rejected (the CR makes the copy an object in exile; effects and the view see it there). A copy that carries `card` (a second object of the same card): rejected (one card, CR 722.2c). A general "you may" for spells: rejected (it turned 39 pinned results of other texts; only the offer to discard is read).
- Consequences: `ENGINE_VERSION` 58, `PARSER_VERSION` 62. Pompous Battlemage // Improvised Act and Fatehold Chronologist // Peer Review are supported, and so is Studious First-Year // Rampant Growth of the training corpus (golden training 162 to 163 of 192). Limits: a token copy of a preparation card has no prepare spell (CR 722.2b), "becomes prepared" and "becomes unprepared" have no node, and the copy in exile is not a card, so effects that count the cards of exile do not count it. Tests: `packages/engine/test/scenario-xx-prepare.test.ts` (a SYNTHETIC card; every rule above, a copy of the prepare spell, the opponent), `convert-grammar-engine-p51.test.ts` (both real cards: entering prepared, casting, resolving, the Cadet token, the permanent leaving, two prepared permanents), the layout tests, the soak style `vraska`. State shape of a precon game against main (key paths of the state at every step, 10 seeds): the only new paths are `turnLog.leftGraveyard[]` (group 2), `objects.*.stack.castFrom` and `lki.*.object.stack.castFrom` (group 3, set on a stack object cast from a zone), and `resolution.thisWay.discardedBy[]`, `discardedCreature`, `discardedNoncreature` and `milledValue` (counts of the later groups), plus the same `leftGraveyard` and `castFrom` inside `casting.snapshot`. No path was removed. The prepare fields (`prepared`, `prepareCopy`, `prepareOf`) do not appear in a game that has no prepare card. The two-seat views and legal actions are identical step by step on all 10 seeds; only the state hash differs, as it covers `engineVersion` and the new fields.


## D-215: Decks and lands in the web app: the opponent's deck from the saved decks (issue 108), precons you can edit locally (issue 93), the versions of the build (issue 104) and equal lands stacked in columns (2026-11-05)
- Context: Four owner requests, web only (no engine or parser change: `ENGINE_VERSION` 58 and `PARSER_VERSION` 62 stay). (1) Issue 108: a saved deck could be played only as the player's own deck, through "Open" and "Play this deck"; the opponent was always a shipped precon. (2) Issue 93: the precons were not on the decks page and could not be changed. (3) Issue 104: nothing on the page said which app, engine and card parser a player runs, so the owner could not tell whether they had the latest. (4) The owner's request in chat: on the battlefield the lands sat in a flat row in the order they entered (plains, mountain, plains, forest, mountain), where players at a table group equal lands in small columns.
- Decision: (1) **Deck picks.** A pick is a precon id, or `saved:<deck id>`; `Precons.prepare(id)` understands both (`precons/build.ts`; `createPrecons` takes a third argument, the `DeckLibrary` of the deck store and the Scryfall client, which `main.tsx` passes; without it behaviour is as before). A saved deck is prepared like any pasted list (names resolved through Scryfall and its IndexedDB card cache, the support cache, then `checkPlayable`), so the one rule of D-137 and D-056 holds for the opponent too: a deck with a card the engine cannot run, or that breaks the Commander rules, is refused, with the reason `"<name>" cannot be played: <reason>.`; nothing is half played. The menu's two pickers list the shipped precons, then "Saved in this browser"; the opponent picker of "Play this deck" is a select with the groups Precons and Your saved decks and checks a saved deck or an edited precon before Play (a status line, and Play is disabled with the reason); a shipped precon is not checked there (it is tested). `ui/use-deck-choices.ts` and the pure `precons/choices.ts` build the lists. The saved deck needs a connection unless its cards are in the browser's cache; a shipped precon still starts offline. (2) **Precon overrides.** The decks page lists the built-in precons ("Built in", or "Edited by you") under the saved decks. "Edit" opens the list in the import editor (the name is fixed, a banner says what saving does); "Save my version" stores a record `{ id: 'precon:<id>', preconId, name, text, savedAt }` in the existing `decks` store of IndexedDB (`DeckStoreApi.overrides`, `saveOverride`, `removeOverride`; `list()` leaves such records out and `save` never matches them by name, so no store version bump and no new store name: older builds had an `overrides` store with another meaning, D-167).
