The snapshot in `apps/web/src/precons/snapshots/` is never touched. Saving the shipped list again removes the override. "Reset to default" (the decks page asks twice, the editor once) removes it. The edited list is read with a layered client (`precons/layered-client.ts`): the precon's own cards answer from its snapshot, so a list that adds nothing new works offline, and only a card the player added is looked up on Scryfall, as in any import; it is judged supported or not by the same pipeline, and the menu marks an edited precon "edited". A precon whose edit has an unsupported card is refused when started (menu and "Play this deck") with the reason, until it is fixed or reset. The text is stored, not resolved cards, as for saved decks. (3) **Versions.** `apps/web/build-info.ts` runs when Vite starts and injects `__APP_COMMIT__` and `__APP_COMMIT_DATE__` with `define`: the short hash of `git rev-parse` and the date of that commit (`git log -1 --format=%cs`), so one commit is one build (no clock is read); without a `.git` it takes the hash from `WORKERS_CI_COMMIT_SHA`, `CF_PAGES_COMMIT_SHA` or `GITHUB_SHA` when one holds a hash, else `dev`, and an unknown date is left out. The footer of the start screen only reads `Build <hash> (<date>) · Engine <ENGINE_VERSION> · Card parser <PARSER_VERSION>` (`src/version.ts`; the game screen keeps its one line). The app package version stays `0.0.0` and is not shown. (4) **Land grouping** (`ui/board/lands.ts`, `LandRow.tsx`; the other rows are unchanged, in `Row.tsx` as `PlainRow`). A group is the lands with the same name, token or card, counters, chosen color or type and control effect; a land with an Aura on it stands alone. A column holds at most five cards of a group and is filled in order (the sixth starts a new column, so a land that arrives never moves the cards already laid out); inside it the cards are in entry order, the last in front, each lying over the one before so its top edge (the colour band and the name) shows; tapping never moves a card (a click taps it, a second click untaps it, as on the flat row), and the front card is the first in the document, so a click at the middle of the stack and the keyboard reach it first. Groups are ordered Plains, Island, Swamp, Mountain, Forest, Wastes (snow-covered after the plain ones), then the nonbasic lands by name; a nonbasic land is grouped by card name (two Command Towers stack). Each land stays a `Tile`, so click, hover, targeting, drag and drop and mana tapping are unchanged; a tapped card in a stack keeps its rotation and a mark on its strip; a column of two or more shows a count badge. Sizes (`layoutLands`): the capacity is the deepest column the row height allows at a tile of at least 48 (times the text scale), at most five; the row asks for more of the field while its columns are deep (`landGrow`); a short row (about a laptop screen at the default Large text) gets columns of two or three, a tall one columns of five; then the tiles shrink to fit the width down to 40 and past that the row scrolls, as before. The tokens of the other rows keep their grouping (identical tokens collapse into a counted tile only when a row overflows); Treasure and similar tokens are not lands and are not stacked. A hidden SYNTHETIC deck `synthetic-lands` (basic lands of every type and a nonbasic land) is the e2e deck.
- Alternatives: Adding saved decks only to "Play this deck": rejected, the menu is where the owner picks the opponent. A new IndexedDB store for overrides: rejected, the version bump and the old `overrides` name; a flag on the same record kind is enough. Storing the resolved cards of an edited precon: rejected, a saved deck stores text too and the pipeline stays one. localStorage for overrides: rejected, the decks already live in IndexedDB with the memory fallback. A runtime clock or `git describe` for the build id: rejected, not reproducible; the app version number: rejected, it is `0.0.0` and says nothing. Stacking by a fixed step regardless of the row height: rejected, at 1366 by 768 the tiles would be too small to read; the capacity follows the height instead. Balanced columns (6 as 3 and 3): rejected, a new land would move the cards already placed. Sorting nonbasic lands by color identity: not built, the view carries neither the produced mana nor the color identity of a land; by name is stable and groups the copies. Letting an empty creature row give its height to the land row: not done, it would change every board.
- Consequences: The owner can pick any saved or edited deck for either seat and sees why one is refused. An edited precon is local to a browser (clearing site data resets it). A saved deck as the opponent needs the network on first use, like importing it. The footer line says whether the page is the latest build by its hash; a Cloudflare build reads the commit from its own variable or from `.git`. At laptop heights the stacks are two or three deep; a taller window shows five. SPEC changes this needs (the SPEC is not edited here; the owner approves): section 10 "Screens" should say that the menu's pickers and "Play this deck" offer the saved decks as well as the precons, that the decks page lists the precons and lets the player edit them locally with a reset, and that the start screen shows the build, engine and parser versions; section 10 "Board" should say that the land row stacks equal lands in columns of up to five in the order above. Tests: `apps/web/test/land-groups.test.ts` (the grouping model), `decks-library.test.ts`, `decks-page-render.test.tsx`, `version.test.tsx` and `e2e/land-groups.e2e.ts`, `e2e/decks.e2e.ts`, `e2e/version.e2e.ts`.

## D-216: Group 1 of the Vraska EDHREC deck: an optional shuffle, untapping lands you choose, sorting the top cards, "that creature" of the line before, a sacrifice of a kind as a mana cost, "you created a token this turn", an artifact creature with numbers (stage P63, 2026-11-05)
- Context: The owner's second deck (`decks/vraska-edhrec.txt`, issue 120): 21 cards the engine did not run (`reports/decks.md`, parser 62), to be built on one branch for one pull request (`docs/proposals/vraska-edhrec-build-status.md` is the running checklist). The first group is the cards that need one small primitive each. Every rule was driven from the real line in the golden corpus.
- Decision: (1) **Ponder: `You may shuffle.`** The engine's `may` of a `shuffle` (`MAY_EFFECT_KINDS` gains `shuffle`; the shuffle reports what it did to `didPrevious`); the spell sentence accepts "You may shuffle." (`SPELL_SENTENCE` `may: 'discard'` now means "the offers a spell reads": discard and shuffle) and `lowerLoneMay` lowers a lone optional instruction of `LONE_MAY_KINDS`. `effect.shuffle` also reads a bare "shuffle". (2) **Frantic Search: `Untap up to three lands.`** `ChooseSelector.upTo` and `untap` of a `choose` selector; the instruction `chooseTap` gains `untap`; the question is a `choosePermanent` of the new purpose `untapChoice` (none up to `max`) over the tapped permanents of the battlefield the filter matches, whoever controls them (it is not a target and the words do not say "you control", CR 701.26a, 608.2d); a permanent with a stun counter loses one instead (CR 122.1d). `effect.untap-chosen`. Agents: the casual agent untaps as many of its own as it may; the opponent's lands are never chosen. Web: `permanents-untap.ts`, `untapChooseText`. (3) **Expressive Iteration: the new effect `lookAndSplit`** (`count`, `hand`, `bottom`, `exile`, `count = hand + bottom + exile`): the controller looks at the top cards and puts `hand` of them into the hand, `bottom` of them on the bottom of the library and exiles the rest, choosing the first two piles with a `chooseCards` decision of the new purpose `lookSplit` (`to` says which pile, `looked` the cards seen; asked only when there is a choice; with fewer cards the first instructions are done and the last are not, CR 608.2c); `moved` is what it exiled, so "You may play the exiled card this turn" (`mayPlay`, which now reads "the exiled card") follows. `rules/look-split.ts`; the segmenter keeps the two sentences together (`effect.look-split`). The casual agent keeps the best card (a land while it has fewer than four) and bottoms the worst. Web: `lookSplit` in the picker (title, button, badge, waiting words). (4) **Dispatch: the line "Metalcraft — If you control three or more artifacts, exile that creature."** is a paragraph of its own whose "that creature" is the target of the paragraph before; `joinReferenceLines` (spells only) reads the two lines as one text when the second is a test and an instruction on "it" or "that <thing>", and `effect.exile` reads `noun.that-object`. (5) **Kykar: "Sacrifice a Spirit: Add {R}."** A mana ability may sacrifice a permanent of a kind the controller has (`ManaAbility.cost` `sacrifice` with a filter, no zone, no count; CR 605.1a, 701.21a): `physicalRefusal` needs a candidate, `manaSacrificeChoice` picks it (the one the payment names, `payManual` taps and `activateManaAbility` take `sacrifice`; otherwise a token before a card, then the lowest mana value, never the source itself unless it is the only one), the payment planner treats it as the last-resort sacrifice tier as for a Treasure. Ashnod's Altar and the other sacrifice-a-creature mana abilities read since. (6) **Idol of Oblivion: "Activate only if you created a token this turn."** `condition.created-token` is the engine's `enteredThisTurn` of tokens (`count` 1, `token` true): the player who creates a token owns it and it enters under their control (CR 111.2), so a token that entered under the controller's control this turn is one they created. No new state. (7) **Hammer of Purphoros:** the token "3/3 colorless Golem enchantment artifact creature" (`token.custom`). (8) **Cyberdrive Awakener: "each noncreature artifact you control becomes a 4/4 artifact creature until end of turn".** `effect.each-becomes` (a group, the numbers required) and `setTypes.basePt`: the types and the base power and toughness are one effect over the objects the group named as the effect began (CR 611.2c; two effects would read "noncreature" again after the first). Not additive: "becomes an artifact creature" without "in addition" replaces the card types (CR 205.1a), so an artifact that was also an enchantment stops being one for the turn. Unverified against a ruling: Scryfall is not reachable from the sandbox.
- Alternatives: A new `shuffle` decision for Ponder: rejected, `may` is the question the engine already asks and the web already words. Two effects for Cyberdrive Awakener: rejected, the second would not see the permanents the first changed (a card-name special case to avoid it would be worse). A separate `tokensCreated` log: rejected, `entered` already records the token and who controlled it as it entered; the difference (an opponent who creates a token under your control) is outside every card of this deck. One `activateAbility` action for each Spirit that could be sacrificed: rejected, it multiplies the legal actions of every payment; the engine chooses and a manual payment may name the permanent. A `lookAtTop` with three piles: rejected, its second stage puts the rest where the effect says without a choice.
- Consequences: Ponder, Frantic Search, Expressive Iteration, Dispatch, Kykar, Idol of Oblivion, Hammer of Purphoros (its other line already read) and Cyberdrive Awakener are supported; seven of them moved from unsupported to supported in the golden snapshot, with training and hold-out unchanged. The web cannot yet name the Spirit that Kykar's mana sacrifices when the player pays by clicking: the engine chooses (a token first). The payment planner uses one activation of a source for each payment, so a plan never sacrifices two Spirits to one Kykar. `ENGINE_VERSION` 59, `PARSER_VERSION` 63. Tests: `packages/cards/test/convert-grammar-engine-p63.test.ts` (the real cards through the engine), `parser-registry.test.ts` (the examples and rejects of the new rules).

## D-217: Group 2 of the Vraska EDHREC deck: gain-then-pump, "those creatures", a group of tokens, a copy with an added type, delayed draws and mana of the countered spell (stage P64, 2026-11-05)
- Context: Second group of `docs/proposals/vraska-edhrec-build-status.md`: the cards whose gap was a sentence shape or a small extension of the delayed triggered ability (CR 603.7), each driven from its real line.
- Decision: (1) **Craterclaw Colossus: "creatures you control gain trample and get +X/+0 until end of turn, where X is ..."**: `gainParser` reads the keywords first and the pump after ("gain A and get +X/+0"), for every gain rule; the "where X" of the sentence is the existing one. (2) **Jeskai Ascendancy: "Untap those creatures."** `effect.untap-those` and `lowerUntapThose`: the group the sentence before it pumped or granted (an `each` selector), untapped as it stands right after (CR 611.2c; nothing happens in between). Refused after any other sentence. (3) **Roar of Resistance: "Creature tokens you control have haste."** `noun.token-permanents` ("creature tokens you control", "tokens you control": the engine's `token` filter), accepted as a subject of `static.permanents`; "Creature tokens you control get +1/+1." reads too (Intangible Virtue and its kin). (4) **Saheeli: "-2: Target artifact you control becomes a copy of another target artifact or creature you control until end of turn, except it's an artifact in addition to its other types."** `effect.target-becomes-copy` (quiet: it shares its first words with `effect.becomes`), `becomeCopy.addTypes` (the copiable values the copy effect gives have the types in addition, CR 707.9b), and "another target" after a first target is `TargetSpec.differentFrom` that slot (CR 115.3; the lowering of a noun with `otherTarget`). (5) **Arcane Denial: "Its controller may draw up to two cards at the beginning of the next turn's upkeep."** `draw.upTo` (the player the selector names, who is not the controller of the effect, is asked how many from none to the number: a `chooseX` of the new purpose `drawUpTo`, `rules/draw-up-to.ts`, answered through the same record as "pay any amount"), and a delayed trigger that remembers the player (`DelayedTrigger.player`, read as `triggerPlayer`; the player is the controller of the target spell as it resolves, from last-known information, CR 603.7c). The sentence is `effect.delayed-draw-up-to`. (6) **Mana Sculpt: "If you control a Wizard, add an amount of {C} equal to the amount of mana spent to cast that spell at the beginning of your next main phase."** `delayedTrigger.at.step` `nextMain` (the first main phase of the controller's that begins after the ability is created: `rules/next-main.ts`, CR 603.7a), a delayed `addMana` whose number of times is `manaSpent` `of` a target (the amount is read when the ability is created, from the countered spell's last-known stack data, and written into the ability, CR 603.7c), and the condition "if you control a Wizard" is the sentence's own (`conditional`), checked as the spell resolves. `effect.delayed-mana`. (7) Cyberdrive Awakener's tests are in `convert-grammar-engine-p64.test.ts` with the others (its engine work is D-216).
- Alternatives: A separate decision kind for "draw up to": rejected, the number question already exists (`chooseX`) and its answer path serves; the web has one dialog for it. A second state list of delayed abilities for other players: rejected, one optional `player` is enough. Reading "next main phase" as two delayed triggers (precombat and postcombat) that cancel each other: rejected, a trigger that waits for either would need the other removed; the phase is found when the ability is created. Untapping "those creatures" by a new object reference: rejected, the group is the same selector as the pump's.
- Consequences: Craterclaw Colossus, Jeskai Ascendancy (both lines), Saheeli (all lines), Mana Sculpt and Arcane Denial are supported; Roar of Resistance's first line reads (the card waits for group 3). The golden snapshot moves from 127 to 133 of 159 (training and hold-out unchanged). Sixteen or so other corpus lines that were unread now read ("Creature tokens you control get +1/+1", "Untap those creatures", gain-then-get). The opponent can be asked "draw up to two cards?" (a dialog with a stepper and no Cancel); the casual agent draws all it may. Limits: the delayed draw is only by the controller of a target spell; a delayed mana ability adds mana only at a main phase of its controller. `ENGINE_VERSION` 60, `PARSER_VERSION` 64. Tests: `packages/cards/test/convert-grammar-engine-p64.test.ts`.

## D-218: Group 3 of the Vraska EDHREC deck: batch triggers of attackers and of tokens, cast or copy, the attackers of your opponents (stage P65, 2026-11-05)
- Context: Third group of `docs/proposals/vraska-edhrec-build-status.md`: the four cards whose trigger the engine could not see.
- Decision: (1) **"Whenever one or more creatures attack" (Roar of Resistance) and "Whenever one or more artifact creatures you control attack" (Alibou).** `trigger.attack-one-or-more`, the engine's `attackBatch` with `atLeast` 1; `attackBatch.who` gains `any` (whoever declares them: the first form says it of "creatures" alone, a kind of creature is said of "you control"). The damage and the scry of Alibou read "the number of tapped artifacts you control" (`countOf` with `tapped`) as the ability resolves; the same count is written into each place X appears, so a damage that destroys one of the controller's own tapped artifacts before the scry changes the scry (limit, no card of the deck can do it unless the player targets their own artifact creature). (2) **"Whenever one or more tokens you control enter" (Mister Fantastic).** The trigger `entersBatch` (like `diesBatch`: every permanent `what` names that enters in one batch of events is one occurrence, so two tokens of one effect trigger it once); `trigger.enters-one-or-more` reads a group of tokens (`noun.token-permanents`, D-217). The "may draw" is the ability's own `optional`. (3) **"Whenever you cast or copy an instant or sorcery spell" (Magecraft: Storm-Kiln Artist).** `castSpell.orCopy`: a `spellCopied` event (a copy put on the stack, CR 707.10: not cast) is an occurrence under the control of the player who has the copy; `spellCopied` is a relevant event for triggers. `trigger.cast-or-copy`. A card that reads "cast or copy" elsewhere (the 6 cards of the corpus line) is read too. (4) **"creatures attacking your opponents and/or planeswalkers they control" (Roar of Resistance's second sentence).** `ObjectFilter.attackingOpponents`: the creature is in combat and attacks an opponent of the controller as a player, or a planeswalker or battle that opponent controls or protects (`attackersOfOpponents`, as `attackingYou`); refused where `attacking` is refused (statics, replacements). `noun.attacking-opponents`, accepted by `effect.pump-all`. The offer "you may pay {1}{R}. If you do" is the existing `mayPay`; the group is fixed as the effect resolves (CR 611.2c). Agents: the casual agent pays only when one of its creatures is attacking (`payForEffect`), not when the opponent declared the attack (the ability triggers for any player). Web: the wording of `entersBatch`, `orCopy`, `who: 'any'` and the filter.
- Alternatives: A trigger event for each token that enters: rejected, the card says "one or more" and two tokens would draw twice. Reading "one or more creatures attack" as a trigger of each attacker: rejected, CR 603.2c. A filter for "attacking a player other than you": rejected, "your opponents and/or planeswalkers they control" is the card's own set (a planeswalker of yours is not in it).
- Consequences: Mister Fantastic, Storm-Kiln Artist, Alibou and Roar of Resistance are supported. The golden snapshot moves from 133 to 137 of 159 (training and hold-out unchanged); the six cards that read "cast or copy" and the cards that say "one or more creatures you control attack" read too. `ENGINE_VERSION` 61, `PARSER_VERSION` 65. Tests: `packages/cards/test/convert-grammar-engine-p65.test.ts`.

## D-219: Group 4 of the Vraska EDHREC deck: replacement of the creation of tokens (stage P66, 2026-11-05)
- Context: Draconic Visitor and Stridehangar Automaton, whose real lines are replacement effects of CR 614.1a on the tokens their controller would create. The brief asked for the affected player's order (CR 616.1) as for damage (D-191) if it generalizes, else the limit.
- Decision: The replacement `tokensInstead` (`what`: the tokens it names as they would be on the battlefield, here `{ types: ['artifact'], token: true }`; `mode` `thatMany` or `plus`; `token`, a described or predefined token). `createTokens` (`rules/tokens.ts`, the one place every token of every effect is made: `createToken`, copies, Treasure, Food, Clue, tokens that ask, riot and devour) asks `replacedTokens` (`rules/token-replacement.ts`) first: the replacement abilities of the permanents the creator controls, read as the event begins and oldest first, each applied once (CR 614.5) to the batch of tokens one creation makes, the batch a replacement leaves being what the next one reads (so the Thopter of the Automaton is an artifact token that the Visitor then replaces, while the Dragons of the Visitor are not, and the Automaton does not apply to them). `thatMany` replaces the matching tokens with as many of its own; `plus` leaves them and adds one. The tokens a replacement makes enter untapped and without the choices (tapped, devour, riot, "as this enters") of the original. Parser: `replacement.tokens-instead` (both lines of the two cards; the tokens by the grammar's own description, `customToken`), lowered by the verb `tokensInstead` of `lower/abilities.ts`.
- Alternatives: Asking the affected player the order with the machinery of D-191: not done. That machinery is a decision asked in the middle of one event whose result is computed from a list of effects (`rules/damage-order.ts`); a token creation is made by a function that every effect calls and that returns at once, so a question would have to suspend each of its callers (about fifteen). Only two cards of this deck and no pair of effects in which the order changes the result besides Draconic Visitor with Stridehangar Automaton (n Dragons if the Visitor goes first, n+1 if the Automaton does) make it matter; the order is the timestamp, the same limit as the "would die" replacements (D-156), and is written in `docs/ROADMAP.md` (Known rules deviations). Making the replacement a trigger: wrong, it must not create the replaced tokens at all.
- Consequences: Draconic Visitor and Stridehangar Automaton are supported (the Automaton's other line already read). The golden snapshot moves from 137 to 139 of 159. Limits: the order of two such effects is the timestamp's; a replacement that makes tokens ignores "tapped" and the entry choices of the original. `ENGINE_VERSION` 62, `PARSER_VERSION` 66. Tests: `packages/cards/test/convert-grammar-engine-p66.test.ts`.

## D-220: Group 5 of the Vraska EDHREC deck: a triggered ability that triggers an additional time, and Equip with a creature type (stage P67, 2026-11-05)
- Context: Harmonic Prodigy and Wizard's Staff, the last two cards of the deck: "If a triggered ability of a Shaman or another Wizard you control triggers, that ability triggers an additional time." and "If a triggered ability of equipped creature triggers, that ability triggers an additional time." (CR 603.2d), and the Staff's "Equip Wizard {1}" beside "Equip {3}" (CR 702.6c). The brief called the trigger doubling a medium piece in scope.
- Decision: (1) **The static ability `doubleTriggers { subject }`** (`subject`: a group of permanents with `controller: 'you'` the controller of the permanent with the ability and `other` leaving it out, or `attached`). `collectTriggers` (`rules/triggers.ts`) passes the triggers `findTriggers` found through `withDoubledTriggers` (`rules/trigger-doubling.ts`): for each trigger of a permanent's own triggered ability (an index among its abilities), one more identical pending trigger for every permanent on the battlefield with a `doubleTriggers` whose subject names the source (last-known information when it has left, so a "dies" ability of a Wizard is doubled). Each is put on the stack and resolves on its own, choosing its own targets (CR 603.3d); two permanents make three triggers. Delayed, monarch, Ring, reflexive and state triggers are not abilities of a permanent and are not doubled; "this ability triggers only once each turn" is counted before the doubling. The permanent with the ability is not its own subject when the text says "another". The parser reads one or two creature types of the controller ("a Shaman or another Wizard you control", the second excluding the permanent) or "equipped creature" (`static.triggers-additional-time`; lowered in `lower/statics.ts`). (2) **Equip with a creature type.** `keyword` `equip` gains `restriction` (an `ObjectFilter` of creature types): the expansion's target is "a creature you control" that the filter also matches (`rules/derive-keywords.ts`); `keyword.equip-quality` reads "Equip Wizard {1}" (one type of the table, a mana cost). The permanent has both abilities. The target slot is refused by the engine for a creature without the type (CR 601.2c).
- Alternatives: Doubling by running each trigger's effect twice when it resolves: wrong, the abilities are put on the stack separately (CR 603.2d: the ability triggers again), can be responded to and chose targets again. A replacement effect: it is not one (603.2d is a rule about triggering). A new field on every triggered ability: rejected, the ability belongs to the permanent that doubles, not to the one that triggers. A separate Equip keyword: rejected, one field says it.
- Consequences: Harmonic Prodigy and Wizard's Staff are supported, and the whole deck is: `packages/cards/test/vraska-edhrec-deck.test.ts` reads every card of the deck that is in the golden corpus completely (the owner's `pnpm corpus:decks` with the bulk file is the check that counts). The golden snapshot is at 141 of 159 (acceptance; training and hold-out unchanged from the start). Limits: a doubled trigger of a permanent that is gone is made from its last-known information; a doubler that leaves in the same event as the trigger still doubles it only if it is on the battlefield afterwards; the optional "may" of a doubled trigger asks twice. `ENGINE_VERSION` 63, `PARSER_VERSION` 67. Tests: `packages/cards/test/convert-grammar-engine-p67.test.ts`; the AI soak style 'edhrec' (`packages/ai/test/edhrec-games.test.ts`, with the SYNTHETIC cards of `synthetic-edhrec.ts`) plays every piece of the program.

## D-221: The player chooses the order of two replacement effects of the creation of tokens (2026-11-06)
- Context: D-219 applied the replacement effects `tokensInstead` (Draconic Visitor, Stridehangar Automaton) oldest first and never asked. CR 616.1: "If two or more replacement and/or prevention effects are attempting to modify the way an event affects an object or player, the affected object's controller (or its owner if it has no controller) or the affected player chooses one to apply", and CR 616.1f repeats the process "taking into account only replacement or prevention effects that would now be applicable" until none is left, each applying once (CR 614.5). With both cards in play the result depends on the order: the Visitor first makes n Dragons and the Automaton no longer applies (Dragons are not artifact tokens); the Automaton first makes n artifact tokens and a Thopter, which the Visitor then replaces: n+1 Dragons. The owner asked for the CR to be followed, with the design of D-191 for damage.
- Decision: (1) **Settling before making.** `rules/token-replacement.ts` `settleTokens(state, seat, source, parts, flow)` takes the tokens one effect creates at once (`TokenBatch`: a definition, a count and whether they are the tokens the instruction itself describes, `original`) and applies the replacement effects of the permanents `seat` controls one at a time, the player choosing: it lists the effects that apply to the batch as it is now (each applies at most once and only when a part of the batch matches what it names), asks when two or more apply and the order can change which tokens are made (`OrderSearch`, an exact search over the orders memoised on the effects used and the tokens left; more than eight effects asks whenever two apply), and repeats with what is now applicable (CR 616.1f). The question is a `chooseOption` of purpose `replacement` (the same dialog as damage), answered by the creator of the tokens (`seat`), with `replacement.tokens` (the tokens as they would be created now) in place of `replacement.event` and one `TokenReplacementChoice` for each effect (`kind: 'tokens'`, the words of the effect, the permanent, and `outcome.tokens`/`outcome.total`: what is created if it goes first and the rest follow the default order); `ReplacementQuestion` is now the union of `DamageReplacementQuestion` and `TokenReplacementQuestion`. Nothing is asked when every order ends the same (two Visitors, two Automatons: `canonical` batches are compared). The default order, which is also the first option, is the one that can make the most tokens, the older permanent first on a tie. (2) **The same replay as damage.** The instruction that creates the tokens (`createToken`, `createCopies`: `rules/token-batch.ts` `makeSettled`; the `enterToken` instruction of a token that asks, `rules/enter-token.ts`) runs with the answers given so far (`ResolutionContext.damageAnswers`, whose comment now covers both questions), returns the question with nothing changed when it needs another, and runs again from the same state with the answer. `createCopies` settles all its copies as one event. An effect settles the creation once, for all the tokens it creates at once, and then makes each part: the tokens that ask a question as they enter (a choice, riot, devour, a land copy's question) are made by one `enterToken` instruction each marked `settled`, so a count of three with riot is one event, not three. Encore's copy (`enterToken` not marked `settled`) is settled when its instruction first runs and is replaced by settled instructions. The creations that cannot wait for an answer (the token a "would die, exile it instead and create a token" replacement makes inside a move, Empower Jace's token, the rider of a mana ability) use `createTokens`, which settles with a flow that does not ask: the default order. (3) **What the replaced tokens keep (CR 614.1).** An "instead" effect replaces the event with another: what the instruction said about the tokens it replaced ("create a tapped Treasure token", the choice "as this enters", the counters of devour and riot) is about those tokens and does not carry over to the Dragons, which are the tokens the replacement describes and enter as their own definition says; the tokens a `plus` effect leaves are still the original ones and keep it (tapped), and the Thopter it adds is untapped. Other replacement effects (a permanent that makes tokens enter tapped, a counter each other Angel gets) still apply to every token that is made (`makeTokens`). D-219's limit on this point is closed by this reading, not by code. (4) **Agents.** Casual and greedy take the first option (the most tokens, which the engine lists first); the heuristic agent picks the choice whose `outcome.total` is largest; random picks. The web words the question as "You would create 2 Treasure. Several effects replace that. Choose which to apply first." and each button "Then: 3 Dragon" (`replacementPrompt`, `namedOptionRows`).
- Alternatives: Keeping the timestamp order and listing it as a limit (D-219): the owner asked for the CR. Making the replacement a trigger or a static modification of the amount: wrong, the Dragons replace the artifact tokens. Asking inside `createTokens` by making it return a question to its fifteen callers: only five callers exist, and only the three that are effects of a resolving spell or ability can wait (`createToken`, `createCopies`, `enterToken`), so those settle first and the other two use the default order. Asking at the death replacement and Empower: the first is deep inside a move that state-based actions also call, the second makes a planeswalker token that no replacement of an artifact token names.
- Consequences: `ENGINE_VERSION` 64. Tests: `packages/cards/test/convert-grammar-engine-p66.test.ts` (the real Draconic Visitor and Stridehangar Automaton: both ages, both answers, the question asked of the creator with the better order first and nothing made before the answer, an answer by the wrong player or outside the options refused, non-artifact tokens, two Visitors and two Automatons asking nothing, three effects asking again, tapped Treasures replaced and kept), `apps/web/test/damage-order-render.test.tsx`. Limits: a token made inside a death replacement or by Empower, or a token made by the rider of a mana ability, uses the default order (the most tokens), which is what a player would choose; Encore's copies are settled one opponent at a time (with two seats that is one event).

## D-222: The player chooses the permanent a mana ability sacrifices (2026-11-06)
- Context: D-216 read Kykar's "Sacrifice a Spirit: Add {R}." as a mana ability that sacrifices a permanent of a kind, and chose the Spirit itself (a token before a card, then the lowest mana value) unless a manual payment named one; the web's click-to-pay flow had no way to name it. CR 601.2b: the player announces the choices that go with a cost; CR 118.3 and 701.21a: a player sacrifices a permanent they choose; CR 605.3b: a mana ability's costs are paid as it is activated. The same rule as the sacrifice cost of any other activated ability, which already asks (`choosePermanent`, purpose `sacrifice`).
- Decision: (1) **A cost that sacrifices one of several permanents is the player's choice, by hand.** `activateManaAbility` (`rules/mana-engine.ts`) refuses an activation of an ability with a "Sacrifice a <kind>" cost when the player has more than one permanent to give up and does not name one (`sacrifice`), and refuses a named permanent that is not one of them; with exactly one candidate there is nothing to choose and the activation needs no name; a cost that sacrifices only the source (a Treasure) is unchanged. `manaSacrificeCandidates` (`rules/mana-abilities.ts`) lists them. (2) **At priority.** The `activateAbility` action and option gain `sacrifice`; with more than one candidate `getLegalActions` offers one activation for each permanent (and each color). (3) **While paying.** `PayManaDecision.manaSources[].sacrifices` lists the permanents when there is a choice, and a `payManual` tap names one as `sacrifice` (the field D-216 added): a tap that does not is refused, with the payment unchanged. (4) **The default.** `payAuto` (the planner pays for the player) still gives up the one the planner prefers (a token before a card, the lowest mana value, then the oldest, the source last), which is the default the agents use because they only pay automatically; the human player who wants another Spirit pays by hand, and the dock says so. (5) **The web.** `clickSource` opens the chooser popover for a source with `sacrifices` ("Sacrifice which permanent?", the names of the permanents), the tap carries the choice (also through the color question of a source that asks both), the dock names the permanent that "will be sacrificed", and at priority the existing menu lists one entry for each permanent. No new dialog kind. (6) **The testing DSL** takes `sacrifice` in `tapForMana` and `payManual`.
- Alternatives: Asking a `choosePermanent` decision in the middle of a payment: the payment is a transaction of taps that is checked as a whole, and the click-to-pay flow already lets the player name everything else that a tap needs (a color, a combination). Making `payAuto` ask: the planner exists so the player does not have to choose each source; auto-pay is the player's delegation and is documented as a default. Requiring `sacrifice` for every sacrifice cost: with one candidate (or the source itself) there is nothing to choose.
- Consequences: `ENGINE_VERSION` 65. Tests: `packages/cards/test/convert-grammar-engine-p63.test.ts` (the real Kykar: the options for each Spirit, an unnamed or illegal sacrifice refused with the state unchanged, the one named is the one that goes, one Spirit means no choice, the payment lists the Spirits, auto-pay is the cheapest), `apps/web/test/sacrifice-choice.test.tsx`. Limits: auto-pay chooses for the player (the default above).

## D-223: Several permanents connive at once (CR 701.50b, 701.50c) (2026-11-06)
- Context: D-209 made each creature a `connive` names draw and discard one after the other in the order of the selector, skipping one that had left. CR 701.50c: "If multiple permanents are instructed to connive at the same time, the first player in APNAP order who controls (or, in the case of a permanent no longer on the battlefield, last controlled) one or more of those permanents chooses one of them and it connives. Then this process is repeated for each remaining instruction to connive." CR 701.50b: "If a permanent is no longer on the battlefield as an effect instructs it to connive, its last known information is used to determine which object connived and who controlled it."
- Decision: The effect `connive` becomes the instruction `conniveNext` (`rules/connive.ts`, `state/types.ts`) holding the permanents still to connive with the player who controls each (the controller read from the battlefield, or from last-known information for a permanent that has left, CR 701.50b). Each step takes the first player in APNAP order (`seatsInOrder` from the active player) who has one, asks them which connives next when they have two or more (`choosePermanent`, purpose `conniveOrder`, answered like the other permanent choices of a resolution), and queues the draw, the discard (with the conniver, so a nonland card puts the counter on it if it is still on the battlefield) and the next step. A permanent that left still draws and discards for its last controller and gets no counter (the counter needs it to be there). The agents take the first permanent listed; the web words the question ("Several permanents connive: choose which of yours connives next (...)", badge "Connives") and reuses the permanent panel.
- Alternatives: Asking the order for every connive: only a player with two or more of the permanents has anything to choose. Taking the permanents that left out of the question: the CR lets the player pick any of them.
- Consequences: `ENGINE_VERSION` 65. No supported card connives a group today (the grammar reads one permanent: "up to one target creature you control connives", "~ connives", "it connives"), so this is the rule for a card that does; the real Unstable Experiment plays as before. Tests: `packages/engine/test/scenario-xx-connive.test.ts` (the active player first and the choice among theirs, the other order, no question when each player has one, the opponent's turn, a permanent that left still connives for its last controller). Limits: the web board cannot click a permanent that has left the battlefield, so a human cannot pick one of those first (the engine and the agents can); the connive-N variant (CR 701.50d) is not read.

## D-224: Suspend's haste ends when control is lost; "becomes a 4/4 artifact creature" keeps the other types (2026-11-06)
- Context: Two supported cards played against the CR text. (1) CR 702.62a: a creature cast by suspend "gains haste until you lose control of the spell or the permanent it becomes"; `derive-alt.ts` gave the haste to the permanent whoever controlled it. (2) CR 205.1b: "Some effects state that an object becomes an 'artifact creature'; these effects also allow the object to retain all of its prior card types and subtypes", with the example of an artifact enchantment that becomes an artifact enchantment creature. D-216 read Cyberdrive Awakener's "becomes a 4/4 artifact creature" as replacing the types (CR 205.1a), though the grammar already read the same phrase without the numbers as additive.
- Decision: (1) `alternativeAbilitiesOf(state, obj)` gives a suspended permanent haste only while the player it entered under controls it and has controlled it without a break (`controlledSince` not after its timestamp): once an opponent has it the haste is gone, and it does not come back when control returns (the effect that ended is not restarted). (2) The rule `effect.becomes` reads "a N/N artifact creature" as additive, like "an artifact creature": the types are kept and `artifact` and `creature` are added, the base power and toughness set (CR 613.4b).
- Consequences: `ENGINE_VERSION` 65, `PARSER_VERSION` 68. Tests: `scenario-xx-suspend.test.ts` (the haste is lost to a steal and does not return), `convert-grammar-engine-p63.test.ts` (an artifact enchantment keeps being an enchantment and its subtype, 4/4). The golden snapshot is unchanged in what it reads (only the lowering of one rule).

## D-225: The audit of the limits written since D-175: four more deviations fixed, the rest closed or kept with their reason (2026-11-06)
- Context: The owner asked that nothing supported play "partially" or against the rules. Every item called a limit, a deviation or "not built" in the entries since D-175 (D-175 to D-224), in `docs/ROADMAP.md` and in the table `DEV-01` to `DEV-22` was read against the CR text of `docs/rules/` (`pnpm rule`), and each was either fixed, shown to follow the CR, or kept as a limit that no supported card reaches.
- Decision, fixed (each has a test that failed first): (1) **Path of Ancestry** (D-208): "a creature spell that shares a creature type with your commander" read the types printed on the front face of the card. A commander on the battlefield or on the stack has the creature types it has now (CR 613.1d, 702.73a); only a commander in another zone is the card (`commanderCreatureTypes`, `rules/commander-identity.ts`). (2) **Doubled triggers** (D-220): a "dies" or "leaves the battlefield" ability looks back in time (CR 603.10a), and so does its doubling: the doubler that left in the same events still doubles it (`departedDoublers`, `rules/trigger-doubling.ts`, from last-known information, for the look-back trigger kinds only). (3) **A token that is a copy of a permanent that may enter as a copy** (D-211, "Relm's Sketching" on "Cursed Mirror"): the token asks which creature to become a copy of, the first question it asks (CR 614.12, 616.1c, 707.9), and is made a copy as it enters (`rules/enters-copy.ts`, shared with the card's own entry, `runEnterToken`). (4) **The card revealed for a reveal land** (D-208): with more than one card that qualifies the player chooses which is revealed, whether the land is played, put onto the battlefield by an effect or is a token copy (`chooseCards` of purpose `reveal`, `MoveRequest.entersRevealed`, `ResolutionContext.entersRevealed`, `Instruction` `enterToken.revealed`); a behold with a permanent to choose reveals nothing, which is what a player would choose. (5) **A token that is a copy of a preparation card** (D-214 wrote that it has no prepare spell and cited CR 722.2b, which says the opposite: "The existence and values of these alternative characteristics are part of the object's copiable values"): the token definition carries `prepareOf` (the card whose prepare spell it has, set where a copy is made: `tokenDefinitionOf`, `createCopies`, Encore), `GameObject.token.prepareOf` keeps it, `prepareCardOf`/`hasPrepareSpell` (`rules/prepare.ts`) read it, and a token with the copied "This creature enters prepared." becomes prepared as it is made (`makeTokens`), with the copy of the prepare spell in exile. These five, with D-221 to D-224, are `ENGINE_VERSION` 66.
- Decision, checked against the CR and left as it was: (a) **Alibou's X** (D-218): the CR says a value defined by the text is its definition wherever X is read and "the value of X may change while that spell or ability is on the stack" (CR 107.3c, 107.3i), and that information from the game is determined "when the effect is applied" (CR 608.2h). Each instruction reads the count as it is applied, which is what the engine does (`scenario-xx-amounts.test.ts` pins CR 107.3c already). Damage only marks damage on a creature (CR 120.3e) and a creature with lethal damage dies at the next state-based check (CR 704.5g), after the ability finished resolving, so the damage cannot change the count the scry reads: a test (`convert-grammar-engine-p65.test.ts`) pins X = 3 for both with the target a tapped artifact creature the damage will kill. The brief's reading, a count taken once as the ability begins to resolve, is not what the CR says (an earlier instruction of the same ability that moves a permanent does change the count of a later one), so the engine was not changed. (b) **Magnificent End's cast check** (D-207): CR 601.2 lets a player begin to cast a spell and rewinds it when a requirement cannot be met (CR 601.2, 732: "the game returns to the moment before the casting of that spell was proposed"); a spell shown as castable because its reduction may hold, whose real cost (CR 601.2f, after the targets) cannot be paid, is cancelled, which is the CR's rewind. It is not a deviation. An agent that keeps proposing it is a limit of the agent, not of the rules. (c) **"The doubling does not apply to delayed, monarch, Ring or reflexive triggers"** (D-220): CR 603.2d says an effect that makes a triggered ability of an object trigger additional times "refers only to triggered abilities that object has, not to any delayed or reflexive triggered abilities"; the monarch's and the Ring's abilities belong to no object. The engine follows it. (d) **Ring-bearer that stops being a creature** (D-196): CR 701.54a keeps the designation until another creature becomes the Ring-bearer or another player gains control of it; CR 701.54e only makes "is your Ring-bearer" read the battlefield and the controller. The engine follows it. (e) **"Up to N cards drawn only by the controller of a targeted spell"** (D-217) and **"a delayed mana ability only at a main phase of its controller"**: these name the shapes the grammar reads (Arcane Denial, Mana Sculpt: "its controller", "your next main phase"); any other wording is not read and the card is flagged, so no supported card plays differently. (f) **Doubled "may" triggers ask twice** (D-220): each is a separate triggered ability (CR 603.2d, 603.3d). (h) **A player with no card in hand is asked "may discard a card"** (D-210): the answer does nothing either way, and the players that discarded (for "each player who discarded a card this way draws") are those that did. (i) **A copy that Gogo makes has the copied creature's abilities** (D-212): CR 707.2. (j) **The reveal cost of a behold** reveals nothing when a permanent can be chosen (D-208): a dominated choice, kept.
- Decision, kept as a limit that no supported card reaches, or a limit of the AI or the UI (not a rules deviation): each-player questions asked one after another (`playersMay`, Ruin Grinder and Mog): the owner's decision to leave alone (CR 101.4); the order of the replacements of an entering permanent, of "would die" and counters (DEV-04, on hold by the owner); the web cannot click a permanent that has left the battlefield to connive it first (D-223); an agent that proposes a cast whose cost it cannot pay (Magnificent End) is rewound. The honest refusals (every "not built", "not read" and "refused" of D-175 to D-220: a card that needs one is flagged unsupported by `validateCard` or the grammar, `docs/ROADMAP.md` "Deferred engine features" and "Deferred grammar") do not change the play of a supported card. The rows DEV-02, DEV-07 to DEV-22 are unchanged: none is reached by a supported card in a way a player can tell apart from the CR (DEV-02: the legend rule asked after the other actions of a check gives the player the best of the orders the CR allows).
- Alternatives: Making Alibou's X a snapshot taken at the start of the resolution: rejected, it contradicts CR 107.3c and 608.2h and would make a later instruction of an ability read a stale count. Making Cursed Mirror or the reveal lands unsupported instead of fixing the token path: rejected, the fix is the same question the card already asks, asked for the token.
- Consequences: `ENGINE_VERSION` 66. Tests: `convert-grammar-engine-p49.test.ts` (Path of Ancestry with a commander that became a Frog), `convert-grammar-engine-p67.test.ts` (a doubler that dies with the Wizard, alone, with none), `convert-grammar-engine-p51.test.ts` (a token copy of Cursed Mirror: the choice, none, nothing to copy; a reveal land with two cards, played and as a token, declined, with one; Relm's Sketching on a prepared Pompous Battlemage), `convert-grammar-engine-p65.test.ts` (Alibou), `apps/web/test/sacrifice-choice.test.tsx`.

## D-226: Combat screens: the damage getting through, a docked damage division, blockers beside their attackers with arrows, no play box on the import screen and combat animations (2026-11-08)
- Context: Four owner issues, web only (no engine, parser or protocol change: `ENGINE_VERSION` 66 and `PARSER_VERSION` 68 stay). Issue 106: while blocking, the player could not see how much damage they would take. Issue 92: the modal that divides combat damage covered the battlefield and named the creatures only by name. Issue 19 (items 1 and 3 were done in #37: a click on a land tapped for unspent mana untaps it, and the attack buttons read "Attack with all" and "Declare attackers (N)"): item 2, grouping blockers by the attacker with arrows, and item 4, the "Play this deck" box of the import screen, which the owner called too crowded. Issue 9 (and the rest of #34): combat, damage and deaths pass too quickly to follow.
- Decision: (1) **Damage getting through** (`ui/decisions/combat-damage-preview.ts`, `PassingDamagePanel.tsx`, in the dock of the declare blockers question above "Cost of blocking"). A pure function of the view, the question and the blocks picked so far: for each attacker with no chosen blocker, its derived power (twice with double strike) goes to what it attacks; a blocked attacker with trample puts through what is left over lethal damage to its blockers (toughness minus damage marked, one point with deathtouch, CR 702.19b; with double strike the second strike passes the blockers the first one killed, CR 702.19e); a blocked attacker without trample puts nothing through. The result is one row for each defender, in the attackers' order: "You take 7", the life left ("Life 40 to 33"), the sources with their share, a "Lethal" mark when the damage is at least the life (or at least the loyalty or defense counters of a planeswalker or battle, which "takes" the damage and shows "Destroyed"); infect damage to a player is poison, with the 10 poison check (CR 702.90b). It updates with every pick and release. It reads only public numbers. It is a preview of plain combat damage: first strike killing a blocker early, deathtouch or damage on the blockers' side, prevention, damage doubling, tricks and toxic are not simulated, and the panel says so in one line; the engine stays the judge. (2) **A docked damage division** (`DamagePanel.tsx`, `board-highlight.ts`). The "Divide combat damage" question is a panel in the controls column, like the other panels of a decision, not a modal: the action bar keeps the prompt and Confirm, and the board stays visible and hoverable. Each creature (the attacker and every blocker) is a row with its card face (`CardFace`, as in the hand), power and toughness, damage already marked and the lethal amount; the steppers are as before. Hovering or focusing a row (a stepper inside it counts) shows the card in the preview panel (the hover of the board's tiles) and sets `data-assign-hot` on the creature's tile, which `decisions.css` draws as an accent outline and glow. (3) **Blockers beside their attackers** (`ui/board/combat-order.ts`, `BlockArrows.tsx`). Once blocks are declared, a creature row puts the creatures in blocks first, ordered by the attackers' numbers (the numbers of D-141), the blocked attackers first in the attackers' row, the rest in their places: the blockers of attacker 1 stand together and the first blocked attackers face them. While the player is still picking, nothing moves (a tile never leaves the pointer). An arrow runs from each blocker to the attacker it blocks, in the colour of the pair (`--pair-N`), while picking and after the declaration; the geometry is that of the stack's arrows (`panels/arrows.ts`) and the boxes come from `data-object-id`; a token inside a counted group has an arrow only from the group's first creature. Proximity is the order of the row: a creature cannot move into the other player's row, and drawing a pair as one block on the field would change the layout of every board. (4) **The attack buttons** stay on one line in the narrow controls column (two buttons share the width and the label wraps inside its button; `[data-count="2"]`), "Attack with all" on the left and "Declare attackers (N)" on the right (the owner wrote "Declare Attackers"; the sentence case matches "Block (N)" and "Resolve"). (5) **No play box on the import screen.** `PlayPanel` and `playReport` are gone; the results end with `PlayNote`: "The deck is ready. Save it, then pick it as "Your deck" on the menu to play it.", or the reasons it cannot be played (`playBlockers`, unchanged). The menu picks any saved deck for either seat (D-215), with the seed and the free mulligan, and refuses a deck by the one start rule (D-137); what is lost is playing a pasted list without saving it. (6) **Combat animations** (`ui/board/combat-effects.ts`, `CombatEffects.tsx`, `ui/panels/animations.ts`). From the steps of each snapshot: a red number floats up from a player (their strip) or a permanent that took damage (damage to the same recipient in one step is one number); a permanent that took damage gets a red glow and a short shake (the `translate` property, so its own `transform` is not touched); a permanent that died fades out where it stood, as a grey ghost with its name and "Dies" (the page reads its box from the store's subscription, which runs before React redraws, because the tile is gone after). 400 to 750 ms, at most 24 effects a snapshot, the Web Animations API on elements the layer adds itself to a fixed layer with `pointer-events: none`; no dependency. Visual only: the effects are never awaited, never touch the store, the Worker or the autopilot, so AI turns and autopilot passes run at the same speed. `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` draws nothing (a media rule on the layer and a check in the code). The Settings panel has a "Combat animations" checkbox, on by default, kept in localStorage like the text size and the side (`commander-arena.combat-animations`; without storage it holds for the visit); the page root carries `data-combat-animations`. Two hidden SYNTHETIC decks, `synthetic-trample` and `synthetic-rats`, give the e2e a trampler that the AI blocks (so a division is asked).
- Alternatives: Showing the passing damage as a number on the player's strip only: rejected, it names no source and cannot show a planeswalker; the dock panel has room for the words. Simulating first strike and deathtouch on the blockers' side: not done, the owner's brief excluded it and a wrong forecast is worse than a plain one with its caveat. Keeping the division modal and moving it aside: rejected, a movable modal needs drag handling and the dock already has the pattern and the column. Moving blockers into the attackers' row or pairing tiles side by side: rejected, it changes the layout of every board and fights the rows' scroll and grouping. Arrows from stack-style fixed elements only while picking: rejected, after the declaration the damage step is when the player most needs to tell who fights whom. Animating with CSS keyframes on classes React toggles: rejected, a dying tile no longer exists after the redraw, and a class toggled in render ties the effect to React's pace. An animation library or canvas: rejected, no dependency is needed for three effects. Delaying the next AI action until an effect ends: rejected by the brief; the host and the autopilot never wait on the page. Keeping the play box in a collapsed form: rejected, the owner asked for it gone and the menu now does the job.
- Consequences: A player sees what they will take as they block, can read every creature while dividing damage, sees who blocks whom, and combat damage and deaths are visible for a moment. The damage preview is plain combat damage (it ignores first strike killing a blocker early, prevention and tricks); it never touches the answer sent to the engine. A pasted deck must be saved before it is played (the save message and the results say so); `playReport` and the opponent status line of the box (D-215) are gone, and the opponent of a saved deck is chosen on the menu as before. The ghost of a creature that died is a name card, not its picture. Death effects need the creature in the previous view, so a creature that arrives and dies inside one snapshot shows only its damage number. SPEC changes this needs (the SPEC is not edited here; the owner approves): section 10 "Action bar", "Decisions" and "Board" should say that the declare blockers question shows the damage getting through per defender, that the division of combat damage is a dock panel with the card of each creature and not a modal, that declared blockers stand in the order of their attackers with an arrow from each blocker to its attacker, and that combat animations (damage numbers, a hit flash, a fading ghost of a creature that died) exist, can be switched off in Settings and are off under reduced motion; section 10 "Screens" should drop "Play this deck" from the import screen: a deck is saved there and played from the menu. Tests: `apps/web/test/combat-damage-preview.test.ts`, `passing-damage-render.test.tsx`, `combat-order.test.ts`, `combat-effects.test.ts`, `decisions-render.test.tsx`, `import-ui-render.test.tsx`, and `e2e/combat-screens.e2e.ts` (with `e2e/harness/blocks.ts`), `e2e/import.e2e.ts`, `e2e/decks.e2e.ts`.

## D-227: SPEC section 10 updated for D-199, D-215 and D-226 (2026-11-08)
- Context: D-199 (PR #114), D-215 (PR #118) and D-226 (PR #124) each changed what the web app does and each listed the SPEC section 10 changes it needed, left unapplied because AGENTS.md requires the owner's approval for SPEC edits. Section 10 had drifted from the app: it did not mention the stop for every opponent spell, the top of the stack in the preview panel, the saved decks for either seat, the editable precons, the version line, the land stacks, the damage getting through panel, the docked damage division, the blockers beside their attackers, the attack buttons, the combat animations, and it still listed "Play this deck" on the import screen.
- Decision: The owner approved this update on 2026-11-08, covering exactly these changes and nothing else. Section 10 now says, each confirmed against the code under `apps/web/src`: in "Board", the land stacks (A33) and the blockers' order and arrows (A34); in "Stack panel" and "Action bar", the top of the stack in the preview panel, the announced X, the log line of what resolved (A32) and the attack buttons (A34); in "Auto-pass", the stop for opponent spells (A32); in "Decisions", the damage getting through panel and the docked damage division (A34); in "Information and accessibility", the combat animations and their Settings switch (A34); in "Screens", the pickers with saved decks, the version line, the decks page with editable precons (A33) and the import screen without a play box (A34). Section 17.5 gains A32 (D-199, PR #114), A33 (D-215, PR #118) and A34 (D-226, PR #124), and the opening line of section 17 counts thirty-four amendments up to 2026-11-08. Nothing else in the SPEC and no code changed.
- Alternatives: Leaving the SPEC as it was with the D- entries as the amendments: rejected, the SPEC is the authoritative statement and had become wrong on the screens. Copying the D- entries into section 10: rejected, the SPEC stays short; the entries keep the detail. One amendment for the three entries: rejected, the index lists one amendment per approved change with its D- entry and PR.
- Consequences: Section 10 describes the app as of D-226. `AGENTS.md` and the SPEC's first paragraph still say "A1 to A31" and "31 amendments" (the first is the history of the collapse, D-169); the owner may want `AGENTS.md` updated to "A1 to A34". The three entries' "SPEC changes this needs" lines are now applied.

## D-228: Bigger, slower combat animations with a speed setting and a wait in the autopilot (2026-11-08)
- Context: The owner tried the combat animations of D-226 and said they were too fast and too discreet: effects lasted 400 to 750 ms, a number floated and a tile flashed, and the autopilot passed through the combat steps so quickly that the next step began while an effect was still playing. Issue 9 asked for damage and death to be visible. Web only: no engine, parser or protocol change (`ENGINE_VERSION` 66 and `PARSER_VERSION` 68 stay).
- Decision: (1) **A model that orders and times** (`ui/board/combat-effects.ts`, pure). `combatBeats` turns the steps of one snapshot into beats, in the order a player should see them: the attackers' hits, then the blockers' and other damage, then what follows (life gained, life lost beyond the damage, poison), then deaths. An attacker is a permanent of the previous view's combat (or of the active player when no combat was shown yet). Damage to one recipient inside one step is one beat (all its sources lunge, at most four); damage of 0 shows nothing; infect damage to a player is a poison beat (no life changed: CR 120.3b), damage to a planeswalker reads as loyalty lost; gains, losses and poison show only in a step that dealt damage, so paying life for a land animates nothing. `scheduleBeats(beats, scale)` gives each beat a start: beats start 450 ms apart, a death starts 250 ms after the blow that killed that permanent lands (or in its turn, whichever is later), and no beat starts so late that it ends after the cap of 4 s for the whole snapshot, so the tail of a big combat plays together. The one exception to the cap is a death that has to wait for its killing blow. `scale` is the speed and multiplies every time, the cap included. A snapshot holds at most 24 beats. (2) **What plays** (`ui/board/combat-fx-play.ts`, `combat-fx-dom.ts`, `CombatEffects.tsx`; Web Animations API and CSS only, no library, canvas or dependency; the layer ignores the pointer and is hidden under `prefers-reduced-motion`). At Normal: a hit is 1.8 s with a lunge (1.5 s without an attacker to show, for a spell): each attacker winds back 16 px over 0.3 s and lunges at the recipient (a copy of its tile moves, the real tile dims where it stands; travel is 60% of the distance, at most 160 px, so row clipping never cuts it), the blow lands at 0.5 s with a radial flash, two shockwave rings and 12 sparks (6 when more than 8 beats play), the recipient shakes with a brightness flash and a squash, a glow ring holds around it, a life total swells and settles, and a 40 px outlined number pops to 1.8 times, settles and rises while lingering for 1.3 s. A death is 2 s: the dying tile is copied into the layer the moment the snapshot arrives (it is still on the page then, and a ghost is the card itself now, not a name card), stays until its turn, cracks for 0.5 s (an SVG crack fades in, the copy shakes and flashes), then desaturates, blurs, shrinks and fades while 12 shards fly off it, 8 ash puffs drift up and "Dies" shows under it. A hit on a creature that dies lands on its ghost. Gain, loss and poison beats are 1.4 s: a glow, a burst, a life pulse and a signed number ("+3", "-1 life", "+2 poison"). Tones come from tokens (`--bad`, `--good`, a violet for loss and a lime green for poison with light-theme variants) and every number carries a sign and a word, so no tone is the only cue. (3) **Speed**: Settings has "Animation speed", Fast, Normal, Slow (0.5, 1 and 1.5 times every duration, stagger and cap), kept in localStorage (`commander-arena.animation-speed`) with the other settings, mirrored on `data-animation-speed` of the page; the "Combat animations" switch stays on by default. (4) **The autopilot waits** (`policy/animation-gate.ts`, the one mechanism): the layer `hold`s the gate for the length of the plan it starts (a plan is held for at most 2.5 s, and for the cap's worth of effects of one snapshot that is the longest wait there is), and the store's autopilot `wait`s on it before each automatic pass it sends for the player, after "Passing..." shows and before its 160 ms pause. Only that branch of `drive` waits: a decision of the player, a payment (`payAuto`), the Worker, the host and the AI's search (which runs in the Worker) never look at the gate, so AI decision time does not change. `release` ends every wait at once and is called when the player clicks (the queued click), seizes priority, cancels a Pass Turn, undoes, taps mana back, starts a game or leaves it, so a click is never refused or delayed by a picture. The gate is an option of `createAppStore`; without it (every store test, every engine and AI loop) nothing waits, and the layer holds it only when effects were drawn: switch off, reduced motion and a hidden tab hold nothing. (5) **Tests**: the model (order, stagger, a death after its blow, the cap, Fast and Slow), the gate on a manual clock, the store with a gate through the real host (each automatic pass waits, a wait that never ends sends nothing and a seize ends it), the player on a small fake page (starts, numbers and signs, a ghost kept and removed, `clear`), the settings, and `e2e/combat-screens.e2e.ts`: an effect is still on the page about a second after the first number, numbers last over a second and ghosts over two at Normal, they are staggered, Fast halves and Slow stretches them, the speed is remembered, "Passing" shows and the next log line comes after a pause, a click ends the wait, the switch and reduced motion draw nothing. `e2e/hud.e2e.ts` scopes its "Normal" button to the Text size group because Animation speed has one too.
- Alternatives: A promise the host awaits: rejected, the host and the Worker stay free of the page's pictures (D-226), and only the web policy that passes for the player may wait. Making the autopilot wait on a fixed pause: rejected, it would slow every pass, not only the ones that follow an effect; the gate waits for exactly what was drawn. Waiting for each animation's `finished` promise: rejected, a cancelled or hidden animation never settles, and a plain timer from the plan's total is bounded and testable with a manual clock. Lunging the real tile: rejected, the rows clip (`overflow-y: hidden`); a copy in the layer is free to cross rows. CSS keyframes on classes toggled by React: rejected again (D-226): a dying tile no longer exists after the redraw. Animating the tile's `transform`: rejected, a tapped tile uses it; the individual `translate`, `rotate`, `scale` and `filter` properties compose with it. Canvas particles or an animation library: rejected, small absolutely positioned elements with WAAPI are enough. Setting `reducedMotion` for the whole Playwright config: not done; the e2e files that pass through combat pass with the gate on (it adds seconds, not failures), and each animation test sets what it needs.
- Consequences: A combat is now watchable: hits, lunges and deaths play one after another for about 2 to 4 s at Normal, and the game waits for them (up to 2.5 s) before the next automatic step, with the "Passing..." box visible and clickable. Games with animations on take a few seconds longer per combat that deals damage or kills; the switch and reduced motion restore the old pace, and `?autostart` tests that need speed can turn the switch off. The effects are measured when the snapshot arrives and again when a blow lands; a recipient that has left the page still shows its number where it stood. Known limits: the lunge copy is the tile as drawn, so it does not show the card's picture before it has loaded; standalone loyalty changes from abilities do not animate (only damage to a planeswalker does); attackers that left combat before damage do not lunge; a death that waits for a late killing blow may end a little after the 4 s cap. SPEC changes this needs (the SPEC is not edited here; the owner approves): section 10, where D-226 asks for combat animations, should say that they are paced and queued (a hit about 1.8 s, a death about 2 s at Normal, started 450 ms apart and capped at about 4 s per snapshot), that Settings has "Combat animations" and "Animation speed" (Fast, Normal, Slow, remembered like the other settings), and that the page's autopilot waits for the effects before each automatic pass, for at most 2.5 s and never while the player has a decision, while a click ends the wait at once.

## D-229: The Hofri Ghostforge deck, group 1: graveyard and exile triggers, the second spell of a turn, protection from a color, "isn't a creature", the mana of another player and small statics (2026-11-08)
- Context: The owner's deck `decks/hofri.txt` (issue 128) has 37 cards the engine did not run, in the golden corpus with their real texts (golden before the build: training 163 of 191, hold-out 53 of 60, acceptance 141 of 196, parser 68). The program builds the whole deck in groups on branch `m72-hofri`, one pull request (`docs/proposals/hofri-build-status.md` is the running checklist). Group 1 is the cards that need a trigger, an amount, a condition or a static the engine lacked, and the small keyword protection from a color.
- Decision: (1) **Triggers.** `leftGraveyard` ("one or more cards leave your graveyard", CR 400.7, 603.2c: a batch of the controller's own graveyard, once however many left in one run of events) and `exiledFromLibraryOrGraveyard` (Laelia: cards of the controller put into exile from their library or graveyard), both read from the `zoneChanged` events (`rules/triggers.ts`); `castSpell.nth` ("an opponent casts their second spell each turn", the `spellCast` event carries `nth`, the caster's spells of the turn including this one); the `entersBattlefield` occurrence now knows the player the permanent entered under (`triggerPlayer`). Tocasia's Welcome and Staff of the Storyteller reuse `entersBatch` (creatures with a mana value, and "you create one or more creature tokens", which CR 701.7a defines as tokens entering). (2) **Amount and condition.** `Amount` and `StaticPtAmount` `commanderCasts` (CR 903.8: the commanders of the controller cast from the command zone, summed; `of: 'triggerSubject'` is the one commander the spell is); the `PlayerStat` `lands`; the condition `subjectControllerHasMore` (Archaeomancer's Map: "if that player controls more lands than you", an intervening "if" that keeps the trigger subject on the stack); the condition `cardsInGraveyard` (plain: no characteristic, so a layer 4 static may have it). (3) **Statics.** `untapInOthersUntapStep` (Drumbellower: `rules/untap-others.ts`, run as the untap step begins, with the active player's own untap; a stun counter is removed instead, "doesn't untap" is said of the controller's own step); `loseTypes` ("~ isn't a creature", layer 4: a `setTypes` change with `remove`; the subtypes only that type allowed go with it, CR 205.1a). (4) **Protection from a color** (CR 702.16, `rules/protection.ts`): damage that would be dealt to a permanent with protection from a color of the source is prevented (applied before the other prevention effects: the affected player may choose the order, CR 616.1, and taking protection first never costs them), it cannot be enchanted or equipped by an Aura or Equipment of that color (`canAttach`), cannot be blocked by creatures of that color, and cannot be targeted by spells or abilities from sources of that color (`canBeTargetedBy` takes the source). Protection from anything but colors is not read. (5) **Mana and costs.** `chooseOne.chooser` and `addMana.player` ("Target player adds one mana of any color": the lowering builds a `chooseOne` of five `addMana` for that player's pool, chosen by the target player; the ability uses the stack, CR 605.1a); `spentRider` `commander` and `scryCommanderCasts` (Study Hall: scry X where X is the times that commander has been cast from the command zone, read as the scry resolves); the costs "Mill a card" (an ordinary ability pays it, CR 118.3: not payable with fewer cards), "Exile ~" (`exileThis` from the battlefield too) and "Discard this card" (the ability then works from the hand, as Cycling does), `ObjectFilter.attackingOrBlocking` (Gideon's Memorial), the duration `forAsLongAsYouControlThis` of `grantKeyword` (Thancred Waters). (6) **Parser** (stage P68): rules in `trigger/hofri.ts`, `condition/hofri.ts`, `cost/hofri.ts`, `effect/hofri.ts`, `amount/hofri.ts`, `static/hofri.ts`, `keyword/protection.ts`; "Protection from red" is now read, so the tests that used it as the unsupported keyword use "Banding". Web: the wording of the new triggers, conditions, amounts, the rider and the filter. `ENGINE_VERSION` 67, `PARSER_VERSION` 69.
- Alternatives: A trigger per event with a list of cards for Spirit of Resilience now: left to the group that builds it (the trigger needs `triggerCards`). "Target player adds one mana of any color" as a new decision kind: rejected, a `chooseOne` whose chooser is the target is the existing decision with a seat. Reading "isn't a creature" as setting the types: rejected, the layer 4 effect that removes a type is what the CR says (205.1a) and keeps the other types. Applying protection as a regular prevention effect in the order of D-191: rejected for now, protection prevents all the damage, so applying it first is the best order for the affected player and the only observable difference is a shield used or not (listed in `docs/ROADMAP.md`).
- Consequences: 17 real cards of the golden corpus read and are supported (the 16 of the deck and Otawara): Archaeomancer's Map, Drumbellower, Gideon's Memorial, Karmic Guide, Laelia, Monologue Tax, Phoenix Down, both Quintorius, Spirit Mascot, Staff of the Storyteller, Study Hall, Thancred Waters, The Warring Triad, Tocasia's Welcome, Vanguard of the Restless. Golden after the group: training 163 of 191, hold-out 54 of 60, acceptance 157 of 196; no supported card changed its AST. Limits: `docs/ROADMAP.md`, "Hofri deck leftovers".


## D-230: The Hofri Ghostforge deck, group 2: returns from the graveyard, Backup, finality counters, "that card", linked exile of a token and Hofri's copies (2026-11-08)
- Context: Group 2 of the whole-deck program (D-229, `docs/proposals/hofri-build-status.md`) is the cards that bring cards back from a graveyard or exile with a limit that is an amount, with an exception, or as a copy: Teshar, Venerable Warsinger, Guardian Scalelord (Backup), Sevinne's Reclamation, Excava, Valkyrie's Call, Storm of Souls, Ceaseless Conflict, Fiend Hunter, Hofri Ghostforge and Ao, the Dawn Sky. Golden before the group: training 163 of 191, hold-out 54 of 60, acceptance 157 of 196 (parser 69).
- Decision: (1) **Mana value limited by an amount.** `ObjectFilter.manaValueAtMost: Amount` ("mana value X or less, where X is this creature's power" and "... the amount of damage dealt to that player"), read when the filter is read as targets are chosen and again as the ability resolves (CR 202.3, 608.2b); the amount is one that needs no target (`manaValueLimitOf` in `rules/select.ts`, kept in `select.ts` because `amounts.ts` imports it). The parser reads "with mana value X or less" with a "where X is" clause, and "historic" (CR 700.6: an artifact, a legendary permanent or a Saga). (2) **Backup** (CR 702.165): the keyword `backup { count }`; `derive-keywords.ts` writes the enters trigger from the abilities printed after the keyword, and the new effect `grantAbility` (layer 6, until end of turn) gives them to a creature that is another one; the abilities are fixed as the ability goes on the stack (CR 702.165d). Only the engine writes `grantAbility`. (3) **Finality counters** (CR 122.1h): a permanent with one that would go to a graveyard from the battlefield is exiled instead (`rules/zones.ts`). (4) **"That card"** of a dies trigger: `ObjectRef` `triggerCard` (CR 400.7, 603.10a), the card the subject became in the graveyard while it is still there; a token is none. `triggerSubject` stays on the stack for the triggers that read it (`readsTriggerSubject`), and an intervening "if" about the controller of the subject (`subjectControllerHasMore`) is checked on resolution. (5) **A token that copies a creature** gets `addSubtypes` (it is a Spirit besides, CR 707.9b, 205.1b), `abilities` and `linkExiled` (the token remembers the card the effect before it exiled, CR 607.2a; its leaves-the-battlefield ability returns it with `linkedExile`, which now falls back to last-known information once the token is gone). (6) **"Copy this spell"** (`copySpell` of `thisSpell`, Sevinne's Reclamation: a spell cast from a graveyard is copied as it resolves, a new target may be chosen). (7) **A destroy that counts** the nontoken creatures its controller controlled that it destroyed (`thisWay` `destroyedOwnNontoken`, CR 608.2c). (8) **A look with a total mana value** (`lookAtTop.take.totalManaValue`, Ao): the cards taken add up to the limit or less (CR 202.3), checked by the engine on the answer (`ChooseCardsDecision.totalManaValue`) and listed by `legalActionsForDecision` only when they fit; Aura cards put onto the battlefield from the library choose what they enchant (`withAuraEntries`, CR 303.4f). (9) The parser's segmenter no longer splits a sentence at the comma between two modifiers ("nontoken, non-Angel"), and the cost reduction of spells refuses a modifier it would have dropped ("Historic spells you cast cost {1} less" was read as every spell: a silent drop, now refused as before).
- Alternatives: The Backup trigger as a card-side expansion in the parser: rejected, the keyword has to stay a keyword so the engine can order and display it, and the abilities printed below it are the object's. A `Keyword` for finality: rejected, it is a counter kind the zone-change replacement reads. Choosing the amount of mana value from a target for Guardian Scalelord's trigger: the amount is the power of the source as the ability resolves (the text says so), no target involved.
- Consequences: 11 real cards of the deck read and are supported (the list above); the golden snapshot moves to training 163 of 191, hold-out 54 of 60, acceptance 168 of 196, with no supported card losing its status. Spirit of Resilience (the cards that left, `triggerCards`) and Coin of Fate are still open. Limits: `docs/ROADMAP.md`, "Hofri deck leftovers".


## D-231: The Hofri Ghostforge deck, group 3: exile until an opponent becomes the monarch, an exiled card's owner, each player exiles from their graveyard, the permanents each player keeps (2026-11-08)
- Context: Group 3 of the whole-deck program (D-229, `docs/proposals/hofri-build-status.md`): Palace Jailer, Skyclave Apparition, Augusta, Order Returned and Tragic Arrogance (Fiend Hunter, planned for it, came with group 2). Golden before the group: training 163 of 191, hold-out 54 of 60, acceptance 168 of 196 (parser 70).
- Decision: (1) **"Until an opponent becomes the monarch"** (CR 610.3): `exile.until: 'opponentBecomesMonarch'`.
