The second one-shot effect is the engine's `ExileReturn` (`rules/exile-return.ts`) with `untilMonarch`: `becomeMonarch` and the loss rule `monarchAfterLoss` (CR 725.3, 725.4) go through one function that moves the designation, stamps `GameState.monarchBecameAt` for the seat and marks the returns of other players `released`; `settle` returns them under their owners' control, whatever happens to the permanent. CR 610.3b: if an opponent became the monarch after the ability went on the stack, as the exile would happen, nothing is exiled (the stamp is compared with the timestamp of the ability). (2) **An X/X token with an amount** (`createToken` of a custom token with `ptAmount`, CR 111.4: its power and toughness are read as it is created) made by the owner of the card a permanent exiled (`controller: ownerOf linkedExile`), with `manaValueOf linkedExile`: Skyclave Apparition. The exile of its first ability is marked linked by `parse-face` as soon as another ability reads the cards (CR 607.2a). (3) **"Each player exiles a card from their graveyard"** (`exileOwnGraveyardCard`, CR 701.13, 101.4): each player chooses among their own cards, the active player first (`chooseMove` with the choosing seat, a `choosePermanent`-free `chooseCards` decision of the player); a card that really went to exile and is not a land is counted as `thisWay` `exiledNonland` (a commander that goes to the command zone instead is not). The `reflexive` effect has `ifThisWay`: "When one or more nonland cards are exiled this way" (CR 603.12) is created only when that count is positive, and the count ("that many") is carried to the ability with the trigger (`PendingTrigger.thisWayBefore`, `StackData.thisWayBefore`). (4) **Tragic Arrogance** (`sparePermanents`, `rules/spare.ts`, CR 608.2d, 701.21a, 101.4): the controller of the effect chooses, for each player (the active player first) and each card type the text lists, a permanent of that type the player controls (a decision `choosePermanent` of purpose `spare`, asked only with two or more candidates), then every player sacrifices the nonland permanents they control that were not chosen, together. (5) The reading of "nonland, nontoken permanent" (a comma between two modifiers), the segmenter keeps the sentences of the two new instructions together (`splitSentences`).
- Alternatives: Reading "until an opponent becomes the monarch" as a state (the monarch is an opponent now) instead of an event: rejected, a creature exiled when an opponent was already the monarch would come back at once and the rule says the player has to become it (CR 610.3). A general "that many" for any earlier instruction: kept to what the reflexive ability counts, for now. Forbidding the same permanent for two of the types in Tragic Arrogance: the text names no such limit and the Comprehensive Rules have none; the choice is the player's (the owner confirmed this reading on 2026-11-08; recorded in `docs/ROADMAP.md`).
- Consequences: 4 real cards of the deck read and are supported (Palace Jailer, Skyclave Apparition, Augusta, Tragic Arrogance); the golden snapshot moves to training 163 of 191, hold-out 54 of 60, acceptance 172 of 196, with no supported card losing its status. Agents: the casual agent (and so the heuristic one) keeps the most valuable of its own permanents and the least valuable of the others' (`chooseSparedPermanent`). Web: the prompt of the `spare` choice, the wording of `exiledNonland`. Limits: `docs/ROADMAP.md`, "Hofri deck leftovers".


## D-232: The Hofri Ghostforge deck, group 4: "once during each of your turns, you may play a land or cast a spell from your graveyard" (2026-11-08)
- Context: Group 4 of the whole-deck program (D-229, `docs/proposals/hofri-build-status.md`): Edgar, Master Machinist (cast an artifact spell from the graveyard, which enters tapped) and Serra Paragon (play a land or cast a permanent spell with mana value 3 or less from the graveyard, which gains an ability). Golden before the group: training 163 of 191, hold-out 54 of 60, acceptance 172 of 196 (parser 71).
- Decision: A static ability `playFromGraveyardOnceEachTurn { cast?, land?, entersTapped?, gains? }` of a permanent (CR 601.2a, 305.1, 113.6, 604.1), read from the abilities the permanent has (`derive-statics.ts`, `graveyardPlaySources`) and used by `rules/graveyard-play.ts`: in the turn of the controller (the permission is "during each of your turns") a card of their graveyard that `cast` matches (as the card it is) may be cast, or a land played, at the timing of its type and for its ordinary cost; each permission is used once a turn whatever it is used for (`TurnLog.graveyardPlays`, a use marks it when the cast begins, so a cancelled cast gives it back with the state before it). A card that has its own permission to be cast from the graveyard (D-133) is cast with that one and uses nothing of this. What the permanent the card becomes has because of it is kept on the spell (`StackData.graveyardPlay`) and applied as it enters the battlefield: it enters tapped (a spell only, "that artifact") and gains the triggered ability (a continuous effect `grantAbility` that lasts, CR 611.2a, so the ability is read when it leaves the battlefield, CR 603.10a). A land played from the graveyard counts as the land drop (CR 305.2) and gains the ability too (Serra: "it gains"). The parser reads the rule as one line (`static.graveyard-play-once-each-turn`); a "permanent spell" is an artifact, creature, enchantment, planeswalker or battle spell.
- Alternatives: Reading the permission as a `mayCast` continuous effect given at the start of each turn: rejected, the permission belongs to the permanent while it has the ability and ends with it. A once-a-turn mark kept on the permanent: rejected, `TurnLog` is the place that resets every turn.
- Consequences: Edgar, Master Machinist and Serra Paragon read and are supported; golden after the group: training 163 of 191, hold-out 54 of 60, acceptance 174 of 196, with no supported card losing its status. The web lists the graveyard cards by the options of the priority decision, so nothing else is needed there; the agents pick from the same options. Limits: `docs/ROADMAP.md`, "Hofri deck leftovers".


## D-233: The Hofri Ghostforge deck, group 5: exile cards from the graveyard as a cost, the cards a cost exiled, the cards that left a graveyard (2026-11-08)
- Context: Group 5 of the whole-deck program (D-229, `docs/proposals/hofri-build-status.md`): Coin of Fate (the cost "Exile two creature cards from your graveyard", an opponent chooses one of the exiled cards) and Spirit of Resilience ("Whenever one or more cards leave your graveyard, put a +1/+1 counter on this creature, then you may have it become a copy of an artifact or creature card from among those cards"). Golden before the group: training 163 of 191, hold-out 54 of 60, acceptance 174 of 196 (parser 72).
- Decision: (1) **The cost `exileFromGraveyard` of an activated ability** (CR 118.1, 406.1, 602.2b; it is in `SUPPORTED_FEATURES.costKinds` now, and refused as an additional cost of a spell, where the cast flow does not pay it): paid after the discard (`rules/activate.ts`, `payExileCards`): with exactly as many matching cards in the graveyard as asked the engine exiles them, with more a `chooseCards` decision of purpose `exile` with `forCost` asks (`cancel` rewinds the activation, CR 733); the objects the cards became in exile are kept by the ability on the stack (`StackData.exiledAsCost`, read as `ResolutionContext.costExiled`). The activation is offered only when enough cards match (`costRefusal`). (2) **`splitCostExiled`** (CR 608.2d, 400.7): an opponent of the controller (the first in turn order that is still in the game: with the two players of v1 there is only one) chooses one of the cards the cost exiled (a `chooseCards` decision of purpose `split`, none when only one is left); it goes to the bottom of the controller's library and the other, if it is still in exile, returns to the battlefield tapped under the controller's control. The effect needs a cost that exiles cards (`validateCard`). (3) **The cards that left a graveyard**: a `leftGraveyard` trigger carries every card of its controller that left their graveyard in the events that triggered it, as the objects they became (`PendingTrigger.cards`, `StackData.triggerCards`, `ResolutionContext.triggerCards`), the way `triggerSubject` is carried. (4) **`becomeCopyOfCard`** (CR 707.2, 613.2a, 400.7): of those cards, the ones with an artifact or creature card type, in whatever zone they are now (a card that moved again is a new object and is not found), the controller chooses one when there are several (a `chooseCards` decision of purpose `copy`, which shows the cards with the decision), and the permanent becomes a copy of it until end of turn (`rules/copy-card.ts`, the layer 1 effect of `becomes a copy`, `copyEffect`). The `may` before it asks even when no card can be copied. (5) Parser: `cost.exile-graveyard-cards` (one pattern, so a line that is another cost leaves no trace), `effect.opponent-splits-exiled` (two sentences kept together), `effect.become-copy-of-those-cards` (reads "you may" itself, as `effect.return-chosen-card` does, so that "then you may ..." works).
- Alternatives: An opponent chosen by the controller when there are several: not built, v1 is one opponent; recorded in `docs/ROADMAP.md`. The cards a cost exiled as an `ObjectRef` (like `sacrificedCost`): rejected for now, the only reader is `splitCostExiled`, which names what it does with them.
- Consequences: Coin of Fate and Spirit of Resilience read and are supported; golden after the group: training 163 of 191, hold-out 54 of 60, acceptance 176 of 196, with no supported card losing its status. Agents: the opponent agent picks, for `split`, the card it fears most (it goes to the bottom of the library); for `copy` the creature card with the most power. Web: the words of the two decisions (`cards-picker.ts`). Limits: `docs/ROADMAP.md`, "Hofri deck leftovers".


## D-234: The Hofri Ghostforge deck, group 6: phasing (2026-11-08)
- Context: Group 6 of the whole-deck program (D-229, `docs/proposals/hofri-build-status.md`): Guardian of Faith ("When this creature enters, any number of other target creatures you control phase out", CR 702.26). Golden before the group: training 163 of 191, hold-out 54 of 60, acceptance 176 of 196 (parser 73).
- Decision: A permanent that phases out is kept in a zone of its own, `'phased'` (`GameState.phased`, `GameObject.zone`, `GameObject.phasedBy`: the player who controlled it as it phased out), so that every rule that looks at the battlefield, at the zone of an object or at a target does not see it (CR 702.26b: "treated as though it does not exist"): it is no legal target, state-based actions and triggers skip it, nothing counts it. It is the same object: no zone-change event, so no leaves-the-battlefield or enters trigger (CR 702.26d), and its counters, damage, tapped status, attachments, timestamp (so its summoning sickness) stay; it is taken out of combat (CR 506.4, 702.26b). The Auras, Equipment and Fortifications attached to it phase out with it, indirectly, and phase in with it (CR 702.26g, 702.26h). It phases in as the untap step of the player who controlled it as it phased out begins, before the untap (CR 702.26a, `rules/phasing.ts`, `flow.ts`). The effect is `phaseOut { objects }`; the view lists the phased-out permanents (`GameView.phasedOut`) and the web shows a "Phased out" button beside the exile. The target slot "any number of other target creatures you control" is `TargetSpec.anyNumber` (none at least, every legal target at most). The parser reads "<operand> phase(s) out" (`effect.phase-out`) and `noun.any-number-targets` accepts "other".
- Alternatives: A flag `phasedOut` on a permanent that stays in the battlefield list: rejected, state-based actions, the invariants and the many reads of `zone === 'battlefield'` would each need the exception. A new `Zone` only for the AST: not needed, `ZONES` lists it so the type holds it, and no card text names it.
- Consequences: Guardian of Faith reads and is supported; golden after the group: training 163 of 191, hold-out 54 of 60, acceptance 177 of 196, with no supported card losing its status. Not built: the keyword Phasing (a permanent that phases out in each of its controller's untap steps), phasing in the untap step of a player who has left the game (CR 702.26k, 702.26n: the phased-out permanents of a player who loses stay phased out), "phase in" as an effect, the continuous effects that end as an object phases out beyond those that already end as it leaves the battlefield. `docs/ROADMAP.md`, "Hofri deck leftovers".


## D-235: The Hofri Ghostforge deck, group 7: Class cards and the level bar, a random exile from the graveyard, spells cast from anywhere but the hand (2026-11-08)
- Context: Group 7 of the whole-deck program (D-229, `docs/proposals/hofri-build-status.md`): Advanced Reconstruction, a Class (CR 716): a first main phase trigger that mills and exiles a random card of the graveyard (which may be played), and two level bars whose abilities are "whenever one or more cards leave your graveyard, this Class deals 2 damage to each opponent" and "spells you cast from anywhere other than your hand cost {2} less to cast". Golden before the group: training 163 of 191, hold-out 54 of 60, acceptance 177 of 196 (parser 74).
- Decision: (1) **The layout `class`** (one face: an enchantment with the subtype Class, CR 716.1; `SUPPORTED_FEATURES.layouts`, `validate-layouts.ts`). (2) **The level bar** (CR 716.2, 716.2a): the activated ability `{cost}: Level N` is an ordinary activated ability with the effect `gainLevel { level }`, `timing: 'sorcery'` and `activateOnlyIf: classLevelIs { level: N-1 }`; the abilities printed with a bar are the new ability kind `level { level, abilities }` that follows it in the face; the permanent has those abilities as long as its level is at least `level` (a permanent with no level is at level 1, CR 716.2d). The level is `GameObject.level`, a designation that is not a copiable value (CR 716.2b): `copiableValues` hands out the abilities of the object's own level (`atLevel`), so the derived abilities, the triggers, the statics and the activations all see the Class as it is at its level (the index of an ability among the derived abilities changes with the level; an activation stores its ability, so one in progress is not affected). `GameObject.level` is shown in the view (`ObjectView.level`) and in the web preview. (3) **`exileRandomFromGraveyard`** (CR 701.13): one card of the controller's graveyard picked with the game's generator; it is what `moved` names, so `mayPlay` ("You may play the exiled card this turn") follows it. (4) **`ObjectFilter.notCastFromHand`** (CR 601.2a, 601.2f): a spell on the stack that was cast from another zone, read as the cost is determined (the cost code passes the zone the card comes from, as the card has not moved yet, `SelectContext.castFrom`). (5) Parser (stage P75): the level bar line gets its period (`normalize.ts`), `effect.gain-class-level`, `effect.exile-random-and-play` (two sentences kept together), `static.spells-cost-reduction` reads "from anywhere other than your hand", "this Class" is the permanent itself, and `parse-face.ts` groups a Class's abilities by level bar (bars out of order refuse the card).
- Alternatives: A counter for the level: rejected, CR 716.2b says it is a designation that stays when the permanent stops being a Class and is not a counter. One `level` field on every ability: rejected, a wrapper kind keeps the other ability kinds as they are.
- Consequences: Advanced Reconstruction reads and is supported; golden after the group: training 163 of 191, hold-out 54 of 60, acceptance 178 of 196, with no supported card losing its status (Caretaker's Talent, the other Class of the golden corpus, stays unread: its "when this Class becomes level 2" trigger is not read). The deck test `hofri-deck.test.ts` lists no pending card; Turbulent Steppe is still missing from the golden corpus. Limits: `docs/ROADMAP.md`, "Hofri deck leftovers".

## D-236: Turbulent Steppe: "enters tapped unless your opponents control N or more lands" (2026-11-08)
- Context: The last card of `decks/hofri.txt` (issue 128, D-229 and following) was Turbulent Steppe. The owner pasted its text ("({T}: Add {R} or {W}.)" and "This land enters tapped unless your opponents control eight or more lands.", type line "Land — Mountain Plains"); the Scryfall extraction (`pnpm corpus:extract`) is not in the repository yet and Scryfall is not reachable from the sandbox, so the card is treated as read from the owner's text and no golden line or Scryfall record was written. Run through the parser, the reminder text and the two basic land types already read; only "your opponents control eight or more lands" stopped (`replacement.enters-tapped-unless`, the slot `condition`). The engine already had everything needed: `amountIs` of a `countOf` whose filter has `controller: 'opponent'` counts the permanents of every opponent together through `controllerOf` (CR 110.2, 613.1b), and the `entersTapped.unless` replacement reads any condition with the permanent not yet on the battlefield (CR 614.12).
- Decision: One parser rule, `condition.opponents-control-at-least` (`rules/condition/hofri.ts`, `PARSER_VERSION` 76): "your opponents control N or more <plural permanent phrase>" with N one or more, no controller, no "other" and no zone of its own, lowered as the engine's `amountIs { amount: countOf { filter { ..., controller: 'opponent' } }, compare: atLeast N }`. It is not `opponentControlsAtLeast` (D-135), which is "an opponent controls": some one opponent. With several opponents the lands of all of them are counted together, which is how "your opponents control" reads (CR 102.2 makes each of them an opponent; the text names the group, not one of them). The game has two seats today (one human against one AI), so the difference cannot show; I found no ruling on this wording and did not guess a different one. No engine change: `ENGINE_VERSION` stays 73 and the derive digests need no new recording. The Steppe is not special-cased and is covered by its own tests (`convert-grammar-engine-p73.test.ts`: it reads completely from the owner's text, 7 lands keep it tapped, 8 untap it, your own lands do not count, control and not ownership decides the side) until the owner's `corpus:extract` lands it in the golden corpus; `hofri-deck.test.ts` then measures the real record and will fail if it does not read.
- Alternatives: A new engine condition kind `opponentsControlAtLeast`: rejected, `amountIs` of a `countOf` already says it and is validated (D-131); one more kind would be a second way to say the same count. Extending `controlsAtLeast` with an opponent filter: rejected, it counts "you" by definition and the validator refuses another controller (D-135 chose the same split). Writing a Steppe line into `golden.jsonl` or inventing a Scryfall record: rejected (AGENTS.md: never invent data).
- Consequences: Turbulent Steppe reads and is supported from the owner's text; the golden snapshot is unchanged except for its parser version (no supported card gained or lost anything); the corpus-replay line "~ enters tapped unless your opponents control eight or more lands." (8 cards in the first corpus run) now reads. Limits, in `docs/ROADMAP.md`: the card is measured by the deck test only once the owner extracts the real record; the count is of all opponents together with more than two players.

## D-237: The AI never casts a creature that X sizes at an X that kills it (2026-11-09)
- Context: Issue 131 (child of issue 80). The owner saw the AI cast Shivan Devastator, a 0/0 that "enters with X +1/+1 counters on it", with X = 0: it entered and died (CR 704.5f). The cause: `spellPlays` (`casual-priority.ts`, shared by the casual, greedy and heuristic agents) skipped an instant or sorcery with an {X} when X could only be 0 (D-103) but cast every permanent "whatever X can be", and `chooseXAnswer` takes all the X on offer, which is 0 when the agent has one land for {X}{R}.
- Decision: One reading of the view, `minXToSurvive` (`casual-x.ts`): for a creature whose text says it enters with X +1/+1 counters, the least X is 1 minus its printed toughness (1 for a 0/0; 0 for a body that survives with no counters). `xSpellHasRoom` asks for the mana of the rest of the cost (`effectiveCost`, so reductions and commander tax count) plus that least X for each {X}, and `needsPaidX` makes such a creature, like an X instant or sorcery, a play only when cast with its mana cost paid (X is 0 for a free or alternative cast, CR 107.3b) and with room for that X. The agent therefore does not cast it when X = 0 is all it can pay, and `chooseXAnswer` never answers below the least X (it still takes all the X on offer otherwise, so it spends the mana it has). Greedy and heuristic go through `spellPlays` and get the same rule; the random agent plays randomly on purpose. Static effects that would keep a smaller creature alive (a lord) are not read, so the agent is only ever too cautious.
- Alternatives: A special case for the card by name: refused (AGENTS.md). Simulating the cast in the engine to see whether the permanent survives: rejected for the casual agent (no simulation there) and not needed, the printed toughness and the counters are the whole of it for this wording. Treating every permanent with an {X} like an instant: rejected, a creature with a body that survives X = 0, or whose X sets no size, is still a creature.
- Consequences: An X creature that is dead at X = 0 is held until there is mana for it. The room test for instants and sorceries now counts the mana value of the rest of the cost (not the number of symbols) and one {X} payment for each {X}; this only makes the agent more careful. Limits, in `docs/ROADMAP.md`. `ENGINE_VERSION` unchanged (a SYNTHETIC fixture, `SYNTHETIC Hydra Zero`, was added to the engine fixtures for the tests).

## D-238: A token the card makes shows its abilities in quotes as rules text (2026-11-09)
- Context: The owner saw the Smaug token of There and Back Again without its last ability. The engine had it (flying, haste and "When Smaug dies, create fourteen Treasure tokens" are abilities of the token definition, and the scenario tests play the death trigger), but the definition's `oracleText` was `''` for every token the parser made, and the card face prints `oracleText`: a keyword showed as a chip, an ability in quotes showed nowhere.
- Decision: `tokenRulesText` (`lower/tokens.ts`) gives a custom token that has at least one ability in quotes its rules text: its keywords as one line ("Flying, haste"), then each quoted ability as the card writes it, one to a line. The quote was read with `~` for the token, so the words say what the card prints: the name the card gives the token (Smaug), or else "this creature" ("When this creature dies, you gain 1 life."), capitalized after a cost colon or a period as printed; a `~` inside a quote of the quote is another token's and stays. A token with no quoted ability keeps `''`, because its keywords are the chips. `PARSER_VERSION` 77.
- Alternatives: The text for every custom token, keywords too: rejected, it changes every flying token for words the chips already show, and churns every test that spells out one. Words composed in the web app from the abilities (the engine nodes): rejected, the engine and the golden snapshot would keep a token with no text, and the web would need a second composer for what the card already prints. Leaving `~` in the text: rejected, it would print as is.
- Consequences: Smaug and every token with quoted abilities (Pests, Eldrazi Spawn, Dragon Egg, Servos, Spirits with a death trigger) show their abilities on the card face and in the preview. The text is part of the token's copiable values (CR 707.2), which it should be: a copy of the token has it too. The derive fingerprints were re-recorded because the ring fixture's Smaug has the text; no engine rule changed (`ENGINE_VERSION` unchanged). Tokens from a Treasure-like preset or a copy have their own text paths and are unchanged.

## D-239: Layout polish: no stray scroll bar, the face-down card inside its place, a choice bubble that is always on screen (issues 138, 59 and 85, 2026-11-09)
- Context: The owner saw "two scroll bars out of nowhere" at 1798x1003 (issue 138), a face-down card drawn over its area (issue 59, at 1293x557) and the Play / Cycle bubble of a land below the window (issue 85). Web only: no engine, parser or protocol change.
- Decision: (1) **Scroll bars.** The headless browser of the tests hides bars, so the cause was found with a visible-bar run (`--hide-scrollbars` off) and a probe of every element: the card box of the info column, `.board-preview`, was a pixel too narrow for its card (`--preview-card-w` took off the column's padding and the box's own, but not the column's right border), so the card overflowed by one pixel and a horizontal bar showed under it, beside the vertical bar of the log. `--preview-card-w` is 35px less than the column, the box has `overflow-x: hidden` and the card is `min(--preview-card-w, 100%)`, so a vertical bar (a card taller than the box) never adds a horizontal one. The bars that belong stay: the log, the stack list and, for a card with a long rules text, the box of the card. `e2e/scrollbars.e2e.ts` reads the geometry (an `overflow: auto` or `scroll` element, not `scrollbar-width: none`, with content larger than its box) at every step of a mid-game with the stack and a decision, at 1366x768 and 1798x1003: no bar on the page, no horizontal bar, no scrolling area inside another. (2) **Face-down card.** The exile viewer's card button (`.board-zone-card`) had the height of the card, and its label ("Opponent's", "Graveyard ability") hung under it, outside the button and out of the viewer's scroll area, which then scrolled; the button is as tall as card plus label (the card keeps its own height). The strip of cards in exile lost the bullet of its list. (3) **The choice bubble.** `placePopover` (pure) puts the popover under the card it points at when all of it fits there, above the card when not, and always inside the decision layer (pushed in from every edge); a hand card rests with its lower part under the window edge, so for it the bubble opens above. `Popover.tsx` is the frame of every popover of the layer (ability menu, mana colour, sacrifice choice) and `usePopoverPlace` measures it before the paint, reads the card again after its lift transition (`transitionend`) and on resize. The first item is focused without scrolling; the arrow keys, Enter and Esc work as before.
- Alternatives: Hiding the preview's scroll bar (`scrollbar-width: none`): rejected, a long card would silently be cut off. One scroll area for the whole info column: rejected, the log has to keep its place. Fixing the bubble at a side of the card: rejected, the room on each side changes with the window.
- Consequences: A card longer than its box still shows a vertical bar beside the log's (two bars, side by side); shortening what the preview prints (the keyword reminders) would remove that, and is left open. The geometry check of `scrollbars.e2e.ts` can be used for any new panel.

## D-240: Bigger cards and the whole picture: the art is no longer darkened (issue 137, 2026-11-09)
- Context: The owner asked for bigger cards and more visible art ("it feels like the art is a bit darkened, is it?") and decided it is not a setting: make them bigger and brighter. The darkening was real: `.board-tile-art` (the picture behind a permanent's tile) had `filter: brightness(0.62)` so the text laid over it could be read. The hand, the zone viewer and the preview panel never had a filter. Web only.
- Decision: (1) **Brightness.** The filter is gone. The name of a tile sits on a title bar of its own (the ground colour at 78 percent, as the title line of a printed card; also the token line); the chips, the counters, the damage mark and the power and toughness already had their own backing, so no text depends on the picture. (2) **Size.** The largest tile of each row is a quarter bigger (`ROW_SHAPE` in `Row.tsx`: creatures 136 (108 before), other permanents 105 (84), lands 88 (70, `landSpec`); the text size factor still multiplies them), the hand cards and the cards of the zone viewer are 135 by 188 (108 by 150), and the hand area, the part of a card that shows at rest, is 108px in a short window and grows a little with it (`Hand.tsx` reads the height it was given). The window decides the height of a row, not the cap, so the creature row takes a larger share of the field (`flex` 1.6 against 1 for each of the others, 1.85 from 900px high and 2 from 1000px) and the hand area stays near its old height (`clamp(108px, 12vh, 128px)`). Measured on a full board (5 creatures, 3 other permanents, 9 lands against 4, 2 and 8; text size Large; width by height of one tile, before then after): at 1366x768 creatures 50x67 then 56x75, other permanents 41x46 then 38x42, lands 58 then 53; at 1440x900 creatures 68x92 then 84x113, other 59x65 then 50x55, lands 64 then 69; at 1798x1003 creatures 82x111 then 103x139, other 71x79 then 58x64, lands 80 then 63; at 1920x1080 creatures 93x126 then 115x156, other 81x90 then 65x72, lands 84 then 73; the hand card 130x180 then 162x226 at every size. An empty creature row is only its label (34px, as the row of other permanents is 26px when empty), so a player with lands and no creatures gives the lands the room, and the land row's extra share for deep stacks grows with the creature row's (`landGrow` 1.4 and 1.6 against 1.2 and 1.35), so a stack of equal lands still shows at 1366x768 as it did (`e2e/land-groups.e2e.ts` failed on the first version of this change and passes now). The land stacks (D-215) keep their rules (a shallower column in a short row), the stack tile stays 48. (3) The preview panel's card is unchanged (it already shows the whole picture at the width of the column).
- Alternatives: A setting for the picture's brightness: refused by the owner. A lighter filter (0.8): the owner asked for the picture as it is. Merging the row of other permanents into the land row to give every row more height: a bigger change of the layout (and of the e2e tests that name the rows) than this issue asks, noted in `docs/ROADMAP.md`.
- Consequences: The art shows as printed (the e2e `board-polish.e2e.ts` reads the colour of a tile's middle from a screenshot and compares it with the colour of the picture served), the creatures and the hand cards are bigger (the height of the field is shared, so the rows of other permanents and lands are up to a fifth smaller where the creature row grew, which is the price of it; at 1366x768 the creature row gains 12 percent in height and the others lose about 10). The hand at 1366x768 shows the same 108px of each card (larger text, wider cards). The pictures load only in a real browser (Scryfall is blocked in the sandbox), so the checks used a plain picture served by the test; the owner should look at real art with the title bar on it.

## D-241: The active player's area is marked by its border alone, on all four sides (issue 58, 2026-11-09)
- Context: D-153 marked the active player's area (the strip, the battlefield and, for the viewer, the hand) with a tint on the ground and a bar along the left edge, with a line at the outer edge. The owner: "the active player highlight does not need to highlight the background too. just the borders is enough. and the left border is missing."
- Decision: No tint: the ground of an active part is the ground of an idle part. The edge is a line of the accent colour (`--active-edge`) round the area as a whole: the left and right edge of every part (the strip's own left border takes the colour, the other parts draw it as an inset shadow of 4px), the top (3px) of the first part (the opponent's strip, the viewer's battlefield) and the bottom of the last (the opponent's battlefield, the viewer's hand), so the area is a closed frame. The lines do not take any room, so nothing moves when the turn passes. `e2e/board-polish.e2e.ts` reads the computed styles.
- Alternatives: One element wrapping the area with a real border: rejected, the parts are siblings of one column and the hand sits under the exile strip of the cast-from-elsewhere chips; moving them would change the whole board markup.
- Consequences: The frame is interrupted where a chip strip (cards you can cast from the graveyard or exile, the exile strip) sits between the viewer's strip and hand, as the area is made of the parts that carry the class. I could not see the owner's screenshot, so I read "the left border is missing" as the lack of a complete frame (the old edge had no right side and the left bar was only 4px of inset shadow under the cards of a row); if the left border was missing elsewhere, the owner should say where.

## D-242: Issue 36 again: a stack of tapped tokens is checked, not changed; token images wait (2026-11-09)
- Context: The owner's report ("when I had 13 tapped tokens, it showed untapped and tapped cards. The tokens don't have images") was answered in the first playtest round (D-138, point 4, "Tokens"): the grouping key of equal tokens (`tokenKey`, `ui/board/group.ts`) already holds the tapped state, and what looked mixed was the decorative card behind a stack, drawn upright behind a tapped front card, which now turns with it. The owner's list gave the issue again, so it was reproduced anew on the current code.
- Decision: Reproduced in a browser with a board of 30 equal tokens of which 13 were tapped, at 1366x768 (a page that renders the real app over a doctored view, kept out of the repository): the row groups them in two stacks, "x13" tapped (the front card turned, the card behind it turned with it) and "x17" untapped; 13 tapped tokens alone are 13 tapped tiles when they fit and one tapped stack when they do not; the hover list of a stack shows every member with the state it has. I found no case in which one stack shows both states, so no code changed. Land stacks (D-215) do show tapped and untapped lands in one column, on purpose (each card of a column is a tile that turns where it lies); that is not the tokens of the report, and the owner can ask for lands to be kept apart by state. Tests that fail if it comes back: `test/tokens-render.test.tsx` (a row too narrow for 13 tapped and 17 untapped tokens makes two uniform stacks; 13 tapped alone make one tapped stack; the stylesheet turns the card behind a tapped stack). Token images: the owner decided they are not a priority now; nothing was done (`docs/ROADMAP.md` keeps the need: Scryfall `all_parts` data in the snapshots).
- Alternatives: Keeping tapped and untapped lands apart in a column: not asked for, and a column mixes them by design. Writing a failing test for a bug that could not be reproduced: refused, the new tests describe the guarantee instead.
- Consequences: If the owner still sees tapped and untapped cards in one stack, a screenshot of the board (which stack, which permanents) would show whether it is a land column, an Aura-bearing token (never grouped) or something not yet seen.

## D-243: The monarch, the Ring and the emblems as small cards in a strip beside the battlefield (issue 84, 2026-11-09)
- Context: The owner: "the monarch is very discreet; make the monarch and other emblems cards on the battlefield, discreetly but more visible", and decided: yes, as cards, with images if possible. The monarch was a chip in the life box and the top bar (issue 34), the Ring a chip with a tooltip (D-196), and emblems small chips of the command zone strip, which the action dock covers on the player's own strip (D-201). The view has what is needed: `GameView.monarch` (a seat, public), `SeatView.ringTempted` (a count) and the emblems as objects of the command zone (`ObjectView.emblem`, name "Emblem", their abilities in `oracleText`). Web only: no engine change and no view change.
- Decision: (1) **A strip of small cards**, `ui/board/Emblems.tsx` (`emblems.ts` is the pure model): at the left of each player's battlefield, a column of cards 112 by 72 (name and the beginning of the words on the card; a coloured left band for whose it is, the player's own blue or the opponent's red, as the strips) under a caption "Yours" or "Opponent's"; two cards to a column, the third starts a column to the right. It sits inside the player's `.board-field`, beside the rows (`.board-field-rows`), not in them: no row, no tile, no drag, nothing to target, and it takes width, not height, from the battlefield; a player with none has no strip. The order: the monarch (the monarch's player), the Ring (a player the Ring has tempted: "The Ring", an emblem by CR 701.54c, with the abilities that are on at its count), the emblems of the command zone in order. (2) **Texts** as the rules give them: the monarch has the two abilities of CR 725.2 ("At the beginning of the monarch's end step, that player draws a card." and "Whenever a creature deals combat damage to the monarch, its controller becomes the monarch."), the Ring the abilities of CR 701.54c from the first up to its count of temptations, an emblem the text of its abilities. The type line is "Designation" for the monarch (CR 725.1: it is a designation) and "Emblem" (the Ring: "Emblem — tempted 2 times"). (3) **Preview.** Hovering, focusing or right-clicking a card shows it whole in the preview panel (`useHoverPreview`, `CardFace`). The monarch and the Ring are no objects of the view, so `game/designations.ts` builds one of the view's own shape for each, with an id that no engine object has (`o-1` for the monarch, `o-100` and up for the Ring of a seat; engine ids start at 0), and `findObject` resolves them first; the preview says whose it is ("You are the monarch (CR 725.1)"). (4) **Pictures.** The monarch card asks for the card named "The Monarch" through the existing `Art` component and keeps the drawn card, with its name and words on backings of their own, when the picture does not load (the same fallback as the permanents); the Ring and the emblems are not looked up (an emblem is named "Emblem": there is nothing to look up and Scryfall's emblem cards are named by their source, which the view does not carry). (5) The command zone strip keeps the commanders only (the emblems moved to the strip; the command zone viewer still lists all); the monarch chip of the life box and the top bar stay.
- Alternatives: A row of the battlefield for them: rejected, a row would take height, which is the scarce room (D-240), and the rows are for permanents. An overlay in a corner of the field: rejected, it would cover tiles of a full row. Putting the monarch in the engine view as an object: rejected, it is a designation, not an object (CR 725.1), and a view addition needs a version and digest change for what the page can build alone. The Ring's own card from Scryfall: not done, I do not know that a card of that name exists to be found by name, and a wrong picture would be worse than the drawn card.
- Consequences: A player sees the monarch, the Ring and every emblem of both players as cards that stay on the board. The picture of the monarch loads only in a real browser (Scryfall is blocked in the sandbox), so I could not see it or check that "The Monarch" resolves on Scryfall; the fallback was checked with the request refused. A strip with three or more cards takes a second column of width from the rows. The card is a quarter of a real card's height, so the preview is where the whole text is read; the rules text clamps to three lines on the card. Tests: `test/emblems-render.test.tsx` (no strip; the monarch; two emblems; the opponent's labelled; both strips each beside its battlefield; the preview of each) and `e2e/board-polish.e2e.ts` (the monarch of the hidden synthetic deck beside the rows, hovered, no stray scroll bar).


## D-244: A button on the import results opens a prefilled GitHub issue for an unsupported deck (2026-11-10)
- Context: The owner asked for one click, on the import screen, to open a GitHub issue "with all the information you need" when a deck is not fully supported. Until now the owner pasted by hand what the issues for decks 128 and 136 hold: the decklist, a rule, the "Template report for ..." text (the existing "Copy template report" button) and nothing about the build.
- Decision: `deckIssue` (`apps/web/src/import/deck-issue.ts`, pure) builds the issue from the `ImportReport`: the title "deck support <deck name>", and the body: the decklist as resolved (a Commander section, then the Mainboard, `1x Name`), a rule, the template report, the list of the unsupported card names, the names the lookup could not find, and the build line (`versionLine`: commit, engine and parser versions). The coverage report shows "Ask for support on GitHub" above the collapsed "What blocks this deck?" panel, only when a card is unsupported. It opens `github.com/pliniosilveira/commander-arena/issues/new` with the title and the body in the address; the player reads it and presses Submit there. A body whose address would pass 7,000 characters (GitHub refuses requests of about 8,000) is copied to the clipboard first and the page opens with a short body that says to paste it; with no clipboard the message points to "Copy template report". The tab is opened without the `noopener` feature (it makes `window.open` answer null, so a blocked tab could not be told from an open one) and its opener is cleared by hand.
- Alternatives: Creating the issue from the app through the GitHub API: rejected, the app is a static site with no secret of its own, and a token in the page would be readable by everyone. A small server or function that holds the token: rejected for this change, it is a new service to run and to protect (and spam target), against one extra press of Submit. Putting the button inside the collapsed panel: rejected, the owner asked for one click.
- Consequences: One click opens the issue form complete, so the owner no longer assembles the decklist and the report by hand; the player needs a GitHub account to submit. A very large deck takes the clipboard path (a paste). The report uses the names the lookup resolved, not the text the player typed.

## D-245: The support issue carries the unsupported cards' data, compressed, and `pnpm corpus:from-issue` adds them to the corpus (2026-11-10)
- Context: D-244's issue had the decklist, the template report (one example per shape) and the names, but not the cards themselves, so before a deck could be built the owner had to run `pnpm corpus:extract` on Scryfall's bulk file, which this sandbox cannot reach (the network policy is organization-managed and blocks Scryfall). The owner does not want to extract for every deck. An attachment to the issue would have no size limit, but this session's GitHub access only reaches paths inside the repository and issue attachments live outside it (`github.com/user-attachments/...` answers 403), so they cannot be read here. GitHub refuses an issue description of more than 65,536 characters.
- Decision: The app writes the unsupported cards' golden records (`toGoldenCard` of the card as the player's browser received it from Scryfall at import; `source` "app import (Scryfall API)", `acceptance`) into the description, as JSON lines gzip-compressed with the browser's `CompressionStream` and written in base64url (lines of 76 characters) inside a collapsed "Card data for the golden corpus" block. The format (the marker, the text, the checks) is one module of the cards package (`corpus/issue-block.ts`) that both sides use. `pnpm corpus:from-issue --body <file> --issue <n>` (`tools/corpus/from-issue.ts`) finds the block in a saved description, decompresses it with Node's zlib, checks every record (oracle id, name, layout, faces with their text fields) and merges the cards into `golden.jsonl` like `corpus:extract` (same `mergeGolden`), with the source "app import (Scryfall API), issue #<n>". The readable part of the description keeps, per unsupported card, the cost and type line of each face and why it is blocked; the whole Oracle text is in the compressed data. The body stays at or under 60,000 characters: the cards that do not fit are named and left out. The issue is prepared when the report shows, so the click opens the tab at once (a browser blocks a tab a click opens only after waiting); a browser without `CompressionStream` gets the issue without the block and a line that says so.
- Alternatives: The card data as plain JSON: rejected, a dozen cards took about ten thousand characters and pushed most reports to the clipboard; gzip makes card text four to nine times smaller. A QR code or another image: rejected, it can only travel as an attachment, which this session cannot read. Building from the template report's shapes alone: rejected, the rest of a card (type line, layout, its other abilities, reminder text) decides how it is built and its tests need the real wording. A server holding a GitHub token to make the issue in one click: rejected for now (D-244).
- Consequences: Once an issue is filed, the owner runs nothing: the cards come from the issue (the session reads it with the repository-scoped GitHub tools, saves the description and runs `corpus:from-issue`). The corpus entries' source says they came from the app's Scryfall import through an issue, not from the bulk file. The data in the issue is not readable by eye; the readable part says what blocks each card.

## D-246: Wizards' text is not committed; the Scryfall card data stays (2026-11-11)
- Context: The owner is thinking again of making the repository public and asked for the licence items of the ROADMAP to be checked. Nothing found shows that Wizards allows its Comprehensive Rules to be redistributed in a public repository (`docs/rules/README.md` asked for written confirmation before that), and the Fan Content Policy FAQ excludes "verbatim copying and reposting" of Wizards' IP (its example is proxy cards); other open projects keep the rules text out of their repositories. The sandbox cannot read the policies themselves (the hosts are blocked and the search returns excerpts), so none of this is legal advice. For the Scryfall card data, Scryfall's API page says the data and images are free to use for Magic software and community content under the Fan Content Policy, and forbids paywalling access, its logos and implied endorsement; nothing found says whether committing the data is allowed.
- Decision: (1) The Comprehensive Rules text (`docs/rules/comprehensive-rules.txt`) and the Update Bulletin texts (`docs/rules/bulletins/`) are removed from the repository and ignored by git; the owner fetches them with `pnpm rules:fetch` (`rules-source.json` and `RULES_VERSION.md`, which hold no Wizards text, stay). The checks that read the file (the creature type and planeswalker type tables against CR 205.3m and 205.3j, the ability words of CR 207.2c, the subtype lists, `cr-real.test.ts`) skip when it is absent and run where it is present; the tables themselves, lists of type names, stay committed. `COMMANDER_ARENA_CR_FILE` points the tools and tests at a copy kept elsewhere, and `pnpm rule --file <path>` reads one for a lookup. The git history still holds the files: this change does not purge it, and the owner has not asked for that. (2) The Scryfall card data in the precon snapshots and the golden corpus stays committed, with the Fan Content Policy notice and the Scryfall credit the README already has: the owner judges the risk small. (3) The mana symbols are drawn in the repository's own style (`apps/web/src/ui/mana.tsx`), so the ROADMAP item about the mana font no longer applies.
- Alternatives: Asking Wizards in writing for permission to commit the rules text: not done, the owner chose to remove it. Purging the history now: not asked for, and it rewrites every commit hash; needed only if the repository is made public and the old files must not be in it. Removing the Scryfall data as well: rejected by the owner (small risk); it would need a fetch step for the offline precons and the corpus tests.
- Consequences: The repository no longer carries Wizards' rules text from now on; the CR-dependent checks do not run in CI (the runners would have to fetch the file, and `cr-real.test.ts` pins one exact file by its sha256). A cloud session cannot fetch the CR either (`magic.wizards.com` is blocked), so `pnpm rule` there needs the owner to provide a copy (`COMMANDER_ARENA_CR_FILE`, or `--file`). Before the repository goes public the history question remains.

## D-247: A private repository keeps the CR text for cloud sessions; the tests read it through one variable (2026-11-11)
- Context: D-246 removed Wizards' rules text from the repository, so a cloud session (which cannot reach Wizards' site) has no CR for `pnpm rule` or for the checks that read it. The owner agreed to a private repository for it. Three tests of the cards package still read a hardcoded path and ignored `COMMANDER_ARENA_CR_FILE`.
- Decision: `pliniosilveira/commander-arena-rules`, a private repository holding `comprehensive-rules.txt` (sha256 `8d860e45…`, checked equal to the file `rules-source.json` records) and the bulletin, with a README that says to keep it private. A session attaches it (`add_repo`), clones it and points `COMMANDER_ARENA_CR_FILE` at the file. The card tests take the path from one helper (`packages/cards/test/cr-file.ts`), the tools from `tools/rules/paths.ts`; both honor the variable and skip when there is no file. Checked: `pnpm rule --file` and the CR-dependent tests of tools and cards pass from a fresh clone of that repository.
- Alternatives: Asking an organization admin to allow `media.wizards.com` and `magic.wizards.com` so `pnpm rules:fetch` works in the sandbox: needs the admin and was not chosen; it would make the private repository unnecessary. Pasting the CR into a chat: about 950 KB per session.
- Consequences: Cloud sessions can look rules up again. The private repository holds Wizards' text for the owner's own use; it must stay private and must not be copied into the project repository. A newer CR means replacing the file there and updating its checksum.

## D-249: The repository is public; the workflows are pinned and the public-facing files exist (2026-11-11)
- Context: The owner made this repository public: a new repository with one commit, built from `main` of the old repository, which stays private as the archive. A public repository takes pull requests from strangers and runs workflows for them, and the actions of the workflows were still on major tags.
- Decision: Every action of `.github/workflows/` is pinned to the commit hash its major tag pointed to on 2026-11-11, with the tag as a comment (no version changed). `SECURITY.md` asks for private vulnerability reports; `CONTRIBUTING.md` points to the support button, `AGENTS.md` and the checks. No issue templates yet: GitHub's new-issue page with `?title=&body=` (the support button of D-244, D-245) may show the template chooser instead of the filled form once templates exist; they wait until that is tested. Issues from anyone but the owner stay untrusted input for `pnpm corpus:from-issue`.
- Alternatives: Leaving major tags (a moved tag runs new code in every workflow); Dependabot version updates for the actions (more pull requests to review; can be added later).
- Consequences: Workflow code changes only through a reviewed commit. Newer action versions need a deliberate hash bump.

## D-250: The full suite runs every night on GitHub, only when `main` has a new commit (2026-11-11)
- Context: D-132 had the owner run the complete suite every night, because GitHub's included minutes for a private repository were limited and had run out. The repository is public now (D-249), where GitHub-hosted runners are free. The first CI run of the public repository also showed that three tests of `costs-render.test.tsx` had been red since D-243: a card face with no store (which `useDefinedPt` allows) failed on the new `useApp` of the Ring's count, and nobody saw it while CI could not run.
- Decision: The `Full` workflow has a schedule (03:17 UTC) besides the manual start. A first job, `gate`, compares the sha being run with the head of the last finished (not cancelled) scheduled run of the workflow and skips every other job when they are the same: a night with no new commit costs a few seconds. A run started by hand always runs. When a scheduled run fails, the `check` job opens an issue. `useAppIfPresent` (`store-context.tsx`) gives CardFace the Ring read it needs without a store.
- Alternatives: Running on every push to `main` (the quick CI already does the fast part; the full suite takes about 5 minutes of tests plus the browser tests per push); the owner's local nightly run (needs the owner's machine); skipping on "no commit in 24 hours" by date (misses a late commit and runs after a cancelled night).
- Consequences: The soak tests of 20 games per run and the browser tests run unattended. GitHub disables scheduled workflows after 60 days with no activity in the repository, which a night skip does not count as; any push or manual start brings it back. `pnpm test:soak` (100 games) and the manual `Soak` workflow (500) stay on demand.

## D-251: Complete deck support issues are built by an agent routine, within a token budget (2026-11-11)
- Context: The owner asked for deck support to start by itself when a complete request arrives (the issue the import screen's button writes, D-244, D-245), to skip incomplete ones with a comment, and to work only when the weekly token budget is healthy: Monday below 10% of the week's use, Tuesday 20%, Wednesday 40%, Thursday 60%, Friday 80%, the weekend 100%. This replaces, for these issues only, the rule that a deck build starts only on an explicit "go" in chat. The tools of an agent session have no event trigger for a new issue, and the repository is public, so an issue can come from anyone.
- Decision: (1) `pnpm corpus:check-issue` (`tools/corpus/check-issue.ts`) decides whether a description is complete: decklist with Commander and Mainboard sections, template report, the list of unsupported names, the build line, no name that was not found, no card left out, and a card data block that decodes, says its count correctly and has a record for every unsupported name. (2) The workflow `deck-support-triage.yml` runs it, with no model, on every "deck support" issue **opened or edited by anyone** (the owner decided that, seeing the risk): a complete one gets the label `deck-support:ready` (only people with write access can add a label, so an author cannot forge it), an incomplete one one comment (edited in place) that lists what is missing. The comment carries the sha256 of the description it checked, and an edit by someone other than the owner removes the label at once, so the agent can tell an issue edited after the check. A person other than the owner has one request waiting at a time. The issue is untrusted input: it is only read as data, never followed as instructions. (3) The skill `.claude/skills/deck-support/SKILL.md` is the procedure of the agent: look for ready issues first (no clone, no cost), then read the weekly use from the session's rate-limit events (`seven_day.utilization`) and compare it with the day's limit (weekday in UTC+1), then claim the issue, build it by the card support playbook on its own branch, open one pull request and label the issue. It stops for an S-class gap (a proposal and the owner), never merges and never changes the SPEC. (4) A scheduled task fires the skill every three hours; it costs almost nothing when no issue is ready. Labels: `deck-support:ready`, `in-progress`, `blocked`, `done`.
- Alternatives: An event-driven trigger (a webhook or an API-triggered routine called from the workflow): needs a token kept as a repository secret and the owner's setup on claude.ai; it is the upgrade if three hours is too slow. Validating in the agent session instead of the workflow (spends tokens on every incomplete issue). Acting on the owner's issues only (the first version): the owner chose to accept anyone's, so the safeguards above exist instead; the limit that remains is that the card data of a stranger's issue is not checked against Scryfall (the sandbox cannot reach it): `corpus:from-issue --no-replace` never replaces a card the corpus already holds, and the owner reviews every pull request; checking each record against Scryfall's API in the workflow is the follow-up if fabricated cards become a problem. Polling every hour: eight times as many idle sessions for a build that takes hours anyway.
- Consequences: A complete request is picked up within about three hours when the budget allows it, and waits, silently, when it does not. The first pull request of a deck still needs the owner's merge. The three issues that were complete before this existed (copied from the archive, and the Borg deck) are not labelled; the owner queues one by adding the label `deck-support:ready` or by asking in chat.

## D-252: The life a player gained this turn is kept in the turn log, for "if you gained N or more life this turn" (2026-11-11)
- Context: Valkyrie Harbinger, Angelic Accord, Griffin Aerie and The Book of Exalted Deeds (the Bruna deck, issue 5) make a token "if you gained N or more life this turn". The turn log kept each life gain as an event (D-149), not the amount.
- Decision: `TurnLog.lifeGainedTotal` holds the life each seat has gained this turn, summed after replacement in `gainLife` (CR 119.3); the condition `lifeGainedThisTurn { atLeast }` reads it as an intervening "if" (CR 603.4) and in plain static conditions. Parser rule `condition.life-gained-this-turn`, lowered with the feature `condition:lifeGainedThisTurn`. `PARSER_VERSION` 78, `ENGINE_VERSION` 74.
- Alternatives: Adding the amounts of the `lifeGained` events after the fact (the turn log holds no amounts); a condition for any player (every card of the deck says "you").
- Consequences: Only "you" can be asked. An "an opponent gained life" wording needs the same field and a `player` choice.

## D-253: "Otherwise," is the `else` of the conditional instruction before it (2026-11-11)
- Context: Cosmos Elixir (the Bruna deck, issue 5): "draw a card if your life total is greater than your starting life total. Otherwise, you gain 2 life." The engine's `conditional` effect had an `else` (CR 608.2c) that only an "instead" sentence filled.
- Decision: A sentence that starts "Otherwise, " (`IrSentence.otherwise`, read where conditional sentences are read) lowers to the `else` of the step before it, which must be one conditional with no `else`; anywhere else it is not read. New condition rule `condition.life-above-starting` for "your life total is greater than your starting life total", the engine's `lifeTotal` with `aboveStarting` and at least 1 (CR 119.1, 903.7). Both condition rules of the deck are read after an instruction as well as before one. `PARSER_VERSION` 79.
- Alternatives: A condition node for "greater than the starting life total" (the engine already has it); reading "Otherwise" only for a trailing "if" (the leading form, "If X, ... Otherwise, ...", is read by the same code).
- Consequences: Other "Otherwise" lines read when the condition before them is one the grammar knows.

## D-254: "Enters with a counter on it for each time it was kicked" is a replacement count (2026-11-11)
- Context: Everflowing Chalice (the Bruna deck, issue 5): "Multikicker {2}. ~ enters with a charge counter on it for each time it was kicked." The replacement `entersWithCounters` counted a number, X or a `countOf`; a trigger would have put the counters on later (CR 614.1c: it is a replacement).
- Decision: `entersWithCounters.count` may be `{ kind: 'timesKicked' }`, the kicks of the spell the permanent resolved from (`timesKickedOf`, CR 702.33c); 0 for a permanent put onto the battlefield by an effect. The counters tail of the parser takes `amount.times-kicked` as well as `amount.for-each`; the old "rejects" line of the rule became an example. `ENGINE_VERSION` 75, `PARSER_VERSION` 80; the derive digests were recorded again (`UPDATE_DERIVE_DIGESTS=1`).
- Alternatives: A trigger "when this enters, put counters" (a different timing, CR 614.1c says enters-with is a replacement).
- Consequences: Every Multikicker permanent of this shape reads. The kicks come from the stack object only, so a copy of a permanent does not carry them.

## D-255: A cost reduction with "of the chosen type" and no "you cast" is for every player's spells (2026-11-11)
- Context: Urza's Incubator (the Bruna deck, issue 5): "Creature spells of the chosen type cost {2} less to cast." The grammar read only "... you cast cost ...", and listed this wording among its rejects.
- Decision: `static.spells-cost-reduction` also reads "<spells> of the chosen type cost {N} less to cast" and then leaves the `controller` of the filter out, so the engine's `costReduction` matches the spell of any caster (CR 601.2f, 604.2); with "you cast" the controller stays `you`. Only the chosen-type wording, not any "spells cost less" line. No engine change; a SYNTHETIC `SYNTHETIC Shared Discount` and a scenario test pin the effect on both players' hands. `PARSER_VERSION` 81.
- Alternatives: Reading every "Creature spells cost {1} less" (more lines, but none of them is in the deck); reading it as "you cast" (wrong: the opponents' spells are cheaper too).
- Consequences: Other symmetric reductions of the chosen type read. A symmetric reduction without the chosen type is still unread.

## D-256: "That many" of a life gain trigger is the life gained; "Do this only once each turn" is CR 603.2h, not the once-per-triggering flag (2026-11-11)
- Context: Nykthos Paragon (the Bruna deck, issue 5): "Whenever you gain life, you may put that many +1/+1 counters on each creature you control. Do this only once each turn." The occurrence of a lifeGained event had no amount, and the engine's oncePerTurn (D-149) counts how often an ability triggers. CR 603.2h says an ability with "Do this only once each turn" triggers only if its source's controller has not yet taken the indicated action that turn, which differs in two cases: a "you may" that was declined has not taken the action, and two triggers that are on the stack before the first resolves both exist.
- Decision: The occurrence of lifeGained carries the amount gained after replacement (event.amount, CR 119.9, 614.1) as its `damage`, which is what the engine's `triggerDamage` ("that much") reads; validateCard allows triggerDamage for a lifeGained trigger too. A new triggered-ability flag `doOnlyOnceEachTurn` and a new turn-log list `TurnLog.actionTaken` (source object, ability index, and the player who took the action) implement CR 603.2h: the trigger is dropped when (source, ability index, controller of the trigger) is in the list; the entry is added, with the source's controller read by controllerOf, as the ability begins resolving, or, for an ability with "you may", when its controller accepts (rules/action-taken.ts). The action counts as taken once the ability resolves even if its effect then does nothing. A permanent that changes controller mid-turn, or comes back as a new object (CR 400.7), starts again; two permanents with the same ability are two sources, each with its own limit (a reading of the rule's wording; no official ruling was found to confirm it). The flag is refused together with oncePerTurn, on a state trigger and on a triggered mana ability. Parser: rule `effect.do-once-each-turn` (clause verb doOnceEachTurn, taken from the last sentence like "This ability triggers only once each turn"), `amount.that-many` is allowed as the count of `effect.add-counters`, and in a body whose every trigger is a life gain a "that many" in the FIRST instruction of the body lowers to `triggerDamage` (ctx.lifeGainTrigger); after any other instruction (mill, discard, gain life, draw ...) it is not changed and the lowering refuses it, since it may count what that instruction did. Feature `ability:doOnlyOnceEachTurn`. Web: the ability label of payAnyAmount handles the new shape. PARSER_VERSION 82 and ENGINE_VERSION 76 (with the other groups of the Bruna deck); derive digests re-recorded (TurnLog gained a field).
- Alternatives: Reusing oncePerTurn (rejected: it would stop the ability from triggering again after a declined "you may", which CR 603.2h allows). A new `lifeGained` AST amount kind (rejected: triggerDamage is already the amount of the triggering event and every consumer, validator and the stack data already carry it). Keying the record on the source and ability only (rejected: CR 603.2h speaks of the source's controller, so a permanent that changes hands would be limited by what its old controller did). Retargeting every "that many" of a life gain body (rejected: it gave 'mill two cards, then draw that many cards' the life gained as its count, a guess).
- Consequences: Every "that much/that many" of the first instruction of a life gain trigger and every "Do this only once each turn" trigger can read. Per the CR text two life gains in one resolution put two Nykthos triggers on the stack and both resolve (the second was triggered before the action was taken); this follows the rule's wording and is pinned by a test, not by a ruling I could look up. A "that many" after another instruction of a life gain trigger stays unsupported until its meaning is modelled. `doOnlyOnceEachTurn` on a non-optional ability whose effect holds a `may` or a `payAnyAmount` is refused by `validateCard` (the engine would count a declined or zero payment as the action taken).

## D-257: "You may pay {X}, where X is less than or equal to ..., If you do, ..." is payAnyAmount with a generic symbol, a most and an inline follow-up (2026-11-11)
- Context: Well of Lost Dreams: "Whenever you gain life, you may pay {X}, where X is less than or equal to the amount of life you gained. If you do, draw X cards." The engine's payAnyAmount (D-151) paid one colored symbol any number of times and made a reflexive triggered ability (CR 603.12), which is "When you do", not "If you do" (CR 608.2c).
- Decision: payAnyAmount accepts the generic symbol '1' (a generic {1} paid X times), an optional `atMost` amount (read as the effect starts; the chooseX decision's maximum is the lesser of it and what the controller can pay) and `ifPaid` in place of `reflexive`: an effect run as the next instruction of the same resolution, with X the number paid (the resolving ability's stack X is set, so the {kind:'x'} amount of the follow-up reads it, CR 107.3f). No new decision kind: the chooseX decision of purpose payAnyAmount and the payMana decision are the existing ones, so the AI and the web UI need no new handler (the AI pays the maximum, as for any payAnyAmount). Validation: exactly one of reflexive and ifPaid; atMost may not read X; ifPaid may read X but not as a manaValueX filter. Parser: rule `effect.pay-x-at-most` (only the wording "pay {X}, where X is less than or equal to the amount of life you gained"), lowered together with the "If you do," sentence by lowerPayXAtMost, only in a life gain trigger and only as the last two sentences of the body.
- Alternatives: A reflexive triggered ability (rejected: "If you do" is not a trigger and opponents could respond between the payment and the draw). A new effect kind (rejected: the instruction, the decision and the payment already existed). A new decision kind for the optional payment with a bound (not needed: chooseX with min 0 and a max is exactly that).
- Consequences: Other "pay {X} up to a limit, then do something with X" cards can be read by adding a limit phrase. The limit is read only for the life gained today. The AI spends up to X mana per life gain with Well of Lost Dreams (acceptable, unrefined).


## D-258: "Sacrifice it unless you return a permanent you control to its owner's hand" is a may and an if-you-don't (2026-11-11)
- Context: Karoo (the Bruna deck, issue 5): "When this land enters, sacrifice it unless you return an untapped Plains you control to its owner's hand." The engine's `unlessPays` pays only mana, life, discard and energy. The parser read only mana and energy after "unless you pay" and did not read "unless you return ...".
- Decision: Use the existing nodes, which is exactly CR 118.12a ("[Do something] unless [a player does something else]" means "[A player may do something else]. If [that player doesn't], [do something]"). The new parser rule `condition.unless-return` (in `rules/condition/bruna.ts`, read as the "unless" of one clause by `UNLESS_PAYS` in `sentence.ts`, IR test `unlessReturn`) reads "unless you " followed by one `effect.return` clause whose noun says "you control" (so the controller chooses the permanent). `lowerUnlessReturn` (`lower/sentences.ts`) lowers it to `sequence [ may(moveToZone { objects: choose { subtypes: [Plains], tapped: false, controller: you }, to: hand }), conditional(not didPrevious, <the instruction>) ]`. The offered clause must lower to a choosing return to hand, otherwise the sentence is refused. One engine change, in `rules/effects.ts`: the `mayEffect` question is not asked when the offered `moveToZone` with a `choose` selector (permanents, not card zones, not to the battlefield) has no candidate permanent. The player has nothing to say yes to (CR 608.2d), so `didPrevious` stays false and the "if you don't" runs. This is the same rule D-187 already applies to "you may sacrifice one or more Treasures". The guard is general, not Plains-specific: a SYNTHETIC `SYNTHETIC Bounce Offer Land` ("you may return a creature you control to its owner's hand") is also not asked with no creature, and a SYNTHETIC `SYNTHETIC Plains Karoo` fixture with `scenario-xx-return-or-sacrifice.test.ts` pins Karoo: an untapped Plains is returned (a single candidate is automatic after yes); with several candidates the controller chooses, and tapped Plains, other lands and the opponent's Plains are never offered; declining sacrifices the land; with only tapped Plains, with no Plains (the land is no Plains itself) and with nothing else the land is sacrificed without a question. Parser rule `condition.unless-return` has examples, rejects and cites. A card with the "you may" form ("you may sacrifice it unless ...") reads as an optional ability, which is also correct.
- Alternatives: (a) A `return` cost kind in `unlessPays` (rules/pay-unless.ts): a new payment stage with a permanent choice and a filter, a new decision purpose and AI handling, which would change existing flows. (b) does the same thing with no new decision kind. Asking the may question when no permanent qualifies: harmless to correctness (declining and sacrificing is the same result) but a pointless prompt for the player and the AI.
- Consequences: Other "[instruction] unless you return a <permanent> you control to its owner's hand" lines read (the instruction may be any single clause, not only a sacrifice). Other "you may return a <permanent> you control" offers with no candidate are no longer asked, which changes the derive-differential digests of the soup games (re-recorded). An unless cost of any other kind (tap a land, exile a card, return a card from the graveyard) is still unread. PARSER_VERSION 82 and ENGINE_VERSION 76 (the parser reads a new rule and the engine's may question changed); golden.expected.json and the derive digests are regenerated.


## D-259: "Equip commander {N}" and a static grant of protection from colors, including those outside the commander's color identity (2026-11-11)
- Context: Commander's Plate (the Bruna deck, issue 5): "Equipped creature gets +3/+3 and has protection from each color that's not in your commander's color identity. Equip commander {3}. Equip {5}". The engine's equip had a creature-type restriction only (D-220), the validator refused `commander` in it (`readsCombatOrSource`), and no static ability could give protection (`GRANTABLE_KEYWORDS` has only keywords without parameters; "Enchanted creature has protection from red." was a reject of `static.attached`).
- Decision: (1) `Keyword` equip's `restriction` may be `{ commander: true }` (or `'yours'`): CR 702.6c lets an equip ability further restrict its target to a creature the activating player controls that has the quality; "commander" is a card a player designated (CR 903.3), so a commander I control but do not own counts and a token that copies one does not. The validator allows `commander` there (`readsCombatOrSourceBesidesCommander`, a split of `readsCombatOrSource`) and still refuses zone, controller, owner and combat. Parser rule `keyword.equip-commander`, lowered to `restriction: { commander: true }`; `IrKeyword.commanderOnly`. (2) New protection quality `{ kind: 'protection', from: 'colorsNotInCommanderIdentity' }`: protection from each color that no commander of the controller has in its color identity (CR 702.16h, 702.16i, 903.4). With no commander the quality is undefined and that part does nothing (CR 903.4f), so it gives no colors; a colorless identity gives all five. "Your" is the controller of the static ability that gives it (the Equipment's controller, not the equipped creature's), resolved to plain `from: 'color'` colors as the grant is applied in `derive-statics.ts`; printed on a permanent it uses that permanent's controller (`rules/protection.ts`). `rules/commander-colors.ts` (new, no `derive` import, so no import cycle) holds `commanderIdentity` and `colorsNotInCommanderIdentity`; `commander-identity.ts` re-exports `commanderIdentity`. (3) A static `grantKeyword` may carry a protection keyword (`checkGrantedKeyword`), also with named colors; `GRANTABLE_KEYWORDS` is unchanged, so an effect "gains protection from red until end of turn" and a keyword filter ("with protection") stay refused. The parser reads "has protection from <colors>" and "has protection from each color that's not in your commander's color identity" after "has" in `static.attached`, `static.permanents` and `static.each` (IR `grantProtection`, lowered to `grantKeyword`). The protection is exercised through targeting, blocking, damage prevention and Aura/Equipment attachment (CR 702.16b, 702.16d, 702.16e, 702.16f) by `scenario-xx-commander-plate.test.ts`. `PARSER_VERSION` 82 and `ENGINE_VERSION` 76; the derive digests are re-recorded because the new SYNTHETIC Plate Armor joins the static pool of the soup decks.
- Alternatives: A new `StaticEffect` kind `grantProtection` (about ten more places to teach: features, supported, validate, continuous, lowering); putting protection into `GRANTABLE_KEYWORDS` (it also feeds keyword filters, the parser's keyword vocabulary and the effect grants, none of which resolve "your commander"); resolving the colors when the card is parsed (they depend on the game's commanders); reading the commander of the creature's controller (wrong: "your" is the Equipment's controller); `commander: 'yours'` for "Equip commander" (stricter than CR 702.6c, which asks only that the creature has the quality).
- Consequences: Commander's Plate reads and plays (golden: no card lost its status). Other "has protection from <colors>" lines of Auras, Equipment and anthems read as well (the template corpus line 'Equipped creature gets +1/+1 and has protection from black and from green.' now reads). Not read: "has flying and protection from red" in one list, protection from a quality that is not a color, an effect that gives protection for a duration, "Equip your commander", "Equip legendary creature". A copy of a commander (a token) cannot be the target of "Equip commander".


## D-260: The snow mana spent to cast a spell is counted, and a spell reads it in its own effect; a search may be for a union of kinds of card (2026-11-11)
- Context: Search for Glory (the Bruna deck): "Search your library for a snow permanent card, a legendary card, or a Saga card, reveal it, put it into your hand, then shuffle. You gain 1 life for each {S} spent to cast this spell." The engine kept the mana spent to cast a spell (total and by card type of the source, D-183) but not whether it came from a snow source, and `manaSpent` could be read only in "When you cast this spell". The grammar read a search for one kind of card (and a choice of types), not a list of cards of several kinds, nor "permanent card".
- Decision: `ManaSpent.snow` (left out when 0, so existing spells keep their shape) is set from the snow flag of the sources the plan spends on the cost (`PaymentPlan.spentSnow`, CR 107.4h; mana that pays the cost of a mana ability is not spent on the spell, as before). The amount `manaSpent` takes `snow: true` (not with `fromType`; the same read for the enters-with counts) and may be read in the effect of a spell itself (`scope.owner === 'spell'`), a copy having 0 (CR 707.10). `noun.library-card` reads "a snow permanent card", "a nonland permanent card" (the permanent types less the 'non' words, CR 110.1, 205.4g) and a union "a X card, a Y card, or a Z card" (an `anyOf` of filters, one of them with its own `anyOf`); `amount.for-each-mana-spent` reads "for each {S} spent to cast ~". The search prompt names such a union. SYNTHETIC `SYNTHETIC Frozen Quest`, `SYNTHETIC Snow Plains` and friends pin it.
- Alternatives: Encoding snow as a pseudo card type in `fromTypes` (it is not a type; CR 107.4h says it is neither a color nor a type of mana); reading the amount only in a cast trigger (Search for Glory is the spell's own effect).
- Consequences: Any spell whose own effect counts mana spent ("where X is the amount of mana spent to cast ~") now lowers and runs; the grammar's reading of "mana spent" in a spell is for "~" only. Adding the SYNTHETIC cards changes the derive-differential soups, so the digests must be re-recorded.

## D-261: "That shares a creature type with it" is a filter on the creature a dies trigger is about, read from last-known information (2026-11-11)
- Context: Heirloom Blade: "Whenever equipped creature dies, you may reveal cards from the top of your library until you reveal a creature card that shares a creature type with it. Put that card into your hand and the rest on the bottom of your library in a random order." The engine's `revealUntil` took a filter of the library cards only; nothing could refer to the creature that died. The two sentences of "reveal until ... Put that card" were joined only when the first began with "Reveal", not "you may reveal".
- Decision: `ObjectFilter.sharesCreatureTypeWith: 'triggerSubject'`: the object has a creature type (CR 205.3m, the CREATURE_TYPES table) that the trigger's subject had, as it last was (CR 603.10a, 113.7a; a changeling, which derive already gives every type, CR 702.73a, shares with any creature). `matchesFilter` computes the subject's subtypes from `ctx.triggerSubject` (the new `FilterContext.subjectSubtypes`); `runRevealUntil` passes the resolution's `triggerSubject`. `validateCard` allows it only in the filter of a `revealUntil` in the effect of a `dies` trigger (refused in targets, `each`, statics, other triggers and spells), so it can never silently match nothing. Grammar: " that shares a creature type with it" after a creature card (read quietly, so no other diagnostic moves), lowered to the filter; `segment.ts` joins "you may reveal cards ... until ..." with the "Put that card" sentence. Feature `selector:sharesCreatureTypeWith`. The rest go to the bottom in a random order from the game's generator (CR 401.4).
