- Alternatives: A condition `objectMatches` on each revealed card (the engine has none for library cards); a pairwise "shares" comparator between two objects (no other card in the deck needs it; the new field names its one source).
- Consequences: Other "creature card that shares a creature type with it" reveals of a dies trigger read. "Enters", "attacks" and a batch subject are refused until someone needs and tests them.

## D-262: "Up to two basic land cards that share a land type" is an option of the search, checked on the whole answer (2026-11-11)
- Context: Myriad Landscape: "{2}, {T}, Sacrifice this land: Search your library for up to two basic land cards that share a land type, put them onto the battlefield tapped, then shuffle." The share is a condition on the cards found together, which a filter on one card cannot say; the legal answers of `chooseCards` were any cards of `legal` between `min` and `max`.
- Decision: `search.sharedLandType: true` (max at least 2, land filter). The `chooseCards` decision carries `shareLandType`: the land types (CR 205.3i, the new `LAND_TYPES` table, which also feeds the old NON_CREATURE_SUBTYPES) of each card of `legal`; an answer is legal when its cards have one land type in common (one card or none always, CR 701.23b); `applyAction`'s check and the listed legal actions share `sharesLandType` (`rules/share-type.ts`, also exported from the engine index for the web app). The cap of 500 listed answers (`legal-actions.ts`) counts the answers that share a type: `firstCombinations` takes the check as a predicate and gives up after 200,000 combinations tried, so a large library cannot leave the list without a pair that exists. The prompt says "that share a land type". `CasualAgent` picks a land type (the most cards, then a colour it lacks), `RandomLegalAgent` takes one of the listed answers, the web Confirm waits for lands that share a type. Grammar: " that share a land type" after "up to N basic land cards" (quiet), turned into the option by the search lowering; `lowerFilter` refuses the flag elsewhere. Feature `selector:sharedLandType`.
- Alternatives: Listing only the legal pairs in `legal` (the first pick would have to constrain the second: an S-class interactive decision); a per-card filter (cannot express it); checking only in the UI.
- Consequences: A basic land with two land types shares either one. No new decision kind, only an optional constraint of an existing one, like `totalManaValue` (D-230). The listed answers are the first 500 that share a type; the engine accepts every legal one.

## D-263: "That player" of a step of another player: Keeper of the Accord (2026-11-11)
- Context: Keeper of the Accord (the Bruna deck) has two abilities "At the beginning of each opponent's end step, if that player controls more creatures [lands] than you, ...". The engine's intervening "if" subjectControllerHasMore (D-229) reads the controller of the permanent an event is about, which the beginning of a step has not (the validator refused it), and a step trigger had no event player, so "that player" of an opponent's step could not be named (the lowering gave `selector:triggerActor`).
- Decision: (1) The beginning of a step (`step`, `upkeep`, `endStep`) now has the active player as the player of its event (`Occurrence.player`; CR 102.1: the active player is the player whose turn it is; CR 603.2b), so `triggerPlayer` ("that player") in such an ability is the player whose turn it is; `triggerHasPlayer` accepts those triggers. The pending trigger keeps the player only for an ability that reads it (`eventPlayer` in `rules/triggers.ts`), so no other step trigger changes its state. (2) New condition `triggerPlayerHasMore { stat }` (life, cards in hand, creatures, lands; `PlayerStat`): the player of the event has a greater stat than the controller, an intervening "if" (CR 603.4) read as the ability triggers and again as it resolves (what a player controls: CR 110.2); `ConditionContext.triggerPlayer` carries the player (from the occurrence, from the player damaged in a `combatDamageBatch` trigger found by `batchTriggers`, and from `StackData.triggerPlayer` on resolution), `readsTriggerPlayer` counts the condition so the player stays on the stack and in the identity of grouped triggers; validated only as the intervening "if" of a trigger whose event is about a player. `subjectControllerHasMore` stays for triggers about a permanent (Archaeomancer's Map) and its AST does not change. (3) Parser: the rule `condition.that-player-more-lands` reads "creatures" as well as "lands" (IR `subjectControllerHasMore` stat `lands | creatures`); `lowerCondition` writes `triggerPlayerHasMore` when "that player" of the trigger is the engine's `triggerPlayer`, `subjectControllerHasMore` otherwise, and refuses it when "that player" is "you"; `thatPlayerOf` names `triggerPlayer` for the step, upkeep and end step of each opponent or each player. The second ability is the existing optional triggered search of a basic Plains, tapped, then shuffle. Web: the wording of the condition (`condition-text.ts`).
- Alternatives: Making `subjectControllerHasMore` fall back to the trigger player when there is no subject: rejected, one condition would mean two things and Map's reading ("the controller of the land as it is now or as it last was") would be mixed with an event player. Giving only the end step a player: rejected, "that player" is the same fact for every step, and the parser and validator now agree for all of them. Refusing `triggerPlayerHasMore` on a `combatDamageBatch` trigger (found by review: it never fired because the batch path passed no player): rejected, the player damaged is the player of that event (CR 603.2c, 510.2), so the batch path passes it. A new decision or object model: not needed.
- Consequences: Keeper of the Accord reads and is supported (golden acceptance 185 to 186, no other card's AST changed). Every "that player" of an opponent's or each player's upkeep, end step or other step ("At the beginning of each opponent's upkeep, that player sacrifices a creature", "..., draw a card unless that player pays {1}") now reads too, with engine-level tests for the sacrifice, the unlessPays and the life loss; four older parser tests that asserted them unsupported (needs `selector:triggerActor`) were updated, and two engine validation tests use a death trigger as the trigger without a player. A trigger of "your" step with "that player" is refused (it would compare you with yourself). The derive-differential digests and the golden snapshot are re-recorded; PARSER_VERSION 82 and ENGINE_VERSION 76.


## D-264: Ascend on a permanent gives the city's blessing, a per-seat designation, checked with the state-based actions (2026-11-11)
- Context: Arch of Orazca (the Bruna deck, issue 5) is "Ascend", "{T}: Add {C}" and "{5}, {T}: Draw a card. Activate only if you have the city's blessing." The engine had one designation, the monarch (D-127, D-131), stored as a single seat on the game state and read by the condition playerHasDesignation. The city's blessing is a designation that any number of players may have at once (CR 702.131c) and that is kept for the rest of the game (CR 702.131b: Ascend on a permanent is a static ability, "any time you control ten or more permanents and you don't have the city's blessing, you get the city's blessing for the rest of the game"). Ascend on an instant or sorcery (CR 702.131a) is a spell ability.
- Decision: (1) State: the optional field SeatState.citysBlessing?: true, absent until gained (the shape of ring and energy, so no saved or digested state of an existing game changes). It is public: SeatView.citysBlessing. The event citysBlessingGained { seat } is emitted once per player. (2) Keyword: { kind: 'ascend' }, printed only, not grantable, with no parameter; it is a supported feature (keyword:ascend). (3) Rule: gainCitysBlessings (rules/city-blessing.ts) runs first in checkStateBasedActions, like the control and Ring-bearer checks (an early return with performed: true, so the next pass continues from the new state): a player in the game who does not have the blessing and controls (controllerOf; battlefield permanents only, so a phased-out permanent does not count; tokens included) ten or more permanents, at least one with the ascend keyword in derive (so a permanent that lost its abilities in layer 6 is not a source), gets it. "Any time" is read as "checked whenever a player would get priority" (CR 704.3), which is the engine's own choice (Ascend is not a state-based action in the CR); the state is derived afresh before triggers are looked at (CR 702.131d). Nothing ever removes the blessing. Known approximation: inside one resolution, between two steps of one effect, the blessing has not been gained yet (docs/ROADMAP.md). (4) Ascend on an instant or sorcery (CR 702.131a) is not built and is refused: validateCard (ast/validate-artifacts.ts, checkAscendFace) reports an issue for the ascend keyword on a face with the instant or sorcery type, so such a card is imported as unsupported, never accepted with the keyword doing nothing. (5) Condition: Designation is 'monarch' | 'citysBlessing'; playerHasDesignation asks rules/designations.ts designationHolders(state, designation) (a list, since the blessing has several holders; the monarch is a list of at most one) and holds when any selected player is a holder; the dynamic condition (conditions.ts) and the static one (static-conditions.ts) use it. designations.ts is a separate file from city-blessing.ts because derive reads the static conditions and city-blessing.ts reads derive. (6) Parser: Ascend is a SimpleKeyword; the existing rule condition.designation also reads "you have / you don't have / an opponent has / a player has the city's blessing" (so the restriction.if rule, trigger intervening-ifs and static conditions read it with no new rule id); "you don't have" lowers to not(playerHasDesignation). (7) Web: a chip "City's blessing" on the player strip, a log line for citysBlessingGained, the condition words ("you have the city's blessing") and an Asc keyword chip. The AI heuristics do not read the blessing. (8) Testing DSL: scenario seat option citysBlessing() and expect.citysBlessing(seat, has).
- Alternatives: A GameState list of holders: same information but a second place to keep in sync with the seat; the seat field matches ring and energy. Making Ascend a triggered ability or a continuous effect applied in derive: the designation is a state change that must be stored, and a trigger would wait on the stack and give the opponent a window the rule does not allow (702.131b is static; 702.131d reapplies continuous effects before triggers). Computing "has the blessing" every time from the permanent count: wrong, the blessing is kept after permanents leave. Counting only objects that are not tokens or only lands: the rule says permanents. A separate condition kind for the blessing: the existing playerHasDesignation already carries the designation as a parameter, and the parser rule already reads the player phrases. Putting the check in derive-keywords or in a trigger scan: neither is a place that may change state. Checking between the steps of an effect to remove the mid-resolution approximation: needs a hook inside effect resolution for one keyword; deferred to the roadmap. Accepting Ascend on a spell and doing nothing with it: breaks honesty about supported cards, so it is refused.
- Consequences: Every Ascend permanent and every "if you have the city's blessing" wording of the same shapes reads and runs. Ascend on an instant or sorcery (702.131a) and any effect that gives the blessing without Ascend (none exists in the CR text) are not built; a card with the first is unsupported. A card that asks for the blessing in the middle of the same resolution that raised the permanent count to ten would read the answer from before the effect (ROADMAP). The initiative can later join Designation with its own holder rule. Existing games are unaffected until an Ascend permanent is in play (the seat field is absent otherwise); the SYNTHETIC cards added to the pool change the derive-differential soup digests. PARSER_VERSION 82 and ENGINE_VERSION 76.


## D-265: Nykthos, Shrine to Nyx: the anyColorDevotion mana production (2026-11-11)
- Context: Nykthos, Shrine to Nyx (Bruna deck) has "{2}, {T}: Choose a color. Add an amount of mana of that color equal to your devotion to that color." That is a mana ability (CR 605.1a): it does not use the stack, the color is taken with the activation, and the amount is read as it resolves, after its costs are paid (CR 605.3a, 605.3b, 700.5). No mana production sized by devotion existed. The payment planner counts what each source makes before it knows which costs the plan pays by giving permanents up. A review found that auto-pay over-produced: the {2} paid by sacrificing a creature that carries the devotion counted that creature's symbols, though it was gone when the ability resolved.
- Decision: (1) Engine: a new `ManaProduction` kind `anyColorDevotion`, valid only in a mana ability (a spell or `addMana` effect with it is refused by `validateCard`). `plainOutcomes` gives one outcome per color, with as many mana of it as the controller's devotion to it now, via `devotionOf` (now exported). A color with no devotion is an empty outcome and is not offered; with no devotion at all the ability is not offered and a hand activation is refused. The planner, the legal actions and hand activation read the outcomes as they do for `anyColor`. Devotion counts hybrid symbols for each of their colors (`devotionSymbols`). (2) Parser: `effect.choose-color` ("Choose a color.") is read only together with the devotion sentence after it, as one mana ability (`lowerChosenColorDevotion` in `lower/activated.ts`; IR `devotionToChosenColor`). Anywhere else "choose a color" and "that color" are still reported unsupported (`selector:colorChoice`). (3) The parser reads the pair only with costs that cannot change devotion (`{T}`, mana, life, mill); a sacrifice cost, of the permanent or of another, makes the ability unsupported, because devotion is read before such a cost is paid. (4) `planFor` checks each plan (`devotionConflicts` in `rules/mana-sources.ts`): a plan that taps an `anyColorDevotion` ability and also sacrifices a permanent of the seat that counts toward the devotion of the color that tap names is replaced by a plan without the sacrificing abilities, then without the devotion abilities (up to 6 rounds), or is not offered. The sacrificed permanents are found by paying the costs of the plan's sacrificing taps in plan order, as `applyPaymentPlan` does.
- Alternatives: (a) Recompute the devotion in the planner after the plan's sacrifices, in the order it activates them: a fixed point between the plan and the amounts the planner searches over, not practical in a one-pass exact search, and a wrong guess gives wrong mana. (b) Refuse only the plan where the sacrificed source paid the {2}: it misses a sacrifice for the spell's own cost, because the order in which `applyPaymentPlan` taps is not the order the rules fix. (c) Read the sacrifice-cost wording in the parser and compute devotion after the cost: wrong for the planner, which counts before it knows the costs. (d) A card-name special case for Nykthos: forbidden by AGENTS.md.
- Consequences: auto-pay never counts mana a devotion ability will not make; a plan that would is replaced by one without the conflict or not offered, never guessed. It is conservative: a cast that is really legal, with the sacrificed permanent gone but other devotion left, is not offered through auto-pay, nor is a sacrifice for the spell's own cost that would come after the devotion tap. Paying by hand in the order the player chooses is unaffected. A planner that recomputes the amount per plan could lift this later. Effects that raise devotion (Altar of the Pantheon, CR 700.5a) are still not built. Tests: `packages/engine/test/scenario-xx-devotion-mana.test.ts` (SYNTHETIC `synthetic-devotion-mana.ts`), `packages/cards/test/parser-p69-nykthos.test.ts`, `packages/cards/test/convert-grammar-engine-p69-nykthos.test.ts`. `PARSER_VERSION` 82 and `ENGINE_VERSION` 76.

## D-266: A token named after the card that makes it (2026-11-11)
- Context: Ajani, Strength of the Pride creates "a 2/2 white Cat Soldier creature token named Ajani's Pridemate". Normalization writes the card's whole name and its short name (the part before the comma for a legendary card) both as `~`, so the token name reads `~'s Pridemate` and the parser has no card name to put back (CR 111.4: the effect that creates a token sets its name).
- Decision: The token grammar reads ` named ~'s` followed by capitalized words (`SELF_TOKEN_NAME`); the lowering writes back the shortest name the card calls itself by (`LowerContext.selfName`, set per face in `parse-face.ts`, "Ajani" for "Ajani, Strength of the Pride", the whole name for a card with no short name). It refuses, never guesses, where the name is not known (a token made inside a quoted ability, where `~` is the token) and where the text as written names the token with the card's whole name when that differs from the short name (`named Ajani, Strength of the Pride's Pridemate`): normalization cannot tell the two apart, so `tokenSelfName` checks the text before normalization and leaves `selfName` empty, which refuses the name. Near misses (card name not first, no possessive, lowercase words) are not read.
- Alternatives: Keeping the short name for a whole-name wording (rejected: a guess, against the honesty rule); keeping the tilde in the token name (rejected: wrong name); special-casing the card (rejected: no card names in code).
- Consequences: Cards whose token is named with the card's short name are supported by the general mechanism; a whole-name token name is unsupported until a distinct normalization of the two names exists (ROADMAP).

## D-267: A life-total test at the start of a sentence (2026-11-11)
- Context: Ajani's 0 ability reads "If you have at least 15 life more than your starting life total, exile Ajani and each artifact and creature your opponents control." The condition existed only as a trigger's intervening "if" (CR 603.4).
- Decision: `condition.life-total` ("you have 30 or more life", "you have at least N life more than your starting life total", N a whole number above 0) may begin a sentence, "If <condition>, <instruction>", and lowers to `conditional` with `lifeTotal { compare, aboveStarting }`, tested as the ability resolves (CR 608.2c; starting life total CR 119.1 and 903.7). It works in a loyalty ability and as the text of an instant or sorcery (spell rules); as a static line of a permanent it stays unrecognised. A trigger's own "if" stays the intervening "if". The condition after the instruction, another player's life, and "X" or "0" as the number are not read.
- Alternatives: Reading it only for loyalty abilities (rejected: the sentence means the same in a spell); making the test intervening (rejected: a loyalty ability is not triggered, CR 603.4 does not apply).
- Consequences: Any sentence of this shape before a supported instruction is read by the general rule; the engine is unchanged.

## D-268: "each artifact and creature your opponents control" (2026-11-11)
- Context: The same ability exiles every artifact and every creature the opponents control; `noun.each-permanent` stopped in the middle of the union.
- Decision: `noun.each-type-union` (`parser/rules/noun/ajani.ts`) reads "each <type>, <type>, and <type> <controller> control" (card types of a permanent, CR 110.1, 205.2a), lowered to an `each` selector whose filter is `anyOf` the types, so a permanent of two of the types is chosen once; every verb that takes `PERMANENT_OPERANDS` accepts it. "exile ~ and each ..." runs as an exile of the walker and then of the group, not one simultaneous event (ROADMAP).
- Alternatives: Two separate instructions (rejected: an artifact creature would be hit twice and the wording would not match the card); a new engine node (rejected: `anyOf` already exists).
- Consequences: Unions of card types read for every group verb; the simultaneity limit is recorded in ROADMAP.

## D-269: The effect "loses the game" and "each player this creature attacked this turn" (2026-11-11)
- Context: Angel of Destiny ends the game with "each player this creature attacked this turn loses the game", and the emblem of Vraska, Golgari Queen says "that player loses the game". The engine had no effect that makes a player lose (a loss came only from state-based actions and a concession) and no record of the players a creature attacked.
- Decision: Add the effect `loseGame { player }` (CR 104.3e) for any player selector: you, that player, target player, each opponent, each player, and the new selector `attackedPlayers { of: this }`. It marks every named player who is still in the game and not under "can't lose the game" (CR 101.2) as lost, together, with a `playerLost` event of reason `effect`; all remaining players losing at once is a draw (CR 104.4a); the monarch designation of a player who loses passes on as for a concession (CR 725.4, `monarchAfterLoss`, covered by a scenario). `TurnLog.attackedPlayers` records each creature and the player it was declared attacking (CR 508.6), written only in `declareAttackers`: an attack on a planeswalker or battle adds none, a creature put onto the battlefield attacking adds none (CR 508.4: it never "attacked"), a reselected attack (CR 508.7a) keeps its first entry. The parser reads "loses the game" / "lose the game" for one player or a group the subject names, not for a list ("you and target opponent each lose"), and not with a delay or a condition; "you win the game" is not read.
- Alternatives: Reading only other players' losses (rejected: the parser and engine handle "you lose the game" correctly under CR 104.3e, so refusing it would be an artificial limit); reading the attacked players from the combat state at resolution (rejected: combat is gone at the end step, and a turn log keyed by the source id lets an ability that outlives its source still read it); adding a win effect (rejected: out of scope, a card that says it stays unsupported).
- Consequences: Angel of Destiny and the emblem of Vraska, Golgari Queen read as supported. Permanents of a player who leaves a game of more than two seats are not removed (CR 800.4a is not built, as for a concession). The ability reads the log by the id of its source, so a copy or a creature that changed controller is read by the id it has now.

## D-270: A target slot of two zones, read by exile in a triggered ability (2026-11-11)
- Context: Angel of Serenity (the Bruna deck, issue 5) targets up to three other creatures that are on the battlefield or creature cards in any graveyard with one slot (CR 115.1, 115.2: a spell or ability can say it targets an object in another zone). The engine's targets were permanents, players, or cards of one zone, so there was no slot that spans zones, and every effect that could name such a slot would have to say what it does to a card in a graveyard. The graveyard half has no "other" of its own, and on a dies or leaves-the-battlefield trigger the source is a new object in a graveyard when the targets are chosen (CR 603.10a, 400.7), so "other" would not exclude it.
- Decision: `TargetSpec.what` gets `objectOrGraveyardCard { filter, card }`: a permanent on the battlefield that `filter` matches or a card in the graveyard of any player that `card` matches (zone graveyard, no controller, owner, other or stack kind), with a count (`min`, `max`). `legalTargets` lists the permanents, then the cards of every graveyard. The validator accepts the slot only in a triggered ability with no modes and refuses any effect other than an `exile` of the slot that names it (`validate-cross-zone.ts`). "Other" in the permanent half is accepted only where the source is on the battlefield as the targets are chosen: its own enters trigger, an attack, an upkeep, an end step or a step trigger, and not in an ability that works from the graveyard; on a dies, leaves-the-battlefield or any other trigger it is refused (the card is unsupported, never read with a wrong meaning), while the same slot without "other" is read on any trigger. The parser has one noun rule for the exact phrase (up to N other target creatures from the battlefield and/or creature cards from graveyards, N at least 2), read by `exile` only; near wordings (another graveyard, another type, "or", singular, "them" after the exile, "until") are refused. The AI aims the slot at the opponent's creatures on the battlefield only, and the web says the slot in words.
- Alternatives: Make the engine apply "other" to the card half by excluding the source's new graveyard object on a look-back trigger: rejected for now, it needs the engine to know the source's identity after the zone change and a rules change for one card; refused honestly instead. Let every effect take the slot: rejected, each would have to guess what it does to a graveyard card. Two slots (one per zone): rejected, the text has one count for both zones.
- Consequences: Angel of Serenity and its synthetic siblings are supported; other types, a single graveyard, an activated ability or a spell with such a slot, another verb, and "other" on a dies or leaves trigger stay unsupported (`docs/ROADMAP.md`). Widening the slot to another verb means deciding what the verb does to a graveyard card first.

## D-271: Roll a die and read its result (2026-11-11)
- Context: Arden Angel needs "roll a four-sided die. If the result is 1, ..." and a graveyard trigger with an intervening "if". The first reviewed version let "Roll a d6. If the result is 6, draw a card instead." parse as supported with a wrong meaning: the generic "instead" handling made the roll the else branch of the result test, so the test ran before the roll, the result was unset and the die was rolled with its result never read.
- Decision: The engine has the effect rollDie (one draw of the seeded generator plus 1, CR 706.1a), the condition dieResult read from the latest roll of the same resolution (CR 706.3b), and the condition thisInYourGraveyard (the card itself in its owner's graveyard, read live, CR 113.6b, 603.4, 400.7). The parser lowers a roll only as a plain sentence of its own, and a roll is never a step that a following "instead" sentence replaces: such text is refused as unsupported, never guessed (CR 706.3b, 608.2c, 614.1a). A sentence after the roll can still be replaced by an "instead" sentence that reads the result.
- Alternatives: Refusing only a dieResult conditional that has "instead" set. This is narrower and would miss other sentences that read the roll. Making the engine evaluate the else branch after a roll in the conditional. This would change what the sentence means and would guess.
- Consequences: Text of the form "Roll a die. If the result is N, X instead." shows as unsupported and does nothing. The edges of the atMost and equal comparisons and both guards of thisInYourGraveyard are pinned by tests, so a strict-comparison, zone or owner mutation fails a test.

## D-272: Dawnbreak Reclaimer: a card of each graveyard, returned in one event (2026-11-11)
- Context: Dawnbreak Reclaimer says "Choose a creature card in an opponent's graveyard, then that player chooses a creature card in your graveyard. You may return those cards to the battlefield under their owners' control." No existing effect lets one player choose in the opponents' graveyards, the owner of that card choose in the controller's graveyard, and a single "you may" cover both cards. Review then found the engine returned the two cards by two consecutive moves, so (a) a creature with "whenever another creature enters" in one graveyard did not see the card from the other graveyard enter (CR 603.6a), (b) the as-enters replacement effects of the second card saw the first card already on the battlefield (a copy choice could pick the permanent entering in the same event; counters, untap and counts of the battlefield included it; CR 614.12 applies only continuous effects that already exist and 614.12a asks choices before anything enters), and (c) an instant or a sorcery card cannot enter the battlefield (CR 304.4, 307.4) and the engine does not apply that to a return.
- Decision: New effect `returnGraveyardPair { cardType }` and instruction `graveyardPair` (`rules/graveyard-pair.ts`), in three steps: (1) the controller chooses a card of the type in the opponents' graveyards; (2) the owner of that card ("that player") chooses a card of the type in the controller's graveyard; (3) the controller is asked once, with `confirmOptional` purpose `pairReturn`, whether to return both. Accepting puts both onto the battlefield under their owners' control (CR 110.2a, 400.3); declining returns neither and drops only this instruction. A choice with no candidate is not made (CR 608.2d): with none in an opponent's graveyard nothing is asked, with none in the controller's graveyard the first card alone is offered; a choice with one candidate is made by the engine and logged as `permanentsChosen { automatic: true }`. Graveyards are public (CR 404.2), so all choices are shown to both players. The parser reads only the exact wording (`effect.choose-graveyard-pair`, stage P69); the card types are artifact, battle, creature, enchantment, land and planeswalker, and an instant or sorcery card is refused by the parser and by `validateCard`. The two returning moves carry `together`: their `zoneChanged` events carry `simultaneous`, and `findTriggers` checks every permanent of the run for the triggers of all of them (CR 603.6a), so each card's enters triggers see the other. Each move also carries `MoveRequest.alongside`, the permanents of the run already on the battlefield, taken from `ResolutionContext.lastMoved`, which the pair starts empty and every move extends, so it survives a pause for a question. `moveOne` reads every replacement effect of the entering card from the battlefield without them (`withoutRun` in `rules/enters-run.ts`): copy candidates, enters tapped (and "unless" conditions), enters-with-counters counts, `othersEnterWithCounters`, `groupEntersUntapped`, riot grants, devour candidates and behold. A card of the run neither sees nor affects the other for replacement effects, and a copy question keeps its candidate set across the pause. The `CasualAgent` and the web UI handle the new decisions. Documented limit, pinned by a `test.fails`: when the second card asks a question as it enters, the resolution pauses and the first card's enters event is scanned before the second is on the battlefield, so the second card's own "whenever another creature enters" misses the first card (the reverse works and is tested). The two cards are still two objects created one after the other.
- Alternatives: Returning with two plain `move` instructions (rejected: the first card never sees the second for triggers and the second sees the first for replacements). Making the whole run a new primitive that creates both objects in one step (rejected as too large; `together` plus `alongside` gives the same observable result with one extra argument and one small module). Holding the events of a paused run until the run is done, or asking all as-enters questions before the first card enters, would close the remaining limit; rejected for now because it changes event logging or the move pipeline and needs its own proposal (recorded in `docs/ROADMAP.md`). Refusing the pair whenever a card of the run might have a replacement effect (rejected: it would lose the card, and the general fix works). Applying CR 304.4 and 307.4 to every move to the battlefield (rejected as out of scope: instants and sorceries are refused at the card level).
- Consequences: Dawnbreak Reclaimer is supported; Clone-style, counter, untap and count effects behave as CR 614.12 says for the pair. Any future effect that puts several permanents onto the battlefield at once can reuse `together` on its moves and a `lastMoved` that starts empty. The known gap is visible in the ROADMAP and as a `test.fails` that turns into a failure when it is closed. Devour, riot and behold in a pair are covered by construction, not by a scenario test. The SYNTHETIC fixtures live in `synthetic-dawnbreak.ts`. `PARSER_VERSION` 83 and `ENGINE_VERSION` 77.

## D-273: "For each opponent, destroy up to one target ... that player controls" is the slot of D-149 read for destroy (2026-11-11)
- Context: The brief for the group described a kicker-like destroy of artifacts and enchantments with a variable count. The real Oracle text of Dismantling Wave in the golden corpus is different: "For each opponent, destroy up to one target artifact or enchantment that player controls." then "Cycling {6}{W}{W}" and "When you cycle this card, destroy all artifacts and enchantments." There is no kicker, multikicker or variable count. The golden diagnostic flagged only ability 0 (reason unrecognised, closestRule none); Cycling and the cycle trigger already read (D-180). The engine already has the target slot "up to one target for each opponent" (`TargetSpec.onePerOpponent`, D-149), used so far only by an ability that exiles (Grasp of Fate shape). The parser read only the exile wording (`effect.exile-per-opponent`, D-150) and refused the destroy wording.
- Decision: (1) No engine node changed. A scenario test with a SYNTHETIC sorcery (`synthetic-destroy-per-opponent.ts`) pins that a spell with the slot asks the same `targets` decision at cast (min 0, max 1 for one opponent, `onePerGroup`, legal targets only the opponent's artifacts and enchantments), may be cast with no target, destroys only the chosen permanent, refuses two targets for one opponent, and offers neither creatures, lands nor the caster's own permanents. (2) New grammar rule `effect.destroy-per-opponent` in `rules/effect/angels.ts`, reading only "for each opponent, destroy up to one target <permanent phrase> that player controls". The noun parser is shared with the exile rule through the helper `perOpponentNoun`, with no behaviour change for the exile rule. Lowering is the existing `lower.destroy` and the existing `perOpponent` noun, which writes `onePerOpponent`. (3) Refused, tested as 'rejects' and as face-level near misses: no "up to" (each opponent would need a target, and the engine slot has no minimum), "up to two", "any number", a plural after "one", no controller, "you control", "an opponent controls", "that player owns", a graveyard phrase, "for each player", "for each other opponent", "for each opponent who ...", a duration, "unless they pay", "you may", a quality after "controls" ("with flying") and the bare line without "for each opponent". "... and you draw a card" reads as a second effect of a sequence, not as part of the slot. (4) The parser-p33 near-miss that listed the destroy wording as unread was changed to the form without "up to", which stays unread.
- Alternatives: Making one rule for exile and destroy with a verb alternation: rejected, the exile rule has its own "until" tail and a card-specific reject list, and a second small rule keeps each reject list honest. Reading "for each opponent, destroy target ..." (no "up to") as the same slot: rejected, the engine slot has min 0, so it would silently turn a required target into an optional one. Building a count from kicks ("up to N targets"): not applicable, the real card has none, and no card of the group asked for it. Adding a multi-opponent scenario seat: rejected, the DSL builds two seats.
- Consequences: Dismantling Wave reads as supported (Cycling, the cycle trigger that destroys every artifact and enchantment, and the per-opponent destroy); the rule also reads the creature, nonland permanent and single-type siblings. The scenario DSL has two seats, so the several-opponents case is pinned only through `targetAnswerError` (as in D-149); this is in docs/ROADMAP.md. A one-per-opponent destroy inside an ability of a permanent reads too (tested with a SYNTHETIC enters trigger). No engine, derive or digest change, so ENGINE_VERSION need not move for this group; PARSER_VERSION must move because a card changed status and golden.expected.json must be regenerated by the integrator (only Dismantling Wave flips). Tests: `packages/engine/test/scenario-xx-destroy-per-opponent.test.ts`, `packages/cards/test/parser-p96-dismantling-wave.test.ts`, `packages/cards/test/convert-grammar-engine-p96-dismantling-wave.test.ts`.

## D-274: Miracle (2026-11-11)
- Context: Entreat the Angels ("Miracle {X}{W}{W}") of the Bruna deck needs Miracle (CR 702.94a-b), a static ability linked to a triggered ability (CR 603.11): a reveal made as the card is drawn, a trigger, and a cast from the hand for the miracle cost. It builds on the machinery of Madness and of the commander question of the draw, so it is a K-class change, not an S-class subsystem. The review found that a miracle line on a face other than the front face was accepted as supported but never offered, because the engine reads the front face only, and that the reveal question shows in the other seat's view.
- Decision: A named alternative cost `miracle { cost }` on a face (mana only; an {X} is allowed here and in no other named alternative cost; not on a land; one per face), with the three abilities of the keyword added by the engine. (1) The reveal: a card drawn that has a miracle cost and is the first card its owner has drawn this turn (the `nth` of `cardDrawn`; a replaced draw is not a card drawn, CR 121.1) asks its owner `confirmOptional { purpose: 'miracleReveal' }` right after the draw, in the draw step (the step waits) and between two draws of a resolving spell (the instruction `miracleReveal`). The question is asked whether or not the cost could be paid. Accepting emits the public `cardsRevealed` and `miracleRevealed`; declining emits nothing, because the events are public. (2) The trigger goes on the stack from `miracleRevealed`, with the card in the hand as its source (CR 702.94b). (3) As it resolves, when the card is still the same object in the hand and could be cast, its owner is asked `confirmOptional { purpose: 'miracle' }`; accepting is `beginCast(card, 'miracle', resolving)` (CR 601.2a-i, 118.9, 608.2g, 107.3a: no timing restriction, no priority, X announced as the spell is cast). The parser reads "Miracle {M}" (with {X} through `cost.mana-x`) as an alternative cost of the face. `validateCard` refuses a miracle cost on any face after the first (CR 702.94a: the engine reads the front face only), so such a card imports unsupported with a reason. The reveal question is private (no `pending`, no card in the other seat's view), but because it is asked only for a card with miracle, the other seat's `decidingSeat` is the drawing seat while it is open; this is recorded as a known limit in `docs/ROADMAP.md`.
- Alternatives: Reading the miracle cost of every face and offering the reveal for a back face (rejected: a double-faced card is cast front face up, so the back face's cost could never be used and nothing models it). Emitting an event when the player declines (rejected: the events are public and would tell the opponent the card has miracle). Asking the question for every first draw and answering it for cards without miracle, or hiding `decidingSeat` (not built: harmless against the AI, a listed limit for two humans). Skipping the question when the cost cannot be paid (rejected: revealing is the player's choice and mana and targets can change before the trigger resolves; the AI declines when it could not pay).
- Consequences: Entreat the Angels is supported and the keyword is general for any front-face miracle with a mana cost, with an {X} as in "Miracle {X}{W}{W}" (the 14 cards of the owner's run counted in reports/templates.json are the template "Miracle {M}" without an X, a different wording). Not built: miracle granted by another effect, two miracle costs on a face, a miracle cost on a back face (unsupported by `validateCard`), a persistent "revealed" mark on the card in the hand, and a `decidingSeat` that does not tell an observer that the card has miracle.

## D-275: A static ability an effect gives for good, read after the layers (2026-11-11)
- Context: The Book of Exalted Deeds gives a permanent "You can't lose the game and your opponents can't win the game." for the rest of the game (CR 611.2a). The engine ran the two statics only as printed abilities, and `grantAbility` existed only for Backup (until end of turn).
- Decision: The effect `grantAbility` takes `duration: 'permanent'`: a layer 6 continuous effect (CR 613.1f, 613.7) on the permanents the selector names as the effect begins, read by `derive` from the abilities the object has after the layers (`mayHaveStatic`, `cannotLoseGame`, which protects the controller of the permanent that has the ability, CR 113.6). `validateCard` accepts a card's `grantAbility` only with `'permanent'` and only with the static abilities `cantLoseGame` and `opponentsCantWin`; a given ability that carries a `condition` is refused too, because the engine reads the given ability with none and would drop the condition silently. `'untilEndOfTurn'` stays the engine's own (Backup).
- Alternatives: Giving any ability for good was rejected: an activated or triggered ability needs its own tests. Applying a condition to the given static ability was rejected: no card needs it and `derive` does not check one there. Silently ignoring a condition was rejected as dishonest.
- Consequences: One new ability of cards is supported (The Book of Exalted Deeds). The protection follows the permanent: an opponent who takes the Angel is protected and the owner is not, and it ends with the permanent (CR 400.7). Other granted statics, conditions on them and durations are refused by `validateCard` and listed in `docs/ROADMAP.md`.

## D-276: Read "It gains \"<static ability>.\"" with no duration, for a target only (2026-11-11)
- Context: The Book of Exalted Deeds gives an Angel "You can't lose the game and your opponents can't win the game." with no duration, so the grant lasts for the rest of the game (CR 611.2a). The grammar had no rule for a quoted static ability given to an object, and the review found that "it" after a token the text made (for example "Put a counter on target Angel. Create a 3/3 token. It gains ...") would have been read as the earlier target, though CR 111.1 makes the pronoun name the new token.
- Decision: Rule `effect.gain-static-ability` (stage P69) reads "<target, it, that creature> gains \"<static ability>.\"" with no duration. The quoted text is read as an ability of its own and lowered by `lowerAngelStatic`; the lowering gives only `cantLoseGame` and `opponentsCantWin`, with no condition, and only on a target of the same text. It refuses (the text stays unsupported) "it" or "that creature" after a target the text destroyed, exiled, sacrificed or returned (`ctx.removed`, CR 400.7) and after any instruction that created a token, also when a target came first (`ctx.madeAToken`, set by `lowerSentences` for every `createToken` effect, so Treasure, Investigate and a copy token count; CR 111.1). The segmenter ends a sentence at a quote that closes after its period when an "Activate ..." or "This ability costs ..." restriction follows, so the restriction reads as the timing restriction.
- Alternatives: Reading "it" as the last target regardless of a token before it was rejected: the grant would go to another object than the text says. Tracking the exact token and granting to it was rejected: the engine's `grantAbility` fixes its objects from a target, not a created token, so it would need a new object reference. Extending the lowering to every static ability was rejected: only the two protection statics are read after the layers.
- Consequences: A line with a token before "it" stays unsupported and is flagged instead of getting a wrong meaning. `ctx.madeAToken` is general and available to other rules (the sibling `gain-keyword` rule has the same pre-existing flaw and does not use it yet). Giving another static ability, a quoted activated or triggered ability, or a duration remains refused.

## D-277: Meld object model: one permanent on the battlefield, two cards in every other zone (2026-11-11)
- Context: Bruna, the Fading Light and Gisela, the Broken Blade meld into Brisela, Voice of Nightmares (CR 701.42, 712.4). The owner approved docs/design/meld.md with the model that a meld card is an ordinary card with its own front face in the library, hand, graveyard, stack, exile and command zone, that a melded pair is one permanent on the battlefield shown as one object, and that when it leaves it becomes two cards again (a commander goes to the command zone as CR 903.9c says).
- Decision: `GameObject.card` is the first card of a melded permanent and `GameObject.meldedWith` the second, with `face` 1, the combined back face, which the first card's definition holds as `faces[1]` (the same face on both cards, CR 712.8g); derive, the layers, abilities and the view read that face and needed no change. `CardDefinition.layout` is `'meld'` and `CardDefinition.meld.partner` names the other half. Every read of "the card of an object" that must see two cards goes through `rules/melded.ts` (`cardsOf`, `commanderCardOf`, `isCommanderCardId`, `isCommanderObject`, `successorsOf`, `meldPairIssue`, `meldCardsIssue`, `meldedManaCost`, `arrangeMeldedCards`); `test/meld-reads.test.ts` fails when a rule reads the commander flag of `obj.card` directly. The commander card of a melded permanent is always its first card (the meld effect orders them so, `checkInvariants` checks it), so `commanderCardOf` reads only the first card. A melded permanent may be phased out (`checkInvariants` allows a non-front face in `phased`, CR 702.26b). Leaving the battlefield is one move that makes two objects (`MoveRequest.meldWith` going in, `MoveResult.alsoNewObject` coming out): one `died` event and one leaves trigger, two `zoneChanged` events with the second flagged `component` so a trigger about permanents counts it once (CR 712.21), last-known information with `companionSuccessor` so "it", `triggerCard`, `thisCard`, "exile it", `lastMoved`, `exileReturns` and `linkedExile` find both cards (CR 712.21c); a replacement effect applies once to both cards (CR 712.21d); the commander card alone goes to the command zone when its owner chooses it under CR 903.9b, the other card to the zone the permanent would have gone to (CR 903.9c), and in a graveyard or exile each commander card is an object that CR 903.9a asks about; the owner of both cards gets them whoever controlled the permanent. A copy of a melded permanent copies the combined face, has mana value 0 and is not melded (CR 707.8); a token copy is one ordinary token. `GameState` and `ObjectView` carry the new fields (`ObjectView.meld`), ENGINE_VERSION is 78. The scenario DSL places a melded permanent with the option `meldedWith`; the cards are SYNTHETIC (`synthetic-meld.ts`).
- Alternatives: One permanent object plus an object for the second card kept off the battlefield was rejected: two objects in a zone that the rules say has one. Two permanent objects linked on the battlefield was rejected: it breaks "one permanent" for triggers, damage and the view. A second card on every battlefield object (an array) was rejected: only a melded permanent has two. Reading the second card as a possible commander was rejected: the invariant makes it unreachable and dead code hides mistakes.
- Consequences: Every reader of a card of an object must use `rules/melded.ts`; the state shape changed, so the derive digests were checked against the previous version (they differ only through the new SYNTHETIC cards in a pool, none of an existing game changed). Two commander cards of one pair are not built (D-278). Face-down melded permanents are not built (CR 712.16, no effect turns a permanent face down yet). Real-card behavior is proven only through SYNTHETIC cards; Bruna, Gisela and Brisela come from the owner's extraction (D-280).

## D-278: The meld effect, its condition and the parser rules for Bruna and Gisela (2026-11-11)
- Context: Bruna and Gisela say "At the beginning of your end step, if you both own and control this creature and a creature named X, exile them, then meld them into Y." and Brisela has a static ability; none of it was readable.
- Decision: The AST has `Effect` `meld { partner, result }` (`rules/meld.ts`, `runMeld`) and `Condition` `ownsAndControlsNamed { name, type }` (`rules/meld-condition.ts`), checked as the ability triggers and again as it resolves (CR 603.4). The effect exiles the source and the creature named `partner` that its controller owns and controls (a candidate that can meld is preferred over a token that shares the name; the choice among equals is not a player decision), as two ordinary moves that replacement effects apply to (CR 701.42a); then, if both exile objects are still in exile and form one pair (CR 701.42b: both meld cards of one pair with the same combined face, same owner, neither a token) it puts them onto the battlefield with `face` 1 and `meldWith` as one permanent under the controller of the ability (CR 712.14c); otherwise they stay and a `meldFailed` event says why (CR 701.42c). The commander's exile object goes first. Two commander cards of one pair are not built: such a partner is not a candidate (`twoCommanderCards`), so the ability does not start and nothing is exiled, rather than exile cards that could not be melded; CR 701.42 would meld them, so it is a known deviation (docs/ROADMAP.md). Parser (stage P70, PARSER_VERSION 84): `condition.own-and-control-named`, `effect.meld`, `static.opponents-cant-cast-spells`; IR `IrNameArg` and the lowering in `lower/meld.ts` take the partner from the condition, only as an intervening if; `segment.ts` keeps a comma inside "a creature named Bruna, the Fading Light"; the graveyard phrase "Angel or Human creature card" reads creature types only (the card type must be creature) or is refused. `validateCard` checks the structure of a meld card (two faces, a partner name, a combined face that is a permanent with no mana cost, the ability naming the same partner and result, no replacement effect, riot or devour on the combined face); the reminder text "(Melds with X.)" is checked against the data, not an ability. Only the end-step shape of Bruna and Gisela is read.
- Alternatives: Reading the meld as a flicker plus an enter-as-copy was rejected: the result is a different object made of two cards. Choosing among several same-named candidates by a player decision was left out (unreachable in a tested deck). Melding two commander cards was rejected for now: 903.9c would have no tested answer.
- Consequences: Other meld pairs with other trigger shapes stay unsupported until their shape is added with a test. A token copy named like the partner is exiled and the real card stays exiled (CR 701.42c example), which is tested.

## D-279: The order of the two cards of a melded permanent that left the battlefield (2026-11-11)
- Context: CR 712.21a lets the owner arrange the two cards of a melded permanent put into their graveyard or library (the order of a library is not revealed); CR 712.21b says that a player who exiles a melded permanent determines the relative timestamp order of the two cards, an exception to CR 613.7m, as in the Duplicant example, where the controller of the exiling ability chooses. The review showed that the first version always asked the owner.
- Decision: A move of a melded permanent to a graveyard, a library or exile records a `MeldOrder { seat, first, second, zone }` in `GameState.meldOrders`; `seat` is the player asked: the owner for a graveyard or a library, and for exile `MoveRequest.by`, the controller of the spell or ability whose instruction moves the permanent (set by the instruction runner of `rules/effects.ts`, also when a replacement effect turns that move into exile), else the controller of the permanent when a rule or a cost exiles it. When state-based actions are next checked, `sba.ts` `meldOrderDecision` asks `seat` a `chooseOption` with `purpose: 'meldOrder'` and `meldOrder: { first, second, zone }`; the two options are the names of the two cards and the answer is the card that goes on top of the graveyard or library (the order is not revealed) or that is exiled last (the later timestamp); `answerMeldOrder` in `api.ts` applies it with `arrangeMeldedCards`, which reads the zone owner from the objects, and state-based actions are checked again. A pair that is no longer together (not both in the zone, or in a graveyard or library not adjacent) is dropped without asking. Nothing is asked for a hand or the command zone. The decision is on the web as the named-option dialog "Order the two cards" with a prompt for each zone, and the casual agent answers with the first option (`casual-options.ts`).
- Alternatives: Always asking the owner was rejected: it is wrong for exile (CR 712.21b). Asking inside the move as the cards are put into the zone was rejected for now: it needs a question in `moveOne` for every path that moves a permanent (destroy, state-based death, sacrifice, bounce).
- Consequences: An instruction later in the same resolution that reads the top of the library or graveyard sees the default order, and a library shuffled so that the two cards stay adjacent is still asked (docs/ROADMAP.md). When a replacement effect, not an instruction, exiles the permanent and no spell or ability moved it, the controller of the permanent decides. "The last card exiled with it" (`linkedCardOf`, CR 607.2a) is read by timestamp, so the answer to the exile question decides which card a Shape-Twin-like permanent copies. The tests are `test/scenario-xx-meld-order.test.ts` (including an opponent exiling) and `apps/web/test/meld-order-render.test.tsx`.

## D-280: The melded face comes from Scryfall with the pair (2026-11-11)
- Context: Brisela, Voice of Nightmares is a card of its own that no decklist names; the owner's decision is that its Oracle text, data and art are fetched like every other card and nothing is invented or hard-coded. The cloud sandbox cannot reach Scryfall, so the component names of `all_parts` could not be checked.
- Decision: The stored card already keeps `relatedParts` (the name and component of each `all_parts` entry). `packages/cards/src/convert/meld.ts` reads them: `meldRelation` says whether a card is a `half` (layout `meld`, exactly one other `meld_part` and exactly one `meld_result` named), the `result` (it lists itself as `meld_result`, or it is a one-faced card with no mana cost that lists `meld_part` entries and no `meld_result` and not itself, whatever its layout) or `none` with the problems that say why; the reminder text "(Melds with X.)" must name the same partner as the data. The component names `meld_part` and `meld_result` are UNVERIFIED and read defensively, and docs say so. `importCard(card, ..., related?)` embeds the combined face as `faces[1]` of both halves; `resolveNames` makes a second pass to fetch the result with the pair (`ResolveResult.related`, `relatedLookup`, `MeldLookup`), the import screen passes it to the converter, and a deck's cards carry the third card although the list does not name it. A meld card whose result is missing, ambiguous or unreadable is unsupported with a reason that starts with `layout "meld"` and its support is never cached (`cachedSupport`), so a bad day does not make a card unsupported for good; the combined face seen alone is unsupported (CR 712.4b). The tools carry it too: `corpus:extract` takes the result with the pair as a `related: true` golden record that no group counts and counts a requested name taken that way as found, `coverage:cards`, `corpus:decks` and `precon:snapshot` defer a half until its result is seen (`CardIndex.meldFaces`), `corpus:check-issue` calls a deck-support issue without the result's record incomplete, `corpus:from-issue` does not make a `related` record an acceptance card, and the "Ask for support on GitHub" button writes the result's record too. Bruna and Gisela stay unsupported in the golden corpus for a data reason only (no `relatedParts`, no record of Brisela); the owner runs `pnpm corpus:extract` with the three names and commits the result.
- Alternatives: Hard-coding Brisela's data was rejected by the owner. Indexing the melded faces by the name a half's `meld_result` gives was rejected in favor of a sturdier `meldRelation` that recognizes a face with the layout meld that lists only the halves, which fixes every tool at once. Treating a card with an incomplete relation as normal was rejected: it is unsupported with a reason.
- Consequences: A deck with a meld card costs one more request, for the combined face, and the face comes from the cache the next time. If the real component names differ, change `MELD_PART` and `MELD_RESULT` and nothing else. The tests use SYNTHETIC trios (`convert-meld.test.ts`, `tools/corpus/meld.test.ts`, `apps/web/test/import-meld.test.ts`).

## D-281: Mana value, devotion, copies and transform of a melded permanent (2026-11-11)
- Context: CR 202.3c gives a melded permanent the combined mana cost of the front faces of the two cards (so 11 for Brisela), and CR 707.8, 712.8g and 202.3c say a copy of it has mana value 0; CR 712.4c and 712.9 say a meld card cannot transform; CR 712.16 says a melded permanent cannot be turned face down.
- Decision: `meldedManaCost` sums the front faces' costs for a melded permanent on the battlefield; the combined face has no cost of its own, so a copy (which takes the combined face, CR 707.8) has none and mana value 0, and a token copy is one ordinary token. Devotion reads the copiable cost (`devotionCostOf`, CR 700.5a), so a melded permanent counts the front faces' mana symbols (this also repairs the transformed back face), and `mana-sources.ts` reads the same cost. `transform` does nothing to a melded permanent; no effect turns a permanent face down yet, so a melded face-down permanent is not built.
- Alternatives: Giving the combined face a stored mana cost was rejected: the data has none and the rule sums the fronts. Letting a copy keep the sum was rejected: CR 202.3c says 0.
- Consequences: Everything that asks for a mana value goes through `layouts.ts`. Face down melded permanents come with the face-down proposal.

## D-282: Cast restriction by mana value: "Your opponents can't cast spells with mana value 3 or less" (2026-11-11)
- Context: The combined face of Bruna and Gisela has this static ability; the engine had no restriction on casting by mana value.
- Decision: The static ability `opponentsCantCastSpells { spells: ObjectFilter }` (CR 101.2: "can't" beats "can"; CR 604.1; CR 601.2) makes a spell that matches the filter illegal to cast, by any means, while the permanent is on the battlefield; its subject is the controller. `rules/cast-restrictions.ts` judges the mana value a spell would have on the stack (CR 202.3e: an announced X counts), so a spell with {X} is legal when some X makes its mana value pass (`legality.ts` `canCast` uses the least allowed X, `cast.ts` raises the minimum of the `chooseX` decision) and the announced X cannot go below it; a free cast uses X 0. The parser rule `static.opponents-cant-cast-spells` reads one subject (the controller), one number and the comparison words; another subject, a card type of spell, a time, "or activate abilities" and numbers in words are refused. The restriction is read from the permanent on the battlefield only.
- Alternatives: A hard-coded rule for the one card was rejected: it is a general filter. Checking only the printed mana value was rejected: it would let an X spell with a low announced X through.
- Consequences: The least X is read when the spell is cast; a copy of a spell, a cast "without paying" beyond X 0, an X chosen by another effect and a restriction that appears while a spell is being cast are not re-checked (docs/ROADMAP.md). Tested with SYNTHETIC Gatekeeper and SYNTHETIC X Surge (`test/scenario-xx-cast-restriction-spells.test.ts`).

## D-283: Last-known information of permanents that leave together (2026-11-12)
- Context: CR 603.10a makes "dies" and the other leaves-the-battlefield triggers look back in time, and its own example is two permanents put into graveyards at the same time, each seeing the other. The engine moved the permanents one after the other and derived the later ones' last-known information after the first had left, so an ability a permanent granted to its neighbour (layer 6, CR 613.1f) was lost for whichever creature moved second: a grant from one creature to both of a pair fired for one of them, depending on timestamp order. Found while building soulbond.
- Decision: The last-known information (CR 113.7a, 603.10a) of every battlefield permanent of one event is recorded against the state as the event began, before the first moves (`rules/simultaneous.ts` `recordTogether` for the instructions of one effect and `recordObjectsTogether` for movers that move objects directly; `rules/sba.ts` for its own batch). The move carries `lkiRecorded` (`MoveRequest`, the `move` and `sacrifice` instructions) and `moveOne` keeps a record only for a flagged move whose record exists, so a record of a permanent that did not leave (a regeneration shield) is never reused by a later departure. Covered: state-based actions, destroy, exile, return-all (`moveToZone` of an `each`), sacrifice-all, the chosen sacrifices, a spare effect, a choice of several permanents to move, a sacrifice cost of several permanents, the legend rule and devour. A batch of one is unchanged. The state-based-action batch writes an entry for every member of a batch of two or more, including a creature that then does not move (a regenerated creature keeps an unread entry): reads are live first, so behaviour is the same, but the derive digests of two of the nine boards of `derive-digest.expected.json` differ from the base by this state.
- Alternatives: Deriving the information lazily at the first read was rejected (the neighbour is gone by then). Recording for every move was rejected (it changes the hash and the cost for no gain; a lone departure records itself). A card-specific fix for the Seraph was rejected (no card-name special cases).
- Consequences: The audit of the movers was a search for every place that moves a battlefield permanent to a graveyard, not a proof: another mover found later is a bug of the same kind and must record before the first move (`docs/ROADMAP.md`). Tests: `scenario-xx-lookback-batch.test.ts`, `scenario-xx-soulbond-batch.test.ts`.

## D-284: A dies trigger may create a delayed return of the card the creature became (2026-11-12)
- Context: The grant of Breathkeeper Seraph is "When this creature dies, you may return it to the battlefield under its owner's control at the beginning of your next upkeep." The engine had delayed triggers that move the cards a spell moved (`moved`), but none that names the card a creature became in the graveyard (CR 400.7, 603.7c).
- Decision: Slice P, built first: `delayedTrigger { at: { step: 'upkeep', whose: 'you' }, effect: moveToZone { objects: triggerCard, to: 'battlefield', controller } }` is valid as the effect of a `dies` trigger (`ast/validate-later.ts` accepts `triggerCard` only in a dies trigger, since a leaves-the-battlefield trigger may find the card in any zone). `rules/effects.ts` creates one delayed ability for each card `triggerCard` finds now, in a graveyard; a token that died and a commander that went to the command zone give none; a card that left the graveyard since is a new object and is not found (CR 603.7c). The "you may" is the `optional` of the dies ability, made as that ability resolves (CR 603.5): declining creates no delayed ability and it is not asked again at the upkeep. A dies that resolves in the controller's own upkeep returns the card at the next one (CR 603.7a). The parser reads it as `effect.return-at-upkeep` (`DELAYED_RETURN_AT_UPKEEP`) only in a trigger of `~` dying and, since D-287, only as the first instruction of the trigger.
- Alternatives: Asking "you may" again at the upkeep was rejected (CR 603.5: the choice is made on resolution of the dies ability). Reading "it" in a leaves-the-battlefield trigger was rejected (the card may be in any zone).
- Consequences: Any dies trigger of `~` that returns "it" at the beginning of your next upkeep now parses; "at the beginning of the next end step" with `triggerCard` is not read. Tests: `scenario-xx-dies-return.test.ts`, `parser-soulbond.test.ts`.

## D-285: The pair is a designation on two creatures, read only through rules/pairing.ts (2026-11-12)
- Context: CR 702.95 (soulbond): a creature becomes paired with another as a soulbond ability resolves and the pair ends when either leaves the battlefield, another player gains control of either, or either stops being a creature (CR 702.95e). A stored link can be stale for a moment (the partner left and is a new object, control changed, the partner is phased out) before the state-based actions run.
- Decision: `GameObject.paired?: { with: ObjectId; by: SeatId }` on both creatures, absent unless paired (the hash of a game with no pair is unchanged), not copiable and absent on a new object after any zone change (CR 400.7, 707.2). `rules/pairing.ts` is the only reader (`test/paired-reads.test.ts` scans the sources by property, bracket, destructuring and literal access, with no escape comment): `linkedPartnerOf` (the pair stands: both exist, in play, that is on the battlefield or phased out, linked from both sides, same player, and that player controls both, read through `controlOf`, which reads layer 2 effects of a phased-out permanent too) decides "unpaired" for CR 702.95d; `partnerOf` (the pair stands and both are on the battlefield) is what static abilities, conditions and the view read. `rules/pairing-sba.ts` `endBrokenPairs` runs with the state-based actions (CR 704 does not list it; the engine's choice, as for the Ring-bearer and Ascend), clears a pair that no longer stands and emits `creaturesUnpaired { a, b, why: 'left' | 'control' | 'notCreature' }`; it is the one place that asks `derive` whether a creature is still a creature (CR 613.1d: reading it inside the layers would be circular). Phasing, the owner's approved reading: a pair survives one creature phasing out (CR 702.26d: phasing is no zone change or change of control, and CR 702.95e lists no phasing) and what it gives is switched off while either is phased out (CR 702.26b), also for the creature still phased in; a creature whose partner is phased out is still paired, so it is not offered to another soulbond creature (`ObjectView.pairedPhasedOut`, "Pair on hold"). CR 702.26f (with 611.2b) ends "for as long as" effects that track a phased-out permanent, and CR 702.95a words the pair "for as long as both remain creatures on the battlefield under your control": that is the reading against this one, weighed and not decisive; no published ruling was checked. If it turns out the other way the change is confined to `rules/pairing-sba.ts` and `linkedPartnerOf`. A melded permanent is one creature and one object (D-277): a pair names that object.
- Alternatives: Storing the pair on the player or in a table was rejected (a designation of the object follows CR 400.7 for free). Reading the field everywhere was rejected (a stale link would read as a pair). Ending the pair on phasing was rejected as the owner's approved reading above.
- Consequences: Between a creature losing its types and the next state-based-action check, inside one resolution, the pair still gives what it gives (`docs/ROADMAP.md`). Tests: `scenario-xx-soulbond-lifecycle.test.ts`, `pairing-stale-link.test.ts`, `paired-reads.test.ts`.

## D-286: Soulbond: the keyword, the pair choice, the grant to the pair, the parser and the AI (2026-11-12)
- Context: The Bruna deck's Breathkeeper Seraph reads "Flying, soulbond" and "As long as ~ is paired with another creature, each of those creatures has <dies-return ability>". The owner approved the proposal with its defaults: slice P first (D-283, D-284), then soulbond; one decision for one or several candidates; the AI always pairs with the strongest creature; scope is the Seraph's shapes only.
- Decision: (1) `Keyword` `soulbond` (printed only, not in the grantable keywords; `validateCard` refuses it on a face or token that is not a creature) expands in `rules/derive-keywords.ts` into the two triggered abilities of CR 702.95a (`rules/soulbond-abilities.ts`): "When this creature enters" with the intervening if `soulbondReady { with: 'another' }` and "Whenever another creature you control enters" with `soulbondReady { with: 'triggerSubject' }`, each followed by `pair`. The condition `soulbondReady` and the effect `pair` are the engine's own and refused in card data. (2) `rules/soulbond.ts`: the intervening if is read when the event happens and again on resolution (CR 603.4); `runPair` checks CR 702.95c again (both creatures on the battlefield under the controller's control, neither paired; the re-checks repeat the intervening if and are kept as the engine's own guard), then asks one `choosePermanent` decision of purpose `soulbond` with `min` 0, `max` 1 and the unpaired creatures as `legal`, even for a single candidate: choosing none is the "may" (CR 603.5); nothing is asked, and nobody paired, when there is none. A pair is never formed over another (CR 702.95d). With two soulbond creatures and one newcomer the controller orders two triggers and the second finds them paired. (3) The grant: `StaticSubject` `{ kind: 'pair' }` ("each of those creatures": the permanent and its `partnerOf`, read at call time so the derive caches never answer for another pair) and `Condition` `{ kind: 'paired' }` (through `partnerOf`); one static `grantAbility` of the dies-return ability with subject `pair` and condition `paired` is the Seraph's second line (CR 702.95b, 611.3a, 613.1f, 613.7a). An unpaired source affects nothing, not even itself. The validator accepts `pair` for `modifyPt`, `grantKeyword` and `grantAbility` only, and `paired` only as the "as long as" condition of a static ability that `derive` reads (D-287). With D-283 the partner's dies trigger, the Seraph's own and both together all fire (CR 603.10a). (4) Events `creaturesPaired { a, b, by }` and `creaturesUnpaired { a, b, why }`, `ObjectView.pairedWith`, the scenario DSL `pairedWith`, `expect.paired`, `expect.unpaired`. (5) Parser (PARSER_VERSION 85, then 86 with D-287): `keyword.line` reads "soulbond"; `condition.paired`; `noun.paired-creatures` ("each of those creatures"); the pair subject is lowered only for a granted triggered ability under the condition `paired`, so a keyword or +N/+N for the pair, "both creatures", "paired with a Human", "isn't paired", the activated grants and a granted soulbond stay unsupported and a card with soulbond and an unread line is unsupported as a whole. Any quoted triggered ability granted to the pair is read, not only the Seraph's. Breathkeeper Seraph is the only golden card that moves (unsupported to supported). (6) AI and web: the casual agent (and so the greedy and the heuristic agent, which delegate) always pairs, with the creature with the most power, then toughness, the first listed on a tie (`casual-soulbond.ts`); the "you may" of the dies-return ability is worded and answered from the ability on the stack, not from the text of the creature that died; the web panel offers "Pair them" / "Don't pair", both tiles show a Paired flag, and the log words both events.
- Alternatives: One decision per candidate was rejected (one `choosePermanent` with `min` 0 is the may and the choice). A smarter pairing heuristic was deferred to `docs/ROADMAP.md` (it needs the evaluator; not guessed). Making the keyword grantable was rejected (the abilities are built from the printed keyword). Reading the second lines of the other soulbond cards was deferred until the owner's next coverage report (the ROADMAP records which shapes the engine now makes cheap).
- Consequences: The engine runs a keyword, +N/+N or activated ability granted to the pair although the parser does not read them yet. Tests: `scenario-xx-soulbond*.test.ts`, `ast-soulbond-validate.test.ts`, `parser-soulbond*.test.ts`, `convert-grammar-engine-soulbond.test.ts`, `casual-soulbond.test.ts`, `soulbond-games.test.ts`, the web soulbond tests.

## D-287: The condition "paired" is read only as a static "as long as"; a sentence that asks another player is read only when it names nobody else (2026-11-12)
- Context: Review of the soulbond branch found four ways a card read as supported and meant something else. (1) `condition.paired` as the intervening "if" of a dies or leaves trigger: the source is a new object in the graveyard (CR 400.7) with no pair, so the trigger never fired. (2) The same condition in an attack trigger: a Lightning Bolt in response kills the source and the intervening "if" is checked again as the ability resolves (CR 603.4), where CR 608.2h reads the permanent with its last-known information (paired) but the engine reads no pair of a permanent that is gone. (3) "At the beginning of your next upkeep" inside "each opponent may ...": with no "have you" the engine runs the instruction with the asked player as "you" (`runsAs: 'chooser'`, CR 608.2d), so the delayed ability came at their upkeep; the same for any "you", "your" or "opponent" of the controller in such a sentence. (4) "it" in "Each creature you control has flying as long as it's paired" was taken for the card itself. Also, `DELAYED_RETURN_AT_UPKEEP` read "it" as the dying creature after a created token, a Treasure or a discard, where "it" may be that other object.
- Decision: (1) and (2): `paired` reads the pair of the permanent on the battlefield now and keeps no last-known information, so it is read only as the "as long as" condition of a static ability (`LowerContext.staticCondition`, set by `lowerStaticStatement` alone). Every other use (triggered, activated, mana and replacement abilities, conditional effects, spells, a face's alternative or additional costs, a static ability that works from the graveyard, the same inside a quotation granted to the pair) is refused by the parser and by `validateCard` (`checkPairedPlacement`, defence in depth for hand-written data). (3) `lowerPlayersMay` refuses a sentence without "have you" whose text says you, your, opponent, another player or other players in any clause (including "if they do/don't"), and never reads one inside a quotation (no text); the delayed return and the delayed mana carry a further `askedPlayerActs` guard. The positive paths stay: the controller's own "you may", no "may", and "each opponent may have you return it". (4) "it" is `~` in "as long as it's paired" only where every subject of the static ability is `~` (`LowerContext.staticSubjectIsSelf`). `DELAYED_RETURN_AT_UPKEEP` is lowered only when no instruction was lowered before it (`LowerContext.lowered`), so after a token, a Treasure or a discard the card is unsupported. PARSER_VERSION 86; ENGINE_VERSION unchanged (evaluation did not change). Tests: `parser-soulbond.test.ts`, `parser-asked-player-you.test.ts`, `ast-soulbond-validate.test.ts`, `convert-grammar-engine-asked-player.test.ts`, `scenario-xx-soulbond-lifecycle.test.ts`, `pairing-stale-link.test.ts`; the refusals are mutation-checked.
- Alternatives: Evaluating `paired` with the last-known information of the source (CR 603.10a, 608.2h) was rejected for now: it needs the pair in `recordLki` and a read in `evaluateCondition` for a source that left, an ENGINE_VERSION bump and new derive digests, and no known card needs it (`docs/ROADMAP.md`). Refusing only the dies trigger of `~` was rejected: "whenever another creature dies, if ~ is paired" and the attack trigger killed in response have the same problem.
- Consequences: A card is unsupported, never wrong, for these shapes; the Seraph's own line and the printed "as long as it's paired ... has flying" forms are static abilities and are read. Known and recorded in `docs/ROADMAP.md`: a delayed ability created in a sentence that asks another player is controlled by the asked player where CR 603.7e gives it to the controller (the right player still acts); the same distributive "it" convention for other static conditions ("as long as it's untapped") is not audited here.

## D-288: Automatic payment taps the least flexible mana first and keeps the colors the hand needs (2026-11-12)
- Context: The owner's issue 18: with automatic mana the game "makes dumb choices", for example a colored land before colorless mana, and once a Treasure before an untapped land. The payment planner (`mana/payment.ts`) preferred lands to creatures to artifacts, which taps a Forest before a Sol Ring, and its `reserve` (colors to keep untapped for other plays) existed and was tested, but no caller passed it.
- Decision: (1) The planner's preference order becomes: life, sacrifice-tier sources, reserve, extra effect, creature-tier sources, produced mana left over, then **flexibility lost** (the number of colors the tapped sources could have made, so a colorless land or rock goes before a colored land, a basic before a land of two colors and any-color mana last), then artifact before land at equal flexibility, then pool, then determinism. (2) A cast passes the colors of the mana costs of the other cards in the caster's hand as the `reserve` (`handReserve` in `rules/cast-cost.ts`; a hybrid or Phyrexian symbol counts each of its colors), a preference and never a reason to fail. `ENGINE_VERSION` 75 (80 once merged with the Bruna program), derive digests recorded again.
- Alternatives: Reading the whole hand and the board to pick the best order for the next turn: a search of its own, not needed for the cases the owner named. Keeping lands before artifacts: it is the rule that taps the Forest before Sol Ring. Applying the reserve to every payment (abilities, taxes): a cast is the case where another spell follows.
- Consequences: Sol Ring and colorless lands pay generic costs first and the colors a hand needs stay untapped; the AI pays the same way. The Treasure part of the issue could not be reproduced: a Treasure is a sacrifice-tier source, which is spent only when nothing else can pay (`mana-payment.test.ts`, "a sacrifice source is used when it is the only way to pay"), so it needs the owner's cast and board to find.

## D-289: The strength of the heuristic agent is measured on paired arena games; the soak decks only give a floor (2026-11-12)
- Context: Issue 21. `heuristic-games.test.ts` asserted a win rate of at least 0.8 for the heuristic agent against the random agent over the 20 games of the soak decks, and the sample gave 0.75 (15 of 20; 16 before group 6 of the Bruna program, 0.76 against 0.79 over 100 games). Measured: on the arena decks with every seed played twice with the seats swapped, the same agent wins 200 of 200 games against random (`pnpm ai:arena --a heuristic --b random --games 200 --seed 1`) and 60 of 60 on the real precons (`--precons --pairing cross --games 60 --seed 5`). The soak decks are 20 to 24 cards of a style pool, unbalanced on purpose to put every decision kind in front of the agent; some style pairs give the random agent the better deck (the heuristic agent won 1 of 6 games of "spells against mana" and 6 of 11 of "triggers against triggers" in the 100 games), and every card added to the pool changes which decks the seeded games deal. So the rate on those games measures the decks, not the agent, and 20 games have a standard deviation of about 0.09.
