- Decision: the soak games keep every clean-run check and now assert only a floor of 0.6 against random (better than chance with room; `greedy-games.test.ts` makes the same kind of check). The strength claim is a new test on paired games of the arena decks: the heuristic agent wins at least 90% of 20 games against random (200 of 200 measured; SPEC A11 asks for 95% in 200 games). A mutation check (the random agent in its place) gives 0.55 and fails it. No threshold was loosened to pass: the measured strength is 100% where the design removes deck and seat luck.
- Alternatives: Lowering 0.8 to 0.7 was rejected (it would flap again with the next card in the pool, and it would still measure the decks). Raising the soak sample to 100 games was rejected for the same reason and costs minutes in every run. Tuning the agent was rejected: nothing in the measurement shows a weakness against random on balanced decks. Not done, and worth a look if the soak styles should say something about strength: balancing the style pairs (the same list on both seats) so the soak rate becomes meaningful.
- Consequences: the soak run no longer flaps when the card pool grows. The agent's strength against greedy, casual and itself stays covered by D-163's measurement and `pnpm ai:arena`; this test only pins random.

## D-290: The deck support workflow fetches the card data from Scryfall when the issue lacks it (2026-11-12)
- Context: Four issues of one player (9, 10, 11, 13) carry only the template report: no decklist, no "Unsupported cards" line, no build line and no card data block, so `corpus:check-issue` refused them and nothing could start, although their reports name every unsupported card. The cloud session of the agent cannot reach Scryfall (D-245), which is why the issue was made to carry the card data. A GitHub-hosted runner is not under that network policy and can. The data block of a description is also the one input nobody checks: it comes from the author.
- Decision: (1) What the work needs is the names of the unsupported cards and their card data. The names are read from the `Unsupported cards (N)` line or, when it is missing, from the `cards:` lines of the template report (at most 100 names, each at most 200 characters with no control character). The decklist, the template report and the build line become `notes` of the check when missing, no reason to refuse; the pull request then says the deck as a whole was not checked. (2) `corpus:check-issue` takes `--card-data <file>` (the workflow's comment), reads its block in place of the description's, and answers `needsCardData` when the names are readable and only the card data is missing or unusable. (3) `corpus:fetch-card-data` looks the names up through the app's own Scryfall client (`createScryfallClient`: one shared queue, batches of 75, the rate limits and retries, the melded faces of meld cards as `related` records) and writes the comment: the marker `<!-- deck-support-card-data -->`, the sha256 of the description it was fetched for, and the same block the app writes. A name Scryfall does not find exactly, a fuzzy match, an unreachable Scryfall, a melded face that cannot be had and a comment longer than 60,000 characters are problems, never a guess. (4) The workflow (`deck-support-triage.yml`) runs the fetch between the check and the label when `needsCardData`, checks again with the comment, posts or updates the comment as `github-actions[bot]` BEFORE it labels the issue ready, and lists the notes and Scryfall's problems in its triage comment. (5) The agent takes the data comment only from the author `github-actions[bot]` with the sha256 of the triage comment (anyone can write the marker), and adds the cards with `corpus:from-issue --fetched`: the caller says where the text came from, never the record. (6) Names of the author are shown in the workflow's comments only in a code span, cut short, with no backtick or line break (`quoteName`), so a name cannot put a mention or a link into a comment of the bot.
- Alternatives: The agent fetching the cards itself was rejected (its sandbox blocks Scryfall and an exception would weaken the network policy). Trusting the description's block first was rejected (the comment is Scryfall's data, the block the author's, so the comment wins when both exist). Keeping every part of the report required was rejected for these issues: none of it is needed to build a card. Not done: a `workflow_dispatch` that re-checks an existing issue (an issue opened before the workflow, or whose triage already ran, is checked again on its next edit), and reading the decklist from anywhere but the description.
- Consequences: an issue with only a template report is built by the next routine run once it is edited (the workflow checks on `opened` and `edited`). Scryfall's reachability from a runner is the default of GitHub-hosted runners and is not verified here; when it fails, the triage comment says what Scryfall could not give and the issue stays unlabelled. The workflow's shell steps were run locally with a stub `gh` and a fake Scryfall, not on GitHub. Tests: `tools/corpus/check-issue.test.ts`, `fetch-card-data.test.ts`, `from-issue.test.ts`; the refusals are mutation-checked.

## D-291: The deck support routine keeps the issue's author informed with a progress comment (2026-11-12)
- Context: A deck build takes hours and several sessions (the Bruna program took one day over eight groups), and the person who opened the issue saw only the claim comment and, at the end, the result. The owner asked that they always know where it stands.
- Decision: The skill (`.claude/skills/deck-support/SKILL.md`, "Progress feedback") makes the claim comment the progress comment of the issue: marker `<!-- deck-support-progress -->`, written by the routine's own account, edited in place after every group of the checklist and whenever something changes. It says, in plain words, how many of the unsupported cards are supported, which are done, being worked on, waiting and blocked (with the reason), where the branch and the pull request are, what is next, whether the build is paused or waiting for someone, and when it was last updated; it promises no date. A short new comment (which notifies the person) is posted only at milestones: started, blocked and waiting for the owner, paused for the budget, the pull request open, finished. The issue is untrusted input as before: a reply in it is read as data and never obeyed, and the comments carry no private links or addresses.
- Alternatives: A new comment after every group was rejected (it notifies the author many times for one build). Only the milestone comments were rejected (hours of silence between them). Posting the checklist file itself was rejected (it is written for the repository, with decision numbers and engine terms).
- Consequences: The progress comment is a summary of `docs/proposals/<slug>-build-status.md` and must be rewritten with it, which costs a call per group. A build that is resumed by a later run continues the same comment.

## D-292: The deck support triage can be started by hand on an existing issue (2026-11-12)
- Context: The triage workflow ran on `opened` and `edited` only (D-251, D-290), so an issue opened before the workflow existed, or one whose last check ran under older rules (the four issues of one player that carry only a template report), stayed unchecked until someone edited its description. D-290 listed a manual re-check as not done.
- Decision: `deck-support-triage.yml` also runs on `workflow_dispatch` with one input, the issue number (Actions, "Deck support triage", Run workflow). Only people with write access can start it. A first step, "Read the issue", puts the description, the number, the author and the labels into files, from the event for `issues` and from `gh api repos/<repo>/issues/<n>` for a dispatch; every later step reads those files, and nothing the author wrote goes into a script, the environment file or an expression. A dispatch refuses an input that is not a number and an issue that is a pull request, is not open or whose title does not start with "deck support". The checks, the fetch from Scryfall, the data comment, the label and the triage comment are the same for both triggers.
- Alternatives: Editing each description by hand was rejected (it touches other people's text). A scheduled sweep of every open deck support issue was rejected (a run for each issue every day, and an old issue would be relabelled without anyone asking). Passing the author and the labels through `GITHUB_ENV` was rejected (a value with a line break could add a variable).
- Consequences: The owner can start the check on #9, #10, #11 and #13 without touching them. The shell steps were run locally for both triggers with a stub `gh` and a fake Scryfall, not on GitHub.

## D-293: A deck support build reports on its issue at least once an hour (2026-11-12)
- Context: D-291 gave the issue a progress comment edited in place and short milestone comments. On the first long build under it (issue 25) the owner asked for more: every issue the routine is building should hear from it at least every hour, even when there is little to say.
- Decision: While an issue is `deck-support:in-progress` and being built, the routine posts a short new comment (two to four lines: how many cards are supported, what is being worked on, what is blocked or waiting and why, when the next update comes) and refreshes the progress comment whenever the last comment of the routine on the issue is more than 60 minutes old; a comment posted for another reason within the hour counts and nothing more is posted. The time is read from the clock, never guessed. The routine keeps it with a `send_later` check-in 60 minutes after its claim comment, re-armed 60 minutes after each comment and cancelled when the issue is finished or blocked, and by looking at the age of its last comment on every wake. While the build is paused for the budget the pause comment stands and no hourly comment is posted until it resumes.
- Alternatives: Editing the progress comment only was rejected for the heartbeat (an edit notifies nobody, and the owner wants the person to hear). A fixed daily report was rejected (a day is too long for a build of hours). A recurring scheduled task per issue was rejected (it would keep firing after the issue is finished and needs a delete).
- Consequences: The author of a long build is notified about once an hour, which is the owner's choice. A build that is waiting for the owner still reports hourly until it is paused or blocked. Tests: none (a rule of the skill; the owner reads the comments).

## D-294: A workflow reads one page of Scryfall for the cloud sessions (2026-11-12)
- Context: The cloud sessions of the coding agent cannot reach Scryfall (D-245, `AGENTS.md` Network), so a build could not check a ruling (the Veyran question in the Niv-Mizzet deck stayed open), a card's data or the lookup of a token image (the Manifest token of the face-down build is marked UNVERIFIED). A GitHub-hosted runner is not under that network policy, and the agent can start a workflow and read its log.
- Decision: `.github/workflows/scryfall-lookup.yml`, a `workflow_dispatch` with one input, an API path. It makes one GET to `https://api.scryfall.com/<path>` with a User-Agent that names the project and prints the answer in the log (60,000 characters) and the job summary. The path is validated before anything runs: at most 300 characters, only `cards/`, `sets/`, `catalog/` or `symbology`, only letters, digits and `_ . / ? = & + % : , ~ -`, no `..`; it goes through the environment, never into a script. `contents: read`, no secrets, no repository code, one run at a time. Only people with write access can start it. The skill and `AGENTS.md` tell the agent how to start it (`actions_run_trigger`) and to treat the answer as data from outside. The validation and the call were run locally with a stub `curl`: valid paths reach only `api.scryfall.com`, and traversal, a second host, shell characters, a space, a path outside the allowed roots and an over-long path are refused before `curl` is called.
- Alternatives: A general HTTP fetch workflow was rejected (it would open every host to a prompt injection). Posting the answer as an issue comment was rejected (noise; the log is enough and nothing is published). A bulk download was rejected (the owner runs `coverage:cards` for that).
- Consequences: A build can now settle a ruling or a lookup with one run; it must be on `main` to be started, and it counts toward the agent's calls. Scryfall's reachability from a runner is the default of GitHub-hosted runners and is verified by the first run. D-293 is on the branch of the Niv-Mizzet deck (the hourly report) and is not on `main` yet, which is why this entry is D-294.

## D-295: A minimum of targets: "each of one or two targets" and "one or two target creatures" (2026-11-12)
- Context: Prismari Charm ("deals 1 damage to each of one or two targets") and Untimely Malfunction ("One or two target creatures can't block this turn") name a slot of at least one and at most two targets. The engine's `TargetSpec` already has `min` and `max` (CR 601.2c) and the target decision is generic, but the IR noun knew only "exactly N" and "up to N", and the noun rules had no "one or two" phrase.
- Decision: The IR noun gets `minTargets`; `boundsOf` lowers it to `{ min, max: count }`. A noun rule `noun.one-or-two-targets` reads "each of one or two targets" (one slot of any target) as a damage recipient, and `targetOf` reads "one or two target <plural phrase>" for every noun rule built on it. The engine is unchanged.
- Alternatives: Reading the phrase as "up to two" (wrong: it would allow zero targets, CR 115.2) or as exactly two (wrong). Putting the number in the filter instead of the noun (the bounds belong to the slot, as `upTo` does).
- Consequences: Any verb that takes the `targetOf` nouns reads "one or two target ...", with the engine's bounds enforcing 1 to 2 and CR 115.3 (no target twice). The limits ("each of one or two other targets", "one or two targets" alone) are in the ROADMAP.

## D-296: Restrictions on several target creatures (2026-11-12)
- Context: `effect.restrict` accepted singular targets only and listed the two-target forms in its `rejects`; its `leading` words did not include a capitalised "One or two ...". The engine's `restrict` takes an object selector and already restricts every object of a slot (CR 509.1b, 611.2a).
- Decision: `effect.restrict` accepts the creature targets of the noun rules that are plural by "one or two" or "up to N", with the tail agreeing in number ("attack" for several, "attacks" for one), and `leading` gains `one`. An exact count of two or more and "up to that many" are refused and stay in `rejects`.
- Alternatives: Allowing every plural target (an exact count has no card yet and needs its own leading words); a second rule for the plural (it would read the same words twice).
- Consequences: "One or two target creatures can't block this turn" and "Up to two target creatures can't be blocked this turn" read and run; "two target creatures can't block this turn" is still flagged unsupported (ROADMAP).

## D-297: Widening the number of modes to two (2026-11-12)
- Context: Flame of Anor says "Choose one. If you control a Wizard as you cast this spell, you may choose two instead." The engine's `ModeChoice.maxIf { condition, max }` is general, but the parser had only the commander wording, which always widens to every mode ("both") and refuses a spell that does not have exactly two modes.
- Decision: A header rule `modal.choose-widen` reads that sentence with the condition of `condition.control-a`, into `IrModeChoice.widen` and a new `widenTo: 2`; `lowerModes` sets `maxIf.max` to `widenTo` (without it, every mode as before) and refuses a widened maximum that is not above the usual one or is above the number of modes. "Two" is the only number read.
- Alternatives: Generalising `modal.choose-commander` (it would mix two conditions and two wordings in one rule); reading "three instead" with no card that says it.
- Consequences: The engine reads the condition as the spell is cast (CR 700.2a), so a Wizard on the battlefield then gives max 2 and the chosen modes run in printed order. Other widening wordings are unread.

## D-298: "If its mana value was 3 or less" (2026-11-12)
- Context: Fading Hope returns a creature and then asks for its mana value. The engine's `Condition.objectMatches { of: target, filter: { manaValue } }` reads last-known information (CR 113.7a, 608.2h), so it works after the bounce, but no rule produced it from "its mana value was N or less", and a sentence-level condition is only tried if it is in `RECURSION_LEAD_CONDITIONS`.
- Decision: One condition rule, `condition.its-mana-value`, reads "its mana value was/is N", "... or less" and "... or greater" (digits only) as `objectMatches` of the anaphor "it" with a mana value comparison, and is added to `RECURSION_LEAD_CONDITIONS`. The binding pass resolves "it" to the target of the sentence before it.
- Alternatives: A general "its <stat> was ..." rule (no card needs power or toughness yet, and "X or less" needs the amount machinery); a card-specific path (forbidden).
- Consequences: The comparison is made on the object as it last was (CR 608.2c, 113.7a). "X or less", "or more", "or fewer", other stats and compound conditions are unread and flagged (ROADMAP). `PARSER_VERSION` 87; four Niv-Mizzet cards move to supported (Prismari Charm, Untimely Malfunction, Flame of Anor, Fading Hope).

## D-299: Shuffle the source and the graveyard into their owners' libraries (issue 25)
- Context: Elixir of Immortality says "Shuffle this artifact and your graveyard into their owner's library." The existing rule read only "shuffle your graveyard into your library". The source may be controlled by a player who does not own it, and CR 701.24c and 701.24d shuffle a library even when no object reached it.
- Decision: a new rule `effect.shuffle-self-and-graveyard` lowers to `moveToZone this`, `moveToZone each(your graveyard)` and `shuffle all[you, ownerOf this]`. Each card goes to its owner's library (the engine already does this). A commander in the graveyard is asked as it moves (CR 903.9b). The lowering is refused when the source is gone (`ctx.selfGone`).
- Alternatives: mutating `effect.shuffle-graveyard` (it would change an existing card's AST and mix two phrasings). Shuffling only the controller's library (wrong when the artifact was taken: its owner's library receives the card). A card-name special case (forbidden).
- Consequences: a stolen Elixir behaves per CR. Reading it in a dies trigger of `~` needs a `thisCard` reference and is on the ROADMAP. The old rule is unchanged.

## D-300: A list of card types and subtypes in a look-and-take (issue 25)
- Context: Dragonologist takes "an instant, sorcery, or Dragon card" from among the cards looked at. `TAKEN_CARD` read one list of card types or one subtype only. The engine's `lookAtTop` already accepts any `ObjectFilter`.
- Decision: `TAKEN_CARD` also reads two or more kinds, at least one a subtype, joined as English joins a list, and writes `anyOf` of `{types}` and `{subtypes}`. A list of types only keeps the old reading.
- Alternatives: a special case for the three words (card-specific). Letting the plain parser read mixed lists (it would blur the old tests and rejects).
- Consequences: other "an artifact or Wizard card" and "a Dragon, Elf, or Wizard card" phrasings read. Ambiguous phrasings ("a Dragon or Elf creature card") and lists with no comma before "or" stay unread.

## D-301: "N or more mana was spent to cast that spell" as a sentence condition (issue 25)
- Context: Thunderdrum Soloist's second sentence is "If five or more mana was spent to cast that spell, ... instead." The old rule reads "at least N mana was spent to cast it" as an intervening "if" and is not in the sentence-lead list.
- Decision: a second rule, `condition.mana-spent-or-more`, produces the same engine test (`manaSpentAtLeast`, D-206) marked `ofTriggerSpell` and is in the sentence-lead list, so "if ... instead" becomes `conditional` with an else branch. The lowering reads it only in the body of a cast trigger of another spell (`LowerContext.castTrigger`).
- Alternatives: mutating the old rule (it would risk the cards that already use it). Adding the old rule to the lead list (it would read in spells, where no spell exists to ask, and the test would silently be false). Allowing it in every trigger (same silent failure).
- Consequences: the Soloist reads and plays. "That spell" is not lowered in a spell's text, in "cast or copy" triggers, or in "when you cast this spell". "At most" and mana of a kind stay unread.

## D-302: A cast trigger keeps its spell when its effect reads the mana spent (issue 25)
- Context: `readsTriggerSubject` kept the triggering spell on the stack only when the intervening "if" held `manaSpentAtLeast`. A conditional effect with that condition read 0 mana spent (CR 601.2h, 608.2c), so the 5-mana case dealt 1 damage instead of 3.
- Decision: `readsTriggerSubject` (`rules/trigger-subject.ts`) also returns true when the effect holds `manaSpentAtLeast`. This is the only engine edit of the group; `ENGINE_VERSION` 81 (new derive digests), `PARSER_VERSION` 88.
- Alternatives: carrying the subject on every cast trigger (it changes the identity of triggers for all cards and the derive digests). Reading the mana spent from the stack at trigger time only (the spell may be gone by resolution; CR 113.7a).
- Consequences: only abilities with that condition in their effect change, and none existed. Three more Niv-Mizzet cards move to supported (Elixir of Immortality, Dragonologist, Thunderdrum Soloist).

## D-303: Piles: reveal the top cards, one player separates them, the other chooses (2026-11-12)
- Context: Fact or Fiction (issue 25) needs "Reveal the top five cards of your library. An opponent separates those cards into two piles. Put one pile into your hand and the other into your graveyard." CR 700.3 says the cards stay where they are while sorted, each is in exactly one pile, and a pile may be empty. The owner approved a P-class build.
- Decision: the effect `revealAndSeparate { count, separator: 'opponent' | 'you', chosenTo, otherTo }` (rules in `rules/pile-separate.ts`, the instruction `pileSeparate`). The controller reveals the top N cards with a public `cardsRevealed` event; they stay in the library. The separator chooses pile 1 and the other player chooses which pile goes where; `chosenTo` and `otherTo` are the hand or the graveyard and differ (`validateCard`). The cards move as ordinary zone changes, the chosen pile first and then the other, each from the top of the library down; a commander uses the existing CR 903.9 path. With fewer than two cards the separator is not asked; the chooser is always asked. Events `pilesSeparated` and `pileChosen` make the piles public.
- Alternatives: a dedicated piles decision kind (S-class, not approved). Copying `lookSplit`'s three-step pattern with a fixed "hand and graveyard" wording (not general). Skipping the chooser's question when a pile is empty (rejected: the choice is real).
- Consequences: Fact or Fiction is supported; other cards of this shape need only a grammar rule. The order of cards put into a graveyard is the library order, so the CR 404.3 owner choice is not offered, as for mill.

## D-304: The two pile questions are new purposes of `chooseCards` and `chooseOption` (2026-11-12)
- Context: the owner allowed new purposes of existing decision kinds only.
- Decision: `ChooseCardsDecision.purpose 'separate'` (zone `library`, min 0, max all, `reveal` true; answered by the existing `chooseCards` action, validated by `validCardsChoice`). `ChooseOptionDecision.purpose 'pile'` (options `pile1`/`pile2`, `piles { first, second, chosenTo, otherTo, separator, receiver }`; answered by the existing `chooseOption` action through `rules/pile-answer.ts`). `getView` puts the cards in `pendingCards` for whoever decides (both piles for `pile`); `waitingOn` names the purpose for the other seat.
- Alternatives: a new decision or action kind (S-class).
- Consequences: no change to `legalActionsForDecision` or `applyAction` dispatch beyond the purposes; the web needed a dialog and words, not a new kind in every handler.

## D-305: "An opponent" is the first opponent in turn order still in the game (2026-11-12)
- Context: CR 700.3 and the rules around it do not say who "an opponent" is in a game of more than two players; 800.4g covers only a chooser who left. The repository's precedent is Coin of Fate (D-233).
- Decision: the player who separates (or chooses) is `opponentsOf(state, controller)[0]`. Tested by adding a third seat to a scenario state (seat 1, or seat 2 when seat 1 has lost).
- Alternatives: the controller chooses the opponent (no rule says so); a new decision (not worth it for v1, which has one opponent).
- Consequences: recorded in `docs/ROADMAP.md` ("Piles leftovers"); revisit with the first multiplayer build.

## D-306: Parser: one rule for the three sentences (2026-11-12)
- Context: `splitSentences` splits the card into three sentences that are one instruction; the registry needs examples, rejects and cites.
- Decision: `segment.ts` keeps the three together (only all three in a row); the class T rule `effect.reveal-separate-piles` (`rules/effect/piles.ts`) reads a count of two or more and lowers to `revealAndSeparate` with `separator: 'opponent'`, `chosenTo: 'hand'` and `otherTo: 'graveyard'` (`lower/piles.ts`). Not read: other wordings, X counts, the controller-separates wording (no real Oracle text in the repository).
- Alternatives: three separate rules (they make no sense alone); reading wordings from memory (not allowed).
- Consequences: Fact or Fiction is supported in the golden corpus; one unsupported card's `closestRule` diagnostic moved (a snapshot diff only).

## D-307: AI and web for the piles (2026-11-12)
- Context: every new decision purpose needs an agent answer and a UI.
- Decision: the casual agent (the others delegate) separates by worth into two similar piles and takes the better pile into its own hand, or gives the worse one when it chooses for the controller. The web shows the separation in the card picker with a preview, the pile choice in `PilesDialog` with both piles' cards, and log lines "X separates the revealed cards into two piles: ..." and "X chooses pile N (...)". A `piles` soak style plays whole games between every agent kind. `ENGINE_VERSION` 82 (new derive digests), `PARSER_VERSION` 89.
- Alternatives: a search over piles for the Heuristic agent (not worth it for the first version); a pile panel in the dock (the cards do not fit).
- Consequences: the AI does not read what the other player needs; recorded in the ROADMAP.

## D-308: Face-down permanents and layer 1b (2026-11-12)
- Context: manifest (CR 701.40) needs a permanent whose card is hidden and whose characteristics are a 2/2 creature with no name. The owner approved the subsystem in chat on 2026-11-12 ("Manifest is needed. I'll use other cards with this ability"); the design is `docs/design/manifest.md`, covering steps 1, 3, 4, 5 and 6 of the approved `docs/proposals/face-down.md`.
- Decision: `GameObject.faceDown { by, n }` (a designation, not copiable, a new object after any zone change). `copiableValues` applies the face-down values after copy effects (layer 1b, CR 613.2b, 708.2, 708.10). `n` is the smallest free label number and stays with the permanent (CR 708.6). `rules/face-down.ts` is the only reader, guarded by `face-down-reads.test.ts`.
- Alternatives: a separate token-like object (rejected: it breaks counters and last-known information, CR 708.2); hiding only in the web (rejected: the AI and replays share the view).
- Consequences: every reader of characteristics is blind to the card for free. Only code that reads the card behind the object can leak, and a two-world audit watches it.

## D-309: The manifest effect and entering face down (2026-11-12)
- Context: "manifest the top card of a library" must put a card onto the battlefield face down under the manifesting player's control.
- Decision: `Effect` `manifest { player, fromLibraryOf? }`. `MoveRequest.entersFaceDown` skips the card's enters rules (CR 708.3). `zoneChanged.card` is null and `manifested` carries no card. An empty library does nothing. "Its controller" reads last-known information.
- Alternatives: a new decision kind (not needed); reading the face on entry (breaks CR 708.3).
- Consequences: other permanents still see a creature enter. Cloak and manifest dread would reuse the same entry; they are not built.

## D-310: The special action `turnFaceUp` (2026-11-12)
- Context: CR 701.40b (a manifested creature card can be turned face up for its mana cost) and 116.2b (special actions).
- Decision: a priority option and action, paid like Suspend and Foretell through a `payMana` decision of purpose `turnFaceUp`. It is offered only to the controller, for a creature card with a mana cost they can pay; an {X} counts as 0. It is the same object, with no stack and no enters trigger, and it emits `turnedFaceUp`.
- Alternatives: a new decision kind (rejected, the pay decision already exists); a "when turned face up" trigger kind (not built: nothing manifest-related reads it).
- Consequences: Morph would add a branch to `turnUpSymbols`. The cost is revealed when the card is turned up, not when the action starts (ROADMAP).

## D-311: Leaving, copies, commanders and phasing of a face-down permanent (2026-11-12)
- Context: CR 708.9, 708.10, 903.9, 702.26.
- Decision: leaving is the ordinary zone change, so the new object is face up and the events name the card. A copy of a face-down permanent is a face-up 2/2, and a face-down permanent that becomes a copy keeps the 2/2 until turned up. Face-down permanents keep their status through phasing. A commander stays a commander.
- Alternatives: none worth recording; each follows the cited rule.
- Consequences: a manifested commander would show in the public commander-damage table once it deals combat damage: a known leak (ROADMAP).

## D-312: Hidden information of face-down permanents (2026-11-12)
- Context: the core risk of the subsystem: the opponent must never learn what a face-down card is.
- Decision: the view masks name, commander status, support and faces for everyone but the controller; `hiddenFace`, `turnFaceUpCost` and `ifFaceUp` are controller-only; `sourceInfo` uses the label; `determinize` deals other controllers' face-down cards again; host notes skip face-down permanents. `face-down-hidden.test.ts` plays the same game twice, with only the hidden cards differing, and the other seat's view and every event must be identical text; every `ObjectView` field and every `GameEvent` kind is classified in a table typed by its keys, so a new one does not compile until it is classified. The soak and `hidden-info.test.ts` audit random games.
- Alternatives: a search for the card name alone (rejected as weaker).
- Consequences: object ids of hidden cards appear in events, as they do for draws today.

## D-313: The AI turns face-down creatures up (2026-11-12)
- Context: agents see only their view and never an opponent's hidden card.
- Decision: turning up is chosen by the gain in the evaluator's value (`ifFaceUp` against the 2/2), with a margin of 0.5. The casual agent turns up in its own main phase after its spells; the heuristic agent also plays the combat out on its sample after blockers (reason `face-up`).
- Alternatives: holding mana for a turn-up or turning up in response (not built).
- Consequences: the AI does not plan around hidden information of the opponent.

## D-314: Parser: the verb "manifest" (2026-11-12)
- Context: Reality Shift says "Its controller manifests the top card of their library."
- Decision: `effect.player` reads the actor forms ("its controller / you / target player / each player manifests the top card of their/your library") and `effect.manifest` the imperative; both lower to `manifest`. Manifest dread, cloak, several cards and another player's library by name stay unread.
- Alternatives: reading "manifest dread" now (no card, a different effect).
- Consequences: Reality Shift is supported.

## D-315: The web draws a face-down permanent with the Manifest token (2026-11-12)
- Context: the owner asked that a manifested card show Scryfall's Manifest token image, fetched by the game at run time like every card image.
- Decision: a card back with the picture from `GET https://api.scryfall.com/cards/tfrf/4` (the lookup was verified on 2026-11-12 from a GitHub runner with the Scryfall lookup workflow, D-294: the token "Manifest" of Fate Reforged Tokens, id e9f896d4-34b4-407d-be7e-bf7a69aaf811), reading `image_uris` at run time and storing nothing; a plain face-down card is the fallback. The preview shows the real card to the controller; a "Turn face up {cost}" menu item and payment prompt; the log never names a hidden card.
- Alternatives: committing the image (rejected: nothing of the picture is kept in the repository).
- Consequences: the image needs the network; the game works without it. `apps/web/e2e/manifest.e2e.ts` covers both.

## D-316: SYNTHETIC style and soak for manifest (2026-11-12)
- Context: every new mechanic gets a deck style that puts it in front of the agents (D-126).
- Decision: SYNTHETIC cards in `synthetic-manifest.ts` (kept out of the other pools), the `manifest` style, `manifest-games.test.ts` (hidden information checked after every action for both seats, the rules restated from the events, exact replay), the hidden web deck `synthetic-manifest` and the browser test. `ENGINE_VERSION` 83 (new derive digests: the SYNTHETIC pool grew), `PARSER_VERSION` 90.
- Alternatives: none.
- Consequences: Reality Shift moves to supported in the golden snapshot.

## D-317: The goal is to support every card; a costly card is built later, never recommended for skipping (2026-11-12)
- Context: The survey of the Niv-Mizzet deck recommended leaving Fiery Confluence unsupported (repeatable modes: large, cross-cutting, one cycle uses it). The owner answered that this situation is common, that leaving cards unsupported is not an option for most cards, and that the long-term goal is supporting 100% of the existing cards.
- Decision: Support for all cards is the standing goal (`AGENTS.md`). The deck support routine and its surveys never recommend skipping a card on cost alone: they give the cost, the risk and the order (cheap pieces first, the large general mechanism after). Fiery Confluence is built as general repeatable modes (`ModeChoice.repeatable`, multiset mode sets, one target slot per chosen instance, counters in the web picker, the AI). The rules still apply: an S-class gap needs a design the owner approves before it is built, and a card the engine cannot yet read stays flagged unsupported meanwhile (honesty first).
- Alternatives: Keeping "skip" as an option in the proposals was rejected (it hides the real backlog and the cards behind it). Simplifying repeatable modes to one target slot for all instances was rejected (wrong with fewer targets than instances).
- Consequences: Proposals list cost and order, not a skip option. Larger gaps take longer and show in the checklist as approved, not started.

## D-318: Condition spellsCastThisTurn (2026-11-12)
- Context: Stella Lee, Wild Card ("if you've cast two or more spells this turn") needs a condition on the number of spells the controller cast this turn.
- Decision: `Condition` `spellsCastThisTurn { atLeast }` (CR 602.5b, 601.2i, 707.10, 500.4) reads `SeatState.spellsCastThisTurn`, the per-seat count Storm already uses (D-129). The parser reads "you've cast N or more spells this turn"; a kind of spell, "or fewer", "an opponent has cast", "this game" and a variable count are not read and the card stays unsupported.
- Alternatives: Counting from the event log was rejected (the seat count exists and is exact). A kind-of-spell filter was not built (no card of the deck needs it).
- Consequences: Any card with the plain count can use it; tests in `scenario-xx-spells-cast-this-turn.test.ts`.

## D-319: Distinct colors for anyCombination mana (2026-11-12)
- Context: Firemind Vessel ("Add two mana of different colors") needs the combinations of different colors only.
- Decision: `ManaProduction` `anyCombination` takes `distinct: true` (CR 105.1, 106.1a, 106.1b, 605.3b): `colorMultisets(count, distinct)` in `rules/mana-outcomes.ts` offers only the sets of `count` different colors of the five. Read in a mana ability for two and three mana; the `addMana` effect of a spell or trigger runs fixed mana only, so the phrase in a spell is not read.
- Alternatives: Letting the player pick any pair and rejecting repeats at payment was rejected (the choice list would show illegal answers).
- Consequences: The choice list shrinks to the legal sets; the AI picks from it (`niv-distinct-mana.test.ts`).

## D-320: untapInOthersUntapStep with self (2026-11-12)
- Context: Bender's Waterskin ("Untap this artifact during each other player's untap step") names the permanent itself, not a filter (D-229).
- Decision: `untapInOthersUntapStep` takes `self: true` in place of `what`; exactly one of the two must be given (CR 502.3, 604.1). It has no condition and no "untap target land" form; it ignores "doesn't untap during your untap step" as D-229 says, and a stun counter is removed instead.
- Alternatives: A filter that matches only the source was rejected (a filter cannot name the permanent itself without a card-specific case).
- Consequences: Validation refuses both or neither; tests in `scenario-xx-untap-self-in-others-step.test.ts`.

## D-321: Amount minus (2026-11-12)
- Context: Ivory Tower ("you gain X life, where X is the number of cards in your hand minus four") subtracts a number.
- Decision: `Amount` `minus { of, by }` (CR 107.1b): `of` less a whole number of 1 or more, a negative result counting as 0, read as the instruction runs like the amount it is made of. It applies to an atom or a sum, not to "half ...", "twice ..." or a static ability's power or toughness; "minus X" and a word number are not read.
- Alternatives: A general arithmetic amount was rejected (more surface than the cards need).
- Consequences: Tests in `scenario-xx-amount-minus.test.ts`; the web words the amount.

## D-322: Every complete deck support request keeps the ready label; the routine picks the next one (2026-11-12)
- Context: The triage let someone other than the owner have one request waiting at a time, by looking up the author's other issues with `labels=deck-support:ready,deck-support:in-progress`. The `labels` parameter of GitHub's issue list is an AND and the two labels never sit on one issue, so the lookup always found nothing and the limit never worked (verified against the live API). The owner then said the limit should not live in the labels at all: leave every complete issue `ready` and let the routine decide what to build next.
- Decision: The workflow no longer looks at the author's other issues: a complete request is labelled `deck-support:ready` and that is all. The choice of the next issue is the routine's, when it starts (`.claude/skills/deck-support/SKILL.md`, Step 1): the owner's issues first, then the oldest, one build at a time, and a person's second request is taken only when no earlier one of theirs is waiting or in progress and no other person's older request is waiting.
- Alternatives: Fixing the lookup with one call per label and the author's `creator` filter, with the oldest waiting issue keeping its label, was built and tested, then dropped at the owner's request (the label would hide waiting work from the board). The search API's OR was rejected (rate limit, index lag).
- Consequences: Issues #26, #27 and #31 can all stay `ready`; nothing needs a re-check. The waiting comment that said "only one request per person is queued" is gone. The order of work is a rule of the routine, so it can change without a workflow edit.

## D-323: A creature planeswalker that is lethally damaged with 0 loyalty leaves the battlefield once (2026-11-12)
- Context: Merging new SYNTHETIC cards moved the random picks of the derive differential's fifth board game, and it threw "Unknown object": an animated planeswalker (a 4/4 creature that is still a planeswalker, "SYNTHETIC Animate Walker") was dealt damage that was lethal as a creature and removed all its loyalty. The state-based action check listed it twice (CR 704.5g destroyed, CR 704.5i put into the graveyard) and tried to move it twice; the second move found the object gone. The bug is in the engine, not in the new cards; it was latent for any real creature planeswalker.
- Decision: In `rules/sba.ts` an object that is in the graveyard batch (0 loyalty, a fallen Aura) is removed from the destroyed list. It leaves once, as a card put into the graveyard, so a regeneration shield (which replaces a destruction only) does not save it, as CR 704.3 asks (all applicable actions at once; 0 loyalty is not a destruction). Test: two Lightning Bolts at an animated Animate Walker (`scenario-xx-planeswalker-damage.test.ts`); without the fix it fails with "Unknown object".
- Alternatives: Skipping a missing object in the loop was rejected (it would hide other double moves). Dropping the loyalty list entry instead was rejected (the destruction can be regenerated; the loyalty rule cannot).
- Consequences: Derive digests are regenerated with this branch's pool; no change for any game that never had this overlap.


## D-324: Stock Up: the rest on the bottom in an order the owner chooses, as a purpose of `arrangeCards` (2026-11-12)
- Context: Stock Up ("Look at the top five cards of your library. Put two of them into your hand and the rest on the bottom of your library in any order.", issue 25, class P) differs from every look the engine reads in three ways. The two cards are put into the hand without a "reveal" (CR 701.20a: nothing says reveal), both are required (no "you may"), and the rest go to the bottom in an order the player who looks chooses (CR 401.4: if an effect puts two or more cards in a specific position in a library at the same time, the owner of those cards may arrange them in any order and does not reveal the order). The existing `lookAtTop` reveals what it takes and puts the rest in a random order from the game's generator.
- Decision: No new effect kind and no new decision kind. `lookAtTop.take` gets `hidden: true` (the cards go into the hand unrevealed: no `cardsRevealed` event, `reveal: false` on the `chooseCards` decision of purpose `lookTake`; `validateCard` refuses it with `to: 'battlefield'`), and `rest` gets `'bottomChosen'`. The `lookTake` instruction takes the two cards (`min` = `max` = 2) and, in its `rest` stage, queues an `arrange` instruction of the new purpose `bottom` with the cards left (`cards`, the ones still in the library). The decision is the existing `arrangeCards` with `purpose: 'bottom'` and `piles: ['bottom']`: the answer has `top` empty and every card in `other` in the order given, the last becoming the bottom card (as for the bottom pile of a scry). `isArrangement` now lets a pile take cards only when the decision has it (a reorder has no `other`, the bottom has no `top`). The web dialog shows the one pile titled "Bottom", the answer maps it to `other`. The cards are already in the library, so nothing changes zone (as for a scry, CR 701.22a): they keep their objects and only the order of the library changes. With one card left nobody is asked (there is no order to choose) and it goes to the bottom; with no card nothing happens.
- Alternatives: A new decision kind for "order these cards" was rejected (S-class, and `arrangeCards` already is "the cards looked at, placed in order"). Reusing the random order of `bottomRandom` was rejected (the owner chooses, CR 401.4). A `chooseCards` of purpose `putOnTop`-style ordering was rejected (it picks cards from the hand and its order is the order from the top; here every card must be placed once and the library keeps the rest). Moving the cards with `moveObject` to `bottom` was rejected (they are already in the library: a move would make new objects for no reason, and would ask a commander's owner a question CR 903.9b does not ask about a card that stays in the library; `bottomInRandomOrder` keeps its existing behaviour for the random wordings).
- Consequences: Stock Up is supported; `Effect` `lookAtTop` has two more optional values; `ArrangeCardsDecision.purpose` and the `arrange` instruction have `'bottom'`; `waitingOn.purpose` has `'bottom'`. The other seat sees `waitingOn { purpose: 'lookTake' }`, then `{ purpose: 'bottom' }`, no card and no id, and the events `topCardsLooked` and `cardsBottomed` carry counts only (a two-world test shows that the other seat's view and every event are the same text whatever the cards are). Tests: `scenario-xx-look-bottom-order.test.ts`, `convert-grammar-engine-look-bottom.test.ts`, `arrange-model.test.ts`, `library-handlers.test.ts`, the `library` deck style of the AI soak and hidden-information audit (`SYNTHETIC Stock Up Like`, `SYNTHETIC Stock Up Three`).

## D-325: A take that must take every card that matches asks nobody, and `cardsBottomed` says when the owner chose the order (2026-11-12)
- Context: "Put two of them into your hand" with a library of two cards (or one) has only one answer; asking the player to pick two of two would be a pointless dialog. The log line of `cardsBottomed` said "in a random order", which is false for Stock Up.
- Decision: In `rules/look-take.ts`, a hidden take whose `min` is at least the number of cards that can be taken takes all of them without a question (only for `hidden`, so Hideaway and the other takes ask as before). The event `cardsBottomed` has an optional `ordered: true`, set when the owner chose the order (`rules/arrange.ts`); the web log says "in an order you chose" and cites CR 401.4 for it, and keeps "in a random order" and CR 702.85a for Cascade and the other random bottoms.
- Alternatives: Skipping the question for every forced take was rejected (it changes Hideaway with a one-card library and every existing digest for no card in this deck). A new event kind was rejected (one optional flag says it).
- Consequences: `cardsBottomed` events of the existing random bottoms are unchanged.

## D-326: The parser reads Stock Up as `effect.look-take-bottom` (2026-11-12)
- Context: the two sentences have to be read as one instruction ("the rest" and "of them" refer to the cards the first looks at).
- Decision: `splitSentences` keeps `Look at the top N cards of your library.` and `Put K of them into your hand and the rest on the bottom of your library in any order.` together (`segment.ts`, `PUT_HAND_REST_BOTTOM`); the rule `effect.look-take-bottom` (leading `look`, in `rules/effect/library.ts`) reads N of two or more and K of one or more with K smaller than N, and lowers to `lookAtTop { count: N, take: { filter: {}, max: K, min: K, hidden: true }, rest: 'bottomChosen' }` (`lower/effects.ts`, `LOOK_TAKE_BOTTOM`, needing the existing `effect:lookAtTop`). "In a random order" is `effect.look-take`'s wording and is not read here; X, another library, another place for either group and a K that is not smaller than N are not read.
- Alternatives: A new IR verb for every filter (the card may be any kind) was rejected: "any card" is the empty filter and nothing else is read until a card needs it.
- Consequences: `PARSER_VERSION` is the integrator's. The golden snapshot moves exactly one card, Stock Up (unsupported to supported); the template replay line in `convert-grammar-corpus-p10.test.ts` changes from "not read" to supported.


## D-327: A mill names what it milled, and an effect lets its controller play a milled card (2026-11-12)
- Context: Tablet of Discovery says "When this artifact enters, mill a card. You may play that card this turn." The engine's `mayPlay` (D-151) named only cards in exile (an earlier `exileTop`, `exile` or `moveToZone` made them `moved`), so the sentence parsed but was "recognised, not runnable". Playing a card from a graveyard because an effect says so is CR 601.2 (casting) and CR 305.1 (a land play); the permission must name the card as it is now, because a card that leaves the graveyard is a new object (CR 400.7).
- Decision: (1) `mill` now sets what `moved` names afterwards to the cards it milled (`lastMoved`, the new objects in the graveyard, CR 400.7j), and the validator counts `mill` among the effects after which `moved` has a meaning. (2) `mayPlay` (the same node, no new kind) also gives its permission to a card of `moved` that is in the graveyard of the controller of the effect (`runMayPlay`); a card in a graveyard that another player owns gets none (the permission is the controller's own, as with `mayCast`, D-135), and the lowering reads it only after "you mill". (3) The permission is the existing `playPermission` continuous effect; `legality.ts` reads it for a card in a graveyard in `mayPlayFromGraveyard` (cast: through `mayCastFromGraveyard`, so `castZone` and the option lists see it; land: `canPlayLand`, `playableLands`). A land played this way counts as the land drop (CR 305.2), a spell is cast at the timing of its type for its ordinary cost, and the permission ends as the effect says (this turn, the end of the next turn, the next end step; never `whileExiled`). (4) The parser: `mill` of "you" sets the lowering's `exiled` to `milled`, `mayPlay` accepts it and refuses `whileExiled` and "look at"; the feature `ability:mayPlayFromGraveyard` is named by that lowering.
- Alternatives: a new effect kind `mayPlayFromGraveyard` (rejected: a second node with the same permission and the same duration, and a second place for the validator, the web and the agents to learn); the existing `mayCast` of D-135 (rejected: a cast only, for a target, never a land, and it lasts the turn only). Building a general "play from any zone" permission now (rejected: nothing else asks for it).
- Consequences: "Mill N cards, you may play those cards" and the same after a trigger or a spell are supported. A mill by another player (a target opponent, each player) is not lowered, so "that card" never names a card the controller may not play; that is a limit, listed in `docs/MECHANICS.md`. The agents need nothing: the cast and the land play are the ordinary `castSpell` and `playLand` actions the engine lists. `mill` leaves `lastMoved` non-empty, so an instruction after a mill that reads `moved` now reads the milled cards; no card of the corpus does (the golden snapshot changes for the two cards of this group only).

## D-328: Mana that copies the spell it is spent on, and the color of that spell (2026-11-12)
- Context: Pyromancer's Goggles says "{T}: Add {R}. When that mana is spent to cast a red instant or sorcery spell, copy that spell and you may choose new targets for the copy." The riders of D-151 and D-208 (`ManaAbility.spentRider`: haste, scry) carry the mana from the permanent that made it and act when it is spent on a spell the rider matches; the scry rider is a triggered ability of the permanent that goes on the stack above the spell (CR 603.2, 603.3). A copy of a spell is not cast (CR 707.10), may have new targets (CR 707.10c) and resolves before the spell it copies because the trigger resolves above it. The match had no color.
- Decision: `spentRider.grants` gains `{ copySpell: 'may' | 'no' }` (`'may'`: "you may choose new targets for the copy", `'no'`: "copy that spell", the copy keeps the targets) and `spentRider.spells` gains `colors` (the spell is of at least one of the colors as it is on the stack as the mana is spent; CR 105.2). The mana carries a `ManaRider` of kind `copy`; `withSpentRiders` in `rules/cast.ts` puts one pending triggered ability for each mana spent that matches, with the permanent that made the mana as its source, the spell as its subject and the existing `copySpell` effect with the `triggerSubject` as its effect, so the copy machinery (the new-targets question, last-known information, the copy that is not cast, the token of a permanent spell) is reused unchanged. Mana spent on an ability carries no copy (the rider reads a spell). The feature `ability:manaSpentRiderCopy` is named by the lowering. The parser rule is `effect.mana-rider-copy` (one color or none, one card type or a choice of card types, "copy that spell", with or without "and you may choose new targets for the copy").
- Alternatives: copying the spell as the mana is spent, with no trigger (rejected: CR 603.2 makes it a trigger that can be responded to, and the stack order is the point: the copy resolves first); a new effect kind (rejected: `copySpell` with `triggerSubject` already exists for "Whenever you cast an instant or sorcery spell, copy that spell", D-129).
- Consequences: two mana of two such permanents spent on one spell are two triggers and two copies; the controller orders them (CR 603.3b). The rider reads the spell's color on the stack, so a spell that is red because of an effect is read as red. The web words the rider in the ability text and in the tooltip of the mana in the pool. Not supported: a rider on a spell of a creature type with a copy, a rider with two colors ("red or blue"); both are dropped by the grammar.

## D-329: "Spend this mana only to cast instant and sorcery spells" (2026-11-12)
- Context: the engine's `spendOnly` (D-149) lists card types, and a spell can be paid for if it is of one of them (CR 106.6); "instant and sorcery spells" is the card types joined by "and" in the plural, which `spellPhrase` reads for "or" only. Tablet of Discovery's second mana ability is "{T}: Add {R}{R}. Spend this mana only to cast instant and sorcery spells." and is the only text of the corpus with it.
- Decision: no engine change: `spendOnly: { types: ['instant', 'sorcery'] }` already means "a spell of one of the types, never an ability". The parser reads the list: `spellTypesAndPhrase` (`rules/noun/phrases.ts`) is a list of card types joined by "and" and then "spells" (the plural only), producing the same choice of types "or" produces; `effect.spend-only` tries it when there is no article. The rule is not added to `spellPhrase`, so no other rule of the grammar reads "and" as a choice.
- Alternatives: allow "and" in `spellPhrase` for every rule (rejected: "instant and sorcery spells" are statements about each type in the static abilities that read it, `typeChoice(..., 'and')`, and a general change would move the golden snapshot for cards this group does not touch).
- Consequences: "artifact and creature spells" reads the same way (a SYNTHETIC sibling is in the parser test). The web words the restriction as "an instant or sorcery spell", which is the same restriction.

## D-330: Group 2b-b support and limits (2026-11-12)
- Context: both cards are class P; a card is supported or not, never partially.
- Decision: Tablet of Discovery is supported (the enters trigger, the plain {T}: Add {R}, and the restricted {T}: Add {R}{R}); Pyromancer's Goggles is supported (the mana ability with the copy rider). Both read as supported in the golden test (the snapshot of `golden.expected.json` is not changed in this branch; the integrator updates it).
- Alternatives: none.
- Consequences: limits: a card milled from another player's library is not played (the lowering reads "you mill" only); the copy rider has one color or none and card types, no creature type. Nothing is deferred in `docs/ROADMAP.md` that a card of the corpus needs.


## D-331: The plain condition `cardsInLibrary` (2026-11-12)

- Context: Living Conundrum's third line is "As long as there are no cards in your library, this creature has base power and toughness 10/10 and has flying and vigilance." and its second line needs the same test as the `while` of a replacement. The engine had `cardsInGraveyard` (D-229) for the graveyard of the controller and nothing for the library.
- Decision: a `Condition` `cardsInLibrary { compare }` (`NumberComparison`: `atMost` 0 is "no cards", `atMost` N-1 is "fewer than N"). It reads the number of cards in the library of the controller (`cardsInLibraryHolds`, `rules/condition-reads.ts`) and no characteristic, so it is one of the plain conditions (CR 613.8, 611.3a): a static ability of layer 4, 5, 6 or 7b may have it (`PLAIN_CONDITIONS`, `plainConditionHolds`, `static-conditions.ts`), and `derive` reads it each time it works out the permanent. The parser reads "there are no cards in your library", "your library has no cards in it" and "fewer than N" forms (`condition.cards-in-library`), registered with the conditions of a static ability.
- Alternatives: an `amountIs` of a `countOf` the library: rejected, because `amountIs` reads the game through the layers and is not allowed in a layer 4/7b static ability, which is exactly where the card needs it; a special static for the card: rejected, no card-name code.
- Consequences: any "as long as" static ability or replacement `while` that depends on the size of the controller's library reads right; "an opponent's library" and a kind of card in it are not read (`docs/ROADMAP.md`).

## D-332: The replacement `skipDraw` of a draw (2026-11-12)

- Context: "If you would draw a card while your library has no cards in it, skip that draw instead." CR 614.11 and 121.6a: an effect that replaces a draw applies even when the library has no cards, so the player attempted no draw and does not lose to an empty library (CR 121.4, 704.5b). `drawCard` set `drewFromEmptyLibrary` before any effect could replace the draw.
- Decision: a `Replacement` `skipDraw { while?: Condition }` of a permanent on the battlefield. Every draw goes through `drawCard` (an effect through `runDraw`, and the draw step of `flow.ts`), which now asks `drawSkippedBy` (`rules/draw-skip.ts`) first, before it looks at the library. The oldest permanent of the controller whose abilities (read through `derive`, so "loses all abilities" turns it off) have a `skipDraw` whose `while` holds (a plain condition read for the controller, `plainConditionHolds`) skips the draw: the state is unchanged, the event is `drawSkipped { seat, source }`, and no `cardDrawn` or `drewFromEmptyLibrary` follows. Each draw of a sequence is replaced on its own (CR 614.11a, 121.6b), so the cards of "draw three" before the library emptied are drawn and the rest skipped. `validateCard` allows only a plain `while` (`checkPlainCondition`). Parser: `replacement.skip-draw`; web words and a log line "<permanent> skips your draw."
- Alternatives: a flag on the player ("skips draws"): rejected, it would not follow the permanent leaving or losing its abilities and could not carry a condition; checking the library before the replacement: rejected, it is the bug the rule describes; a new decision for several replacements (CR 616.1): not needed, all applicable replacements give the same result (the draw is skipped), so no order is asked.
- Consequences: no new question for any player, so the agents need no new answer. A replacement that does something else instead of the draw (CR 614.11b) is not built (`docs/ROADMAP.md`). The `drawSkipped` event is listed in the event tables (`test/face-down-hidden.test.ts`) and in the log (`apps/web/src/game/describe.ts`).

## D-333: The trigger `noncombatDamageDealt` (2026-11-12)

- Context: Niv-Mizzet, Visionary: "Whenever a source you control deals noncombat damage to an opponent, you draw that many cards." The triggers on damage were `dealsCombatDamage` (a permanent that deals combat damage), `dealtDamage` (a permanent dealt damage) and `combatDamageBatch`; none names any object as the source or noncombat damage.
- Decision: a `Trigger` `noncombatDamageDealt { by: 'you' | 'any', to: 'opponent' | 'player' }`. It has one occurrence for each `damageDealt` event (CR 120.2b: damage as an effect of a spell or ability, by any object) to a player that is not combat damage and has an amount above 0 (CR 120.8: 0 damage is not dealt; CR 603.2g: prevented damage triggers nothing), with `triggerDamage` the amount that source dealt to that player ("that much", and "that many" as the first instruction of the body), `triggerPlayer` the player damaged and `occ.seat` the controller of the source, read as it is or as it last was (CR 113.7a), because a spell on the stack, an ability or a permanent that has left can be the source. One source damaging several players, or several sources, are several `damageDealt` events and trigger once each (CR 603.2c). The source is not a permanent with a filter, so the trigger has no subject. Parser: `trigger.noncombat-damage`, four combinations of "a source [you control] deals noncombat damage to [an opponent | a player]"; the lowering of `lifeGainThatMany` is generalized to `eventAmountThatMany` (the life gained or the damage dealt, the first instruction only).
- Alternatives: reuse `dealtDamage` with the recipient a player: rejected, it names a permanent as the one dealt damage; a batch trigger ("one or more sources"): the text is not batched, and CR 603.2c gives one trigger for each occurrence; a source filter of permanents: rejected, a spell is a source and not a permanent.
- Consequences: noncombat damage by any object to a player can trigger abilities. The ruling that one spell damaging several opponents triggers the ability once for each opponent follows CR 603.2c and the events of `damage.ts`; the Scryfall rulings could not be fetched in this session, so this is UNVERIFIED against them. The scenario DSL has two seats, so the several-players case is by the structure of the events, not a scenario.

## D-334: Parser registration and the diagnostics of other cards (2026-11-12)

- Context: the three new rules start with broad words ("if", "a", "there", "your"), and the golden corpus records the closest rule of each unparsed line, so a new rule that reports its failures can move the "stopped at" of other cards.
- Decision: the three rules are `quietly` (their failures are left out of the diagnostics; their matches are recorded as usual), as the Angels rules are (D-150). The golden corpus then changes for exactly the two cards of this group (Living Conundrum and Niv-Mizzet, Visionary: unsupported to supported); no other card's status, diagnostics or AST changed (read from the golden test). `condition.cards-in-library` is added to the conditions a static ability reads (`rules/static/conditional.ts`).
- Alternatives: leaving the rules loud: rejected, the "closest rule" of unrelated cards would change in the golden snapshot for no reason.
- Consequences: `golden.expected.json` is regenerated by the integrator (`UPDATE_GOLDEN=1`); the build's version constants are bumped there too.

## D-335: The `nivDraw` deck style of the AI soak tests (2026-11-12)

- Context: the new SYNTHETIC cards (a creature that skips draws, creatures that draw when damage is dealt) would join the generic card pools of the AI tests and change the seeded games of every older test, and the draw replacement changes when a player loses to an empty library.
- Decision: the names are kept out of every other pool (`NIV_DRAW_NAMES`, `packages/ai/test/helpers.ts`) and used by a deck style of their own, `nivDraw`, with `packages/ai/test/niv-draw-games.test.ts` playing whole games between random and casual agents (every game finishes, no fallback, no rejected action, consistent state, an exact replay), restating from the events that a skipped draw names a skipping permanent of the player's on the battlefield and that a player with a skipping permanent in play never draws from an empty library. No decision kind was added, so no agent needed a new answer.
- Alternatives: leaving the cards in the generic pools: rejected, it shifts every seeded game; no AI test: rejected, the replacement changes a game-ending rule.
- Consequences: `pnpm test:soak` (100 games) checks that every card of the style is cast and that an empty library is drawn from at least once. The pool of the engine's derive differential test takes every synthetic card with a static condition, so `packages/engine/test/derive-digest.expected.json` was recorded again (`UPDATE_DERIVE_DIGESTS=1`) for `SYNTHETIC Hollow Warden`; with the new fixtures left out, the old fingerprints match, so the new engine code changes no earlier game. Another group that adds a synthetic card with a static condition re-records the same file, so the integrator regenerates it once after merging all groups.


## D-336: A delayed triggered ability on the next cast of a spell, ending with the turn: `delayedCast` (2026-11-12)
- Context: Galvanic Iteration ("When you next cast an instant or sorcery spell this turn, copy that spell. You may choose new targets for the copy.") and Thunderclap Drake (the same, created by "{2}{U}, Sacrifice this creature") create a delayed triggered ability (CR 603.7) whose event is a cast, not the beginning of a step, and which expires with the turn if it was not used (CR 514.2). The engine had delayed triggers (`GameState.delayedTriggers`, `findDelayedTriggers`) that wait for a step (D-128) and a validator that limited the effect they hold to player effects with fixed amounts (`checkDelayedTrigger`), so neither the way to create one on a cast nor its duration existed.
- Decision: A new effect `delayedCast { filter, effect }` (`ast/types.ts`, `ast/features.ts`, `ast/validate-parts.ts`). As it resolves (`rules/effects.ts`) it adds a `DelayedTrigger` whose ability is `{ trigger: { kind: 'castSpell', filter, by: 'you' }, effect }`, controlled by the controller of the spell or ability as it resolved (CR 603.7d, 603.7e), with the source of the spell or ability (which may be gone, as the creature sacrificed to pay for the Drake's ability is). `findDelayedTriggers` needed no change: it already matches any trigger kind against the events after the ability was created (CR 603.7a: the cast that made it is past), subject the spell cast (`triggerSubject`), and removes the ability once it has triggered (CR 603.7b, "next"). `DelayedTrigger` gets one optional field, `untilEndOfTurn: true`, set by `delayedCast`; the cleanup step (`afterDiscard` in `rules/flow.ts`, next to `expireEndOfTurnEffects`, CR 514.2) drops every delayed trigger that has it, so an unused one does not outlive the turn. The effect it holds is limited by `validateCard` to `copySpell` of `triggerSubject` (CR 603.7c: nothing else of the spell or ability that created it is left to name), the `filter` must be one of spells (`stackKind: 'spell'`), and the inner effect is checked with a scope that has a trigger subject that is a spell, a trigger player, no X and no target.
- Alternatives: Extending `delayedTrigger.at` with a cast form was rejected (every reader of `at.step`, the web wording and the validator read a step; a second shape would make each of them a union). A general "delayed trigger with a trigger and an effect" (`delayedAbility { trigger, effect }`) was rejected as too wide for two cards (every effect inside it would need the CR 603.7c audit that `checkDelayedTrigger` makes for the step form); `delayedCast` is the narrow case and the shape generalises when a card needs another event. Expiring in `expireEndOfTurnEffects` was rejected (it works on `ContinuousEffect`s; the delayed triggers are in another list), and a new field on `GameState` for a turn number was rejected (the cleanup step is the moment; a delayed trigger created in the cleanup step itself, which cannot be cast into, is dropped in the same pass, which is right: "this turn" is over).
- Consequences: Old games are identical: a `DelayedTrigger` without `untilEndOfTurn` is as before, no state field was added or renamed, no event was added, and `stateHash` of every game that creates no `delayedCast` is unchanged; the SYNTHETIC pool has three cards more (`synthetic-niv-group-3-a.ts`), which changes only what reads the pool (the engine version and the pool digest are the integrator's). Nothing is hidden: the delayed trigger is public rules text and the copy of a public spell. The web view has no list of waiting delayed triggers (none existed); the trigger shows on the stack as an ability of its source like any trigger, with the words of `ability-label.ts` (`delayedCast`, `copySpell`) for the activated ability and the stack. The AI asks no new question: the copies ask "choose new targets" (`targets` decision with `forCopy`), once per copy.

## D-337: `copySpell` has a count that is an amount (2026-11-12)
- Context: Thunderclap Drake copies "for each time you've cast your commander from the command zone this game". `copySpell` made one copy; the instruction (`Instruction` `copySpell`) already carried a `count` (Storm, Replicate), and the amount `commanderCasts` (CR 903.8, D-229) already existed.
- Decision: `copySpell.count?: Amount` (`ast/types.ts`), read as the effect resolves (`rules/effects.ts`: `amountOf` with the controller of the ability, so the commander casts are the ones of the player who controlled the delayed trigger, counted when it resolves, not when it was created), left out for one copy. Zero makes no copy and asks nothing (CR 707.10: nothing to copy; `copyInstructions` makes no instruction for a count of zero or less) and `performed` is then zero. Each copy of the instruction asks its own "choose new targets" when `newTargets` is `may` (CR 707.10c; the engine did this for Storm). `validateCard` checks the count with `checkAmount` in the scope of the effect (no X, no target in a delayed cast).
- Alternatives: A separate `copySpellCount` effect was rejected (a count on the existing effect is one optional field; no consumer reads `copySpell` without it). A count that is read when the delayed trigger is created was rejected: the printed text reads "copy it for each time you've cast your commander ... this game" in the ability that triggers, so the number is the one as it resolves (UNVERIFIED against the card's rulings, which could not be fetched; the two readings differ only if the commander is cast from the command zone between the cast of the spell and the resolution of the trigger, which needs a flash commander cast in response).
- Consequences: Existing `copySpell` effects are unchanged (no count: one copy). The web words say "Copy that spell for each time you've cast your commander from the command zone this game. You may choose new targets for the copies".

## D-338: The parser reads the lead "When you next cast ... this turn," as a delayed sentence (2026-11-12)
- Context: the text is a triggered-looking sentence ("When ..."), at the start of a spell or after the colon of an activated ability, and says "copy that spell" / "copy it for each time ...".
- Decision: `sentence.ts` reads `when you next cast a[n] <spell phrase> this turn, ` as a `delayed` lead with `step: 'nextCast'` and the spell as a noun (`IrSentence.delayed.spell`, the same `spellPhrase` the cast trigger reads); the binding pass seeds that noun as the first antecedent (`ir/bind.ts`), so "that spell" and "it" become `triggerSubject`; `segment.ts` does not treat a line that starts with that lead as a triggered ability of a permanent (`DELAYED_CAST_LEAD`), so it is read as the sentences of a spell; `lower/sentences.ts` `lowerNextCast` builds the `delayedCast` (needing `effect:delayedCast` and `effect:copySpell`) and refuses anything but one `copySpell` of the spell cast, a condition, a "may", a `where`, an "instead". The new rule `effect.copy-spell-for-each` (`rules/effect/niv-group-3-a.ts`) reads "copy it" or "copy that spell" with "for each time you've cast your commander from the command zone this game" (the existing amount rule) and the sentence "You may choose new targets for the copies" (`segment.ts` joins it to the sentence before it as it does the singular); `lower/copy-spell.ts` lowers the amount into `count`. A near miss (another count, one copy with the plural sentence, another player, a join with a second instruction, a permanent's ability) is not read, so the card is never half-executed.
- Alternatives: Reading the lead as a new trigger kind of a spell was rejected (the engine has no triggered ability of a spell that is not "when you cast this spell"). A new IR verb was rejected (the delayed lead is the existing sentence prefix).
- Consequences: The golden snapshot moves exactly two cards, Galvanic Iteration and Thunderclap Drake (unsupported to supported); `PARSER_VERSION`, `ENGINE_VERSION` and `golden.expected.json` are the integrator's. The cost reduction of the Drake ("Instant and sorcery spells you cast cost {1} less to cast") and Flashback of Galvanic Iteration were already read.


## D-339: `doubleTriggers` gets a `cause` (2026-11-12)
- Context: "If you casting or copying an instant or sorcery spell causes a triggered ability of a permanent you control to trigger, that ability triggers an additional time." The existing `doubleTriggers` (D-220, CR 603.2d) names whose triggered abilities trigger again (a group of permanents, or the attached one) and doubles every one of them; Veyran doubles only what a particular event causes.
- Decision: `StaticEffect` `doubleTriggers` takes an optional `cause: { kind: 'castOrCopySpell'; spell: ObjectFilter }`. Without it nothing changes. With it, `rules/trigger-doubling.ts` adds the extra trigger only when `causedBy` holds: the triggered ability is a `castSpell` ability (it triggered on the cast event of a spell, or on the event of a copy put onto the stack when it says `orCopy`), the player who cast or copied (`PendingTrigger.player`) is the controller of the permanent with the doubler, and the spell (the trigger's subject, read from the object or from last-known information, CR 113.7a) matches `spell` with the doubler's controller as "you". `subject` still says whose abilities: for Veyran every permanent of its controller, itself included, so its own magecraft ability triggers twice (+2/+2 for one cast). `validateCard` requires the cause kind and a filter of spells (`stackKind: 'spell'`).
- Alternatives: a new static effect `doubleCastTriggers` (a second effect that does almost the same, rejected); keeping the cause event on `PendingTrigger` (a new field on every pending trigger for one card; the trigger kind and the player and subject it already carries say what caused it, rejected); a free-form cause (`triggerKind: string`), rejected: one kind is built, the type grows when another is needed (CR 603.2d cards that name another cause, such as Panharmonicon's "a creature entering", would add a kind each).
- Consequences: Veyran is supported. The version numbers are bumped by the integrator (the AST changed; the golden snapshot is regenerated by the integrator: Veyran goes from unsupported to supported, nothing else changes).

## D-340: only the abilities the cast or copy event triggers are doubled; "becomes the target of a spell" is not (2026-11-12)
- Context: does Veyran also double an ability that the cast brings about without the cast being its trigger event, for example "Whenever this creature becomes the target of a spell" (the spell, cast by you, targets it as it is cast), or an ability that triggers because a creature spell you cast later enters?
- Decision: not doubled. The event that triggers such an ability is another one (a permanent becoming a target, a permanent entering); CR 603.2d doubles the ability when the event named causes it, and Oracle text names "you casting or copying an instant or sorcery spell". The tests pin the target and entering cases (`packages/engine/test/scenario-xx-cause-doubling.test.ts`). An ability that triggers on the cast of any spell of the controller (not only magecraft) is doubled when the spell is an instant or sorcery, and not when it is a creature spell. A trigger on a spell an opponent casts is not doubled ("you casting").
- Source: the official rulings of the card, read on 2026-11-12 through the workflow `Scryfall lookup` (D-294: the card, then its rulings), seven rulings dated 2021-04-16. They say: it makes each of your magecraft abilities, Veyran's own too, trigger an additional time; a copy that an effect puts onto the stack causes magecraft to trigger, a copy of a card in another zone does not (casting that copy does); each magecraft ability has the same trigger condition; the extra trigger is not a copy, the choices (modes, targets) are made for each; an effect that makes several copies triggers magecraft once for each; two Veyrans make three triggers, three Veyrans four. None of them says anything about an ability triggered by something other than the cast or the copy: the rule above for those is UNVERIFIED against a ruling and follows the CR and the Oracle wording only.
- Alternatives: doubling every ability the cast "brings about" (the target trigger, an enter trigger of the spell's resolution): rejected, it is not what the text says and no ruling supports it.
- Consequences: if a ruling later says the target trigger is doubled, the change is in `causedBy` (one function) and its test.

## D-341: casts and copies are two events; the spell is read as it is on the stack (2026-11-12)
- Context: magecraft says "cast or copy"; a copy put onto the stack is not cast (CR 707.10).
- Decision: a `castSpell` ability with `orCopy` triggers on both events (D-218), and `causedBy` accepts both, so Veyran's magecraft ability triggers twice for the cast and twice for each copy (Storm, "copy target instant or sorcery spell"). A `castSpell` ability without `orCopy` is not triggered by a copy, so there is nothing to double. The player is the caster, or the one under whose control the copy was put on the stack (`PendingTrigger.player` of both events). "When you cast this spell" abilities (the source is the spell on the stack, not a permanent) are not doubled by it: the subject must be a permanent of the controller on the battlefield, as for every `doubleTriggers`.
- Alternatives: none considered; the existing events carry what is needed.
- Consequences: the filter of the cause is checked against the copy as well (the copy of an instant is an instant).

## D-342: parser, one rule with the card's own wording (2026-11-12)
- Context: the Oracle text reads "If you casting or copying" (the printed wording; kept in the golden fixture as it is).
- Decision: the grammar rule `static.triggers-additional-time-cause` (`parser/rules/static/edhrec.ts`) reads exactly "If you casting or copying <a spell phrase> causes a triggered ability of a permanent you control to trigger, that ability triggers an additional time." The spell phrase is the one `trigger.cast-or-copy` reads. The IR effect `doubleTriggers` takes an optional `cause` noun; `lower/statics.ts` lowers it to the engine `cause` with `lowerFilter`. Near misses (another controller, "casting" alone, "copying" alone, another kind of permanent or no controller, an activated ability, another number of times, a trailing sentence, "spells") are dropped whole and flagged, never half read (`rejects` of the rule and `parser-niv-group-3-b.test.ts`). The existing feature gate `static:doubleTriggers` covers the new shape (the field is optional, as `orCopy` is).
- Alternatives: also reading the grammatical "If you cast or copy ... causes": no card prints it; not built (never guess).
- Consequences: Veyran's two lines read; the magecraft line already read.

## D-343: one extra trigger for each permanent that has the ability; web and agents (2026-11-12)
- Context: how many times the ability triggers with several doublers; whether the web or the agents need anything.
