- Decision: each permanent with a matching doubling adds one trigger (CR 603.2d: the number of times is determined, then that many; an effect that makes an ability trigger additional times does not apply to other such effects), so two Veyrans make three triggers for one cast. Unchanged from D-220: a permanent with two matching `doubleTriggers` abilities still adds one. The extra triggers are identical, so ordering them is no question (the engine asks about ordering only between different abilities, CR 603.3b). Web: static abilities are shown by the card's Oracle text, which is unchanged; nothing was hidden or reworded. Agents: no new question (the targets and modes of each extra trigger are the ordinary decisions of a trigger).
- Alternatives: counting an ability with two matching abilities twice: left as D-220 had it; no card does it.
- Consequences: the Veyran ruling (two Veyrans make three) holds, and is tested with a stand-in.


## D-344: Repeatable modes: `ModeChoice.repeatable` and a choice of modes that is a multiset (2026-11-12)

- Context: "Choose three. You may choose the same mode more than once." (CR 700.2d) lets the controller choose a mode several times; "If a particular mode is chosen multiple times, the spell is treated as if that mode appeared that many times in sequence." D-114 built `legalModeSets` for sets of distinct modes and listed "the same mode twice" as not built. The owner decided (D-317) that a card that is common enough is built as a general feature, not for one card.
- Decision: `ModeChoice.repeatable?: true` (`ast/types.ts`). The modes chosen stay an array of mode indices in printed order, now with repeats allowed when the text says so (`[0, 0, 2]`): `StackData.chosenModes`, the `chooseModes` action and the `modesChosen` event keep their shapes, so no new decision kind, no new action kind and no new event kind. `ChooseModesDecision.repeatable` (present only when true) says the `sets` are multisets and that `max` may be more than the number of modes. `legalModeSets` lists, for a repeatable choice, every multiset of between `min` and `max` of the modes that can be chosen (fewest first, then lexicographic: a mode may be taken again), `isLegalModeSet` compares the sorted array with the listed sets (the list says whether a repeat is allowed), `modeLimit` has no widening for a repeatable choice, and the invariant "chosen modes are in printed order" is non-strict for a repeatable choice. The instances of a mode run one after the other in printed order of the modes (CR 608.2c, 700.2d).
- Alternatives: A counted map `{ mode: count }` in the state and the action: rejected, every consumer (the view, the log, the AI, the copy code, the tests) already reads an array of indices, and a sorted multiset is the same information. A separate `repeatableModes` field on the spell text instead of a flag on the choice: rejected, the flag is a property of how many modes are chosen and the choice already has `maxIf` and `notRepeatedThisTurn` beside it. Making the number of choices a list of an enumeration without a bound: rejected, the engine lists every legal answer (D-114), so the number of multisets is bounded (D-346).
- Consequences: A mode chosen once is exactly what it was, so no old text, action log or digest changes (the digest of 6 precon games from `tools/perf/precon-digest.ts` is identical before and after, and the soak games of every older style are unchanged because the new cards are kept out of the generic pools, D-349). Escalate (D-145) counts the instances (`chosenModes.length`) as it counts modes, which is what a repeatable Escalate card would need; no such card is supported or tested yet.

## D-345: Every instance of a mode has target slots of its own (2026-11-12)

- Context: A single slot for all instances of a targeted mode would be wrong when there are fewer targets than instances (CR 700.2d: the same target may be chosen for each, or different ones; CR 601.2c: targets are chosen for every instance of the word "target"), and a slot of the whole spell would also make "destroy target artifact" three times with two artifacts a different spell. The slot ids of a mode are unique across the modes, and effects name their slots by id.
- Decision: The first instance of a mode keeps its slots' ids; the later ones get `<id>#2`, `<id>#3`, ... (`instanceId` in `rules/modes.ts`; `baseSpecId`, exported from the engine, undoes it for a reader that wants the slot of the text). `chosenModeSpecs` returns the slots of every instance in printed order, each a copy of the mode's `TargetSpec` with its own id (and `differentFrom` renamed within the instance); `chosenEffect` rewrites the `{ kind: 'target', id }` nodes of the instance's effect to the instance's ids (`instanceEffect`), so the resolution reads each instance's own targets from `chosenTargets` with the code it always had (`stillLegalTargets`, CR 608.2b: an instance whose target is gone does nothing and the spell fizzles only when all its targets are illegal). `TargetChoiceSpec.instance` (present from the second instance on) says which instance a slot is, for the web prompt. A slot never takes the same target twice (CR 601.2c), but two slots may take the same one. `targetChoiceSpecs` takes a map of `{ mode, instance }` (`specModes`). The same code serves a spell, an activated ability, a triggered ability and the copy of a modal spell (the copy keeps `chosenModes` and `chosenTargets`, CR 707.10 and 700.2g, and its new-targets question lists the slots of every instance with `forCopy`). A triggered ability whose slots are all forced (one legal target for each) takes them without asking (CR 603.3d), as before.
- Alternatives: One slot with a larger `max` for all instances of a mode: rejected, it cannot express two instances aimed at the same target with fewer targets than instances, and it changes `targets` decisions that the web and the AI read one slot at a time. Rewriting the effect text when the card is imported (copies of the mode in the AST): rejected, the number of instances is the player's choice as the spell is cast. A different id syntax (`id@2`): `#` was chosen because no id the parser or the fixtures write has one; the validator refuses an id with `#` in a repeatable choice.
- Consequences: Old spells and abilities have no instance slot: their slot ids, decisions and events are unchanged. `legal-actions.ts` lists the combinations of targets of a decision that has instance slots up to 500 (as `choosePermanent` lists its choices, `MAX_LISTED_CHOICES`), because three slots of ten artifacts is a thousand combinations; any legal answer is accepted all the same. Decisions without instance slots are listed in full as before.

## D-346: What a repeatable choice may say (2026-11-12)

- Context: The validator must refuse what the engine cannot run or list (D-114: "the engine lists every legal choice").
- Decision: `validateCard` accepts `chooseModes { min, max, repeatable: true }` with `0 <= min <= max`, `max >= 1`, and `max` may be more than the number of modes; `min` 0 is "Choose up to N. You may choose the same mode more than once." (an empty choice is a legal answer for a spell and an activated ability: it resolves and does nothing; a triggered ability with no mode chosen is removed from the stack, CR 700.2b, which the engine does not run, so the validator refuses `min` 0 on a triggered ability and such a card stays unsupported). A repeatable choice has no `maxIf` and no `notRepeatedThisTurn`. The number of multisets between `min` and `max` of the modes may not exceed `MAX_REPEATABLE_SETS` (2000, `ast/validate-modes.ts`). A target id with `#` is refused in a repeatable choice. The 2 to 8 modes limit (`MAX_MODES`) is unchanged. A choice that is not repeatable is validated as before (1 <= min <= max <= number of modes).
- Alternatives: No bound on the number of sets: rejected, the action list and the decision would grow without limit. A lower bound on `min`: "up to" is a real wording and costs one case.
- Consequences: Eight modes and up to five choices (1286 multisets) are allowed, ten choices of eight modes are refused with the card unsupported, honestly, rather than half run.

## D-347: The parser reads the header of a repeatable choice (2026-11-12)

- Context: The Oracle text of Fiery Confluence is "Choose three. You may choose the same mode more than once." followed by bullets, with no dash after the header; the bullets already parsed. `modal.choose` reads only the dash forms.
- Decision: The rule `modal.choose-repeatable` (`parser/rules/modal/index.ts`) reads `Choose <two..ten>. You may choose the same mode more than once.` and `Choose up to <two..ten>. You may choose the same mode more than once.`, as the lead line of a spell, a triggered ability (after "When ~ enters,") or an activated ability (after the cost); the engine runs "up to" on a spell and an activated ability only (D-346). `IrModeChoice.repeatable` carries it and `lowerModes` writes `chooseModes { min, max, repeatable: true }` (`min` is the number, or 0 after "up to"); the lowering no longer requires `max <= number of bullets` for a repeatable choice. Not read: "Choose one. You may ...", "Choose up to one. You may ...", "Choose X ...", "Choose any number ...", a bare "Choose three —", a number above ten. `PARSER_VERSION` is not changed here (the integrator does it once for the group).
- Alternatives: Reading the sentence "You may choose the same mode more than once." as a separate rule that modifies any header: rejected, the number word is part of the same sentence ("Choose three.") and a header that is not read must not leave a half-read modal.
- Consequences: Fiery Confluence is supported from the grammar alone (no override). The golden snapshot (`golden.expected.json`) changes for that one card (unsupported to supported, acceptance 226 of 245) and is regenerated by the integrator.

## D-348: The agents and repeatable modes (2026-11-12)

- Context: The agents answer `chooseModes` with one of the listed sets and `targets` with a legal answer; a repeated mode must not make the opponent waste a whole choice on one artifact.
- Decision: `RandomLegalAgent` picks one of the listed sets, as it did. `CasualAgent` (and `HeuristicAgent`, which uses it for modes) scores a set as the sum of its modes (`chooseModesAnswer`); when `ChooseModesDecision.repeatable` is set, an instance of a mode that names a target scores only while there are targets for it (`worthRepeating`: the opposing creatures for "destroy/damage target creature", the opposing permanents of the type for "target artifact"), so three instances of "destroy target artifact" are worth no more than the artifacts there are; a mode that can go to a player each time (damage to each opponent) is worth every time. `chooseModalTargets` plans a slot of a later instance with the plan of the slot it repeats (`baseSpecId`) and takes other targets than the earlier instances of the same mode when there are others. `isModalText` reads "Choose three" and the other number words.
- Alternatives: Always choosing the best single mode three times: rejected (three destroys of one artifact). Reading the legal targets of each mode in the agent: the agent reads the view, as for X (`casual-x.ts`).
- Consequences: No change for a choice without repeats (each mode appears once, the first instance scores as before). The agent's answer is always a listed set.

## D-349: Web, soak and the SYNTHETIC pool (2026-11-12)

- Context: The mode picker was checkboxes and radio buttons; the stack and the log said each chosen mode once; the SYNTHETIC cards that test the feature must not change the seeded games of the other styles.
- Decision: The mode dialog shows, for a repeatable choice, a counter for each mode ("-", the count, "+", `data-mode-times`) and the heading of the card ("Choose three. You may choose the same mode more than once."); a digit adds one choice of the mode, Shift and the digit takes one away; Confirm is enabled only for a multiset the engine listed (compared sorted). The targets prompt groups the slots of a mode chosen more than once by the time the mode is chosen ("Mode 3, time 2: Destroy target artifact"). The stack and the log say a mode chosen more than once once with how many times ("Fiery Confluence deals 1 damage to each creature (x2); Destroy target artifact"). The five SYNTHETIC cards of `synthetic-repeatable.ts` have their own deck style `repeatable` in `packages/ai/test/helpers.ts` and are filtered out of the generic pools (as `nivDraw` is), with a soak test `repeatable-modes-games.test.ts` that restates the rules from the cards' texts. The synthetic pool therefore gains five cards, but no existing style draws them: the soak games and the precon digests of every other style are unchanged. No Playwright test was added in this change: the sandbox had no Chromium, and an unrun browser test is not left for the nightly job to find out (the click and key paths are covered by model and static-markup tests, `apps/web/test/modes-repeatable.test.tsx`).
- Alternatives: Adding the cards to the existing `modal` style: rejected, that test restates distinct-mode sets and would change its games.
- Consequences: A browser test of the counters is owed once Chromium is available (`docs/ROADMAP.md`).


## D-350: Casting a target card from a graveyard as an effect resolves: the effect `castCard` and the cast during resolution that pays the mana cost (2026-11-12)
- Context: Quistis Trepe ("When ~ enters, you may cast target instant or sorcery card from a graveyard, ...") lets its controller cast a card of any player's graveyard while the trigger resolves (CR 608.2g), paying its mana cost. The engine's casts during a resolution were all free or for an alternative cost of the card (`castFree`, Cascade, Suspend, Madness, Miracle) and only from exile or the hand; casting from a graveyard needed a standing permission (`mayCast`, flashback, D-232), never a one-time effect on a target, and `beginCast` with `resolving` had no way to pay the ordinary cost.
- Decision: A new effect `castCard { object: target, anyManaType?, exileInstead? }` (`ast/types.ts`, `ast/features.ts`, `ast/validate-parts.ts`: the card is a target of the ability; the riders are `true` when present). As the effect runs (`rules/effects.ts`) the target is read from the targets still legal (CR 608.2b: a card that left its graveyard is an illegal target, so the ability loses it or does nothing) and an instruction `castCard` is queued in two stages like `castExiled` (`rules/cast-card.ts`, dispatched from `rules/stack.ts` because it needs `legality.ts`): `start` asks `canCastDuringResolution(state, controller, card, 'normal', anyManaType)` and goes on to `ask` only when the card could be cast now; `ask` is the existing decision kind `confirmOptional` with a new purpose `castCard` (the card as `subject`, public because it is in a graveyard), so no new decision kind. The answer is routed in `api.ts` `answerConfirm` to `rules/cast-card-answer.ts`: accepting calls `beginCast(state, controller, card, undefined, 0, true, false, riders)`, declining leaves the card in its graveyard. `canCastDuringResolution` gets the alternative `normal` (the card is in a graveyard, whoever owns it: the effect names it; no timing, X as the cast announces it; the cost is the mana cost with no alternative; the check reads the cost with `anyType` when the effect says so); `beginCast` with `resolving` and no alternative reads it as `normal`, takes the zone of the card (a graveyard now, besides the hand and exile), does not use up the standing graveyard permission of D-232 (`graveyardUse` only when not resolving), and writes the riders on the spell's `StackData`. The caster controls the spell and pays; the card keeps its owner (CR 108.3). The cast can be taken back with `cancel` as the others (CR 733: the state at the question is the snapshot).
- Alternatives: Reusing `castFree` with a `paysCost` flag was rejected (its question is a `chooseCards` among a set the effect names, with lands and a hand filter; here the card is a single target and the question is a yes or no). Reusing `mayCast` ("you may cast ... this turn") then letting the ordinary cast action do it was rejected: the cast must happen as the trigger resolves (CR 608.2g), before any player has priority, and the permission would let the player cast it later or not at all, and would leave the card in the graveyard for anyone. A new decision kind was rejected by the task (and is unnecessary: the existing `confirmOptional` with a purpose carries everything). Folding "you may" into an ability-level `optional` plus a plain mandatory cast was rejected: it would ask twice (the ability's question, then the cast's), and the effect has to be optional itself for the cases that are not triggers.
- Consequences: Another card that lets a player cast a card of a graveyard when an effect resolves needs a parser rule and perhaps one more flag, not an engine change. The cast from a graveyard during resolution is never a land (the `canCastDuringResolution` check refuses a land) and never a card of another zone with this effect (the exile and the hand keep `castFree` and `castExiled`). Quistis's rulings could not be fetched (the host is blocked): nothing beyond the CR text is assumed.

## D-351: "Mana of any type can be spent to cast that spell": `SpendTarget.anyType` and `StackData.anyManaType` (2026-11-12)
- Context: CR 609.4b: an effect that says mana of any type can be spent "affects only how the player may pay a cost. It doesn't change that cost, and it doesn't change what mana was actually spent to pay that cost". The engine had no way to let a spell be paid with mana that is not of the colors of its symbols (a restriction on the mana was the only rule that changed what could pay).
- Decision: `SpendTarget` (the description of what the mana is spent on, `mana/pool.ts`) gets `anyType?: true` for a spell. The payment planner (`mana/payment.ts` `buildProfiles`) folds, in each profile, every demand for a color or for colorless into the generic demand when the target has it, so any mana pays any symbol: the colored symbols, `{C}`, the colored half of a hybrid symbol (CR 107.4e: the symbol is then paid by one mana of any type) and the mana option of a Phyrexian symbol (CR 107.4f; the life option is unchanged). The snow demand (`{S}`, CR 107.4h) stays: it needs mana from a snow source, which is not the type of the mana. A restriction on the mana itself (CR 106.6) stays: `restrictionAllows` is not touched. The plan still records what was actually spent (`spentTypes`, `spentSnow`), so "the amount of mana spent" and the mana-from-a-source readers see the real mana (CR 609.4b). The flag is set where the spell's mana is checked and where it is paid: `CostRequest.anyType` and `SpellCost.anyType` (the check that the card can be cast, `canPayRequest`, `canPaySpellCost`), `castManaPlan(..., anyType = spell.stack?.anyManaType)` (automatic payment, the payment options of Convoke and the like), `answerPayment` (the payment by hand, `payByTapping` with the target). `StackData.anyManaType` is written on the spell by `beginCast` from the riders of the effect and is read from the spell on the stack afterwards; it belongs to that one spell (a copy has none, a spell of the same card cast later has none).
- Alternatives: Rewriting the cost symbols to generic before planning was rejected: the cost is shown to the player as printed (the payment prompt, the log, the view's `totalCost`), and a Phyrexian or hybrid symbol is not generic. Giving every mana object a type override was rejected: the permission is the spell's, not the mana's. Folding in `buildItems` (making each source produce `C`) was rejected: it would change what is recorded as spent.
- Consequences: Another effect of this family ("you may spend mana as though it were mana of any color to cast spells of ...", Mycosynth Lattice, Chromatic Orrery) can set the same flag on the target (a static ability is the next step: it would be read in `castManaPlan`). The permission is for spells only; an ability cost is not given it.

## D-352: "If that spell would be put into a graveyard, exile it instead": `StackData.exileInstead` and the replacement in the zone-change pipeline (2026-11-12)
- Context: CR 614.1a, 614.6: a replacement effect that uses "instead" makes the modified event happen, not the original one. The engine has the same shape for Flashback (a spell cast with flashback is exiled when it leaves the stack, `StackData.flashback`), Unearth and finality counters, all in `rules/zones.ts` `moveOne`. Quistis's rider is bound to one spell cast by one effect and applies only to a move to a graveyard.
- Decision: `StackData.exileInstead?: true`, written by `beginCast` from the riders of the effect. In `moveOne`, before the commander replacement and next to the flashback rule: a spell on the stack with the flag that would be put into a graveyard goes to exile instead (resolving as a non-permanent, being countered by an effect or by the rules for illegal targets, any other move to a graveyard); a move to another zone (the battlefield for a permanent spell, hand, library, command) is not changed, and a permanent spell is not affected until it would be put into a graveyard from the stack, which it does not do. The exile is nobody's zone, so `toSeat` is cleared and the card keeps its owner. The flag is on the spell, not the card: the card in exile is a new object with no stack data (CR 400.7), so it is cast again later without the rider.
- Alternatives: Reusing `flashback` as the flag was rejected: it makes the spell cost its flashback cost, appears in the view as a flashback cast and is checked by the invariants against the card's own flashback ability. A continuous effect that names the spell was rejected: the spell is the same object only until it moves, and `StackData` is already where the other per-spell riders live (`free`, `alt`, `hasteUntilEnd`, `graveyardPlay`).
- Consequences: Any card that says "if that spell would be put into a graveyard, exile it instead" (Ephemerate-like riders on spells, Rebound is another mechanism) can set the same flag. Only the move from the stack is replaced.

## D-353: An instant or sorcery that resolves goes to its owner's graveyard (2026-11-12)
- Context: The finishing of a resolution (`rules/stack.ts` `finish`) moved a resolved spell with `toSeat` set to its controller, so a card cast by a player who does not own it ended in the caster's graveyard. CR 400.3: "If an object would go to any library, graveyard, or hand other than its owner's, it goes to its owner's corresponding zone". The two are the same player for every earlier card, since only a card of another graveyard (this effect) is cast by a player who does not own it.
- Decision: the destination seat of a non-permanent spell that resolves is its owner; a permanent still enters under its controller (CR 110.2) and an Adventure is exiled for its caster (CR 715.3d). Found by the first scenario test (the Bolt of an opponent's graveyard went to the caster's graveyard when cast without the exile rider).
- Alternatives: None considered: the CR is explicit. A countered spell already goes to its owner's graveyard (`moveObject` defaults to the owner).
- Consequences: Nothing changes for a card cast from its owner's zones. The same applies to any later effect that lets a player cast another player's card.

## D-354: Reading the text: one sentence with its rider, and the sentence's own "you may" (2026-11-12)
- Context: "Blue Magic — When ~ enters, you may cast target instant or sorcery card from a graveyard, and mana of any type can be spent to cast that spell. If that spell would be put into a graveyard, exile it instead." is a trigger whose body is two sentences, the second of which is a rider of the first, and begins with "you may", which the triggered-ability lowering turns into an `optional` of the whole ability (CR 603.5) with the clause lowered as a plain one. The cast effect asks its own question, so that reading would ask twice. ("Blue Magic —" is an ability word, no rules meaning, CR 207.2c; the flavor-word rule of the parser already takes it off when the line does not read as written.)
- Decision: `parser/segment.ts` joins the sentence "you may cast target ... from a graveyard[, and mana of any type can be spent to cast that spell]." with a following "If that spell would be put into a graveyard, exile it instead." (as it does for other two-sentence instructions). The rule `effect.cast-graveyard-card` (`parser/rules/effect/niv-group-3-c.ts`; leading `cast` and `you`) reads "(you may) cast target <types> card from a graveyard" with the optional riders, only one target and only "a graveyard" (not "your graveyard", not "up to", not several, not "this turn", not "without paying its mana cost"), with nothing joined after it. The lowering (`parser/lower/niv-group-3-c.ts`, `acceptsOptional`) writes `castCard` and refuses a clause that is neither optional (the sentence's "you may") nor says "you may" itself, so a mandatory cast is not read. In `parser/lower/triggers.ts` a sentence of `castCard` clauses that are optional is a permission (like `mayPlay`): the ability gets no `optional` of its own and the clause keeps its optional mark for the lowering. The second sentence is taken into the clause (it is "that spell"), not read alone: "If that spell would be put into a graveyard, exile it instead." as a line of its own is still unread.
- Alternatives: Lowering to a `may` effect around a mandatory cast was rejected (two questions, and the engine's `castCard` is optional by itself). Reading the rider as its own rule was rejected (it needs the spell cast by the first sentence, which no other reading names).
- Consequences: The same lead and riders read for an activated ability when the second sentence is absent; with it the activated and spell routes classify the line as a replacement before the sentences are split (ROADMAP). `PARSER_VERSION` and the golden snapshot are the integrator's: the real card reads as supported with the AST of `docs/MECHANICS.md`.

## D-355: SYNTHETIC card names are unique across fixture lists (2026-11-13)
- Context: Two builders of the Niv-Mizzet deck each wrote a fixture named "SYNTHETIC Quiet Bear" (a 1/1 for {1} and a 2/2 for {1}{G}). `SYNTHETIC_CARDS` is keyed by name, so the later one replaced the earlier one without a sound, and the cast-or-copy tests of Veyran saw a card that costs {1}{G} and could not be cast with the mana they gave. The full test run found it.
- Decision: The 2/2 is renamed "SYNTHETIC Quiet Cub". The combined list is exported as `SYNTHETIC_ALL_LIST`, and `test/synthetic-unique-names.test.ts` fails when a name belongs to two different cards. One older clash ("SYNTHETIC Wither Imp", two lists that predate the guard) is allow-listed in the test, because renaming it would move old seeded games.
- Alternatives: Making `SYNTHETIC_CARDS` throw on a duplicate was rejected (it would fail every test file at import for the old clash). Renaming Wither Imp was rejected (digests and soak games).
- Consequences: The pool order of the generic soak and derive games changed once, and the derive digests were regenerated. A future clash fails one small test with the name.
